13226: A lord of a castle is known for his cruelties and excesses. To make up somewhat for his misdeeds, he regularly gives a feast. On Christmas Eve another such feast takes place. During the meal there is a knock at the door and the lord sees a poor child begging for alms. He gives the child nothing and has it chased away by his dogs. It is said that the child was the Christ Child Jesus. The lord is destroyed together with his castle, and he returns in the shape of a wolfhound. As punishment for his sins, the lord must roam the churchyard in the shape of a dog during the six weeks around Christmas.
48812: Account of a Zeeland witch trial in which the accused, Cathelynken, is found guilty and burned. She had earlier been reprimanded by the authorities for deceiving the people who came to consult her.
49768: The farmhands of Jan the brewer die one after another. Jan and the priest begin to suspect witchcraft, and when a little black cat walks into the brewery, Jan throws boiling brew at it. The next morning his own wife's face turns out to be burned.
49772: A clog maker and his family are about to die of hunger. In exchange for the soul of the youngest child, the devil offers a meal for them all. The clog maker accepts but is helped by Mary: with the cry "Break my clog" the devil is struck. In the end the family is found dead, having died of hunger, but with a blissful smile on their faces.
156120: Whoever was ridden by the mare felt as if all the devils of hell were sitting on his body. In the morning he woke up drenched in sweat and could not sleep for a week. Whoever placed his clogs crosswise on top of each other was protected against the mare.
156124: When fishermen set out to sea at night and met a black cat on the way, they went back home. For they believed that the cat was a sorceress who would bring them bad luck.
156144: Whoever was ridden by the mare saw a woman approaching and was tied up shortly afterwards.
156151: A woman who was mistreated by her husband saw black cats everywhere. Near her cat there actually was a black cat roaming about, so people believed the woman had been bewitched by that cat. One day that black cat wandered around the church during mass. The children shouted: "Sister, the witch cat is inside!" Just as the priest began mass, the cat jumped onto the pulpit. When the parishioners began to sing, the cat began to miaow. The sister said to one of the schoolgirls: "Do you dare catch that cat? Then I'll give you a reward." The girl went towards the cat, which then walked to the choir. When the cat was caught, the sister put the animal in a sack, which she tied shut with iron wire. A farmhand then buried the animal alive, after he had asked: "Sister, am I not committing a sin by burying the cat this way?" The cat went on miaowing for a while and then died. The following night the sister heard noise in her room the whole time. For a good half hour the sister lay sweating with fear. Then she lit the light and saw that there was a mouse sitting at the foot of her bed.
156153: Sorcerers who had learned their arts from books of magic could make people lose their way by pointing their walking stick at them.
156167: A woman said to a man riding a bicycle: "By the time you reach the end of the cobblestones, the chain will fall off your bike!" And so it happened.
156176: A man coming back from Staden saw two nuns sitting in a pollard willow next to a farm. The man spoke to the nuns, but they did not answer. A moment later they had vanished.
156192: A mother went to the priest with her child because the child's little head had been turned around. The priest said to the mother: "Go home quickly, for she will come by at such-and-such a time looking for her donkey." When the mother got home, a woman did indeed come by and asked: "Haven't you seen my donkey?" The mother did not answer and went inside. The child was cured some time later, just as the priest had predicted.
156196: A carter's cart was stuck in a muddy hole. As long as a woman from the village stood by the cart, no horse could get it free. When the woman went home and did something peculiar, the cart came loose at once. If Easter nails were put under the door, that woman could not come in. If she had touched a child, she had to be struck on the head at once.
156210: After combing your hair, you were not supposed to leave any hairs in the comb. Anyone who did could fall victim to a sorceress, who could make the person whose hairs they were dance!
156218:
No farmer dared to live on a haunted farm any more because all the animals died there. At night the butter churn could be heard turning and the buckets falling over. In the morning all the buckets and pots were found scattered across the farmyard.
One day it was decided to put the buckets and pots twenty metres further from the farm each year until the ghosts were finally driven away. That put an end to the strange happenings.
156233: A woman named X who owned a billy goat visited people who had a small child. After the woman left, the child cried the whole time and shouted: "X is there!" The priest advised the people to lay all the child's clothes on the bed and then went to the witch's house. The priest prayed for the child until drops of sweat rolled down his face.
156249: A farm near the 'Tasche' was haunted. The cows were untied there without anyone being seen. The cutlery on the table began to float. The farm was surrounded by a moat. When the sexton tried to reach the farm, he was thrown into the water. The priest, however, got across unharmed. After the priest had read prayers over the farm until he was sweating heavily, the strange happenings came to an end.
156252: A mother was visited by a peddler woman. The peddler came in with her basket, walked to the cradle where a little child lay and said: "What a lovely child that is!" The mother bought nothing from the peddler. Just after she had left, the child turned blue. The mother hurried with the child to the priest, who said: "That was a fine woman who came to visit you. What would you rather have: that your child dies or that it stays with its mother?" "I would rather it stayed with its mother...", the woman answered. Then the priest said: "Look at that bend in the direction of Koksijde. That is where your child is..." The child was dead.
156253: A girl from Westkerke heard her dead father making noise in the attic in the evenings. The man had been a rabbit dealer, and after his death he came to throw the rabbit skins around the attic. When the man died, people had said that he had cursed himself to death.
156255: A man from Abele always placed his shoes upside down beside the bed to keep from being ridden by the mare.
156283: In Vlamertinge there was a house that was haunted at night. That is why nobody dared to go on living in it. One night three curious fellows went to have a look in the house. But there was nothing strange to be seen.
156293: In Leke there lived a woman who bewitched many children. Such children had to be prayed over by a clergyman.
156323: A German shepherd could cover people in lice or fleas. When the power of the clergy grew, the German shepherds could no longer do such things.
156327: In Watou there lived an old woman who was said to be a witch. A girl who had been given sour gooseberries by that woman was advised not to eat the berries if she did not want to be bewitched.
156331:
If you were touched by a witch, you had to quickly strike higher up to break the witch's power.
Pregnant women were not allowed to let anyone touch them.
156336: The wife of the German Shepherd always tried to get near children in order to bewitch them. Once when the woman was near a child again, she said: "What a lovely child!" The next moment the child began to cry. The child cried for a whole year until it finally died. The friars could no longer help the child.
156362: On his way home a man had killed a cat. The next moment a whole pack of cats appeared, crying: "Fientje is dead, Fientje is dead." When he got home the man saw one of his relatives holding a cat and he cried: "Get rid of that cat!", for he was terrified. When the man told what had happened to him, the cat in the house said: "Is Fientje dead?" Then the cat leapt away. The animal was never seen again.
156378: People used to believe that witches could give people lice. In reality, children often got lice at school.
156379: On the Toveressehoek lived a sorceress from whom everyone ran away. That sorceress always gave marshmallow sweets to the children. Anyone who had eaten the sweets fell ill and had to go on pilgrimage.
156417: Shortly after a farmer's funeral, the noise of a party was heard in the farmhouse at midnight. Glasses and plates were heard clinking. In the morning there was no trace of any of it. After a few days the farmer's wife went to the priest, who advised her to say: "If you are sent by God, speak. If you are sent by the devil, then all of you hurry out of here." When the woman spoke those words the next night, the party noise fell silent. The woman heard the voice of her dead husband whispering in her ear: "Money is hidden here in the house. It lies under the tiles of the cupboard in the corner." The next moment all the revellers had vanished. After the money had been found at the indicated place, nothing strange happened anymore.
156418: Some men were carting away tree bark. When a sorceress from the village passed by, the carts tipped over.
156420: A woman from Elverdinge who lived in Hooglede always went to fetch meat from a farmer's wife in the neighbourhood. She always paid the money to the farmer's wife's daughter, whom she then shook hands with. After a while, however, that daughter fell ill. A doctor was called, but because he could not help, another doctor came from Roeselare. The child grew thinner and thinner and did not recover. At their wits' end they had a woman from Ardooie come to the child. That woman said it was not too late yet and that the mother had to go on pilgrimage for the girl. The daughter had a heart disease, you see. The woman also predicted that the mother would become very ill within nine days but would soon recover. The mother did as she was advised. One day she spat up a large bag (?), which astonished the doctors.
156423: In Deerlijk there once lived an experienced poacher. One night the poacher saw a hare running in the moonlight. The poacher shot at the hare several times, but the animal always jumped away. From eleven at night until three in the morning the poacher tried to get the hare. Although the hare always hopped about in the same spot, the poacher did not manage to shoot the animal. It was a phantom animal.
156452:
A man who was married to a witch could no longer stand the witchcraft and sent his wife away.
A witch sometimes stuck pins into the children she bewitched.
156457: Behind the Beernemse Kassei were seven pits that were haunted. A man who had to go and fetch milk one evening was flung back and forth between the trees near those pits. So when the man got home, he did not have a drop of milk left.
156469: To be freed from the mare, one had to hang mistletoe above one's bed.
156473: On a farm in Poperinge there was a cow about to give birth to a calf. All the farmers from the area came to help, but the calving went exceptionally hard. After a while they saw an old woman from the neighbourhood leaning over the stable door. That woman was suspected of witchcraft. The woman stood there calmly and asked: "Well, isn't it working for you?" The farmer got angry and chased the witch away with the words: "You ugly redhead, now we know why it isn't working!" As soon as the witch was gone, the calf was born.
156480: A man who went somewhere to help with cows that were about to calve saw the plates fall to the floor at midnight. When the door was opened to go and look, the plates were, strangely enough, back in their place. When the outside door was opened, a bundle of wood fell in.
156482: A boy could make mice out of clay, which he set running after blowing on their backsides. One day the parish priest took the boy's magic power away.
156485: People who sold their soul to the devil had as much money as they wanted. Whenever they had given money to someone, they always got it back in a mysterious way. Only when the money had already passed into a third person's hands could it no longer be recovered.
156495: A priest had to come back after his death because he had failed to say a number of Masses. The parish priest asked a man to attend the Mass at midnight. He was not allowed to look at the priest's face. After the Mass the man saw that the priest had no face; it was a skeleton wearing church vestments.
156500: A horse groom from Stavele always saw cats in the trees or a dog in the brook. Strangely enough, these apparitions were not visible to others.
156501: A family had been visited by a man about whom someone said afterwards: "If I were you, I wouldn't want that man in my house!" The next day one of the family's sons was covered in lice. The father burned one louse and then sprinkled some DDT powder on the boy's head. After that the lice were gone.
156504: After mass, seven women remained sitting in the church with their backs to the altar. Once the curate had closed the missal, the women were able to go outside.
156529: A farmer came home late one night. The geese were cackling so loudly that he said to his son: "Tomorrow we will have to harvest all the turnips." After they had done so, it froze for thirteen weeks.
156531: A church with bells is said to have once sunk into a pit in Eernegem. Later there were many frogs at that spot.
156549: When two women were milking the cows, the animals suddenly fell over. The cows grew very thin and developed sores. The animals were under the influence of the evil hand.
156552:
Whoever was ridden by the mare in his sleep felt oppressed and had the impression that someone was sitting on him. The mare usually came to people lying on their backs.
In reality it was a stagnation of the blood.
156553: Some people from Houthulst had a big dog. When a sorceress from the village stood in front of that dog's kennel, the animal did not raise its head. If it had been anyone else, the dog would have torn that person to pieces.
156555: An old woman had touched a little child in a cradle in a house. After that the child got 'the old man' (a wasting illness) and pined away completely. Because the doctors could not help the child, the parents went begging to have a Mass said. The parents had enough money, but for something like that it was best to go begging. In the end the child recovered.
156566: Whoever was ridden by the mare was seized by the throat in bed and could no longer move. The mare was sent by someone who hated a particular person.
156574: A pregnant woman worked in a hotel in Blankenberge. When that woman walked home in the evening, strangely enough she could not make any headway. A passer-by advised the woman to lay the strings of her apron crosswise on the road. After the pregnant woman had done so, she could walk on without effort.
156596: In Lendele lived a man whose mother-in-law was a witch. Whenever the man had sewn his shoe soles on in the evening, the soles were loose again the next morning.
156615: Whoever was ridden by the mare felt oppressed and could not say a word. A man who was sometimes ridden by the mare was advised by someone to place his clogs upside down beside his bed from then on. After that the man was no longer troubled by the mare.
156626: A man from Westkerke had to deliver butter in Ettelgem together with the maid. Although the two knew the way well, they got lost. In the end the man and the maid ended up back where they had started. The two had been bewitched by someone.
156629: In a haunted café footsteps were heard every evening. At midnight the doors burst open through a mysterious force, even though they were locked.
156649: Three boys walking home in the evening met a woman at the station and mocked her. Twenty metres further on, however, the boys met the same woman again. The boys got scared and ran home quickly. Just before they got home they saw the woman once more. After that frightening incident the boys never mocked that woman again.
156652: People who were ridden by the mare were bewitched.
156658: 'The old man' was a children's illness caused by a witch. Witches could make children ill by looking at them when no one else was around.
156680: When the cowherd of a farm in Harelbeke went to Bavikhove, he met a woman who gave him sweets. When he got home the man was ill and was only the size of a newborn baby. In the end the man became so small that he died.
156688: In Moorslede lived a woman who was suspected of being a sorceress. Whenever a child was ill in a house, that sorceress kept walking past that house.
156690: Cats always used to roam the wooded lane of Nieuwenhove. People walking past there at night could not go on because the cats blocked their way.
156740: A man coming back from Ieper saw masses of fat rats at a farm, which went to another farm at night. Those were rats sent by a framasson (freemason, believed to be a sorcerer).
156741: Because of a witch, a farmer could no longer make butter. There was always dung in the butter churn. After a priest had prayed over the milk, butter could be made effortlessly again.
156744: A young man had a girlfriend who could do magic. One day the girl made a mistake when speaking the magic formula and said: "Over everything and through everything" instead of "Over everything and above everything".
156760: A man who was struggling with a plague of rats was talking to his neighbour, who said mockingly: "You have so many rats and I don't have a single one!" The next morning the man sent all his rats to his neighbour's house.
156772: On a haunted farm the stable hand was always forced at midnight to leave his bed and ride one of the horses. In the morning the horse was drenched in sweat. One morning a horseshoe was found lying by the farmer's wife's head. Then they knew that it was she who was working the hand to exhaustion.
156788: Some people going to the field together passed a house full of books where a cat was walking about. One of the people said: "You pretty pussycat." When the people came back from the field later in the day, that person was sitting in a tree calling out: "You pretty pussycat!"
156791: Because some boys were not allowed to go to an inn, one Sunday they went to a Duitse schaper (German shepherd, a travelling shepherd said to have magic powers) who could tap beer from his staff.
156797: A woman whose child cried loudly all the time went to the friars for advice. "You must keep silent," the friars had said. The woman went home and began working. A little later a mother and a daughter came along from house to house. The mother could not enter the woman's house.
156823: A woman who had a small child was visited by a witch, who went to the cradle and said: "What a lovely child that is!" Then the child began to cry without stopping. Since the child was bewitched, the doctor could not help. The next morning the child was dead.
156827: A witch visiting a farmer stirred the milk standing there with a spoon. Then the witch said: "You will never again have problems churning butter."
156834: A man from Marke worked at a haunted manor in Emelgem. In the moonlight in the evening he saw officers on horseback riding into a well. Because the man always used holy water in the morning, the apparitions disappeared.
156837: A farmer's wife could no longer churn butter. Her neighbours said: "That milk is bewitched. You'll see!" The next night an old woman was seen dancing around the butter churn. To put an end to the evil, they had to pray and go on pilgrimage.
156852: A sorceress had turned the legs of newborn piglets back to front. After that the sorceress never came to that bewitched farm again.
156872: A man was in the habit of always leaving a little light burning at night. When he forgot to do so one night, he got up and walked to the attic window. That night the man was ridden by the mare until the moment his wife called his name.
156875: One evening a man from Zedelgem was returning with a friend from the fair in Ruddervoorde. On a back road in Veldegem the two men saw a black cat sitting. The man's friend kicked the cat so that it flew some five metres into the air. Strangely enough, a moment later the cat was sitting again where it had been before. The men grew frightened and believed the cat was a sorceress. When the cat sat on a tree trunk a little further on, there was no way to chase the animal off.
156879: A man was playing cards in a café with a stranger. At around eleven o'clock the man left for home. When, after walking for an hour and a half, he went into another inn, strangely enough the stranger was sitting there playing cards too. He claimed it was already his fourth card game. That wizard could also, for example, make himself invisible. He would then sit in the bellows that stood by the oven.
156891: A woman from Wakken was suspected of being a witch. When a child had been touched by the woman, it got a heart ailment. After pilgrimages had been made for the child to Zwevegem, Wannegem and Sint-Eloois-Vijve, the child recovered.
156894:
German shepherds could do magic.
A farmer who could no longer churn butter was advised by the priest to dismiss his maid. After the maid left, the farmer had no more problems churning.
156910: A farm that had been struck by the evil hand went bankrupt nine years later. After a friar had put something in the ridge of the barn, the evil came to an end.
156914: A friar from whom people had often come to steal wood said one day: "Whoever still dares to do that will stick to the wood". When the thieves came to steal wood again, they did indeed stick to the wood.
156917: If one placed one's shoes on the floor with the heels towards the bed, the mare could not reach the bed.
156933: On a haunted farm people saw a procession walking through the house at night. One day the farmer's child was even thrown from his lap. The people sent for the curate, who banished the evil to the farthest corner of the farmyard. The clergyman said: "It will now come one metre closer every year."
156935: A man coming back from the paint factory was often followed by a meowing cat that got under his feet. The man kicked at the animal, but he always missed. The man was so frightened that his hair stood on end.
156939: A farmer's wife was visited by a woman who came to say that a pig lay dead. Before that, however, nothing had been wrong with the animals. When the farmer's wife was cooking the meat, the woman lifted the lid of the pot. Because of that the meat went bad.
156957: On a farm where all the calves died, the people had to walk three times around the little chapel on three consecutive days and 'throw a height into the emptiness' (?). Moreover, no animals with cloven hooves were allowed to go out by the Zuidpoort. That whole farm was bewitched.
156959: If someone was seriously ill and a barn owl was heard calling "Dead, dead…", the sick person would die within three days. It was said that death candles were then burning.
156963: A family from Poperinge had the custom of giving the maid a loaf of bread every Saturday. One Saturday, however, it was not convenient and they said to the maid: "We'll give you the bread next week." The maid ran off angrily. From then on those people could do nothing with their youngest child. The friars of Ieper found that the child was bewitched and advised the parents to make a novena. After the novena had been made and the maid had been given a few things, the child was cured.
156982: A cooper claimed he could do magic. One day the cooper made a barrel without hoops and rolled it across the ground. The sorcerer owned magic books that were collected by the clergy after his death. Whenever someone crossed the sorcerer, that person was soon covered in lice or fleas.
156994: If you saw a black cat in the evening, you had to keep quiet and certainly not speak to the animal. If you dreamt of the animal, you would fall ill.
157007: In Waarmaarde lived a witch who shook weeds out of her skirt whenever she was angry with the farmers.
157015: Two young women on their way to the fair walked past a German shepherd tending his sheep without greeting the man. A little later both women were covered in lice, so they had to go back. When the shepherd saw the women coming, he said: "Back already? If you wished people good day, this sort of thing wouldn't happen to you!"
157046: A house along the canal in Leffinge was haunted after the mother had died. At night it seemed as if the house was full of devils.
157047: In Snellegem lived a woman who could bewitch children. It seemed as if that woman was compelled to enter houses where children lived. Because such a bewitched child cried day and night, the parents had to take the child to the friars.
157052: A farm in Oostrozebeke was haunted. There was a pen in which no animal could be put, because all the animals died there. When the farmer went to keep watch over a cow that was about to calve, he fell under the cow so that his feet were twisted. There was also always noise in the attic. When people went to look, there was nothing to be seen, but they were almost thrown out of the attic by a strange force. At night ladies and gentlemen always appeared in the bedroom and turned everything upside down. Friars had already been called in, who had prayed until they were sweating, but it had not helped. In the end the farmer moved away with his family. The new occupant of the farm claimed there was nothing wrong, because his animals in the stable were still alive. However, the new occupant's wife fell ill and died shortly afterwards. One evening the well next to the farm was on fire. And once, on a windless day, the man was driven towards the water as if by a gale, so that he had to resist with all his might not to end up in the water.
157057: A man was walking through the woods in the morning when suddenly a strong wind started to blow. A little later a large black dog appeared and walked along with the man. As soon as the man had left the woods, the dog had vanished and the wind died down again.
157066: A woman who slept in a room above the cellar vault heard dogs fighting at a certain moment. She warned her brother, who got out his gun and went to take a look. The brother saw only one dog, lying on its back. He shot at the animal, but could not hit the dog. The next day the neighbour woman said to the man: "You shot at that dog yesterday, didn't you! You'll never be able to shoot it dead!" In the evening the man put a piece of a medal in a bullet and shot at the dog again. This time the animal was killed instantly.
157067: In Kortemark lived a mother whose four children were always falling ill. The mother often took her children to the fathers of Roeselare to have prayers of exorcism read over them. People believed that a witch lived in the parish.
157082: In Gistel lived a woman who could lay the evil hand on children. And so it happened that a pregnant woman gave birth to a child with water on the brain. At the age of twelve that child suddenly died. There was no point in going to the fathers; if a child was born with defects, the fathers could do nothing about it. Clergymen could only read away the evil hand, but they could no longer undo its effects.
157097: Every evening a woman saw a black cat walking around her farm. Because the woman had a lot of misfortune, she sought advice from the priest, who said: If you see the cat again, pour a pan of boiling fat over it. The woman did as she was advised. The next day the woman was visited by a strange woman who had burns on her head. After that the woman had no more misfortune.
157103:
A man claimed he could make someone do whatever he wanted if he could put his pipe in that person's left hand and his glass in their right hand. In the old days it was the custom in the inn to drink from the same glass. So the man managed to saddle a poor fellow with his glass. When the lad went home, he walked all night round a pond where geese and ducks were. The next morning the lad claimed he had seen strange beasts that struck at him. The lad was drenched in sweat.
That sorcerer had done it to him.
157125: A woman had been covered in lice by a witch.
157131: A farmer had twice driven home with a load of wood. Each time the cart overturned by the brook, where an old woman lived. The farmer believed that this sorceress had made the cart tip over.
157149: A farmer's farmhand had said that he would come back after his death. Three days after his death the farmhand was indeed sitting on the gate. When the farmer asked what things were like in the hereafter, the ghost answered: "Everything is strictly accounted for and nothing is forgiven." Then the ghost disappeared.
157170: On the Menenheirweg lived a blind girl. When the girl was still small, she was given a carrot by a woman from the neighbourhood. The child fell ill and some time later went blind. It was said that the child had been bewitched by that woman.
157171: The castle of Moorsele was haunted at midnight. When people walked around the castle rampart, they could hear music. The woman who lived there was rich but had a bad character. After she had invited the secretary and other important people to dinner, all those people died in strange circumstances. When the woman herself was dead, the castle was haunted. There was not much to see, but all kinds of sounds were heard, including the whistling of birds.
157174: The returning dead were vampires who were after the blood of the living.
157189: A man passing the Hellebus one evening saw a horse without a head and without a tail. Even in broad daylight people did not dare to go past the Hellebus.
157190: Whoever had touched a black cat was bewitched.
157195: A man who had moved the boundary post of his field had to haunt at night after his death as punishment.
157204: The mare was a stagnation of the blood.
157215: In Beselare there was a little child who cried day and night, though nothing strange could be seen about it. The mother took the child to the fathers of Kortrijk. From the moment the woman reached the church door with the child, it stopped crying. A woman had seen the mother pass by with the child. That woman never visited the mother again afterwards. She probably had something to do with the evil. The fathers had read prayers over the child and given the mother a blessed object.
157232: On a farm worked a German Schaper who always went to drop off his dirty laundry at midday. At two o'clock on that farm one always heard noises as if straw were being chopped and fodder prepared for the horses. On the farm a pig, a horse or a cow regularly died in a strange way. Sometimes no butter could be churned on the farm. Some of the farmer's daughters were bewitched and even died of their affliction. The fathers of Steenbrugge said to the farmer: "If you want to know who is to blame, we will make her come to your house. You must not say a word then. The next animal that dies, you must tie to the gate with its forelegs crossed and you must lay this little golden cross on its legs." When the witch came by and said: "Ah, you are churning!", nobody said a word. After a dead sheep had been tied to the gate with its legs crossed, there was no more evil on the farm.
157235: On a farm they always had bad luck with the animals. The beasts always got foot-and-mouth disease or some other illness. After a chapel was built by the farm, the bad luck came to an end.
157250: A man coming home from work along the canal always saw doodkeersen (death candles, ghostly lights) among the trees. They were probably dead people who had returned.
157273: A mother whose child had been bewitched by a woman from the village went with the child to the fathers. On the way the cart kept overturning. The fathers said that this would not happen on the way back and that the child would recover. The clergymen were proved right.
157289: In Aartrijke lived a witch. One day that witch had been at a farm. After she left, the farmer found that one of the piglets had disappeared. The witch had taken a piglet without anyone seeing it.
157290: Whoever was ridden by the mare felt that something was pressing on him. A man who always saw something coming towards him from a corner at night had himself blessed by the friars.
157312:
In a wood where a witch lingered, one had to make the sign of the cross and hold the cross of one's rosary.
A farmer who, through that same witch's doing, could no longer churn butter sent for the fathers. After that the farmer could make butter again.
157313: Two farmhands worked on a farm, one of whom was a real idler. One morning the other farmhand dressed up as a ghost in a white sheet and stood on the willow along which the lazy farmhand walked to work. Convinced that it was a returned dead person, the lazy farmhand did not dare pass the willow. When the other farmhand grew tired and wanted to come down, he saw that a real ghost was floating under the willow, crying "Hi, hi, hi, hi!" After the lazy farmhand had prayed for a long time, the ghost disappeared.
157314: A man walking home around midnight saw a white figure coming towards him in the moonlight. It was a woman with a white cap on her head. Without feet, the woman floated over the ground. Strangely enough, the apparition had no shadow.
157320: A farmer on his way with a load of hay met a witch from Les Moères, who said: "You'll have a late lunch!" A little further on, the hay cart overturned into the water.
157322: Around All Saints' Day doodkeersen (death candles, ghostly lights) were seen in the churchyard. They were the little souls from purgatory coming back.
157339: In the past, dangerous diseases such as smallpox and typhus were common. In Langemark lived a woman who always went visiting people who had children. Whenever that woman had touched a child, the child would cry day and night afterwards. Often it even came to the point that the child had to be taken to the fathers to have prayers read over it.
157346: A priest went walking on the Zomerweg, a road notorious for the many robbers who hid there to take money from passers-by with death threats. As the priest walked there, a robber suddenly appeared and said: "Your money or your life!" The clergyman replied: "You may have my money, but first let me take a pinch from my snuffbox". As the priest did so, he quickly began reading from his book. The next moment the robber could no longer move; he seemed nailed to the ground. The next day, after he had eaten and drunk, the priest took his book, went to the robber, who was still standing there, and said: "Will you threaten clergymen again in the future?" After the robber had promised never to do so again, he could move once more.
157347: The mare seized sleeping people by the throat. Sometimes the mare was a man, sometimes a woman.
157366: When the shrimp fishermen went through a creek to Nieuwpoort, they saw lights in the distance. When they came closer, the lights had vanished. They were will-o'-the-wisps. These were the spirits of the dead who returned because they had not kept a promise, or because they had been murdered and wanted to bring the murderer to repentance.
157369: Whoever passed the Bruges cemetery in the evening was jumped on by a sheep.
157370: One night a milk seller had thrown hot water at a cat that was sitting on her bed. When the woman did her milk round the next day, one of her customers had a burned face. That witch had turned herself into a cat. The milk seller had a friar come to read prayers over her house.
157400: A woman from Rozebeke who saw the ghost of her dead husband appear every night was advised by the priest to ask: "If you are sent by Our Lord, speak. If you are sent by the devil, go back where you came from." The ghost did not say a word. Since then the woman has not seen the ghost again.
157423: A man who had been ridden by the mare said afterwards that he had heard the door open and the mare come in. The man had wanted to cry out, but it was impossible.
157427: A witch from Oostende could bring cooked shrimps back to life in someone's hand.
157438: A farmer's wife who had taken her husband to the station early in the morning found a woman from Aartrijke in her house when she returned. The woman said to the farmer's wife: "You have a lovely child!" Because the woman had taken hold of the child's little hand, the child began to cry loudly. That night the farmer's wife went to her parents because she was at her wits' end. The curate came to read prayers over the child. Some time later the farmer's wife cut her own throat and died. She had been bewitched.
157510: On a farm in Oostkamp lived an old woman who covered everyone in fleas. In the end the fathers of Steenbrugge had a little chapel built on that spot.
157532: Two boys coming home at midnight were startled when the crystal chandelier in their bedroom began to move. The whole house shook to its foundations, so that nobody dared to go to sleep. The friars of Steenbrugge advised the people to give alms to the poor. After that the house was no longer haunted.
157534: The Koude Schuur was haunted. No farmer has ever been able to grow rich there.
157536: In a house where there was always a cat, someone one day threw boiling water over the animal. The next day people said that one of the neighbour women had badly burned herself.
157560: A man claimed he could make mice out of clay.
157563: A farmer's wife who had put bread in the oven was visited by an old woman. When the farmer's wife wanted to take the bread out of the oven, it turned out to have disappeared. Yet the visitor had not been near the oven.
157564: At midnight it looked as if everything in the moated castle of Loppem was on fire.
157573: In Brugge a maid saw the latch of her door moving up and down. One day, when the maid was home alone, the latch broke in two. The maid's cousin was a friar. The clergyman had told her to say: "If you are sent by God, speak. If you are sent by the devil, go back where you came from."
157576:
Next to a farmer's sugar beet field was a narrow private path. One day the farmer forbade a woman to use that path. The woman then said: "You won't get a cartload of beets from that field!" The woman's prediction came true.
That woman often walked about at night, dressed in a hooded cloak. Whenever one went to the brook around midnight, one always found that woman there.
157580: A priest could bewitch people to stay fixed to the ground for as long as he wanted.
157587: Some liberals who were against the priest took a dog to church and made the animal bark. After mass the liberals could not get outside. They stood there as if nailed to the ground.
157592: Every Saturday a woman came into a bakery in Ieper. Each time that woman had left the shop, the baker's wife's child began to cry. When the strange woman was sent out of the shop one day, she slammed the doors and stormed off angrily.
157602: Children who had been healthy at birth got 'de oude man' (the old man, a wasting illness) through the doing of a witch. The curates went everywhere collecting the witches' books. Since the Gospel of Saint John has existed, there has been much less witchcraft.
157612: When an old woman had stroked a newborn baby's head, the child was bewitched and turned completely black. The child then cried all the time.
157625:
A pregnant woman from Gistel was often visited by an old neighbour. It was said of that neighbour that she could lay the evil hand on young or unborn children. Some time later the woman gave birth to a baby with water on the brain. The mother went to the dean for advice, hoping that her child would be cured. The dean said to the mother: "If you want to keep that woman out of your house, you must put paasnagels (blessed Easter nails) under the threshold." When the mother had done so, the neighbour indeed could no longer come in. She did come up to the door, but said: "It's not convenient to come in now. I'll come back another time."
That mother's child was never able to walk properly and died at the age of eight.
157634:
A man could not go to church for six months, although he was not ill. The man went to the fathers as many as six or seven times.
On Good Friday the man was determined to go to mass. He wrapped a woollen cloth around his neck and set off, so that the sweat dripped from his face. The man said: "Come what may, I'm going to Boeschepe to kiss Our Lord!" The fathers advised the man to leave all evil alone. The man had prayers read over him and was blessed by one of the fathers. "You will go home content!" said the father. When the man got home, he felt fine. The witch could no longer get into his house. That witch owned evil books which had been brought from India by the English.
Anyone who spoke about witches had to keep his thumb in his fist, or else the witches would hear what was said about them.
157644: On the eve of their father's funeral, the children slept in the attic above the café. At midnight the children heard chains rattling.
157653: A beggar woman visited a family who had a baby in the cradle. "What a lovely child!" said the beggar woman, and she picked the child up and stroked it. After the beggar woman's visit the baby cried day and night. The child also grew very thin and eventually died.
157665: Near 't Lappersfort and the Viervermeulehoek there were many haunted woods.
157671: A woman who was often ridden by the mare heard a tapping in the attic, as if someone were walking around in hobnailed shoes. She heard the mare coming by way of the stairs and the door. When the mare seized her, the woman wanted to cry out, but could not. Nor did she manage to knock on the wall. In the end the woman put a branch in her bed that had also been ridden by the mare. She also had to eat at regular times. After that she was no longer ridden by the mare.
157702: The toveresseknok (witches' knoll) was always haunted. At night white goats always roamed there, and people were very afraid of them.
157710: A farmer passed a tree-lined lane where a black cat was sitting. A little later the farmer saw that he was being followed by a whole pack of cats. The closer the farmer came to home, the bigger the cats grew. When the farmer got home, the cats turned into an elephant and then disappeared.
157732: A mother with a three-month-old baby was visited by a woman who asked to see the child. The woman took hold of the little boy and removed the paasnagel (blessed Easter nail) that lay on the child's chest. Then she took something from her neck and laid it on the child. Shortly afterwards the child died after much suffering. That woman was a witch who had already caused many children to suffocate.
157747: Every evening a cat appeared at the water drain in a woman's house. Because the cat annoyed her, one day the woman poured melted fat over the animal. The next day one of the neighbour women had a burned face.
157749: A man worked on a farm that was haunted. At night the cows were untied and the horses roamed about. One night someone jumped on one of the horses and rode it to the blacksmith to have it shod. The next morning it was found that the farmer's wife had horseshoes on her hands and feet.
157754: A mother with a child had been visited by a woman. Since then the mother could no longer control her child. The priest prayed for the child. He advised the mother not to show her child to just anyone in future.
157763: On the night of All Saints, a large four-master could be seen sailing off the beach of Koksijde. Normally that ship needed fifteen feet of water.
157770: A man who had heard a lot of noise at night found in the morning that the cows were hanging in the stable with their legs in the air. The friar advised the man to say: "If you are sent by God, stay. If you are sent by the devil, go away." When the man had said this, he heard a voice saying: "You must give so much to the poor." The dead person had weighed short and charged too much. After the man had fulfilled the ghost's wish, it stayed quiet on the farm.
157773: In Adinkerke lived a woman who lay reading under a tree all day. One day the woman asked her neighbour: "Wouldn't you like me to look after your little child a bit, since you have so little time?" The neighbour refused. Then the woman said: "I'll give your rabbits something to eat." The next day all the rabbits lay dead in their hutch. The woman's child also eventually fell ill and died. It had been given a marshmallow by the witch.
157782: The eternal hunter was in the woods and called: "Tsjagouw, tsjagouw!"
157788: At the klokkenputten (bell pits) in Eernegem, bells could be heard ringing on Christmas night. So bells must have sunk into those pits.
157816: A man going to church in Loppem had been given a pat on the shoulder by a woman. Because of this the man wasted away completely.
157817: A man's sister-in-law had lost all her hair after being bewitched by a witch. "Leave that woman alone, or I'll knock you against the wall," the man had said to the witch one day. When the man got up a few days later, he found that half his hair had turned grey. So the man had his head shaved bald. When the hair began to grow again, it was all black once more.
157819: A woman who ran a café sent customers she had something against outside. Those people would then get lost, so that they did not get home until the next morning.
157824: A sorcerer could send rats from one farm to another. The rats only went to a farm where they would be better off than at the previous one.
157832: In Westkapelle a witch peddled zwijneblommen (pig flowers, likely dandelions). That witch was always out to take hold of children's little hands. Afterwards something always happened to those children.
157877: A frog had come into a house and nobody could kill it. In the end the woman grabbed the animal and threw it into the stove. The next day the neighbour woman lay in bed with burns. When the woman asked what had happened, the neighbour answered: My stove wasn't working and suddenly a flame shot out. But the woman knew better.
157880: A boy who had been struck by the evil hand cried for nine days in a row. The father who had come to read prayers over the boy had said: "For nine days you must put bread in the boy's porridge. After that he will either recover or die." The boy recovered.
157900: A farmer found it strange that everyone always knew what had happened on his farm, even though nobody had visited. The farmer noticed that every evening a cat came and sat by the hearth. One evening someone threw boiling water over the cat, which ran off screeching. The next day a neighbour woman had severe burns. She was a witch who came every evening to eavesdrop on what was said on the farm.
157907: Some shepherds sitting on a dike tapped beer there as if they were drawing it straight from a well-stocked cellar.
157913: A mother was visited by a woman peddler, who said: "Oh, do you have a little baby? Let me see the baby!" The peddler lifted the blankets for a moment and then covered the baby again. After the peddler left, the child began to cry incessantly. The mother was advised to go to the priests of Steenbrugge. While the mother was sitting with the priests, the peddler came in there too. The peddler kept moving closer and closer to the fire the priests had made. She asked if she could hold the child. The peddler took a mass of pins out of the child's wrappings and threw them into the fire. After that the child was cured. If the peddler had not been given the child, she would have had to jump into the fire.
157922: On a farm there was a mare that was due to foal. Because there were problems with the animal, the farmer told his farmhand to hit the first person he met. The farmhand met the maid, but he did not hit her. "You didn't do what I told you!" the farmer said to the farmhand afterwards. The second time, too, the farmhand did not dare hit the maid. The third time the vet said: "Come, let's get that foal born." The vet made the maid hover above the mare the whole time. This time the foal was born without any trouble.
157932: Some women could bewitch children by touching them. Such bewitched children were taken to the fathers to have prayers read over them. The clergymen often gave the parents of those children paasnagels (blessed Easter nails) to put under the threshold. Then the witches could no longer come in.
157941: On a farm, through the doing of a witch, a thousand rats sat on the roof every morning and evening. At a certain moment the rats had all disappeared.
157948: After a miserly farmer had died, a hellish noise was heard on the farm every night. The priest went to the farm every day, which reduced the haunting somewhat. Nobody dared to work on that farm anymore. The farmer came back to point out his money, which he had hidden somewhere. Some people claim they had seen P. the singer digging in the farmer's field at night. Shortly afterwards the singer had a new barrel organ, a new dog cart and a fine dog.
157967: A girl who slept in her sister's room was ridden by the mare every night for four years. As soon as the sister came to stand by the bed and called her name, the girl was freed from the mare. Her confessor advised the girl to place her clogs upside down and to get into bed the wrong way round. When the girl had done so, she was no longer troubled by the mare.
157970: A woman from Veldegem could not sleep at night because she always saw the ghost of a dead person standing by the pincushion. The priest advised the woman to say: "If you are sent by God, say what you come for. If you are sent by the devil, go back where you came from." The priest also predicted that the dead person would come back to thank the woman for fulfilling the wish. He added: "You must not give the dead person your hand; you must give a cloth." The ghost came back and asked the woman to have a Mass said with the money that lay hidden in a certain place. Afterwards the ghost came back to thank the woman. The ghost burned a hand into the cloth. The priest burned that cloth.
158007: One evening a farmer went outside because he had heard chains rattling. But when the farmer came out, he was pushed over. The next morning the farmer found all the chains with which he had tied up his cows in the manure pit of the cowshed. Because the ghost came back every evening, nobody dared to go outside any more.
158018: On a farm that was haunted at night, the butter had already been churned by morning.
158060: A horse groom coming back from 't Veugeltje at night went home on foot. Suddenly the groom heard someone in clogs walking behind him. Yet there was nobody to be seen. A little later the groom saw a large black calf, which the next moment had vanished without a trace. Because the groom had not walked on the grass, he had remained unharmed.
158085: A woman knew everything her daughter-in-law had said and eaten during the day, although she had not been there herself.
158102: Near the Stereik in Anzegem there used to be a lot of haunting. A man coming home through the woods suddenly heard shouting and raging. When he looked round, he saw a beautiful white coach with three shouting monsters in it. Although hoofbeats could be heard, the horses could not be seen. The man saw the coach coming at him and quickly ran away. A little further on he was run over by the coach. At that moment the white figures laughed.
158105: A woman was always visited by a witch who came to fetch milk. Because the woman found this very annoying, she went to the fathers of Steenbrugge for advice. The fathers came and read prayers over the farm until they were drenched in sweat, and then said: "Now she won't come in here any more!" When the witch came to visit the next day, she said: "Oh, it stinks in here!" and walked away. Everywhere the witch had walked, the clover was scorched.
158117: A man coming back from a café in Zerkegem saw a little goat tied to a post by a small chapel at a crossroads. The goat butted the post so wildly that sparks could be seen on the chain. "You're no goat," said the man, at which the animal vanished. Further on the man was thrown into a hedge, losing his cap. The man cursed and went on. When the man came to another hedge, he flew over it.
158118: A man who worked for a farmer walked home every evening along a road lined with high stacks of wood. One day the man heard a voice at that spot say: "Mind you don't walk into my nails!" The man assumed it was a joke and began to laugh. Then the man was beaten by the wooden stakes.
158127: At the station in Ingelmunster stood a man who had been splashed by the engine drivers. When the drivers wanted to set their train in motion, they could not. The sorcerer on the platform then said: "If you stop here again, you must not splash me any more! If you hadn't done that, you could leave now! If I want, I can keep you standing here until tomorrow". After that the sorcerer did let the trains leave.
158128: On a farm the pigs had broken out on a Sunday evening. The doors of the pigsty were shut and the animals were sitting on the dung heap. When the pigs had been put back in their sty, a little later they were outside again.
158132: Whoever was ridden by the mare was awake and fully aware of what was happening, but could do nothing to protect himself.
158138: In Komen lived a woman who was suspected of being a witch. When a man and a woman were walking to church on a Sunday, the suspected woman was walking ahead of them. The man said to his wife: "We'll soon see whether it's true," and he placed his feet crossed in the woman's footprints. At that moment the suspect turned around and said: "You've tricked me nastily now, but you'll be sorry for it!" When the man went to bed that evening, he was covered in lice. His wife had no lice.
158139: One evening a farmhand was driving home with two horses. At a certain moment a nun came and sat on the horse cart. The farmhand was terrified and did not dare say a word. When he got home, he saw that the nun had vanished.
158146: A farmer struck at a mole that was running around his yard. The next day a wizard from the neighbourhood had a bruise.
158150: At Misere in Sint-Joris-ten-Distel, the Templars came to haunt. They said: "The day is yours, the night is ours."
158155: Whoever was ridden by the mare felt as if someone jumped onto his bed and then squeezed his throat shut. Whoever wanted to protect himself against the mare had to place his clogs upside down under the bed.
158164: A forester woke up at night because he had heard shots. When the man got up, he saw a kind of coffin with a white sheet in the woods. Although the forester had shot at the coffin, he saw it again a little further on. The man saw these ghostly scenes because he was not wearing his scapular.
158180: A woman who was baking cakes saw a cat come in through the water drain. Since the mewing cat had come in, the woman could no longer bake cakes. In the end the woman struck the animal's neck with a red-hot poker. The next day a woman with burns on her neck was walking around the village.
158183: A man who went to steal cherries in the priest's garden during mass stuck in the tree until mass was over.
158187: Three men going on pilgrimage to Varsenare passed along the Diksmuidsesteenweg between Aartrijke and Brugge. There the men suddenly heard a rustling in the woods. Two men immediately ran away in fear. The other man went to look and saw two little white animals.
158192: In Merkem three women had a bad name. After all, many children in the village were bewitched and some farmers could not churn butter. Since the Gospel of Saint John has been read at the end of mass, there has been much less witchcraft.
158206:
Two young girls walked past an old woman, laughing. The old woman believed the girls were mocking her and covered them in lice.
A woman who had been cursed by some children during the division of an inheritance was also suddenly covered in lice.
158219: At the Molenhoek in Deerlijk a doodkeers (death candle, ghostly light) was seen hanging in the air every evening. When people came closer, the light always vanished. One day a man went to pray at that spot together with the priest. After the prayers, the man and the priest began to dig. A lot of money was found there. The priest gave half to the man, who had three children, and with the other half he wanted to do good works.
158227: A man saw a good hundred cats by a brook in Knesselare. The man was so frightened that he called for help.
158246: In a meadow there was always a hare that nobody could shoot. When someone shot at the animal with a blessed bullet, a woman ran away bleeding.
158248: On a haunted farm all the household goods were found in disorder in the morning.
158263: On a farm in Sint-Baafs-Vijve there were so many rats that the farmer decided to call in the help of a wizard. The wizard read spells over the farm and then lay down with the farmer in the orchard, after saying: "We'll lie side by side on our stomachs in the grass. Whatever you hear, you must on no account look up." Because the farmer had heard nothing for quite a while, he could not restrain his curiosity and looked up. In the distance he saw countless rats running away from the farm in a long line. Because the farmer looked, the rats immediately turned round and ran back to the farm. The last rat in the line was almost as big as a cat and held its tail high in the air.
158278: People who came back after their death were actually old tovermetjes (witches). After all, it was always women who returned and never men, because men could not do witchcraft. These tovermetjes always grew very old, some hundred or hundred and twenty years.
158285: Between 1800 and 1820 a farm in Westkapelle was haunted. When the farmer and his wife came back from early mass, they saw the ghosts. They threw linseed into a woodpile so that the ghosts would leave, but it did not help. Then the couple mixed buttermilk with fresh milk. Because the ghosts could not separate the two kinds of milk, they had to leave.
158328: A pregnant woman who was bewitched gave birth to a child with a chicken's head. The woman strangled the child after the birth.
158355: A man who often went hunting saw a billy goat standing at a crossroads. The man shot at the goat and fell on his back. The man immediately went to confession. The priest advised him to put a five-stuiver coin under his knee. When the man had done that, he did manage to hit the billy goat.
158356: In Nieuwpoort there lived a freemason who was extremely rich. The maids and farmhands who worked there were curious about their employer's practices. When they looked through the keyhole, they saw the freemason playing a bugle while little men danced around and climbed up the legs. When the freemason had died, it was noticed at the funeral that the coffin was very heavy. It was filled with cobblestones, since the devil had come to take away the freemason's body.
158379: During mass two men sat chatting the whole time. After mass the priest made sure those two men could not leave the church.
158385: Roesschaert was a tormenting spirit that the fishermen greatly feared. When people had bad luck, they believed Roesschaert had caused it. Roesschaert sometimes appeared in the shape of a black lady or a black cat. When the fishermen met a black cat or a black-haired woman on their way to the boat, they turned back. The fishermen would then wait until the next high tide to set out.
158387: Some dead people returned because they had not kept a promise. If a dead person wanted to shake your hand, you had to offer the corner of your handkerchief.
158388: A woman claimed that her husband had died through the evil hand of a witch.
158402:
On a farm where the cows often walked through the banks and among the tobacco plants, no butter could be churned. Because people believed the misfortune was the work of a witch, they put dung in the butter churn. After the churn had then been thoroughly cleaned, the people could make butter again.
One day the farmer's wife had the witch knit a pair of socks. Although there were no knitting machines yet in those days, the witch was already at the farmer's wife's door with the socks the next day.
158403: A castle in Loppem was haunted. At midnight a hearse came out of the castle and went past the village square to the church.
158433: On a farm where a woman always came to fetch buttermilk, one day no more butter could be churned. When the woman had come by two or three times in vain, she said: "If you have no butter now, you will never get any again." The people went to the fathers for advice, who read prayers over the farm and then said: "You must keep that woman away." The woman never came by again and the people could make butter again.
158444: A man cycling from Houtave to Zuienkerke was startled when, at the Zielebrug, his cap was knocked off his head by a figure that vanished a moment later.
158458: A mother who had just given birth to her first child was often visited by a woman who peddled blankets, thread and ribbon. One day the peddler came in to ask how the child was. She lifted the child's blankets and said: "The baby is doing well." Some time later the priest came to visit. The clergyman gave the child a little cross and said: "Now the baby will grow." A week later the peddler came by again. She opened the door and asked three times: "Need anything?" But the people gave no answer. After that the peddler never came by again.
158462: A few days before a cow or a sow was due to give birth, the farmer was visited by a witch. One evening the farmer decided to keep watch with some men, so that the witch could not get in. While the men were playing cards, the witch suddenly came in saying: "Don't you know? The calf has already been born!" The witch was right. A few days later the calf died. When the witch lay on her deathbed, she suffered terrible pains and could not die. The father would only give the witch the Last Sacraments after she had burned her books of witchcraft. After that the witch did die.
158463: The number '365' was written on a cellar door. The door had been repainted a hundred times, but the number always reappeared. The dean decided that it was probably a promise that had never been kept. The occupants of the house then had 365 Masses said.
158467: A man who worked on a farm in Ooigem often saw a woman sitting on the roof of the barn or on the door of the horse stable. As soon as someone came outside, the woman screamed and vanished. It was said that she was one of the returning dead.
158472: To protect oneself against the mare, one must not put one's slippers side by side.
158489: On a farm the animals in the stable always lay with their legs in the air. A witch had hidden something somewhere there.
158501: A fisherman's wife whose husband was at sea crawled into bed alone one evening and felt a mouse at her toes. The woman got up and saw the mouse running across the floor. When she lay back down in bed a little later, she felt the mouse at her feet again. The woman got up once more. When she crawled into bed for the third time, she felt the mouse running over her face. The next day the woman went to the little chapel. She told no one what her problem was, because otherwise misfortune would come of it, so people believed. Since then the woman's health has steadily worsened. Because of this the woman believed she was bewitched.
158514: A farmhand who slept in the horse stable told the farmer that someone always came at night to pull off his blankets. The farmer told the curate, who laughed but came by in the end anyway. Later the farmhand found a copper kettle full of silver under the stones of the horse stable.
158519: At a little chapel in Bulskamp something strange could always be seen. One time a woman was seen there, another time a cat or a rabbit. When a man picked up the cat one day, he could hardly get it home because the animal grew heavier and heavier. Had the man looked closely, he would even have seen that the animal had human ears.
158534:
In the past there were always floods in Avelgem in winter. When a hunter was out in his boat, he met an old woman who asked if she could have a hare. The hunter refused and said: "You may think you can harm me, but I'm not afraid of you. If you can work magic, go ahead!" But the woman said she wasn't going to do that.
Some time later the man was talking to that woman again. Afterwards he had a hunchback, which made him unhappy for the rest of his life.
158547: A woman who was to be churched saw four black cats lying by the front of the house. The cats looked at the woman and followed her. Some time later the woman's baby fell ill. Near her house, however, lived a sorceress. She had turned herself into a cat to bewitch the baby while the mother was at church.
158556: People who were ridden by the mare had to go through hedges and thickets to Cologne. In the morning those people were back home. Because such people, like everyone else, also had to work during the day, they became as thin as rakes. To prevent being ridden by the mare, one had to place one's shoes heels first under the bed.
158564: When a child died somewhere, people often believed that a witch had caused it.
158568: A woman who was ridden by the mare cried out in a hoarse voice in her sleep. When someone lay in bed with her, the woman was less troubled by the mare. Some claimed that the mare was in reality a stagnation of the blood.
158585: Many accidents happened on a road in Veldegem. People believed that a woman from the village was responsible for those accidents.
158617: In the past people kept their money at home. When they had died, they often had to return to point out the place where they had hidden their money.
158632:
One evening in October a man walked to a party for pigeon fanciers. On the way the man met a neighbour who was said to be a witch. The woman asked the man where he was going, and he answered: "To a pigeon fanciers' party." Then the woman patted the man on the shoulder and said: "Then it will be late before you are home again!"
Around midnight the man went home with four friends. Because the man first had to go and relieve himself, his friends were already well ahead. The man could no longer see his friends in the dark and strayed from the road. The man was drenched in sweat from fear. About two hours later the man saw the carriage of the doctor-mayor coming along. At that moment the man could find his bearings again and went home. When the man reached his house, he could not find the keyhole and started shouting for his father to come and open the door. The man's father believed his son had been bewitched by a witch. The man crawled into bed but could not sleep.
The next day the man was visited by the curate, who always came to eat soup with them. The clergyman admitted that people had often complained about that woman before, and he advised the man from then on to strike higher if the witch touched him again. Through the doing of that same witch, the household had earlier suffered a plague of rats. The rats could be heard squealing and felt crawling over the blankets, but nothing could be seen. The friars of Dendermonde came to drive those rats away.
The curate gave the man an Easter nail to put under the front door. When the witch wanted to come for meat the following Sunday, she could not get in. She died during the war and the curate took away her books of witchcraft.
158636:
Before the First World War, a man went to a café one evening with his brother. A fat woman always sat by the stove, and she would call out: "They're there, they're there!" Then a noise was heard on the roof, and people saw that a corner of the roof had vanished. The roof tiles stood neatly in a row beside the house. Then the woman began to laugh.
When the café owner grew tired of this game, he stood by the door in the evening with his double-barrelled gun. Whenever the woman had called "They're there", sometimes the door disappeared, other times the bricks of the henhouse. The café owner never got the chance to shoot, however. One day the café owner had seen a large and a small figure jump over his house.
In the end the café owner sought advice from the friars of Ieper. The man had to say a prayer every day for nine days. On the ninth day the woman would die. What the friars predicted came true. On the ninth day the woman was dead and the house was full of crosses.
158657: A farmer coming back from a café saw a sorceress on his way home. "You'll never find the gate to your yard," said the sorceress. And indeed the farmer could not get home.
158669: In Aartrijke there was a farm that had the finest cabbages even in the worst years. No one could steal a cabbage there, because at night the cabbages strangely turned into little heaps of earth.
158679: On a farm in Knesselare noises were heard at night as if someone were baking and churning.
158684: Some people heard knocking in the stove. It later turned out that at that moment their son had already been drowned for eight days.
158701: A man who went fishing at night had his biggest catch around midnight. One night a woman passed by and said to him: "Go home. The days are for you, the nights are for us!" That night the man did not catch a single fish more.
158715: A man from Wenduine lying in his bed was pulled up by his hair by the mare.
158716: A gravedigger who had dug a grave in the churchyard of Ingooigem saw, to his great fright, the dug-up earth crawling along. Terrified and drenched in sweat, the gravedigger ran home. He was convinced that the spirit of a dead person had made the earth move. The man fell ill. Because the gravedigger's brother was afraid of nothing, he decided to go and take a look in the churchyard himself. When he too saw the earth moving, he said: "If you are sent by God, speak. If you are sent by the devil, I will resist you!" The man struck the earth and saw a large black beast come out. Although the man had struck hard, the animal was unharmed. Frightened, the man ran home.
158791: A man driving home in his horse cart had dozed off. Suddenly the man woke with a start because the horses had become restless. In front of the horses stood a big white dog. Strangely enough, that big dog vanished a little later into a small ditch. After that the horses calmed down again and the man could go on.
158801: In the castle of Beveren lived two lords who behaved like tyrants. The castle sank into the ground between two cafés. After their death the lords roamed about in the shape of two black dogs chained together. When a passer-by came, the chains opened so that the person could pass. The dogs did no one any harm. Where the castle sank there is now a marsh. When those lords came out of the wood one moonlit night, a loud thunderclap suddenly rang out. One of the strong old oaks was struck by lightning.
158813: Three witches lived in Houtkerke. When the children cried in the cradle, a cushion with pins was often found in their mattress. When a witch came near a child, she usually said: "Oh, what a lovely baby, let me see it!"
158816: A man who was himself ridden by the mare went to fetch the farmer because he suspected that the horse in the stable had also fallen victim to the mare. "That horse isn't about to foal, is it?" the man asked. After three buckets of water had been poured over the horse, the most beautiful woman in the world was seen sitting there. It was an Englishwoman, who said: "Please let me go. I will never come back. I was sent here." The farmer replied: "You must not come back, or else we will take you prisoner."
158825: Some people who were binding the harvest kept seeing a black cat jumping from one sheaf to another. However they tried, they could not chase the animal away.
158834: On a farm where there was not much in the barn, people were plagued by rats. The barn was completely full of tame rats. When the cat went towards one of the rats, the rat sat calmly. Strangely enough, the cat turned around and came back. In the evening by moonlight the rats were always playing. The farmer and his farmhand threw pieces of pottery at the rats, but the animals would not be chased off. After it had rained, the rats could be seen sitting with their heads above the roof tiles. As soon as anyone went to look in the barn, however, there was nothing to be seen. The rats had first been at another farm a kilometre further on. Between that farm and the farm where they now were stood another farm, which strangely enough had been spared the plague. One day, when the men had finished threshing, they attacked the rats with a spade, a dung fork, a stick and pea sticks until they had a whole horse basket full. Then the men saw rats sitting behind them again. Someone must have sent those rats to the farm.
158835: In church some people had been talking during the sermon. After mass the priest made sure those people could not get up from their chairs.
158846: In Anzegem an old woman went peddling with a basket full of laces, shoe polish, needles and pins. One day the old woman stood by the cradle of a child whose mother was briefly at the neighbours'. One of the other children quickly went to warn his mother. The mother was convinced that the peddler had bewitched her child. Ten or fourteen days later the baby did indeed die. The father was so angry that he decided to kill the witch. He went to lie in wait for her at her house in the evening, but she did not come home. The next morning people saw that the peddler was at home. So she must have made herself invisible to get home. The witch must certainly have known that she had done wrong!
158881:
Sometimes people heard someone coming upstairs during their sleep. Then they felt as if they were being seized by the throat. People who were ridden by the mare had to be woken by slapping them in the face.
In reality the mare was a stagnation of the blood.
158885: Some men who were going home saw a whole pack of cats walking ahead of them. The men could not get home.
158892: On fine, clear summer nights the ghost of the dead marquis often returned. He would be in the Boekedreef, having great fun with three others.
158925: In the old days people said that the churchyard was haunted and that a woman in a white cloak walked about there.
158931: Nobody could keep living in a house in Zillebeke because all the animals there died. This was caused by a woman who had it in for those people.
158938: In Papinglo bells had sunk into a pit. One day a stone on a rope some 200 metres long was lowered into the bell pit. Even with that stone the bottom could not be reached. That is why people believed the bell pit had no bottom.
158952: A man had a small farm with four cows. Every time a cow was about to calve, a sorceress came to visit. One day the farmer's wife sought advice from the parish priest, who gave her an Easter nail to put under the threshold. When another calf was due, the sorceress stood at the door. "Do come in," the farmer's wife said to the sorceress. But the sorceress replied: "No, I don't have time." Of course she could not come in, because there was an Easter nail under the threshold.
158957: When two men were coming home from work, they saw a little sheep standing on either side of a small bridge. A priest had once drowned at that spot.
158963: If a woman struck you on the hand, you had to strike her on the shoulder to break her power.
158971: A man who had been bewitched by a woman lost all his hair in a single night.
158988: A sorcerer who worked as a cooper could make a barrel without using hoops. When the sorcerer was angry with someone, he covered that person in lice.
159009: A man who wanted to go gathering wood on a Sunday was cursed, so that he had to carry his bundle of wood forever. That was the man in the moon.
159029: Between Steenkerke and Eggewaartskapelle lived an old woman who bewitched passers-by.
159042: Whoever was ridden by the kokkemare (the mare) felt as if a ghost were sitting on him, squeezing his throat shut. In reality that person was simply having a bad dream.
159043: A woman saw her dead neighbours appear at night with a collar around her neck.
159067: Three boys were mocking the priest during mass. The clergyman then said to the boys: "You must stay sitting on your chairs and the others may leave". After mass the naughty boys could not get up from their chairs until the priest had given them permission.
159085: In Eernegem lived a man who was accompanied every evening by a black cat. At a certain point the man fell ill. Strangely, everyone always knew what had happened in the man's house, though nobody had seen it. When the man had died, the cat still hung around the house. One day someone struck the cat on its paw. The next day a woman's arm with a wedding ring on the finger was found lying in that spot. After reading the engraving in the ring, people knew who the witch was.
159086: A boy who lived on the border of Kortrijk and Heule was walking with his father along a narrow lane one evening. When the boy saw something shining, he asked: "Father, what is that?" The man answered: "That is a glow-worm." The boy, however, thought it was a dead person who had returned, as he had heard from many people.
159089:
The mare was a stagnation of the blood during a dream. People who were ridden by the mare had to be woken up. Whoever had fallen victim to the mare could hardly do anything the next day.
Plants that had been ridden by the mare had a flattened stem.
159104: A woman whose child cried all night went to the friars of Steenbrugge. One of the friars established that the child had been touched by the evil hand and advised the mother not to let the first woman she met on the way home near the child. That is how the mother found out who the witch was.
159107: A farmhand had poured boiling water over a cat. A while later the farmhand found that the farmer's wife was burned all over.
159111: A bricklayer who could work magic kept a cage of rats at home. The sorcerer could order the rats to bite or make sure that they just did not bite. When the sorcerer was told at the town hall that he could do nothing, he took a little stick of wood, hung it on the wall and hung the kettle from it.
159124: A man who went to steal wood one night had to stand still until morning with the sack of wood on his back. The priest had bewitched the man to stay fixed to the ground.
159125: The dead sometimes returned because they had neglected a promise.
159140: A twelve-year-old boy who was ridden by the mare went completely stiff and could no longer breathe. His mother advised the boy to pray an Our Father every evening before going to sleep.
159164: A witch from Oostende could make people get up at night and dance in the street or on the quay. After her books of magic had been burned, the woman lost her powers.
159167: Scarphout was a village where Blankenberge now stands. The village sank. In fine weather with a little wind, the small bell of the church of Scarphout can still be heard ringing. For that little bell sticks out half a metre above the water.
159172: A woman claimed that the mare was a white horse that pressed on its victim's heart at night. Whoever wanted to protect himself against the mare had to take a bread knife to bed and lay it on his heart 'to cut off the evil'.
