159192: Poachers sometimes saw phantom hares running at night, which could not be caught in any way.
159196: In the evening a light was often seen around the churchyard. People said these were the souls of the dead coming back.
159210: A twenty-year-old man had to take a sack of flour to a woman's house. People said that this woman was a sorceress. When the man came into the house with the sack, the woman put her hand on his side and said: "Just put it there." The man barely made it home because he had such terrible pain in his side.
159215: A man who was still working in his field in the evening suddenly saw a calf with big eyes standing in front of him. The man ran home in fear. When he got up that night to smoke a pipe, he saw the same calf again. It was a haunting.
159218: Some men returning from Wevelgem on a Saturday evening were chased by a black cat in Ooigem. One of the men took a stick and struck at the animal, although the others had said that anything roaming about at night should be left alone. The man's stick went right through the animal and a loud scream rang out. When the group split up a little further on, two cats suddenly appeared. After the men had jumped over a ditch, the cats had vanished.
159230: A young man of about twenty-five was going home at around one o'clock at night. The man did not believe in ghosts. Suddenly, however, he heard a noise above his head as if dogs were fighting. The man then ran home as fast as he could.
159238:
A man set out with a horse-drawn cart full of wood. When the man saw a sorceress lying in the middle of the road, he lashed at the woman with a whip. Strangely enough, however, the woman had vanished without a trace.
A cowherd who was moving house drove past a sorceress's house. At that very moment the ropes broke, so that everything fell to the ground. Since nobody had any cords at hand, the sorceress came out and said: "Wait, I'll fix it." When the sorceress produced a very thin little cord, people laughed. But the sorceress said: "Don't laugh. It won't break." And indeed the cord did not break.
159239: A farmer's son fell ill after he had stood talking one evening with a woman who carried an umbrella. The woman had stuck the umbrella into the ground, almost against the farmer's son's shoes. When the friars of Ieper came to say prayers over the boy, they said: "The first woman who comes to visit tomorrow morning, you must send away." The next morning people did as the friars had advised. Nevertheless, the boy was not cured.
159254: A man who worked in the brick kilns in France during the war saw a good twenty cats jump out of a rye field one evening. The man had his gun in his hand, but he was too afraid to shoot.
159280: A widow heard knocking on the window at night. It was the ghost of her late husband, who should have told her something during his life but had not yet done so.
159304: A man out walking with his wife came across a black cat near a silo, making crazy leaps. "That is witchcraft," said the woman. Every time the man went towards the cat, the animal leapt away.
159311: Strange things happened on a farm in Torhout. The cows gave no milk there, and at night all kinds of noises were heard, as if someone were threshing and driving around in a coach. It was said that the pigs had once dug up a pot of old coins there. The farmer caused the haunting himself so that he could move to a farm he had bought.
159314: In Otegem there lived a man who had sold his soul to the devil. When the devils came to fetch the man's soul, the man poured a sack of linseed into the woodpile, so that the devils had too much work to take the man with them.
159325: There was a ghost at the Bedhoek in Kortemark. A little light was burning. When people went to look, they saw the ghost backing away with a horse's head. Everyone ran away in fear.
159334: In the area of Oost-Vlaanderen there lived a farmer who very much wanted a new barn. The farmer sold his soul to the devil, who had to have the barn finished before the first cockcrow. When the cock began to crow, however, the devils had not yet finished the work; there was still a hole of about three hundred bricks in the wall. No one ever managed to brick up that hole, because the bricks always fell out. That barn was called the 'Duivelsschuur' (Devil's Barn).
159337: In Sint-Kruis lived a woman who was tormented by a witch every night between twelve and one o'clock. The woman was dragged across the floor by her hair by an invisible person.
159344: A sergeant of the Belgian customs saw a dead witch standing by a little green gate every morning. All the animals on that farm died. In the end the farm had to be demolished completely. The sergeant was so frightened that he requested a transfer.
159351: Whoever was ridden by the mare had a stagnation of the blood. The mare could be heard coming.
159365: In 1913 people saw a large comet in the sky every evening. That was an omen of the First World War.
159379: A woman who had rolled money up in her handkerchief lived above the house of a Duitse Schaper (German shepherd, a travelling shepherd thought to have magical powers). When the woman opened the handkerchief one day, the money had turned into mice.
159389: The mare was a heavy weight lying on people. People who were ridden by the mare could not move. Whoever turned onto his side was freed from the mare.
159398: A man who always went out at night met a woman by a marsh, dressed all in white, who walked beside him. After the man had boxed the white woman's ears, the apparition was no longer to be seen.
159402: On a farm no butter could be churned. The cows wandered about among each other at night. Since pregnant women go on pilgrimage and the Gospel of Saint John is read, such evil no longer exists.
159407: In a family in Vichte the mother had died before she could tell where she had hidden her money. One evening a chair was dancing in a corner of the house. After the tiles under the chair had been broken up, the hidden money was found there. Since then no strange things happened in the house anymore.
159417: A woman who was ridden by the mare at night saw a black hand on the door in the morning. That was the evil hand, which was also called 'the black hand'.
159445: People who were pursued by the kokkemare (the mare) felt as if they were being beaten and could not go on.
159495: A man from Oostnieuwkerke was ridden by the mare at night. He was seized by the throat and could no longer breathe. An old woman advised the man to place his clogs under the bed with the toes pointing towards him.
159510: A Duitse schaper (German shepherd, a type of sorcerer) was sitting in the grass with a friend. When a thief suddenly passed by and took the shepherd's coat, the friend said: "Look out, they're running off with your coat!" The German shepherd replied: "That doesn't matter", and he made sure the thief could go no further and had to bring the coat back.
159518: By a house in Assebroek stood a hedge whose branches grew very wide because they had been ridden by the mare and the woman.
159520:
On a farm in Wijtschate there was a fine cow that had calves. One day a woman came to visit and said: "What a fine animal! Does she still give some milk?", to which the farmer's wife replied: "Always a full bucket!"
From the next day on, the cow did not give a single drop of milk.
159526: In the past people believed that stalkeersen (ghostly lights) were ghosts.
159529: A man saw a ball of fire moving back and forth at a culvert by the rotte Vijvers. It was probably the soul of a man who had gone to fetch the midwife and was later found dead with a bramble branch around his head.
159543: When someone was going somewhere and suddenly felt short of breath, people said that the person had been ridden by the mare.
159580: On a farm near the Rattevalle all the sheep died because the people had not given milk to a hunchbacked woman who lived nearby. Such women, after all, read books of magic.
159597: Strange things happened at a castle in Proven. Whoever walked along the hedge was followed by a dog or a goat, which disappeared at the corner of the hedge. When you were in the attic, you heard the sounds of a meal downstairs, though no one could be seen. Little lights and candles were also seen at the castle. People believed a pot of money was hidden in the castle. The haunting only stopped after the castle had been demolished.
159610:
Kerkhove used to be badly haunted. Because a farmer who lived there had much misfortune, it was decided one day to build a small chapel. Although the chapel was already half built, it was knocked down at night three times, so that each time they had to start again. Moreover, the maid who milked the cows got a skin rash, and the farmer was twice thrown onto the dung heap by a strange force.
In the end the friars advised the farmer to build the chapel on the other side of the farm. When that was done, the chapel remained standing.
159624: At a willow tree people always heard someone calling at night: "I'll put it here. I'll put it there. Where should I put it?" One day a drunkard shouted: "Put it, damn it, where you found it!" Since then the ghost has never been heard again.
159633: On a farm there was a cow that was due to calve. When the farmer was with the cow in the stable, he saw an old woman pass by, who said: "What's wrong? Isn't it working?" The farmer answered angrily: "If you don't go away, I'll bash your head in!" That old woman was a witch who was holding back the calf.
159639: People keeping watch over a dead person heard a gold coin fall down in the attic.
159664: In a house people had to deal with a plague of rats that had been sent by a sorcerer. The priest managed to drive the rats away by praying. The people were not allowed to hit the rats.
159670: A doctor who was at the end of his life had said that the devil could take him, but that he was not allowed to break in. One day the doctor's maid heard beautiful music at the door. She slid the window open, after which the devils all came in and took the doctor away.
159677: At 'Osschaarts planksken' between Aaigem (Adegem?) and Kleit, two poachers always met a woman. Every time that woman had let the poachers walk past, the poachers got lost.
159683: A man always saw cats and other animals when he walked to the sea at night. Every time he got home, the man was covered in lice. That was the fault of a witch who had mastered the black arts.
159691: People who had been ridden by the mare could not work for two days. To get rid of the mare as quickly as possible, one had to go on a pilgrimage.
159720: When Mr V. of the castle had died, his son spent all the money. People said that Mr V. came back after his death to settle his son's debts. Sometimes a ghost was seen passing by, or a light appearing in the marshes.
159730: Two women on their way to Pieterskapelle saw a circle of flames in the meadow. When the women crossed the meadow, however, they felt nothing of the fire.
159741:
Every day at about the same time a woman came to a farm to fetch milk. Many accidents happened in the cowshed of that farm. When the people sought advice from a priest, the clergyman said: "You must pray. The first person who comes to fetch milk in the morning, you must chase away."
No sooner said than done. The first woman who came to fetch milk the next morning was chased away. They did not even need to open the gate, because the woman walked right through the closed gate.
159743: A man returning from Izegem was startled when his cap was suddenly taken off his head. A little further on the cap was put back. Further still, a goat jumped onto the man's back.
159753: Since the First World War a woman could no longer get onto the bridge over the Schelde. She always had to wait until other people were crossing the bridge; only then could she get across. During the war a man from Avelgem had been gruesomely murdered on that bridge. The radiation of that dead man held back people and horses on the bridge.
159757: A man walking to Wielsbeke one evening was followed by a beast. When the man looked back, the beast was in front of him; when he looked ahead, the beast was behind him. When he arrived, the man was out of breath from kicking at the animal. Yet he had never been able to hit it.
159786: On a farm in Ruddervoorde everything could be seen shaking and trembling.
159804:
Some people claim that the mare is a stoppage of the blood.
Anyone who slept on his back could feel the mare creeping up from his feet. Victims of the mare tried to call out, but no sound came. As soon as such a person woke up, the mare was gone.
159823: An old woman came to visit a farm where there were three litters of piglets. After the woman had laid her hand on the piglets, the animals died.
159826: In Eggewaartskapelle lived a woman who always tormented her neighbours. One day a man shot at a bird sitting in a tree. Afterwards people said that the witch had a gunshot wound in her arm.
159867: A sorcerer who always carried a magic wand was laughed at by someone one day. The sorcerer then made the mocker lose his way and wander around for hours.
159869: A fifteen-year-old boy went fishing. Next to him another man sat fishing. That man, however, could not catch anything. He had passed a witch's house, and the witch had said: "Well, mate, are you going fishing? You won't catch a single fish!"
159873: At full moon a ghost in a black priest's robe walked along the gutter of the military hospital in Oostende.
159882: A girl had promised to go on a pilgrimage. Whenever the girl was doing the dishes, a little rabbit always jumped onto the plates. The girl went to the priest, who said: "You must ask in the name of God what that rabbit is doing here. If it is sent by God, it must speak. If it is sent by the devil, it must go back to where it came from." When the girl had spoken those words, the rabbit answered: "I am your mother. I made a promise that I never kept. Will you do it for me?" The girl agreed and threw a handkerchief at the rabbit, as the priest had advised her. The rabbit burned its paw on the handkerchief and then disappeared for good.
159890: A pregnant woman from Hooglede who was feeling unwell had prayers said over her by the friars of Steenbrugge. The friars told the woman: "Your complaints are caused by someone who begrudges you that child. When you go home by bus, you will see that woman get on somewhere. You must then make sure you get off the bus immediately." On the way back the woman did as she had been advised. Even so, some time later the woman had a backward and deformed child.
159894: In Oostnieuwkerke no butter could be made. Moreover, the sacks of wheat were always thrown about. After the friars had visited the unfortunate people, the tormenting came to an end. The previous occupants must have caused it.
159905: In a family in Anzegem the children were ill. Because the doctor could not help, they sent for a friar. The clergyman asked the people: "Doesn't a certain woman come by here?" When the people confirmed this, the clergyman said: "If that woman comes here again, you must make a fire and threaten to throw her into it if she will not stop doing evil." When they had done that, the child was soon cured.
159919:
A castle is said to have once sunk in the Tegelbos.
A place where a bell had once sunk was called the 'klokkepitje' (little bell pit).
159940: A man coming back from Kleit saw a pig running about. The man quickly went into a neighbouring house to fetch a lantern. When the man came back, the pig had vanished.
159948: People believed that the dead brewer had returned, because the door of his house always opened even though no one was there.
159962: A man out hunting hares saw a cat approaching. The cat appeared three times, but the man did not see a single hare. When he had shot at the cat, he heard a voice cry: "Fientje is dead..." Deathly pale, the man went home. He told his wife what had happened. The cat on his wife's lap cried: "Is Fientje dead?" and ran outside. It was a sorceress.
159967: A pregnant woman had been slapped on the ear by a witch. The next day the pregnant woman lay ill in bed. Her child died of the 'plane' (1).
159995: On the quay in Oostende there was a haunted house. Every evening it seemed as if a rat was gnawing at the bedroom door. In the morning, however, there was nothing to be seen. When the Norbertine canons came to exorcise the house with prayers, they were drenched in sweat. After that the house was no longer haunted.
160003: Around 1902 screaming was heard every evening in a wood between Beselare and Zonnebeke. The sound resembled a bird's call, but some claimed it was a flying goat. Every evening thousands of people came to listen to the goat. A few even claimed they had seen the goat fly. A farmer called in the police because the onlookers were trampling his crops.
160033:
In 1910 the Kattenkerkhof in Sint-Jan was said to be haunted. People passing there were drenched in sweat and could not go a step further. Only around one o'clock at night could they move on again.
A man returning from France could not get past the Kattenkerkhof and began to sweat heavily. The man saw two big eyes and then something like a flash of lightning. He arrived home drenched in sweat.
160036: Some girls who went to pick hops at night were followed by a pack of cats. "You mustn't kick at them!" said one of the girls. Suddenly the cats had vanished.
160042:
A farmer's wife was sitting with a sow that was about to give birth to piglets. Suddenly a woman from the neighbourhood came to the farm and said: "What fine pigs!" When the piglets were born, they turned completely black. By evening they were dead.
The piglets had been bewitched by that woman.
160075:
Anyone ridden by the mare began to shout and rage, but could do nothing.
A man who was often ridden by the mare was freed from the torment after going to confession with the friars. To protect oneself against the mare, one could also put one's clogs under the bed.
160081: On a farm, three sows sat against the wall of the house in which a sorceress lived. When the pigs were fed, those sows could not move.
160082: A mother had gone into the garden to fetch vegetables for the soup. When she came back inside, she saw a woman standing by her child's cradle. The baby fell ill and two weeks later it was dead. The mother believed that the witch had bewitched her child.
160084: Two boys on their way to visit their girlfriend heard a beautiful sound in the woods and saw a large building. When the two opened the door of the castle, the whole scene had vanished and the boys were simply standing at a crossroads. They were terrified and had lost all sense of direction, so they had to wait there until it was light again.
160098: A woman from Sijsele went to her brother's by moonlight. On the way the woman saw a kitten run across the street. A little later the woman saw a little dog with a chain. Although there was no wind, the gate flew open. A little later the woman got lost. When the woman sat down on the ground, she could find her bearings again.
160099:
In Rollegem lived an old woman who always tried to get near the children. The doctor was at a loss. A neighbour advised the mother to go on a pilgrimage. The neighbour had also said: "The guilty woman will come to visit here this evening!" When the mother returned from her pilgrimage, the woman she suspected was indeed standing by her house.
Ten days later the boy was cured.
160101: Duitse schapers (German shepherds, travelling shepherds thought to have magical powers) had special powers. Anyone who mocked them was plagued by tricks. The mocker's house would then, for example, be full of rats.
160129: People who had not fulfilled their duty returned after their death.
160156: A woman who owned books of magic wanted to buy piglets at a farm. Because the farmer refused, the woman rubbed her hand over the animals' backs. The next day the piglets all lay dead.
160174: Anyone ridden by the mare had to take a pitchfork with three prongs to bed and lay it on his chest with the prongs pointing up. A man who had accidentally laid the pitchfork the wrong way round was himself killed.
160177: In the marshes doodkeersen (death candles, ghostly lights) were often seen by moonlight, and people were very afraid of them. If you came closer, the light drew back. If you walked away, it came closer. It was a soul returning to where it had lived to ask for help.
160188:
On a farm where all the animals died, witches were going about. One time there was misfortune with the cows, another time with the pigs. When the people went to the friars for advice, the clergymen asked: "Do you want to see who is doing this to you?" The people, however, did not want to know. The clergyman gave the people blessed medals.
A while later the farmer was plagued by rats. "You must give the rats another home," the friar had said. Then the clergyman sent the animals to another farm.
160197: In a house in Hertsberge a ball was seen rolling every evening. When a chair was moved to catch the ball, it had vanished. In the morning there was no trace of the ball.
160208: Some vagrants had been locked in the 'koten' (lock-up cells) in Wulpen. As if by miracle, the vagrants had disappeared the next day.
160229: One morning a farmer saw a doodkeers (death candle, ghostly light) on the oast. It was a dead person who had returned because he had failed to fulfil a promise.
160232: A cat was often seen sitting on the street corner. The cat ran between the legs of passers-by and could not be caught. People were afraid of such cats.
160234: During the First World War a German officer shot his mistress dead in a villa and then killed himself. After that the officer's boots were heard walking around the villa and the doors were heard slamming. The villa could never be rented out again.
160251: No one dared to walk past the nekkerput (water-sprite pit) because it was haunted. A man who had to pass there one day with his horses noticed that the horses began to sweat and foam at the mouth. The man made the sign of the cross and began to pray, but the horses bolted in fear.
160266: Werewolves were people who were born with a special caul on their head. If they did not remove that caul, they were forced to go about at night with a chain and do evil. A werewolf could be freed, however, by throwing his skin into the oven.
160286:
In the old days many German shepherds worked on the farms. These shepherds went to Germany now and then. One day a cowherd asked a German shepherd whether he could come along to Germany once. The two waited until it was dark and there was a white goat standing outside. The shepherd said to the cowherd: "Jump on. I'll sit in front." Then the shepherd said: "Over everything and through everything," and the goat flew into the air. The cowherd's feet touched the church tower of Meulebeke. In no time the pair were in Germany and back again. 
But the cowherd remained fascinated by the German shepherd. He had often seen the shepherd read in books and make little black men appear, who came to do all the work. During the harvest the cowherd once summoned the little black men too. When the little men had no more work, linseed was poured into the branches of the hawthorn hedge. Because the little men gathered that linseed in no time, the German shepherd had to be fetched to drive the little black men away. 
The German shepherds lived around the years 1600-1700.
160291: Many parents no longer let their children go outside in the evening, because old women then walked about who were said to be sorceresses. Those witches could give the children the evil hand without touching them.
160308: A man who was fishing for eel at the Vlèruskot saw a ghost pig walking over the water.
160326: In a haunted convent there was knocking on the door and the ringing of a bell. In the end the sisters were so frightened that the four of them slept in the same room with a blessed candle.
160329: A farm along the road to Sleyhage was haunted. A little light was always seen moving above the ground there.
160336:
Some women who owned books of magic could get children in their power. Bewitched children were troublesome except when the woman in question was visiting. Such women pricked the children with pins.
A mother whose child was bewitched sought the advice of the parish priest. The clergyman read prayers over the child until he was drenched in sweat and then said: "On your way home you will see the woman standing by the side of the road". After that the woman could no longer get into the house where she had bewitched the child.
160365: A butcher who had to go out at night left the road at the willow hedge. The man got lost and had to stay sitting there until the next morning. In the morning he told a farmer what had happened. The farmer claimed that other people had experienced the same thing at that spot. When they went to look at the place together, they saw a big hole there. The farmer put his hand into the hole and pulled out two cats. Those were the animals that had been haunting the place.
160372: The castle of baron d'Ydewalle in Kortrijk was haunted. Around midnight a burning horse-drawn coach drove along the lane. The farm next to the castle was also haunted every year. People knew this because the cows then had diarrhoea.
160377: A woman from Zarren always went to visit pregnant women. If that sorceress managed to touch someone, that person met with misfortune.
160399: A woman went on a pilgrimage to Dadizele after a sorceress from Wervik had come to visit. The sorceress had asked if she might have a look at the baby in the cradle. When she did so, however, the baby began to cry. Later all the rabbits on the farm died. The sorceress had said: "There's going to be thunder and lightning," although there was not a cloud in the sky. A little later a thunderstorm did indeed break out.
160420: Some people had been given a few slices of bread and butter by a farmer's wife. When those people went to eat them in a café, they all saw mice crawling out of the bread! Yet they had watched while the farmer's wife was buttering the bread.
160424: On a farm in Waardamme there was a little child who was ill. It seemed as if the child was being pricked by needles. After the priests had read prayers over the child, it recovered. People knew which woman was responsible for the harm.
160429: A woman always had her hair combed by her maid. Whenever there were hairs in the comb, the maid would say: "I'd better get rid of that hair quickly, because you can do a lot of harm with it!" That same maid had once bewitched a child, but her employer did not know that at the time.
160433: A woman had a child that was ill. People said: "The first woman who comes into the house in the morning has bewitched that child." The first woman who came in was the neighbour. After that woman had been chased away, the child was cured.
160449: On a haunted farm all the children died. The magpies were always chattering and in the morning the cows lay in the stable with their legs in the air. The friars of Diksmuide exorcised the farm with prayers until they were drenched in sweat. The friars advised the farmer to put a tub of water in the stable.
160458: A farmer who did not believe in witchcraft was walking through his garden. Suddenly a goat jumped up with her front legs on the farmer's shoulders. "Now take a good look at me," said the goat.
160461: In the convent of Moorsele lived a woman who led a dissolute life. The woman had promised to have a Calvary erected, but she had never kept that promise. After the woman's death the convent was haunted. A man walking in the garden outside got a fright when his cap was suddenly lifted off his head. Chains were heard rattling in underground passages. Windows and doors were slammed shut. After the nuns finally had a Calvary erected themselves, the convent was no longer haunted.
160471: A farmer who was being shaved by the barber and had a visit from a neighbour saw a man approaching who sold rat poison. It was just nine o'clock, the time when farmers ate for the second time in the morning. The farmer let the pedlar join them at the table. After the meal he bought a box of rat poison. Then his neighbour said: "But you don't have rats, and neither do I!" At that the pedlar stood up and said: "But you can get them!" The neighbour laughed. A month later, however, half of his thatched roof had been eaten by rats. That pedlar was someone who could send rats. The farmer always bought something, whether he needed it or not.
160487: When a dead person returns, he always has a cloth over his head, because he is not allowed to make himself known.
160503: The mare was a man with chains around his neck. He sat on his victims and tried to strangle them. People ridden by the mare were drenched in sweat and short of breath. They tried to call out, but could not.
160508: A house in Esen was haunted. The man who lived there was pulled out of his bed by his beard.
160509: A farmer had to go to a wedding of people he did not get on very well with. On the way the farmer met a woman who owned books of magic. The woman said to him: "You shouldn't go, because you won't get there anyway!" The farmer set off all the same. He had barely reached the lane of his farm when he fell into the mud in his best clothes. As a result the farmer had to stay at home.
160512: A man who lived by the Kortekeer went one evening with a friend to visit people on the Schare. At a little chapel next to a tree the men saw a kitten rubbing against their legs. But the men could not catch the kitten. When the men came to a crucifix, the kitten had suddenly vanished. When the men came home late that evening, the same kitten appeared again at the crucifix. The animal went with the men as far as the chapel, but the two never managed to catch the cat.
160528:
A farm in Zwevezele was haunted. The people there were thrown out of their beds at night. Sometimes a little light flew from the cowshed to the henhouse. When the cows were being milked, cats ran across the 'dilteperse' (1) and urinated on the people. Children also died in that family.
The friars of Steenbrugge came to the farm and went round the stables with a sprig of blessed palm. They also said who the woman was who was bewitching the farm.
160537: A man was ridden by the mare every night. The mare looked like an ugly old woman who held her grey hair between her teeth and crawled onto the man's chest.
160573: In the hamlet of Zwijnebak, for several evenings people heard a goat bleating near the trees. People came from far and wide to listen to the flying goat. After a week all the innkeepers had sold their beer to those people and the goat had disappeared. Later it turned out that there is a bird that makes the sound of a goat.
160578: A man whose sister had died saw a light in his bedroom. "Who is here?" the man asked, and a voice answered: "It is me. I would like masses to be said with the money I had." The man told the priest everything and had the masses said. The clergyman had said: "You will see that light once more. It will come to thank you." And so it was.
160583: If a magpie sat around the house, a misfortune would happen. A family from Deerlijk had seen magpies before the news came that a distant relative had died. Then the magpies went to the house of the family's brother. In this way the magpies went to warn everyone in that family.
160591: In Gistel lived a man who owned books of magic. With those books the man could make mice out of clay. When the man then read in his books, the mice began to run around. When the man had died, the dean came to collect his books.
160627: People who were possessed by the mare no longer had control over themselves.
160633: A man taking a load of straw to Westende met a witch. A little further on the man suddenly could not go on, so that he had to leave his load in Middelkerke until the next day.
160645: A castle is said to have once sunk in Zillebeke. On Christmas night, at twelve o'clock, bells could be heard ringing there.
160652: Witches could make children fall ill or die. They could also bring a plague of lice or rats upon people.
160654: Mijnheerke van Maldegem lived in the middle of the woods of Brugge. One day, as he was riding his horse along his lanes, he met a shepherd. "What a fine horn you have!" the man said, and he blew the shepherd's horn. At that, all the 'ketelaars' (1) of the gang the shepherd belonged to appeared. The gang wanted to murder Mijnheerke van Maldegem. His life was spared on condition that he would tell no one what had happened. White sand lay on the main market square of Brugge. With his toe, Mijnheerke van Maldegem drew a picture showing what had happened. Because of this, the 36 gang members were eventually arrested after all by the soldiers of Brugge. Mijnheerke van Maldegem had a cellar built, which was called 'the dark pit'. In that cellar 36 chains were hung, with an iron collar that the prisoners had to wear. The prisoners were given a rye bread and a jug of water to survive. As soon as all the prisoners were in the cellar, the door was bricked up. Later the ghosts of those prisoners came to haunt. One day Mijnheerke van Maldegem was struck by lightning as he stood on his tower.
160662: A brewer had often tried in vain to shoot the hare that came to eat the cabbages in his garden. When the priest had given the brewer blessed cartridges, the brewer did manage to shoot the hare. The moment the hare was hit, the brewer heard a scream like a human's. The next day the brewer followed the trail of blood from his garden to some small cottages where many poachers lived. In one of those cottages lived the woman who had turned herself into a hare.
160665: All the children who had laughed at an old hunchback were full of lice the next day.
160686: A priest could make a couple in love stand still. That priest always walked around with his eyes closed.
160730:
People ridden by the mare actually had a stoppage of the blood. Such people tried to call out in their dream, but could not. Then they woke up sweating.
To protect oneself against the mare, one had to place one's clogs crossed beside the bed.
160735: When a small child looked older than it was, this was often attributed to the influence of witches.
160744: On a farm in Roesbrugge worked a farmhand who was ridden by the kokkemare (the nightmare). The mare was a woman who was in love with someone whose feelings were not returned. Someone claimed that one should stick one's knife in the keyhole of the door. When the mare tried to come in that way, she would be cut in two.
160750: A witch stuck little sticks into the ground and covered them. Then she slapped her knees a few times. After that little mice were running all over the ground.
160766: A man from Bambeke was often visited by a woman who came to fetch buttermilk from him. When one day the man refused to give the woman anything, she became angry. The witch made the milk in the man's cellar go sour. At his wits' end, the man sent for the parish priest. The clergyman began to pray until the drops of sweat ran down his face. Then the priest said: "Now it is over. You must take all the food out of your cellar and throw it away." The next time the man churned butter, everything was fine.
160774: Near the café 'het Zwarte Gat' in Moregem was a place that had been badly haunted for a hundred years, because Emperor Charles had had criminals hanged there. That is why lights and ghosts were always seen there at night. Every evening a big white goat also appeared and jumped about. That was said to have been one of the greatest criminals.
160799: A man who lay sleeping on a bench was ridden by the mare and so could not move. The man tried to call his friends, but could not.
160814:
Because of the mare, a woman lost her way. The woman kept walking around until she saw a light above a door somewhere.
The mare could also stupefy sleeping people.
160819: A woman who was embroidering one evening with a rosary in her lap suddenly heard a loud thump on the door. The following night the woman heard strange noises the whole time. She was so frightened that the next day she went to the curate. After the clergyman had come to read away the witchcraft, the woman heard no more strange noises. The curate was a learned man who owned books.
160821: It was said that the Legestraat was haunted. A man walking home asked a passer-by what time it was. "I'll feel the church clock to see what time it is," the passer-by answered. The passer-by looked behind him and said what time it was.
160827: If a child looked ill, people believed it was being ridden by the mare. Plants that grew too thick or lost their leaves were also ridden by the mare.
160836: People ridden by the mare could not move and felt as if someone was lying on them. In reality the mare was probably a stoppage of the blood.
160850: In Egem lived a family with a mentally disabled son. One night the son was found dead in the woods. The body was brought home and buried by the farm. Since then a rattling was always heard on the farm. When a girl was walking in the woods during the day, it suddenly grew dark. The girl died of fright. One night the family's other son called out from the skylight: "Will you stop now? On Sunday we'll go to Meulebeke to pray to Our Lady of Help." In the end a priest from Meulebeke was sent for to banish the spirit. Every year a pollard willow by the farm withered. It began with the tree farthest from the farm and came closer and closer. The people cut down all those trees and moved away. The new occupants also still heard noises. After they had been to the priest, the noises stopped.
160858: If the parish priest had left his missal open after the gospel, a sorceress could not leave the church after mass. Clergymen who knew that someone owned a book of magic tried to get hold of that book.
160861: A dead woman had to come back to haunt because during her life she had promised to go on pilgrimage to Marc-Marquette. The woman came to tell her father that she was in the limbo of heaven. She asked her father to go on pilgrimage for her.
160881: The white lady of the Beukendreef was a powerful woman who could bewitch people. For instance, she could make people stand still and a little later make them go on again.
160885: In Westrozebeke lived a woman who was said to be a witch. At school some children conjured mice out of their handkerchiefs during break. When the sorceress's son saw this, he said, "Can't you do better than that? I'll make some mice this afternoon!" During the lunch break the boy rolled bits of clay into the shape of little mice. When he struck the little balls with his hand, they all turned into mice. The schoolmaster went to fetch the curate and swept the animals into the air vents in the corners of the classroom. Then he said to the boy, "You needn't come to school anymore, you already know enough!"
160898: In Knesselare lived a little old woman who always wore a black apron and a black neckerchief. One day a mother went to the field with her seven-month-old son. The mother left the child sitting in the pram. A little later the old woman came by and stroked the child's head. After that the little boy cried all the time. Shortly afterwards the child died of 'the old man'.
160901: The Vaartbrug in Kortrijk was haunted. Every evening a woman's voice was heard there calling: "Half water and half milk, scantly measured, our Lord has forgotten my soul too."
160929: At a crossroads everyone was attacked by a dog. One day a man kicked the dog, injuring its legs. Because the people of the neighbourhood felt sorry for the wounded dog, they tended it. While they were doing so, the dog turned into a little old woman.
160934: To protect their garden, the friars could make intruders get stuck in the hedge as they tried to escape.
160943: People whose child cried all the time because it had been bewitched by a woman from the village went to the friars. After that the child did not cry any more.
160965: A man out for a walk one evening suddenly saw a big tree standing in front of him. The tree was so big that the man could not see over it.
160974: Some people could send a plague of rats or bees to a house. A man whose house was full of bees found one day that the creatures had disappeared. They had been sent to another place.
160983: A church is said to have sunk one night beside the railway in Anzegem. The bells of that church can still be heard ringing underground.
160988: A man from Middelkerke walking home around midnight found many walnuts and chestnuts on the way. The more the man picked up, the more he saw lying there. That was the work of a witch who made sure the man could not get home.
161008: When an unbelieving man lay dying, a crow sat on the windowsill. No one managed to chase the crow away. When the man had died, the crow flew off. The bird never came back after that.
161037: A writer decided to spend the night in an uninhabited haunted castle. As the writer sat at his desk in the castle, he heard the door open at midnight. A ghost came in, sat down next to the writer and said: "I am a soul from purgatory." The ghost asked for a mass to be said; then it would be released.
161049: A witch who appeared in the shape of a toad was thrown into the fire. The next morning it was found that a neighbour woman had burns all over.
161052: In Houtem lived a mother with a baby that always cried. The baby grew so thin that it eventually died. The baby had often been visited by a woman from the neighbourhood. Only when the child's body was laid out did people see that it was full of pins.
161058: The Gospel of Saint John was a good remedy against evil, especially evil caused by witches and sorcerers. To find out whether someone was a witch or a sorcerer, the parish priest had the suspected person come to the presbytery. He would then open the Gospel of Saint John and tell the person that he or she could go home. Whoever could not get up was a witch or a sorcerer. If he wanted, the priest could keep such a person sitting on their chair for years!
161067: A woman who was said to be a sorceress came to visit a house in Torhout every day. When a child in that house fell ill, the people went to the friars of Tielt, who advised the parents to make a novena. Within those nine days the child died nonetheless.
161079: A farmer's wife had much misfortune with her children. Four or five times in a row the newborn child looked emaciated and died after about eight days. Finally the farmer's wife sought the advice of a clergyman, who gave her a pot of holy water. The clergyman said to the woman: "If an old woman from the neighbourhood comes by again, you must ask her to sit by the fire. Then you must put the holy water under her chair and make the fire hotter and hotter. The witch will then be unable to get up." Everything happened as the clergyman had predicted. When the witch could no longer bear the fire, she cried in despair: "Please, take that out from under my chair!" Then the farmer's wife said: "You murderess, now tell me what you have done to my four children!" The witch answered: "Go to my cupboard. You will find a little doll there full of pins. When you have taken the pins out, your baby will recover". And so it was.
161083: Near the hill people could be heard walking and singing at midnight. A man who lived nearby had once tried to shoot at the company, but had not succeeded. When the man shot with salt, the ghostly figures disappeared.
161103: A man who came home late every evening was annoyed that a woman always came to sit beside him in the coach. One time the man threw that woman out of the coach. When the man got home, he saw the woman sitting on the toll barrier. The horse could go no further. After the man had chased the woman away once more, she never turned up again.
161106: At the Veldschool in Ingelmunster it was haunted at midnight. Because the nuns were afraid, they called the police to guard the school. The officers, however, were so frightened that they did not dare to stay and ran away. Fortunately the situation improved when the bishop allowed the nuns to keep the Blessed Sacrament in the school.
161112: On a farm a dead person came to haunt in the shape of a flying goat.
161141: A witch could turn herself into a hare or a cat. One day someone shot at a hare sitting in a garden. That is how the witch lost an eye.
161153:
A man from Lendele had to fetch the doctor for his wife. On the way the man was set upon by a witch three times. After that the man was able to beat the witch until she lay still.
A girl had a relationship with that witch's son against her parents' wishes. One day the witch said to the girl: "When you go home, you will walk from one ditch into the other." That did indeed happen, so that the girl nearly fell ill from it.
161167: By making the sign of the cross, one could free oneself from the mare.
161174: In Heist and in Zeebrugge lived two well-known sorceresses. One of them could make mice by rolling lumps of mud in her hand.
161178: Every night as she lay in bed, a girl saw two men with a cigar come in through the window and a little later leave by the chimney. After prayers were read over the girl, she no longer saw the strange apparitions.
161187: It was said of a sorcerer's daughter that she could work witchcraft. Whenever that woman walked past a house, misfortune came upon that house. At one place where this had happened, the people were advised by their neighbours to make the sign of the cross and chase the woman away. The people did not dare to, however. A while later their father fell ill.
161192: On a haunted farm no butter could be made. Because the people were at their wits' end, they sent for the friars to exorcise the building. When the friars came out of the cellar, they were drenched in sweat.
161195: A man who worked for a farmer heard it said that a black cat often sat at the crossroads between Diksmuide and Torhout. People believed the crossroads was haunted. When the man came home one evening around ten o'clock, he saw a black cat sitting in the ditch. Frightened, the man walked on. The man told the parish priest what he had seen, but according to the clergyman it was nothing more than superstition.
161199: A witch from Houtem always made people drive into the ditch. On a farm near the witch's house, there was misfortune with the cows every year. After a small chapel was built there, things improved.
161232: Templars are said to have once hidden bells in the Klokkenput (Bell Pit) in Koekelare. The bells can still be heard ringing now.
161250: Some farmers from Houtkerke could never get to the horses with their implements when they set off along a certain road. For at the end of that road lived a sorceress.
161257: The werewolf was a man who jumped onto the backs of passers-by and made them carry him.
161262: A fisherman had sold his soul to the devil. Whenever the man was at sea, he always saw a ship with little black devils sail past. The man always caught a lot of fish in his nets, while on other fishing boats they caught almost nothing. The man believed the devil was responsible for this.
161265: A man who had to transport a load of wood was plagued by a witch who stood watching at the door of her house. The witch made the horses refuse to go on. The man was so angry that he threw a stone at the witch.
161277:
A woman with three or four children was often alone at home for several days and nights because her husband went to work in France. Every day at around eleven o'clock the house was haunted. In the kitchen the pot hook over the fire swung back and forth the whole time without anyone being seen.
Since revolvers have existed, there are no more ghosts. The woman became so frightened that she no longer dared to stay home alone in the evenings.
161281: A woman carrying a bundle of nettles on her back walked past a witch's house. The witch bewitched the woman so that she had to dance with the nettles on her back. Perhaps the witch was jealous because she would have liked the nettles for her goat.
161306: A sorceress lived in a neighbourhood in Loppem. One day two men from Loppem were coming back from Sint-Andries, where they had fetched eel. On the way the ox fell ill and lay down on the ground. Nobody managed to get the animal back on its feet. When evening had already fallen, the sorceress from Loppem came to the ox. After she had been alone with the ox for a quarter of an hour, the animal, strangely enough, sprang up.
161323: Two women who were said to be able to work witchcraft often walked about in the evening, dressed in hooded cloaks. One of these women often visited a seamstress from the village. A while later the seamstress suspected that her child had been bewitched by that woman. After the seamstress had put a paasnagel (an Easter nail, a blessed charm) under the threshold, the witch could no longer come in. All pregnant women were afraid of that witch.
161343: On a farm where butter could no longer be churned, the friars were sent for. After the friars had said prayers over the farm, they advised the people to chase away the first person who came to visit. When they did so, the witch said: "I wish you were eaten by lice!" When the farmer's wife died, she was full of lice.
161363: In the Meerlaan (1) lived a man who could make mice run on the table.
161366: In Waardamme worked a farmhand who slept with his head at the foot of his bed when the moon was shining. The sexton of Ruddervoorde also could not sleep when the moon shone.
161385: The devil presided over the meetings of the framassons (freemasons). One day a mission friar preached that the cross could drive away the devil. Then a freemason said to the clergyman: "Come, let's see if that is true". The friar went with the freemason to a meeting in a luxuriously furnished hall with beautiful chandeliers. At a certain moment all the freemasons came in. The last to come in was the devil. He wore the same clothes as the freemasons, but he could be recognised by his tail, which hung a little way out from under his coat. At the start of the meeting the friar took out the cross and made the sign of the cross with it. The next moment all the chandeliers fell to the floor, the lights went out and the chairs flew about. The devil had vanished.
161393: A man who went to visit his girlfriend in Geluwe on Sundays had to pass an old chapel where something white could be seen jumping about on four legs. People said it was a returned dead person in the shape of a big white dog. It was a punishment of someone who had been bewitched.
161394: A woman from Nieuwpoort often went to the fish market, where she asked the fishermen for a few small fish. Anyone who gave the woman nothing could be bewitched. Many fishermen refused to go to sea if they had met the beggar woman beforehand.
161397: A man woke up at night because he heard knocking. It sounded as if someone were hitting the attic stairs with a ham bone. Because the man was afraid, he lit a blessed candle and began to pray. Suddenly the man realised that it was probably the ghost of his aunt, come to ask for her Masses. After the man had some Masses said the next day, nothing strange happened any more.
161403:
During the sermon a priest said: "At this moment someone is sitting in my cherry tree stealing my cherries. That person will have to stay sitting there until I come home". 
The same priest was once put in prison because he had said that the town council consisted of several donkeys and a mule.
161423: A farm in Veldegem always had misfortune. In the morning the animals lay dead in the stables.
161436: A man's house was full of lice and fleas. The priest advised the people to clean the house completely and set fire to it. If they then still saw vermin, they had to catch it by hand. They followed the priest's advice and washed the whole house. Although it was winter, they found that the house was already completely dry by evening.
161453: Some people walking past a house saw a goat standing there, bleating loudly. A woman went to the goat, put her rosary over the animal's horns and said: "Go back where you came from." The next moment the goat turned into a woman.
161484: A farming family had to move because they were always woken at midnight by ghostly noises in the house.
161495: Duitse schapers (German shepherds, travelling shepherds said to have magic powers) were strange people who wore an ugly hat. When the shepherds threw that hat against a door, the bolt slid back by itself. After a while people were clever enough to lock their doors with two locks.
161502: When the boys in Avekapelle had to draw lots for conscription, they first gave some money to a witch. If the witch laid her hand on the shoulders of one of the boys, that boy drew a good number.
161505: In Lauwe lived a farmer's wife who promised to give the poor as many sacks of grain as there were grains in a 'houwe' (1). That year the harvest on that farm was exceptionally good. The farmer's wife, however, forgot her promise. Some time later the people on the farm were woken by the noise of carriages and horses with bells. In the morning nothing could be heard. A man going on pilgrimage saw two devils on the two pillars in front of the farm, writing in thick books. When the man looked back again a little further on, he no longer saw the devils. Only when it grew light could the man find his way home again.
161528: In Menen lived two old women who were said to be able to work magic. One evening the children were talking about the women when suddenly a black cat came in. The cat was chased away, but the animal kept coming back. The next morning a girl saw the same cat walking behind the house. The girl began to cry and then turned into a cat herself. The parents thought it was the first cat and went after the animal, and the father went to fetch his gun. The cat had climbed a tree. Just as the father was about to shoot, the cat screamed and turned back into the girl. In revenge the girl's parents went to set fire to the sorceress's house. But they could not find the old woman anywhere. A little later they saw her flying through the air on a broom.
161546: One day a farm was visited by a disabled man who asked whether they had any rats. Because the people were struggling with a real plague of rats, they accepted the stranger's help. The man asked for an old spade, went to a spot behind the farm and dug a little hole there. Because the man had only one arm, the farmhand offered to do the work for him, but the man refused. From the hole the man took a book, in which he began to read. The next moment all the rats came running to the hole. "The last rat will be a crippled one," said the man, and so it was. After that the farm was rid of the rat plague.
161547: A cat always roamed around a house where there was a small child. One day boiling water was poured over the animal. The next day a woman from the neighbourhood was burned all over.
161551: Fishermen were very superstitious. If the helmsman saw a black long-haired woman or a black cat as he went on board, the ship was not allowed to sail.
161577: A girl was so frightened that she did not dare to sleep anywhere. The girl told the priest that she always saw the ghost of her grandmother appear. At first the priest dismissed the story as nonsense, but in the end he promised to come and have a look. The priest advised the girl to say to the ghost: "If you are sent by God, say why you come. If you are sent by the devil, go back where you came from!" The ghost answered: "I am sent by God, and by the leg of the big horse so much money lies buried!" Afterwards a great deal of money was indeed found at that place.
161583: A man who had pulled out a boundary post from his field had died. At midnight a light always appeared at the spot where the post had been removed. The light kept calling: "Where shall I put them, where shall I put them!" The light was the soul of the man who had once pulled out a post there.
161585: A farmhand who was going to visit his parents met a woman on the way, who said: "Won't you come and look at my piglets?" The farmhand went to look. The woman put her hand on the farmhand's shoulder. A little later the farmhand was full of lice.
161603: Whoever walked past Tillegem castle in the evening saw glowing spots in the undergrowth. Someone is said to have been murdered in the castle long ago during a fight between two knights. People believe that this dead person comes back to haunt.
161613: Some young people who rang the priest's doorbell as a prank suddenly could not move. The pranksters had to stay standing by the door until the priest came.
161617: A woman ridden by the mare saw a hand pull the blankets tight so that she could no longer breathe.
161628: In 't Nieuwland lived a farmer who wanted to bring in the last part of his harvest. The farmer saw at least a hundred mice crawling out of the crops. He was convinced that a woman from the neighbourhood was responsible for that misfortune.
161640: A sorceress had given a neighbour a shawl for safekeeping. Shortly afterwards that neighbour's daughter fell ill. They went on pilgrimage to Zwevegem for the girl. A woman from the village, however, said to the worried mother: "If your daughter is bewitched, it is because you still have that shawl in your keeping. You must burn the shawl in the stove." While the shawl was still in flames, the neighbour came running up, sweating, saying: "Oh, it is already too late, I can do nothing more now!"
161656: In Waardamme there was a little child who was ill. The parents took the child to the fathers of Steenbrugge, where they told them that a certain woman visited them every day. The fathers read prayers over the child and advised the people not to let that woman in any more. After that the child recovered.
161661: A farmer who had sown clover was annoyed by a hare that came to eat his clover every evening. The priest advised the farmer to shoot at the animal with a blessed half-franc coin. The next day a woman from the village had lost her eye.
161671: Anyone ridden by the mare actually had a stoppage of the blood.
161673: A woman going to market at night saw a horse without a head. In a lane at the foot of a hill she heard noises as if blocks of glass were being thrown.
161675: An old woman was buried in the churchyard of Desselgem. On her grave stood a wooden cross. A long time after her funeral some men came past the churchyard on their way back from the inn. To their great astonishment the men saw the cross glowing. They went back to the inn to fetch the others. They too saw the cross glowing. Every evening many people came to look at the glowing cross. One evening, as part of a bet, two boys armed with a club went to the cross. Terrified, the two approached the glowing cross. Suddenly a gust of wind made the cross move gently. Then a hoarse cry rang out and one of the boys fell against the cross. The other fled. The next morning the boy was found dead by the haunted cross.
161679: A man driving piglets from Moerbrugge to Steenbrugge suddenly could go no further along the canal. On the other side of the canal lived a woman who was said to be able to work magic. At that very moment the man saw that woman appear from behind a tree.
161687: A woman who had been cursed by her mother saw a little dove sitting beside her every day. After the curate had read prayers over the dove, it did not appear again.
161742: A werewolf was someone who was half human, half animal. A farmer had a farmhand who had to roam as a werewolf at night to torment people. One day the farmer found a werewolf skin in a woodpile. When he asked the farmhand what it was, the farmhand fell to his knees in fright and begged: "Farmer, burn that skin quickly! Then you will be released and so will I!" After the farmer had burned the skin, nothing strange happened on the farm any more.
161766: When certain women came near a cradle, the baby immediately began to cry. One day, when people had seized one of those women and said: "It's you!", the woman denied all guilt. After long insistence, however, she took a wax doll full of pins out of her pocket. After the woman had pulled the pins out of the doll, the child fell silent.
161782: A witch had cursed a fisherman. The next time the fisherman went to sea, his ship was lost with all hands.
161800: A twelve-year-old girl walked to school. The forester had told the girl that she must not look back on the way. The girl did so anyway and saw a red lady who followed her for ten minutes. The forester claimed that he had often seen that lady.
161825: When setting out on a journey, one had to greet the first woman one met. If one did not, one would have bad luck on the way. A man had set off with his farmhand on a long journey. On the way the men saw a woman in a hooded cloak walking. Just as the man was about to greet the woman, she crossed the road and jumped over the dyke. That day everything went wrong. The lantern on the cart blew out and the axle even came loose. Later that day a cat jumped onto the wagon. That cat stayed sitting there.
161840: A man who had sat with friends in the café for a while walked home. A little later, however, the man was back in the café, because he had seen a black figure by the church wall and had run away in fright. When the friends went to the church wall together with the man, however, there was nothing more to be seen.
161856: Some people were keeping watch by a sick man who was dying. At a certain moment one of the women said: "There are so many of you here already, I'm going home." When the woman walked past the house of a witch, she suddenly felt very cold. When she got home she was so ill that she crawled into bed with her clothes and clogs on. The woman's husband went to consult someone, from whom he got tea for his sick wife. At first the man had given gin, but the husband had explained that his wife did not like drinking it. "Yes, things are bad with the witches!" the husband said to the man, to which the man replied: "Between the 'Haai' and the 'Tap uit' (1) live eighteen witches!"
161890: Some boys were coming back together from a party. One of the boys could not get into his house because a sheep was walking in front of his door. When the other boys came closer to see what was going on, the sheep suddenly vanished. The mischief was caused by an old sorceress who lived a little further on.
161897: A woman from Knokke passed a farm that was haunted. In the barn of that farm people always heard sounds as if someone were threshing, and in the kitchen they heard plates rattling, although there was nothing to be seen. Under the farm was an underground passage through which the friars could go to Brugge.
161916: To protect oneself against the mare, one had to put an old sabre or bayonet under one's pillow.
161928: A man had bought a cupboard somewhere and put it in his attic. Because a hellish noise was always heard in the attic at night, it was decided to break the cupboard open. A lot of money was hidden in a false bottom. The owners had returned to look for their money.
161945: A man walking along the dyke saw a dog running in the distance. The dog grew bigger and bigger. When the man reached the dog, the animal had turned into a woman.
161949: The farmhand of a farmer in Westkapelle always saw a stalkeers (ghostly light) in the evening. One evening the farmer went there and saw the ghost of a dead woman who had come back because she had failed to fulfil a promise. The woman asked the farmer to fulfil the promise in her place. When the ghost wanted to shake his hand, the farmer gave her his handkerchief. The woman burned her hand into the handkerchief.
161959: In Heist lived a sick child who had been bewitched by an old woman. A neighbour advised the child's mother to pour boiling water over a toad that often sat by the water drain. The next day one of the neighbour women lay in bed with a burned arm. She was the witch who had turned herself into a toad.
161962: A man stood talking all day instead of working in his field. By evening the work had been done by a crowd of little devils.
161984: A boy ridden by the mare became short of breath and could not call out or move.
161990: A priest who had to go and administer the Last Rites to someone had to cross the bridge in Steenkerke. It was a bridge that had to be raised when a ship came by. The woman at the bridge raised it, although she could easily have let the priest through first, since the ship was still far off. Because of this the priest had to make a detour via Veurne. When he came back, the woman was still standing by the bridge as if nailed to the ground. "You may go now", said the priest. After that the woman could move again.
162011: A woman worked for a farmer's wife who always found something to complain about. One day the woman filled the farm with rats.
162014: A boy slept with the son of a witch. Although that son's head was full of big lice, the boy himself never got any.
162017: On the road from Zwevegem to Kortrijk something strange is said to have happened long ago. A farmer coming back from his field in the dark saw white women dancing in the treetops of a large avenue.
162018:
In Lokeren there lived a rich man who gave a great deal to the poor. When this freemason had died, the nuns kept watch by his body. Suddenly the sisters heard noise in the room. The dead freemason was fighting with a dog. After that incident the sisters no longer dared to stay with the body. The freemason's body was taken away by the devils. So that the pallbearers would suspect nothing, the coffin was filled with something else.
In Rijssel there was a house where only such wicked people lived.
162025: Two women who had gone to spin flax were coming back past the Bollewalletjes. Suddenly the women saw a beautiful white cat. One of them picked up the cat and carried the animal in her apron. At the Bollewalletjes the animal jumped into the water.
162035: In a house the windows and doors always banged open and shut in the evening. When the people went to the priest, the clergyman said: "No, I am not coming, because you have mocked the students. You will have to go to the white friars; they will surely put an end to the haunting."
162048: A man from Tongeren who was coming back one night from visiting his girlfriend was annoyed by a cat that kept getting under his feet. The man picked up the cat and walked on. At the main road the cat fell to the ground and turned into a woman who said: "Let run what runs and pretend you don't see it."
162058: On a farm in Houtkerke they had much misfortune with the animals. So the farmer went to consult the fathers of Ieper. The fathers advised the man to go home; he would find out who the witch was, but he was not allowed to say anything. A woman who had received the Last Sacraments two days before walked onto the farmer's yard and stopped halfway, saying: "How is the horse?" The witch could not come any closer to the farm and so went on her way.
162066: The Duitse Schapers (German shepherds, a type of sorcerer) came from Friesland to Belgium during the wars of religion. A German shepherd worked as a farmhand on a farm in Snaaskerke. Before Sunday mass began, the farmhand went into a café with his dog. He threw his pocketknife at a beam on the ceiling. The dog jumped at the knife and stayed hanging from the beam until its master came back from mass.
162090: In Bellegem lived a woman who led a sinful life. One day the woman suddenly died after eating mussels. When people heard the shutters banging open and shut at night, they believed it was the dead woman, returning because she had forgotten something. After masses had been said, the spirit did not return again.
162091: A woman going to mass met a witch on the way, who looked her straight in the eyes. When the woman went to the toilet that evening, she could no longer see anything. The witch had done that to her.
162116: A farmer drove a horse and cart past the house of an old woman. Although the cart was not heavily loaded at all, the horse suddenly could go no further. A little later the old woman came out of her house, saying: "I'll give a bit of a push." When the woman did so, the horse immediately started moving.
162122: A man went to the beach to see whether the weather was good enough to go out to sea. In the dunes the man saw a cat. He threw a stone at the animal, but the cat stayed sitting there. A little later there were three cats instead of one. The man was attacked by the animals.
162133: People ridden by the mare at night felt as if a woman was squeezing their throat shut.
162155: In the evening lights were often seen in old oak stumps. People said they were spirits.
162186: When people returned after their death, it was usually because they had buried money somewhere and wanted to point it out. The mother of a woman from Reningelst, for example, returned in the garden where she had buried her money.
162191: A man went to Bruges to fetch straw. In Bredene the man's horses suddenly refused to go any further. On the way the man had met a witch, who had probably cursed him. The Norbertine canons were able to tell the man that an evil hand regularly came to the farm, who had to be sent away. That was her.
162209: In the past priests always preached about the sins of people who went to a dance hall. One Monday morning the organ of a dance hall lay in a thousand pieces by the bridge. The devils had come to fetch that organ.
162216: In a family in Zwevezele the father had died. They had promised to go on a pilgrimage for the man, but had forgotten that promise. After the father's death the animals broke loose and the carriages were seen dancing. One day a visitor saw a light fly from the churchyard to the house. The light fell to the ground right in front of that person and said: "Three people must go on a pilgrimage for me, because they forgot." After the promise had been fulfilled, the friars were called to exorcise the farm. The friars were drenched in sweat. To drive out the evil, the people also had to pour out two buckets of water on the farthest part of the farmyard. The evil would then still come one horse's step closer every year.
162222: A man who had already lost many children was keeping watch by a little child who was dying. Although all the windows and doors were shut, a cat was walking around the house, and it walked through the fire four or five times without getting burnt. When the child had died, a witch from the neighbourhood was blamed.
162239: Some dead people returned to point out where they had hidden their gold jewellery.
162257: People ridden by the mare had a bad dream. Sometimes people hung mistletoe above their bed so as not to be ridden by the mare.
162271: The witches always held their feasts on the Toveresseknok in Izegem. A large oak tree stood at that spot. One day one of the witches had accidentally said: "Over everything and through everything". That witch arrived at her destination badly injured.
162276: A man had often tried to shoot the cat that always sat mewing on the roof at night. One day the man had the priest bless some silver. After the man had shot with the silver, the cat was gone for good.
162285:
People ridden by the mare were drenched in sweat and felt as if they were being strangled. One could hear the mare approaching.
A man who was afraid of the mare always left his slippers downstairs. Some people also claimed that one could protect oneself against the mare by placing one's slippers upside down under the bed.
162299: Some fishermen had sold about six hundred kilos of fish in Blankenberge. The fishermen had seen some women whispering to each other. They did not know, however, that one of those women was the daughter of a witch. The daughter had said: "If we don't get half, you won't have to catch a single fish any more." When the fishermen had cast their nets at night on the Schelde by the Paardenmarkt, a strange little light could be seen in the mast. A moment later the light had disappeared. At the harbour of Zeebrugge a large Scheldevorch (a bird) was suddenly sitting on the ship. When the fishermen headed home, they heard a ticking the whole time. When the ship's boy came back from a café in Nieuwpoort, where he had gone for a drink, he was terrified.
162304: Along the Ieperse Weg in Poperinge there was a well called 'de Carosseput' or 'de Magdalenaput'. That well was haunted. Nobody dared to go near it after dark.
162309: A mother from Gistel went to the parish priest with her child because it cried all the time and was growing very thin. The priest asked the woman whether anyone ever came near the cradle. The mother replied that every day a woman came to fetch potato peelings for her sheep. The priest gave the mother a paasnagel (an Easter nail, a blessed charm) to put by the little window above the door. The next time the woman came by for potato peelings, she got no further than the door and went on her way.
162326: A girl began to cry every evening at about ten o'clock. The girl's mother went every evening to eat gingerbread at an old woman's house. In the end the mother went to the parish priest, who gave her a medal. When the old woman came to visit, she fell three times. Since then she never visited again.
162327: A woman lived with her sick husband in Klemskerke. One day the woman went to bed early because the next morning she had to take butter to market. The woman woke in the night and by mistake left for the market in Oostende two or three hours too early. As soon as the woman reached the Doorne Bilk, she took out her rosary and began to pray, as everyone did at that place. Suddenly, to her great fright, the woman saw a black figure approaching. The woman could not flee, for she was rooted to the spot with fear. Two men came along carrying a small ladder on which lay a dead body. A third man wore boots and had a spade in his hand. Silently the three men walked past the frightened little woman. When the woman reached the bridge and found that the gate was still closed, she realised she had got up far too early. The woman waited there until the gate was opened at six o'clock. The woman was so shaken by the night's events that she died six weeks later.
162329: A doodkeers (death candle, ghostly light) was a dead person who had returned. People often joked about doodkeersen. Pranksters tried to frighten people with a hollowed-out turnip with a candle inside.
162339: In Moerschoote near Sint-Laureyns there was a farm that was haunted and where all the animals died. In the end the family that lived there was completely ruined.
162341: On a farm in Sint-Denijs all the horses fell ill. Because the vets could not help, a builder was sent for to disinfect the stables. The builder was in the stable together with a vet. Sweating, the vet closed the doors and told the builder to repair the stable and plaster the walls. When that had been done, the horses stayed healthy. A witch had caused the illness.
162345: A woman walking home one evening saw a herd of piglets running in the meadow. When the woman came closer, the piglets had strangely vanished.
162371: If a ladder stood somewhere, people made a detour so as not to have to walk under it.
162391: A man had to fetch the midwife in Bulskamp. When the man passed a little chapel, a witch jumped on his back and had herself carried all the way to Bulskamp. When he got home the man went to bed. He could not get up any more because he suffered from lumbago (1).
162397: A mother carrying a child on her arm opened the door to a pedlar woman. The pedlar touched the child and said: "What a beautiful child!" The next day the child was ill and a doctor had to be called. The doctor said the child could not recover. A neighbour advised the people to have prayers read over the child by the fathers. The next morning they wrapped the child in a woollen scarf and carried it to Roeselare. There they had a father read prayers over the child. When they came home with the child, the doctor could not believe his eyes: the child was cured.
162399: A child who had been bewitched by an old woman had prayers read over it by the fathers of Steenbrugge. Afterwards the fathers said: "You will be cured now."
162400: In the Vormebeke castle on the road from Hooglede to Sint-Jozef everything was knocked over, and people heard ghosts in the cellar.
162409: A wizard often went to a café for a drink. One day the landlady said: "There are so many rats here. Can't you do something about it?" The wizard answered: "You needn't worry about that." The next day all the rats were in the house across the street.
162417: A farmhand who was ridden by the mare at night was forced to carry twenty-five buckets of water to the cows. In the morning the farmhand lay outside on the ground, frozen with cold.
162424: A Duitse schaper (German shepherd, a travelling shepherd said to have magic powers) coming back from the fields met some people who said: "We're thirsty!" The shepherd answered: "From which brewery, which beer cellar and which barrel should the beer come?" and he stuck his magic staff into the ground. The next moment enough beer for all the bystanders came out of the staff.
162427: The mare was a stoppage of the blood. If someone was ridden by the mare, one had to call out that person's name. The person then woke up and was freed from the mare.
162444: The chapel of Papinglo is said to have once sunk into a bottomless pit.
162453: In Pittem lived a sorceress whom everyone feared. She could make children full of lice and she could roast potatoes on the grate of a stove that was not lit.
162476: When going to bed, one was not allowed to place one's clogs crossed, for then one would be ridden by the mare at night.
162480: On a farm where things were going badly, they sent a farmhand away so that they could burn his animal skin in the oven in the meantime. As soon as the skin caught fire, the farmhand was already standing by the oven.
162486: On Friday nights the witches met on the Toveresseknok in Izegem. Once one of the witches had said: "Over everything and through everything". That witch arrived at her destination badly injured.
162498: People coming back from Moerkerke did not dare to walk along the Zandstraat, because a black cat roamed there that stopped them.
162502: Some Iceland fishermen shot a crow from the mast of their ship. When the captain came home, he found that his wife had lost her hand.
162524:
A stonemason stayed at an inn together with his thirty-year-old son. In the village lived a girl who was in love with that son, but the love was not mutual. The girl suspected the innkeeper's wife of having turned the young man against her.
One evening at the inn, when they were about to fold up the sheets, a bat fell out. The innkeeper nailed the animal to the gate. Two days later a row of mice was seen running along a cupboard in the inn. One evening the innkeeper's wife sat knitting. At a certain moment she bent down to pick up a dropped ball of yarn. To her great fright the woman held not yarn but a bat in her hands.
Later another bat was caught in the bedroom.
162527: In the past there were old people who could make children ill and cry day and night. The clergy then had to read prayers over those children.
162533: A man saw a witch sticking pins into a doll and saying: "I am now busy tormenting a child".
