162555: A doodskeers (death candle, ghostly light) was the soul of a deceased person who returned to dig up hidden money. People were afraid of doodskeersen, because they could break your neck. Sometimes farmers ploughing their fields found a pot of money.
162559: Three farmer's sons no longer dared to go outside in the evening for fear of the notorious ghost coaches without horses that were sometimes seen in the area.
162561: A woman who always wore a pink dress often came from Wevelgem to the German cemetery in Lauwe. Although not a scrap of wood was to be seen on the road, the woman kept picking all sorts of things up. When she reached the cemetery, she had a whole bundle of wood on her back.
162569: It was said that witches could appear in the shape of an animal.
162590: When the fishermen had met a black cat in the morning, they turned back and went to the church to offer five centimes. They believed that the cat was a witch in animal form who would bring them bad luck.
162594: One evening a poacher who was afraid of nothing was standing under a poplar when he heard a voice call: "There stands a poacher, there stands a poacher!" The man looked around but saw nothing and no one. The same thing happened several evenings in a row.
162603: Whenever a fisherman wanted to go to his boat, he always met a woman in an apron. "Where are you going?" the woman would ask, and the fisherman would answer: "Don't you dare come closer or I'll knock you down!" The woman jumped into the fisherman's basket, so that he could not get to his boat.
162622: People ridden by the mare began to scream loudly and felt as if someone was jumping on them. In reality those people had a stoppage of the blood.
162645: In the past almost all old women were suspected of witchcraft. In Westkapelle, for example, lived such a woman who could throw eggs into a basket without the eggs breaking.
162648: A Duitse schaper (German shepherd, a travelling shepherd said to have magic powers) who could work magic could tap beer from his magic staff. When a farmer went to his cellar one evening, he found that his beer barrel was empty.
162652: People ridden by the mare had a stoppage of the blood at night, which made them feel short of breath. One could hear the mare approaching before being seized by the throat, but one could not resist.
162656: A woman walking from Kortrijk to Izegem between midnight and one o'clock suddenly saw little lights hanging from her hat. The man who was with her also saw little lights on his cap. A sorceress from the neighbourhood had done it.
162666: The bells of Papinglo are said to have once sunk. Every year the bells could be heard ringing on Christmas Eve.
162669: A sorceress wanted to have her rabbit mated with a rabbit belonging to a woman from the neighbourhood. That woman claimed she had no rabbits because she did not want to let the sorceress in. The next day that woman's rabbit lay dead in its hutch.
162695: A man from Vlamertinge who worked at the railway station in Poperinge was visited by an old man who came to ask for tobacco to roll a cigarette. When the man was about to leave for home on his bicycle a few days later, the same old fellow said to him: "Get home safely!", to which the man replied: "Well yes, why wouldn't I get home safely? I've been travelling that road for years and I've always got home safely!" and left. But when the man reached the Meiboom, he lost his way and saw no other option than to ride back to the station. The strange little man was still standing there and again asked for a cigarette. When the man tried a second time, he again lost his way at the Meiboom and had to turn back again. The same thing happened a third and a fourth time. By the fourth time the man was fed up with the game. He suspected that the strange fellow had something to do with it and decided to use his revolver if he lost his way again. On reaching the Meiboom, the man did as he had said and fired a revolver shot. The next moment it was as if a curtain was drawn back. The man could find his bearings again and got home without further trouble.
162698: A man who had gone to play cards by the calvary in Otegem saw a nun walking through the ditch on his way home in the evening. Because the man saw the same thing again the next day, he went to consult the parish priest. The priest asked the man and his family whether they had promised anything. The mother had indeed promised Masses for her husband, but she had not yet had them said. After the Masses had been said, the apparition was never seen again.
162702: On a farm the tables and chairs were always dancing. The farmhand who worked there had been bewitched. After the fathers had read prayers over the farm, everything returned to normal.
162728: A boy's father would not let him accept candy from a certain woman, because she might bewitch him.
162732: Some boys on a farm kicked at a mewing cat. A little later the place was swarming with cats, so that the boys could not go any further. After the boys had made the sign of the cross, the cats had vanished.
162733: A woman coming back from church walked in the footprints of a sorceress. Not ten steps further, the sorceress stopped and asked the woman whether she would like some snuff.
162741: Some women could bewitch children. When such a person had touched a child, the child began to cry and got 'the old man'. When the dean came to read prayers over bewitched children, he sweated a great deal.
162756: A woman was sewing in the kitchen when a pedlar woman came by. The pedlar patted the woman on the shoulder and said: "Buy a nice piece of cloth from me!" After that the woman fell ill. She had to go on pilgrimage to be cured.
162781: A woman who worked on a farm heard sounds at night as if someone were churning butter, making bobbin lace and throwing clogs. When people went to look, strangely enough there was nothing to be seen. When one night the woman heard noise beside her bed, she saw a white goat walking across the attic floor. A little later the goat disappeared through the closed attic window. Afterwards the house stood empty for a long time. The new occupants had a child with a mental disability.
162795: Near Wevelgem an ugly little old woman lived alone in a cottage. Because she had a crooked back and went begging everywhere, people said she was a witch. For fear that the witch would bewitch the animals, people never dared refuse to give her something.
162806: Some boys always called an old woman a sorceress. When the boys had to help bring in the harvest, they drove their cart over the Slijpe bridge. Meanwhile they shouted at the witch again, who was approaching in the distance. The next moment the cart overturned, and all the grain ended up in the water.
162816: When people could not die and were in a lot of pain, the priest was sent for. After all, it was believed that the devil had a hand in it. As soon as the priest was with the dying person, he found peace.
162826: A man on his way home met a woman who could work magic. The sorceress asked the man: "Aren't you afraid?", to which the man answered no. A little further on the man saw a goat that jumped up at him and rubbed against his knees. At that the man became so frightened that he ran home as fast as he could.
162833: In Lichtervelde a woman had said that she absolutely wanted to marry a certain man, alive or dead. After her death the woman came to haunt because she had not yet married the man. The priest had to join the woman and that man in marriage. After that the woman no longer came to haunt.
162842: Some dead people had to return to point out the place where they had hidden their money.
162843: The friars noticed that part of their stock of peas was regularly being stolen. One Sunday morning around five o'clock, one of the friars went to see whether anything suspicious was happening. When the friar saw the thief at work, he used his magic power and bewitched the man to stay fixed to the ground. Only after high mass was the thief set free again.
162867: Roesschaert was a tormenting spirit that could take on various shapes. Sometimes he turned himself into a dog or a cat in order to torment the fishermen. In the dunes stood an old hut in which a witch lived. Everyone was afraid of that witch and no one dared walk past her house. When the house was washed away during a heavy storm, the people were relieved. A little later, however, they saw in the dunes a little black dog with bells around its neck, which kept growing bigger and cried: "Roes! Roes!"
162869: On the Eiland in Harelbeke stood a farm where a baby lay in the cradle with a dummy in its mouth. Every night a cat appeared and stole the dummy. One night someone managed to stab the cat in the eyes with a fork. The next day it was seen that a woman from the neighbourhood had lost an eye.
162870: A brush seller coming home at night saw a large ghost on the road and said: "If you don't go away, I'll set the dogs on you!" The ghost, however, kept following the man until he was home. There the ghost kept hovering in front of the man so that he could not go in. Only after a long time did the figure disappear and could the man open the door. People had always advised that man to come and live in that house, because it was believed to be haunted. The man stayed there only a year. After three of his sons had fallen ill and died, the man moved to Poperinge.
162888: In Beveren-Leie lived a witch of whom everyone was afraid. A mother on her way to be churched met the witch on the road and could not go on. The witch had used her books of magic to fix the woman to the ground by magic.
162932: On a farm an old farmer's wife lived with her son and her daughter-in-law. The daughter-in-law did not get along with her and often said: "Are you praying again?" The old woman would answer: "Yes, I am going to pray three more Our Fathers so that I may come back after my death." When the old woman had been dead for two years, the daughter-in-law heard noise in a room when she went to make the beds. That same evening a blind calf was born on the farm.
162939: A farmer's wife who was ridden by the mare every night was advised by someone to lay a knife on her belly. She followed the advice and the next day found that the cowherd who slept in the horse stable had a wound on his belly.
162943: In the past there were cats all around the castle of Rumbeke. In reality they were people who had turned themselves into cats. Passers-by were stopped there and became so oppressed that they could not move a foot. Sometimes people got lost. It also happened that the cats spoke to someone and the next moment had vanished without a trace.
162960: When a man grabbed at torches in the air, he found he was holding an arm or a leg of a dead person.
162984: In Oudenburg lived a German woman whose house was haunted. Every evening around five o'clock the stove poker began to rattle. The woman was ridden by the mare at night. When the priest came to read prayers over the woman, he advised her to lay her rosary in front of her bed.
162985: In Uitkerke lived a heavily pregnant woman who was about to give birth. On the same day one of the cows was due to calve. While the men were with the cow in the stable, a rat kept running back and forth under the roof. One of the men took his gun and shot at the animal. When the man went inside a little later, his wife had lost a leg.
162991: A child born out of wedlock was ridden by the mare every night between twelve and one o'clock. The child was then thrown up against the ceiling, only to fall down again a moment later. The mother had prayers read over the child, but it did not help. In the end the child died.
162996: In Steenkerke there was a bridge that had to be raised when a ship came by. The woman at the bridge raised it, although she could easily have let the priest, who was just arriving, through first. But the woman could not stand the priest. The clergyman made a detour and crossed the water by another bridge. When the priest came back, the woman was still standing by the bridge as if nailed to the ground. The clergyman said: "Now you may go home".
163014: A farm in Rollegem was bewitched by the farmhand who worked there. In the mornings the horses stood sweating. The animals could not even pull an empty cart.
163018: In a house, a horse could always be heard stamping at twelve or one o'clock at night, although there was nothing to be seen. The priest claimed that these strange noises were caused by the previous occupant, who had hanged himself.
163021: A man on his way home met at least a thousand rats along the way. They were rats that someone had sent.
163024: In the 'toveressekot' (witch's hovel) in Ghyvelde there were black ants everywhere at night. During the day the creatures could not be seen. The ants were even in the little child's mouth. In the 'toveressekot' lived a woman who always wore a white pointed cap.
163041: A farmhand who had to pass an embankment every day saw there one morning a willow with a good thousand white cats in it. The man ran home as fast as he could. He did not even have the chance to open the front door; he literally knocked the door flat. Then the man went with a farmer to the place of the trouble. The two men took a stick to hit the cats with. When the men came to the willow, not a single cat was to be seen. But all the leaves had fallen from the tree.
163064: In Merkem lived a man with special powers. At a crossroads this man met the priest and turned himself into a bush. The priest urinated on the bush, so the wizard got wet and took on his human form again. One day the wizard had turned himself into a cat lying under the stove to avoid the doctor.
163067: Witches could turn themselves into an animal. A man who shot at a hare found that his gun did not work. On his way home the man fired into the air again as a test. Oddly enough, the gun did work then. Someone advised the man to crush a silver half-franc coin and put it in the gun. The man did not dare to try it, however.
163084:
In Waardamme lived a woman who could bewitch children, but she herself claimed that it was not true.
People who were bewitched went to the fathers of Steenbrugge, who gave them a medal to put on their plate.
163089: After someone had died in Manderens (?), a coffin appeared in the orchard every night. One night the people said: "If you are sent by God, say so!" The coffin then answered: "I am sent by God. You said you would go and serve, and you have not yet done it!"
163091: A man was always ridden by the mare around four o'clock in the morning. The man felt his bed shaking and could no longer breathe. He felt the blankets being pulled away, but in the morning the blankets lay normally again. For four nights in a row the man was ridden by the mare. In reality it was a stoppage of the blood.
163093: A farmer could not get away with his horses because of a witch.
163120: In Langemark lived a woman who could make people stand still by the lane leading to the inn 'de Kwakkel'.
163146: A woman from Cassel went to Vlamertinge with her eldest son. Although there were no trees to be seen anywhere, the boy bumped his head against a tree trunk on the way. When the boy came home he had a bump as big as an egg on his forehead. "That wouldn't have happened to me!" said the boy's father. The next moment the father slid down the stairs and got a herniated disc in his back.
163170: On a farm in Herzele there was a horse that was bewitched. Whenever that horse had to pass a certain house, it refused to go on and walked along the dyke. People were convinced that the woman living in that house had bewitched the horse.
163190: A woman had a baby that cried all the time because it was tormented by a woman who came to visit every day. That woman pricked the child with pins.
163206: A house in Otegem was haunted after a man had hanged himself there. Around 1957 a man came all the way from Moeskroen to that house to hang himself there too. The owner of the house died in an accident in 1967.
163210: If the fishermen saw a black cat when they had to go to sea, they believed they would have bad luck.
163213: A witch who always walked about on the quay cursed the fishermen who gave her no fish.
163214: Some people from Harelbeke went on a pilgrimage for children suffering from a heart disease and from an inflammation of the stomach and intestines. On the way the people came across fighting cats. A man who struck at the animals lost his arm.
163217: A man was returning from the fair in Uitkerke around midnight. Near Sint-Job the man saw two white figures, one metre tall, floating above the ground. The figures floated along with the man as far as Houtave, where they disappeared. They looked like two white angels.
163246: A woman who was often visited by a neighbour went to the fathers because she had a pain. The fathers read prayers over the woman until they were drenched in sweat. The woman was given blessed rose petals to put in her drink three times a day. Then she had to pray. One night when the woman was in great pain again, she got up and looked out of the window. At that very moment she saw the neighbour walking to her house. Later the woman was cured thanks to the fathers' help.
163256: A woman innkeeper could work magic. If a carter tried to drive past the inn without having a drink, he met with misfortune on the way; the cart overturned or a wheel came off. No carter dared to drive past the inn without going in for a drink.
163266: When the grandchildren went to clean the house of their recently deceased grandmother, they found a cradle full of lice there. About the two candlesticks and the two cushions the woman had left, the priest said: "You must not take that home before I have come by." The priest prayed in front of the oven until the drops of sweat dripped from his face. When the priest had finished praying, he said: "You may safely buy that house now, because the vermin is out."
163271: On her way to work, a working woman always met a woman who went to sleep in Zarren and carried a stick. One day the working woman asked her why she always took a stick with her. The woman answered: "This stick is for beating black cats to death, because they are wicked women who turn themselves into cats."
163278: Every morning a black cat walked through the classrooms of the girls' school. Although all the windows and doors were shut, the cat always got back in. The clergy sent for the parish priest, who came to say a few prayers. At that the cat ran off and drowned in a well. A little later an old woman passed by who was suspected of witchcraft.
163289: In a street in Pittem stood a haunted house where all kinds of noises were heard in the cellar every evening. People believed they were returned souls.
163319: Three women became clairvoyant when they tied three black cats to the table.
163323: In the past, when people could not churn butter, they believed the milk was bewitched. In reality the cows had 'de brand' (?).
163350: Every evening a large spider hung behind the stove in a woman's house. When they tried to catch the spider, it crept away. The people began to pray, and a little later they did manage to throw the spider into the stove. At that moment a woman who lived four houses away lay burning in her bed!
163365: A young man coming back at night from visiting his girlfriend in Wijgmaal was followed by a cat. He gave the creature a kick so that it rolled off the verge. The next day his girlfriend's mother had scratches all over her face. People believed that woman was a witch.
163394: Two young ladies walked past a Duitse schaper (German shepherd, a travelling shepherd thought to have magical powers) without greeting the man. A little later the shepherd saw the girls coming back and said: "Why are you turning back?" The girls answered: "How can we go anywhere like this? We are completely full of lice!" The shepherd answered: "Go on then, but next time show a little respect for old people and say good day to them!"
163413: A woman was full of lice after a witch had bumped into her.
163422: Near the Canadien stood a remote house called 'het kloppertje' (the little knocker), because its former occupant had returned as a knocking spirit. One night the priest, together with a man carrying a walnut stick, sat in the house to drive the spirit away. At midnight the door opened and an ugly man appeared with his arms spread. The priest fainted with fear. The other man then chased the knocking spirit out of the house. But the knocking never disappeared completely. When it was no longer heard in the house, it had moved to a small shed behind the house.
163441: A drunkard who rang the curate's doorbell as a prank stuck to the doorbell.
163448: The mare was a hand that seized people by the throat.
163460: In Moere lived a man who had sold his soul to the devils. When that man stood at a crossroads at night, he got as much money as he wanted.
163468: A man went into a house where the woman was home alone. "Is nobody home?" the man asked, and the woman replied: "Can't you see, I'm home. I know you've come for my daughter, but you won't get to see her!" The woman pushed the man and the man pushed back. As he left, the man felt he was going to fall ill. So, to be safe, he went on pilgrimage to Hulst. In the end the man did not fall ill.
163474: A man was buried in Beveren. A woman from the village attended every funeral that took place. At the end of the service the coffin fell crooked into the ground. Since there was no way to straighten the coffin, the people had no choice but to go home. They were convinced that the woman had bewitched the coffin.
163480: One evening a farmer met a gentleman with goat's legs. The gentleman knew that the farmer had no money to build a new barn for his cattle. If the farmer would sign a piece of parchment in blood, the gnomes would come at night to build him a barn, which would be finished before the cock crowed in the morning. That evening the farmer told his wife what had happened to him. The farmer's wife understood at once that the devil was involved, and she thought up a trick. At midnight a great many gnomes began building the barn. Towards morning the farmer's wife got up and imitated the crowing of a cock. This woke the cock, and it began to crow as well. At that moment the barn was not yet finished. On the east side there was still a large hole. The bricklayers tried several times to close the hole, but they never succeeded.
163493: A man travelling with a cart suddenly could not go on. After the man had poured some holy water over the cart, the problem was solved.
163505: In a house near the Prume a man woke one night to the blowing of the wind. When the man opened the window, he could hardly get it shut again because the wind was so strong. In the distance the man heard bottles being smashed. The man went to look, but there was not a single shard of glass to be found.
163513: Some people who were baking bread saw a witch pass by and began to mock her. The witch then said: "Go ahead and laugh, soon you will laugh even more!" The bread in the oven would not bake. When the people went to the parish priest for advice, the clergyman said: "The woman responsible for the misfortune will pass your house again. If you leave her alone, nothing more will go wrong." And so it happened.
163522: Two girls walking home together had seen ghosts in the shape of little soldiers.
163527: During the war some soldiers had to cross the Spermalie bridge in Sint-Pieterskapelle to get to the front. At that bridge there always sat a woman who said: "This far and no further." Because of this the soldiers could not get across that bridge in any way.
163535: On a farm in Zedelgem they could no longer churn butter. After a man had poured a bucket of liquid manure into the butter churn, there were no more problems with churning. The sorceress's milk, on the other hand, turned into liquid manure.
163544: A woman who lived on the Sterre (a corner by the market of Koekelare) saw a horse walking there in the evening.
163561: A farmer from Ardooie went to the fair in Oostrozebeke. At the fair the farmer saw an innkeeper's wife. He greeted her and was surprised that she was still at the fair. When the farmer went home, he stopped at the inn. The innkeeper's wife was there pouring beer!
163602: At the Waterkasteel in Loppem a coach without horses was always seen passing at midnight. Many people who went to an inn near the castle took a detour of as much as three quarters of an hour because they did not dare to go home past that castle.
163613: A widow was visited by her dead husband and said: "Are you coming to sleep with me again?", to which the ghost answered: "No." The woman had promised to have Masses said and had not kept that promise.
163614: A woman always gave a piece of bread, a little lard and five centimes to a beggar woman who came by regularly. When the woman was lying in childbed, she could not go to the door to give the beggar something. The woman's little daughter had no money, and she heard the beggar say: "I wish all your cows lay with their legs in the air and all died. May you never have any luck again." From then on those people always had bad luck. A cow or a pig was regularly found dead. In the end the people had to leave their house because they had become so poor.
163636: A young man had seduced an underage girl. After mass this young man never wanted to stop and talk to the girl. The priest, however, bewitched the young man, so that he was forced to stay and wait for the girl after mass.
163656: A farm in Veldegem was haunted. The strangest things happened there.
163664: Every night a ghostly priest came to say mass in a church. The priest always said "Kyrie Eleison" three times, but nobody answered. Then the priest went back to the sacristy. One night someone sat in the church and answered three times: "Lord, have mercy on us". After the priest had said "Kyrie Eleison", the man answered: "Christe Eleison". The priest was released.
163673: Witches were easy to recognise in church: if you stood at the back of the church and looked through a blessed wedding ring, you could see the witches sitting with their backs to the altar.
163678: A mother with a child was often visited by a woman from Eggewaartskapelle. As soon as that woman had left, the child always began to cry loudly. The parish priest advised the mother not to let that woman in any more, since she had magical powers.
163687: A family had a son who was ill and would no longer eat. When they took the child to the parish priest, the clergyman read prayers over the boy and predicted that the woman who was the cause of the evil would come by. They were, however, not allowed to harm her.
163712: A sailor had to run an errand at the captain's wife's house. When he arrived, the sailor heard the woman scheming with some others. The women said: "I know when the ship sails. We will make them all disappear." The sailor told everything he had heard to the parish priest, who gave him this advice: "At midnight you will see high waves coming. If you then make the sign of the cross with holy water, you will see the waves disappear again." When the sailor went on board, he demanded of the captain that he be allowed to stand on the bridge at midnight. In this way the sailor managed to avert the disaster. When they came home, the seamen found that their wives had been split in two.
163722: A woman had to look after the children in someone else's house. At a certain moment a sorceress came by and called: "Open up!" But the woman did not, because she realised that the sorceress was out to harm the children.
163728: Some boys were playing marbles by a little hole in the street. One of them said, "Instead of marbles I can make mice come out of that hole." Three times mice were indeed seen crawling out of the hole. Because the boys told at school what had happened, the parish priest also heard about the strange affair. When the boys were playing marbles again one day, one of them called to the priest, "Father, come and look! Here's a boy who can make mice!" The priest saw that it was true and said, "Well, that's nice. Do it again!" Through the priest's power and prayer, the boy could no longer make mice appear after that.
163740: The Lourdes chapel was haunted. Hares and little rabbits always ran about there that nobody could catch. At midnight a young lady walked there, going as far as the mill. The sails of the mill turned at a slant, and strangely enough there were also little sails.
163781: Two women went into the woods to gather dry wood. At a certain moment they met someone and asked: "What are you doing here?" The stranger answered: "Gathering dry wood for the fire. And you?" One of the women explained that she was doing the same. When that woman wanted to light the fire that evening, her skirt caught fire. If she had not taken off her skirt so quickly, she would have burned up completely.
163789: People ridden by the mare felt something hairy pressing down on them. Those people could not find their bearings and also grew very thin. Anyone who was a victim of the mare had to go to the friars.
163791: A woman could make mice by taking a lump of earth in her hand and blowing on it.
163807: A woman who was always visited by a neighbour had a child that cried all the time. Her sister advised her to go to the friars of Steenbrugge. The next morning at four o'clock the woman set off with her sister and her child to the friars. The two women took off their shoes so that the neighbour would not hear them leaving on pilgrimage. When the friar read prayers over the child, he was drenched in sweat. The friar advised the women to say nothing if they met the neighbour on their return. When the neighbour asked on the way back: "Why did you leave so early?", the women gave no answer. In the end the neighbour moved away. The child recovered. The neighbour must have given the child the evil hand when she had taken off her wedding ring to knead bread.
163815: In the past there were many women who bewitched children. A mother from Woumen had a child of eight months old. When the child was eleven months old, it had become five kilos lighter. The mother went with her child to the friars of Ieper. Because of that the child recovered and eventually grew up into a man of eighty kilos.
163818: During the war a priest who was saying mass was murdered on a farm. The priest's spirit kept wandering at that spot in the form of a light that could not be put out.
163835: A farmer carting hay had to pass the house of a witch. Every time the farmer passed there, the hay fell off his wagon. Every year the witch also turned over the first two furrows the farmer had ploughed.
163842: In a house in the Pannestraat in Voormezele all kinds of noises were heard at midnight. The clock rattled, the drawer fell out of the table by itself and the spoons and forks fell on the floor. The doors opened by themselves. When the people went to look, there was nobody to be seen and the doors were shut again.
163862: A bell from the church tower is said to have once sunk into the bell pit in the woods of Piers. At night that bell could be heard ringing.
163869:
A nurse had to look after a sick woman who was said to be a witch. In the supposed witch's house only a candle was burning. At night the woman said to the nurse: "Don't you hear anything, sister?" The sister heard nothing, but the woman went on: "If you hear something, you must not open your eyes." This remark made the nurse uneasy, and to be safe she hung her rosary on the door. At midnight the nurse heard a loud bang against the door. It was as if a horse had run into it. Ten minutes later the same thing happened again. The nurse turned on the light but saw nothing. The next day the nurse said to the woman: "You are not ill. I am not staying here." The woman tried to stop her, but the nurse would not be talked round. The nurse left, and the witch's neighbour helped her carry her suitcases. After the two women had walked a little way, they were both out of breath. When the nurse took hold of her rosary, she came to her senses again.
Later that witch was murdered by someone.
163875: In the horse stable of a farm a white ghost was always seen walking on the manger. A friar had to be called in to exorcise the evil. The farmer's son had diarrhoea because of the haunting.
163898: On a farm a dead man came to haunt, looking for his hidden money. Masses are still said every day for Schoendale.
163909: A woman could turn herself into a pig. One day the pig was beaten. The next day the woman lay injured in bed.
163919: A witch lived along a dirt road in Westrozebeke. On Sundays a painter always went to the fair with a little cart of tobacco, cigars and cigarettes. When the man drove his cart past the witch's house, she was leaning with her elbows on the hedge. The man said to the witch: "Lovely weather, isn't it!" She replied: "Yes, you'd better hurry to get to Passendale, or you won't get there at all." Fifty metres further on, the man's cart fell apart. So the man was forced to return home.
163938:
A woman married to a pedlar always rode with her husband in a little cart full of nails and other tools. One day in Ursel that woman stroked a little child on the head, saying: "Ah, my good little child." The child then began to cry. Two days later the child was dead.
A girl had to look after her little sister while her mother was at the shop. The sorceress came to visit and stroked the little sister on the head. Two days later the child died of 'de oude man' (the old man, a wasting illness).
163953: A farmer was always troubled by a dog. One day the man went to a witch who might be able to help him. On the way the farmer met a dog. He kicked the dog in the snout, and the animal dropped dead. When the farmer got home, he found that his neighbour woman was dead. She had the same scars on her nose as the dog had had.
163977: In a house in Bambeke a witch had bewitched the children. The little boys did nothing but cry and became dehydrated. The children's parents then had to go on pilgrimage to Roesbrugge. Since the Gospel of Saint John has been read after Mass, such evil no longer exists.
164009: Seven people were sitting in the castle lane one Sunday afternoon. Suddenly a man dressed in black came by and took a note from his pocket. When the man had read out a certain formula, the people could leave again.
164015: In Nieuwpoort lived a sorceress whom everyone feared. At night the woman often sat on her doorstep in a hooded cloak.
164017: The Blinde Kapelle in Heestert is said to have been built on the spot where a church once sank. For a long time the bells of that church were heard ringing at night or even during the day. When a chapel had been built on that spot, the ringing of the bells was no longer heard.
164032: A man out hunting saw a wild duck. The man shot at the animal three times, but each time the duck flew away. When the man had shot for the fourth time, he no longer saw the duck fly away. The man went to look, but there was no trace of the duck.
164043: A mayor's house was haunted. The horses died and there was constant misfortune. One day a dove was shot down with a blessed wedding ring put in the gun. Later a woman from the neighbourhood was found dead and completely naked in her bed.
164051: People had the custom of placing burning candles in the churchyard on All Souls' Day. That is why it was often thought that little souls came haunting the churchyard.
164060: People ridden by the mare could not breathe or call out. One could hear the mare coming in by the door. On waking, victims of the mare had severe heart palpitations.
164069: A man was working on a dyke when a thunderstorm suddenly broke. The man quickly fled to a small chapel to stay dry. A little later a woman came to stand next to him and said: "I don't suppose you could carry my basket a little way?" The man carried the basket a short distance, but he immediately broke out in a sweat because the basket was as heavy as lead. Strangely enough, the basket was empty.
164083: A hunter who had shot at a hare suddenly saw a woman with a gunshot wound standing right in front of him.
164088: A priest was threatened by three robbers and asked what they were going to do with him. "Stay here until I come back," said the priest, and he went to a nearby café, where he treated everyone to a glass of beer. Then the priest said to three men: "Go and take a look a bit further on. There are three robbers standing there. You must say: 'Are you coming?'" The priest had fixed the robbers to the ground by magic.
164109: During the procession of Rozebeke some shy girls went to the fair. The Duitse schaper (German shepherd, a travelling shepherd thought to have magical powers) met the girls and greeted them. One of the girls laughed, another answered: "Good day!" and others said nothing. The annoyed shepherd replied: "If you don't say good day, you won't be in Rozebeke for long." The girls had only just arrived in the dance hall when they felt itchy all over. Some girls found they had lice, but there were also some who had nothing at all. Four girls were forced to go back home. On the way they met the shepherd and said: "We are going back home, because we are full of lice." To that the Duitse schaper replied: "Go back to Rozebeke, but if you see a shepherd again, greet him just as the other girls did. You will have seen that those others have no lice!"
164147: A man ridden by the mare felt a tightness around his heart. To protect oneself against the mare, one had to place one's clogs under the bed heels first.
164162: A witch could make mice appear by throwing a few blades of grass on the ground.
164164: Anyone who wanted to avoid being ridden by the mare at night had to put his clogs beside his bed instead of under it.
164177: In 1921 people in a house in Roesten called in the priest because they always heard knocking there. A sick child lay on a mattress on the floor. The priest saw that the child was secretly knocking on the floor under the blankets.
164192: On the border of East and West Flanders stood a stone called 'de Lange Pee'. There used to be a wood there that was badly haunted. People were so frightened that they went and sat on that stone.
164200: A ship was never christened on a Friday or a holiday. Otherwise nothing but skulls would be caught on that ship.
164204: A farmer's wife was often ridden by the mare when she lay on her back. She would then see two horses coming and say to the farmer: Quick, throw two buckets of water at those horses!
164220: In the past, black cats were often not animals but sorceresses in animal form!
164228: In Ettelgem lived a wizard who could turn himself into a dog.
164240: Children who were always crying were in fact being ridden by the mare. Such children were taken to the friars.
164250: A woman who could do witchcraft could turn herself into a hare. When someone shot that hare in the eye, the woman lost her eye.
164256: The water castle in Loppem was haunted. It was said that passers-by were pulled into the moat there. In reality, of course, they could also have been drunkards who fell into the water.
164270: The French convent of Moorsele was haunted. The woman who lived in the convent had promised to erect a Calvary by the church, but she had never kept that promise. After the woman's death, chains were heard rattling in the convent and windows and doors slamming. After the nuns had made a novena, the haunting came to an end.
164276: A man coming home around midnight saw a goat with a long chain. That was witchcraft.
164277: On Christmas night, around midnight, near the toverput (magic well), a pond in Gullegem, bells could be heard ringing and starlings screeching. There were so many starlings that one could hardly see anything. Then singing was heard, followed by a sermon of which nothing could be understood.
164301: In a village the new priest was welcomed with music. The clergyman said: "There is much evil here, but I will take it all away." By the next day the priest had already taken fifty-two books of magic from the people. The day after, the clergyman went to fetch the last book of magic from a sorcerer in the village. The sorcerer had set out two glasses of wine in advance. The priest came in and said: "I have heard that you have books here that you really should not have." The sorcerer replied: "First we will drink a glass of wine." The priest sat down and drank the wine he was offered. The sorcerer said to the clergyman: "Don't think you will get those books from me. Now I would like you to leave." But the priest could not get up from his chair. "You see, Father, you may have studied a lot; I can do even more, and I do no one any harm with these tricks."
164305: In Brugge there was a haunted house for which no tenant could be found. Every night a man in a nightcap appeared at one of the windows. One day someone found the nightcap behind a built-in cupboard. After the cap had been burned, the haunting was over.
164306: A man who had just died came knocking on the door of his wife, now alone, every evening.
164309: The nails of an Easter candle had been blessed four times. One day some altar boys had stuck a piece of an Easter nail under the threshold of the church. After mass four women could not leave the church. "My godmother is one of them!" cried one of the altar boys. When the priest saw what was going on, he shouted angrily: "Take that away!" After that the witches could leave the church without difficulty.
164314: A married couple lived along the Drieweg near the Lokedieze in Kortemark. That farm was haunted. At night a little candle was often seen burning there and sounds were heard as if someone were threshing. The daughter was sometimes thrown against the cupboard by an invisible force. The cows stood with their heads clamped between their forelegs and the two horses were often drenched in sweat. After the friars of Ieper had been called in, things improved somewhat. When the lease ran out, those people moved away all the same.
164316: 'Klinkaard' used to roam the streets of Waregem often. It was a large dog that accompanied people walking at night. If you threw something at the dog, you could never hit it. A little chapel was hung on a tree in one street to make sure Klinkaard would do no more harm.
164326: Whoever met a black cat would have unlucky days.
164333: Between Zwevezele and Ruddervoorde stood a house that was bewitched. The boys who came to visit the sorceress's daughters in that house got their ears boxed, although no one could be seen. When the boys were in that house, they saw the plates on the mantelpiece dance. At the neighbours' the animals died and the children fell ill.
164334: On a farm in Esen a man was lifted up by his beard at night to the beams of the ceiling.
164355: A boy who was always ridden by the mare at night let his hand hang out of his bed to catch the mare. However, he did not succeed.
164381:
Anyone ridden by the Kokkemare could not call out or run away. In the morning the mare was gone. Anyone who wanted to protect themselves against the mare had to pray an Our Father and a Hail Mary before going to sleep and say:
Mare, mare, go and sail
through all the waters and through all the seas
through all the branches and all the trees
through all the little pipes of the straw roofs
before you come to touch my bed!
164385: A few people were sitting by the stove in the kitchen of a farm in winter. Suddenly the attic door was heard opening, and then heavy footsteps on the stairs. This had happened several times before. The shadow of the ghost could also be seen on the wall. After a friar had said some masses for the dead person, it no longer appeared.
164429:
Anyone ridden by the mare wanted to call out but could not. Victims of the mare felt something hairy.
That hair could of course also have been the blanket they slept under.
164453: A woman driving two carts of fruit to Ichtegem had to pass a witch's house. At that spot the cart overturned, so that all the fruit fell on the ground.
164478: Some poachers went to the 'rotte bos' (rotten wood) on the evening of All Saints' Day. Suddenly the poachers saw a whole herd of horses running along the lane. The poachers lit a light to lure the hares. Instead of hares, lots of cats appeared in front of the lamp.
164502: People who could not sleep at night said they had been ridden by the mare. That was superstition.
164505:
A man whose pigs would no longer grow called in a healer. After the healer had been in the sty for a while, he said to the man: "When you have bought a pig at the market, you must not show it to anyone afterwards." When the man followed that advice, he could keep pigs again. A witch had been responsible for the evil.
A man from Otegem who was going home one day with two pigs met a witch who laid her hand on one of the animals. After that, that one animal would not grow any more, but the other did.
164510: Sorceresses could make a child cry all day long. Such children were usually taken to the friars to have prayers read over them.
164516: A carter from Staden or Roeselare came to fetch wood in Beselare every week or every two weeks. On the way the carter always saw a white lady with cats. One day someone advised the man to address the woman with the words: "If you are sent by God, speak. If you are sent by the devil, be gone". The man did so and promptly got a blow in the face. After that the carter never saw that woman again.
164517: A man walking to the sea met a funeral procession in the Kaaistraat. When the man reached his ship, he saw that the quay was full of little chicks. The man put the chicks in a basket and went aboard. On the ship the man opened the basket and saw that devils were jumping out of it. The man was scared to death.
164544: On the Beverhoutsveld in Beernem there were thousands of rats destroying the harvest. When the people complained about the plague of rats after mass, the priest said: "Come on, go home, that's all nonsense." The next night someone had to go to Beernem at two o'clock to fetch the doctor. That man saw the curate walking around the field, praying. The next day not a single rat was to be seen.
164547: A nun who had been transferred to another convent always heard noises on the attic stairs there at night. It seemed as if someone were walking up and down all night long.
164548: At night in the woods a man often saw friars in white robes singing vespers. When one day he had the courage to come closer, the friars suddenly vanished and he heard the singing behind him.
164562: In the Meerlaan (1) in Gistel lived a woman who could work magic. If children stuck their tongues out at her, that woman could make them stand stock-still. Only after the woman had made a movement with her hand could the children move again.
164584: A farmer plagued by rats sent for a wizard. The wizard came to the farm and put one of the rats on his hand. Because the animal sat still, the wizard said to the farmer: "See, they're not so bad!" To the rat the wizard said: "You have eaten enough at this farmer's now. Go on to that other one. You can get there along that furrow." A little later the rats walked in a line along the furrow to another farm.
164587: A big cat sat in the churchyard of Wijtschate every evening. Because of this, no one dared to walk past that place any more.
164603: On a bewitched farm in Heule strange noises were always heard. When the friar came to read prayers over the farm, he said: "I cannot drive out the evil, but I will put it on the apple tree." After that no more strange things happened on the farm, but that tree never bore another apple. The farmer's wife's sister-in-law was responsible for the evil. After the friar's visit she never came to the farm again.
164633: People often took sick children to the priests. They were then given a small loaf to fight a heart illness. While the priests read prayers over the child, its clothes fell to the ground. Those clothes were not to be picked up. Then it could be seen that the child was being pricked all over by needles.
164636: A woman had a daughter of two and a half years old. When the girl was playing outside, an old woman came by and gave her a sugar sweet she had made herself. The child eagerly ate the sweet. The following night at twelve o'clock the girl sat up in her bed and cried: "Save me, save me, she is there!" The child fell ill. The parish priest did not know what to do. When the child had been ill for five weeks, a friar came to visit, read prayers over the child and then said: "This afternoon at three o'clock you must pray and spread your arms, wherever you are." The woman did what the clergyman had advised. At a certain moment the child cried that it was hungry and had to vomit. In the child's vomit the mother found a long grey hair. The old woman had bewitched the girl because she wanted that mother's son to have to go into the army. The boy had been exempted from military service because there were still four underage children at home. The witch's son did have to go into the army. The parish priest advised the mother not to speak to the witch, since she had power over the whole family. The mother laid a paasnagel (an Easter nail, a blessed nail) under the door. She then also realised that her two eldest sons, who had died at the age of seven months after their bellies had turned blue, had likewise been victims of the witch.
164643: In Waregem lived a witch who made a farmer's pigs die and sent a plague of rats to the farm's attic. Two children also died on the farm. Every time the farmer's wife wanted to breastfeed her youngest child, a hellish noise sounded in the attic. As soon as she put her child back in its little chair, it was quiet.
164659: Every evening at about the same time, a woman saw a cat with a large head appear. However the woman tried to hit the cat, she could not touch the animal.
164660: In Sint-Jan lived a small old woman who had a speech impediment. Everyone was afraid of that woman, who sat in the street all night. A man who always went to fetch rabbits in Kemmel and Reningelst had to pass the German cemetery. Because that old woman stood by the cemetery, the man's horse could not go on. One day the man was visiting a friend when he suddenly said: "Look there!" All over the yard little white and black dogs were jumping about, and a moment later they had vanished. These strange events were caused by that old woman; she had many books of magic.
164672: People claimed that doodkeersen (death candles, ghostly lights) were cursed dead who came back.
164695: On a farm the people were plagued by a cat that always crept into the milk tub. One day the farmer's wife poured a bowl of hot water over the animal, which began to scream. The next day a woman from the neighbourhood was seen whose face was completely burned.
164696: Strange things happened on the Barsdamkruusstrate. Whatever people took with them to the field always overturned after sunset.
164724: Two women coming back from the fair in Aalter met a woman on the way. After that the two women got lost, so that they were still not home late in the evening. The two women had been bewitched by the woman they had met.
164729: In Aalbeke lived a sorceress from Ieper. In the neighbourhood of that sorceress's house people always had bad luck. For example, a girl had developed a heart disease. When someone went on pilgrimage for the child, a woman predicted that in three hours the child would leap up out of her bed. And so it was. Later the girl recovered.
164739: The mare was a black hand that made people unable to breathe.
164745: A man who had robbed everyone during his life had died. At night the heirs always heard noises in the man's former room. After a medium had made contact with the soul, the children asked: "Father, are you unhappy?", to which a voice answered: "Boys, keep what you have and I will suffer what I feel". The dead also returned if they had hidden something somewhere.
164747: Three men were coming back from the fair in Vlamertinge. At the Middelburg (1) it suddenly began to rain hard. Two of the men said to the third: "You're lucky, you're almost home. But it's not that far for us either." The third man replied: "We'll see about that." At five o'clock in the morning those two men were still walking around in the rain.
164760: A man went to a witch to fetch a basket to put chicory in. In the witch's house the man saw rats all over the floor, so that he did not know where to put his feet.
164787: The horses would no longer pull the cart after a woman had given the animals the evil hand.
164791: You could hear the mare come in. Once a man waited under the blankets with a drawn knife for the mare to come. If the mare fell, she would fall onto the knife. That time, however, the mare did not come.
164796: In 't Gavere the doodkeersen (death candles, ghostly lights) flew above the water from one post to another. Not everyone could see those lights. They were dead people who had returned.
164807: The house of a widow in Adegem was haunted. The animals died there and no butter could be churned any more. In the end the friars went to the house.
164816: In Sint-Joris there was a house where every evening howling and raging could be heard, together with the rattling of chains. When the door was opened, strangely enough there was nothing to be seen. The friars of Steenbrugge were called in to exorcise the house. The friar knelt down and began to pray until he was soaked in sweat. Then the friar said: "If you are sent by God, come in. If you are sent by the devil, go away." Only after the friar had repeated this formula three times was the knocking no longer heard. Then he opened the door and heard a man running away shouting and raging.
164817: A man from Roeselare had some pigs with which he paid his rent. But that man had a lot of bad luck with his animals. When the man got up one night, he saw a woman from Klerken sitting there, who sometimes came to spend the night in his house. The man went to the friars of Ieper for advice. The clergymen assured him that he need not worry, because the sorceress would never enter his house again. And so it was.
164837: Two men who were near the 'torrelen' heard the trampling of horses, although there was nothing to be seen.
164848: Every time a woman went to do the washing at her aunt's, she was accompanied by a cat. When the woman left the cat alone, nothing happened, but when she had hit the animal, something strange always happened.
164853: Through the window a woman saw a man going to the market with a basket to make butter. Suddenly the man dropped dead, and the basket flew some distance. When the woman was with the dead man's wife some time later, she went to the cellar, where that basket stood. The woman quickly went back upstairs, because she had seen the ghost of the dead man standing by the basket. An object that someone had with them when they died stayed with that person's ghost even after death.
164854: Every evening a will-o'-the-wisp was seen above a farm on the road to Bizet. It was a dead person who returned to purify himself for a time.
164859: The dean found it annoying that a certain woman always came to confession on Saturday evening. One day the dean said to the woman: "You'd better come a bit earlier. Women shouldn't be walking the streets late at night." The woman answered: "I'm not afraid of anything, Father Dean." When the woman went home, a horse followed her. In fear the woman ran around a tree, but the horse followed her the whole time. On leaving the wood, the woman saw that the horse had vanished. Perhaps that horse had been the dean!
164867: A doctor had sold his soul for ten years to the devil, who had appeared in the shape of a handsome gentleman in black clothes. The doctor made the little devils work so hard that three weeks before the end of the contract they were still willing to break the agreement. The doctor, however, did not want that. When the contract had expired, the doctor was found dead in his house one morning. The devils had beaten him so badly that his brains were stuck to the wall.
164874: A man from Beselare was in hospital because he had had to undergo an operation. He was visited by a woman from the village who had brought him eggs. As soon as the man had eaten those eggs, he was completely in that woman's power.
164888: In Westkapelle lived a woman who owned a book of magic. A fishwife noticed that this woman always secretly picked out the best fish. One day the fishwife said to the woman: "You are a rascal!" The next day the fishwife sold nothing, and moreover her horses would not move forward. After the fishwife had told the woman that from now on she could have the best fish again, the misfortune came to an end.
164908: In a village the priest sometimes came to haunt in the shape of a goat or a dog.
164919: In Dottenijs lived a woman in whose house a cat was always walking around. One day the woman was so fed up with the cat that she poured boiling water over it. The next day the woman heard that one of her neighbour women had been burned alive after boiling water had spilled over her.
164920: During her pregnancy a woman had spoken with a sorceress. That woman's child died. The friars gave the woman this advice: "If you are pregnant again, come here to have prayers read over you. Then that misery will be over!"
164928:
A mother whose first child had died was afraid when her second child fell ill. When the mother had gone to her churching, she had given change to a woman with a bad reputation. After that the child had begun to cry. It also had a mark on its upper arm. In the end the parents took the child to a healer in Waregem. When they were halfway, however, the horse began to limp. The man had to take his horse to the stable and borrow his cousin's horse. A little later the wheel axle caught fire, so that once again they could not go on. At his wits' end, the father went on foot to the healer and told him everything. For a few days there was improvement, but then the child's condition worsened again.
When they went to the friars for advice, the mark on the child's arm had disappeared. The clergyman read prayers over the child and then said to the parents: "If you have more children, you must dress them in blue until their seventh year." The following night there was a hellish noise in the house, as if everything was being thrown about. The child died the next day.
164934: A mother had a child with diarrhoea. Whenever the mother took the child to the hospital, all symptoms of the illness suddenly disappeared. As soon as they came home, the complaints returned. In the end the mother had prayers read over her child by the monks of the Sint-Sixtus Abbey in West-Vleteren. She believed that someone wanted to harm her child.
164944: A church with bells is said to have once sunk into the klokkenputten (bell pits) in Eernegem. Later people tried to bring those bells back up, but they did not succeed.
164962: On the border between Aalter and Maldegem a sow roamed with thirty or forty piglets. People said it was a ghost sow.
164973: People who had hidden money somewhere returned after their death. In the house of a dead man who had failed to keep a promise, noises were always heard.
164991: A mother who had been slapped by a woman was bewitched. Three of her children died of the 'plane' (1).
165017: In a house in Gullegem there was much misfortune. The children often fell ill there. One evening the man who lived there saw a sorceress crawl through the hedge and slip into the house through the garden. The man went after the sorceress, but he could not find her. At his wits' end, the man went to the friars. After much praying, the clergymen were able to say who the sorceress was.
165022: A woman always heard a ticking near the lamp in her house. When she went to look, however, there was nothing to be seen. After a friar had walked around the house, the woman heard nothing more.
165054: In an uninhabited building a little light was always seen at night. That was 'something' that came back to look for something hidden in the building.
165072: On a farm there was a newborn baby that cried and was in pain all over. People believed a witch was responsible for the misfortune. The witch pricked a piece of butter with a pin. With every pinprick the baby felt pain.
165095: The archers' wood of Sint-Anne used to be haunted. In windless weather the branches could sometimes suddenly be seen moving back and forth.
165098: A man coming back from the barber got lost near the Steenovenbos. Almost everyone got lost at that place.
165107: A farmer plagued by rats got help from a wizard, who said: "You must pray an Our Father for nine days." Although the farmer did not do so, the rats were gone nine days later. When the wizard visited again, he said to the farmer: "Well, why didn't you pray?" The wizard had had to do all the work himself.
165109: A witch had filled a farm in Wilskerke with fleas. The desperate inhabitants went to a clergyman, who advised them to go on pilgrimage to Nieuwkerke. After they had done so, the fleas were gone.
165127: Anyone ridden by the mare at night had to have a clergyman read prayers over them.
165130: A man met a woman and slapped her on the buttocks. At that the woman crowed like a rooster and then struck the man on the head. Where the woman's fingers had touched the man's head, white stripes could be seen. Those stripes did disappear later.
165142: Some people heard a dead relative strike the clock, although there was nothing to be seen. If a farmer had sold something at too low [high] a price, or had not given the correct weight, the dead sometimes returned to punish him.
165159: Opposite the presbytery was a café where many young people came. A black cat always sat by the presbytery. One day the road worker shot at the cat with a half-franc coin. The cat lost its eye and jumped over the stream to go home. The next day the road worker found that a woman from the neighbourhood had lost her eye.
165171: A farmer from Ingelmunster saw a goat come into his house and asked the animal: "What have you come here for?" The goat answered: "I've come to have a look at your house. Don't you mind?" Then the farmer cried: "Get out of here!" After that the animal vanished.
165225: On a farm in Ruddervoorde lay a horseshoe that came a little closer every year.
165241: Anyone ridden by the mare tried to resist but could do nothing, because they were seized by the throat. As soon as they woke up, they were freed from the mare. Some people claimed the mare was caused by eating certain things.
165246: A farmer's wife was visited by an old woman who stroked the piglets and said: "Lovely little animals." The next day the piglets were all dead.
165280: Anyone ridden by the kokkemare had to put their shoes upside down under the bed.
165297: At the separation of Church and state, the doors of the church in Halewijn were closed. The people wanted to open the doors, but they could not. At their wits' end, they went to a wizard from the village. The wizard stood in front of the church doors and called: "Open up! X has told you!" A moment later the doors flew open, although no one had opened them.
165317: A farm in Snellegem was haunted. At night people heard coal being thrown about in the barn. When they went to look, remarkably enough there was nothing to be seen. Since then paasnagels (Easter nails, blessed against evil) have been hung everywhere in the farm.
165333: A sick man saw a black dog walk into his room every day. The dog always came to lie in front of the bed. One day the man slashed at the animal's neck with a knife. The next day a farmhand was walking around the farm with a wound in his neck.
165338: Two farmhands working late in the evening in the smithy heard loud moaning outside. It was the smith's wife being ridden by the mare.
165342: If someone refused to kneel before a sorcerer, the sorcerer made sure that person could not move a foot.
165351:
On a farm in Vuylsteke music was heard in the cowshed in the evening. The cows would then start dancing and jumping with their tails in the air. In the end it even got to the point that the cows gave no more milk. The friars came to read prayers over the animals.
In the cowshed lay an object that had been put there by a woman with evil intentions. That object had to be burned in the stove.
165359: A farm where a man had murdered his wife was haunted. Near that farm, passers-by got lost, so that they did not get home until the next morning.
165365: On a hill where a mill stood, stalkeersen (ghostly lights) were always seen. They were ghosts.
165374: People who suffered from some ailment or other were said to have been ridden by the mare.
165388: At a clog maker's house a lot of noise was heard in the attic every evening. When people went to look in the evening, the attic trapdoor always fell shut. In the morning nothing unusual was to be found in the attic.
165398: A man had beaten a cat to death in his house. The next morning the neighbour woman lay dead.
165423:
On a summer day a man drove to the mill near the Rattevalle. Although there was no wind, the man's cap flew into the canal.
The woman (the witch?) lay in her bed for twenty years. Only at night did the woman get up. Whenever people passed her house, they always saw a light burning.
165429: Near an ash tree on a farm, a doodkaars (death candle, a ghostly light) was seen dancing back and forth. If something returned, it was a sign that money was buried in that spot.
165436: At the 'Blauwe Zwaan' there used to be a café that was haunted. Later a little chapel was built on that spot, after which the haunting stopped. That little chapel is no longer there.
165441:
A man from Rollegem knew a girl from Harelbeke.
One day that girl went to the fair with two friends. The girl said to her friends: "Today I want a sweetheart, even if it is the devil". On the way the three met a handsome young man, who gave the girl an apple. The girl bit into the apple and saw that the fruit was covered in blood. After that the girl was possessed by the devil. The girl was forced to do evil, causing people to drive into the water and the lining to fall out of their trousers.
When a friar had exorcised the girl, he said: "I will have to die". The clergyman began to pray until he was drenched in sweat, and he later died. The girl was cured, but she became as small as a child.
165444: An old beggar woman always came to a farm. When the farmer's wife had once chased the beggar woman away, the farmer said: "We will have bad luck." The farmer had to take grain to the mill with the horse and cart. After the horses had taken three steps, they refused to go on. The farmer went inside, took a knife and struck with it in front of the front wheels of the cart. At that moment he heard a scream. He went inside and saw that his wife had a broken leg. When the farmer set off, the horses started moving without effort.
165449: A man taking his sister to Halewijn by horse and cart met a German on the way, who asked: "Haben Sie nichts zu rauchen?" (Don't you have anything to smoke?) The man did not want to give the German a cigarette. The next moment, however, the man's horse stood still, so that he could not go on. At his wits' end, the man gave the German a cigarette after all. Then the horse started moving again.
165456: During a walk in the churchyard, the lord of the Keukaord castle kicked a skull and said: "If there is still life in you, come and eat with me tonight." That same evening the castle doorbell rang. The maid opened the door and saw a ghost with glowing eyes. Terrified, the maid slammed the door and told the lord what she had seen. It was the end of the lord, for he was cursed.
165490: Lange Jan was a tall man with whom one must not speak unless one wanted to end up with a broken neck. One Sunday evening around half past eight a boy was coming home. The boy deliberately went to the bowling lane because he had heard it was haunted there. In the middle of the lane he met a large horse, which walked along with him until he was home. Terrified and drenched in sweat, the boy told his mother what had happened.
165502: A farmer who could not churn butter sought advice from the priest to have prayers read over the milk. The clergyman said to the farmer: Tie brushwood around the butter churn. With every turn of the churn the witch responsible will receive a blow. She will be beaten black and blue. The farmer did as he was advised and so could make butter again. The next day a woman who had been beaten black and blue was walking around the village.
165513: Just before the war, a gamekeeper in Voormezele saw a fireball flying through the sky. The man saw the ball coming straight at him and a moment later it burst apart in the Kriekbos. The ball was a good fifty metres across. Just like comets, fireballs were also omens of a war.
165516: A farmer who went to wash at the pump at night dropped dead. After his death the farmer came back at night to look for his money. After a paasnagel (Easter nail) had been laid under the door on the priest's advice, the farmer no longer appeared.
165547: Some people returning from Diksmuide were followed by a cat. At a small chapel the cat ran off. When the people reached the church, the cat disappeared for good. It was believed to be a returned dead person.
165557: A man from Avelgem who had sold his soul to the devil went to the dean because he wanted his soul back. When the dean held a church service for the man, the devil could be heard in the churchyard shouting that the man was a coward. The dean had to exert himself so hard that the sweat stood in his shoes. After the service the devil could be heard screaming. The man was saved.
165561: Some people drove a cart of manure past a witch's house. Right at that spot the wheel came off the cart, even though the screw was still on it.
165562:
A man whose wife had been dead for three weeks was looking for another woman to remarry. A man from the village sent a woman to the widower. The widower had the greatest trouble getting that woman out of his house. The children often jeered at that woman in the street, although they were strongly advised not to.
The woman had a lot of money and she had a kind of illness that made her collect everything, because she did not want anything to go to waste.
165567: A farmstead in Torhout was haunted. One day a pig rooted up a pot of money there. With the pot was a letter that read: "Under this pot there is another pot".
165568: Anyone who walked past a sorcerer's house ended up in Donk instead of Maldegem. For sorcerers could make people lose their way.
165569: Every evening a woman saw a big spider sitting behind the stove. Whenever the woman tried to catch the spider, the creature vanished. One evening the people began to pray and threw the spider into the fire. At that very moment a fire broke out four houses away.
165576:
During his sermon a priest said: "At this moment thieves are stealing my cherries." Half an hour after mass the thieves were still sitting in the priest's cherry tree.
The priest could also fix people who chatted during mass to their chairs by magic.
One day a woman told the priest that money had been stolen from her. "Just go home," said the priest, "the money is hanging on the door handle." And so it was.
165577: The Vollebeke castle in Hooglede was haunted. When pancakes were baked in the cellar, a ghost could be heard saying: "Into the first pancake you bake a leg will fall. Into the second another leg will fall, into the third an arm, into the fourth another arm, into the fifth a trunk and into the sixth a head. Then the whole body will stand before you."
165581: A witch who was angry with someone tormented that person by sticking needles into a little doll. The witch also used candles and prayer books.
165588:
In Tiegem there lived a man who had obtained a galgenjong (a devil's familiar, literally 'gallows child') by fasting for three days in honour of Satan. A galgenjong had to be fed a drop of blood every day. People who wanted to throw away such a galgenjong were murdered by the creature. The only way to get rid of the galgenjong was to wrap it in a handkerchief and let someone steal it that way.
One day the man from Tiegem came to a farmer who was working in his field. The harvest had to be brought in quickly because a thunderstorm was coming. The man said to the farmer: "If you like, I will see to it that this work is done within ten minutes. But the farmhands and maids must not look at what happens." The farmer agreed, and ten minutes later the work was indeed done. One of the maids, however, had secretly looked back, and so her part of the work was not finished.
165603: Around midnight a father called his children outside to listen to the eternal hunter. The eternal hunter ran after his dogs and called: "Jago, Jago!" Because he had been cursed by his parents, the eternal hunter had to wander through the air forever.
165606: Anyone ridden by the mare could no longer breathe and felt as if their throat was being squeezed shut. You could see the mare come hopping and jumping. In reality the mare was a stopping of the blood.
165621: The witches from Oedelem went to Zillegem to learn to haunt. Witches could lie on the ground as if dead while their spirit went to torment people in the shape of a dog, a cat or a goat.
165629: A man saw three little lights beside the moat, although there were no people in the moat.
165632: A woman who was a guest on a farm where a Duitse Schaper (German shepherd, a travelling shepherd thought to have magical powers) worked saw mice running all over the table.
165644: People ridden by the mare could not speak or move and felt as if their throat was being squeezed shut. The mare came in through a closed door.
165658: Whenever a farmer from Knokke took his horse out of the stable, a phantom horse stood in the stable. That was the water devil. As soon as the farm's horse was put back in the stable, the water devil had disappeared.
165660: In Waarmaarde an unmarried woman had died. Afterwards the dead woman's sister heard something rattling at night in the trunks in the attic. One night the sister's husband got up and asked: "What do you want?" The dead woman answered: "You must still have a mass said for me. I need it so badly." After the man and woman had the mass said, the rattling in the attic still did not stop. The noises grew louder and louder. After a while it had even come so far that the ghost opened the bedroom door. When the door opened once more, the man threw a stick at the ghost. After that the dead woman never returned.
165697: Two men coming home in the middle of the night saw a returned dead person dressed in white and wearing white clogs. "You mustn't say anything or we're done for too," said one of the men. In silence the men rode past the ghost.
165701:
A pregnant woman went to a little chapel and saw a pair of beautiful black gloves lying there. The woman put the gloves on and went home wearing them. Later the pregnant woman's baby died. A year later the woman became pregnant again, but that baby died too. The woman then went on pilgrimage to Dullemonde near Waasten. After that the woman had no more misfortune.
She believed the gloves had belonged to a witch from the village.
165704: In Vonderbeke Castle in Hooglede there was a cellar that no one was allowed to enter, because it was haunted.
165722: A farmer who was plagued by mice sent for the priest. The priest predicted that the mice would disappear and told the farmer that a Dutch farmhand was responsible for the evil. That farmhand himself, however, did not know it. The farmer was advised to hang medals everywhere. Shortly afterwards the Dutch farmhand said that he could no longer get along with his colleague and therefore wanted to leave. To that the farmer said: "Then come and work on the farm, you can clean the stables." The farmhand, however, could not get into the stable because medals were hanging everywhere. When the farmhand announced that he wanted to leave the farm, he could not even get inside to fetch his money. When the farmhand used to sit in the house, he kept sticking needles into his cushion. Every time a foal was born, the animal was dead. Sixty years ago the devil still had a lot of power.
165743: A beggar woman had been with a fishwife's child and had said: Oh, what a lovely child! After that the child cried all the time and became as thin as a rake. A black cat always roamed around the child's cradle. One day boiling water was poured over the animal. The next day the beggar woman lay in hospital with burns.
165744: A workman who had beckoned to a doodkeers (death candle, a ghostly light) slammed the door shut in panic. Afterwards a hand was burned into the door. When a new door was hung, the handprint was, strangely enough, in it as well. A pot of money was found in the ground.
165745: People ridden by the mare had a high fever.
165750:
People ridden by the mare felt as if an animal was crawling from their feet up to their chest. Sometimes the animal pulled at the blankets with its mouth. When ridden by the mare, one could not call out or move. A man prayed an Our Father to protect himself against the mare.
In the old days there were people who sat crying on the roofs out of fear of the mare.
165751: One day boiling water was thrown over a cat that always lay under the kitchen stove. The next day it was found that the neighbour woman's face was completely burned.
165753: On a farm there was a baby that cried day and night and grew smaller instead of bigger. One day two nuns came to visit and said: "The child has been touched by the evil hand. You must have it overlezen (have prayers of exorcism read over it)." After the child had been overlezen in Steenbrugge, it recovered.
165771: A sorcerer could send a plague of rats to a house. The clergy often tried to get hold of a sorcerer's books of magic.
165789: The dead sometimes returned because they had failed to keep a promise or because they had hidden money somewhere. If a ghost took hold of someone's hand, the hand was completely burnt.
165808:
Some farmhands cursed all the time and so, without knowing it, summoned devils. One day the farmhands had nothing but bad luck: their clothes were torn to pieces and when they put milk into the butter churn, water came out. When a fire had been made to burn the devils, the fire kept burning without the wood burning up.
A farmhand who wanted to go to mass could not put on his shoes because they always jumped away when he reached out for them. The cows were dancing in the stable. When the farmer's wife held her hand with her wedding ring in the stable, everything became calm. But as soon as she drew her hand back, the noise began again. The priest advised the people to send for the friars of Diksmuide.
165813: If a witch had a hair from someone, she could bewitch and torment that person.
165816: A sorcerer came into a house where some women were doing needlework. The sorcerer filled the house with rats and mice by magic. On seeing the vermin on the needlework cushions, the women cried: "X, you must stop it!", to which the sorcerer replied: "But it doesn't matter, they are pretty little creatures and they do nobody any harm!"
165832: A pregnant woman was ridden by the mare every night until she was drenched in sweat. The woman had a difficult child and claimed the mare had caused it.
