165843: A man went poaching at night with his friend. At a certain moment the man saw a hare and shot at the animal. The hare was hit, but when the poacher came closer, he found that the hare was nowhere to be seen.
165854: People said that the lights seen in churchyards were little souls who came back because they had not yet reached heaven.
165861: A farmhand who was taking his dirty laundry home one evening saw two eyes as big as lanterns on a small bridge. When the farmhand came closer, the apparition stood up. The beast was as big as a calf and had exceptionally large eyes. The farmhand quickly ran away. Since the existence of the Gospel of Saint John, such sorcery no longer exists.
165863: In an inn in Wielsbeke as many as fifty cats sat meowing in the attic. It was impossible to catch the cats and some people could not even see the animals. When the innkeeper had died, another man came to live in the house. When that man's father spent the night in the house, lots of cats jumped onto the bed.
165866: Whoever told an old woman what time it was fell into that woman's power and got lost.
165872: A priest had heard that two thieves were stealing apples in his garden. By magic the priest fixed one of the thieves, with a load of apples, to the ground until the next morning.
165875: Nobody dared to live in a house in Poperinge because people said a dead person came to haunt it. In the end a notary moved into the house.
165876: A woman whose husband had drowned saw the ghost of her dead husband in a hooded cloak walking behind her along the quay.
165884: A man walking at night near the 'Doodlage' met an old woman. When he had given the woman a pat on the shoulder, she suddenly vanished without a trace.
165917: In the old days, if you met a black cat, you had to make the sign of the cross. You must not kick the animal, or else you would be tormented all night.
165930: A boy coming back from a music society rehearsal heard a sound behind him as if someone in clogs was following him. The boy believed it was the ghost of the dead marquis.
165934: In a house the little wooden block had accidentally come out of the drain hole for the water, so a cat had crept into the house. The cat jumped onto the children's cradle, and the children were bewitched. The woman of the house said that next time she would hit the cat on the head with the stove poker. When the woman had done so, a woman from the neighbourhood was seen walking around the next day with a wound on her head.
165954: Two rich people had died before they could tell anyone where they had hidden their lard pots full of gold. Every evening a death candle appeared at the spot where the gold lay hidden. One evening a man threw a stone at the death candle. When the man went digging the next day, he found a lard pot full of gold coins. On the pot lay a sheet with the words: "Under me there is one more". The man dug further and did indeed find a second lard pot.
165971: Between Beselare and Zonnebeke there was a plain called 't Noordende, which used to be called 'the poison corner'. For a woman lived there who used snake venom to harm people. Because of that woman, many cows and pigs died on the nearby farms. One day the woman was denounced by a man from Beselare. The woman was then arrested and taken to Ieper.
165980: A cowherd could make mice by putting his hat over little balls of clay and then tapping his hat with a stick. One day the priest took away the cowherd's books of magic.
165987: In Westkapelle lived a witch who always tried to get near small children. Children who had been given an apple by that witch started crying incessantly. In the end people had to go on a pilgrimage or consult the parish priest. If you had received a blessed candle or an Easter nail from the priest, you were protected against witches.
165997: Near the embankment there was a place that was bewitched. A man who passed by there one day saw a fellow standing with a big dog. The man was forced by a strange power to jump into the water. Afterwards he was, of course, soaking wet.
166002: A woman going home late in the evening was attacked by cats. The woman fled and decided to go home only the next day. The next morning the woman no longer had a single scratch on her skin.
166005: A farmer had a lot of bad luck with his cows. The milk of one of the cows was always bad. When butter was made from the milk of the other cows, the butter had gone off by the time they wanted to eat it. When the farmer greased his wagon with that butter, the wagon caught fire. The evil hand caused all that misfortune. People who did such things did not know it of themselves. You could bring the evil hand upon yourself by giving away buttermilk without salt. Because the farmer was at his wits' end, he went to the fathers of Steenbrugge, who said: "On that day we will say a mass and she will be with us!" The farmer and his wife did not attend the mass, because they did not want to know who the witch was. A farmer who lived nearby laughed at what his neighbours had been through. A while later, however, that farmer himself fell victim to the evil hand. He too had to go to the fathers.
166009: A mother from Sint-Andries went outside for a moment to fetch water. When the mother came back in, she saw to her great fright a witch standing beside her child's cradle.
166013: A man had fallen ill after a woman had visited him. The people who came to keep watch by the sick man heard horses walking in the attic. When the priest had overlezen (read prayers of exorcism over) the house, the witchcraft came to an end.
166062: The eternal hunter was cursed and had been banished from Germany or Holland. That is why the eternal hunter had to hunt forever in the coastal region.
166064: A woman always got a fever after a witch had visited. So the woman put something blessed under the door.
166084: Three boys coming back from their work at the brick kiln walked home through a spruce wood. When the boys reached the last ditch, they could not get across because branches kept appearing in front of their feet. A witch lived in the wood who had bewitched the boys because they always made fun of her.
166088: A statue of Mary was once said to have been found by a brook in Poperinge. The statue had been carried to two different churches, but it always returned to the brook by itself. Only when it was taken to the Sint-Janskerk did it stay where it was.
166092: Along the road to Izegem in Alveringem lived a witch. Close to the witch's house a little chapel had been placed with the inscription: "All who pass here, on horseback or on foot, pray an Our Father and a Hail Mary." No fewer than seventeen witches lived in that neighbourhood. Sometimes those witches bewitched the children and twisted their little heads askew. During his sermon the priest had said that he would name the witches if they did not stop bewitching children.
166113: A boy went to visit his girlfriend, who was working with a pincushion. When the girl had licked one of the pins, she fell asleep. The boy did the same and also fell asleep. The next morning the two of them found themselves in an unknown place.
166125: On a haunted farm in the Braamhul, people heard noises all night as if someone were churning. At midnight no one dared to walk past that farm.
166134: A man who was out alone heard someone walking behind him, although there was nothing to be seen. Wherever the man went, he was followed by that strange apparition.
166142: The mare was an invisible spirit that squeezed people's throats shut. People ridden by the mare sweated heavily.
166155: The mare was something one saw in one's sleep. One believed one was being threatened by someone with a knife, and so one screamed in one's sleep. Such a thing never happened twice in the same night.
166156: A man who was out at night was chased by a roll that lay in the street.
166161: A Duitse schaper (German shepherd, a travelling shepherd thought to have magical powers) was tending his sheep when two ladies passed by who did not greet him. A little later the ladies were full of lice, so that they had to turn back. When the shepherd saw the ladies passing again, he said: "Go on, and next time say good day when you meet a shepherd!"
166171: The mare was a stopping of the blood. People ridden by the mare felt as if they were being seized by the throat.
166213: A woman ridden by the mare could hardly breathe. After she told her confessor what had happened to her, she was no longer troubled by the mare.
166221: There were always cows in the street blocking the way for passers-by. When the sweating passers-by tried to drive the cows to the meadow, they got a box on the ear from an invisible apparition.
166242: South of the church of Beveren stood a castle where two brothers lived. The two brothers each entered the church by a different entrance. One night the brothers held a great feast with a real drinking bout. That night the castle sank into the ground. In a damp meadow only a deep pit could still be seen. The counts were both buried in the church. Their corpses turned into two dogs bound together with a chain. In bad weather the dogs were seen running through the streets.
166247:
A woman had received a chain letter from a sorceress. The letter asked the woman to pass the message on to seven other families. If she did not, she would meet with misfortune. The priest advised the woman to throw the letter into the stove, but she did not dare. When the dean read the letter, beads of sweat rolled down his face. Because the woman's children cried all the time, the dean said the sorceress owned a pincushion. Every time she stuck a pin into that cushion, the children felt pain. The dean gave the woman something blessed and predicted that something would happen to the sorceress. Some time later the sorceress did indeed have a heart attack. The sorceress had such trouble dying that her tongue hung down on her chest.
"It is a great stroke of luck," the dean said to the woman, "that you brought that letter to me."
166258: Some people who were binding the harvest saw a kitten jumping from one sheaf to another the whole time.
166277: A mother of two children fell victim to the witchcraft of a woman from her family. The mother's two children died because their bodies were covered in pinpricks.
166292: Anyone who did not want to be ridden by the mare must never put their slippers side by side under the bed. The slippers had to be set at an angle or tossed together in a jumble.
166304: Everyone who passed the Hellebus between midnight and one o'clock was followed by a coachman with a coach drawn by two horses. Every year the ghost came as far as the gate. The farmer always had to lay a new shirt at the gate, or else his animals were possessed by evil. One day the priest drove the ghost away to the farthest corner of the farmer's land. Every year the ghost came a metre closer. It was the ghost of a rich lord who had once left the farm because he had been cursed by his subjects and because he had let someone starve.
166305: A woman came to a farm peddling ribbons and thread. Because no one bought anything, the woman said: "If you buy nothing, you will still think of me!" A while later the farmer's wife found a pair of glasses with a silver frame by a post in the yard. The farmer put the glasses on because he could see well through them. That very same day everyone living on the farm was crawling with lice. Because the fathers of Steenbrugge could not help, the farmer's wife threw the glasses into the water. After that everyone was rid of the lice.
166324: Near an inn in Sint-Baafs-Vijve, every night people saw something flying through the air that looked like a sheep. The apparition flew back and forth bleating and sometimes sat in a tree. As many as a hundred people came from far and wide to that place to see the sheep.
166329: In Blankenberge lived a woman everyone was afraid of. A mother who was whitewashing the walls of the pigsty saw all sorts of heads and bears on the wall.
166335: In Breda (Rollegem) lived a weaver who always heard a salt box fall when he sat weaving at night. Because the weaver was afraid, he moved away. At the spot where the weaver had heard the sound, a farmer later found gold coins while tearing down the wall. Long before, there had been two men who had not paid their debt to the farmer. One had spent the money on drink and the other had kept it for himself.
166336: A farmer who could not churn butter was advised by a woman to pour a bucket of manure into the milk. When the farmer had done so, he had butter at once.
166342: A man who often came to a farm in Tiegem to smoke a pipe always got pains in his heart. On the way the man always met the same woman. After the man had been on a pilgrimage, he was cured of his heart complaint.
166364: Some people from Gullegem prepared the porridge in the evening for the next morning. One morning, however, they found that their porridge was gone. When the people kept watch over the porridge the following night, they saw a cat come in. They struck off one of the animal's forelegs. The next day they saw that one of the women who came to work there had lost her hand.
166389: If one went back to sleep for a while after getting up in the morning, one sometimes saw two fellows coming towards one. These apparitions seized their victim by the throat. Some claimed that the mare was in reality a stopping of the blood. People being ridden by the mare had to be called by their name.
166394: When people could not make butter, they often believed the milk was bewitched. In reality the problem had to do with the acidity of the milk.
166413: By reading a certain prayer, one could send rats to someone's house.
166451: A woman who lived between Komen and Brielen had special powers. One day that woman had sent a curse upon a house, so that in the morning the house was full of black crows. Because the crows were damaging the roof, the man came outside to chase the birds away. At that moment the woman came by with the words: "That doesn't matter, hop!" A little later all the crows were gone.
166473: By a brook in Kemmel a goat could be heard bleating every evening and night.
166476: Some people working in the field saw their dead godmother come back in broad daylight. The priest advised them to ask the ghost next time why it was coming back. When the people were carting grass, their godmother appeared again. They asked: "Godmother, why do you come back? Are you sent by God?" The ghost answered: "I am sent by God. Twelve one-cent candles were to be burned and that has not been done." The people immediately went to buy candles at the shop. But the shop had only six candles. When they tried to light those six candles, strangely enough it did not work. Only when they had bought six more candles at another shop could they light them. Since then the dead woman never returned. She had been released.
166494: Some people went to visit their parents, who lived in the woods. When they went home again, they were accompanied the whole time by a small child dressed in white who walked between them. The people did not dare say a word. The moment they reached their house and put the key in the keyhole, the apparition had disappeared.
166496: A farmer plagued by rats was visited by a wizard, who said: "Would you like to be rid of those rats?" The farmer answered: "Of course!" The next day all the rats had disappeared for good.
166511: A statue of Mary lay by the dunes of Bredene. It was placed in the little chapel that had been built in honour of Our Lady. One day the priest took the statue out of the chapel and put it in the church. The next morning, strangely enough, the statue was standing in the little chapel again.
166515: A man who was out at night and walked past a tobacco field heard the tobacco leaves make a strange crackling sound. When the man went to look at the same spot the next morning, there was nothing strange to be seen.
166518: Some people driving to Ieper in a covered wagon at one point saw white ghosts moving through the wagon. Only when those ghosts had disappeared could they drive on.
166535: A man travelling with his horse and cart was plagued by a witch from the neighbourhood. The horse would not pull the cart and kept tearing itself loose from the harness. After the man fastened a medal of Saint Benedict to the harness, the horse was willing to pull the cart again.
166536: A man who had to take a corpse to the churchyard by cart was accompanied by a witch who sang the whole time: "X, in fine big golden letters, X". X was the name of her son. When the people came home, X lay ill in bed: he had smallpox.
166547: Whoever stood at a crossroads on St John's Eve would get money from the devil if he sold a completely black hen. One had to ask an odd sum for the hen.
166554: The procession of Sint-Jan could not take place at the beginning of July because the weather was too bad. When the faithful came into the church the next morning, they saw that the bottom of the statue of Mary was covered in mud. Since that incident, people never dare to cancel the procession, however bad the weather.
166571: A baker had a little child that had started crying incessantly after a woman from the village had come to visit. When that woman returned a few days later, the baker seized her and threatened to throw her into the oven if she would not undo the spell. At first the sorceress denied all blame, but in the end she asked for a wet towel. After she had rubbed the child's head with that towel, the cradle was full of pins. After that the child no longer cried.
166574: A girl who had to go to the toilet at night asked her mother to light the lamp. Then the girl said: "Mother, don't you see uncle Johan? He is standing there leaning with his arm against the cupboard." But the mother saw nothing. A little later the girl said: "He is in white. Now he is going up and disappearing through the ceiling." The mother promised to have a mass said for uncle Johan. In the church the ghost wanted to give the mother some holy water. The priest advised the woman to offer a corner of her apron. The mother did so and saw the corner of her apron burned away. That was a sign that the man was not yet in heaven. After the mass the mother and her daughter made a pilgrimage procession. After that the uncle never returned.
166577: Three men talked the whole time during mass. When mass was over, however, the men could not get up from their chairs. The priest went over to them and asked: "Well, why are you staying seated?" The men answered: "Because we can't leave." Only when the priest had said: "You may go," could the men leave the church.
166596: A man who had been touched by the evil hand fell ill and died. It was his mother-in-law who had bewitched him.
166597: A farmer had promised to give so much grain to the poor that it would flow back inside when he poured it out through the attic window. Because the farmer could not do this, after his death he drove around his farmyard in a coach with two horses.
166598: The castle of Loppem was haunted. A procession was always seen passing there. A man coming home from work one evening saw, near the castle, a beast with long curly hair and eyes as big as a hand. When the man reached the gate, the animal stopped. The frightened man ran away as fast as he could.
166605: On a farm, noises were heard at night as if butter were being churned in the attic. At another farmer's, the cows were untied at night.
166640: A boy coming back from Winkel-Sint-Elooi heard a loud scream on the way home. The boy believed the sound was caused by a band of ghosts. So the boy crawled under a pile of tree trunks lying at a sawmill. When the ghosts passed by, it looked like a 'smoking liquid' (?) running past the man's hiding place.
166641: On a farm where they could no longer churn butter, they went to the fathers for advice. The clergymen advised the people to drill a hole in the door, put a wooden peg in it and then fill the hole up again. The first person to come for milk would be the one who had brought the evil upon the farm. The next day a neighbour came by, but she turned back.
166649: A farm in Woesten was haunted. The calves there crawled through a tiny hole.
166664: A man who peddled bay leaves had a son who said one day: "Father, I'm going to look for a wife". At the edge of the wood near the Knok stood a little house where a mother lived with her daughter. The boy wanted to try his luck with that daughter, although his father had advised him against it. In that house people slept until noon, and everyone knew what that meant! But the boy claimed he was not afraid of witches and wanted to get to the bottom of it. One evening when the boy was visiting his girlfriend, around nine o'clock he pretended to have fallen asleep at the table. The mother and daughter let the boy sleep and took a cloth out of a cupboard. After sprinkling some powder on their heads, they said: "Over hedges and fences, over woods and stumps, before the moon has sunk away". Then mother and daughter vanished without a trace. The boy, who had seen and heard everything, decided to follow the two women. He sprinkled some powder on his head, but then made a mistake speaking the formula and said: "Through woods and stumps" instead of "Over woods and stumps". Around ten in the evening the boy's father grew worried. He took his lantern and went looking for his son. By the wood he heard moaning and groaning. After a while he found his son, who had nearly suffocated. If the boy had not made a mistake with the formula, he would never have been seen again. For those two women were never seen again afterwards either.
166671: A woman married to a drunkard often did not know where her husband was. The woman's sister read from a book of magic and had the woman hold a key. "If the key turns, he will die," said the sister. The key turned and the man did indeed die.
166672: At 't Vloogje there was always a doodkaars (death candle, a ghostly light) at night, at about the same time. People said money was hidden in that spot.
166680: A man coming back from Desselgem along the main road saw a lit coach with a white horse and a white lady approaching. He stood at the side of the road and saw a black horse with a black rider coming from the other direction. The white and the black apparitions crossed each other three times. At midnight the lady stepped out of the coach and the lights went out. The next moment there was nothing more to be seen.
166686:
When Osschaart was dead, his skin was put into a tree stump.
On a farm there worked a farmhand who always went home after the meal and came back two hours late. One day they decided to spy on the farmhand. In this way they found that the farmhand put on Osschaart's skin and then flew over the field. The farmer tried to take the skin out of the tree stump and burn it, but he did not succeed. One day the farmer sent his farmhand far away on a job so that he could burn the skin in the meantime. But the skin had barely caught fire when the farmhand was already standing by the oven. When Osschaart's skin had burned up, the farmhand was saved.
166696: When a farmer was on his way with a cart full of fodder, a witch made the grain fall off the cart. That way the witch had free fodder for her own animals.
166704: A farmhand working on a farm was sitting on a bench in the kitchen while the potatoes were boiling. Although the lid of the pot was closed, the potatoes suddenly flew through the kitchen.
166714: People ridden by the mare had to put a sprig of mistletoe under their pillow to protect themselves.
166720: When people slept, they often felt something heavy come and lie on them. That was the mare coming to ride them.
166723: A man out on horseback one evening met some thieves who demanded his money. The man handed over his money, but fixed the thieves to the ground by magic so that they could not get away. Only the next day did the sorcerer let the thieves leave.
166730: A man got lost in a meadow. For four hours the man walked around the meadow without finding an opening in the fence. Because the man was bewitched, he had no choice but to wait until the next morning.
166732: A man coming home on a Sunday evening saw a castle along the way, which a little later had disappeared.
166735: Before the First World War a man went somewhere for a drink one evening. The sky was completely coloured. That was an omen of the war.
166743: On a farm a lot of noise was sometimes heard in the evening. The cows lowed, the horses stamped and the buckets rattled. Those strange sounds were always heard when an old woman from Zonnebeke had passed by with her books.
166754: In a small house in Lapscheure, a white sheet was seen crawling across the floor in the evenings.
166762: People were always stealing apples from a priest's garden. One day the thief was left stuck in the apple tree.
166770: A curate had to go and give the last rites to a sick person. On the way the curate was teased by some young rascals. When the clergyman had to cross a little bridge, the boys stood at the side jumping, so that the clergyman would fall into the water. So the curate took another route. When he returned, the boys were still jumping on the little bridge. They could not get away until they had promised the curate never to do it again.
166788: When people saw a pretty little animal that could not be caught, it was often an animal sent by a sorcerer or a sorcerer appearing himself in the shape of an animal.
166794: A family had a late-born child who was completely emaciated. A woman advised the family to take the child to the friars of Steenbrugge. On the train the family met a woman who said: "The child won't make it." When the family came home that evening, the child was full of lice. That woman on the train must have done it.
166813: In a meadow near the 'Hazewind', a little light appeared every evening that shot up out of the ground and a little later disappeared into the ground again. One day people began digging in that spot, but found nothing. When they dug somewhat deeper the second time, they found a treasure there.
166822: The crossroads on the road to Hoekstrate used to be haunted. On Christmas Eve the people going to church were stopped by a pack of cats. If you took a 'pielle' (1) along, you could surely chase the cats away!
166835: Whoever walked past a house in Stavele in the evening met a white ghost with a bell, which disappeared a little later.
166842: Near a haunted farm there was always a hare. After a priest had shot at the animal, a woman from the village had a bandage around her head.
166848:
In Esen lived a man who had mastered the black arts. When this man died, he first had to hand over his books before he could go to heaven. If the wizard went to market and meanwhile someone picked two plums from his tree, the man knew what had happened. One day the man went to the café with some friends. But the door was locked. When the wizard threw his cap against the door, it opened by itself. When the man saw prudish women, he conjured a hole in their clothes.
The man met a carter who swore the whole time. "Just wait, he'll swear even more tomorrow!" said the wizard. When the carter drove back, the wheel of his wagon broke.
166863: A woman who saw that a frog had come in threw the animal into the stove. The next moment the fire in the stove went out. When the woman left for the village the next morning, she met her neighbour, who said: "I burnt my foot yesterday and I can hardly walk anymore".
166867: A pregnant woman was always visited by a little old woman. When the child was born, it cried all the time. When the parents had the fathers come to overlezen (read prayers of exorcism over) the child, they were advised to put Easter nails in the cradle. Because of that the witch could no longer enter the house. She had to stay standing at the threshold.
166869: Anyone ridden by the mare tried to call out, but no sound came.
166875: A little woman always put her pan over the fire. When she came back at midday, the pan had always been knocked over. The parish priest said to the woman: "As soon as the cat comes in, you must tell it to undo the witchcraft." The woman, however, did not have the courage to throw the cat into the fire. After the woman had put salt under the threshold, the owner of the house could no longer get in.
166885: A little child who always cried was cared for by the midwife. One day a small cushion stuck full of pins was found in the child's wrappings. The priest claimed it was the work of a sorceress. When people told the priest about the midwife, the clergyman said: "That is the sorceress. Put a wedding ring under the threshold! Then the midwife will no longer be able to come in!" And so it was.
166896: A Duitse schaper (German shepherd, a travelling shepherd said to have magic powers) who was tending his sheep asked a passer-by whether he wanted red or white wine. Then the shepherd tapped wine from his shepherd's staff.
166922: A farm was home to rich unmarried brothers and sisters. When they had all died, ghosts were seen walking about the farm around eleven o'clock at night. A large pot of money was found at that spot.
166925: Two women were walking on a deserted road when one of them said: "Come, let's get away from here." The other woman replied: "But there's no such thing as ghosts!" The next moment the women saw two hundred cows standing before them.
166949: Stable hands who were ridden by the mare often laid a knife on their stomach.
166955: A dead priest came back to haunt because he had promised to ensure the continuation of the faith but had not done so. In the pin-makers' school a man without a hand appeared and asked the boys two lessons from the catechism on the continuation of the faith. Then the priest went back to the churchyard, where he vanished in the blink of an eye.
166983: A man coming back from Kortrijk suddenly saw a gentleman standing before him at the little chapel on the Lange Munte, who said: "Let's light a pipe." The man replied: "Yes, but I have no tobacco." The gentleman said: "Just feel in your pocket." The man felt that his trouser pockets were suddenly full of tobacco. The man and the gentleman sat down by the side of the road, but when the man wanted to light the pipe, he said: "I have no matches." The man answered: "Just feel in your pocket." The man did so and felt matches in his trouser pockets. When the pipe was lit, the man looked aside and saw that the gentleman had disappeared.
167041: People ridden by the mare had a bad dream. To protect themselves, they hung an alder branch above their bed. Afterwards it was found that the alder branch had lost its leaves along a length of thirty centimetres.
167049: The mare was something to do with sorcery. People plagued by the mare saw all kinds of strange things and were forced to do things.
167068:
In the old days children were warned about old people who wore a hooded cloak. Such people owned books of magic and consorted with the devil. By touching the children, they got them in their power.
If those people could get hold of a hair of someone's, they would give you an egg in which they had made a small hole and ask you to drink the egg empty. After that, the hair was put into the egg and the egg was buried somewhere. As the egg rotted, the victim slowly wasted away.
167076: At the toveresseknok (witch's hill) in Ardooie a white goat always roamed in the evening, of which people were very afraid.
167087: A man who was out at night between twelve and one o'clock met a woman and asked her: "Aren't you afraid at night?" The woman said: "Of whom?" The man answered: "Of men." Then the woman said: "It's precisely men I'm looking for," and disappeared.
167088: A man who had stolen the anchor and rope of the priest's fishing boat had to wander around the dunes for hours and hours, until he had brought back the stolen goods.
167089: A white cat always lay sleeping by a culvert in Zuienkerke. One evening a man went to deliver coal with a dog cart. When the man passed the culvert, the cat disappeared for a moment, only to reappear a little later. The next moment the dog cart tipped over, so that the coal merchant's wife fell to the ground.
167099: A man sitting in the café said to a card reader: "Well, go on, bewitch me then!" One evening, when the man was lying in bed, he heard a strange noise in the hallway. It sounded as if a newspaper was being crumpled. Yet there was nothing to be seen in the hallway.
167125: On a farm the farmer's son had been locked up in the cellar. The parents brought their son food, but the boy only ate after his parents had left. The boy grew very thin. Because the farmer and his wife believed their son's food was being eaten by a witch, they went for advice to the friars of Steenbrugge. Then a volunteer was sent on pilgrimage on the people's behalf. The pilgrim was to box the ears of the first person he met. Because the first person was a nun, the pilgrim did not dare do as he had been told. So the farmer and his wife had to go to Steenbrugge again. This time the pilgrim had to shoot the first animal he saw in the morning. The first animal was a hare. The pilgrim shot at the hare, then heard a roar of laughter and saw the animal run away. After that incident the friar of Steenbrugge came to the farm. He asked for a silver coin, crushed it and loaded his gun with the powdered silver. After all, a witch had to be shot with silver. At the moment the farmer's son was given his food, the clergyman managed to shoot a hare. The next day it was noticed that the woman next door was wearing a bandage around her head. The witchcraft had come to an end.
167129: A mother was visited by a fishwife who came to ask how the child was doing. The mother answered: "Fine! Go on in round the back." Then the fishwife stayed alone with the child for quite a while. A while later the child fell ill. It no longer wanted to eat and got 'the old man' (a wasting disease). At the moment the child died, there was a knock and the fishwife stood at the door. In the fishwife's family there was a child with exactly the same illness. The fishwife had passed it on to the other child.
167136: In a house where people had often gone on pilgrimage for a sick child, the father one day asked his wife whether a black cat ever came into the house. When the woman said that this was indeed so, her husband advised her to pour boiling water over the animal. The woman did as she had been advised. A little later she saw a neighbour with a burnt face walking to the doctor.
167151: If you met a dead person who had returned, you had to say: "If you are from God, speak. If you are from the devil, depart". At a thornbush people heard a voice say: "I have buried money here and as long as it is not found, I must come here". After the money had been found, the ghost no longer appeared.
167156: Some people claimed that they could hear the voice of the eternal hunter in the woods of Wijnendale.
167157: Witches could appear in the shape of animals, such as hens, rats or cats.
167160: Bells are said to have once sunk into the klokkenputten (bell pits) in Eernegem.
167162: A farmer had harnessed two horses to the threshing machine. After that, six white horses were seen threshing for eight nights in a row. After the horses had been at the farm, those strange events came to an end.
167173: In Blankenberge people told of the ghost of a dead man who walked past the houses saying: "Give back my boots!" Someone had stolen the wooden boots from that dead man's corpse, but a man had seen it. The man wanted the boots for himself and went to haunt the thief, who then fearfully threw the boots outside.
167194: People who were completely emaciated by a long illness were said to suffer from 'the old man'. That illness was usually caused by a witch.
167197: A strong woman was visited by the mother-in-law of a farmer at whose place she often came. The mother-in-law stroked the woman's legs, saying: "You have fat legs!" A while later the woman got a large boil on her leg. After that her leg became paralysed. The witch had caused it.
167205: A mother had a baby that would not grow because a witch had touched the child's dummy. When that witch had died, the child did grow.
167218: People who were often ridden by the mare had to make a novena by candlelight.
167237:
Near Geluveld lived a little boy of four or five years old. The boy fell ill, so that he was always nervous and stopped eating. The child collected all sorts of bits of paper and little blocks of wood in a corner of the garden. One day the child went for a walk with his godfather. When the boy saw a sack flying in the field, he ran after it and pressed the sack against his body.
One day the mother took the child to the priest of Geluveld. On Saturday afternoon the priest overlas (read prayers of exorcism over) the child on the altar with a blessed candle. After that ritual a mass had to be said for nine more days. After that the child was cured.
If the priest had not been called in, the child would have died, for it was bewitched.
167270:
A man saw a big rat jump behind the wardrobe. Some time later the man's little son was ill. The man went on pilgrimage to Sint-Eloois-Vijve with his brother and his father. When the three had gone a short way, a ball of fire fell at the brother's feet. The brother made the sign of the cross and went on. After the pilgrimage the child was cured.
The man let his own cat and the neighbours' cat into his house to catch the rat behind the wardrobe. But the cats would not catch the rat and kept trying to leave the house. In the end the two cats were let outside. The man never saw his own cat again. A few days later the neighbour woman fell ill. In that house noise was heard every night. A flying dog in a ball of fire always appeared. When the man had gone to stay in his sick neighbour's house and had seen the dog there, he came home sick with fear. The sister of the man's brother was also ill. A few days later the doctor was called for the man. Because the man could not go to Mass, he prayed often. After his brother had gone on pilgrimage to Steenbrugge for him, the man was cured. In his brother's house, however, things went less well. Six chickens, four rabbits and four goats had already died. When a terrible noise was heard one night, the brother went to the barn with his gun. He opened the door and saw a dreadfully big dog with eyes like lanterns come out. The brother fell to the ground in fright. The fathers of Steenbrugge advised the man to send his wife to Tielt with their greetings. The fathers of Tielt came to the brother's house and put something blessed in every room. After that everything went well again on the farm.
167296: A farm in Wilskerke was haunted. Noises were always heard there at night, although no one was to be seen. After a while the haunting stopped.
167304: At the castle of Kwaremont the lord's son had murdered a woman who had rejected him. After the murder accidents always happened in the castle. The castle was often fully lit up at night. The fathers of Doornik advised the lords to leave the castle and build a new one at least two hundred metres away. And that is what was done.
167319: A man from near Klerken peddled birch brooms in Watou. One day the peddler told a strange story: "When I was staying in Lokeren, one night I slept in a stable with a stable hand. There were two horses in the stable. The stable hand told me that around midnight there were always three horses in the stable. At twelve o'clock the stable hand and the peddler decided to go to the smith to have the third horse shod. The next morning the farmer's wife walked around with horseshoes on her hands and feet. Because the farmer's wife was bewitched, they took her to the priests".
167331:
People who were born as werewolves had a mark on their head. They did not behave normally and had to roam all night.
A werewolf who worked on a farm always went to the bakehouse to fetch his skin before his nightly wanderings. When he returned, the boy put the skin back in the bakehouse.
When the farmer understood what was going on, he felt sorry for the boy, who had to work all day and had no rest at night either. One day, while the boy was working in the field, the farmer found the skin in the bakehouse. The farmer threw the skin into the oven. But as soon as the skin caught fire, the boy came running up, screaming and raging. If four people had not held him back, he would have jumped into the fire to save his skin. When the skin had burned up completely, the farmhand thanked the farmer.
167337: A boy could make a mouse out of a handkerchief. When he laid the handkerchief on the ground, the mouse ran away. The parish priest asked the boy how he did it, but the boy did not know himself.
167339: A man had himself locked in the haunted castle of Loppem for a night because he wanted to know what was going on there. The man had to sit down as if he were going to be shaved. The next day the man found that his beard was gone.
167346: By a crucifix in the churchyard lay a woman wrapped in a white sheet, crying out. The woman was forced to do so by a witch. Only after the woman had been sprinkled with holy water could she get up.
167348: A farmer's wife had bought a house from a witch. The farmer's wife always regretted it afterwards, because she had so much bad luck. When her husband was not at home, the farmer's wife saw millions of creatures moving under the wallpaper.
167357: During the war some policemen came to the church to listen to what was said in the sermon. After mass the policemen could not leave the church. They had to wait until the priest came to tell them they could go.
167368: In Vlamertinge a mother was walking with her baby on her arm. The baby was looking over the mother's shoulder. The mother was followed by a strange woman, who probably wanted to harm the child. Fortunately a woman from the neighbourhood had seen it; she gave the strange woman such a threatening look that the latter no longer dared to do anything to the child.
167378: You were never to let an elderly woman come near a newborn baby. For witches were out to stroke such children on the head and say: "What a lovely baby! I'd like one like that too." After that the child was bewitched.
167384:
On a farm the pigs suffered from a strange disease. One day the farmer's wife said to her father, who was a dealer: "Our pigs are coughing. Wouldn't we do better to sell them?" The dealer advised his daughter to sell the animals as quickly as possible. When a buyer had been found, one of the pigs had a broken leg even before delivery.
Because the farmer's wife's baby seemed undernourished, her mother advised her to go to the priests. The priests asked the farmer's wife whether she went to mass. "Certainly, Father," said the farmer's wife, "every Sunday. During the week we have no time to go." The clergyman advised her not to think of evil and to pray a lot. At their wits' end, mother and daughter decided to go to the fathers of Steenbrugge with the skinny baby. The baby cried the whole way. When one of the fathers came out of the sacristy, the farmer's wife, sitting with the baby on her lap, had to turn her chair and hold the clergyman's stole while he read from a book until the drops of sweat rolled down his face. Then the farmer's wife had to go with him to the sacristy, where the father gave her blessed medals, which she had to hang in a little bag in every room of the farmhouse. The next morning she also had to give her animals a bit of sourdough. Under the farm gate she had to bury a palm branch in the shape of a cross. She also had to lay two sprigs of blessed palm in the shape of a cross in the child's cradle.
After the visit to the fathers, the baby fell into a deep sleep until the next day. The child then quickly recovered. A woman who had always come to the farm before was no longer seen. The woman used to bring a bread roll that had been handed out at the funeral of some rich gentleman. The farmer's wife would always give her a copper coin of five centimes. The woman would also stand by the child's cradle for a moment and say: "What a lovely baby!" When that neighbour came by again a while later, she could not get past the hedge. So she called to the farmer's wife: "Could you pick me a bunch of 'reseda's' (?) there to put by a sick person's bed?" The farmer's wife answered: "Come and get as many as you need yourself!", but the neighbour said: "I can't!"
167404: In the past it was said that bells always rang in the Marelputten on Christmas Day.
167418: A boy was going out with the daughter of a witch. On the day before the army draft lottery, the boy was fishing for eels next to the girl's house. The girl said to her boyfriend: "If you come fishing for eels here today, tomorrow you'll draw only a low number!" The girl's prediction came true and the boy always stayed angry with her.
167423: In Moerkerke there was a large farm that was haunted in the time of the Templars. In the cellar someone was always heard singing. But when people went to look, the singing stopped.
167429: The mare was an evil dream from which one could not wake.
167437: A man from Roesbrugge was ridden by the kokkemare at night. The man got up and walked around on the roof of his house.
167439: In Aartrijke lived a witch who could trim a thorn hedge with a sieve.
167460: Whoever ventured into the orchard in the dark got one sheaf after another against his head. During the day, however, nothing happened.
167477: The doodkaarsen (death candles, ghostly lights) seen in the churchyard were souls who returned and asked for prayers.
167479: A farmer driving home with a load of hay met a witch who said: "You'll never get home with that hay!" When the farmer was almost home, the load fell off the wagon.
167489: A woman who was said to be a witch went to the chemist to buy ointment because she had lice. Because the witch had a terrible number of lice, she bought several tins of ointment. When she got home she rubbed her armpits with the ointment. The remedy did not help, however, so the woman went back to the chemist to buy more ointment, so that she could smear the stuff over her whole body. Because that did not help either and the witch had been eaten by the lice almost down to her ribs, she said: "I'll pour some paraffin on my woodpile and set it alight, so that I can jump on it." The witch did as she had said. As her body burned, there was a terrible stench in Rozebeke. In this way the witch was punished for all the evil she had done.
167507: If anyone dared to steal the priest's shoes, that man had to wander about all night because he could no longer find his way.
167509: A farmer always heard someone in heavy shoes walking across his attic. But when the farmer went to look, there was nothing to be seen.
167513: A man found it strange that his neighbour always knew what had been said in his house the previous evening. A black cat always came into the house through the drain hole for the water. One day the farmhand struck the animal with a hot poker. The next day the neighbour had a burnt jaw.
167516: A man who peddled prayer books and rosaries filled a house with mice by magic.
167517: In the past the people of Westende did not dare pass the churchyard in the evening because lights floated there. Those lights were little souls who had to wander about. One had to pray so that the souls would not have to wander as long.
167529: A farmer's wife from Lendele had bought a new coat. When the farmer's wife proudly went to church in her new coat, everyone moved away from her. The coat was full of lice. The woman told the priest what had happened to her, and she hung the coat up in the yard of a café. After mass the priest left his prayer book lying open and then went to say prayers over the coat. There was not a single louse left on it. The woman who had filled the coat with lice was still sitting on a chair in the church. She could not get away until someone led her outside.
167531: Behind the Kerkdreef in Assebroek it was haunted. Passers-by were jumped on by sheep there in the evening.
167550: On a farm there was a child who was ill. Because the doctor could not help the child, they went to the parish priest. The priest said to the parents: "You must make a cross on the floor with holy water. Then that woman will no longer come by." The people did as they had been advised. Afterwards the child recovered. An old woman lived near the farm.
167560: A man was in the habit of weaving until midnight by the light of an oil lamp. At a certain moment the light always went out, although there was still enough oil in the lamp. Under the roof of the house a purse was found. When the money had been found and the roof of the house renewed, the lamp no longer went out. It had been the former owners who came to haunt the place.
167565: A farmer's wife who was said to be able to work magic was anxiously kept away from the children of the neighbourhood.
167583: A woman who had been ridden by the mare said afterwards that she had tried to call out, but it was impossible.
167587: A man who went fishing in winter fell over twice in front of a witch's door.
167590: Children who had been struck by the evil hand had been confronted at birth by a witch who had breathed over them. Such children were taken to Zevenkerke to have prayers read over them.
167603: When the fishermen went to sea with their horse at night, lots of boys ran around them.
167646: A woman was visited by a man peddling rat poison. "I don't need poison, because we have no rats," said the woman. The next day the woman's house was swarming with rats. Two days later the animals had all disappeared again.
167680: A man had said on his deathbed: "When I am dead, I will come back to sting people." One morning the farmhand saw a bee flying. The farmhand got angry and before he knew it, he was stung in the neck by the bee. That bee must surely have been the dead man.
167686: People ridden by the mare during their dreams started to scream.
167702:
A rich unmarried freemason from Ieper never went to church, except when one of his acquaintances or relatives was buried. When he was in church on such an occasion, he stood at the back with his arms crossed. Nor did he kneel.
Anyone who had ever crossed the freemason could be sure he would be punished for it.
When the freemason heard that the gamekeeper arrested the guilty and the innocent alike, he decided to teach the man a lesson. The freemason went to one of his farms and said to a farmer's son: "Change your clothes and come with me, because you must stay with me for a few nights." The boy moved in with the freemason, who then went to the gamekeeper and said: "I have heard about a farmer's son who goes poaching every night." The gamekeeper promised to keep an eye out. Two days later the freemason went to the gamekeeper again and said: "I think I have caught that poacher. Come along, because I have locked him up in my house." When the gamekeeper saw the farmer's son, he said: "I arrested that fellow, but he ran away. I'm sure it's him!" Since the freemason now saw for himself that the gamekeeper was lying, he said: "I see that you do not do your job properly, and I will pursue you until your death!" The freemason kept his promise.
People often said that after his death the freemason would be fetched by the devil and that his coffin would therefore be empty. Because the freemason had heard this, he had a little window made in his coffin, so that everyone could see his body lying there. The possessions the freemason left were not to be divided, for he was convinced he would come back after his death.
167704: After the First World War a woman came peddling clothes in Roeselare. The woman of the house got a garment. Afterwards she was ill for a long time. She went on a pilgrimage together with her mother and then recovered.
167708: In Otegem there once stood a castle called 'Diesveld'. Later the cellar of that castle was found. When the door was opened, rattling and clanking of chains was heard. No one was ever able to enter the cellar, because every light brought along was put out there. That castle is haunted.
167723: Doodkeersen (death candles, ghostly lights) were souls that moved back and forth in the air and had to find or bring rest. It was best to leave doodkeersen alone.
167731: In the meadows of Ingelmunster there was a horse that at night jumped onto people's necks and had itself carried.
167732: A woman who was milking saw a black cat come in. The next time the woman had milked, she could not churn any butter!
167735: A baker who lived by the church of Ijvegem went out at night for a breath of air. Around midnight the baker saw the dead rise and go round in procession. The man who had been buried last was poor and wore no shroud. After the procession the dead all lay down in their graves again. The next day the baker's hair had turned completely grey.
167780: A farm in Sint-Denijs was haunted. At night fire flew over the farm and the horses were untied in their stables. The stable doors opened, after which the horses stood in the yard. In the barn a thundering noise was heard as if someone were working with a flail. After a clergyman had visited and a promised chapel had been built on the corner of the Kruisstraat, the farm was no longer haunted.
167785: Some altar boys had stuck a blessed Easter nail under the church door. After mass three or four women stayed sitting on their chairs because they could not leave the church.
167799: A farmhand had to deliver something with a large cart and four horses. The farmhand reached his destination without any trouble. On the way back, however, the horses could hardly move forward. By evening the farmhand was still not back at the farm. The horses were drenched in sweat and had the greatest trouble pulling the cart. In a reed hut sat a German Schaper (shepherd) with his dog. The Schaper went up to the farmhand and said: "My, you are having a lot of trouble!" The next moment the horses went on without any trouble. When the farmer wanted to put the animals in the stable, however, they again refused. That was the German Schaper's doing again. The animals wandered about outside all night.
167820: Some women owned little books of magic. When such women could lay their hand on a cradle, the child became bewitched. The friars could make sure that witches could no longer enter a house.
167825: In Beselare a bleating goat was always flying through the air. One evening around ten o'clock a pig dealer met a calf, which jumped up with its front legs on the man's shoulders. The calf only vanished when the dealer got home. In the end a curate put an end to all that evil. But the clergyman lost his own life doing so.
167829: A witch had stroked a little boy's head, saying: "What a beautiful child!" A few days later the child had a heart condition. The parents went on a pilgrimage to Wannegem for the child. They brought back a cake and a ribbon. The child had to eat from that cake for nine days and the parents had to pray for nine days. In the end the child recovered.
167834: A farm in Westkapelle suffered much misfortune. The horses often fought each other. One day, when green fodder had to be taken to Brugge, there was no way to get the horses outside. The animals had been beaten a lot, but that did not help. When a neighbour woman tapped the horses with a straw, they set off at once. Whenever the horses had to pass that woman's house, they ran at great speed on the far side of the road. One day the farmer could not keep his horses under control at all. He ended up under the animals and was killed. Later a small chapel was built on the spot where the farmer had died.
167849: Some boys went to steal wood and apples from the priest during mass. When mass was over, the apple thief was stuck with his head in the hedge. The other thief could hardly hold on to the stolen wood.
167852: A woman ridden by the mare in her sleep saw an old woman grab hold of her. The priest advised her to put her shoes beside the bed with the toes pointing in different directions. After that the woman was no longer ridden by the mare.
167874: Some bakers had been given flour by a woman and had mixed it with their own flour. Because of that, however, the bread turned sour. The next time, the bakers secretly threw that woman's flour into the ditch or the cesspit.
167880: There was once an abbey in Moorsele, which was later moved to Wevelgem. On the spot where the abbey had stood was a large orchard that was haunted. Figures could be seen floating among the trees there.
167882: A man staying in France came home because he had heard that his brother was ill. On the train the man saw a magpie fly against the window. That was a bad omen. When the man got home, he found that his brother had died.
167897: A woman whose child cried all the time had been advised by someone to put something blessed under the threshold of the front door. When the woman had done so, one of the neighbour women could no longer come in through the front door. Because that neighbour then always came in through the back door, the woman decided to put something blessed there too. After that the neighbour could no longer get in to bewitch the child.
167904: Some Iceland fishermen who saw a large bird sitting on the ship believed the creature was the harbinger of the devil. Whenever there was a storm, the fishermen blamed the bird.
167907: When people saw a frog crawl in through the drain hole for the water, they chopped off one of the animal's legs. The next day it was seen that a woman from the village had lost a leg.
167908: A widow who had remarried had a son who was studying to become a priest or friar. During the holidays the son came home with a friend. The two boys would then fill the room with running rats. For they could work magic.
167914: A mother from Lendelede had a little child. A strange woman who had special powers often came to visit her. Every time that woman had been in the house and had touched the child, it got convulsions. At a certain point they decided not to let the woman in any more. After that the child recovered.
167929: A witch used to live near Desselgem station. If the witch was at home when flax was being delivered, the flax wagons always overturned. Otherwise nothing happened.
167937: A woman from Bulskamp went every day to bring some meat to two young people from the village. Strangely enough, those two people grew very thin, until they eventually died. When the witch who had done this to them died, nobody wanted her furniture. Everything had to be burned.
167940: A pregnant woman met a witch in the street. When the woman dropped her newspaper, the witch picked it up for her. The woman's child was never normal.
167965: Strange things happened on a farm in the Klerkenstraat. One night the farmer went to the attic with his gun because he had heard creaking. When the farmer stood at the top of the stairs, he said: "All of this here is mine." After that the creaking grew even louder. The farmer's daughter was grabbed by the arm whenever she went to the attic to fetch flour or grain.
167988: A girl went for a walk with a friend who had a little child. When the girls saw an old woman coming towards them on the way, they quickly turned back, because that old woman might touch the child and bewitch it that way. That morning a bewitched child had been buried in the village. When they got home, the girls quickly put something blessed under the threshold so that the witch could not come in.
167989: A man had said to an unmarried old woman: "Why don't you marry my neighbour? He doesn't drink, he doesn't smoke and he is a handsome fellow!" When the woman married that neighbour a few months later, she said to the man who had given her that advice: "We won't live long anyway." Less than a year later the woman's husband fell ill. The doctor came and advised the sick man to go to bed. A few hours later the man was dead.
168003:
An old man claimed he was ridden by the mare, for at night he saw the strangest figures standing beside his bed. The man lay in his bed drenched in sweat.
Children ridden by the mare were very disobedient.
168027: When a woman believed to be a witch was buried in Reningelst, a fierce snowstorm raged. The weather was so bad that the coffin could not be taken to the churchyard by cart or even by sledge. Some men had to carry the coffin on their shoulders. That witch owned books of magic, which the parish priest collected after her death. If that witch said something, you had to say: "God will reward you!" and if she hit you on the shoulder, you had to hit her on the head.
168030: A lady of the castle who had relationships with several men was with the framassons (freemasons). When the woman lay dying, she sent for the priest. On the way, however, a big black dog jumped in front of the priest's carriage, causing the horse to bolt and the priest to be injured. It was believed that the black dog was the devil, who wanted to stop the priest. Before her death the lady had made a will stating that all her money should go to the poor and to charities. Her relatives, however, did not carry out the will. Some years after her death the lady appeared in white clothing in the castle garden. She also appeared once in the shape of a pig that made a lot of noise. The dead woman kept appearing until the will was carried out.
168052: After his death a creditor came to haunt the people who still owed him money. People who then gave money to good works were no longer troubled by the ghost.
168074: A woman always told her children: "You must be home by twelve o'clock, because between twelve and one the witches are about and from one to two they make you lose your way." After two o'clock the witches' time was over.
168075: At a farmer's, the evil hand made it impossible to churn butter any more. There was always dung in the butter churn. A friar came to read prayers over the milk and said to the farmer: "You must pour a bucket of dung into the churn and then churn." After they had done so, they could make butter effortlessly again.
168081: A man went to have his hair cut by a barber whose house was full of rats. The man stamped his feet at the animals, but he could not hit a single rat. They were, after all, rats that had been sent by someone.
168108: Two girls on their way to the fair met a German shepherd, but they did not greet him. A little further on the girls found they were covered in lice. The girls went back to the shepherd and said: "Good day!" The next moment the lice were gone. The shepherd said to the girls: "Next time, just say good day!"
168113: A man who was threshing pretended as a joke that he wanted to hang himself. Suddenly a cat came into the barn and pulled the cord, so that the man was really hanged.
168121: A child about eight months old cried all the time and became skin and bone. The friars said to the child's mother: "Your child is bewitched and that problem will not be solved quickly." The clergymen read prayers over the child until they were drenched in sweat, and gave her nine sugar lumps and nine floorcloths to take home. The mother also got something blessed to put under the front door and the back door, so that the witch could no longer come in.
168139: A sorcerer could make sure that people who walked on his field could not get off it. When there was a fair in Veurne, the sorcerer forbade his girlfriend to go there. On the way back the girl got lost in the meadow, where she walked about all night. The sorcerer had learned his magic when he was a friar. As soon as he could work magic, he had left the seminary.
168149: A sorceress lived in Boezinge. She was a dirty old woman who always wore five or six skirts on top of one another. One day the sorceress was at a farm where there was a statue of Saint Joan of Arc. She took hold of the statue, went around the farm with it and made several signs of the cross. Then the sorceress said: "No fire will ever break out here again because I have done this."
168150: In Lapscheure an old woman had given a child a piece of sugar candy. After that the child cried itself to death.
168155:
A farm in Bellegem was haunted. Passers-by saw a wedding feast there in the evening, of which nothing was left to be seen in the morning. At night people were also seen falling into a pit with horses. In the morning all of it had disappeared. In the farm's cellar there were two beasts.
Later a chapel was built on that spot.
168159: Some people who could not churn butter, and on whose farm a horse had died, went on a pilgrimage to the friars of Steenbrugge. "Does someone come to fetch milk from you?" one of the friars asked the farmer. When the farmer said yes, the friar said: "Tomorrow that woman will come by again. You must not refuse her anything and you must not ask her for money either." The farmer did as he had been advised. After that the misfortune came to an end.
168163: If a black tomcat sat on the gate bar of a farm, it was a bad sign.
168193: People ridden by the mare felt something lying on them and could not call out. When one began to pray, the mare went away.
168198: It was haunted by the Kogelsdreefje. Sorceresses who had turned themselves into cats always came there.
168211: At a castle in Beveren, noises were always heard at night. In the end the castle sank into a swamp.
168219:
An old cooper who had lice went to the mill one day. The miller's son saw a little creature crawling and removed it with a cloth. When the cooper left, the miller's son shook off the chair he had sat on. The cooper did not say a word.
The next day the clothes and beds of the miller's family were full of lice. They had to go and ask the cooper very kindly to make the lice disappear.
When the cooper died, the parish priest went and collected all the man's books. They were books of magic.
168224: Strange things happened in the castle lane in Beveren. At night the trees there were cut down, and in the morning they stood upright again.
168247: During the French Revolution, bells were said to have been hidden in the pit on the road from Hooglede to Roeselare. Every year those bells could be heard ringing on Christmas Day. One day the bells were brought up again and carried in procession to the church.
168250: If a magpie or an owl flew past in the evening while someone lay dying, it was a sign that that person's death was near.
168258: A horse could no longer walk after a witch had struck it on the knee.
168270: A mother was watching a procession in Gistel together with her little son. Next to the boy stood a woman who kept stroking his forehead. Although the mother never let her children go out without a scapular, she did not trust the situation and gave the witch a shove so that she moved a little further away.
168272: In a convent in Houthulst all the cows had been bewitched by an old woman. The people found out who was to blame when they had wounded the woman.
168279: If one did not want to be ridden by the mare, one had to put one's clogs upside down beside the bed.
168282: On a farm in Wervik a friar was called because they could not churn butter. The friar had to send someone else to the farm because he himself did not have enough power to overcome the evil.
168308: In Lendele lived a woman who tore hooded cloaks in the church. That woman claimed that the devil forced her to do evil.
168315: In Staden there was a haunted house. At night the tubs were heard rattling there as if someone were watering the cows.
168341: A man from Snellegem got hopelessly lost on his way home. When the man finally got home after wandering about for a long time, he was drenched in sweat.
168353: In a haunted café chains were heard rattling every evening. Long ago a mother was said to have murdered her child there and walled the body into the wall. After the priest had blessed the house, it was no longer haunted. The occupants moved out all the same.
168363: At the three Duikers (culverts) some people had seen a sorceress and said: "Good evening, X." The woman, however, did not answer. When they repeated their greeting and again got no answer, they boxed the woman's ears, so that she fell into the ditch. The sorceress stumbled out of the ditch and, strangely enough, was not wet.
168381: In the past one often heard about bewitched children, because there was a lot of poverty then, so people did not have much food and fell ill easily. Old women were often suspected of having given the children a 'tightened heart'.
168402: A girl from Harelbeke was walking home in the dark and on the way met a lady, who gave her an apple. After the girl had eaten the apple, she felt ill. After a while the girl was doing so badly that the friars had to be fetched. The clergymen, however, could not reach the farm, because each time they were thrown into the moat.
168405: A farmer's wife coming back from Mass saw her shoe suddenly come undone. An old woman passing by said: "Come, let me fasten your shoe." When the farmer's wife got home, she found that all her cows were tied up and dying.
168424: A girl from Houtkerke fell ill after accepting a sweet from a witch. The child withered away completely.
168427: Bewitched children could turn into an animal.
168430: On the Kluisberg near d'Helle lie two large stones called 'Peetje en Meetje' (Granddad and Grandma). The druids were said to have once placed the stones there to burn their victims on them. Later the place was haunted; the druids came back to burn their victims.
168441: A woman who ran a café had a four-month-old child. A little woman often came peddling in the café. One day the peddler asked to use the toilet. When she came back, she looked into the cradle and said: "Well, well, what a beautiful child!" Then the child suddenly began to cry. Moreover, the child got the 'old man' (an illness). The parish priest who came to read prayers over the child advised the mother to go to the friars, as they were more powerful. The priest had prayed until he was drenched in sweat. A friar from Oostende sent the woman to the friars of Nieuwpoort and said: "You will meet a woman in a hooded cloak there, who will say: 'But little lady, where are you going so early?' You must not answer then." When the woman set off for Nieuwpoort at five in the morning, everything happened as the friar had foretold. The woman was given a blessed palm sprig in a red velvet bag, which she had to put above the door. Because of that the peddler could no longer come in.
168456: People ridden by the mare hardly dared go to sleep and set their shoes with the heels towards the bed. If they did not, the mare could crawl onto the bed.
168470: A woman was visited by her neighbour, who came to fetch grain. The woman had to pass her neighbour, who was standing in the doorway. The neighbour bumped into her briefly. A little later the woman found she was covered in lice. The woman was furious and never wanted to let her neighbour in again. It was said of that neighbour that she was a witch.
168479: In Zande there was a haunted farm. At night noises were heard there as if someone were threshing and separating the chaff from the grain with a winnowing machine. When people went to look, there was nothing to be seen.
168486: A girl had been given flowers by a woman suspected of being a sorceress. After that the horses and cows died on the farm where the girl lived, so that the friars had to come and read prayers over the place.
168510: A castle in Hooglede was haunted every night. In the trees that stood there, little lights were always seen burning.
168511: A sorceress lived in Loppem. One day, after that woman had walked past a load of hay, the cart overturned shortly afterwards.
168513: A man often saw his dead father sitting in his house, although he kept all his doors shut. At night the glass plates knocked against each other by themselves. The son had masses said because his father apparently had not fared well in the afterlife.
168527: On the Hofdries in Tiegem a pig with ten piglets always roamed. Because the animals on the farm were all dying, a little chapel was built on that spot. After that the witchcraft came to an end.
168530: The Spittenhoend ghost lingered near Marialoop. The ghost kept calling: "Half water and half milk, short-weighing scales." Every year around Christmas the farmer had to bring a clean shirt to the gate. The ghost would then move on.
168552: Some people who went to fetch milk in the evening were flung back and forth at the seven wells. Strangely enough, not a drop of milk was spilled from the buckets.
168559: The priest's maid put four Easter nails under her mattress because she was ridden by the mare every night. After that the witch no longer came into the presbytery when the maid was at home.
168564: People ridden by the mare were in such misery they could no longer stay lying in bed. They felt as if their throat was being squeezed shut and a heavy weight lay on them. It was as if a woman was sitting on them.
168565: An old woman often came to visit a farmer in Poperinge. One day the farmer and the woman were exchanging money when a pregnant cow stood up. The cow broke her loin. Because the witch had exchanged money, she had gained power over the farm.
168584: At a haunted castle no butter could be made and the calves were born without legs. The farmer's wife sprained her foot. After the farmer had promised to go on pilgrimage to Halle every year, all that was still seen in the castle was a little candle dancing on a hand.
168585: A little boy could make mice out of clay, which he set running in the church after blowing on their backsides. When the parish priest asked the boy where he had learned this, the child answered, "From my mother." The priest went to the mother's house and took her books of magic away from her.
168591: One night the sexton went into the church because he had heard something ringing. It was the ghost of a priest who came to say mass. Afterwards the ghost thanked the sexton for answering during the intercessions and the Dominus Vobiscum. "I am released because you answered," said the ghost. "I have been coming here at night for a hundred years to say masses until someone answered."
168599: A farm in Izegem was haunted every evening. That was the fault of the maid, who always sat reading her books in the evening. One day the roof of the house was full of little red gnomes. The haunting only ended after the curate of Rumbeke had read prayers over the house.
168603: Anyone ridden by the mare in their sleep was seized by the throat by something invisible and could no longer move or call out. To protect themselves against the mare, people hung a sprig of mistletoe above their bed.
168611: A sorceress could turn herself into a black cat and in that way bring the evil hand over the farms.
168614: Fourteen days after the funeral of a man from Mannekensvere, a light was seen in the churchyard. People said the light was the soul of the dead man coming back.
168621: A shepherd who was ridden by the mare sweated heavily and could no longer breathe. Later the man said that an old woman had seized him by the throat.
168640: Whoever was ridden by the kokkemare (nightmare spirit) could hardly breathe and felt as if he was going to die.
168641: A nun had visited a man who feared neither God nor commandment, hoping to instil some piety in him. That evening, when the nuns were in bed, the man rang the bell and said: "I need the priest, because my house is haunted." The nun answered: "Our priest has gone to the priest of Houthulst. If you need him, you will have to fetch him there." The man then left and nothing more was heard of him.
168649: When a farmer from Veurne drove past a witch's house with his load of hay, the hay flipped off the wagon. One day the farmer's horses were stuck in a pit. "I'll help a bit," said the witch. The next moment the wagon drove off by itself.
168662: On three consecutive nights a man had seen a coffin lying in the turnip field. By day the coffin had vanished without a trace.
168663: The mare was a spirit that sat on people. To protect yourself against the mare, you had to place your clogs or shoes under the bed with the heels pointing in.
168684: The baron of Ichtegem was driving to the station with his four horses. At a culvert the baron saw a woman sitting, but he did not speak to her. When the horses had passed the culvert, they became very restless, so that the baron could hardly go on. He was convinced that the woman had been at the castle and had been given nothing there. He drove back and gave her two francs. Then the witch said: "You'll still be in time for the train!"
168694: A man who went round shaving people was found dead one day in a corner by the inn 'De Tien Geboden' (The Ten Commandments). A woman from the village claimed she regularly saw the dead man appear.
168720: In Werken lived a married woman who was said to be able to work magic.
168725: A man returning one evening from visiting his girlfriend heard apples falling to the ground in the orchard of a farm. But the man saw nothing. The next day all the apples turned out to be still hanging on the tree.
168729: People who claimed they were ridden by the mare actually had a stagnation of the blood. Some people believed you had to put your shoes next to the bed to keep the mare away.
168746: Opposite the nuns' school in Blankenberge was a little shop where a small Jewish man lived. When the Jew had died, he had to be laid out. Strangely enough, no body was found in the house. The undertaker urged the people to search very carefully. In the end they found the Jew's body standing upright behind a curtain with a bowler hat on his head.
168756: A miller who had got up at night because he had to turn the sails into the wind saw something pass by, and he called: "Friend, give me a hand!" At that the figure rolled closer. It was a bundle of bones and rags. The miller's neighbours had often said that the place was haunted.
168762: A man who had to walk home through the woods every evening was one day followed by an invisible, giggling ghost. As soon as the man had left the woods, the ghost was gone. Since the Gospel of Saint John has existed, such hauntings no longer occur.
168771: A woman who could work magic made the plates roll off the table in a house, so that they all broke.
168773: Whoever was ridden by the mare felt as if his throat was being squeezed shut. A woman who had often been ridden by the mare once said: "If you are sent by God, speak. If you are sent by the devil, go back where you came from!" After that the woman was rid of the mare for good. To protect yourself against the mare, you could also, for example, put your clogs under the bed.
168786: A poacher had often shot at a hare in vain. One day the man shot at the animal with a crushed silver coin. This time the poacher shot out one of the hare's eyes. The next day he found that a woman from the neighbourhood had lost an eye.
168792: In Proven lived a sorceress who had a frog sitting on her windowsill. Whenever someone came to visit, the sorceress always said: "Watch out that my frog doesn't bewitch you!" Families with small children never let that sorceress into their house.
168793: On a bewitched farm in Roksem many animals died. One day the farmer's wife, who had five children, sat crying over all that misfortune. Moreover, her husband did not like to work. The farmer's wife could always hear the witch coming.
