168810: A man went walking in the dunes with his goats. A little later a woman came to cut grass close to the goats. The man chased the woman away and said she was not allowed to cut grass there. At that the woman grew angry and said he would regret it. In the evening the man went to Oostende with his friends. While his friends were buying apples in a shop, the man vanished without a trace. Five days later he was found in the racecourse of Oostende. The man was completely emaciated and had to be taken to hospital. That woman had done this to him.
168816: A farmer had just paid his rent to a lord when the lord died. The lord's friends had found the money and claimed the farmer had not yet paid his debt. When the sad farmer was working on his land, suddenly a chair stood beside him with the lord's ghost in it, who said: "You have paid everything honestly." When the farmer said: "You must be happy," the ghost said: "Put your dung fork under this chair and you will see how happy I am." The dung fork was completely burned, for the lord was in hell.
168822: People who were ridden by the mare had a stagnation of the blood. Between sleeping and waking you could feel the mare approaching at your feet. If you then quickly turned over and made the sign of the cross, the mare was gone. To protect yourself against the mare, you had to sleep on your right side.
168825: A farm in Torhout was haunted. Little creatures ran on the roof that could never be hit when something was thrown at them. In the end a small chapel was built so the haunting would stop.
168828: A man had a quarrel with the priest. When that man's father had died, the man got nothing. The inheritance was given to the priest for good works. One day the man fell ill. He saw nothing but devils around him and kept shouting: "Kill them! Kill them!" The man's wife sent for the priest. The clergyman could not see the devils, but he began to pray, which made the devils leave. The man died during the priest's visit.
168840: A man going to the farm saw something pass by and heard a scream. Suddenly the man saw that two cats were sitting in the little chapel.
168849: A farmer's wife who needed a new barn sold her soul to the devil. If the devil managed to finish the barn in one night before the first cockcrow, he would have a right to the man's soul. That night, however, the farmer's wife came to regret what she had done. Around two in the morning she got up and clapped her hands, which made the cock start crowing. The little devils who were still working on the roof quickly fled. The farmer's wife was allowed to keep her soul, and she had a new barn as well. No one has ever been able to close the hole in the roof of the barn.
168851: A woman said to a farmer who was on his way with a cart and some cows: "Farmer, I'll make your cart tip over." The farmer replied: "If you think you can, go ahead and try." A little further on, the cart tipped over for no apparent reason. People said it was witchcraft, but the farmer did not believe in such things.
168863: On a farm in Beveren a strange black cat always sat by the fire. Because the cat kept coming back, one day the farmer's wife threw wood at the animal, whereupon the cat jumped into the fire. The next day it was found that a woman from the neighbourhood had lost her arm.
168879: A boy who worked as a farmhand sometimes had to churn for as long as three days. Strangely enough, he still had no butter. The reason was that a witch lived on the farm.
168895: A man always saw a black dog in the evening and went to a friend for advice. But when the friend came to look, there was no black dog to be seen any more.
168902: An old man lived at 't Kruiswater, a place where four streets crossed. One day that man saw a horse running. Because the man believed the horse had broken loose somewhere, he wanted to stop the animal to return it to its owner. But the horse would not stop. When the man struck at the animal, he only saw a black cat running away.
168912: In the old days the German shepherds could all do magic. In Vlissegem too there lived a German shepherd who worked on a farm. Because the farmhand always heard music in the sheepfold on Christmas night, he decided to go along with the shepherd once. In the dark the pair rode on a sheep to the shepherd's house in Germany, where a party was going on. When the farmhand bumped his foot on the way back, the German shepherd said: "Never mind, you hit the Church of Our Lady in Bruges with your foot."
168914: If a child in its cradle had been touched by an ugly old woman, it got 'de oude man' (the old man, a wasting illness).
168934: A man who worked as a cowherd on a farm in Torhout saw a friar sitting on a cart every day. One day the farmer's children found money. After that the friar was never seen again.
168935: To his great astonishment, a farmer could no longer keep a single pig after his wife had died. At night the dead woman knocked on the door and said: "I am sent by Our Lord. I am in heaven. You must still have two masses said." That same night the farmer went to the priest to have the masses said. The next day his wife appeared once more to thank him. After that the farmer could keep pigs again without trouble.
168954: A sorceress could make passing cyclists fall to the ground.
168956: When a witch from Houtem had died, her body was carried on a wagon. "Something is bound to go wrong today," said a farmer from the village. On a bend, the wagon with the body overturned.
168960: The souls in purgatory came back to ask for prayers.
168992: Whoever was ridden by the mare actually had a stagnation of the blood. The victim could hardly breathe and had the greatest trouble pushing the mare off.
169008: If people wanted to gather wood instead of going to Mass, they had to walk around the dunes all night carrying a beam.
169029: At a farm in Zerkegem all sorts of noises were heard at night, as if everything was being turned upside down. When people went to look, strangely enough there was nothing to be seen.
169037: On a farm where butter could no longer be churned, people went to the friars for advice. One of the clergymen claimed that the maid was responsible for the misfortune.
169047: A gamekeeper had caught a poacher. In the Kwakkelbos in Jabbeke the gamekeeper had already seen all sorts of strange things. One night the poacher had seen in the moonlight a hare with a pipe in its mouth. The hare tapped its paw and filled a second pipe. All the hares nearby tapped their paws at each other to ask for tobacco and matches. The gamekeeper was so frightened at the sight of that scene that he had not dared to shoot at the animals.
169049: A man who refused to believe that someone from the village had magic powers was fixed to the ground by the sorcerer.
169058: When a poor old woman had died, nine days after her death she came and banged her pan against the bedstead until everyone was awake.
169068: A stable hand who worked on a farm had to roam all night as a werewolf with a bearskin on his back. The farmer thought it strange that his farmhand was getting so thin, and he told the parish priest what he suspected. The priest advised the farmer to look for the place where the farmhand kept his bearskin. The skin lay under the thorn hedge by the bakehouse. The clergyman then advised the farmer to send the farmhand far away and meanwhile heat the oven to burn the bearskin. The skin had barely been put in the oven when the farmhand came storming up at full speed to save his skin. Because the bearskin had already burned up, the farmhand was released and could sleep peacefully every night again.
169083: In the old days sorceresses could torment children by sticking pins into a little doll. The child then felt pain in the same place where the doll had been pierced.
169100: In Stavele or in Watou, the people were said to have hidden a bell during the French Revolution. When the French soldiers had tried to pull the bell out of the church, the ground had torn open, so that the French disappeared into the deep chasm. Every year on Christmas night those bells can still be heard ringing.
169103: At night there were lots of lights by a big hedge. People said they were the dead returning. After the Gentse Baan was built there was too much traffic at that spot, and the lights gathered at 't Kruis van Beveren.
169109: In Haringe there stood a castle where money was buried. Later, little lights were always seen burning there. One day the lights were no longer seen.
169116: There was a haunted spot in the Kasteeldreef in Beveren. A man passing there with a workman from the brewery saw a cat and said to the workman: "Look, a cat! Give it a quick lash with your whip!" But the workman did not do so and said cautiously: "Shh, shh, you must leave alone what is at rest!"
169117: In a hut in the dunes lived a sorceress who always frightened the fishermen. One day that hut was destroyed by a storm. The people were relieved to be rid of the sorceress, but among the rubble they suddenly saw a black cat walking, which kept crying: "Roesch! Roesch! Roesch!" That cat sometimes became very big. The sorceress could also change into a donkey or a dog. Roesschaert sometimes nearly capsized the boat, so that the fishermen were very frightened.
169135: A woman told the curate that the former curate of the Sint-Janskerk appeared to her every evening. The curate advised the woman to ask the ghost what it wanted. If the ghost wanted to shake her hand, the woman had to offer the corner of a sheet. So the woman learned that the dead curate had once received money to say Masses but had never said them. The curate had also promised to make two processions for two old women from the village. When the ghost wanted to shake her hand, the woman threw it a corner of a sheet. A moment later the sheet had vanished. After the woman had the Masses said, the dead curate appeared no more.
169139: In Lauwe there lived a man who believed in nothing. When that man had been buried, the devils took away his body and filled his coffin with stones.
169144: If a farm was haunted, a small shrine had to be hung beside the gate.
169152: Whoever was ridden by the mare felt his blood flowing faster and could not move.
169170: A woman who saw a cat come in at night poured boiling water over the animal. The next day a burnt sorceress lay beside the woman's bed.
169205: Whoever was ridden by the mare in his sleep woke up feeling that something was flying on top of him. Victims of the mare were drenched in sweat and tried to shout, but no sound came. That feeling could last a quarter of an hour or half an hour. Sometimes it was so bad that people no longer dared to go to sleep for fear of being ridden by the mare again.
169226: A man walking home on a Sunday evening could go no further because dogs kept jumping in front of his feet. After the man's mother had come and made the sign of the cross, the animals were gone.
169233: The priest had to drive the devil out of a woman who was possessed. The woman had already been taken to another priest before. The priest had received permission from the bishop to drive out the devil. Because the priest was afraid, he first went to an old friar who had to pray and fast for many days. Then the priest could begin his task. The woman had foam on her lips. When the friar asked in Latin how the devil had got into her, she answered: "By eating an apple". The priest said that the devil had to leave. To that the devil replied: "Let me stay here a little longer". In the corner of the room sat a cat. At that spot the woman fell over. A ring-shaped apparition flew to the place where the cat sat. Then the cat vanished. The animal was never seen again. Some time later the woman was cured.
169259: A carter from Keiem who carried a lot of money spent the night in a house. The woman was just boiling lard. When the carter was asleep, his mouth fell open and the woman poured a spoonful of lard into it. The carter returned after his death because he had received grace through people's prayers.
169275: When a Duitse schaper (German shepherd, a travelling shepherd said to have magic powers) was thirsty, he could tap wine from his staff.
169281: One evening the priest had to go somewhere together with the sexton. On the way the pair met a robber, who threatened them with the words: "Your money or your life!" The next moment the robber turned into a statue. When the priest returned, the robber was still standing there. The next morning after mass the robber could move again. He came to the priest on his knees to ask forgiveness.
169282: The area near a chapel was haunted. All sorts of animals could be seen walking about there.
169289: A man coming back from the shop saw a fellow standing there who was as tall as the treetops. That fellow lived with a woman who had a bad name.
169292: Alder wood that had been ridden by the mare had young shoots that were completely flat and covered in small spots. Many people hung alder branches in their houses to protect themselves against the mare.
169304: A farmer's wife who could work magic went to the market. Before she left, she said to her maid: "When you start churning, you must say: 'From every churn a lump as big as my thumb'." But the maid did not have a good memory. She made a mistake and said: "From every churn a lump as big as my backside." When the farmer's wife came home, she found her house completely full of butter.
169329: When people somewhere were plagued by rats, they fetched the priest. The clergyman would sit down among the rats and begin to pray. A little later the rats ran off and moved to another farm. Priests are no longer allowed to do this, because other people always ended up with the rats.
169341: A woman came peddling yeast at a farm. Because she did not get on with the farmer, she bewitched the farm. As a result the turnip harvest was ruined and the horses stood sweating in the stable. The witch even forced the farmer to ride around his farm on a pig.
169348: On a farm lived a farmhand who was ridden by the mare every night. Because the boy grew very thin and listless, the farmer's wife asked a friend for advice. The friend said that at night you had to place a knife with its point on your chest. The farmhand decided to place the knife upside down on his chest. That night the sorceress fell on the point of the knife and died. After that the farmhand soon recovered.
169350: In Rugge there was a house where people could not sleep at night, because the loom worked by itself all night long.
169353: German shepherds could work magic by means of their books of magic. For example, they could cover people in lice.
169363: During a flood a child had died in a house in Gistel. The next morning a woman from the neighbourhood came through the water especially to ask whether the child was dead. Strangely enough, the woman was not wet.
169378: A woman who went peddling all sorts of goods took revenge when people bought nothing from her. So it happened that butter could no longer be churned on a farm. The people then went to the friars.
169404: The bells of Leisele were said to have been taken to Flanders by the French. After those bells had sunk, they could be heard ringing on Christmas night. That place was still called 'Klokkenput' (Bell Pit).
169436: A woman often saw her dead mother walking in the meadow behind the church. When she spoke her mother's name, the ghost suddenly vanished.
169446: In Adegem there was a wood called 'het Geetebos' (the Goat Wood), because a phantom goat roamed there. A drunkard who had mocked the phantom goat was jumped on by the animal. The man was drenched in sweat from fear.
169460: At a farm by the Schapenbos in Staden, the tubs in the cowshed could be heard flying about every night. That farm was bewitched.
169461: Two women who were making bobbin lace at about ten o'clock in the evening heard someone singing at the door, although nothing could be seen. Those were the 'vramassons' (1).
169476: A pregnant woman felt a stab of pain in her belly in church. A little further on she saw a witch standing. When the woman came home, the witch was standing by her house, although she had no business being there. The woman's child was stillborn.
169479: One evening when the sexton was in the church, he saw the sacristy door open and a priest in vestments walk to the altar. The sexton fled the church and told everything to the parish priest, who said: "You must help that priest. When you have served mass for him, you must go with him to the sacristy." The ghost said he had been coming back for a hundred years to say a mass he should have said during his lifetime. The ghost was released. The parish priest never accepted money from anyone before he had said the mass. After all, he did not want to come back after his death!
169489: In the old days people sometimes caught a cat to eat on Christmas Day. An unbelieving man who had seen a fine cat went home to fetch a revolver. When the man came back, the cat was still sitting there. After the man had shot at the animal, there were suddenly two cats. The man fired five shots and then saw five cats.
169494: A man from Pittem always went in the morning with his wheelbarrow full of eggs past a beech wood to the market in Izegem. Every time the man reached a certain brook, one of his baskets fell over.
169496: Between Kemmel and Wulvergem a phantom goat roamed about, frightening people.
169509: A beggar woman who had been given a bowl of porridge at a farm bewitched all the cows and pigs. When almost all the animals had died, the farmer's wife went to the friars of Steenbrugge.
169520: A man saw a new spade standing by a farm. He took the spade, although it was not his. On the way the spade grew heavier and heavier, so that in the end the man had to take the tool back to the farm where he had found it.
169550: When an owl flew away sighing, someone would die.
169551: A man whose neighbour was suspected of being a witch went poaching. The poacher saw a fine hare running and shot at it. But the man could never hit the hare. A little further on the poacher saw a woman standing. That was a witch who had turned herself into a hare.
169553: A pregnant woman from Kaster was patted on the shoulder by a witch. The next day the woman gave birth to a child that had kidney stones.
169565: A family living on a farm in Kuurne was visited one morning by a woman who could not bear that those people lived on that farm. The woman had made strange movements and then left again. After that the people on the farm could no longer make butter. After they had been to the friars, the problem was solved. The next time the witch came by, she did not even get halfway up the lane!
169572: Part of Lombardsijde was said to have been flooded by the sea. When there were high waves because a storm was coming, the fishermen heard the bells ringing beneath the sea.
169575: A pregnant woman from Gullegem had been bewitched by a sorceress. Some time later the woman gave birth to a snake that crawled up the wall.
169590:
One day the son of a lord went hunting. While the son was away, the father became seriously ill. The servant went to fetch the hunter, saying: "You must come at once, for your father is dying." The son answered: "Yes, but I am busy now. I will hunt a little longer first." When the servant delivered the message, the lord said: "Well, if he will not come to my deathbed, then he may go on hunting forever." That is why people spoke of 'the eternal hunter'.
A similar figure was 'the wanderer of the Jews', who had to sing forever:
"Seven stuivers is my bread,
seven stuivers is my money,
always counted out and ready."
169601: A woman came to a farm to buy eggs. The farmer's wife, however, did not want to give her any eggs and sent her away. When the farmer's wife wanted to boil eggs a while later, she found that all the eggs were rotten.
169602: One day some children arrived late at the little school on the Gaai in Sint-Denijs. The children had not dared take the usual way to school because the night before a child had died through the doing of a woman. Despite people's warnings, the teacher sometimes went to visit that woman. There was nothing at all wrong with that woman.
169608: A man from Poperinge could make rats come to him. The animals ran over the man's shoes and did not bite him.
169638: Anyone who had promised to have a Mass said or to have a grave planted had to come back after death if they had not kept that promise.
169652: A man who had left the seminary had gone blind. One day the man went to Zillebeke with his little black dog. At the crucifix along the way stood three young fellows who threw stones at the little dog. The three boys were fixed to the ground by magic with their hands in the air. The blind man went on his way to a woman from whom he was going to get herbs to make tea. When the blind man came back, the boys were still standing there. The blind man said to them: "Let someone like me pass unharmed!"
169656: Doodkeersen (death candles, ghostly lights) were dead people who came back. At least, that is what some people believed.
169670: A man walking along the canal saw a beautiful cat sitting by the road. When the man tried to grab the cat, the animal jumped into the canal and swam to the other bank. On the far side the cat walked ten metres further and then jumped back into the water. The cat swam straight towards the man. The man braced himself and wanted to hit the animal with his stick. A moment later the cat had vanished.
169694: A man always saw the mare coming when he crawled into bed. If at that moment he still had the strength to spread his arms, the mare quickly disappeared. One evening the man went to sleep with a knife in his hands. But when he heard the mare coming, he could not move. The man was in distress for a good half hour, so that he believed he would not survive.
169696: A house in Egem was haunted. At night the cupboards were heard creaking and bundles of wood lay in the house. Perhaps it was the returned ghost of a priest who had once been beaten to death in that house.
169713: Two men went fishing at night near the 'torrelen'. The men had the greatest difficulty hauling up their nets. The nets were full of screaming frogs. The men were so frightened that they quickly ran away. That must have been witchcraft.
169731: At a farm in Ruddervoorde noises were heard at night as if threshing were going on and straw were being thrown about. Strangely enough, nothing could be seen.
169733: A brother and sister were always short of breath when they woke up. One morning the boy told his mother that during the night a woman had stood by his bed and grabbed him by the neck. On Sunday the same happened to the boy's sister. The woman had a cat with her and laid the animal on the pillow. People advised the boy and girl to put their clogs beside the bed with the toes pointing outwards. That way they would no longer be ridden by the mare (nightmare spirit). The woman who did this to them was someone they knew. She was also the reason butter could no longer be churned on that farm.
169743: Three brothers who had spent all their money met a gentleman on horseback one evening, who asked why they looked so sad. The brothers answered: "We have no money left and we want to sell our souls to the devil". The gentleman replied: "Well, sell your souls to me. Then each of you must say something. The first must always say: 'All three', the second: 'For the money' and the third: 'As is reasonable'". The brothers agreed and sold their souls. One day the brothers were in a hotel where a rich gentleman was staying. The hotel owner said to his wife: "We will kill that gentleman and blame those three fools who always say: 'For the money, all three, as is reasonable'". When the three brothers had to appear before the judge, they said that the hotel owner had committed the murder. In case of need, the brothers were in fact allowed to say something else.
169754: A poacher hunting in the Vrijbos saw a troop of hares playing. Every time the man wanted to shoot at the hares, his gun did not work. When the man shot towards the ditch, the gun strangely did work.
169757: In Gijzelbrechtegem the ghost of a dead priest was seen lying on the ground. If you stepped on the ghost, your foot went right through it. At some point the ghost was no longer seen.
169765: Sorceresses always tried to get into houses where there was a small child. After a sorceress had touched a child, the child became simple-minded.
169782: A man walking home saw a witch walking ahead of him. The man did not dare overtake her, because as soon as anyone came within ten metres of her, they were thrown backwards or fell into the ditch.
169784: On her way to the castle where she worked, a woman met a big white dog. When she arrived at the castle, the woman told everyone that the dog had been a witch in animal form.
169789: Mermaids still exist in Antwerpen. Mermaids are cursed people who announced bad weather.
169804: A man fell off his bicycle because he was ridden by the mare.
169818: A family in which a man had recently died kept hearing knocking. The people had promised to go and serve, but they had not kept their promise. After the people had gone to serve on the advice of a priest, they heard no more knocking.
169820: When a child was completely shrivelled because it suffered from 'de oude man' (the old man, a wasting illness), people often took the child to the friars, because they believed a witch had caused the illness.
169835: The wood at 't Stroomptje was haunted. Nobody dared to go there.
169839: People used to believe that a cellar of the castle of Wijnendale was haunted. That cellar was said never to have been entered by anyone.
169843: In the Broekstraat in Esen lived three unmarried men who were grabbed by their beards at night. During the mission a priest destroyed the book of magic that had caused these strange events.
169880: During the war a man lived in a little clay house. The Germans claimed that the man's house was haunted. Bricks fell out of the chimney through the roof, although nothing and no one could be seen. Lumps of earth were also always flying through the air.
169889:
In Tiegem lived a witch who bewitched people by taking hold of them by the shoulders. All the children in the neighbourhood died because of this witch. One day the witch visited a mother who had a newborn baby. When the witch took hold of the baby, the mother was powerless; it was as if she were nailed to the ground.
Afterwards the mother sought advice from the parish priest, who came to bless the house with prayers and then went to take away the witch's books of magic. The clergyman came back drenched in sweat. Some time later the witch died.
169928: A stalkaars (ghostly light) came out of the ground and flew around like an aeroplane with a lamp on it. Once a stalkaars flew like that from the Lijsterhoek to the Breile at the Hoorn. People believed a treasure was hidden in those places or that something had happened there.
169935: A witch from near Heule had seen a child and said: "What a beautiful child! It will surely grow!" After the witch's visit the child began to bite at everything it saw. Moreover, the child would not eat, so it became completely emaciated. The clergy did not want to come and read prayers over the child. In the end the little child died.
169950: On a farm there was a fine cow that gave a lot of milk. On the corner of the street lived a woman whom the farmer did not allow into the stable. When one day the witch had been in the stable after all and had touched the cow, the animal did not give another litre of milk. The farmer had the Augustinian friars of Gent come. After the friars had prayed in the stable, their prayer books were completely torn.
169954: Sorceresses had a little wax doll into which they stuck pins while reading from books. In this way they could torment children from a distance and make them die.
169981: When it was full moon and people were allowed to go dancing, they were afraid of ghosts. The ghosts could hide in the wagons standing on the quay to carry away the fish. A girl from Oostende saw a figure in the hallway that suddenly disappeared.
169991: On the road from Beselare to Moorslede stood an old castle of the marquesses. Whenever carters drove past it at night, they always saw a cat walking in front of their cart.
170012: Near the Zwaneput there was a pit in which an old woman had once drowned. On Christmas Day bells could be heard ringing in that pit.
170016: A baker whose child would not grow and had a thin, pale little face went to the friars for advice. The clergymen told the baker that a woman always came near his child. The friars advised the baker to keep that woman away from his child. When the witch next came by, the baker sent her away. The moment the witch slammed the door behind her, all the loaves in the bakery fell to the floor.
170018: A man was unloading a cart of coal at the Blindekapel in Heestert. That place was haunted because a church had once sunk into the ground there. Suddenly the man saw a cat sitting on the 'snak' (1) of his cart. An hour later the cat was still sitting there. In the end the man had to pull the animal off the cart. That cat sat at the Blindekapel day and night.
170039: Someone who had got lost had stepped on doolkruid (straying herb). Such people wandered about and sweated terribly. They had a standstill of the blood or had been bewitched by a little woman.
170058: At the Kruiske (little cross) on the road to the hamlet 'den Broek', a man was once stabbed to death during a fight. Since then three men always sat playing cards at that spot at midnight. One night a passer-by said to the men: "Do you need a fourth player?" The man joined the company and played cards with them. At a certain moment one of the others asked the man: "What are you playing for?" The man answered jokingly: "For my soul!" The man lost the card game. The next morning he was found dead under a tree.
170061: At a farm in Handzame there had been much misfortune since the farmer had met a strange apparition. One day, coming back from the fair, the farmer made the sign of the cross before passing the Vossenberg. Then he heard a rattling and saw a shadow pass by. It looked like a lady whose skirt rattled. The apparition accompanied him until past the Vosseberg.
170064: A woman went to help in a girl's café by the tram station in Poperinge. At a certain point the girl dismissed the woman. After that the woman had to look for other work. Not two days after her dismissal, the woman was covered in lice. Every evening she knelt beside her bed praying for the lice to go away. After a while the woman was rid of the vermin. That girl from the café owned books.
170066: When a farmer with his horse and cart passed a house where a witch was standing outside, the horse would go no further. As soon as the farmer had chased the witch inside, the horse started moving again.
170075: A dead man came back at night in a horse-drawn coach that drove back and forth through the village all night with creaking wheels. Although no one could see the coach, in the morning cart tracks were seen in front of the door. The people went to the priest, who advised them to place a relic of the dead man under the threshold. Since then the coach has never been heard again.
170109: Whoever was ridden by the mare in his sleep wanted to wake up but could not. The mare was a stagnation of the blood.
170129: A mother with a small child was visited by a woman she did not trust. When the mother went to the cellar, she said to the woman: "Stay away from the cradle!" After the woman left, the child began to cry. In the end the child died through the doing of that witch.
170137: In the area around Geluveld many Duitse schapers (German shepherds, travelling shepherds said to have magic powers) used to work. These shepherds could tap beer from their walking sticks.
170142:
During his sermon a priest said to his parishioners: "At this moment someone is stealing my cherries." By magic the priest made sure the thief could not eat a single cherry and could not get down from the tree.
When two lovers were standing behind the priest's hedge, the clergyman asked: "What are you doing here?" The pair answered: "That's none of your business!" The priest then said: "You will stay standing here as long as I wish." The priest fixed the lovers to the ground by magic and left them standing until the next morning.
One day the priest bought a car. When people asked who was going to pull that vehicle, the priest answered: "The ezelraad" (council of donkeys)(1). The priest was taken to court by four women. The clergyman then predicted that those four women would die an early death. And so it was.
170151: A farmer who came to his field saw that the iron hammer that normally stuck in his plough was floating on the water of the brook. When the farmer went home, he met a sorceress, who said: "You can safely go back to your field." The farmer went back and found that the hammer was stuck in the plough again.
170166: One stormy evening a fifteen-year-old boy had gone to play cards with some friends. On his way home he came to the Donkergat, a wooded lane with pollard willows and a brook. The boy was surprised to meet some of his friends there, who said: "We are going back and taking a detour, because the Donkergat is haunted." But the boy was not afraid and went on alone. In the Donkergat he saw a white figure moving up and down. When the boy came closer, the figure had vanished. He never knew what it was.
170172: On a farm near the presbytery in Ijvegem the parents had died, so the children were left on their own. Although the beds had been made, the sheets were always tangled up in the evening. The neighbours believed the dead father or mother had returned. After the priest had been to the farm, the strange matter improved.
170191: When a child had been touched by an old woman, it cried all night and had to have prayers read over it by the dean.
170213: The mare was a nightmare. People troubled by the mare trembled and tried in vain to shout. When you felt you were being seized, you woke up.
170232: To protect yourself against the mare, you had to cross your arms or your feet. Whoever put his clogs under his bed was sure to become a victim of the mare. You had to put your clogs next to your bed.
170246: Whoever was ridden by the mare at night felt as if he was being strangled.
170249: In the past people were sometimes ridden by the mare. That had something to do with devils or ghosts.
170258: Just after the First World War a German shepherd said to the people: "This year there shall be no crops anywhere." After that the crops in the whole area were eaten by big mice and rats.
170267: A man went for a drink in a café where the family had a strange daughter. Because the man did not trust the place, he left the café. On his way home the man got hopelessly lost, so that the next morning he found himself in Nieuwkerke.
170268: On the road from Sint-Joris-ten-Distel to Hoekstrate a castle is said to have sunk once. One day a man on his way to Aalter met a young lady, who said: "Come inside". An ugly beast lay there. The young lady said to the man: "Take the key out of the beast's mouth". But the man did not dare and ran away. After that the castle sank.
170274: On his way home from work in the evening, a man was always followed near the Kegelsdreef by a kitten that got under his feet. The man had often tried to kick the animal, but he never succeeded.
170300: Whoever was ridden by the mare felt that he was being strangled.
170304: A man had promised to go on pilgrimage to Oostakker so that his sick wife would recover. The woman recovered, but the man never went on pilgrimage. Ten years later the man and woman heard strange things at night. It sounded as if planks were being struck in the attic and a horse and cart were being driven around. Strangely, the children sleeping upstairs heard none of it. The man went to a priest, who advised him to go to Oostakker on foot after all. He was allowed to come back by train.
170313: A woman whose little child had died heard a knock on the door one evening. The woman opened it and saw a floating lady and a gentleman. Then the woman said: "X, if I pray too little for you, I will add as much again." The next moment the lady and the gentleman vanished. Since then there was never again a knock on the door.
170322: In Sint-Kruis there was a horse that went ploughing of its own accord every night. When one day the horse was shod by a smith, the next morning the farmer's wife lay in bed with horseshoes.
170344: When people were ridden by the mare, they no longer knew what they were doing. You could free such a person by grabbing hold of him and calling his name.
170355: The area by the Kapelletje ter Ruste used to be haunted. At night noises were heard there as if someone were weaving. But when people went to look, there was nothing to be seen.
170367: While his farmhand was baking bread, a farmer from Aalbeke found a werewolf skin in the alder wood. The farmhand advised the farmer to burn the skin. The farmer threw the skin into the oven. Before the skin had burned up completely, the woman who had to play the werewolf came running up.
170370:
In Vlamertinge a man lived with his mother and his six-year-old son in a small house. Whenever the occupants went to sleep, they always heard knocking. People from Elverdinge and Beselare came specially to the house to listen to it. They would call towards the ceiling: "If you are from God, speak. If you are from the devil, go away!"
One day a policeman came to investigate. He found that the knocking always began the moment the little boy had gone to sleep. So it was discovered that the child was secretly knocking on a piece of wood with his hand under the blankets.
170395: On the quay in Oostende a witch went about who often knelt beside a post praying for the ships. When the witch had gone, the fishermen of the ship tied to that post said: "We will have a bad voyage, because the witch has been praying at that post."
170399: A man who lived in a large castle in Langemark had promised to donate something to a monastery. However, the man had given all his possessions to his farmhands and maids. After the man's death a light was seen near the castle and a strange bird was heard screaming there.
170415: A woman who was said to be able to work magic always went to visit newborn children. When that woman had looked at a child, the child died from bewitchment.
170421: A farm was haunted. A rich lady in white clothes walked around there.
170430: If blessed bread had been placed behind the door, no witches could come in. A witch from Stavele walked about day and night with a white wicker basket in her hand. That witch visited everyone who had children. If the witch had been in the house for an hour, it was already too late. When a family had refused to give the witch what she asked for, their child died.
170448: In 1884 a farm in Varsenare was taken over by a farmer from Snellegem. The occupant advised the new farmer above all to keep a close eye on a small room next to the bakehouse. The cowherd who slept there was beaten every night. One Saturday evening in October the new occupant was sitting by the hearth with his two children and his grandmother, while his wife carried milk to the cellar. Suddenly the door was pushed open and a cat came in that was twice the size of a normal cat. Fearlessly the farmer took a piece of wood from the hearth. However, he did not dare throw it at the cat straight away because the milk jug was still in the cellar. When the cat ran outside, the farmer went after it. He managed to hit the cat just as it jumped over the hedge. The following Sunday the farmer and his wife went to early Mass. On the way the two met the witch's daughter, and the farmer's wife asked: "Isn't your mother going to church today?" The daughter answered: "No, she got a beating somewhere and she's lying in bed". When the farmer's wife met the witch a few weeks later, she said: "Neighbour, since we've lived here in Varsenare, you've never come to visit us. You must come some time!" The witch replied: "I will never set foot over your threshold again".
170460: People who were ridden by the mare while lying in bed felt as if something heavy came to lie on top of them.
170485: Sometimes a newborn child became bewitched because a woman or a man had touched it. People to whom this had happened went to the friars of Ieper for advice.
170488: At a haunted castle a horse-drawn carriage was always seen driving at night.
170494: A woman was going home with a bundle of nettles on her back. When she passed the house of a witch, the witch made her dance in a big puddle of water.
170509: When people saw a doodkeers (death candle, a ghostly light) burning somewhere, they believed that money of a dead person was hidden in that spot.
170536: In Assebroek a little light always burned in the wood. People were afraid of such lights, which they called doodkaarsen (death candles). In reality the light was caused by some jokers who had put a candle in a turnip to frighten people.
170547:
In Zonnebeke a witch often went to fetch milk at a farm. The first two children of the farmer's wife who lived there had died. Whenever there was a baby in the cradle, the witch always came closer and said: "What a beautiful little child that is!"
When the farmer's wife's third child was ill, she went to the friar. The clergyman said: "The woman who has been here will never come back after tomorrow." When the woman came to visit for the last time the next day, a dove was sitting on the roof. As soon as the woman was inside, the dove fell to the ground and vanished.
After that the woman never visited again. The child survived.
170548: A church was said to have once sunk in Raversijde. In stormy weather bells could still be heard ringing there.
170562: In a house that offered lodgings there was a room where everyone had their neck broken. A man who wanted to spend the night in that room asked for a table and a deck of cards. A woman appeared who lost at cards. Because the woman had to pay, she took money out of the wall. That released her.
170595: In the Kortrijkstraat in Izegem there was a little chapel that was haunted. When a boy passed it one evening, he saw to his great fright something crawling. Terrified, the boy ran home. He was so gripped by fear that he still could not sleep the next morning. The boy fell ill and suffered much misery. He died at the age of nineteen.
170601:
One day a sorcerer was sitting in a café in Bekegem. The landlady always wanted to silence the sorcerer because he talked dirty all the time. One day the woman slapped the sorcerer across the face. Then the sorcerer said to her: "You will regret that!" The next day the café was full of rats.
After a while the landlady got the sorcerer to send the rats to a nearby house.
170613: A woman who went to fetch the midwife was followed the whole time by a dog. The midwife said to the woman: "You must not touch that dog, because then the evil could pass to the child. That dog will go back by itself to the place it came from."
170642: In Ichtegem there lived a widow who was said to be able to do witchcraft. For people could never get their carts up the hill when the witch was standing outside. A hunter had shot at a hare a hundred times, but he could not hit the animal. He was convinced that the hare was the witch trying to deceive him. When the hunter went to the witch to ask for help, he could hunt successfully again.
170645: Every day on her way to work a woman passed the house of a witch in Veurne. When the woman walked past that house, her child could not be calmed. Even if the child was asleep, it would suddenly wake with a start at that house. Some time later the woman learned that her mother often showed the child to the witch who lived in that house. The woman went to the parish priest to get a paasnagel (blessed Easter candle nail) to hang above the door.
170656: Next to the 'Kopren Hane' in the Slap, a dead woman had returned because she had neglected a promise. The woman burned her hand into a white cloth.
170663: In a small house lived a witch who came to bewitch the little children. That is why child mortality was such a big problem in those days.
170673: A small part of Oostende was flooded by the sea. At Easter the bells of the sunken Oostende could still be heard ringing.
170701: After something had been placed in a stable, people found the next day that the animals were all standing at the other side of the stable, although nobody had touched them. After the friars of Ieper had walked around the stable and stamped on the ground three times at the door, everything returned to normal.
170704: Fishermen were not allowed to take currant bread on board, because it was believed to bring bad luck.
170706: In the evening people saw silkworms in the woods that gave off light at night. People believed these were returning spirits. These spirits were called 'arme rullen' (poor souls).
170712: In Houtem the horses would not stand on the weighing scale. The animals stood with their legs in the air. Meanwhile a witch stood laughing against the church wall. That witch had caused the deaths of her two daughters and her son-in-law.
170736: A woman had hidden her purse in the leg of her bed. After the woman had died, a strange sound was heard by the bed at night. As soon as the silver coins had been found, the sound was no longer heard.
170738: A pregnant woman had been patted on the shoulder by a visitor. When the child was born, it suffered from 'de plane' (a childhood illness) (1). The mother got a paasnagel (blessed Easter candle nail) from the Passionists, so that the witch could no longer come in. She still had to return a few things, but the people would not accept anything more from her. The mother went on a pilgrimage to Deulemonde in France, after which her little daughter got somewhat better. The child had been bewitched by the pat on the shoulder the mother had received during her pregnancy. If you were struck on the left shoulder by a suspicious woman, you had to hit her on the head to protect yourself.
170758: To protect yourself against the mare, you had to put your clogs upside down next to the stairs, so that the mare thought you had come downstairs. You could hear the mare coming. People ridden by the mare felt as if they were being strangled and could not make a sound. People who were often victims of the mare grew very thin. Plants could also be ridden by the mare. You could see this, for example, when two branches in a wood had grown against each other. Those branches then became flat. This happened especially with spruces.
170767: A witch had visited a sick woman. Two days later the sick woman was covered in lice.
170772: A café landlady had to cross a ditch with a wheelbarrow full of turnips when a witch came by. "Will you manage?" asked the witch, and the landlady replied: "Oh yes, I've done it so often. Why wouldn't it work this time?" When the landlady reached the middle of the plank, the wheelbarrow tipped over.
170788: A house in Zillebeke was haunted. At night the tables and chairs began to dance there. In the end it became so bad that all the inhabitants of Zillebeke came to watch the haunting. The Carmelite friars came to exorcise the house.
170819: One Sunday in church a priest said that someone was stealing his sour cherries. He also said he would leave the thief sitting there until after high mass, so that everyone could see who it was. The thief could not manage to bring the cherries to his mouth.
170823:
A travelling salesman came to a shop where there was a sick child. The child was six months old and had no hair left. The child's hair, nails and bits of skin lay in its nappies. The salesman took the desperate mother to the Godshuis in Lichtervelde. When they arrived, the woman said: "Sister, I am here with a bewitched child." Mother and child were taken to a small room, where an old and a young sister came to pray for the child. Meanwhile the mother had to hold her child in her arms and lay her hand on its chest. Then the young sister began to sweat so badly that the white cloth of her habit under her chin became completely wet. After the sisters had prayed for a quarter of an hour, they gave the mother a holy card with a prayer on the back. One of the sisters said to the mother: "You must read that prayer over your child at nine o'clock in the evening. Then it will be healed. As soon as the child is healed, you must have a Mass said by the Benedictine fathers. Here are two paasnagels (blessed Easter candle nails). Put one above the back door and the other above the front door. That way evil will no longer be able to get in."
When the mother asked how much she had to pay, the little sister said: "Give what you like to the little black boy over there."
Five weeks later the child had hair and little nails again. Afterwards the parish priest of Wijnendale admitted that it must have been a real case of witchcraft.
The child had fallen ill because of a woman who had come to visit. The woman had picked up the child and said: "What a beautiful child!"
After the sisters' intervention that woman could no longer get into the house. One day she was found dead.
170836: One evening a farmer was visited by a woman who asked whether he would come with her to the ast (drying kiln). The farmer went along. When the woman let herself fall on the way, the farmer carried her on his back. When he got home, the farmer crawled into bed ill. He never got out of it alive. The dead farmer had a mark on his back shaped like a sprig of holly.
170841:
a) In Oostrozebeke lived a boy who was the son of a sorceress. When the boy had looked in his mother's books of magic on a Sunday, he could make the plates on the mantelpiece in a house dance without a single plate falling to the floor.
b) A woman who worked for a farmer was dismissed one day. The woman then said to herself: "I won't even be off the farmer's yard before his cart tips over." And so it happened.
c) In Oostrozebeke lived a boy who owned books of magic. When this boy's brother had been dismissed by a farmer in Tielt, two days later that farmer could no longer churn butter. The fathers of Tielt had to come and exorcise the farm. The boy's books of magic were in a large chest. The clergy had already tried to take the books away, but had not succeeded. The chest could only be opened by the boy himself. The boy had received his magic power from his mother when he was fifteen years old. Women could only pass on their power to their youngest son.
d) A girl coming back from vespers was infested with lice by a woman. The girl became completely emaciated and eventually died.
e) A woman sat with her daughters in church for the three o'clock vespers. When the woman was still sitting there at six o'clock and the priest came into the church, he said: "Well, what are you still doing here?" Only when the priest had closed his church book on the altar could the woman stand up and leave the church.
170846: Witches sometimes smeared a substance on doors. If you touched that stuff, you fell ill or had bad luck.
170852: A mother who had a newborn son was visited by a woman from Beernem. The mother's sister-in-law did not want to let that woman near the child, but the woman pushed the door open, went to look and said: "What a lovely child! Congratulations!" The woman had barely left when the child began to cry incessantly. Because people believed the child had been bewitched, the father stayed home in case the sorceress from Beernem came by again. Three days later the sorceress came by once more. The child's father said to her: "Are you going to undo the harm you have done?" The sorceress answered: "Yes, I will" and then said to the father's sister: "You must go to my house. On the cabinet are three wax figures. You must bring the figure standing in the middle here." When the sister came back with the requested object, they saw that the wax figure was stuck full of pins. The sorceress said to the man: "You must throw that figure into the stove and you must hold me tight." The man did as he was asked. When the figure had melted away, the witch had lost her power. The father, however, no longer wanted her to set foot in his house.
170856: A man and a woman whose father and mother had died at the same time had promised their parents something, but had not kept the promise. A few months later the man and the woman saw the two coffins of their father and mother standing on the windowsill. After the man and the woman had fulfilled the promise, they no longer saw the coffins.
170871: Some children had become bewitched after a woman had stroked them and given them sweets. After the children's mother had been to the friars of Jex, the situation improved. Since then the witch never tried to come in again, as there was a paasnagel (blessed Easter candle nail) under the door. If the witch asked: "May I come in?", you had to answer: "If you can."
170876: A woman came to buy a loaf at the bakery in 't Halfweeghuis. The next day all the freshly baked bread in the bakery was bad. The shopkeeper had also given the woman a glass of milk. The next day the freshly drawn milk in the bakery stank. All the people from the Madonna (1) were afraid of that woman.
170877: In rainy weather a man had gone to fill the mattresses with chaff. When the man came back with a cart full of mattresses, a woman standing by her house called out: "A mattress might well fall off!" Six steps further on, the man saw a mattress fall into the mud.
170886: At a haunted farm the horses struck five-franc coins at night. Because the whole wall was always covered in coins, the farmer became extremely rich.
170889: Some people were beaten by a witch.
170892: A boy made mice out of earth at school. When the parish priest found out, he took the boy's magic power away.
170899: A man drove a cart full of coal past a witch's house. Right at that spot the cart overturned and all the coal rolled onto the ground. Strangely enough, the cart was not damaged.
170907: A girl had got lice on her way back from high mass on Sunday. Whatever the girl did, she could not get rid of the lice. The creatures crawled out of her dress. People believed the girl had been bewitched.
170927:
In Tiegem lived a farmer who had sold his soul to the devil. The devil had appeared with a candle and said: "If you light this candle, you can have anything you want. When the candle has burned down, you will see what happens..." Then the devil vanished.
The farmer lit the candle, whereupon the devil appeared and asked: "What do you want?" The farmer asked for a lot of money and immediately got what he had asked for. Then the farmer blew the candle out again. The farmer asked for everything his heart desired, but when the candle had almost burned down, he buried it in the ground, so that the devil no longer had any power over him.
170933: In Lombardsijde lived a woman who was suspected of witchcraft. With her evil hand, that woman made a child cry all the time.
170935: A woman driving a vegetable cart to the market in Menen was accompanied by a big dog with a bell, which walked in front of the cart the whole time. Whenever the dog turned around, one could not move a step further and had to stop the cart. As soon as the dog walked on, the cart started moving again.
170942: One day the owner of Hof ter Hille, on the road to Oostduinkerke, went by carriage to visit her tenant. About thirty metres from Hof ter Hille the coachman said: "By God's grace and God's will we will soon be at Hof ter Hille." The owner replied: "Without God's grace and without God's will we'll get to Hof ter Hille just as well." The next moment two black dogs leapt out of the verge and bit through the horses' traces. While the coachman ran after the horses, the carriage began to spin and disappeared into a bottomless pit.
170954: An innkeeper's wife who could work magic had a six-year-old child. That child could make a tile stick to a beam. People came from far and wide to watch this spectacle.
170969: A farmer's wife always sold milk that was half watered down. When she died, she had to haunt at the Verbrande Brug in Schore. The dead farmer's wife kept calling: "Half water, half milk, scantly measured!" After a while the ghost disappeared.
170975: In Rollegem-Kapelle lived a woman who could be in two places at once. When people walked past the woman's house, they saw her coming from the 'voute' (1). When the woman had come out of the 'voute' and walked past the stove, she jumped outside.
170990: When the cows were ridden by the mare at night, they began to low. People could also become victims of the mare. Wood that had been ridden by the mare became very thin.
171034: After their death witches came back. People could then see them dancing on the chairs at night.
171063: In Passendale there lived a woman who always had a big black cat with her. A farmer saw a group of cats playing in his farmyard. When a strange cat suddenly came running up, the farmer struck with a sabre at the animal, which he had never seen before. The next day the farmer heard that the woman was lying in bed with a wound on her buttocks.
171077: A farmer on his way with a load of fruit met a woman, who greeted him. Shortly afterwards the load flew out of the cart.
171095: In a street in Blankenberge lived two women suspected of witchcraft. That street was so badly haunted that the people living there sometimes could not find their own houses. One day the friars even found that the houses stood with their chimneys pointing downwards.
171111: A man going to Moorslede saw lots of cats in the Beukendreef. As soon as the man reached Moorslede territory, the cats had vanished.
171116: A drunkard who rang the priest's doorbell as a joke got stuck to the doorbell.
171117: A boy who was ridden by the mare felt as if something weighing a thousand kilos was thrown on him. The boy began to sweat and felt the blanket with his hand. Something hairy was lying there, like a dog.
171140: On the Boskant (1) lived a woman who was said to be a sorceress. One day a mother went to that woman's house to fetch water. On the way back, the mother with her buckets of water was pushed over three times on the ash road. When the mother died at the age of ninety, she could still picture those events.
171141: In a house in Veurne people sat by the fireplace with a sick child. The child cried all night. At a certain moment a black cat came in and stroked the child's legs. A neighbour who had just come in said: "Shouldn't you keep that cat away from your child? That's dangerous!" At that a man struck the animal with a blowpipe. The next day they met a man who was limping. He had turned himself into a cat to bewitch the child.
171142: People did not dare go near 't Motje in the evening, because it was haunted. When people walked home, they sometimes saw the branches beating down to the ground, although there was no wind.
171158: A man told of a farmer's wife who dealt with evil, so that the farm was haunted. When the farmer's wife had bewitched a horse, the farmer went to the priests. The clergymen advised the man to keep a sharp lookout from then on. One morning the farmer's wife lay in bed with horseshoes on her hands and feet. That is how it was discovered that the farmer's wife was a witch.
171159: Near the airfield the witheren (white gentlemen) drove underground with horse and cart.
171185: A witch's neighbour was baking bread. A cat kept walking around next to the hearth. Strangely, the bread would not rise. Angrily the man took the red-hot poker from the hearth and struck the cat on the neck with it. The next day the man's neighbour was badly burnt. It had been her fault that the baking failed.
171191: Some people could drive the birds from their field by walking around their land on Palm Sunday. After that the birds often sat twittering on the hedge, but not a single bird came onto the field any more.
171195: A farmer on his way to his field met a witch, who said: "You must not go." The farmer went anyway and his threshing machine broke. In the end the parish priest had a stern word with the witch.
171213: In the old days the old people went to the farmers every day to ask for a slice of bread. One day an old woman from Outrijve fell into the brook and drowned. From then on a little light was always seen above that brook. The farmers in the area claimed it was the old woman's soul.
171222: A man who worked on a farm in Westouter had to deliver pigs to a farmer. Because the pigs were almost as heavy as stallions, the man had great difficulty getting the animals onto the cart. In return for the work, the farmer gave the man a franc. When the man wanted to have a drink at an inn on the way back, strangely enough he could no longer find his franc.
171229: At a place where money lay hidden, doodkeersen (death candles) were seen flying back and forth. The doodkeersen went to the trees and to the houses. They were the souls of the dead who returned because of the money.
171234: At a farm in Maldegem the threshing machine could be heard running at night. When the farmer had ploughed a meadow during the day, nothing of that work could be seen the next morning.
171244: In Nieuwpoort the white devil carried the nets from the beach to the dunes.
171249: A woman whose husband was a werewolf had been advised by someone to burn her husband's animal skin. But every time the woman tried, her husband came in, so it did not work. One day the woman sent her husband far away so that she could burn the skin in the meantime. At that moment, however, the man came in shouting and raging, foaming at the mouth. Because the skin had already caught fire, the man was released.
171256: A girl who was ridden by the mare heard a big dog coming up the stairs to her room at night. The dog jumped on the bed and put its paws on the girl. The girl was terrified and called her father. The man said: "Turn over and sleep." The next day the father believed his daughter had been ridden by the mare. In reality you then had a stagnation of the blood from lying on your back. Children often had it, but old people almost never.
171264: A woman riding a bicycle got a fright when suddenly all the knitting needles flew out of her bag. The woman was convinced it was the work of a witch. That woman regularly had a friar read prayers over her to stay protected against the influence of witches.
171270:
A man had a great deal of misfortune. Three of his children died. When the man left with the wagon, his wife was almost run over. She was black and blue, but she survived the blow. The man himself was run over by a wagon and dragged along for a good six hundred metres. The horses had run away and the man had great difficulty finding the animals again. The man had to have his children's clothes blessed in Dhulsmonde. When the children wore those clothes, nothing happened to them, but when they wore other clothes, they had misfortune. The man had his children blessed in the Church of Our Lady in Roeselare. There the man also received Easter nails to put in the front door, so that the witch could no longer get in. When the children were dead, their backs were completely blue.
The same witch also gave the neighbours lice.
171286: Two people who were outside had left the door open. Suddenly there was a knock on the door, although no one could be seen.
171316: A man from Ardooie who worked in the kiln always heard noise around his house in the evening, although there was nothing to be seen. During the hours he had off at night, the man went home to keep watch. At one point the man went outside to shoot at something he had seen in the field by the light of the moon. But the man missed. On Saturday evenings the man worked as a barber. When a good six men were waiting to be shaved, noise could again be heard around the house. All the customers ran outside. The man's wife sat inside laughing. She was a witch.
171321: On a Saturday a woman took the boat to Bruges. To the farm women who were taking butter to market, the woman said: "When I get home, they had better make sure everything is in order, or else they'll get a beating!" While the woman was away, strange things did indeed happen in the house. There was cleaning and water was thrown about, although no one could be seen.
171339: In Lapscheure there stood a church that was destroyed during the revolt of the Geuzen. The bells of that church were thrown into a pit. Even now some people claim they regularly hear those bells ringing.
171366: In the old days evil often took the shape of a black dog, a cat or a hare.
171368: Some people had seen a witch stick pins into candles. For every candle she let burn, she set the devil on someone. That witch also had special books with which she could harm people.
171372: If the fishermen saw a priest when they had to go to sea, they believed they would have bad luck.
171373: A man coming back from Houthalen kept seeing a big hare running in front of his bicycle. To be able to hit the hare, the man shone his bicycle lamp at the animal. Strangely, the lamp then always went out. The whole way the man was pestered by the hare.
171411: The dead lords of the castle on the Keressen (?) near the Ginsten (?) returned at night because they had buried something somewhere.
171417: In Ramskapelle there was a haunted house. At night the light was blown out and coins were heard falling on the floor. The ghosts were always seen floating above the attic stairs. At night wonderfully beautiful music was heard, although nobody could be seen.
171434: Stalkeersen (will-o'-the-wisps) were the souls of the dead who came back to the churchyard.
171440: A carter transporting trees could not go on because a witch in an inn was blocking his way. The carter went into the inn and said to the witch: "Look, if you don't let me go on with my trees, this building will be torn down!" When the man got back to his horses, the animals could move again.
171446: At the Potteriehoek there were an unusual number of cats. A passer-by who had got lost there could only find his bearings again once the cats had gone.
171494: Two men walking past a small field saw a rabbit running towards a potato field. The lads chased the animal until it suddenly seemed to have vanished. A little further on, one of the men suddenly saw his wife standing there. That woman had once bewitched the other man.
171497: Farmers who could not churn butter went to the friars for advice. If you asked money in exchange for your butter, you could never fall victim to evil. But if you gave your butter away for free, that was another matter.
171505: In the marshes by the inn near ''t Bakje' a goat is said to have roamed in the old days. People came from far and wide to look at the goat, so that the inn had to have beer delivered daily. In the end the police had to forbid people to go there any more, because the crops nearby had all been trampled flat.
171509: A man always saw a whining calf appear when he sat on the toilet. It was a dead person who had returned.
171525: In the church sat a girl who could make mice. "Do that again," said the parish priest. But the girl could no longer do it.
171530: When you were ridden by the mare, you in fact had a stagnation of the blood. At that moment you heard chains rattling.
171534: When a sow was about to give birth to piglets, a mouse was running around in the sty. Every time the mouse squeaked, a piglet dropped dead. That mouse must have been a witch.
171550: A man who went to look at a fishing net hanging out to dry was attacked by cats, so that the man became entangled in the nets. If nobody had got him out, the man would have died.
171554: When people used to see lights at sea, they believed they were omens of bad weather or misfortune.
171560: On a farm there was a cow that always stood sighing in the stable. When one night the lantern had been left burning, a witch was seen sitting on that cow. The farmhand threw a chair at the witch, but the chair flew around the stable a good twenty times without hitting the witch.
171561: On Sunday evenings many people got lost because of a German shepherd (a sheep herder believed to have magic powers).
171569: For three evenings in a row a poacher had seen a hare that he could not shoot down. The next day the poacher put a crushed silver coin in his gun. This time he did manage to hit the hare. The next day a woman who had lost her eye was walking around the village.
171585: A mother whose child was ill often saw a cat come in and jump onto the cradle. One day when the cat was in again, the woman took the hot poker from the stove and caught the animal by the nose. Badly burnt, the cat ran away. The next day the mother found that one of her neighbours had a burnt nose.
171586: Some children were going through a large spruce wood to Sint-Andries. Further on the children were chased by a big goat. Because the goat stayed with them the whole time, the children ran out of the wood as fast as they could. After that the goat was gone.
171604: In the past people were ridden by the mare in their sleep. The victims were then lifted up and carried around until they woke up.
171614: Two women who had been talking during high mass could not get up from their chairs after the service. When vespers began, the women were still sitting there. The priest then said to the women: "What are you still doing here? Will you talk during mass again?" When the women had promised not to do it again, they could stand up.
171616: A girl was bewitched by a witch who passed by every week.
171626: A doodkaars (death candle) was a little light seen burning in the distance. It was the spirit of a dead person who came back. If you pointed at a doodkaars, it flew against the window. The priest came to read prayers over doodkaarsen.
171643: A witch's son had said at school that he could turn bits of paper into mice. When one of the pupils told the schoolmaster, the boy was asked to demonstrate his magic. The boy crumpled all the bits of paper together, threw them in the air and spoke a few words. A little later the whole building was swarming with mice. The astonished schoolmaster said to the boy: "If you can make those mice disappear as well, you needn't come to school any more, because then you are much wiser than I am." The boy made the mice vanish again and no longer went to school.
171650: At a farm in Schuiferskapelle there was much noise. Bells rang, music was played and people were dancing everywhere. The friars banished the evil to the farthest end of the field. All the farms the friars had passed while banishing the evil later suffered misfortune. The pigs died there.
171651: A woman was always ill during her pregnancy. After the birth, the child fell ill. The little boy could not do anything with his hand. After a visit to the friars of Steenbrugge, the child was cured. The first thing the child had to do was take holy water and make the sign of the cross with his hand. He managed it. An old woman was responsible for the evil.
171663: In the churchyard of Houtave a cat roamed that could not be caught. If someone kicked the cat, the animal fell apart into two pieces, which came back together a little further on.
171668: Because the weather was too bad, the Sint-Jan procession was cancelled. The statue of Mary then set out on its own.
171669: The priest of Slijpe came to ask a farmer's wife why her son, who would soon make his First Communion, went to school not in Slijpe but in Middelkerke. "That's none of your business!" the farmer's wife answered. When the priest repeated his question, the woman said to the little child she was carrying on her arm: "Tell him it's none of his business and spit in his face!" Furious, the priest left the farm. One day the priest stood waiting for the schoolboy at the Driewege and asked: "Why don't you go to school in Slijpe?" The child answered: "That's none of your business!" Suddenly a wheelbarrow appeared in front of the boy. The priest climbed into it and the boy had to push the wheelbarrow. Dead tired and soaked in sweat, the boy arrived at the presbytery. There the wheelbarrow and the priest suddenly vanished. A few days later, in his own house, the boy was dragged back and forth between the rungs of a chair by the priest, who had made himself invisible. So the mother could not see the priest. On one of the following days the invisible priest threw the boy into the brook between the Rattevalle and Mannekensvere. The mother was frightened and fetched some strong men, who were able to pull the boy out of the water, for the boy could not move. One day the mother went to the priest of Middelkerke, even though her son attended a secular school. The priest said to the farmer's wife: "We will ask the bishop for advice. As soon as your son is confirmed, he will be cured. But you must make sure that on the day of Confirmation your son gets to Middelkerke before that strange priest can stop him." After the boy was confirmed fourteen days later, nothing strange ever happened to him again.
171675: A woman kicked at a cat that kept following her. Shortly afterwards a woman from the neighbourhood had bruises.
171693: On a farm in Houtkerke butter could no longer be churned. There was always dung in the butter churn. Moreover, the cows fell over in the stable while people stood watching. In the end the friars were sent for.
171703: On a bridge near an old castle in Zwevegem there walked a black dog that people did not dare to pass. That dog was the ghost of a murdered man who had returned after his death.
171705: A pregnant woman met a witch, who gave her a pat on the shoulder. The woman immediately struck the witch on the head. Because she had struck higher, the woman stayed protected against witchcraft.
171725: In Blankenberge a man had hanged himself with a rope from the foot of his bed. When the children had to go to sleep, they were afraid the man's ghost was under their bed. People who had hanged themselves had been ridden by the mare (nightmare spirit) and could therefore come back to haunt. Such people were also not allowed to be buried in church. It was believed that people who had not received a church burial could find no rest after death.
171727: A woman went to the market in Nieuwpoort to sell onions and vegetables. When the woman went home, she met a witch who wanted to buy the leftover onions. Because the woman refused, the witch said: "Sell, and sell diligently." The woman took those same onions to the market three more times, but she never managed to sell them.
171731: In 1940 more than two hundred people died in Tiegem, although there were only eight hundred inhabitants. The mayor at the time had been an officer in the French army. That man preferred to have a coffin made rather than buy bread with the money. One Sunday the mayor opened a grave. According to popular belief someone would die if a grave lay open on a Sunday. That day the mayor dropped dead.
171753: Many devils lingered at the Brupot in Egem. One morning a pregnant maid who worked on a farm had hanged herself. The maid's body was taken naked on a wheelbarrow to the churchyard. The cowherds brought the corpse into the church through the window, because it was not allowed through the door. Meanwhile one of the boys let himself be talked into a bet to sleep in the maid's bed the next night. If he dared, he would get a hundred francs (1). Around eleven o'clock the cowherd lay down in the maid's bed. Around one o'clock the other boys heard howling and roaring in the maid's room. They opened the door and saw the cowherd running around like a madman, saying: "I have seen the devil! He is still there!" Because the cowherd could not be calmed, he was taken to the pigsty. When they went to fetch him the next day, he was calm and said, weeping: "I really saw the devil. God exists and so does the devil. I believe in God now and I am leaving this cursed farm". The boy was never seen again after that.
171769: Sorcerers could make children get 'the old man'. Such children became skin and bone and got shrivelled skin. Those children could not die.
171783: A farmer from Zedelgem saw a little man in a red cap come out of the bakehouse and begin counting his money on a small table. The next day the cowherd said to the farmer: "I know where he has hidden that money". The farmer and the cowherd found the money and became immensely rich. That little red man was a ghost.
171795: A man on his way to a wedding had to pass a sorceress's house. Right at that spot the wheel came off the cart.
171807: A witch who had been to the shop put her marshmallows where children could easily reach them. Yet most parents did not like their children to eat them, because they believed evil was involved.
171828: The captain of a ship always saw his wife appear in the shape of a crow sitting on the mast. Sometimes the woman also came to the ship in a nutshell.
171835: Sometimes people were followed by a little light. A man saw a doodkeers (death candle) at the spot where a horse was buried. Doodkeersen were dead people who came back to point out hidden money.
171846: A girl was coming back from sewing school with her friend, whose mother had just died. When the girls passed the churchyard, they heard a sound: "Ah…ah…". The friend said: "You see, I knew my mother would come back." Frightened, the girls ran home. The other girl's mother also thought the sound had been made by a ghost.
171848:
In Kaster there once lived a woman who could work magic. Every night the woman walked through the streets in a hooded cloak, and she could change herself into a black cat. The municipal council tried to capture the woman, but did not succeed.
The woman often sat brooding on thirteen stones. She would then say she was not allowed to leave her nest. After a while, young donkeys came out of the stones.
One night a man met the strange woman on the road to Tiegem. "Good evening," said the man, to which the woman replied: "The night is for me and the day is for you. Sleep well!" Half an hour later the woman was already seen at the church of Kaster. She was on her way again to do witchcraft somewhere.
171858: Witches took pleasure in making children suffer by sticking pins into a cushion.
171864: In the past it was the custom to hold a bread dole when a well-to-do farmer had died. Rye bread was baked and handed out to the poor. On one farm a noise was always heard in the attic at night, as if everything were being thrown about. At the anniversary Mass for the farmer who had died there, no bread dole had been held. After the rye bread had been baked, no more strange sounds were heard in the attic.
171876: People who were ridden by the mare tried to shout but could not make a sound.
171889: A child who cried all the time had small holes in its skin. On the priest's advice the parents washed the child's sheet in holy water. The parents found all sorts of pins in the sheet.
171891: Because the weather was bad, a carter offered a woman a ride with him. When the wagon began to shake on the bad road, the carter grabbed hold of the woman so she would not fall to the ground. The carter fell ill and two weeks later he died. He should not have touched the witch.
171907: Nobody dared to live in an empty house because it was haunted. At midnight there was always noise there, and the whole house shook to its foundations.
