One day a brave farmer's son moved into the house with his wife. At midnight the man and woman heard noise and saw figures moving in front of the window. When the man heard something in the cellar, he decided to go and look. Three burning candles stood around a small hole. In the hole lay a broken pot of money. The next day the man brought up the money and sent for a clergyman. Part of the money was used to have masses said. The couple were allowed to keep the rest. The money had belonged to the former occupants of the house.
171915: A German Schaper had a relationship with a girl who was said to be a witch. Because the boy wanted to get to the bottom of it, he visited his girlfriend one evening. When the girl asked the boy to leave, he asked for a glass of water. The boy had seen his girlfriend put powder in the water. Convinced it was a sleeping draught, the boy pretended to have fallen asleep. So the boy secretly saw his girlfriend take out a powder, rub it on her face and then say: "Over everything and through everything". Then the girl flew away up the chimney. When the boy wanted to follow his girlfriend, he made a mistake speaking the magic formula and said: "Over everything and through everything". Because of this the boy flew into everything.
171920: A witch came to visit a farm and wanted to see the incubator. The farmer's wife refused, but she would have done better not to. She never got another chick.
171924: A woman who wanted to go to mass in broad daylight could not get across the moat because she was ridden by the mare.
171927: People saw the priest at sea.
171930: In the old days there were women who had evil intentions towards children. When they were with children who wore a scapular, they took the scapular off them, with the excuse that the children could not work like that. By touching the children or laying a hand on their heads and shoulders, they made the children infirm or skin and bone. People faced with such problems had prayers read over their children at Gruuthuze (Bruges) or at the 'Patattemarkt'. Children who had been bewitched usually stayed sickly all their lives.
171935: The nuns had told the director of the convent that their house was haunted, but he did not believe it. One day the director came to visit while the nuns were eating. He heard a noise and said: "It sounds as if a pot of milk is boiling over here." Then he saw with his own eyes that there was no pot of milk anywhere. After that day the director no longer mocked the ghost stories going around about the convent.
171950: A witch had visited a woman. The next day the woman's house was full of rats. After the friars of Tielt had been sent for, the rats disappeared.
171955: If someone was ridden by the mare, you had to call that person's name to free him. Whoever was ridden by the mare had the impression of being strangled by a woman.
171998: A farmer's wife always heard knocking in the stable. But when she went to look, there was nothing to be seen. One day at dusk the farmer's wife saw a woman in a hooded cloak walking. The woman crept under a bridge that the farmer's wife had to cross. When the farmer's wife went to look a while later, the woman had disappeared.
172008: A doctor who was always shabbily dressed and had no maid to keep house for him was laughed at by two boys one day. The doctor fixed the boys to the ground by magic for twenty-four hours. One day the doctor was murdered. No one ever knew who did it.
172019: People believed a castle had once sunk into the ground at 't Hoge Bus. Someone had found a coin in a molehill and decided that the mole had dug the money up on purpose. Some people concluded from this that more money must be hidden there. Moreover, a doodkaars (death candle, a ghostly light) was always seen in a certain spot, which gave treasure hunters even more courage. Even so, no treasure was ever found there.
172022: Some people from Heule claimed that at night the dead from Japan came back and walked around in the marshes of Heule.
172038: In a shop where a woman was about to give birth, the customers could not be served. One of them was a witch. In the end the shopkeeper had to move.
172039: A woman claimed that you could protect yourself against the mare by sleeping with your feet crossed or by putting your clogs upside down next to the bed.
172042: A man with a crooked foot was on his way with three horses to pull a small tree on a timber carriage. On the way the man quarrelled with a woman who wanted to forbid him to drive along that road. That woman made it so that the three horses could no longer move that little tree.
172047: Whoever saw a black cat at a crossroads was in mortal danger. Two men travelling together came across a black cat, which stayed near them the whole time. One of those men never dared to go to that place again.
172071: A man walking past a witch's house one evening saw a black cat that kept running between his legs. When the man grew annoyed with the cat, he struck at the animal with a stick. The cat flew into the air and then landed on the ground again. At that moment the man saw a thousand cats running around his legs. It took a good half hour before the man managed to chase the cats away.
172073: A man going to fetch the doctor at night met a woman at midnight, to whom he said: "Are you out walking at night too?" The woman answered: "The days are for you and the nights are for me." When the man went on, the witch followed him and asked: "Where are you going?" When the man answered: "That's my business," he was bewitched so that he was stuck to the ground, until he said to the woman: "I won't speak to you again." At that moment the woman vanished and the man could go on.
172085: Whoever wanted to protect himself against the mare had to put his clogs next to the bed with the opening facing it.
172089: A newly married couple went to live in Tielt. The owner of the house told them: "You must always close the windows towards evening. And you must certainly not remove that little shrine hanging on the wall." When the couple's child was a year old, it cried all the time. Every time the mother went to look at the child, she saw a tall woman in a blue apron and a cap standing there. The neighbours often saw that strange woman leave the house at around three o'clock at night. Once a big beast had also been seen. Perhaps that woman could turn herself into an animal.
172110: A woman who was always ridden by the mare heard noises on the stairs and a little later saw a ghost in a white sheet standing beside her. Sometimes the mare took the form of a dog or a man. When the woman had prayers read over her by the fathers of Steenbrugge, the rosary broke three or four times.
172112: One Sunday afternoon some men were gathering wood when they suddenly saw the priest approaching. "You would do better to go to vespers," said the priest. The men answered: "But we've got this far already, we might as well keep working a bit longer." A little later the men found a large wooden beam and carried it home on their backs. In the dunes, however, the men got lost. They wanted to throw the beam away, but they were forced to go back and fetch it again.
172119: In Stavele lived a woman who always went to visit small children to bewitch them. Bewitched children became very unhappy.
172125: Someone had hidden his money under a tree on his land. When the land was sold, the tree sawyer Patrice D. found the money. Instead of returning the money to the owner, the sawyer kept it for himself and hid it under a floor tile. After his death the sawyer came back to count the money he had hidden under the tile. One day the rightful owner of the money saw the whole scene. As soon as the ghost had vanished, the man took the money. The man had been told: "Patrice will come back to thank you. Then you must give him your handkerchief instead of your hand". The ghost burnt his hand into the handkerchief.
172127: A baker's daughter was bewitched. The baker was advised to take the girl to the friars, but out of stubbornness he did not. The daughter turned black and blue and eventually died.
172148: A mother who had sixteen children lost six children through the evil hand.
172149: A farmer's wife who sold eggs wanted to dance on the table among the eggs. At that moment a witch passed by and asked the farmer's wife what was in her apron. "Eggs," answered the farmer's wife, but when she went to show the eggs, rats crawled out of her apron. The eggs that fell to the ground as a result were broken. The witch's daughter worked as a maid on a farm. On that farm they often could not churn butter.
172173: A Templar estate was surrounded by water. There was a tree and a well there that no one was allowed to go near. The fathers advised the people to dig a pit. After that the haunting got even worse. After the dead person had returned three days later, the haunting stopped. The clergymen had to live for three days without water or bread.
172187: A priest who had come back from the college in Brugge during the First World War asked a farmer whether he could stay at the farm. Because the farmer refused, the cleric saw to it that the farm had to deal with a real plague of rats. Everywhere the priest was turned away, there were big white rats.
172203: Duitse schapers (German shepherds, travelling shepherds said to have magic powers) could tap beer from their shepherd's staffs.
172221: In the Kortrijkstraat doodkeersen (death candles) could be seen moving back and forth. They were souls of the devil that returned.
172228: In a two-family house in Rumbeke a meowing cat walked around all night. The woman living there poured butter over the cat. The next day the neighbour's eyes were badly burnt.
172231: Because there used to be many witches, children were not allowed to accept a cake from anyone.
172273: A farmer was visited by a beggar woman who asked for alms. The man refused and sent the woman away. When the maid went to milk the cows that evening, she was pushed off her stool because the cows had gone wild. The witch who had come begging was sitting in the hayloft.
172281: A man from Aartrijke stayed the night at a friend's farm. But that farm was terribly haunted. At night the horses came and hung their heads over the stable door. After the priest had exorcised the farm, the haunting fortunately came to an end.
172283: A woman from Lombardsijde had a child who began to tremble with fear every evening. After a friar had read prayers over the child, it became healthy again. It had something to do with the evil hand.
172284:
A brother and a sister had agreed that whoever died first would come back after death to tell what things were like in the afterlife. When the sister had been buried three days and the coffin turned round three times (?), the brother said: "Ah sister, is it as the books tell us? Oh sister, are you in pain? Tell me how things are here." The dead sister answered:
"Even if there were a hundred mouths
And in each mouth a hundred tongues,
Brother, I could not tell you
How the souls here are made to suffer."
172302: Some people who came to live in Watou were warned by their new neighbours about a certain woman from the village. When that woman one day brought a bunch of grapes, the people threw the fruit into the cesspit because they were afraid of being bewitched.
172319: A strong, healthy woman worked in a shop in Proven. One day, however, that woman fell ill after a witch had been in her shop.
172326: A girl worked as a maid for a parish priest. A woman who was probably a witch always came to the presbytery. When the maid lay in bed at night, she heard that woman coming up the stairs. The woman would then lie on the maid's feet and then squeeze her throat shut. In this way the maid was tormented by the mare as many as ten times in one night.
172327:
In winter a woman was visited by her neighbour, who needed a doctor for his wife. The woman went to Sint-Anne for him. She left around eight o'clock and arrived at the doctor's around half past eight. The doctor, however, did not come home until eleven. When the woman said that her neighbour was ill, the doctor answered: "I know what she has" and gave the woman a small bottle. Then the woman went back home. When she had almost reached the end of the wood, she saw a hare, which walked along with her.
If the woman stood still, the hare stood still too. If she went on, the hare walked along with her. The woman was afraid because the hare kept following her throughout the whole way through the wood.
172332: The area near 't Blauw Kasteel used to be haunted. One day when the castle's resident was returning from Oostkamp, he saw a light burning in a copse by the road. The man fearlessly went to look and saw four men sitting at a table playing cards in the copse. The man knew one of the card players. That copse was called 'het Toverboske' (the magic wood). The card player urged the man not to tell anyone what he had seen.
172336:
A boatman who was in Antwerp when the First World War broke out volunteered as a soldier. The man was killed near Nieuwpoort. His body was never found.
The man's mother, who lived in Duinkerke, thought one night that she saw her dead son in his soldier's uniform sitting on the toilet. The woman was said to have had that vision around the time her son was killed.
172337: A priest who still had Masses to say somewhere appeared in a church at night and said: "When I could do it, I would not. Now that I want to do it, I may not. And everyone who is not of my century (?) should not be here either!"
172341: A man from Herzele had much misfortune with his farm. One morning the man found that one of his cows had been hanged by a chain. When the man let his pig out, it dropped dead on the threshold. The farmer went for advice to the friars of Catsberg. These clergymen, however, said they were not strong enough and sent the man to the friars of Ypres. Those friars predicted that the man would meet the witch and advised him to be friendly. The witch would then come back once more and offer the farmer a franc, but the farmer had to refuse it. The next morning at about three o'clock the farmer met the witch in Watou. A day later the witch indeed appeared with a franc. The farmer refused to take the money and never saw the witch again.
172348: People who had special powers had sold their soul to the devil for a few years. After that time those people were free again. In reality, however, it often happened that such people had an accident, so that they died before their time was up and were carried off by the devil. It could then happen that those people had still been seen in the morning and afterwards had vanished without a trace for good.
172366: A woman who was said to be able to work magic sold her best cow to her son-in-law. Once the man had the cow, the animal did not give another drop of milk. The man got angry and quarrelled with his mother-in-law. Then the mother-in-law said to the man: "I wish your child would die!" For the woman's daughter was pregnant. Six weeks after the birth, the child did indeed die.
172375: The mare was a little old woman who walked around the bed and strangled people.
172378: A man out with two horses suddenly saw a third horse walking along. A moment later that third horse had vanished again.
172388: A fourteen-year-old girl worked as a maid for an old farmer. Every night around eleven o'clock the girl had to get up to milk the cow so that the farmer could drink milk. Every night the girl saw a pig in the cowshed. When the farmer went to look, however, there was nothing to be seen. When another man from the neighbourhood also said he had seen a pig, the farmer began to cry. After he had a Mass said to the Holy Spirit, the pig did not appear again.
172407: Whoever was ridden by the mare was actually dreaming. Those dreams, however, were always deceptive.
172413: Whatever one met on the street at night had to be left alone, for it might well be the devil. A man who one night took a rabbit home and put it in his rabbit hutch found the next morning that the rabbit had turned into a skull.
172426: Near the toveresseknok (witches' hill) between Izegem and Lendele stood a farm that was bewitched. Every night a fire broke out, while the cows went mad and the table flew around the house. A woman from the neighbourhood began to tremble every time she entered the farm. The woman sensed that a witch had put a toad under the threshold. As soon as the toad was removed, the strange happenings came to an end.
172457: A poacher wandering in the woods one night was startled when a violent storm suddenly blew up.
172458: When a friar left the gospel lying open on the altar in church, four or five witches could not leave the church.
172459: Sometimes the gospel was left lying open after mass. People believed that the witches could then not leave the church. In Zedelgem three witches are said to have remained sitting in the church this way.
172480: At the brick kiln pits in Veldegem, sunken bells could be heard ringing at midnight.
172484: A woman had got lost on two consecutive evenings. On the third evening her sister went with her. On the way the two women saw something black swarming. They sat down, began to pray and said: "If you are of God, say who you are. If you are of the devil, go away." A little later the black apparition had vanished. After the woman had been exorcised, she never experienced anything like it again.
172492: People who were ridden by the mare had a bad dream and felt unwell on waking.
172521: A woman peddling knitting wool came to a house where she gave something to a little child. The following night that child was almost hanged by a blade of straw, although there was no straw at all in its bed.
172529: In Ingooigem lived a witch whom everyone feared. People who met the witch made the sign of the cross and quickly said a prayer. One day a woman went to the witch with her son. A little later the little boy's hair fell out.
172534: A woman who walked along the beach at night always heard people talking.
172535: Whenever grinding was done in the evening at a miller's in Kachtem, someone always died. A new farmhand, who also ground in the evening, saw a little cat scratching at the mill gate with its paw and stuck a knife into the paw. The next morning the miller's wife had a large wound on her arm.
172542: At a farm the cows in the cowshed were untied every evening. People tried to tie the animals up again, but could not. The rabbits ran up the iron fencing, the hens danced in the yard and the horses no longer wanted to work. The farmer had to leave his farm as many as six times. In the end the man died.
172555: Doodkeersen (death candles) were dead people who returned.
172565: When there was a ball somewhere, no one could enter the hall as long as the priest was walking about there.
172568: A woman claimed that she always heard knocking in her house at twelve o'clock at night, as if someone was walking around in the attic. The woman went to the friars to have prayers of deliverance read over her. The clergymen also gave her a blessed medal. In the end the frightened woman moved house anyway.
172569: A girl from Vlissegem was terrified of a witch from the village. Even when all the windows and doors were closed, that witch could still make the rattling of chains be heard.
172573: In Ichtegem there stood a barn where strange things happened. Every morning the planks of the barn had been pulled loose, so that they had to be nailed back on each time.
172585: A very rich man had lived in Diependale. Every evening a headless horse came there to count his money. Although most people no longer dared to go to that place, a brave man once went to have a look. After the man had taken the money, the horse was never seen again.
172589: In Koekelare lived a farmer who had a litter of healthy piglets. One day a woman came to visit, stroked the piglets and said: "Look what lovely piglets!" Later that day all the piglets died.
172595: A young couple lived five metres from a witch. The couple apparently could not have children. After a long time a baby was born after all. The child, however, did not live long. People believed the witch was responsible for the couple's misfortune.
172599: In the churchyard a little candle burned every night on one of the graves. It was said to be a dead man who had to return because he had not done what he was supposed to do.
172601: By saying a certain prayer, sorcerers could send rats to a house. Such rats could then also be sent on to another place.
172604: Fishermen were very superstitious. For example, they told of water devils. They also believed it brought bad luck to take currant bread or a dog on board. When the fishermen set off for their ship, they also did not want anyone to wish them a good voyage.
172605: In Middelkerke lived a woman who owned books of magic and could put the evil hand on people. After the witch had pulled up grass for her rabbits in someone's field, nothing grew in that field any more. When the farmer chased the witch away, she set the field on fire. Whenever someone was buried, the witch followed the funeral procession to the churchyard last, twenty-five paces behind.
172607: An Augustinian monastery in Elsegem was haunted. One day the ghost Lange Jeanne was caught, put in a little bottle and buried under an oak tree. It was said that the ghost came one metre closer every year. In a few hundred years Lange Jeanne would be back at the monastery.
172634: A woman had stayed sitting all alone in the church. As soon as the sexton closed the missal, the woman had vanished.
172646: At the pits by the church of Marialoop, bells could be heard ringing from afar every year on Christmas night.
172648: At the Vierstraat in Deerlijk a ghost always appeared by a tree at midnight. A man who was afraid of nothing decided one night to go and have a look at the Vierstraat. The ghost said to the man: "The day for you, the night for me, and pass on by!" Terrified, the man ran away. The next day he was dead.
172653: In a house where a small child lay in the cradle, a woman often came to visit who always tried to get close to the baby. Because the mother said: "God will reward you", the witch could not reach the cradle. One day, however, the witch did reach the cradle, because she had come in while the mother was in the kitchen. That same evening the baby was gravely ill. After the priest had read prayers over the child, it recovered. That woman never entered the house again.
172677: A widow from Meulebeke had remarried. At night the new husband saw his wife's dead husband appear. The woman, however, saw nothing. The man went to the friars, who advised him to ask the ghost why it appeared. The ghost then said: "You still have to go on pilgrimage to the chapel of Bijstand in Meulebeke. You must pray from the moment you set out until you arrive." On the way the man could hardly go any further. Drenched in sweat, he reached the chapel. Ten minutes later a heavy burden fell from him. After that the dead man appeared no more.
172682: A farmhand had died on a farm. In the evening the dead farmhand came to haunt the horse stable where he used to sleep. Doors and windows were heard banging open and shut. The dean came and sprinkled the farm with holy water.
172689: The farmhand of a farm in Eggewaartskapelle had to fetch the farmer's wife with the covered wagon. When the party was on the road from Nieuwpoort to Eggewaartskapelle, a heavy thunderstorm broke out. A while later the wagon was almost at the farm, and at that moment the weather cleared a little. The farmhand then said to the farmer's wife: "God willing, we will get home all right," to which she replied: "God willing or not, we will get there anyway!" Then the farm dog ran to the farmhand and bit through the rope of the horses. The horses ran to their stable with the farmhand on their backs. When the farmhand came back outside, he saw a large pit into which the wagon had disappeared. No one ever managed to reach the bottom of that pit with any object.
172691:
A woman could turn herself into a rabbit.
A poacher had tried several times in vain to shoot the rabbit. In the end the poacher sought advice from the priest, who told him to put a piece of a blessed wedding ring in his gun. When the poacher had done so, he shot the rabbit in the head. The next day a woman from the village had a wound on her face.
172717: A farmhand who worked for a farmer went out every evening to play the werewolf. One day, when the farmer's wife went to bake bread while the farmhand was working in the field, she was amazed to see a dog skin lying in the oven. As soon as the farmer's wife had thrown the skin into the fire, the farmhand came running up to save his skin. But it was already too late: the skin had burned up and the farmhand was released. Werewolves were people who had sold their soul.
172734: When you were ridden by the mare, you actually had a cardiac arrest. People who became victims of the mare believed that a sorceress was pressing on them with a heavy object. You then had to throw a crucifix or holy water over the victim. That would make the witch take on her true form again so she could be caught. If that failed, you had to go to the fathers. Animals could not be ridden by the mare.
172735: In Waregem there once stood a castle where bells could be heard ringing in the evening. Near that castle there was also always a lot of wind, although elsewhere it was calm. If people walked two by two in a row, they could hear the ghostly sounds even better.
172737: On his way home a man was followed by a pretty little cat that kept running between his legs. The man took the cat home and put it in a tub. His wife laid a wedding ring on the lid of the tub. The next morning the man and woman were astonished to find not the cat but their neighbour sitting in the tub.
172760: A man whose child had been gravely ill for five or six days went to a friar for advice. The clergyman told the man: "Someone will come to visit and ask for something. You must give the visitor what she asks for." No sooner said than done. A while later the child recovered.
172766: Two men from Staden were coming back together from Zarren. At a certain moment one of the men decided to take a shortcut. The other relieved himself by the side of the road. After a few minutes that man saw a headless goat walking. He believed it was his uncle and called out: "Uncle, don't frighten me!" The man wanted to get up, but fell over backwards...
172775: In Arlembois in Harelbeke there stood a house that was haunted. Anything placed above the door frame was thrown to the floor at night, although nothing could be seen.
172776: On a farm in Zeldonk a beggarwoman had been sent away without being given anything. She went off angry, saying: "You will regret that!" The next day no butter could be churned on the farm. Moreover, copper pins were found at the bottom of the churn. The friars advised the people to give the beggarwoman something. When they had done so, the misfortune ended.
172799:
A doctor who was always shabbily dressed went to visit a sick person one night. In the Kapelleriebos in Wijtschate the doctor was stopped by two policemen who thought he was a tramp. When the policemen asked the man who he was and where he was going, the man answered: "You can stay and wait here for a while. I'll come and tell you tomorrow." The doctor fixed the two men to the ground by magic until he returned from his sick call and said: "Now you may go on. Now you know who I am."
One day the doctor was murdered. No one was ever able to find out who did it.
172804: In the old days, when people heard a death owl call, they believed someone in the neighbourhood would die.
172809: In a street in Hondschote everyone bought milk from the same woman. Strangely, the people on one side of the street had good milk, while those on the other side had bad milk. The priest ought to be called in to pray the evil away.
172820: A farm in Proven was haunted. Anyone passing by at night saw goats walking about and coaches driving without horses. A farmer's wife who had to go and milk her cows could not find the animals. When the animals threatened to break loose one Sunday evening, the farmer's wife went for help. A man from the neighbourhood reluctantly went along with her. When the two reached the stable, the man cried in annoyance: You stupid woman, they're all lying here asleep!
172854: A wizard could enter a place without opening the door.
172857: A woman went with a wheelbarrow to fetch turnips. While she was working in the field, her child fell from the wheelbarrow. A witch passing by picked the child up and put it back on the barrow. A few days later the child fell ill and eventually died. The child had two large bruises on its arms where the witch had held it.
172863: 't Blauw Huis in Beernem had a barn that had been built by the devil. That is why no one managed to finish that barn. Even after three years of work it could not be done.
172875: Whenever a child had been born somewhere, the witches fought to be the first to reach it.
172877: On a farm the cows were tied by their tails to the ceiling beams. Because of witchcraft it also often happened that people could not churn butter. To drive out the witchcraft, the Gospel of Saint John was read after Mass. Everyone had to stay in the church until it was finished.
172884: In Eggewaartskapelle a man went to steal apples from the priest during mass. When mass was over, the thief stood as if nailed to the ground, with the apple in his hand and his mouth open.
172908: A girl whose little brother had measles heard a dog barking at night from her bed. This was believed to be an omen of death. When shortly afterwards the girl heard knocking on her door, she got up and said to her mother: "Mother, they're knocking on my door", to which the woman replied: "You're dreaming, go back to sleep quickly. Your little brother has just died." The girl was convinced that her little brother had come to knock on her door before he departed.
172936: A pregnant woman was bewitched by a witch, so that the child was not entirely healthy. Because the newborn cried all day, the woman went to the friars for advice; they shook their heads and blessed the child.
172955: A farm in Bissegem was bewitched by the maid who worked there. One day when the farmer's wife came in, the cradle with the baby was hanging from the ceiling. At her wits' end, the farmer's wife sent for the priests, but the clergymen were powerless. After the farmer's wife had dismissed the maid, no more strange things happened on the farm.
172980: A man had to babysit on a farm where there was a little daughter. The child always lay crying in her bed. Every day a neighbour woman came to the farm to ask for milk. The man always carried something blessed with him. When the neighbour came by again one day, the man said to her: "It's cold. Come and sit by the fire for a while." The man had put something blessed under the neighbour's chair, so that the woman could not get up. Meanwhile the man kept fetching more wood to make the fire hotter. The neighbour grew hotter and hotter. When she could no longer bear it, the man said to her three times: "You must help that child, because you can." In the end the neighbour gave the man her house key and said: "You must go to my house. In the cupboard you must take one of the doll's heads and pull the pins out of it." The child had always been tormented by the pins stuck in the doll's head.
172982: Some women could make people lose their way.
172989: A little old woman had died in Wingene. In the morning people saw footprints on the ground, exactly as if the dead woman had walked there. They raked the ground, but the next morning there were footprints again. This went on for a whole week. It was the woman who had returned.
173000: In Sint-Jan a woman who had stolen a great deal had died. In the evening people heard a knock at the door. When they opened it, they saw a deer standing there, carrying an unreadable message between its antlers. Because no one could decipher the text, they sent for the priest. He said it read: "You must always live honestly and decently!"
173015: In Reningelst lived a suspicious woman who made strange movements with her hand over the chicks. Shortly afterwards all the animals died.
173027: Whoever walked past the Duivelsput (Devil's Pit) on Christmas night could hear bells ringing at twelve o'clock. For a church was said to have once sunk into that pit on Christmas Day.
173028: A man returning around midnight from his work in a field in Aalbeke saw, by the high bridge not far from the castle, a light moving from the crucifix towards the castle. When the man passed the castle, the strange light had vanished. A man who passed along the canal early in the morning because he had to catch the train in Ingelmunster saw that the castle was on fire. When the man went home that evening, there was no trace of a fire at all. A man who feared neither God nor commandment passed the crucifix saying: "Just because you hang there on that cross, don't think I'm going to take off my cap for you. You won't see my hair!" When the man got home, he had no hair left.
173040: In Diependale (between Wijtschate and Hollebeke) lived strange people who did not shrink from attacking someone. One day a doctor from Wijtschate passed by there. The robbers decided to take the doctor's money, but the doctor bewitched the robbers so they were stuck to the ground until he returned.
173048: A farmer's wife who always added water to the milk had to haunt the cellar after her death. One day people heard the haunting farmer's wife say: "Water and milk, but I forgot my soul."
173087: A woman who had fled during the war and was hiding in a house saw a cat come in every day that could not be chased away by anything. One day there was hot butter on the stove. The woman poured the butter over the cat's head, and it ran off howling. The next day the neighbour had burns all over her face. The neighbour explained that she had accidentally got a bowl of hot fat in her face. The woman believed it. But when her husband came home, he said: "The neighbour was burnt by your butter!" From that day on people knew that the neighbour was a witch.
173089: A man on his way home met a woman who asked whether he wanted to play cards with her. When the man refused, he could not get home. He tried some twenty times, but there was nothing he could do. After the man had played a game of cards with the woman, he got home without any trouble.
173097: On a haunted farm the cows and calves climbed up the walls. The people suspected a woman from the neighbourhood of the evil and went to the friars of Steenbrugge. The road to Steenbrugge was very hard, so the people were drenched in sweat when they arrived. After the friars had sprinkled the animals with holy water, everything on the farm returned to normal.
173099: On a farm in Bellegem all the animals were untied at night. The cowherd was not afraid and decided to spend a night in the stable. After midnight the cowherd heard the animals pulling at their chains. The cowherd ran quickly out of the stable and shouted at the farmhouse window: "Ghosts, ghosts!"
173105: At a Templar farmstead people always saw white friars walking about. They were dead Templars who came back to haunt. When things had been tidied up in the evening, everything was turned upside down again the next morning.
173106: In Bambeke lived a girl who was bewitched. Whenever she wanted to go to church, she began to sweat and had to turn back. When a carter took her to Sint-Sixtus, the horses began to foam at the mouth and sweat. The friars gave the girl a medal, which broke the spell.
173130: On a farm worked a boy who was suspected of witchcraft. It often happened that the wheelbarrow came rolling along by itself, without anyone nearby. One day someone struck the wheelbarrow with a stick. The next day the suspected boy had a wound on his forehead.
173132: There were horses that could be heard walking at night but could not be seen.
173136: A woman was ridden by the mare two nights in a row. As a result she lay drenched in sweat in bed. The fathers gave the woman a prayer card to put under her bed. After that she was rid of the mare for good. If she had not been taken to the fathers, she would have died.
173138: Around midnight a man saw a little light flickering in the churchyard. Convinced it was a returned dead person, the man ran home terrified.
173143: Sorceresses could torment small children by sticking pins into a little doll.
173167: A mother who had one child was always visited by a woman who came to borrow a darning needle. One day the woman came to fetch an ordinary needle. After a while the child fell ill and died. The child was completely full of needles. The witch had stuck the needles into a little doll in order to torment the child that way.
173181: A priest had to visit a sick person who was staying on a lord's land. Because the lord would not let the priest pass, the lord had to wander about among the thorns all night.
173200: A man told a friend that strange things were happening at his home. Every night a cat walked around the house. The man and his wife had already tried throwing a stone at the animal, but the cat seemed to be invulnerable. His friend advised the man to shoot at the cat. One Sunday evening the man shot at the cat. The next day people said that a woman from the village was limping. When she was asked what was wrong, the woman said: "Someone has done something to me, but the culprit may yet regret it later!"
173208: The little castle on the corner of the Nieulantlaan in Sint-Andries was haunted. A goat, a calf, a cow or a cat always roamed there, blocking the way of passers-by.
173211: On a corner lived three women who could turn themselves into cats. One day the three cats had been given a good beating, so that one of the animals was dead, the second had lost a leg and the third had a wound on its head. One of the women who lived on the corner was dead, another had lost an arm and the third had something wrong with her head.
173226: One Saturday a farmer's wife told her maid to melt lard for the sauce. The maid was tired of lard, however, and decided to use butter. The cat walking around the house kept saying: "Lard, lard!" The maid poured hot fat over the cat. Later the farmer's wife turned out to have a burnt face.
173247: A child had fallen ill after a witch had been near it and had said: "What a lovely child!" After that the child had begun crying incessantly. The child was overlezen (read over with prayers) by the friars, who asked who had been near the child. In the end the child died anyway. It had a scratch on its chest and had been pierced with pins from the navel to the throat.
173248: Some people going from Alveringem to Veurne could not get past a woman who sat combing her hair by the roadside.
173264: A man who lived on the Deizelhoek had to pass the churchyard every evening on his way home. He would then hear a voice calling: "What time is it?" When the man asked: "Who's there?", there was no answer. He only saw a glimmer of light floating back and forth above the corpses. It was one of the returning dead.
173266:
A woman had a little son who had been bewitched by a witch. An hour after the woman had put her child to bed, he began to cry and tremble. His teeth chattered and his tongue hung out of his mouth. Especially around All Saints' the boy suffered badly. The child was ill from the age of five to nine. Then a friar read prayers over him. The clergyman was drenched in sweat.
The witch had bewitched the child by means of her husband's evil books. One day when the boy had visited the witch, he had seen her reading a book. She quickly shut it when she saw the boy come in.
173277: A farmer who had remarried had much misfortune with his animals. That evil was caused by the farmer's new wife. After the farmer had received something blessed from the priest, the misfortune ended.
173285: A small child was bewitched after a neighbour had given it a kiss. The child got 'the old man' (a wasting illness) and became skin and bone.
173302: A woman had come back after her death because she had not done her duty.
173310: If a witch offered holy water after mass, you were bewitched or covered in lice. If a witch struck your shoes, you had to strike the witch higher up to break her power.
173341: A man and his mother saw a headless horse walking.
173358: When there was bad luck on a ship, people looked for a culprit, because they believed that person was the cause of the bad luck.
173361: In the Vriebus lived a lord of the castle who was not very religious. Shortly after his death, an owl was heard calling in the oak tree every night. Thousands of people came at night to watch and listen to the owl. It was said that it was the ghost of the lord, who had returned. One day someone shot the owl, had it stuffed and gave it to the countess. After that the calling was never heard again.
173365: People who were ridden by the mare began to cry and called out: "Oo, oo, oo...." When those people woke up, it was all over. A man who was ridden by the mare every night always said in the evening: "If you hear me shout tonight, you must wake me immediately. Then I am freed."
173376: A farmer owned only one horse, which stood in the stable where the stable hand also slept. When the farmer came home one evening, to his great astonishment he saw not one but two horses in the stable. "The other horse wears horseshoes and you don't! We must do something about that", the farmer said to the animal. The farmer then sent his stable hand to the smith in the middle of the night. The smith got up, came to shoe the horse and then put it back in the stable. The next morning the second horse had disappeared and the farmer's wife was crying out with horseshoes on her hands and feet.
173389: In the castle of Moorsele lived a rich woman who led an immoral life. She often held parties to which she invited low sorts of people. After the woman died, no one dared to live in the castle because it was haunted.
173397: A woman who worked as a maid on a haunted farm saw that the cows in the stable had been tied by their tails to the beams. When the maid had to fetch straw in the barn, the bales fell down by themselves. When the maid came back a little later, the straw had vanished. When the maid had to scoop flour or beans, she was pushed into the barrel, although no one could be seen.
173428: People who were jealous of someone could make the mare ride that person.
173444: When a child suffered from some health problem or other, people believed it had been bewitched by a witch. Such children were often taken to the friars to have prayers read over them.
173457: A man had learned from a fortune teller that he would lose his life because of a white horse. From then on the man anxiously avoided every white horse he saw. One day the man had to shelter from a thunderstorm in a café called 'In 't wit peerd verkoopt men bier' (Beer is sold at the White Horse). The man fell on his head and was killed instantly.
173475: On a farm a big rat always sat watching the animals. When people struck at the rat, they could never hit it. Moreover, there was always misfortune on that farm.
173478: A family from Woumen had a child suffering from an incurable illness. One day the parents took the child by horse and cart to the friars of Ieper. When they came to a wall, the horse suddenly could go no further, so the people had to continue on foot with the child. The moment they took the child out of the cart, they saw a woman in a black hood standing behind the wall. The friars read prayers over the child until drops of sweat fell on the prayer book. Then the friars said: "It is all right. You may go now. Your child was bewitched by the woman who was behind that wall." Through the friars' prayers that woman never came back.
173491: A woman lived in a house in Koolskamp. When a farmer wanted to live in that house, the woman was driven out and cried: "You will never have luck again!" Within three years two of the farmer's daughters died. He also had much misfortune with his animals.
173500: On a farm in Oostrozebeke there was a plague of rats. A German shepherd promised to drive the rats away on condition that everyone kept silent. When the shepherd made the rats leave, the maid blurted out: "Look, there's one that's limping!" At that all the rats ran back to the farm.
173504: Some people could torment someone by sticking needles into a burning candle.
173506: Some farms were haunted. When the farmer was indoors, the sound of the flail could be heard outside, although nothing could be seen.
173508: At night people always heard a voice calling: "Where must I put them, where must I put them?" One night a brave man answered: "Put them where you pulled them out." The next morning the posts were back in the right place. Since then the voice has not been heard again. It was the ghost of a dead man in purgatory who felt remorse for the land he had stolen from someone else.
173521: A witch who lived with her daughter had made her son-in-law ill. It was said that a file should be laid in the bed of someone made ill by bewitchment. The man nevertheless died at the age of twenty-seven. Afterwards the woman was thrown out of the house by her daughter.
173527: A man came back to haunt after his death. Fireballs flew about and the son-in-law was thrown from the storage loft above the goats. Every night the ghost could be heard hammering. After his death it took the man six years to get home from the churchyard. The clergy came to pray, but they had great difficulty driving the man's spirit away.
173536: A mother with a child was visited one day by a witch. From then on all sorts of things went wrong with the child. In the end the child even died.
173550: A drunkard walking home one evening met a big dog at a bridge. It was a water devil with a long chain around its neck. When the man reached the second bridge, he saw a big dog sitting there too. At the third bridge the drunkard saw a multicoloured cat with a long tail. The drunkard asked: "You pretty spotted cat, where are you going?" The next moment some twenty-five or thirty cats were leaping around the man. The animals all began to sing: "X asked me: 'You pretty spotted cat, where are you going?'"
173551: A boy who had been given an apple by a woman on a Sunday afterwards felt pain everywhere, as if there were pins stuck all over his body.
173601: A woman claimed that at night she had seen her dead mother appear, asking for prayers. The woman even told her brothers and sisters what she had seen.
173603: In a house in Deerlijk a black cat appeared every morning when the woman of the house was stirring the porridge. One day the woman poured boiling milk over the animal. The next day the woman found that one of her neighbours had a burnt face. After that the cat did not appear again and nothing strange happened in that house anymore.
173608: A man found that a black dog stole his bread from his kitchen every day. The man had shot at the dog but had not been able to hit it. One day the priest advised the man to shoot at the dog with blessed lead. In this way the man managed to hit the dog in its hind leg. The next day the neighbour woman lay in bed with a gunshot wound. The woman died of her injury after receiving the last rites from that same priest.
173628: People who were ridden by the mare could not say a word and felt as if someone was lying on them. If someone called that person's name, the mare was gone.
173633: Some people who had been on a pilgrimage to Aalter were accompanied by the 'klutterhond' (rattling dog). That was a dog with bells. The dog did the pilgrims no harm. It went along as far as Aalter and waited there until the people went back home. It was believed that the dog was a cursed soul being punished in this way.
173645: A sleeping man woke up when he heard a kitten meow. The man tried to grab the animal, but he did not manage. Finally the man ended up at a hut where beautiful music was played and someone sang: "That man asked me, you pretty spotted kitten, where do you come from?" The next moment the cat had vanished and the man sat alone in the hut.
173649: A woman was playing cards with some friends. When the friends had to go home, the woman said: "Are you afraid? I will send a companion with you." The woman sent a big black dog along with the friends. As soon as the friends got home, the dog had vanished without a trace.
173660: A man walking along the canal at night was chased on the bridge by seven cats. The man kicked at the animals, but could not hit them. When he got home, the man was drenched in sweat.
173662: A sorcerer saw a man beat a little dog to death and said: "You mustn't do that, you are harming the animal! Tomorrow you will have many to kill!" The next day the man's house was full of rats.
173669: A child that had been touched by a witch got 'the old man' (illness). The child wasted away completely and looked like Our Lord crucified. In the end the child was taken to the friars of Steenbrugge.
173670: A priest who had been abducted during the war was guarded by armed men. Even so, at a certain moment the priest managed to vanish without a trace.
173673: Some men who were hunting near the castle saw the branches of a hedge part at midnight. A woman appeared and asked the men what they were doing there. The hunter ran off with his friend. When the two reached the other hunters, it turned out that all the hunters had experienced the same thing.
173679: A mother was visited by a neighbour who needed peas. At that very moment the mother's little son began to cry. The mother then pulled a piece of wood from the stove and chased the witch outside. The friars gave the mother something to put under the threshold so that the witch could no longer come in.
173690:
A boy of eight or nine had been struck by the evil hand. An old woman came every day with her daughter to visit the boy's family.
One day the boy's brother went to the friars for advice. The clergymen predicted that the woman would come back and undo the evil. The woman was to be left in peace. She would then never return.
The boy, however, remained unhappy all his life. He died at the age of thirty-two.
173702: A man travelling with a foal met a witch, who said: "By the time you get home, that foal will be dead!" Yet the animal had been perfectly healthy when the man set out with it. When the man got home, the foal dropped dead.
173717: A nobleman who was not a Christian had taken his wife to mass in Bruges. As was his habit, the nobleman went walking in the woods on Sunday morning with his two dogs. In those woods there had long been a strange-looking bird that cried: "Tsachoe, tsachoe!" People had often tried to shoot that strange bird, but they never succeeded. When the nobleman had died, people said the coffin had been filled with stones, because the man's body had disappeared...
173729: In Eernegem there were pits in which bells were said to have once sunk.
173732: A man who had been unjust had to haunt after his death. A drunkard heard a voice ask: "Where should I put it?" The man had pulled out a boundary post. After the drunkard answered: "Just put it there", the dead man was released.
173735: People from Lo (?) had a baby that did not grow and cried all the time. They had prayers read over the child by the friars of Ieper. At one point the mother had great difficulty holding the child. The child had been bewitched by a midwife. The friars gave the mother an Easter nail, so that the witch could no longer come in.
173748: A veterinarian who came across a thief fixed the thief to the ground by magic. When the veterinarian came back, he said to the thief: "Well, are you going to do that again in future?" "No," answered the thief. The veterinarian then let the thief go.
173786: One evening the farmer and his wife from a farm in Merkem were visiting friends. Around eleven o'clock the wife said: "Come, let's go home." But the host kept saying: "Do stay a little longer!" When the farmer and his wife were visiting there again one evening, they saw bolts on the doors everywhere. After a while that witchcraft did come to an end. The people went to the friars of Ieper, who gave them powders to put in the cows' water and prayers to hang in the animals' stables. Every evening at twelve o'clock they heard noise. After the people had said a prayer for nine days, the ghosts left through the front door.
173790: On a farm, noises were always heard on the roof. One day the farmer said: "I'll have to shoot those pigeons some time." One day the pigeons were gone, but then there were mice in the attic. Strangely, the animals shuffled instead of squeaking. The farmer's wife poured boiling water over the mice, but the animals were not scalded and stayed alive. The Dutch farmhand who worked on the farm said: "Now it's full of mice here, next there will be rats." That never happened, however, because the farmer went to the friars.
173808: A parish priest could make lice sent by a German shepherd disappear. He could also hold back a fire to save other houses from the flames.
173813: Some fishermen from Nieuwpoort were annoyed by a cat that kept getting under their feet. The cat had heard that the fishermen wanted to kill her and sat in a tree. When the fishermen began to beat the branches, the cat fell into a well. When they got home, the fishermen found that their grandmother had fallen into a well.
173816: An old woman touched a small child, saying: "What a beautiful child!" The child cried itself to death.
173834: A doctor could tap wine from a table leg.
173854: People who had been ridden by the mare were completely confused.
173868: In Eernegem there lived a rich framasson (freemason). When that man had died and his coffin was being taken to the cemetery, the lights of the hearse suddenly went out. His family understood that the devil had come to fetch his soul.
173894: In a castle in the Goudberg in Brugge a man had hidden his money. After the man's death nobody could find the money. That was why everyone who spent the night in the castle was dead the next morning. When one night a man found the money, the ghost no longer appeared.
173903: If little lights were seen somewhere, it meant that money was hidden in that spot.
173922: A man lying in his bed one evening saw a goat come down the stairs. When the goat climbed on top of the man, he could hardly breathe. The man set his clogs with the toes pointing at the door and laid a bread knife on his belly with the blade facing up to protect himself against the mare.
173926: A man on his way to slaughter saw the snow-covered thistles moving and became so frightened that he dared not take another step, not even with a knife in his hand. The man believed that a ghost was causing the movements.
173944: A brother and a sister always heard chairs scraping at night. The wife of another brother had not long been dead at the time. After the friars had been asked to say masses for the dead woman, the scraping was no longer heard.
173945: The station at Anzegem used to be haunted. The spirits could be heard talking there, although nothing could be seen. When it had snowed in winter, no footprints of the spirits could be seen there either.
173958: A German shepherd who had committed a crime was chased by the police. The shepherd then turned all his sheep into molehills and himself into a wild bee until the policemen had gone.
173959: A man coming home in the dark one evening suddenly saw an aalkarteel (a bundle of worms used for eel fishing) drop to the ground in front of his feet. That evening the man came home deathly pale with fear.
173986: In Moere lived a woman who could do witchcraft. If she wanted to, she could make it so that people could not get past her house.
173992: A cattle dealer had to walk to Brugge every morning. One morning the man saw a fireball. People believed such phenomena were omens of disasters. Shortly afterwards the war of 1870 broke out.
174003: Whoever was ridden by the mare felt short of breath and felt as if something invisible was seizing him by the throat.
174029: In 1911 or 1912 it was haunted at 't Oge between Kemmel and Nieuwkerke. People heard goats bleating in the air there, and the grass was completely trampled flat.
174057: In Les Moères lived a girl engaged to a young man who had to go to war in 1870. "He will not come back," said a woman from the village. The witch's prediction came true.
174073: A farm in Avelgem was haunted. At night there were sounds as if butter was being churned, bread baked and the stable mucked out. When the priest was called in, he lost his hat and was thrown onto the dung heap. Someone wanted to pick up the hat, but the priest said: "No, leave my hat where it is. The one who took it will give it back!"
174077: A man who was covered in lice was convinced that a witch had done it to him, because the woman who slept beside him had no lice.
174084: Two men went to keep watch one night by the cowshed of a haunted farm. On the stroke of midnight, to their great fright, the men saw three figures come out of the dung heap.
174107: In Veurne a freemason had suffered a fatal heart attack on election day. The freemason's wife had always been very devout. After the man's death the maids no longer dared to stay in the house because they heard the devils making noise. When the freemason was buried, it rained terribly. Sandbags had to be laid on the road to be able to get to the funeral. It was said that the last person to go to the funeral was the devil himself.
174128: A girl had caught a hare and put a leash on the animal. When the girl looked back a little later, the animal turned out to have vanished.
174153: Along the coast of Nieuwpoort the fishermen often saw a flying wreck. Many went after the wreck in the hope of still finding something on it.
174164:
A man who was ridden by the mare felt as if something fell on him. The man grew terribly thin and went to the dean for advice. When, on the clergyman's advice, the man always set his clogs upside down under his bed, he was no longer troubled by the mare.
Animals could also be ridden by the mare. A little pig became thin and ugly because of it.
174167: A woman went on pilgrimage to Dadizele for her sick child. On the way the woman kept seeing something white walking ahead of her. A while later the woman saw a shadow beside her. All the way the woman called out: "Pilgrim, I will follow you." When the woman arrived in Dadizele, the shadow had vanished. At that moment the woman's child was cured. The woman had been walking the whole time with the ghost of a dead person on her back.
174177: A farm in the Braamhul was haunted. Sometimes as many as five hundred people appeared on that farm, singing and celebrating. A little later those people had vanished without a trace.
174185: Two boys coming back from the barber saw a spotted cat sitting on a wooden makeshift bridge, looking them straight in the eye. The cat leapt from the bridge to a poplar standing some way off. An ordinary cat could certainly not make such a leap. It must have been a witch's cat.
174192: A woman who was tormented by a witch always heard noises at night, although there was nothing to be seen. When her husband got up, he claimed that seventeen people were baking and talking. Because the woman's child also cried all the time and suffered from 'the old man' (a wasting illness), the woman went to Sint-Jeks. There the priest said to her: "It is high time you came." When the woman told him about the noises she heard at night, the priest said: "You will hear that for a few more nights and then it will be over." The woman's child, however, died while sitting on her lap. It was already too late for the child, the priest had said. The woman had received three medals from the priest: one to fix to the fence, one for the door and one for the gate. "You are being followed by three witches," the priest had said. "If they come to ask how you are, you must let them in," the clergyman added. Because of the medals, however, the witches could no longer get in. When the woman went to the cellar to fetch butter, she found hair on the butter.
174197: A witch made a farmer with his horse and cart fly into the air and fall into the ditch.
174200: On a farm where three stable hands worked, one of the farmhands said to the farmer during Advent: "One of the farmhands always comes home around two or three in the morning and crawls into bed stiff with cold. It's strange that he is out every evening!" The next day the farmer found the skin of a werewolf in an old pollard willow. He sent the farmhand far away to work in the field there. Meanwhile the farmer heated the oven very hot and threw the skin into the fire. At that moment, however, the farmhand was already standing by the oven to save his skin. But he no longer managed it. The farmhand left after that and was never seen again.
174214: When people woke up bathed in sweat, they believed they had been ridden by the mare. That was an old woman.
174216: A woman from Deerlijk said to her husband in the evening when he came home from work: "It's so strange. When you leave for work, a little woman appears here who comes and stands in front of the door and walks back and forth the whole time." When the man asked what the little woman looked like, his wife went on: "She wears black clogs and a blue apron with a bow." The man then said: "Damn, it's my mother!" The man remembered that he and his brother had promised, at their mother's death, to go on pilgrimage to Machelen and offer two living hearts there (e.g. of pigeons or rabbits). After the brothers had done so, their room was lit up at night by a heavenly glow. After that the dead mother never appeared again.
174273: A girl from Zillebeke who was home alone with her little sister was visited by a woman who came for buttermilk. The girls claimed they had no milk. But the woman had already seen the buttermilk and said: "You do have milk, because I've seen it! But if you won't give any, you won't have to eat butter any more!" Shortly afterwards the girls' mother came home. She churned all morning but could not make butter. When she heard from her daughters what had happened, she told them: "You must never refuse such people anything!"
174298: A priest whose orchard had been robbed of apples during high mass made the thief stand still on the bank with his bag of apples. He could not leave until the priest had given him permission.
174302: On a farm in Proven people tried in vain for a long time to churn butter. When there was still no butter at four in the afternoon, they poured the cream out for the pigs. The priest advised the people to sprinkle some blessed salt in the churn. When they did so, they could make butter.
174317: A man shot twice at a hare, but could not hit the animal. Then the hare sat up on its hind legs and stared at the man.
174321: In Nieuwpoort lived a framasson (freemason). One day he said to his workmen: "I have no money to pay you. But wait a moment." Then the framasson shut himself up in his office. A few moments later the workmen were allowed in. All the drawers of the desk were full of money. Perhaps the framasson had had a visit from the devil. The money the devil brought had to be spent every day. Later that framasson was given a civil burial.
174340: A woman from Schraveneke had eleven children. Every year the Poor Clares came to her to ask for alms. On one of their visits the nuns said: "Is that the same child as last year?" The woman's youngest daughter had not grown at all. Because the nuns saw that something was wrong with the child, they came back a while later and gave the mother medals to put under the threshold and under the farm's gate bar. After that the child became healthy and grew up like other children her age. Since the nuns' visit, however, the washerwoman no longer came to visit. That washerwoman also often called at the neighbours'. One day a child died in that family. The child's mother went to the priest and explained that her child had died because of the washerwoman. The clergyman replied: "If you think so, come to church on Friday for seven o'clock mass. Sit at the back. The washerwoman will be in church too. If she is the guilty one, you will see a candle burning above her head during the consecration." When the time came, the mother did indeed see a candle above the woman's head.
174343:
A man who had laughed at a clergyman had to stay standing until the clergyman came home. The man was fixed to the ground by magic.
Some priests could read pearls from people's eyes.
174353: An old woman lived in Brugge. When people went walking on Sunday evening, there were always kittens running around them.
174356: A woman went with her heavily pregnant neighbour to the doctor in Ijvegem around midnight. On the way the neighbour claimed she saw something white moving. The other woman, however, saw nothing of the haunting. "You may well have seen something," the doctor later said to the pregnant woman. That pregnant woman always saw an apparition at the same spot. The doctor saw it too, but the other woman saw nothing.
174378: A man who had gone for a drink at the inn 't Fortuuntje had to walk to the Kruusdoorn. On the way the man saw something white flickering in a hedge. Scared to death, the man ran home.
174387: In Tiegem lived a witch who always wore a black hooded cloak that smelled of pitch and tar. The witch consorted with the devil and bred toads that grew as big as kittens on Saint Bavo's night. Every morning the witch's house swarmed with vermin, because the toads were allowed in through the drain hole. The witch's son had died of appendicitis. That was only to be expected when one consorted with the devil.
174393: Some men were sitting in an inn around eleven o'clock in the evening when suddenly a hen flew in. The hen flew from one to the other, much to the annoyance of the company. One of the men gave the animal a hard kick. At that very moment the landlady fell off her chair. That is how it was found out that the landlady had special powers.
174408: When people had eaten too much in the evening, they often had horrible visions at night.
174416: A boy secretly took three sugar lumps from the table when the lady of the house had briefly stepped out of sight. A moment later the witch came back, saying: "I would have given you a lump, but you've already taken three!"
174422: On a farm the cows' troughs were found tied onto the animals' backs in the morning.
174428: People who were ridden by the mare in their beds at night were seized by the throat until they could no longer breathe. At that moment they woke up and the mare was gone.
174437: A woman out with her mother saw, at eleven at night, three trees, one of which was on fire because a doodkeers (death candle) was in it. The two women were so frightened that they took a detour. The light that burned there every night was the soul of a dead man who had hidden his money there but never dug it up. The man always had to return to count his money.
174441: A farmer always rang the priest's doorbell on Saturdays after he had had a shave. When the maid went to open the door, there was no one to be seen. One day the priest fixed the annoying man to the doorbell by magic. The people going to mass could see the ashamed man standing there.
174459: Some brothers who went outside at about half past eight in the evening saw a fine cow standing there. The boys tried to catch the animal, but did not succeed. The cow ran off, but fell into a pit a little further on. Without much effort the cow jumped out of the pit, ran on and jumped over a beech hedge and over a ditch. The next day it turned out that no one else had seen the cow.
174471: During the war a man said to his comrade: "I have a feeling I'm going to be killed." The comrade tried to reassure him, saying: "Oh no, not all soldiers get killed!" A quarter of an hour later the man was killed by a shell.
174473: In Passendale lived a woman who probably consorted with the devil. All the men who had been to see her were not drawn free in the lottery for military service. During the lottery the woman kept shouting: "Executioners, do your work!"
174484: A farmhand who went fishing saw, to his great fright, two ghosts standing before him.
174485: A man coming back from sea got lost because of a wizard. When the man met someone who said "good evening", he immediately found his bearings again.
174518: A woman shut a pretty little cat, which always hung about the farm, in the attic. One day an old woman was sitting in the attic. When they helped the woman down from the attic, she turned back into a cat and ran away.
174522: Whoever was ridden by the mare felt as if he was being strangled. People who had experienced that lived only three or four more days.
174527: A farmhand saw the farmer he worked for coming home. But the farmer walked past his farm and began to cry at 't Rossekot. A witch had made the farmer lose his way.
174551: When people heard the 'klippertje' (a clicking sound) in the evening, an accident would happen.
174579: Some people going to Mass in Nieuwenhove had to pass the Lepelboom, a notorious haunted spot. By that tree the people saw something moving about. When the people returned from Mass, they saw large tracks of a strange beast by the Lepelboom.
174581: A girl who went to school in the Vierstraat in Kemmel always saw a little light by a small bush on the way. The light had the shape of a face. Close to the bush stood a large tree. People no longer dared to pass there. They said a castle had sunk there and that the lord of the castle returned to point out his money.
174595: If a witch had laid her evil hand on the milk, the butter was full of frogs.
174623: Some people walking home in the evening saw the curate come out, dressed entirely in white.
174653: One morning a woman found a witch in the pigsty. The witch had the piglets on her lap and explained that she found the little animals so sweet. Not a single piglet could be kept, because all the animals were bewitched.
174654: A farmhand who had put seven cows in the meadow was startled when he suddenly saw fourteen cows. The farmhand did not know where the other seven cows had come from. When he tried to chase the strange cows away, the animals trampled him so that he broke out in a sweat. The farmhand ran to the cowshed, where he was struck by a kind of log.
174662: At the 'Paddekot' in Abele the friars were sent for. The clergymen dug a pit and drove all the toads into it. The last toad was exceptionally large.
174666: Some young people who were out and about came across a kitten on a culvert and took the animal with them. The cat grew heavier and heavier until at a certain moment it jumped into the water and cried: "I fooled you, didn't I!"
174685: Two men walking home through the woods at night saw a figure among the trees that said: "I have been standing here for seven years now." That was probably someone who had to do penance for a sin.
174704: A Catholic midwife claimed she had seen a procession in the sky.
174708:
A woman often came to a farm to fetch milk. One day the woman said that it was a 'besloten maart' (closed March) that year (1) and that there would therefore be problems with the cows calving. Women expecting a child would also have a hard time.
When the farmer's wife gave birth that year, she got a fever that lasted as long as four weeks. The doctor advised the woman to drink six eggs every day. The priest even came to give her the Last Rites. Another doctor thought she would die of blood poisoning. The priest, however, believed she would survive. The woman got several illnesses one after another. Each time the priest had visited, she recovered from one illness, but then got another. The last illness she got was tuberculosis. Two days later the woman had no more fever. She was cured.
174729: A woman who had promised to have a Mass said but had not kept that promise returned after her death. On the parish priest's advice, the relatives asked the ghost why it came back. After the people had a Mass said for the dead woman, the ghost appeared no more.
174750: A man who came to a crossroads saw little straw crosses lying there, meant to keep ghosts away. A little later two cats came running up and accompanied the man until he was home. The man had tried several times to kick the animals, but they would not go away. When the man got home, the cats had suddenly vanished.
174754: A man who always came home at one o'clock at night saw a little animal jump towards him each time. The man kicked at the animal, whereupon a loud scream rang out and the little animal vanished. This happened by the 'Waterrat' in Westrozebeke.
174760: On a farm in Ruddervoorde pots and pans could be heard rattling in the washhouse at night, although nothing could be seen.
174789: It was dangerous when a witch laid her hand on your shoulder. People with sweet blood were especially vulnerable to the power of witches.
174794: Some people always ran into a witch from the village, whether they were going to Steenbrugge or to Desselgem. That witch appeared wherever she wanted to be.
174801: A rich gentleman who led a sinful life had a devout daughter who had been raised in a convent home. "But father, won't you stop living like this? Don't you know what awaits you after death? You will go to hell!" The rich gentleman would answer: "Speak to me neither of heaven nor of hell. Let's have another drink, for when I'm dead I'll stink. Everything will die." One day the gentleman was walking with his daughter in the churchyard, where a skull lay. The gentleman kicked the skull and said: "If there is still life in you, you are invited to my party tonight." During the party the doorbell rang at night. The servant opened the door and then went to the gentleman, saying: "There's a ghost at the door that says it has been invited!" The ghost came in, struck the gentleman's head against the wall and said: "You kicked the head of your great-grandfather! And now you will come and burn with me!" The end of the song that was made about it goes like this: "Beware, you youths and young daughters, of taking bad paths. For remember that you will have to give account to God when you stand at the Last Judgement."
174807: In Moorsele lived a sorceress who could make small children ill by shaking their hand. Many of those children died of their illness.
174809: A fishwife who worked at the fish auction had a woman from Gent as a customer. Whenever that woman proposed a price, the fishwife had to sell her fish at a loss; otherwise the woman would bewitch her.
174871: A witch could bewitch the cows, causing the animals to die.
174873: A carter always met a woman by a brook. Whenever the man grabbed at the woman, she flew high into the air and vanished.
174887: German shepherds could make mice by blowing on little balls of clay.
174892: On the morning of Saint Peter's Day a man went with a friend to the horse festivities in Torhout. At a certain moment the friend stepped aside for a white apparition he saw. The other man, however, did not see the apparition.
174894: A woman was staying with a friend, who said before going to bed: "If you hear me cry out, I am being ridden by the mare and you must call my name." To protect oneself against the mare, one had to hold a knife on one's chest with the point upward. One could also set one's clogs with the toes pointing at the bed.
174906: Whenever the notary walked in his garden, the wind always started blowing and the treetops struck against each other. When the notary had died, his coffin was full of stones. The devil had taken his body. The notary was a framasson (freemason).
174915: Four men went to visit a woman. "Would you like to eat potatoes in their skins?" the woman asked. Two men began peeling potatoes. While they did so, all their hair fell out. The man who ate no potatoes kept his hair.
174918: A farmer who owned nine fine piglets was visited by his neighbour, who touched the animals. A while later all the piglets were dead.
174927: When a sorcerer came into a café alone, he said: "Here we are!", to which the people answered: "You are welcome." The next day the café was full of rats.
174936: A woman who was ridden by the mare felt something crawl up from her feet and could hardly breathe. To protect oneself against the mare, one had to set one's clogs at the foot of the bed with the heels under the bed. Some people claimed that the mare was a stopping of the blood.
174948: At a farm in Oedelem a little woman came to ask for a piece of bread. The girl who lived on the farm gave her a slice of bread. On her way out, however, the little woman left the bread on the windowsill. The farmer's wife saw it and threw the bread to the pigs. The next day the sow lay dead.
174958: A man was coming back with his mother from the fair in Esen. On the way the two saw a calf with a chain standing there. The animal did not move. A baker's boy who had gone to deliver bread to Esen with the dog cart could not get his dogs to move in any way.
174974: In Damme lived a witch who could make small children fall ill or die.
174978: In a house where a cat came every evening at about the same time, the people had been advised by the parish priest to throw some hot butter into the cat's mouth. The next day one of the neighbours was badly burnt on the head.
174981: A man coming back from the fair was followed by a dog with a chain. Even when the man walked through the fields, the dog went with him. Although the man was afraid, he did not dare to hit the dog. The gamekeeper had often seen that dog too, but he had never managed to hit the animal.
174983:
Whoever was ridden by the mare at night felt as if someone was sitting on him, trying to strangle him. Strangely enough, however, there was no one to be seen.
Whoever wanted to protect himself against the mare had to set his slippers or clogs upside down beside the bed.
174984: Some people saw a dead relative appear in the house and go up to the attic.
175011: A sorceress made a woman dance in a puddle of water with a bundle of nettles on her back. After the curate had collected that woman's books, the sorceress could do nothing more.
175017: A woman from Leke was on her way to Brugge. A farmer with a carriage offered to give her a ride. The woman refused, however. When the farmer arrived in Brugge, he saw the woman already walking there.
175042: Whoever was ridden by the mare was in reality having a stopping of the blood.
175089: Because it was raining, the Sint-Jan procession could not take place. That night the statue of Mary went walking on its own. The next morning it was seen that her cloak was completely covered in mud. Since then the procession has always gone ahead, whatever the weather. When it rained, a plastic bag was pulled over the statue of Mary.
175090: In the past it was said that the dead could return because they had not kept a promise.
175112: When a sorcerer came out of somewhere, two or three mice were seen jumping out of his pocket.
175114: In the old days German shepherds could send a plague of rats to a farm.
175132: Some girls walking to school saw little lights flying up out of the meadows next to a farm. These were dead people who had no rest.
