175137: Whoever was ridden by the mare could hardly breathe. To protect oneself against the mare, one had to set one's clogs upside down under the bed.
175149: Whenever piglets had been born somewhere, a sorceress walked about at night with a hooded cloak on her back. The next day the piglets lay dead.
175163: In one house there were three children who were all blind because a witch had stood by their cradle just after they were born. One day the children's father chased the witch away. Afterwards his wife had many more children, who could all see.
175166: A farmer noticed that his cow always fell ill when she was pregnant. After a while the farmer realised that a cat always came to sit by the pregnant cow. The farmer burnt the cat's snout. When the farmer went to Mass the following Sunday, he saw one of the women present hurrying away. The woman glanced back and turned out to have burns on her face.
175181: A man on his way to the slaughterhouse was followed by a dog. When the man had shot at the animal, it turned into a hare.
175182: In the Galgenbos near Elsegem many of the returning dead walked about at night. Those people had been hanged hundreds of years ago because they had committed some crime.
175201: In the stable of an old house there were many rats that could not be driven away by any means. They were sent rats.
175253: A man had shot three times at a hare without hitting the animal. When the man left, he saw an ox in a tree.
175271: Two girls coming back from lace-making school met a woman on the way, who gave them coins. One of those girls later went mad.
175293: In the Onzelieveheertjesbos a farmer had found a statue of Christ in a tree. The man took the statue to the Onze-Lieve-Vrouwekerk, where the priest accepted it. The next day, however, the little statue was lying in the tree in the wood again. The same thing happened three times. The priest then decided to build a little chapel on that spot in the wood with the statue inside. Some people claimed that the statue of Christ would bleed if one cut into it.
175296: Some of the dead returned because they still had to fulfil a vow or because they still had something else to settle.
175325: A woman had promised to do a novena for her mother, but she had not kept that promise. The woman always saw the image of her dead mother in the loft hatch. One day the woman said to the ghost: "If you are sent by God, say where you come from. If you are sent by the devil, then vanish." The ghost said that the woman had to go and pray for nine consecutive days at a cross on the road from Menen to Ledegem. The first time the woman did not go alone. At the cross the ghost appeared and said that the woman had to come alone. The woman did as she was asked. She grew thinner and thinner, however. Four months later she died.
175331: Two friends going home on a Sunday evening were accompanied by a black cat. The more the men kicked at the animal, the closer the cat came. When the men reached the farm, the cat had vanished.
175349: When going to bed, one had to set one's shoes with the toes pointing at the bed. That way one was protected against the mare.
175375: In the Molenstraat in Sint-Louis, every night at about the same time, people saw a woman walking, who stopped at the little chapel and then vanished without a trace.
175385: On a farm lived a sorceress who could bewitch people. If she laid her hand on your shoulder, you were possessed. A boy who lived opposite that farm did not dare go to sleep without a burning candle beside his bed.
175394: People said that the blacksmith, who had died some time before, came back as a ghost in the evenings. Whenever someone made a noise in the evening, people believed it was the blacksmith.
175395: In 1871 a farm burned down in Dadizele. People always thought the farmhand had started the fire. In reality, however, the maid was to blame. She confessed it on her deathbed because otherwise she could not die. When the maid was made to wade through the moat around the farm, she was not wet afterwards. The bucket of potatoes always stood on the south side of the farm where she stayed. Yet no one had put the bucket there.
175412: A very old witch with brown skin and jet-black hair is said to have lived in a street in Blankenberge. One day the witch had stroked a little child's head and said: "What a lovely child!" The next day the child had lice.
175413: A carpenter's son had a relationship with a witch's daughter. Every day the boy vanished without a trace from six to nine o'clock. The boy broke the door to be able to leave. One day the boy, who had by then become as thin as a rake, saw fire and flames all before him. A moment later he also saw a fine inn, which he entered. When the boy had ordered a glass of beer, he said: "God bless you". The next moment everything had vanished. The boy floated above the ground. In the end the boy went to the White Fathers of Brugge, who read prayers over him until the sweat dripped from their faces.
175432: Girls who were disobedient at school were often told: "You have been ridden by the mare. You are a she-devil. Go and stand in the corner!"
175454: A man from Hondschote got pimples after a witch had visited, who had said to his children: "You must give each other a kiss".
175460: At Raverschote there were always goats, dogs, cats and other beasts. Farms that were 'zwart goed' (cursed property, literally black goods) always suffered greatly from hauntings.
175468: In Torhout a cow had died through witchcraft.
175469: A man who went to the fair in Ichtegem (1) had to go home around ten o'clock because he had no money left. Between Ichtegem and Koekelare the man saw someone sitting there relieving himself. The man greeted the apparition, but there was no answer. The man struck at the figure with his stick, but he missed. By the moat at Piers' castle the man saw the same apparition again. This time the man no longer dared to strike. By the chapel the man saw lots of little white rats running about. When the man had made the sign of the cross, everything vanished.
175476: People who had not turned their clogs over in the evening were ridden by the mare at night.
175488:
In Vuylsteke a girl was bewitched by a sorceress who came to fetch buttermilk. The girl's face rotted away completely.
A clergyman came to see the girl and predicted that the sorceress would not come back.
The girl died shortly afterwards, because the spell could no longer be undone.
175501: In Izegem lived a family whose children all died when they were a few months old. Every time a child was born, a witch from the neighbourhood came to visit. The witch stroked the child, saying: "Well, what a lovely child!" A few hours after the witch left, the child turned blue. A while later it died.
175514: A man walking to the sea was followed by one cat when he set out. By the time the man had reached the quay, twenty cats were already after him.
175517: In Beselare a castle is said to have sunk into the ground long ago. That place was haunted. The maid who had worked in that castle could tell many ghost stories. When the maid had to fetch hay from the loft one day, she found not hay there, but hair.
175520: A woman was making food one morning while her baby lay in the cradle. Although the door to the attic was always closed, the woman heard footsteps on the attic stairs. A little later the lamp on the table burst. Frightened, the woman took her baby from the cradle and ran outside.
175558: A little creature with a little light sat down on a ferryboat, wanting to be taken to the other side of the Scheldt. After the creature had got off, a franc was found lying in the boat!
175560: On the road by the Zwijnebak between Nieuwkerke and Kemmel a screaming goat flew through the air for three weeks.
175586: A man lay dying while his brother and his two sons were at sea. On his deathbed the man looked at the photo of his brother's ship and said: "Look how the white one is sailing there!" and then died. At the very moment the man died, his two sons had been swept overboard.
175602: On a farm where no butter could be churned, the cowshed was full of mice. The mice ran over the cow's tail and back. The cow could no longer be milked and in the end the animal died.
175605: A man on his way to his girlfriend kept hearing a voice calling: "Help me!" The man went to the place the calling came from, but he saw nothing. When the man continued on his way, the calling began again. After the man had made the sign of the cross, he heard no more strange sounds.
175618: A little boy cried all the time because he was bewitched. Such children usually died in the end. One day an aunt of the child found a small dish of pins on the floor. The boy did recover in the end.
175622: At Christmas the farmers used to play cards until midnight. Then they had to go to the stable with a lantern and speak to the animals. If the animals answered, a bad year would follow.
175637: Near the station lived a man who had special powers. If that man could not stand someone, he would say: "You won't get home today." Then that person would get lost.
175647: A married couple were coming back from a wedding one evening. The woman was wearing a precious necklace. On the way the woman was attacked by a bear that bit her necklace to pieces. When the woman lay in bed that night, she saw in the moonlight the links of her necklace stuck between her husband's teeth. When the woman had told everything to the parish priest, the clergyman advised her to follow her husband. In this way the woman found her husband's animal skin in a pit covered with leaves. The woman sent her husband far away so that she could burn the animal skin in the meantime. After that the man was released.
175648: In Proven lived a sorceress. Along the main road stood a house where cauliflowers were always being stolen. When a policeman one day saw the sorceress walking near that house with a sack in her hand, he said: "Oh, so you're the one who keeps stealing those cauliflowers!" The woman turned her sack upside down and out fell nothing but grass.
175666:
One evening a man coming back from visiting his girlfriend suddenly heard a goat bleating by a brook, in a lane with a lot of undergrowth. Convinced that a goat was caught in the bushes, the man walked to where the sound came from. When he got there, however, he saw nothing and heard the bleating a little further on. So the man went on and on without seeing a goat. In the end he decided to go home.
Some time later another man, who liked to poach, had the same experience. When that man was cutting grass one evening, he suddenly saw an animal leap away right in front of his nose. A tavern keeper's wife from the area said that a man on his way to Tjoenkershove had been thrown into the ditch by a goat. According to her, that goat was a dead woman who had returned. After the First World War such strange things no longer happened.
175667: One day in April a woman said to some boys playing in the street: "Look what a lovely pear!" Although it was only April, in the middle of the street lay the most beautiful pear anyone had ever seen. Not one child dared pick up the pear. When the woman had gone, the pear had vanished too.
175686: A farmer was often visited by a farmer's wife from the village. One night the farmer's sow was to give birth. Every piglet that was born began to dance and then fell dead. By one o'clock all eleven piglets had died. After that the farmer's wife never visited the man again.
175692: A man driving home with a cart of turnips had bad luck the whole way. The cart overturned several times, so that each time the man had to load the turnips back into it. When the man got home, there was nothing left in the cart. On top of that, his cows and horses were all standing the wrong way round in the stable. The man could no longer churn butter either. The man had become the victim of a sorceress who lived nearby. After his son left for America, the man had no more misfortune.
175703: In Oostduinkerke lived a woman whose children had all died of 'the old man' (a wasting disease) after someone had bewitched them. One day, when the woman's brother came back from the café, he had seen a black cat sitting on the child.
175716: In Avelgem there was a hedge that was always haunted between midnight and one o'clock. It seemed as if a white man lingered there who could move through the hedge. On the stroke of one the man had vanished.
175728: A boy coming home from the factory one evening saw two nuns standing by the brook. Terrified, the boy begged to be let into the Pompière. But they refused because they suspected the boy was drunk.
175736: A man sitting at the table eating saw a woman with a bad reputation come in. The woman immediately said: "But you've grown thin!" Afterwards the man became so ill that he could no longer work. When the man had to join the army, he was, strangely enough, cured. But whenever he came home on leave, he was ill again.
175759: If a farmer had refused to give something to a beggar, his farm was often full of rats in the evening. The clergy then had to come and read prayers over the farm.
175765: A witch came into a café where a child was ill and said: "By Easter Monday the child will no longer be here". The witch claimed she could decide whether a child died or lived.
175783: People who were ridden by the mare could see the mare approaching at their feet. Then they saw movement like that of a person. A moment later they felt the mare at their throat, which gave them the feeling of suffocating. At that moment they began to scream and woke up.
175788: A man who went to get a shave on a Saturday evening met a cat on his way home, which kept jumping against his leg. The cat sat miaowing all night at the window of the upstairs room where the man slept. When the man wanted to go to Mass the next day, he decided to polish his shoes first. He stood on a chair to take the pot of shoe polish and fell to the ground. The man broke all his limbs.
175791: On a farm the maid was milking the cows. Suddenly the animals pulled themselves loose and the doors flew open and shut. A wild horse kicked against the door.
175805: In a wood in Eernegem there was a pit where a little light always burned in the evening. People said that if you could put out that light, you would find a fortune in coins. But you were not allowed to breathe, or else you would drop dead.
175807: In Vinkem lived an unbelieving man who always rang the priest's doorbell on Saturdays after he had had a shave. When the priest's maid went to open the door, there was no one at the door anymore. One day the priest had fixed the man to the doorbell by magic. The man could only go home after the priest's maid had given him permission.
175818: A family lived in a neighbourhood called 'de Gemiste Mis' (the Missed Mass) because a wedding couple had once missed mass there. On the road from Rozebeke to Passendale lived a woman who was said to be a witch. One day the family's son went to Rozebeke with the wheelbarrow to fetch bread. The boy took the shortest route and had to pass the witch's house. At the bakery in Rozebeke the boy took fifteen loaves. On the way back the boy was dead tired. The witch stood outside watching and said: "Boy, are you not managing?" When the boy got home, the light went out. The mirrors fell off the walls and the windowpanes were smashed. The boy's parents opened the bread sack and saw mice crawling out of it.
175824: Children who woke up every night at about the same time and began to cry, or who had pain in the same place, were the victims of someone who tormented them by sticking a pin into a wax doll.
175833: A gravedigger asked a friend to dig a grave for a member of his family who had died. While that man was digging, he was nearly frightened to death: in the pit lay a skull that kept nodding back and forth.
175869: People who were ridden by the mare at night felt as if death had visited them. To protect oneself against the mare, one had to set one's shoes upside down beside the bed.
175875: A cat was often seen walking around in a bewitched cowshed. One day the cat was thrown into the manure pit. The next day a witch lay in that pit.
175888: Some boys were playing. Suddenly one of the boys went to ask a woman from the neighbourhood if he could have a light. "Yes, lad, you may have a light," the woman answered, and she struck the boy on the shoulder. At that moment the boy felt an intense pain.
175903: A boy who was out in his clogs one evening was jumped on by a werewolf, which had been woken by the sound of the clogs. When the boy's mother sprinkled him with holy water, the werewolf disappeared.
175906: A man walking past an alder hedge by moonlight quickened his pace because he heard someone walking behind him. The man only lost his pursuer when he got home.
175920: Some men went on foot to the market in Gent to sell a few cattle. The men had not been gone an hour when the people living on the farm heard a voice at the upstairs window saying how much money the cows had been sold for. When the men came home in the evening, they told the same thing.
175928: Some fishermen had caught a statue of Mary in their nets. The little statue was taken to the dunes. The priest proposed putting the statue in the church. The next day, strangely enough, the statue was lying in the dunes again. Then a donkey was let loose, and it stopped at the church of Meetkerke. So the statue of Mary was placed in that church.
175944: In the Kerkdreef in Vichte a werewolf used to roam. A man who had gone to fetch yarn one evening was followed by the werewolf. The man kept throwing skeins of yarn on the ground so that the werewolf had work to do. The next day people found that someone from the village had yarn between his teeth.
175948: In Les Moères lived a child whose ears were withering away because of a witch. The child's parents placed a medal under the door. When the witch came to visit and asked: "May I come in?", the people answered: "If you can". The witch never came back after that.
175952: A witch could make people fall into a filthy ditch. She herself stood by a stretch of the ditch where the water was, strangely enough, very clear. She would say to passers-by: "You're in such a hurry, mind you don't fall into the ditch!" In this way the witch made a good hundred people fall into the ditch.
175953:
Near Kemmel there lived a rich freemason who owned many farms. The man employed a bricklayer who was to build him a new farmhouse in Zuidschote. The freemason, however, was so critical that many walls had to be torn down again. A farmer was responsible for transporting the building materials. That farmer was soon completely exhausted.
Those who got on well with the freemason did receive a lot of help from him. The man cursed all the time and limped a little. At the freemason's funeral it was found that his coffin was full of stones. The devil had come to take his body, so people said.
175954: A man who was ridden by the mare could hardly breathe. The mare was a sorceress who lay down on her victim. If one laid one's socks crossed beside the bed, one was protected against the mare.
175959: A farmer who had worked in France for a while had come back to Belgium with the money he had earned. When the farmer died, people had promised to have masses said, but they had not kept that promise. At night the ticking of a watch or an alarm clock could always be heard, although there was nothing of the kind in the room. After the promised masses had been said, the ticking was heard no more.
176015: At 't Kattekerkhof at 't Wieltje a funeral procession appeared every night. The coaches were drawn by headless horses.
176017: A woman was in the habit of going to church every day with a lantern in her hand. Although she knew the way well, one day she got hopelessly lost. Moreover, a black cat kept walking in front of her feet the whole time.
176019: On a farm with seven milk cows, no butter could be churned any more. A woman from Werken advised the farmer's wife to send for the priest. The clergyman asked the farmer's wife whether she suspected anyone. The farmer's wife said: "There is a woman who had never come here for milk before, but who came to ask for a glass of milk a while ago. She never came back after that". The next morning the cowshed door stood open, and a day later the same thing happened again. The priest decided to come back on Ash Wednesday, because the farmers did not work then. That day the priest asked for a pan of oats, a palm sprig and holy water. Then the priest went with the farmer's wife to the cowshed, read prayers over the animals and gave them blessed oats. Next he sprinkled holy water about the shed with the palm sprig.
176058: Some people going to the fields were followed the whole time by a donkey, which finally lay down in front of the farmhouse door. When one touched the animal, one felt nothing but hair.
176059: In Ichtegem there lived a man who was a member of the freemasons. One evening the man told his wife, who was going to bed, that he wanted to stay up a little longer. Because her husband stayed away so long, the woman went back downstairs after a while. There she found that her husband had been struck dead. Probably the devil had come to fetch him.
176081: A young man taking his girlfriend home saw a small parcel lying by a tree stump. When the man tried to pick up the parcel, he heard a voice saying: "Go on, go away!" A little later the parcel was indeed gone. Further on the young man saw the same parcel lying there. When he tried to pick it up, the same thing happened again.
176085: In the past priests could fix people to their chairs by magic after mass, so that they had to stay seated in the church. When a house was on fire somewhere, they could also make the wind turn.
176097: A farm in Izegem was haunted. One day when the farmhand was going home, he kicked at a cat sitting in the lane, saying: "You cursed cat!" The next moment there was a whole pack of cats. The farmer advised the farmhand to leave everything alone from then on. On that farm all the animals kept had to have a little white spot. Moreover, white crosses were painted all over the building.
176107: In winter a farmer was coming back from Ieper with two donkeys, where he had gone to fetch cloth. Suddenly the farmer and the animals saw something leap onto the road in front of them. That was right next to the farm where a man had been killed by lightning.
176124: A sorceress had gone begging at a farmer's, but had been given nothing. In revenge the witch made the farmer harvest white bread instead of vegetables.
176127: If at night, on seeing a meteor or a shower of shooting stars, you could say "Praised be Jesus Christ", you had released a soul.
176136: A man coming back with a friend from a music society rehearsal met cats on the way that kept running between his legs. The man struck at the cats with his musical instrument, but he could never hit them. They were witches.
176142: Whoever had thought of a sorceress during the day could be ridden by the mare at night. When that happened, one felt as if one's throat was being squeezed shut.
176146: A woman working in a chicory field asked another woman to comb through her hair with a fine comb. When the other woman did so, she found the little woman's hair was full of lice. "What will people say now?" said the little woman. A man who worked in the field with them had once said to the little woman: "You'll get lice one day!"
176168: A farmhand from Vlamertinge was walking home in the dark one evening. On the way he saw a pair of glittering eyes. That was a phantom sheep.
176193: In a ditch lay an object that no one could manage to get hold of. The more people tried, the deeper they pushed the object into the mud. A woman from Veurne could pick up the object without any trouble. That woman was a sorceress. When the sorceress died, she was able to pass her arts on to her sons.
176212: Some people could cover someone in lice by rubbing that person's coat.
176214: A farm in Avelgem was so badly haunted that the people could not sleep at night. The priest, who had established that the evil was around the well, was even pulled into the well.
176218: A stable hand had to fetch yeast between Reninge and Oostvleteren. To his great fright the stable hand at a certain moment saw a ghost come out of the dyke. Some people claimed it had been a prank.
176236: After school the children had to go straight home, because the werewolf sometimes carried small children away from their homes.
176256: On their way home, some workmen often saw a dog with a thick chain. Such dogs were witches in animal form. Many witches who knew a lot of magic still lived in Passendale. They could even make the cows stop giving milk.
176259: In the Templar farmsteads in Sijsele there were certain rooms where no one could sleep because they were so badly haunted. Sounds could be heard there as if grain were being ground and planks were being beaten. Those were the spirits of the Templars at work.
176270: One evening a man was walking with two friends past the Nunkebossen in Ruddervoorde. Suddenly the three men heard an animal bleating. Convinced that it was a bewitched beast, no one dared to go and look.
176275: A man who came to a culvert on his bicycle saw a little cat walking back and forth over the culvert. The man could not move a step further. After he had made the sign of the cross, he could go on again. He was, however, scared to death.
176276: At midnight people in Torhout saw a procession flying through the sky. That was an omen of the war. And indeed a war came afterwards.
176299: One evening a man heard noise in his attic. Someone had sent rats to the attic. Then the people said to the vermin: "We don't want you here. Go back where you came from and run to the Red Sea." After that the rats were gone.
176323: In the attic of a farm people always heard chains rattling and a voice calling: "Jan out and the butter in!" It was the ghost of a dead farmer who had sold his butter far too dearly during the war and had to come back to atone for it.
176325: German shepherds could not only cover people in lice; they could also make a crow appear on every sheaf of corn. German shepherds drew their power from the books of magic they owned.
176340: After a cat had been thrown into the water, someone was heard calling for help. A little later a woman crawled out of the water.
176345: An old woman had been near a little child and had said: "What a lovely child!" After that the child cried all the time and became completely emaciated. Prayers were read over the child, but that did not help. In the end the child died of 'the old man' (a wasting disease).
176346:
On the Madonna in Langemark a woman who suffered from haemorrhaging lay dying. The curate came to say the prayers for the dying. The woman's family had also gone to a man from the village, who had asked: "Is she still alive?" When the people had said yes, that wizard had said: "She will live." The wizard quarrelled with the curate. When the wizard was walking home at night along the Kofferdreef, he saw two men standing by 't Gistelhof, waiting for him. The two men had been paid by the curate to get the better of the wizard. The wizard understood what was going on and turned himself into a tree. Because the men did not yet see the wizard coming, one of them said: "I'll just pee against this tree and then I'm going home." A little later both men went home. When the wizard came home at one o'clock at night and sat down by the hearth, his wife asked: "Why do your trousers smell like that? It isn't raining, is it?" The wizard answered very calmly: "Somebody peed against them over there." After the wizard died, the clergy immediately came to take his books.
Clergymen practise black magic and wizards white magic.
176348: A man had to go and cut grass at a farmer's at four in the morning. Suddenly the man saw a hare, but he could not catch it. The hare disappeared into a barn where a day labourer was changing his clothes. That labourer had turned himself into a hare.
176365: Whoever was ridden by the mare at night had a kind of dream between sleeping and waking.
176366: Two proud girls on their way to a dance met a German shepherd and did not greet him. Ten metres further on the girls were covered in lice. The girls turned back in despair. When they passed the shepherd again, he asked: "Well, going back already?", to which the girls answered: "Yes, we're covered in lice and we can't go dancing like this!" The shepherd replied: "Next time be polite to people and say good day to everyone." "We won't do it again," the girls answered. The next moment the girls were rid of the lice.
176379: In the Langemark lived an old lame man with one hip higher than the other. The man lived there with his daughter. After the man died, a rag dealer from Roeselare who peddled herring came to live in the little house. Later a little light could be seen from the gravel road burning near that house. People believed it was the lame man or the rag dealer returning.
176404: A priest who had been locked up in prison managed to escape in a miraculous way.
176427: Every night a little light appeared at a tree where a treasure was hidden. When two men wanted to dig up the treasure, they heard a noise and ran away terrified.
176445: A boy who slept in his brother's room always saw something crawl over him at night. After the boy made the sign of the cross, the strange apparition disappeared. The mother said that the boy had probably been ridden by the mare.
176456: A farm by the old Leie used to be haunted every evening. A strong wind blew, chains could be heard rattling and birds were seen flying about. A man passing there one night kept seeing something walking around him. The man was so frightened that he quickly ran away. When the man had already been walking for an hour, he saw that he was still standing by the same farm.
176485: When fishermen had met a priest, a nun or a witch, they believed they would have bad luck.
176503: A young lady was seen walking across the water of the canal. She came back to haunt because a castle had sunk into the water and because an injustice had been done.
176516: On a farm there were a few beautiful white horses in the barn every night. One night the horses were taken out of the barn and made to plough the field. The next morning it was found that only half of the furrows had been ploughed. Because the horses were there again the next day, one of the animals was taken to the smith and shod. The next morning the farmer's wife lay in her bed with horseshoes.
176520: A woman who had taken lacework to Wakken met, at the crossroads of the road to Anzegem, a woman who was said to be a witch. The woman said to the witch: "I don't know what's the matter with me, but I've felt so strange all morning. I'm sure something has happened". When the witch asked whether the woman had been away long, the woman said: "First I mucked out the goat shed and took my children away. Then I saw a big rat running, which I chopped in two". "Oh Lord God", answered the witch, "a woman who lives near here has fallen off her chair and broken her neck!"
176555: In the past there were old women who could turn themselves into cats and jumped onto the backs of passers-by.
176558: On a bewitched farm a woman with a neckerchief was found in the horse stable. The witch's teeth were shot out of her mouth with a gun loaded with silver coins. Some time later it was discovered that the maid no longer had any teeth. She was dismissed on the spot.
176561: A woman who had had a miscarriage was lying alone in her bed. Suddenly the woman panicked because she could no longer speak or move. She thought she was going to die and cried: "For the honour of God, no!" The next moment everything was normal again. The woman had fallen victim to a spirit.
176563: A man on his way to Kachtem had to go through a lane lined with poplars. In that lane the man kicked at a black cat that got under his feet. The next moment the cat became so big that its tail reached up into the tops of the poplars.
176571: A disabled woman who lived in a parish cottage asked the priest for help and said: "I'll certainly see when you come." One day, however, the priest appeared in the shape of a crow, without anyone having seen the bird approach.
176576: A woman had made a gesture over the washing laid out to bleach. When a little child put on that washing, it got 'the old man' (a wasting disease). A novena was said for the child. On the last day of the novena, however, the child died.
176578: People who were ridden by the mare felt as if their throat was being squeezed shut. If someone called those people's name, they were freed. One could also protect oneself against the mare by setting one's slippers upside down under the bed.
176586: A baker drove to Brugge with his eldest little son. Some passers-by said: "Why, baker, that's a handsome child!" But a woman who sat smoking said: "He won't stay handsome for long. He will become cross-eyed, and you won't have any others". Seven of the baker's children did indeed become cross-eyed at the age of three. Only the youngest little daughter stayed healthy.
176606: A mother had two little children, the youngest of whom was six months old. One day the child fell ill. It screamed all the time and became completely emaciated. After a while the mother managed to persuade her husband to go to the friars. A friar asked the mother: "Isn't there a woman who often visits you and gives the children sugar?" The mother answered that this was indeed so. The friar advised the mother not to let that woman in any more; she was, after all, the culprit. When the mother followed that advice, the child recovered.
176620: On a farm, rats always came at night to gnaw at the farmhand's clothes. A German shepherd advised the farmhand to stick a knife into the ground. The next morning the rats were hanging from the knife.
176628: Whenever there was a child a few weeks old somewhere, a sorceress always tried to get near it. The child was then bewitched.
176631: In Eernegem there used to be three pits in which bells were said to have once sunk.
176634: A man kicked at a little partridge sitting in the wood. A moment later the wood was full of little birds, so that the man could hardly go on.
176642: A woman said to be a sorceress made her daughter wither away.
176647: People who had been unjust during their lives often had to come back after their death. The ghost could then be heard making noise.
176661: A veterinarian travelling by horse and cart was attacked by three robbers. The veterinarian bewitched the robbers so that they were stuck to the coach until the next day.
176687: A woman who wanted to heat a small pan of milk for her child saw a toad jump out of the pan every time. On the advice of an acquaintance the woman took the toad out of the pan with red-hot tongs. The next day the doctor was called to treat someone whose back and belly were badly burnt.
176689: A man from Leffinge went to work on a haunted farm in France. After a while the man got an inflammation in his foot, of which he died.
176710: If people went to milk the cows after five o'clock in the afternoon, a sorceress made sure no more milk came from the udders. After five o'clock the witch also made the wagons tip over.
176764: A witch lived in Gistel who often stood watching in the doorway of her house. If you did not greet that witch, you fell off your bicycle a few metres further on.
176787: In a house in West-Vlaanderen a mother had died young. One day the twelve-year-old daughter went to the cellar and saw a strange figure sitting there. Then the girl heard her mother's voice say: "You needn't be afraid. Give me your hand, but first go and fetch a handkerchief!" After the girl had done so, her dead mother burned a hand into the handkerchief. Then the mother said: "Child, I will not come back again, but you must pray for me a great deal."
176791: Sorceresses had power above all over pregnant women. They were forced to do evil. Children who had been bewitched went about screaming and raging as if they had been stuck with pins.
176802: A workman from Gistel could make live mice out of clay. The parish priest collected that man's books of magic.
176814: Some women could, at someone's request, torment or kill people by sticking needles into a candle. There were also people who could make the blood of the person they had murdered flow across the table.
176816: In Knokke there was a place that was haunted. People saw a light in the distance. When they came closer, they saw that it was a café, where they heard talking and the clinking of glasses. Because the way was always blocked by thorns, it was impossible to reach that café.
176822: A weaver had hidden his money at the foot of his loom, which stood in a pit. After the man's death the loom began to weave by itself at night. In the morning there was nothing to be seen. After a few months the money buried under the loom was found. The money was taken to the priest.
176825: A woman and a child were both ill and went to the priest. The clergyman said: "When the witch comes to visit, you must put a packet under her chair." When this had been done and the witch could no longer stand up, the farmer said to the witch: "You must undo the harm you have done." To which the witch replied: "It is already too late for that. But you may choose: your wife or your child." After a while the woman recovered, but the child died.
176840: A man used to cycle to France every year. One evening the cyclist got a flat tyre between Houtkerke and Herzele. The man knocked at an old house to ask for a small bowl of water. Two old ladies were sitting by the fire and gave the man water. When the man had repaired his tyre and wanted to set off again, he could no longer find his bearings. Because he was lost, there was nothing for it but to go back home. The man believed that the two old women had bewitched him.
176842: A murdered girl from Alveringem came back to haunt after her death.
176844: When a witch knew that a baby had been born somewhere, she quickly went to the child to bewitch it. She would say: "What a beautiful child. I would like one like that too!" After the witch left, however, the child suffered greatly.
176854: At a crossroads in Adegem lived a woman who was said to be a sorceress. That woman always visited newborn children. As soon as the woman had left, the children began to cry loudly. In the end the children died.
176867: In Abele lived a woman who went to pray with a rosary by children's cradles. The children she had visited all caught an illness called 'the old man' (1). She could no longer enter the houses where something blessed had been placed under the door.
176881: A fisherman coming back from sea on All Saints' Day met the priest, who said: "Well, what are you doing here?" Afterwards the fisherman had to wander about with his basket on his back because he could no longer find his house. Yet his house was right in front of him.
176890: In a neighbourhood where a supposed sorceress lived, a new building was being put up. While the men were building a cesspit, the sorceress's son was nearby. He must have been reading his mother's books again, because he said: "That arch certainly won't hold." The workmen, however, had full confidence in their work. The boy had barely stepped off the arch when the structure collapsed.
176902: At the door of a house where some boys were ill, a cat always sat meowing. One day someone poured hot water over the animal. The next day the neighbour's face was badly burnt.
176905: At a little hill between Torhout and Brugge there were a good thousand cats that chased passers-by.
176912: Every evening a black cat came meowing at a house in Westkapelle. One day a woman struck at the cat. The woman had followed the animal and seen that the cat was a sorceress.
176936:
In the old days strange women were never allowed near a cradle with a child in it, because people believed that witches could prick children with pins.
A woman whose child had fallen victim to a witch had to take the child to the priest, or else it would have died.
176950: When a witch's daughter-in-law was buried, the horses ran off with the coffin and stopped at the church. The witch was sitting in the wagon with her son.
176956: In Lendelede the ghost of a dead woman was seen walking about screaming every evening. A man opened all the windows of his house and then closed them again. After that no more sound was heard.
176981: Between waking and sleeping one could be ridden by the mare. One then felt as if one was being pushed down by a strange force.
176984: In Oostende lived a witch whom everyone feared. The witch always carried a basket of shrimps. One day some men wanted to sail out with their ship. But the rope tying up the ship was around a post on which the witch sat watching. Nobody dared ask the witch to get up. They waited meekly until the witch left of her own accord.
176989: A woman returned after her death to fulfil a neglected vow.
177005: A man had hanged himself in a stable in Tiegem. Since then, every animal put in that stable died. The farmer sent for the curate of Tiegem to exorcise the stable. The clergyman said: "If you put an animal in that stable again, you must put it in backwards. Then it will live." And so it was.
177019: On a farm that had a lot of bad luck, the priest was sent for. After the clergyman had blessed the farm and read prayers over it, one particular woman was no longer allowed on the farm. That put an end to the bad luck.
177042: One must never wish fishermen a good voyage, because it was believed this would bring bad luck.
177044: A farmer from Houthulst had bought a horse. A few days later a sorceress from the village knew that the farmer had a new horse. Because of this the horse lay restlessly turning on the ground at night. The farmer sent for the friars to read prayers over his stable. The clergymen said: "Tomorrow morning something will be lying behind your house. You must throw it into the stove." The next morning there was a white handkerchief.
177057: In the evenings a big black dog roamed the Zwijnhoek. No one knew where the animal came from. Late walkers would suddenly see the dog standing in front of them with eyes like burning coals. In the end no one dared to go to that place any more.
177065: In 1870 three young men were sitting in a café. On the way home one of the lads met a beautiful woman. He did not speak to her and went home. The next day the same happened to the second lad. When the third lad saw the beautiful woman the day after, he asked: "What are you doing here?", to which the apparition replied: "Sir, I am so glad that I have been released!" The following night a cow lay dead at a nearby farm. The second night the farmer's wife lay dead in bed and the third night the child became paralysed. Three weeks later the young man who had released the woman died. The doctor had told the lad: "You have released a witch. You must all move away from here or you will all die." A friar had said: "You must pull a post out of the ground near your house and stick it as far into your field as possible. Then all will go well for years. But one day the haunting will start here again."
177066: After a man had died in a house, in the morning the sandwiches and coffee stood ready on the table. That was the work of the dead man who had returned. The two dogs were there too. After a while the two dogs had disappeared.
177086: In Sint-Jan there lived strange women who could work magic. A woman who did not believe it was addressed by a witch with the words: "Just go and stand by that alder hedge, and you'll see!" The woman did so and saw rats sitting all over by the alder hedge. Terrified, she ran away.
177097: On a haunted farm, the animals were always untied at night. When the farmer went to the stable in the morning, the animals were, strangely enough, tied up again.
177112: A man who worked at the haunted castle of Oostrozebeke was coming back from the pub one Sunday night. Above the moat around the castle he saw lots of little red gnomes floating. When he reached the bridge over the moat, he saw a ghost coach with four horses driving towards the castle. The gates opened by themselves and the coach drove in. It was said that it was the former owner come back to haunt.
177131: A doctor from Wijtschate who was attacked bewitched the robbers so they were stuck to the ground and left them standing there until he got home. In 1900 that doctor was murdered. No one ever found out who did it.
177145: The dead often returned to do or say something they had forgotten during their lives.
177154: At school there was a boy who could make mice by blowing on a little heap of clay. The boy had learned that trick from one of his parents. The dean of Gistel took the boy's magic power away.
177177: When a witch came somewhere, the lights above her head swayed back and forth.
177185: On a haunted farm, the cows were found dead at night. When a widow from the neighbourhood was gone, the haunting came to an end. Some people could harm others by reading in books. It was even claimed that priests could easily do so too.
177190: On some farms the cows and horses were untied. This haunting stopped again by itself. It was the devil's work.
177197: A farmer whose hens had been stolen went to an old woman he suspected of the theft and shouted: "You took my hens!" The woman denied it and said: "Today you can still see your hens' feathers, but in a year you won't be able to!" Two months later the man went blind because of the witch's curse.
177219: In the churchyard of Houtem a few little lights were seen dancing above the graves every evening. In the end people no longer dared to pass by, because they believed those lights were returned dead.
177223: In Loppem lived a sorceress who could cure pearls on the eyes. One day, as a joke, the curate went to ask the sorceress whether she could visit a farmer whose pigs had pearls on their eyes. At that the sorceress grew angry and chased the curate with her broom.
177224: A man coming back from the baker's heard a hellish noise at the 'Oekenbrug' (?). It seemed as if a horse came running up and sat down on the man's shoes. The man had to carry the horse until he was drenched in sweat. The animal grew heavier and heavier.
177234: The mare was a nightmare that made one lie sweating in one's bed.
177265: Near the Toveresseknok stood a farm that was haunted every night. In the morning the fields were completely trampled. At night a ghost was seen coming to the farm. The place was exorcised by the clergy, but that did not help.
177268: If a little owl was heard calling, one of the neighbours would die.
177283: On a farm they could not manage to churn butter. The cream always began to froth. When a friar was sent for, he said: "A woman will come asking for a kilo of butter. You must give it to her." After that the farmer had no more problems with churning.
177291: In Watou stood a farm whose occupants always had bad luck. The people always heard noise and they could not churn butter.
177293: On a farm in Wortegem the cows were sick and no butter could be churned anymore. The farmer rode on horseback through the woods to Waregem, where a sorcerer lived. The sorcerer came to the farm and could not leave for home until midnight. On the way he saw three men standing in the woods, who shouted: "Your money or your life!" The sorcerer then opened his coat and gave each of the three robbers a five-franc piece. Then he rode on and told everyone what had happened. At four in the morning the sorcerer rode back along the same road. The thieves were still standing motionless in the same spot with the coin in their hands. "Are you going to give that money back now?" asked the sorcerer. When the thieves had done so, they could move and speak again.
177316: A man peddling rat poison was at a farmer's who said: "I don't need poison, because we have no rats." The peddler replied: "You'll get some yet!" A while later the farmer's farm was swarming with rats. When the peddler was forty years old, he went to a parish priest. The cleric took his power away from him.
177320: A man from Middelburg was walking along the water with a wheelbarrow and two piglets. By a row of tree stumps stood a witch who kept jumping from the stumps into the water and from the water back onto the stumps. When the man had passed a crossroads, he no longer saw the witch.
177329: On a farm where some men were threshing, they wanted to test whether it was possible to hang yourself with a straw of oats. The men decided to put it to the test and made a noose from a straw. The man who was going to try it said to the others: "If I can't get loose, you must untie me!" Suddenly a hare ran around in the barn, distracting the man on the floor, who ran after the hare. Meanwhile the man with his head in the noose choked. There was an iron wire in the straw. That hare in the barn must have been the devil.
177335: A mother was terrified of a woman from the neighbourhood. The mother's baby had been ill for eleven months. The child did nothing but cry as if its throat were being squeezed shut all the time. When the priest had read prayers over the child, it no longer made a sound. The next day, however, the child was dead.
177337: In the past people believed that children got 'de mare' (a nightmare spirit affliction) after an old woman had been in the house. In reality 'de mare' was an illness. Women who had a bent back or could imitate a dog or a cat were soon called witches.
177362: Whoever was ridden by the mare got lost and could only find his bearings again a long time later.
177375: A woman heard her dead husband walking across the attic in heavy clogs every evening.
177417: Near Lendelede lived a woman who always wore a white pipe-shaped cap. Some people who had gone to celebrate New Year got lost through that woman's doing. Wherever they went, they always met that witch.
177437: A tailor's son had to deliver a parcel somewhere. On the way he met an old woman who was said to be a sorceress. To show he was not afraid, the boy said good day rather cheekily. The woman did not answer and walked on. A little further on the tailor's son was knocked to the ground by an invisible force.
177445:
A mother had a son of seventeen months who cried all the time. Because people believed the child was bewitched, they took the boy to the friars of the Sint-Sixtus Abbey in West-Vleteren. The friars did not believe in witchcraft, but they read prayers over the child anyway. The boy did not get better, however. He neither ate nor drank, yet the mother had to wash as many as thirty-five nappies every day. Three times the mother called in a woman to lay out the child, because she thought it was dead. Because the child then suddenly moved again, they knew it was not dead. When the mother-in-law one day had seen the priest and the friar of Abele walk past, she decided to call the two clergymen in on their way back. A few minutes after the woman had said this, the chaplain of Poperinge came to visit, saying: "I've come to see how things are going here." The chaplain asked for some holy water and began to pray until drops of sweat rolled down his forehead. The women had to pray as well. A little later the child opened its eyes wide and tears rolled out. The child had never shed tears before; they looked like peas coming out of its eyes. The chaplain went on praying for a while and then gave the child a little cross, saying: "It will be all right." The following night the child slept peacefully and shortly afterwards it could even walk.
The woman who had bewitched the child was a friend of the mother.
177452: In the old days rats could be sent from one farm to another by magic. The rats could only be sent to a place where things were better, otherwise they would return.
177456: Little lights were dead people who had returned to ask for prayers.
177457: In Aalbeke lived a woman who had already lost four or five children. One day the woman sent for the priest. After praying for a while, the priest predicted that no more children would die. After that the woman had two more children, who both lived. When the woman came out of church one day, she got a box on the ear from that witch.
177467: On a farm struck by the evil hand, butter could no longer be made. There was always dung in the cream.
177490: When an old woman had stayed sitting in the church, the priest said there was evil in the church. The woman could not get out because the priest had left the missal open.
177496: In Hulsvelde a castle had sunk into the ground, at a place called 'den holden meers' (the low-lying meadow). At midnight a beautiful lady always walked around there.
177511: A man whose wife was heavily pregnant went to fetch the midwife by bicycle one night. At the Kruiswater the man found that one of the wheels of his bicycle no longer turned. The man put the bicycle on his shoulder and went on. A little later he saw a black cat run off.
177513: In Ardooie lived a woman who was said to be able to bewitch. Whenever that woman was talking to someone, she always touched that person. To protect yourself against witchcraft, you had to keep your arm higher than the woman's. A farmer's wife who had already lost two children claimed the sorceress was responsible for their deaths. One day the sorceress had taken one of the children on her lap, supposedly because it was crying. Three days later the child was dead.
177520: In Beselare there was a child who cried all the time. The family took the child to the friars in Ieper, who asked whether a woman had come to visit. The family had indeed had a visit from a woman who was said to bewitch children. They were given a medal to hang on the door. If the witch came again to ask how the child was, they were to say: "Good, thank God." The witch would then leave and never come back. The family did exactly what the friars had advised. When the witch stood at the door, the child's father could not get off the toilet to give her a beating. It was as if he had been bewitched and stuck in place. The whole time the man saw a sword above his head. As long as the woman had not left, the man could not get up.
177522: In Snellegem there lived a man who could make mice by drawing something on the ground.
177533: A man whose godfather had died heard the doors and windows banging open and shut at night. In the doorway a large crucifix appeared with blinding rays of light. The dean came to sprinkle the place with holy water. The apparitions were caused by the dead parish priest, who came to tell what things were like in the hereafter.
177541: A man had promised to have masses said, but he had not kept that promise. Every night in his sleep the man saw the ghost of his father and his mother.
177548: A girl lying in bed felt a big black cat crawl onto her belly. The sweating girl tried to call for help, but she could not make a sound. As soon as her aunt called the girl's name, the cat was gone.
177560: A town has sunk into the 'Briekeput' in Les Moères. Anything that fell into that pit was never seen again.
177567:
A family whose children all died just after birth was the victim of witchcraft. Almost the same happened at the neighbours'; the first three daughters lived, but the first three sons died. When one day one of the girls was ill, a sorceress came by, took the girl's arm and said: "You will get better quickly now." Eight days later the child was perfectly healthy again.
The curate collected that sorceress's books. After that two more children were born in that family, who both lived.
177585: A mother who had a beautiful child noticed that the child was growing very thin. A neighbour advised the mother to go to a healer. The healer examined the child and said: "It is there, but the child will not die. You must go to the Kelderke van Miserie in Kortrijk and to the church of Zwevegem." The mother sent her husband to those places. On his way home the man got lost, so that he had to ask the way some ten times. The mother also had to give the child buttermilk and take the child to Steenbrugge. When the mother did so, she saw a woman in a black hat with a feather coming out of the field. The woman greeted the mother and asked if she could see the child. The mother refused and went into her brother-in-law's house. The woman stayed waiting by the door. Then the woman accompanied the mother all the way to Steenbrugge. The friars read prayers over the child, and afterwards the mother also had to make a novena herself. Then the child recovered.
177587: A girl who was walking through the woods to work one evening with her boyfriend got the following advice from him: "If a werewolf comes at you, you must throw a ball of yarn at the beast. Then you will stay unharmed". At a certain moment the boy said he had to go off for a moment to relieve himself. In reality the boy jumped into the tree stump in which he had hidden his animal skin and appeared to his girlfriend in the shape of a werewolf. Quite a while later the boy came back to the girl. The girl then said: "You were gone a long time. The werewolf was here". The boy was still busy removing the bits of yarn that had got stuck between his teeth.
177589: A woman worked as a maid on a haunted farm in Otegem. When the maid was milking the cows on Sundays, the wooden beams came down as far as the cows' backs, so that the animals ran outside. The maid told the farmer's wife everything, who said: "Oh, you mustn't pay attention to that. That is witchcraft or haunting." Because these strange things happened again every Sunday, the girl eventually no longer wanted to work on that farm.
177590: Whoever was ridden by the mare was in reality having a stopping of the blood. To protect oneself against the mare, one had to lay two knives crossed beside the bed.
177592: A couple from Snellegem had a six-week-old child that cried all the time. One day they had prayers read over the child by the friars. When the mother was sitting by the stove with her child some time later, she saw a toad jump off the child. The toad quickly hopped outside.
177595: Every time a man passed the 'borieputje', a black calf appeared and followed him. The borieputje had come into being when the French soldiers had stolen the cross of Vijve and thrown it away there.
177615: A mother whose baby lay in the cradle was visited by a woman who said: "What a beautiful child!" Two days later the baby was dead. That woman was never let into that house again.
177625: A farmer's wife who could not churn butter sought advice from the friars of Steenbrugge. The clergyman said to her: "The problem will be solved, but first you will see something strange in the butter churn." When she got home, the farmer's wife saw a worm as big as a finger crawl out of the churn. After the churn had been blessed, butter could be churned again.
177626: The blue castle in Aalbeke had been haunted since the fifteenth century. On the evening of All Saints' Day there was a knock at the door. Although the door was bolted, it flew open a moment later. Sometimes balls were heard rolling across the floor all night. At night there was also always a scratching on the wall. When the wall was demolished, money was found. Money was also found on the attic stairs. In 1897 the occupants of the castle moved out. After the First World War the castle was demolished.
177632:
In Koekelare lived a widower who had remarried a woman who could not stand his son. "Even if I have to sell you to the devil, you must get out of here!" the stepmother said to the boy. When the father was out with his son one evening, he met a gentleman on horseback. The gentleman had flaming eyes and asked: "Is it true that you want to sell him?" For fifteen stuivers a month the father sold his son for a period of three years. The boy worked in the service of the devil.
One day the boy had to go along to the freemasons' lodge in Brugge to fetch a dead framasson (freemason).
When the boy had been in hell for a year, his godmother came in.
In hell there were seven halls in which sinners had to suffer according to the nature of their sin.
Three years later the boy came back to his father. He did not speak for a long time.
177640: A witch made the children who passed her house die.
177652: A man who was ridden by the mare woke up in Brugge.
177669: A doctor who could work magic once lived in Wijtschate. When someone said something to the doctor that he did not like, the doctor could fix that person to the ground by magic.
177677: On a farm almost all the animals died. Between midnight and one o'clock an old woman always passed by the farm. However hard they tried, they could never catch up with her. It was a sorceress who lived a little further on. When another woman passed by the farm, she was struck by an invisible figure. A little further on a black cat leapt at her feet, which only vanished when she made the sign of the cross. When the sorceress had died, all these strange events came to an end.
177697: On a farm in Merkem strange things always happened. At night between eleven and one, sounds were heard there, although there was nothing to be seen. The children of the occupants later went to live elsewhere.
177703: A stable hand who was coming back from the shop in the morning passed a hedge that was moving back and forth. Scared to death, the stable hand ran home.
177722: A farmer's wife was visited by a woman who wanted to see the pigs. The woman stroked the animals' backs. The next day the pigs all had lumps on their backs. After that incident the farmer's wife did not let the woman in again. The woman then went to bewitch pigs elsewhere.
177736: Bells were said to have once sunk in the bell pits in the wood of Koekelare.
177740: The Kwaameersen was haunted. When it was dark, a light was seen moving back and forth there. Nobody dared to pass by there.
177750: Children who suffered from 'the old man' grew very thin. People believed this illness was caused by witchcraft, but that was pure imagination.
177778: A woman had visited a farm in Harelbeke and had left behind a cent, a centime and a pin. After a while three animals died on the farm. The cowshed was also full of lice. When seven sows were taken to a buyer, the animals died before they reached their destination.
177781: A farm in Proven was haunted. In the evening a black hen flew in through a small window. The farmer who lived there was very rich, but hanged himself later in life.
177785: Witches could turn themselves into cats. On a farm that had much misfortune, the people sought the advice of the priests. The clergymen advised the people to beat the first animal that came onto the farm. A cat came. After the animal had been beaten, it ran away. The next day it was found that the neighbour had a big scar on her head. The parish priest came to collect that woman's books. After that she had no more power.
177786: In 1913 a comet was seen in the west. That was an omen of the First World War.
177790: In Avelgem lived a woman who often drank a dram and went begging people for food. If the farmers' wives gave her nothing, they got eczema and accidents happened in the stable. Children who had come too close to the witch were covered in lice.
177802: A man was visited by his neighbour, who came to look at his pig. "What a lovely little pig!" the woman had said, and she had made the sign of the cross on the animal's head. When the man went to look in his stable that evening, his pig lay dead on the ground. It was said that the neighbour owned books of witchcraft.
177811: An altar boy kept watch while a boy went to steal apples in the priest's garden. "Hey, the priest is coming!" the altar boy suddenly shouted. When the boy tried to run away, he got stuck in a hole in the hedge. Yet that hole had been big enough.
177815: On his way home a man always met a black cat. A little further on the man saw a woman in a long black cloak standing with her back to him. When the man reached the churchyard, the woman was standing there again. The man was also being followed by a cat.
177826: A woman went to the curate to ask for an exorcism because her house was haunted. The woman claimed that the locks in her house sprang open at night through a mysterious force. At midnight the woman also heard sounds as if a woman in high heels was walking across the attic. The woman believed it was the devil. The curate sent the woman to the friars, who came to exorcise the house. In the end the woman moved anyway. After that the house stood empty for a long time. The later occupants, however, heard no strange sounds there.
177829: A witch could make her hat fly up into the air in the street by twirling it. A man driving past the witch's house with three horses had to stop because the horses could go no further. The witch could also bewitch children.
177838: On a farm in Sint-Michiels a fine pig had been bought. A woman from the neighbourhood had a pig from the same litter, but much less fine. One day the woman came to look at the farmer's pig. As soon as she had left, the pig became very restless and ran up against the walls. The witch had made the mare (a nightmare spirit) ride the pig.
177877: Near the Vosmolen a man kicked at a cat that was bothering him. The next day a farmer's wife from the neighbourhood had a wound in the spot where the cat had been kicked.
177898: Many Duitse schapers (German shepherds, travelling shepherds said to have magic powers) lived around Houtem. One of them was the son of a witch. He had received books of magic from his mother, which enabled him to tap beer from his walking stick.
177909: A woman met a farmer's wife who said: "On your way you will meet a sow with piglets and you will tremble with fear." The woman met no sow, but when she got home the cow lay dead in the stable.
177910: A man who had gone for a glass of beer walked home. Near a small wood the man got lost. For hours and hours he walked around until he broke out in a sweat. Only after a long time could the man find his bearings again. Just before he got lost, he had met someone who asked: "Aren't you afraid to go home alone?" The man believed that this person had made him lose his way.
177913: On a farm where no foal or calf could be kept alive, the farmer had his stable exorcised and hung something blessed in the stable.
177932: A woman from Leffinge had a baby lying in a cradle. One day, when the mother had been out for a while, she found on her return that the child was ill. Her husband told her that a woman had come peddling yeast. The child did not get better, because it had been struck by the evil hand. The people were advised to go on pilgrimage to Nieuwpoort and have clothes blessed there. Although they prayed for nine days, it was already too late and the child eventually died.
177934: In the old days white men walked about in the churchyard. People said they were the returning dead.
177944: Sorceresses roamed the streets all night. Some children who walked through the woods to school always saw beautiful apples and holy cards lying by a witch's house. "Don't pick those up!" their mother always said.
177954: A farmer's wife had died in Abele. It was said that her death had been caused by a woman who had come to fetch butter at midnight.
177963: A woman set out at night with a walking stick in her hand on a pilgrimage to Zwevegem. In a long lane the woman saw a white cat on the road. The woman struck the cat in two with her stick. A bit further on the woman met a little old lady, who said: "The night is for us and the day is for you". The woman was scared to death.
177970: Men, dogs, horses and goats were often seen near Slabbaartsbuze. It was said that people were assaulted there.
177972: A maid who worked for a parish priest hung crucifixes in the stables. An old woman who often came to the presbytery burned all those crucifixes.
177978: The ghost of a dead person stood in a room with a sad look. After the people had a mass said, the ghost no longer appeared.
177994: In Tillegembos a procession was always seen passing by. It even happened that people riding through the wood saw nothing, yet saw turnips flying around everywhere.
177998: A woman was coming back from Gent with her drunken husband. When they passed the house of a sorceress, the woman urged her husband to be quiet. But the man could not keep silent. Twenty metres further on, the man was thrown into the ditch.
178018: On a farm in Hertsberge nobody could keep animals alive, because a witch lived opposite the farm.
178037:
A woman was kept talking by a chatty friend. Because her husband and son were worried, they went to fetch her. When the three of them reached the castle in Diesveld on the way back, a large grey headless horse appeared there with a chain about fifty centimetres long. The horse stood in front of the gate, so that they could not go on. That horse walked around the moat almost every night. In the trees was a little light that flew around the moat together with the horse.
In the old days strange things happened at night. Many farmhands who had been out in the evening did not dare to set off home until near morning.
178039: The mare is a dream that squeezes people's throats shut at night. A fortune-teller could predict where the mare would be the following night.
178052: A farmer had neglected a vow during his life. When the farmer was dead, the children always heard noises in the house. They even heard their father's voice.
178053: In Hulste there was a building owned by the counts of Paris. In that building and in the garden the ghosts of the former occupants were seen walking about at night. For four generations no one there had received the last rites.
178060: A farmhand had gone somewhere to fetch a glass full of yeast. On the way back he met a woman who said: "You'll have to go and fetch some again." The next moment the glass fell to the ground.
178071: A man who was chased by a black cat ran away as fast as he could. It was said that it was dangerous to kick at a black cat.
178072:
People who were ridden by the mare had a stopping of the blood. They heard everything around them but could not move or speak. If someone said that person's name, he or she was freed from the mare.
On a farm in Libbrecht two farmhands slept in the same bed. Because those farmhands were often ridden by the mare, they hung flax above their bed. The next day the flax was completely flattened.
The farmers' wives often walked around with a knife in a towel in order to find the mare that way.
178076: Some people driving to Mass could not get through the lane because a witch was holding back their horses.
178097: People out late at night were not allowed to kick a black cat. After all, the cat might be a sorceress.
178112: Whoever was ridden by the mare could not scream. To protect oneself against the mare, one had to turn one's clogs so that they stood with the heels under the bed.
178124: On the day before a feast day, around midnight in Poelkapelle, a goat flew through the air, bleating loudly. During the First World War this apparition came to an end.
178129: A man who was ridden by the mare saw two hands that wanted to squeeze his throat shut. At that moment the man woke up.
178141: A man got up at midnight to go and urinate outside. Outside, the man saw a smoothed-out sheet flying between the top of the birch and the top of the poplar that stood next to his house. A little later the sheet flew away.
178160: In a farmhouse in Klemskerke there was an attic room where no one was allowed to sleep, because the dead farmhand who had lived there could come back to do harm. For ten years the farmhand could not return because he was being held back. In the end the room was torn down.
178161: An old woman suspected of being a witch often tried to get into a house, but she could not, because the people had placed an Agnus Dei they had received from the priest in their house. In church this witch always tried to get close to the woman who lived in that house.
178166: Will-o'-the-wisps were in reality doodkeersen (death candles, ghostly lights). These lights hung above a particular spot for a few hours to show that money was buried there.
178179: People who were ridden by the mare could not get out of their bed and felt as if someone was sitting on them.
178203: When the farmers' wives went to the stable to milk the cows, they sprinkled some blessed salt into the first bucket of milk. Then, if a witch came to the farm, she would not be able to bewitch the milk.
178222: On the Kuk next to the Abeelseweg in Poperinge, it used to be haunted at dusk. A fearless man always went bird-catching there with three friends. That man never saw the ghost.
178238: A witch from Veldegem always carried a basket filled with marshmallows to hand out to the children. Most mothers did not want their children to eat them, because they believed the children would be bewitched that way.
178244: An Iceland fisherman had mocked a little woman from De Panne. When the man returned from a stay in Iceland, he saw a frog enter his house through the water drain. That was the woman in question. The man's mother went to the priest. The man had to sit at the communion rail, where the priest would read prayers over him. The priest found that he could do nothing more: the bewitchment had gone too far.
178261: A child claimed it had seen its dead godfather. When the priests came to question the child, it said nothing. A mass was said for the dead man.
178268: In Dadizele there was a haunted inn. Everything in the house began to dance and the lights went out by themselves. When the innkeeper's wife died, many books of magic were found in the house. The priests came to take the books away and read prayers over the house. After that, nothing strange happened in the inn anymore. No one had ever known that the innkeeper's wife was a witch.
178269: The little candles sometimes seen in the wood were souls of the dead who returned to point out their hidden money, because otherwise they had no peace.
178273: A witch took a nappy that was hanging somewhere and said to a child's mother: "You have lovely nappies!" Shortly afterwards the child began to cry. Eight days later the child died. If the mother had thought sooner that the child might be bewitched, she could have thrown the nappy away.
178279: A farmer who had to bring butter to the market in Kortrijk stopped at a farm along the way, hoping to be given a cup of coffee there. The farmer saw the butter churn turning, although no one was to be seen. On the churn lay a little red cloth. When the farmer took the cloth away, the churn stopped turning. As soon as he put the cloth back, the churn started turning again. The farmer was impressed, put the cloth in his pocket and continued on his way to Kortrijk. When the farmer came back from his field the next day, he met a woman dressed in black, who asked him to sign a form. "It is too dark here," the farmer replied. No sooner had he said this than the woman's eyes seemed to give off light. Still the farmer again refused to sign the form. "I will find you," said the woman. The next morning the farmer found that his cows had been tied together by their tails and that his chickens had all been plucked. When the priest had buried the red cloth, the strange events came to an end.
178293: A man sleeping in the horse stable heard a creaking at a certain moment. He thought it was the cat, but a moment later the man felt something crawl up along his body. The man wanted to defend himself with his hands, but he could not. When the man recited the act of contrition, his condition quickly improved.
178294: A man had to go and arrange a funeral in Langemark. When the man came to 't Zwartegat, he saw a gentleman approaching, who asked: "Friend, are you going for a walk?" The man answered: "That is none of your business," whereupon the gentleman said: "God keep you." The man then said: "If I am kept by God, I do not need to be kept by you," and went on. A little further on, the man saw a stream and a row of trees on both sides of him. When the man arrived at the farm in Langemark, the people there shouted: "Hey, stop!" The man halted and saw that he was standing right in front of a well.
178325: In Roksem lived a man who owned books of magic. Although that man's wife worked for the priest, the man never went to church. By means of his books of magic, the man could make the devil appear and disappear again. A black beast always appeared at the window of the house. When the woman went to fetch water, the beast ran around her skirts. Because the woman was annoyed by the beast, one day she told the priest. The clergyman asked the woman: "Does your husband have books?" When the woman said yes, the priest promised to come by some time. The priest came to the house praying and sweating. After the clergyman had exorcised the man, he was able to seize the books of magic and take them away. After that the black beast never appeared again.
178341: Sometimes you could meet a witch who asked: "Shall I help you?" But people did not trust the witch. If you were touched by the witch, you might arrive at the market with a basket full of stones instead of a basket of butter.
178342: In a house in Beselare, noises were always heard at night. The tables and chairs danced and the door handles moved up and down. When the people got up, however, there was nothing to be seen. Eventually the people sought the advice of a woman, who came to say a prayer in the house. After that no more strange things happened in the house.
178346: Whoever walked along a river and was ridden by the mare was pushed into the water.
178354: In a convent in Pollinkhoeve, the sisters heard chains rattling in the evening when they went to bed. The sound moved back and forth all night between the convent and the school.
178368: A woman coming back from mass was covered in lice and fleas. All the little boys who had been in church were also full of vermin. A sorcerer had been sitting in the church.
178392: People who were ridden by the mare had a stopping of the blood when going to sleep.
178409: A woman who could do magic always said to people: "You're going to fall." A little later those people really did fall.
178424: A girl lying in bed heard the door handle move. A little later the window flew open. The girl got up to close the door and the window. As soon as she was back in bed, it all started again. It was the fault of the maid, who in the end had to be dismissed.
178440: In the neighbourhood of the parish of Geluwe, nobody dared to go outside in the dark any more. A girl had fallen ill there and all the chickens and rabbits died.
178442: In Blankenberge there was a small dead-end street that led onto the sea dyke. Nobody dared to go there, because people believed it was haunted. In that street the wind could be heard whistling. There were ghosts there.
178457: At the farm of the white canons in Stavele the gate opened by itself at night. A rustling was heard and then a golden coach with several horses drove out. In the morning the coach was back inside.
178466:
Two women who had gone to fetch rabbit feed had to pass the house of a witch on the way back. At that moment one of the women said: "Just look, she'll be standing behind that box hedge again." A little later the woman who had said it had to dance in a puddle in front of the witch's house with the sack of feed on her head.
