181870: A woman from Leke heard knocking in the cesspit every night. One day she went to fetch the friars of Steenbrugge. After the friars had read prayers of deliverance over the pit, the woman no longer heard the knocking.
181876: A witch always tried to get near small children. A woman from Westrozebeke who could work witchcraft was let in almost nowhere. When she knocked on someone's window, people took their stove poker and shouted: "You just stay outside!"
181882: A farmhand told a clergyman that every night he saw a horse appear in the stable where he slept. The clergyman advised the farmhand to ride the horse the next time and have it shod by the smith. The next night the farmhand did as the clergyman had advised. The next morning the farmer stood outside shouting: "My wife is lying shod in bed!"
181901: A farm in Ardooie was badly haunted. A little further on stood a small chapel. A farmhand from Kachtem had to go to the fair in Lichtervelde. When he reached the haunted farm, the horses would not go any further. The farmhand went to the chapel to pray a little. After that the horses went on again. Since that incident the following text has been placed on the chapel: "Whether on horseback or on foot, say a Hail Mary here".
181905: A witch sitting in church could not get up from her chair until the priest said: "You may go now."
181907: Every evening a red light burned above a well in which a treasure was buried. Whoever crawled into that well and could hold his breath for one minute got the treasure. If you breathed anyway, you died. The well lay near Ichtegem or Eernegem.
181914: Anyone who was ridden by the maar (nightmare spirit) could not speak and woke up sweating.
181930: A woman from Bavikhove left for Mass far too early on Christmas Day because her clock was broken. As the woman walked through the wood, she met a burning pig that chased her. The woman only got rid of the animal when she reached the church porch.
181937: A girl was late for school because she had stood watching a woman from Bulskamp who could make mice.
181957: A farmer's wife on her way to mass saw a beautiful foal lying by the road. When she came back, she found that the foal had turned into a harrow. When she got home, she was visited by a woman who wanted something to drink. After drinking, the woman threw the cup away and vanished without a trace. That was a witch who could take on different shapes.
181960:
A German shepherd worked in Moen. One day some young girls passed by and did not greet the shepherd. A little later the girls were covered in lice, so they had to go back and say: "Good day, shepherd."
That shepherd could also make rats crawl up the walls.
182005: A fisherman must never be wished a good voyage when he left. When a fisherman from Blankenberge was about to go to sea, his neighbour, who knew nothing of this superstition, called out without thinking: "Have a good voyage!" Two hours after the ship had sailed, the engine was found to be broken.
182006: On a farm in Ledegem a mother lived with her son's family. When the farmer could no longer churn butter, he sought advice from the friars. A clergyman came by who wanted to look at the mother's books. The mother then claimed she had no books. The clergymen found books all the same. When the mother had been put out on the street, the problems with the butter were solved.
182017: A man on his way to his girlfriend thought he saw a group of people standing in the distance. When the man came closer, however, he realised they were ghosts. The man was so frightened that he started to run. The faster he ran, the faster the ghosts ran after him.
182029: In Bossuit the counts had all criminals hanged in the tower of the manor farm. Later people claimed that the place was haunted. A mound of earth could still be seen there, with a cross on it in memory of the criminals who were buried there.
182032: A dead man who had returned walked around with a stick, calling all the time: "Where must I stick it? Where must I stick it?" After a drunkard answered: "Stick it where you pulled it out", the ghost was released.
182059: Some pub-goers said that skulls always hung in a weeping willow in Merksem at midnight. That is why nobody dared to walk past that weeping willow any more.
182071: At a café where a witch lived, it was always swarming with animals. Sometimes they were cats, other times dogs, sheep or rats.
182077: When a German shepherd saw young women passing on their way to mass who forgot to greet him, he made sure the women were completely full of lice by the time they reached the church. The women then had to go back home.
182092: An engaged couple were walking past a little chapel near the Tempeliershoeve in Vinkem. Suddenly the boy said to his girlfriend: "Wait here a moment, I still have an errand to do". As the girl stood waiting, she felt her gold necklace being torn away. A little later the boy came back. "Look, my necklace is gone!" said the girl. The next moment she saw that her boyfriend had the gold links of the necklace between his teeth. Because of this the werewolf was released.
182109: In the Zolderstraat in Otegem there lived a framasson (freemason) who believed in neither God nor commandment and who was always cursing. One day, as the man was coming back from the castle of Diesveld, two grey gentlemen suddenly came out of the corn and accompanied him home. In the man's house everything began to shake. When everything had been turned upside down, the two grey gentlemen vanished. The next day the framasson had hanged himself. It was two devils who had brought the man home.
182118: A cat sat behind a house in Gullegem. When a man threw a stone at the cat, the animal said: "Ow, ow!"
182119: A woman from Stene tormented people by sticking pins into a little wax doll.
182121: A man and a woman had a seven-month-old child that was full of worms. The parents took the child to the curate. Because the clergyman saw that the child's neck was full of worms, he asked whether the child had been washed. "Certainly," the parents replied. The curate tried to reassure the parents and promised to come by the following Monday. The curate did not come that Monday. On the Friday before the Langemark fair, however, the curate did turn up. He read prayers over the cradle and predicted that the child would recover. For three days the child was calm. Then it began to toss and cry again. The following Wednesday the child's father went to watch the fireworks for the fair. A little later he saw his wife coming after him, although that was not her habit. "And the child?" the man asked, to which his wife replied: "X is with it." That was a man who lived with them. When the parents came back from the fireworks, that man said: "Y (a woman from the village) was here and she wanted to take the child out of the cradle at all costs." The next day the mother laid the child in the cradle. When she went to look a while later, she found that the child was dead. The parents told the curate what had happened. The clergyman then said to the mother: "You surely took off your ring when you were carrying the child?" The woman denied it, but the curate said: "Yes, you did." Then the mother realised the clergyman was right.
182135: People who were ridden by the maar (nightmare spirit) in their bed could hardly breathe.
182167: At the mill on the road to Ingelmunster, past the castle of Thienponds, a procession was often seen in the evening. The people were all dressed in white and even Our Lady was among them. Whenever the procession passed, the mill always stopped.
182172: A man who lived in Kachtem was visited one day by a woman who was coming back from Rumbeke. When that woman had left, the chairs were completely full of lice and fleas.
182173: In Woumen lived a witch. When people saw her coming, they quickly shut their doors. When people could not churn butter, they believed they had to chase away the first person who came to visit the next morning. Small children who were not healthy were also said to be bewitched.
182190: In Oostende lived a woman who, for payment, could make someone's runaway boyfriend or husband come back.
182194: A man who was ridden by the maar (nightmare spirit) reached for the tormenting spirit with his hand and felt a long-haired dog. The maar was a sorceress who sat on her victims.
182204:
At a farm where butter was being churned, a woman came to ask for a litre of buttermilk. But the woman got nothing.
Whenever the people drove past that woman's house, the crank of their cart broke.
182205: A woman who kept a shoe shop had taken a child out of its cradle. Afterwards that child fell ill. After that incident the shopkeeper no longer sold children's shoes. She was also let in nowhere any more.
182215: The devil came into a café, lit a candle there and said: "When that candle has burned down, I will come to fetch your souls". Then the candle was blown out and walled up in the wall so that it would not burn down.
182232: A girl who worked on a farm in Westouter had to take the bus to Brabant in winter. When the girl walked to the bus stop, she had to go through a meadow. In that meadow the girl got hopelessly lost. Only at eight o'clock in the evening could she find her bearings again. The farmer's wife the girl worked for could do witchcraft.
182244: A cowherd who worked for a farmer in Moeskroen slept in the attic. One evening through the attic window the man saw a little light flying from the trees to the hedges, from there to the apple tree and then to a hill. Three freemasons lay buried on that hill.
182247: A man going to his parents-in-law saw a pretty kitten on the way. Because the man wanted to take that kitten with him, he asked his father-in-law for a sack to put the animal in. On his way back the man put the cat in the sack. When he got home, the man put the kitten in the attic and gave it food and drink. Three days later the man went to his father-in-law again. On the way he saw that same kitten, which walked along with him for a while. After that the man never wanted anything to do with cats again. It was a phantom animal.
182263: During Advent people were not allowed to go outside after six in the evening, because then the werewolves were about. One day a farmer said to his farmhand: "Make sure the gate and the stable door are bolted and then hurry inside". The farmer's son then said to his father: "That's not necessary. I know a good way to teach the werewolves a lesson!" When they heard the werewolf coming, they threw yarn from the loom outside. The next day the farmer and his wife saw that their farmhand had yarn between his teeth...
182269: Some fishermen cast their nets at their usual spot. Because after several attempts they still had not caught any fish, the captain decided that the devil must be on board. He ordered all the crew to put their clothes on inside out, so that the devil would not recognise them. The fishermen each took an iron bar and began striking the beams, the pulleys, the planks and so on. After all, the devil had to be hiding somewhere. At a certain moment the helmsman pretended that the ship was returning to Oostende. That is how the ship got rid of the devil. When they went back to the same place, they brought in a great catch of fish.
182287:
A long-haired man who peddled laces was sent away from a farm by a drunken farmer who had just slaughtered a pig. Two days later that farm was full of rats. The farmer went to the peddler's house, just as the peddler was arriving with his basket. The peddler went with him to the farm, where he was given a drink and some food. When the farmer said that his farm was full of rats, the peddler suggested going to smoke a pipe at the neighbours'. When they came home, the farmer and the peddler found that the rats were still there. The peddler had the farmhand called and told everyone to stay inside. He himself went outside with the farmhand. At about eleven o'clock at night the peddler had the farmhand set fire to five bundles of straw. A little later all the rats had gone.
The next day the rats were on a farm where a German shepherd worked. The farmer believed the shepherd had something to do with it and was about to dismiss him. The peddler also called on him and was given a drink and some food. The next day the rats were on a farm in Rekkem.
One day the peddler went to give a dead pig to a farmer. The farmer accepted the gift and kept it in his cellar. The next day, however, the pig had disappeared. The peddler had magicked it away again because he had not received a reward from the farmer.
182288: Some people had special powers. A farmer from Ruddervoorde had sold his pig and was taking the animal to Wingene with a cow. On the way, however, the cow would no longer pull the cart. A man was standing by the road, who said: "What bad luck you're having!" After the farmer had talked with that man for a while, the cow went on again. Because of that conversation, the animals were freed from the power.
182289: A farmer could not keep a single farmhand. One day another new farmhand came to the farm. Whenever this farmhand wanted to take the horse out of the stable, the animal always kicked at him. The farmhand jumped on the horse and rode it until it nearly collapsed. Then he took the horse to the smith. When he came home, the farmer's wife lay in bed with horseshoes on her hands and feet. After the witch was unmasked, there were never any more problems on that farm.
182303: A man who was on the roof putting up an aerial heard a woman passing by say: "You won't get off that roof again." And so it was. When that same man was doing another little job, the witch said: "You'll hit your thumb." That happened too. One day the witch said to the man: "You're going to drink coffee," to which the man replied: "No, no." But because the man could not get his car started, he went inside to drink coffee after all. White mice came running out of the man's trouser pocket. That witch was actually a fortune teller who read cards and owned books of magic. The witch did not get on with the priest because he wanted her to hand over her book of magic.
182305: At the Engelhoek in Ingooigem there was a copse that was always full of leaping doodkeersen (death candles). People said these were the dead returning to their money.
182309: A pregnant woman had a seamstress make clothes for her child. When the child was born, it was completely swollen. The priest came to read prayers over the sick child until he was drenched in sweat. The clergyman advised the mother to let no one in. When the seamstress came to bring the clothes, she was not let in. After that the child recovered.
182329: A man who was always ridden by the maar (nightmare spirit) had become as thin as a rake. When a friend of his slept in his bed one Sunday afternoon as a test, the friend soon woke up sweating. He saw a large rust-brown dog sitting on his belly.
182331: Every week on Sunday evening a man would ring the parish priest's doorbell and then run away. One day the man got stuck to the bell. When the priest got up in the morning, he said to the man: "What are you doing here by that bell?" After the priest had prayed for a while, the man could leave again.
182336: A man who worked as a cowherd for a farmer had to fetch the gardener of the castle of Ardooie one winter night because a cow was about to calve. On the square by the castle, around midnight, the man saw two people in black cloaks walking and said: "Good evening". The two people did not answer and a moment later had vanished without a trace.
182353: A girl had given a slice of bread to a beggar woman. The beggar woman then patted the girl on the shoulder, saying: "You are a good girl." Two days later, however, the girl fell ill. Because the doctor could not help, the priest was sent for. The priest gave the girl a little cross and advised her family to go on pilgrimage. On Saturday morning at about three o'clock two people set off for Zwevegem. When they were halfway, they could hardly go on. After mass in Zwevegem the pilgrims were given a ribbon and a cake. The sick girl had to wear the ribbon for nine days and eat from the cake for nine days. At the moment the pilgrims could not go on, the girl had also been drenched in sweat. At that moment the evil had been turned back. A while later the girl was cured.
182358: A woman looking out of the window saw a white figure standing on the road. When a bicycle passed a little later, the figure vanished. But as soon as the bicycle was out of sight, the ghost was standing there again. The woman went to the priest, who said: "If you see the figure again, you must make the sign of the cross." When the woman had done so, the ghost vanished at once.
182366: A mother who had twice been visited by an old woman who had taken her child in her arms noticed that her little daughter became fretful. The woman took the child to the priest, who asked her whether she had holy water, palm twigs and a wooden cross. The clergyman read prayers over the child until it was drenched in sweat. The sweat had to be left to dry. The priest gave the mother an Easter nail to protect the child. After that the old woman could no longer enter the mother's house.
182373: Anyone who was ridden by the maar (nightmare spirit) in his sleep could not move or scream.
182374:
A black cat always prowled around a house and would not let anyone chase it away. One day a man struck the animal with a hot pan. The next day the man saw that a neighbour had burns on her arms, legs and face.
In the past such things happened often. The priest once threatened that after mass he would bind all the witches fast by magic in front of the church door.
182391: In Steenkerke there was a farm so badly bewitched that the priests were powerless. The clergymen had banished the evil to a remote corner of the land, but every day it came one footstep closer.
182392: At night a man always heard the eternal hunter calling in the sky. He was a man who had done something wrong and therefore had to keep hunting forever. The sound was probably just the call of an owl. The story of the eternal hunter can be compared with the stories about the Wandering Jew.
182396: On a farm the people were always full of fleas after an old witch had visited. Eight days later the fleas were gone in a single night.
182414: During the month of May, people went to the little chapel to pray a paternoster. Some people had seen a doodkaars (death candle, a ghostly light) in the grove next to the chapel. That meant a fortune was hidden there.
182417: In Beveren there was a barn where noises were always heard at night, as if grain were being threshed. Strangely enough, in the morning there was no sign of anything. That barn was later demolished.
182425: Some people claimed that doodkaarsen (death candles) were little worms. According to others they were returned dead.
182442: A sorcerer sat threshing and binding wheat in the barn at night without anyone seeing him. At school he could also make little mice run around. The sorcerer said to a woman: "I'll send you a pack of mice tonight," and the woman replied: "You can't do that!" That evening mice crawled all over the bed and up the legs of the table. The woman saw the mice, but her husband could not see them. One day the priest made sure the sorcerer could no longer make mice.
182495:
The son of a woman from Passendale made mice during catechism class out of earth he scraped from his clogs. When the curate came to see what was going on, the boy made another mouse. Then he wanted to make a second mouse, but that went less well. After that the boy could not make a single mouse any more.
A woman who rode the mail coach to the market in Koekelare always had bad luck when that woman from Passendale was also in the coach.
182496: In Kachtem lived a witch. Nearby lived a man who was often ill. The drive to his house was covered with gravel, so that visitors could be heard arriving. Whenever the man heard the witch coming, he was always afraid. He would then always take a little holy water. One day the witch came to bring eggs for the sick man. But the man did not dare eat the eggs and had them thrown in the toilet after the witch had left. The next time the witch visited, she said: "I haven't brought any eggs, because you just throw them in the toilet anyway." Yet no one had told the witch what had been done with the eggs.
182503: A man returning from the fair was annoyed by a little kitten that kept running between his legs. The man picked up the kitten and a little further on it was thrown into the water. That cat was a sorceress who lived nearby.
182538: In Ledegem lived a man who was afraid of nothing. When that man walked across the field one evening, he was accompanied by a dog a good metre in size. That dog kept running around the man and went with him until he was home.
182539: In Middelkerke lived a woman who could work witchcraft. Wherever she got the chance, she bewitched children. One day, after quarrelling with a family, she made the clothes of their little daughter catch fire. But the body did not burn. The little bird's nest hanging there also burst into flames through the witch's doing.
182570: In Dudzele lived a witch who could force people to walk around until they dropped.
182576: Werewolves were people who had special powers. If you could burn a werewolf's skin, the werewolf lost his power. If that did not work, you had to throw yarn at the werewolf. For as long as the werewolf had work to do, he could do no harm.
182587: Near the Catsberg lived a sorceress who could make passing carts tip over.
182595: A merchant always came home with his horse and cart only around midnight. Whenever this merchant came near a witch's house, he could no longer get home. He had to drive around some twenty times with his horses, which began to foam at the mouth. The man wanted to say something, but he could not.
182600: A green lady always came haunting at the farm 't Leeg Hof. A singing green lady walked about there and threw earth at children who teased her. A little later those children would be full of lice.
182615: A man who was ridden by the maar (nightmare spirit) tried to call out, but no sound came. The curate claimed that the maar was a bad dream that made the blood stand still. Some people believed that someone could send the maar to you.
182618: On the Rode Berg in Westouter lived an old woman who was said to be able to do witchcraft. This woman could make the wheels of a wagon stand still.
182667: A woman about whom there was much gossip bought two cakes for five francs at a baker's. Then the woman gave one of the cakes to the baker's little daughter. The baker's wife then said: "My children don't need those cakes. Now get out of here!" Afterwards the baker's wife burned the cake.
182670: Two farmers who could not churn butter went to the friars because they believed that a woman with books of magic was responsible for their misfortune.
182671: A woman wanted to start a farm in a house in Blankenberge. But a sorceress lived next door to that house. When the woman first came into the house she wanted to rent, she was completely covered in fleas. So the woman refused to rent the house. The neighbour had sent the fleas out of jealousy.
182676: A man lay shouting and raging when he was ridden by the maar (nightmare spirit), but nobody could hear him. When his clogs were under his bed, the man could hear sounds in the clogs, made by the maar.
182690:
A five-year-old girl was perfectly healthy and already weighed twenty-five kilos.
One day, after she had sat on a cart together with a woman, the girl fell ill. The child's belly swelled up. The girl had in fact been bewitched.
After three masses had been said in Zillebeke, the girl recovered.
182698: On a farm worked a maid who was suspected of being a witch. For one morning the cows had been seen hanging from a beam.
182711: On the road from Hollebeke to Zillebeke stood a little haunted house. Chains could be heard rattling there, but when people went inside, there was nothing to be seen. In the end the house had to be demolished because nobody wanted to live in it.
182727: Near the churchyard a man saw a cat with fiery eyes. The more the man backed away, the bigger the cat grew. When the cat was as big as the church, the man ran away in fear.
182734: On summer evenings people at the Noordhoek between the Zwijnebak and Nieuwkerke heard a goat screaming in the air. People came from far and wide to listen to the goat.
182763: A young stable hand was driving two horses past a house where a woman was leaning over the stable door. The horses would not go past the house. "Give me those horses!" said the man accompanying the stable hand. With a lot of cursing, the man managed to get the horses past the house.
182767: At an inn a maid worked looking after the children. The maid's mother also often visited those people. Strangely, one of the children was often ill. When a clergyman came to visit, he advised the people to dismiss the maid. For her mother was a witch.
182772: In Waregem lived a woman who could work witchcraft. That woman hit people on the shoulder and on the head. If one did not quickly make the sign of the cross and hit the witch on her head too, one was soon covered in boils.
182795: A fifteen-year-old girl woke up in the middle of the night and cried: "There was a beast on top of me and I couldn't breathe!" Because the girl was tormented by a cat every night, her mother sent for the curate. Before the clergyman rang the bell, he stood praying at the door for a good quarter of an hour. Then the curate came in and fixed Easter nails to the door in two places. He then said to the girl: "The woman who is doing this to you will no longer be able to come in." That woman owned books of magic with which she could set the devil on the girl. If the curate had not stepped in, the girl would have fallen ill.
182800:
A woman whose child was under the influence of evil sought advice from the friars of Kortrijk. One of the clergymen said to the woman: "Madam, you are too late. Your child is dead. I won't say who is to blame, but it is a woman who comes by every day."
[text incomplete in thesis]
182819: Part of Oostende was said to have been flooded by the sea. When there were high waves because a storm was coming, the fishermen heard the bells ringing beneath the sea.
182842: A castle once stood on a hill in Passendale. The dead lord of the castle and his brother returned there at night. They were always tied to each other.
182858: A bricklayer was standing on scaffolding when the parish priest came by. "Well, Father, where are you going so early in the morning?" asked the bricklayer. The clergyman answered that he was going to the station at Eernegem. "You'll surely be late," the bricklayer then said. "Oh no, I have plenty of time," the priest replied. When the clergyman got to the station, his train had already left after all. On the way back he saw that the bricklayer was still standing with his trowel and the same brick in his hands. In the meantime he had not been able to do any work. The priest had seen to that.
182877: In the Karreweg there was a brothel where there was often singing and dancing. People believed that the Freemasons met there. If the hall was too small, the walls opened up.
182878: In Klerken lived a woman who could not bake bread. The clergy advised her to light the wood in the oven with a blessed candle. When the woman had done so, a dead little woman lay in her bed. At once the woman knew who had made her bread fail.
182889: A maid going to mass early in the morning saw a flame in the shape of a horse come out of a chapel. The same thing happened three times. The maid made the sign of the cross and went on.
182902: A woman from Sijsele went to fetch milk at a farm where there were many sons. Every time the sons had to draw lots, the woman could predict whether they would have bad luck or good luck. If the boys were going to have bad luck, the woman advised the farmer's wife to pray. Because of this the boys did not have to go into the army after all.
182912: A man always felt something strange when he put his hand into a tree in the woods. The man eventually went mad. The man also heard music in a tree stump.
182940: A family in Langemark had a little child who cried day and night. A woman often came to visit that house. One day a small cushion with as many as a thousand pins was taken out of the child's bed. After that the child no longer cried, but it did die in the end. The people were afraid of the woman who came to visit there.
182949: In a house a dead soldier came to haunt whenever someone of the family was home alone. The friars gave the people the following advice: "Ask why he returns and do what he says." So the people learned that the soldier had promised to have two masses said and that he had not kept that promise. The haunting soldier held out his hand and said: "You must not touch my hand with your bare hand. Wrap your hand in a handkerchief first." The dead man burned his hand into that handkerchief. After the promise had been fulfilled, the haunting soldier was never seen again.
182951: A witch's daughter wanted to go away with her sweetheart, but she was made unhappy by her mother, who had bewitched her.
182995: Near Merkem there lived a framasson (freemason). When that man was dead, it was found that his coffin was full of stones. The body had been taken away by the devils.
182997: In a haunted house a greyhound was always seen walking on the stairs.
183032: On a farm a cat was in the cellar. Someone managed to catch the animal and beat it. The next day a woman from the village lay ill in bed. She had been that cat.
183044: One day a Jesuit wizard had been locked up. The guard had only just put the key in his pocket when the Jesuit was already standing beside him.
183051: In Maldegem lived a woman who was said to be able to work witchcraft. Whenever that woman had visited small children, those children always began to cry. One day the witch went to buy meat from a mother in the neighbourhood. Although the witch was not allowed near the cradle, she went to it anyway. As soon as the witch had left, the child began to cry.
183057: A woman was visited by her neighbour, who told how a witch had bewitched her child by looking at it. After that the child began to cry and in the end it died.
183066: One day the Sint-Jan procession could not take place because of the bad weather. The next day it was found that the statue of Mary was covered in mud. Mary had gone out on her own. Since then the procession was never cancelled again, whatever the weather.
183068: Some people who went to the beach on a Sunday to gather driftwood met the parish priest, who said they should go to vespers instead of spending time on the beach. The people ignored the priest's remark and kept working. Only on Monday morning did they come home, exhausted. They had got lost in the dunes. The priest had seen to that.
183089:
There used to be a wood near the Brakke of Nieuwenhove. One day a four-year-old girl passed that wood with her parents. Suddenly three black figures appeared on the road, whereupon the mother said: "If you are sent by God, stay. If you are sent by the devil, vanish!" Only after the woman had said this three times did the figures vanish. Three little lights could be seen in the lime trees.
In the old days there was also a cellar at that spot where many dogs roamed and where the wind could be heard howling.
183137: In Leisele a woman always came to drink coffee with a family. One day that woman rubbed the belly of a pregnant girl. Later the girl's baby was stillborn. The girl's husband then went to that witch's husband to say that the woman must never again come into his house.
183138: A man who went to the field with his horses at six in the morning in summer suddenly saw a big black dog with eyes like lanterns standing beside him. The horses bolted in fear at the sight of the dog.
183144: At the Klokkeput there was always a cat that got under the feet of passers-by. When people kicked at that cat, they could never hit the animal and they lost their way.
183153: If a sick person somewhere was going to die, the little owl came calling: "Dead, dead, dead…"
183179: When a German shepherd hung his walking stick in a tree, he could draw wine from someone else's wine cellar. German shepherds could also make people full of lice.
183184: People often told of the maar (nightmare spirit) that came to ride someone.
183198: A man from Rozebeke came to the procession of Passendale in new clothes. On his way home the man had to pass the house of a witch. There was also a big pit there. At that spot the man got lost, so that he had to wander about until the next morning and his new clothes were completely dirty.
183203: Two men who were fishing at night decided to go home because the fish would not bite. One of the fishermen tried to step out of the boat but fell into the water. The other then said: "You fool, I'll get out first!" But he too fell into the water. On their way home the fishermen met a young lady at a farm, who said: "Do me a favour and you will both be happy. My fortune lies in that castle, but I need the key to get into it". The two fishermen followed the young lady through a long underground passage leading to a cellar where a chest stood. On the chest lay a dog with a key in its mouth. But the two fishermen did not dare take the key from the animal's mouth. When they got home the fishermen were soaking wet. After a while both fishermen were wasted away. Later one could still see the place where the castle had sunk.
183233: In Beselare a castle with a marquis is said to have once sunk into the ground. Near that spot the plants did not grow well and the cows would not eat the grass. Around 1912 people came from far and wide to look at that spot, because a screaming goat roamed there. In the end the fathers of Ieper were sent for.
183254: People whose blood had briefly stood still said afterwards that they had been ridden by the maar (nightmare spirit). A boy who was often ridden by the maar was freed of the affliction after he moved house.
183265: A man who was ridden by the maar (nightmare spirit) in his sleep felt as if he was being seized by something. The man dreamed of a mill and felt as if he was being whirled around by the sails. When you were ridden by the maar, you could not call out. To protect yourself against the maar, you had to put your clogs with the toes under the bed.
183267: In a Friars Minor monastery the brother porter had died. The brother porters had to receive people's money and record in a book how many masses had to be said. A few days after the brother's funeral there was so much noise at night that not a single friar could sleep. Because the noise could be heard every night, the superior of the brothers said: "Fathers, you may believe in ghosts or not, but I think that is the brother porter who comes to haunt. And if he comes to haunt, that is a sign that something is not right with his masses. We will say a few masses for our brother." Since then no strange noises have been heard at night.
183275: A girl worked in a café against her mother's wishes. Because the girl was determined to keep working in that café, her mother went to a witch. Although the girl had always got on well with her boss, one day she quarrelled with him and threw all the money in his face. The witch had brought this about.
183278:
A doctor who could heal with herbs and frogs was a keen collector of antiques. If he saw an old object at someone's house that he liked, he bought it at any price. The fee for his visit, however, was then in proportion to the price of the object.
One night, as the doctor was returning from visiting a patient, he met a robber with a horse and two dogs in Wijtschate, who shouted: "Your money or your life!" The doctor replied: "I have no money on me, but if you wait until tomorrow morning, I'll come and bring you money." The robber stood there all night and could no longer move. Some time later the doctor was murdered. No one ever found out who did it.
183305: In a house where a farmer's son had died young, one of the girls went upstairs. Because the girl saw a strange glow of light, she went back down in fright. When the girl curiously went upstairs again a while later, the light said: "You need not be afraid. There are still two francs in my coat hanging by the stairs. If you have a mass said with them, I will never return".
183320: By a man's house there was a death candle in an alder bush. It looked like a human heart. When the bush was dug up, a butter pot with a hundred francs was found. The money was given to the priest of Ardooie.
183326: The maar (nightmare spirit) was a kind of oppression that went away by itself after a while.
183329: A mother on pilgrimage to Oostakker with her child met a woman who wanted to box the child's ears. The mother pulled the child away, saying: "Not like that! Keep your hands off my child!" If one was touched by a witch, one always had to place one's hand higher to stay protected against evil.
183376: In church a witch had stolen the cat of the woman sitting next to her. When the robbed woman had put a medal under her chair, the witch could no longer harm her.
183379: A witch who was visiting somewhere took the child out of the cradle. Because of this the child began to cry without stopping. The parents threatened the witch, saying: "If you don't take away at once what you have put in that cradle, we will kill you." The witch then took a whole heap of pins out of the cradle.
183388: One night a man saw a sheep along the 'Veurenroute' (road to Veurne?). When the man looked back a moment later, the sheep had strangely enough already vanished.
183390: A farmer who always had a lot of bad luck on his farm because of witchcraft put paasnagels (Easter nails) under his door.
183393: On a farm worked a man who threshed the grain at night and had it ground at the mill. But when the farmer got up, there was nothing to be seen. One night the man made mice as big as moles, which crawled up the walls. Only one girl on the farm could see the mice.
183409: A woman whose husband had died slept upstairs while her husband's coffin stood downstairs. At night the woman heard a lot of noise. It was her husband wandering around the house.
183425: A man was walking along a road lined with alder bushes. When suddenly one of the bushes began to shake, the man shouted: "Don't think I'm scared, eh!" The man went to look, but saw no one. The tall grass had not even been trampled. A little further on the man again saw a shaking bush. That must have been the work of a witch.
183442: In a village lived a priest who was always out walking with his dog. People believed that the priest went haunting with his dog in the evening, since the clergyman had been seen in the evening in places far away from the village.
183446: Near the churchyard burning candles were seen walking among the graves.
183470: A girl from Blankenberge worked as a maid for rich people. The girl became pregnant by the son of the house and was so desperate that she hanged herself. Because she had committed suicide, the girl could not be buried in consecrated ground. On the day of the funeral people saw a gentleman dressed in black who asked where and when the funeral would take place. When the people saw that the gentleman had goat's legs, they quickly made the sign of the cross, whereupon the gentleman vanished.
183473: A woman had been given a young kitten by her sister. The woman carried the kitten in a black basket. On the way, however, the basket became so heavy that the woman had to rest for a while. When the woman opened the basket, she saw that the kitten had disappeared and that a stone lay in its place.
183502: People who were ridden by the maar (nightmare spirit) felt at night as if someone was grabbing them by the throat.
183513: On a haunted farm, one Monday evening, a man was seen walking around the house the whole time. When people went to look, they were knocked over by an invisible force.
183515: On a farm that had much misfortune, a toad was found under every wall of the cowshed. One evening, when the farmer's wife had gone to feed the animals and came back inside, she could no longer speak. The next moment the farmer's wife fell down dead.
183519: One evening a boy had to go and fetch bread somewhere because his mother had not baked enough. By the churchyard he saw a small spotted kitten sitting. Suddenly he received a blow that threw him to the side. Terrified, he ran back home.
183538:
A mother who had given birth to a little daughter went to be churched. When the mother came home, an old woman was standing at her door, asking how the child was. "Why do you need to know?" the mother replied, at which the little old woman walked away. A little later the baby began to cry. It cried for nine months, day and night.
The day after the mother had been churched, the same witch came in in the shape of a cat. The mother struck at the cat with a hot kettle. A day later the witch had burns on her face.
183555: In Beveren a man went to fetch a woman from the neighbourhood for a sick woman. The neighbour came along with the man and said: "Wouldn't you do better to go home? Your wife has had a baby." The man did not believe her, but when he got home, he found that his wife had given birth prematurely. That woman was a witch. She also kept a café. When a cart with a boomezel (a timber wagon) drove past her café, she made the chains break, so that the carter came in for a drink. The witch then mended the chains, so that the carter could go on again.
183556: Near the Sint-Ecarusbos in Houtkerke lived a witch who did harm to people and animals.
183562: A witch was visiting a woman who had a small child. The witch took the child out of the cradle, laid it on her lap and said to the mother: "But woman, your child is deathly ill!" The witch put the child back in the cradle and left. The next night the child died. People were convinced that the witch had caused it.
183574: In the old days, when people were out and about, they were often followed by red meerkatten (monkey-like cats). A man who did not believe such stories went with someone from Kleit to Maldegem through Pappoele. When the men were indeed surrounded by cats, they each took a thick branch and struck at the animals with it. The more they struck, the more cats appeared. To the nearest thousand, no one could say how many cats there were.
183576: A sorcerer was approached by a thief who took his horse and cart from him. The sorcerer then walked home and reported the theft to the police. The next day the thief was still standing in the same place; he could not move a foot. The sorcerer went and released him.
183581: A woman claimed that her house was haunted. At night the woman heard someone going about with a wheelbarrow and tapping on the window. When the woman looked outside, she saw seven small red dogs walking about. The woman's three sons all died within three months.
183584: A woman worked as a kitchen maid in a convent in Rijsel. In the evening noise was heard in that convent. The doors flew open, so that everyone became frightened. In the end it even went so far that the nuns and the staff all slept together in one hall out of fear. It was probably a ghost that caused these strange events.
183589: In a house in Oostduinkerke the furniture and firewood were thrown about at night. This was probably the work of a witch who lived nearby.
183611: When a doctor was travelling from Wijtschate to Voormezele, he was stopped at the Diependale past Sint-Elooi by a robber who forced him to hand over his money. The doctor answered: "My little man, I don't have enough money on me. But wait a minute until I come back!" The doctor went home and read something in a book. When he came back from the ten o'clock mass the next day, the robber was still standing in the same place. The robber had been bewitched so he was fixed to the ground.
183612: In the eighteenth century there was a wood in Kuurne called 'het toveressebusselke' (the little witch's wood). There had once been a marsh there. That place was terribly haunted and sometimes a hellish noise could be heard.
183617: A man who had gone to play cards came home at around nine in the evening. When he had been on his way for an hour, he heard someone shout: "I can't get away from here!" The man saw someone standing there, drenched in sweat because he was being ridden by the maar (nightmare spirit). The man took the poor fellow, who kept stumbling into the ditch, home.
183620: A man's mother-in-law had always said she would come back after her death. When the woman had died, the man and his family heard a noise in the attic every evening. Because the haunting did not stop, the people went to the parish priest. After they had prayed a great deal for the dead woman, nothing more was heard in the attic.
183637: When children fell ill because they had been born too early or had been given bad food, people said they had 'the old man', because a little woman had once come and hung over the cradle.
183641: A boy coming home from school was given a beautiful apple by an old woman. The boy eagerly ate the apple. Shortly afterwards the boy fell ill, and in the end he died.
183649: During the war a castle belonging to a rich noble family in Wijtschate was destroyed. After that the castle was haunted. Lights were seen there and music was heard.
183651: On a farm where some men were threshing, someone said it was possible to hang yourself with a straw. Because the others did not believe it, the man made a noose from a straw and put his head through it to show what he meant. Suddenly a hare ran around in the barn, distracting the onlookers, who struck at the animal with their flails. Meanwhile the man with his head in the noose had died. Later it was said that the hare had been the devil.
183678: A child had been bewitched by a woman who came peddling thread and ribbon. After the child had been overlezen (prayed over to lift a spell) in Zeebrugge, it was cured.
183715: Anyone who was ridden by the maar (nightmare spirit) could not call out and felt as if someone was grabbing him by the throat. As soon as someone called the victim's name, the maar was gone. Some people claimed that the maar was a standstill of the blood.
183731: Strange things happened on a haunted farm. When people tried to put the horses' harness on, it fell to the ground. When people came into the cellar, the plates fell over without breaking.
183757: A boy who had gone weaving in Stacegem came home at midnight with his little dog. When the boy passed the house where a farmer had died, the little dog ran off in fright. People said that the dead farmer was coming back.
183762: On the day a man died, a little light was seen in the churchyard that evening, moving up and down the whole time. The light was seen for nine days. It was the soul of the dead man, asking for prayers because he had not yet found rest.
183791: A man coming back from work one evening met a cat in Sint-Baafs-Vijve and said to the animal: "Pussy, pussy, dear, will you come with me?" The next moment the man was surrounded by a whole troop of cats. As soon as the frightened man had made the sign of the cross, the animals vanished.
183792:
A man had bought two piglets. One day a woman came and stood by the piglets and said: "You have fine pigs!" Not an hour later the pigs all fell ill. The woman had bewitched the animals with her books.
A witch had also once made the hens come out of their coop at two in the morning and start walking around.
183794: A woman and her husband were often ridden by the maar (nightmare spirit) at night. The woman never went to sleep before she had put her slippers next to her bed with the toes pointing outward. Anyone who was ridden by the maar was powerless and could not breathe. To find out where the maar was, you had to roll a bread knife in a towel and wrap that towel around yourself. Then you had to say where you thought the maar was at that moment. If you were right, the bread knife would be exposed and you would be freed from the maar.
183801:
A woman who was ridden by the mare felt as if something heavy was sitting on her, trying to strangle her. The woman tried to scream and call out, but could not.
In reality the mare was a stoppage of the blood.
One day the woman called out to her daughter in her sleep: "You grab it by the head, I have it by the tail!" The daughter did not know what her mother was talking about. A little later she learned that her mother had been ridden by the mare. The mother explained that the mare was a wicked woman who wanted to play a trick on her. If she were ridden by the mare again in the future, her daughter was to pour water over her.
183836: A witch lived in Sint-Denijs. In the places where this witch went walking in the evening, a child died of 'de plane' (1). The child had a black cross on its back. If the witch visited a child that was seven days old, the child died on the ninth day.
183839: A woman who had worked as a farmer's wife for a while sold a milk tub to a farmer's wife from the neighbourhood. The farmer's wife who bought the tub had to promise, however, that she would never wash it out with boiling water and stove ash. When the farmer's wife did so one day anyway, a loud bang was heard.
183857: The nekker was a dog with a chain around its neck. A man who was out alone was accompanied by such a dog, which kept growing bigger and bigger. When the man had walked past the hospital, the dog had disappeared. For nekkers could not pass a place where holy water was present.
183860: A widower with three children always went peddling and then passed the churchyard. On three consecutive days the man felt that he could hardly get past the churchyard. The priest then said to the man: "Go back tomorrow. You must say: 'If you are sent by God, who are you?'" When the man had done so, his dead wife stood before him. The woman asked her husband to light half a pound of candles because she had once promised that.
183876: When one was ridden by the mare, one felt the tormenting spirit arrive at one's feet. One then wanted to call out, but could not make a sound. If one put one's shoes under the bed with the toes pointing in, one was safe from the mare.
183891: A pigeon always sat by a culvert. It was a sorceress who had turned herself into an animal. Whenever someone drove a coach past the culvert, the coach ended up in the water.
183893: A nine-year-old girl from Avelgem was with her father at the celebration for the building of the bridge to Ruien. Her father, who was standing on the hemelwagen (a festive float) and had run out of tobacco, sent his daughter to the shop in Avelgem. On the way, at a bend, the girl met a tall woman dressed in black with black hair, who asked the girl whether she still had far to walk and said: "You're pretty, your hair is so nicely curled!" A man from a nearby house took the child by the hand and said: "Girl, you mustn't talk to that woman." That afternoon the girl became very ill. The mother drove with the girl to a healer in Sint-Louis. On the road from Ijvegem to Tervichten the girl normally always slept. This time, however, the child was awake and cried: "They're coming! They're coming!" But the mother and the stable hand saw nothing. A little later a woman appeared, took hold of the horse's muzzle and asked: "Is the girl asleep?" The stable hand lashed at the witch with his whip, but she had already vanished. The cart overturned and landed in the ditch. The healer knew the people had had trouble on the way, and he said: "You must come back in nine days and then the girl will be cured." And so it was.
183920: A boy had been bewitched by a woman who lived near him. Because of this the child suffered from 'de plane' (1). The boy's mother sought advice from the friars of Roeselare. After that her son was never ill again.
183921: If the fishermen met a black cat as they went on board, they would have bad luck.
183939: A man was coming back from the fair with a girl. At the little chapel of Roksem an old little woman came out of the rye field. That little woman sold brushes for cleaning pots. The little woman walked past and disappeared into the field again on the other side. Because it was said that the little woman could do witchcraft, the man reached for his knife. But he could not get his hand into his trouser pocket, and he did not get home until the next morning.
183943:
In Wijtschate there was a haunted place. At Diependale, a hill leading to a wood, a headless horse always roamed. In the end hardly anyone dared to walk past that spot.
Despite his mother's warnings, a brave farmer's son walked past Diependale every day. When one evening he came from Wijtschate towards Hollebeke, he heard a noise and was flung to the ground. The man scrambled up and ran straight home. Out of breath he said to his mother: "I have seen the headless horse! I'm never going there again!"
183945: One morning a man went to a funeral in Ieper. On the way, at the toveresseknok (witches' hill) in Rumbeke, he was surrounded by cats. There were so many cats that the man could not go on and was forced to return home.
183956: If fishermen met a woman on the way to the sea, they would have bad luck; their nets would tear or a storm would endanger their lives.
183965: Witches could give children the evil hand. Children who were bewitched had to be overlezen (prayed over to lift a spell) by the parish priest.
184006: During the mission a man wanted to go and hear the fathers' sermon. On the way the man met a dog that blocked his path. A little later a woman was standing on the dyke, having appeared out of nowhere.
184021: In the past people would not allow an old woman to come and look at their child, because bewitchment was common.
184032:
An old shrimp fisherman from Nieuwpoort Bad went into the sea with his dragnet and his horse. In Oostduinkerke the shrimp fisherman met two French-speaking fishermen from Bredene, who claimed they had seen the 'eeuwige kruwer' (eternal shrimp-net pusher).
Once a man had gone into the sea at Easter to catch some shrimp. His mother had said: "Aren't you ashamed to do that at Easter! It is enough to bring a curse upon you." To which the man had replied: "If I am cursed for this, then I want to drag my net along the sea here forever." The man never came back.
When a fisherman drowned in the sea, people said it was because of the eternal shrimp-net pusher. Whoever saw the eternal shrimp-net pusher seemed bewitched and went deeper and deeper into the water. Luckily the two fishermen from Bredene had a blessed palm sprig with them, otherwise they too would have drowned on seeing the eternal shrimp-net pusher.
184052: A sick woman was visited almost every day by a neighbour. One day the sick woman found that she had lost her ring. Because her husband found the whole matter rather strange, he went to a healer in Waregem. The healer advised the man not to let the neighbour in any more. When the neighbour wanted to visit the next day, the man slammed the door. The neighbour then threw something away that looked like a black egg. At the spot where that egg fell, the lost ring was found.
184058: One day a statue of Mary was found in the Bruggestraat in Poperinge. It was taken to the Sint-Bertinuskerk, but the next day it was lying in the Bruggestraat again. Then the statue was taken to the Onze-Lieve-Vrouwekerk. Because it was afterwards found in the Bruggestraat once more, it was taken to the Sint-Janskerk.
184061: In a house in French Flanders a knocking was heard every day before mass. When the dean and the bishop were there one day, they decided to say a mass. After that the knocking was heard no more. It was a priest who had received money for a mass he had never said.
184069: In the old days a little pig roamed about in Eentveld, sometimes seen every evening. A woman sitting working at the window one evening suddenly saw the little pig leaning with its forelegs on the windowsill. The woman started screaming in fear. Her neighbour, who had heard the screaming, shot at the little pig with his gun. But the next day there was no trace of the little pig. Two days later the little pig was there again. Three, four or five people tried to catch the little pig, but they did not succeed. That little pig roamed that neighbourhood for a good ten or twenty years. No one knows how the animal finally disappeared.
184071: Between Vlamertinge and Ieper there was a bottomless pit. Around midnight the rattling of cartwheels and chains was always heard in that pit, although there was nothing to be seen.
184072: A man fell victim to the tricks of a witch to whom he would not sell fish. The man was forced to keep driving in circles around the witch's house until he was drenched in sweat. The horses were tired too and were foaming at the mouth.
184079: A hunchback who worked as a tailor had died of an illness. One day a man was cutting grass near the hunchback's house. Suddenly the man saw under the eaves of the house a little light that flew in through the keyhole and a moment later flew out the same way. That had been the hunchback's spirit.
184087: Near the abbey of Zevenkerke, a sorceress appeared in the shape of a black spider whenever a child died somewhere.
184089: At 'de Doolaeghe' there stood a house that was haunted because a whole family had once died there of an unknown disease.
184107: In the Velthoek many returned dead appeared in a tree.
184116: The French village of Soekote sank into the sea in France. Fishing nets always got caught on something under the water there.
184139: Witches could make a plague pass from one house to another. Sometimes it happened that they could no longer get rid of the plague themselves. So a witch from Vlamertinge was struggling with a plague of rats. Because she could not get rid of the rats, she had to hang the food cupboards from the ceiling. Even that did not help, though, for the rats still climbed up into the cupboards. In the end the witch had to move, or she would have starved to death.
184148: A woman from Veurne went to Adinkerke to learn sewing. When the woman came home, she always saw a white apparition standing there.
184154: On a farm noises were heard at night. A herd of horses came in through one door and went out again through another door.
184165: A woman who was raising an orphan always hid the child whenever a witch from the village came to visit. For when this witch had been near a child, the child cried until it died. The witch had already caused three or four children to die this way.
184173: A woman had bewitched a farmer's cows, so that the animals no longer gave a drop of milk.
184181: Some boys on a hike in Vlissingen asked a farmer for some drinking water. The farmer drew water from the well and let the boys drink from a bowl. The last boy to drink smashed the bowl, and the boys ran off laughing. The farmer was very angry and said: "He who laughs last, laughs best!" Although the boys knew the area well, they got lost. All the time they heard the farmer's voice saying: "He who laughs last, laughs best!" When it was almost midnight, they heard the farmer's voice call: "Have you laughed enough now? Go on home!" The next moment the boys could find their way without any trouble.
184210: People who had not died with a clear conscience returned after their death.
184220: A German shepherd playing his flute had the rats of Hamelin follow him.
184225: Some people going out to weed met a woman who said: "You won't be weeding now!" When the people reached the field, they saw that it was covered in walnuts, so that indeed no weeding could be done.
184263: When the cows on a farm stopped giving milk, people often believed that the animals had been bewitched by a woman who regularly came to fetch milk. This had happened, for example, on a farm in Beselare. In reality the cows no longer gave milk because they had the 'blue disease' (?).
184265: A man returning from the inn one Sunday evening saw a big sack lying on the ground near the 'Vogelare meersen'. Although the sack moved back and forth, the man saw no head or feet. "Move aside", the man shouted, whereupon the sack promptly moved to the side of the road. The man was so frightened that he was home in less than ten minutes. When the man talked with a friend some time later about what had happened to him, the friend said that he too had once seen that sack.
184266: Whoever was ridden by the mare felt as if a thousand kilos were pressing on their heart and legs. Victims of the mare could not call out and felt short of breath. To free oneself from the mare, one had to turn over so that the mare would fall to the floor.
184274: The Helleput in Tiegem used to be haunted. A man who was afraid of nothing had bet a bottle of jenever that he dared to walk past the Helleput. The man, however, never came back. The next day only his cap and his clogs were found.
184287: At the Motje in Roeselare a castle had sunk into the ground. The lord of the castle had always led a sinful life. At night, two black dogs with glittering green eyes roamed the place where the castle had stood.
184293: Whoever was ridden by the mare at night could no longer move.
184303: A man who went out in the evenings with horse and cart often saw a doodkeers (death candle) along the way. The man lashed at it with his whip but could not hit it. The light kept dancing back and forth. It was said that doodkeersen were the souls of returned dead.
184313: In a house a cat crept in every evening through the drain hole for the water. One evening boiling water was poured over the animal. The next day the neighbour was burned all over.
184325: In the beech lane at the Zwaantjeshoek opposite the churchyard there always appeared a white lady who made poison for people and animals. That is why that place was also called 'de Vergifhoek' (the Poison Corner).
184329: A man went to the churchyard of Merkem to call his wife. While the man stood there, he saw a large skeleton coming towards him. The man told some others what had happened. Then the man went back to the churchyard with two friends. The skeleton vanished in the blink of an eye.
184331: Two hermits lived on the Hoge in Kachtem. A fire burned in their attic every night. When one of the hermits went to mass at half past five on Sunday morning, he had to carry the ghost of a farmer's wife who had died long ago. The moment the hermit reached the Kachtem bridge, the ghost disappeared.
184334: Lights that returned were called doodkaarsen (death candles). Near a man's house, lights also appeared every evening. People believed something was buried in that spot.
184351: A woman from Zullebeke returned after her death because she had promised to go and serve at a little chapel. After the widower had gone to serve for his late wife, the ghost flew upwards.
184367: A house in Rugge was haunted every night. The butter churn could be heard turning and the calves stood lowing in the stable. Whenever someone in soldier's clothes stayed on the farm, it remained quiet at night.
184373: A man was always drenched in sweat when he walked through the woods to work. For in the woods he always saw a gentleman walking, who kept pace with him.
184374: A seamstress went to wind yarn onto a spool at a farmer's. The farmer thought it strange that his son went out every evening. The farmer's son went about as a werewolf with a devil's skin that he had hidden in a tree stump. When the seamstress had left that evening, the farmer heard a noise near the brook. The seamstress was stalked by a figure and threw her bobbin of yarn on the ground. The next day the farmer's son had bits of yarn between his teeth.
184393: The dead came back in the shape of a black cat that wandered about at night.
184408: A fisherman going to Nieuwpoort met a witch who said: "You shouldn't go to sea, for you might lose your net." The fisherman went anyway and lost his net. Whenever a farmer drove past the witch's house with a cart of fruit, the cart tipped over.
184418:
A woman went to spend the night at her neighbour's because the neighbour's husband was in hospital in Ieper for a prostate operation. In the night the woman suddenly heard a strange noise that stopped as soon as the moon appeared. When the woman set off for the hospital the next day, she heard the noise again. A little later she learned that the man had died.
The neighbour, now a widow, no longer wanted to visit the woman. She had seen her scapular when she came to stay the night. A year after this incident the woman suddenly heard such a strange noise again. It was so bad that the wallpaper fell off the walls. For six weeks in a row the woman went to the friars of Ieper. At the end of those six weeks she received a letter in which her neighbour asked for forgiveness.
184442: A woman who was ridden by the mare began to sweat and could no longer breathe. When that woman called out, no one could hear her. The mare was a man who came in sighing through the water drain and some time later went out again sighing.
184445: A farm in Assebroek was haunted. At night a little light was often seen moving back and forth along the wall. When the farmer grabbed at the light, it suddenly vanished. One night the farmer and his wife heard knocking on the door. When it knocked for the third time, they said: "If you are sent by God, come in. If you are sent by the devil, go away." After that there was never any knocking on the door again.
184450: On a farm all the wooden shutters flew open and shut, although nobody could be seen. After the friars had been called in, the haunting came to an end.
184462: At the Reutelhoek in Beselare lived a woman who owned books of magic. One day this woman made it so that butter could no longer be churned on a farm.
184469: In Oeselgem an old woman was heating butter on the fire. Because a cat always came and sat in the corner of the hearth, the woman threw the hot butter over the animal. The next day a little child in a cradle was burned all over.
184476: A farmer who was ploughing suddenly could not go on. His farmhand had bewitched the plough and the horse so they were stuck.
184484: In Oostkapelle a witch had died. When the witch's body was being carried in a covered wagon, the horses would go no further. The parish priest had the wagon turned around so that the body lay head first. After that the horses could go on again.
184486: A rich childless woman wanted to buy the child of a mother from Sint-Kruis. Because the mother refused, the witch sent a dog to the child's cradle. Only the child's little brother could see that dog. When the child was overlezen (prayed over to lift a spell) by a friar from Steenbrugge, the clergyman was drenched in sweat.
184487: There used to be a beech tree at a crossroads in Veldegem. A man claimed that he had been seized by a ghost at that tree.
184524: Some people were ridden by the mare when they slept on their backs. They felt as if their throat was being squeezed shut.
184577: A woman who liked to drink had a husband who, before his death, had asked her to have a Mass said. The woman had agreed, but she had not kept her promise. Every night a mouse came to lie next to the woman in bed. In the end the woman decided to remarry. When she had remarried, the mouse crept into bed between her and her new husband. The new husband was annoyed by the mouse and asked his wife whether she had ever promised anything. The woman answered: "Yes, when my husband died I promised him a Mass, but I did not keep my promise because I liked drinking so much." The new husband gave his wife money to have a Mass said. While the priest was saying the Mass, a bright light appeared above the house. The mouse disappeared and never came back.
184580:
In Hooglede lived a small woman who came from Lichtervelde. A woman coming back from church was worried because her baby cried all the time. The grandmother went to fetch the midwife so she could examine the child. A tree was pictured on the child's body. The child's mother had one day mocked the little woman from Lichtervelde. The little woman had then said: "I'll know where to find you!" The grandmother took the child to the friars of Roeselare. When the grandmother came to the tram stop at 't Meiboomtje', she saw that the little woman from Lichtervelde also got on the tram. When the grandmother got off at the 'Saumon' stop, the little woman got off too and then disappeared into the crowd. The grandmother reached the friars' church and saw the little woman from Lichtervelde standing there. The grandmother then decided to go to the monastery instead of the friars' church. After the grandmother had told everything to the superior of the monastery, he said: "You won't see the little woman when you come out." And so it was.
Everyone called that little woman 'the witch'.
184588: A man had a pipe in his mouth. Suddenly the pipe fell to the ground. But the man could not find his pipe again. This trick was probably the work of a witch.
184596: In a house, at night, people always heard a great deal of noise, as if the porcelain figures and plates were being thrown off the mantelpiece. But when they got up in the morning, nothing was broken.
184647: Witches could not die. At a butcher's, a witch disappeared through a closed door. The witch's clothes were still hanging on the door.
184649: On a haunted farm between Zonnebeke and Ieper the cows were wild and skittish. The animals also gave hardly any milk anymore. One night the farmhand felt a cold hand on his face. At that, the man ran away terrified. The occupants of the farm eventually moved out for fear of the haunting. Someone else then went to live there.
184660: People who came back after their death had stolen something during their lifetime and came to return it out of remorse.
184678:
In the Hellebos there used to be a café where there was a lot of dancing. One day the devil appeared in that café. When the devil danced with the landlady, the woman suddenly vanished. Even the whole café was gone.
At the spot where the café had stood, a little black dog was always seen dancing afterwards. That place was called 'de Doodlage'.
184682:
During the First World War a man went to his mother's to castrate piglets. While the man was eating, a piece of ham lying on a flat dish suddenly disappeared for no apparent reason. There was also a bucket of porridge. A coat hung on the rim of the bucket, even though the bucket was closed with a lid. In the attic all the socks were lying on the bed and the umbrella stood open above the bed. In the trousers hanging in the wardrobe there was a square-shaped hole.
When the mother baked pancakes in the afternoon, the pancakes always jumped away as soon as she reached for them.
The haunting was probably caused by someone who read bad books.
184694: On a road in Steenkerke a cat roamed about that blocked passers-by. Whoever took it into his head to strike at that cat was attacked himself.
184717: A woman had seen a little man walk around the church three times and then disappear. The priest claimed that the little man was a returned dead person who still had to fulfil a vow. The woman should have asked what the little man wanted.
184745: A witch's daughter wanted to marry or enter a convent, but her mother would not allow it. The mother said to her daughter: "I'll make sure you can't." The daughter was unhappy and got crooked hands.
184761: A woman walking home on a Sunday night saw a goat at a little bridge. The animal jumped with its legs onto the woman's shoulders and pushed her into the water.
184764: A tree in the wood of Wijnendale was haunted. A little woman in a hooded cloak was often seen walking about there, and sometimes a candle could be seen moving up and down.
184772: A poacher out hunting in winter saw a hare running that was almost as big as a dog. The man shot at the animal, but when he went to fetch his catch, the hare jumped up and ran away. The same thing happened a second time with another hare. When the man had shot at a hare for the third time, that animal said: "Have the other two been gone long?" The man was beside himself with fear.
184794:
A doctor who had studied for the priesthood before his medical studies was very learned. The man was always dressed like a poor tramp.
One night in Wijtschate the doctor met two robbers, who asked him for his money. The doctor bewitched the robbers so they were fixed to the ground and could not move on.
One day the doctor was murdered.
184799: At a castle where rich people had once lived, white ladies always walked around in the garden at night. People believed they were the returned spirits of the castle's residents.
184801: A farm in Hertsberge was haunted. People always heard a voice in the hedge saying: "Trezeke is sitting here". A white hand was also seen at the window.
184805: A family in Meulebeke could no longer sleep at night because they were bitten by rats. Strangely enough, no rats were to be seen during the day. A friar attributed the plague to the influence of a witch. The friar took out his prayer book and told the lady of the house to open all the windows. When the friar began to pray, all the rats jumped out of the window into the brook.
184841: People who were ridden by the mare thought they saw all sorts of things and could not make a sound, but in reality they had a stoppage of the blood. To protect oneself against the mare, one had to put one's clogs upside down under the bed.
184846: A hunchback who worked as a tailor had died of an illness. One day a man was cutting grass near the hunchback's house. Suddenly the man saw under the eaves of the house a little light that flew in through the keyhole and a moment later flew out the same way. That had been the spirit of the hunchback, who had not yet been buried.
184848: If the waternekker (water sprite) was heard screaming in the distance, someone would soon die.
184849: When people saw the glowing eyes of a cat in the dark, they often believed a witch was standing before them.
184855: A farmer's daughter, against her mother's wishes, married a different man from the one she was originally to marry. During a horse fair in Tielt the farmer died suddenly. The farmer's wife disinherited her daughter for choosing another marriage partner. After that, people coming from Kortrijk saw the dead farmer appear along the Leie. He came to haunt because his wife had disinherited his daughter.
184866: A sorcerer quarrelled with a woman who ran a café and got a slap round the ear from her. At that the sorcerer said: "You'll be sorry for that!" The next moment the café was full of rats, so that the landlady had to beg the sorcerer to make the animals disappear again.
184871: On a farm butter could no longer be made and the cows did not even give milk any more. One day the farmer's wife went somewhere together with a woman from the village. At a certain moment this woman said to the farmer's wife: "Your goat has had kids." That indeed turned out to be so. After that the farmer's wife could milk the goat. Strangely enough, when the woman from the village was not nearby, the animals gave no milk.
184873: A farmer's wife was annoyed by a strange cat that came and sat at the door every day. One day she could no longer control herself and poured hot butter over the animal's snout. When she went to the shop the next day, she met a woman whose face was burned all over.
184877: In Damme there was a child who suffered from the 'old man' (an illness) and therefore became skin and bone and stopped growing. After an old woman had been near the child, the child had been struck by the evil hand. The parents had to go to the parish priest to have the child overlezen (prayed over to lift a spell).
184903:
One morning three cows lay dead on a farm in Warlops. The day before, a witch had come to visit.
After the friars of Ieper had walked around the farm a few times, the spell was broken.
184908: On a farm in Sint-Eloois-Winkel worked a German shepherd who flew home on a goat every month to fetch clean clothes. One day, after much nagging, the horse groom was allowed to go along with the shepherd. On the way the groom bumped into the church tower because they were flying too low. In Germany the groom was not allowed to go anywhere. The next day the shepherd and the groom were back on the farm.
184909: A mother who had been living in Aartrijke for only two weeks was visited by a neighbour while she was breastfeeding her child. "That's a lovely child! May I see it?" said the neighbour. The mother replied: "That is my child! Get out of here!" It was said of that neighbour that she was a witch.
184912: A man claimed he dared to dance with a witch. Whenever the witch struck the man on the shoulder, the man always struck higher. During the dance, however, the witch had struck the man on the head. The next day the man had lost all his hair.
184931: On a farm a foal was born with a crooked neck. The animal grew up lopsided and never became a proper horse. The mare that had borne the foal had been bewitched by the maid who worked on the farm.
184955: In Ghyvelde lived a witch who owned a little black book with which she did people harm. One day the parish priest took the book away from her.
184956: A man walking home one night suddenly saw a black cat appear between Lokeren and Belle. That cat only disappeared when the man had reached his house.
184962: Some people on their way to mass suddenly saw a hen rolling across the road. The people tried several times to kick the hen, but they never managed to hit the animal.
184970: There used to be a large wood near the castle of the Duc d'Arenberg. In that wood was a clearing with a hill behind it. A man returning from a visit to his girlfriend was followed between midnight and one o'clock by the Motewijvetje. The apparition kept overtaking the man and then letting him walk in front again. The man saw only a hooded cloak, without hands or feet. The man asked what the apparition wanted, but there was no answer.
184978: Two women who were out one rainy evening saw a woman from the village approaching in the distance. As the woman came closer, however, she changed into a priest. That woman could work magic.
184981: When the priest had forgotten to close his missal, six women stayed sitting in the church. They went as far as the door, but then turned back because they could not get outside. The maid saw it and went to tell the priest what was going on. The clergyman then said: "Oh dear, I forgot to close my book".
184994: In the Liembaarstraatje (?) lived a shoemaker whose wife had a hunchback. A few days after the funeral of the hunchbacked woman, X, the little woman who lived above the shoemaker, heard a hellish noise at night and heard the shoemaker calling for help. The next day the shoemaker said to X: "My wife appeared last night and dragged me through the room." Because X was very frightened, she asked her daughter to stay with her the following night. On the stroke of twelve, X and her daughter heard the noise again the next night. When the noise had been heard for three nights, X said to the shoemaker: "You must go to the priest!" The priest asked the shoemaker whether he had ever promised his wife anything, but the man remembered nothing. The priest advised the shoemaker to go on a pilgrimage to the little chapel of Brènienge (Bredene?).
