At the green dike the shoemaker should have said: "Go ahead, I will follow you," but he said: "In God's name, we are off." The next moment the shoemaker felt on his shoulders the weight of his wife, whom he was carrying. When the shoemaker reached the little chapel, he was dead tired and drenched in sweat. After the shoemaker had said his prayers, the burden fell from his shoulders. After that the hunchbacked woman came to haunt no more.
185017: In Werken lived a woman everyone was afraid of, for people believed she could work magic. When a child was born in the family that rented a house to the witch, the witch was evicted by a bailiff. The farmer the witch worked for then built a little house for her, for that farmer did not believe the talk going around about the woman.
185028: To unmask the mare, one had to pour a bucket of water over oneself while being ridden by the mare. That would make the mare visible.
185030: If magpies were heard chattering at night in winter, an accident would happen to the people or the animals.
185032: A woman from Rijssel who thought her house was bewitched sought advice from a clergyman, who gave her a little bag of pieces of blessed candles to put above the doors. The woman suspected a neighbour who regularly came to visit. So the woman also put a piece of candle under the chair where that neighbour usually sat. When the neighbour next came by, she remained standing the whole time. On the wall hung a swallow that the woman had been given by that neighbour. The woman wanted to put a piece of candle behind the swallow as well, but when she did, the swallow fell to the floor and broke. One evening the woman was sitting by the stove with her dog at her feet. Suddenly a big flame shot out of the stove and burned up the woman's apron entirely. The woman beat out the fire with her hand, which strangely enough was not burned. After the clergyman had come to bless the house, the woman noticed nothing strange any more.
185042: One Saturday a pregnant woman was visited by a witch, who touched her and said: "You are yet one of three times seven." When the woman's child was born, its hair looked like wool. Moreover, the child did nothing but cry. The parish priest predicted that the child would recover. He gave the child two blessed rolls and advised the mother to put a piece of the Easter candle under the threshold. Then the witch could no longer get in. The child soon recovered.
185043: A farmer going to the meadow with his horses in the evening saw a black cat running between his legs. When the man reached the presbytery, the animal had suddenly vanished.
185044: If the priest forgot to close his missal after reading the Gospel of Saint John, no witch could leave the church.
185057:
A farm in Leke was haunted. At night the stable doors flew open and a strange noise was heard. The animals ran out of the stable in fear.
When the farm had been exorcised by the Witheren (White Fathers) of Oostende, the strange events came to an end.
185063: A child coming home from school could no longer walk. When the father carried the child, it seemed as if the child weighed a thousand kilos. The parish priest sent the child to the priest of another village. The child could no longer speak and its thumbs grew into its little hands. In the end the child died.
185074: A man coming back from Esen saw seven hares and seven greyhounds running in a large meadow. When the man began to pray the Gospel of Saint John, the animals suddenly vanished.
185103: In a house in Zevekote a woman had poured boiling water on a cat. The next day a woman from the village was burned all over.
185113: Just after the First World War many English people came to Poperinge to visit the military cemeteries. One day a mother was visited by an English woman. The woman stroked the mother's child on the cheek and said: "What a lovely child!" After that the child would not grow any more. In the end it died.
185115: A man returning from the horse market in Brugge suddenly saw a headless horse flying through the air. That was the fault of a woman the man knew.
185131: A woman from Moere met someone on the way to her house. After that the woman got lost.
185150: One night at twelve o'clock a man saw horses with chains and bells running on the other side of the canal. The animals belonged to no one. Fire came from their horseshoes.
185168: In the Onzeheertjesbos someone found a statue of Christ. The man took it home and put it on the mantelpiece. The next morning the man found that the statue had disappeared. It was lying in the wood again where he had found it. When the same thing happened once more, it was decided to build a chapel in the wood on the spot where the statue had been found.
185176: One night a man from Koolskamp went with two cows to fetch coal at the canal of Boendale. When the man was in Waardamme, his farmhand said: "This is the parish of the witches." The next moment a woman threw open her window and shouted: "I don't know why you want to talk about that, especially since there are even more in your parish!" From this the man and the farmhand concluded that they had heard the opinion of a woman who was herself a witch. Fortunately the witch had done them no harm.
185183: When it rained heavily on the day of the procession, it was decided not to carry the statue of Mary along, because people did not want it to get dirty. At the brook, the people in the procession saw the statue standing there.
185210: A woman went with her sister to the little chapel of Bredene. On the way the woman felt a heavy weight pressing on her shoulders. Then the mother said: "Would you believe that father has drowned?" Later it turned out that the man had indeed drowned in the North Sea.
185225: A man returning from the fair in Snellegem saw a headless man standing by a little chapel. The man was followed by that strange apparition.
185230: A farmhand was taking a lord of the manor home in the horse cart. When a heavy thunderstorm broke out on the way, the farmhand said to the lord: "God willing, we will get home all right." The lord replied: "God willing or not, we must get there!" A little later two dogs came running up and bit through the horses' ropes. The coach sank into the ground and the farmhand was saved.
185233: A boy whose mother had just died slept with his father. The coffin stood in the bedroom. At night father and son suddenly heard sounds coming from the coffin. They turned on the light, but there was nothing to be seen.
185279: Some men were busy in the woods digging out tree roots. The woman who was to bring the men food around twelve o'clock did not arrive until two. The woman had lost her way because of the mare.
185291: A man who had been to the café met a little dog on his way home. The man called to the animal and came closer. The closer the man came to the dog, the bigger the animal grew. When the animal had become as big as a donkey, the man fled. The man ran quickly to his house in the Lijnbaadstraatje while an animal as big as a horse chased after him. Once home, the man quickly slammed the door shut. The next moment the big dog stuck its head through the drain hole and made a horrible noise.
185294: A woman who was ridden by the mare felt as if her blood was standing still and as if a heavy weight was resting on her.
185312: A woman on pilgrimage at the little chapel of Alveringem saw a cackling hen in the grass that blocked her way. Only when the woman began to pray with clenched fists could she get away. Herrings lay everywhere in the streets, and a pot of butter and lard stood in front of someone's door. The priest said he would name the witch if she did not stop her tricks. A while later the priest died. The witch had more power than he did.
185315: In Wingene there lived a farmer who could not make butter. The priests advised the farmer to put an oak branch in the churn. When the farmer had done so and began to churn, he heard a hellish noise. It was the sorceress, who was sitting in the churn and was being beaten. After that the farmer could make butter again.
185318: A woman who had walked past an inn three times was accused of witchcraft because people believed the innkeeper's wife had been bewitched. A schoolmaster seized the supposed witch and tried to throw her into the fire. Because the poor woman screamed so loudly for help, someone was able to rescue her. The innkeeper's wife was pregnant and some time later had to leave the village to give birth in peace. People said that the schoolmaster spent more time with the innkeeper's wife than in his school. When the case came to court, the innkeeper's wife was punished.
185320: A man working at night suddenly heard chains rattling in the street. A little later the man saw a black dog standing by the oven. When the man had taken the glowing poker from the fire to strike the dog, the animal had strangely vanished. The man was convinced he had seen the nekker (a malicious water spirit).
185323: On a farm in Veurne worked a farmhand who had been to Diksmuide with a circus. One of the circus performers had given him a book of magic. When the other farmhands were complaining because the maid had not changed their beds, the farmhand with the book of magic said: "Just wait, tomorrow you'll see the blankets hanging outside!" Two days later the maid's blankets were hanging outside on the washing line. The blankets were full of lice. One day the maid had made pancakes for the horse hands. The other farmhands and the maids had not eaten any pancakes. At that the farmhand with the book of magic said: "We'll have some tonight too." When the farmhands and the maids were eating sandwiches in their room that evening, the plate of pancakes suddenly stood before them.
185330: A sorcerer who was dismissed by a farmer said: "Your house will be full of rats!" The sorcerer had not been gone three days before the farm was indeed full of rats. The farmer went to ask the sorcerer to drive the rats away. The sorcerer agreed, on condition that he could come back to work on the farm. Then the sorcerer made all the rats run out through the gate.
185340: The mare carried sleeping people around and then threw them down somewhere.
185358: In Beselare lived a crippled woman who knew many prayers. Whenever it began to thunder, the woman went outside and said: "As far as you can hear me from here, the lightning will not strike." Indeed, lightning never struck in that place.
185374: In Sint-Kruis there used to be many ghosts walking about in white sheets. When people came closer, the ghosts disappeared into the ditch.
185407: A shepherd walking home saw a beautiful woman dancing around him the whole time on a stretch of grass. The woman came with him as far as the threshold of the house where the man lived. There the witch suddenly vanished.
185424: People who were ridden by the mare at night were seized by the throat and could not breathe until they woke up.
185431: A woman from Houtem gave her cats a kiss in the morning and then chased the animals outside. In the evening the cats came back in, but during the day they were never seen.
185445: The fishermen of Blankenberge believed that pointing brought bad luck.
185446: In Anzegem stood seven oaks between which white shades could be seen appearing at harvest time. A man walking home past that spot one evening was chased by the shades. At that, the man ran home as fast as he could.
185451: A man coming home from his work in Belle on Saturdays around eight o'clock always saw a white woman in the Leenvollebos. Every week the figure was a little smaller, until in the end she was no bigger than a child.
185482: A farmer's wife had a maid who possessed strange powers. When the maid churned butter, instead of saying "A lump like my fist" she always said "A lump like my backside." When the farmer's wife heard this, she said: "You mustn't say that, because we will get all the butter of the people in the village. The others won't be able to make butter any more."
185486: In the Onsheertjesbos people were allowed to fell the old trees. Two men found a statue of Christ there. The statue was taken to the Sint-Bertinuskerk, but the next day it was lying in the wood again. After the statue had returned to the wood three times, it was decided to build a chapel on that spot. Later many people came on pilgrimage to that little chapel against fever, whooping cough, convulsions and so on.
185487: A boy who went to fetch eel in Brugge saw a very large pig standing on the road by the watermill, which made his horses bolt.
185503: A man saw a meerkat (a monkey-like creature) come out of an alder hedge. The animal had a beautiful, colourful plumed tail. The meerkat did the man no harm. Sometimes, however, meerkats leapt on people, bit them and cursed them. They were sorceresses.
185512: The son of a witch made little mice run around the school playground. The boy could also make the mice disappear again. The schoolmaster called the boy inside and asked who had taught him those tricks. "My mother," the boy answered. The next day the schoolmaster had the priest come to the school. The priest asked the boy whether he could make the mice run to the drain. Then the clergyman stood by the drain. The first mouse that got there was kicked to death by the priest. All the mice that came to the drain died. The boy turned pale because he felt he was losing his power. After the mice had gone, the priest asked the boy whether he had perhaps been given a book by his mother. When the boy took out the book, the priest took his prayer book in his hand. After that the boy had lost his power. But later he would still learn much evil from his mother.
185533: When a mother took her child out of the cradle to feed it, she saw at least a hundred mice crawling around in the cradle.
185537: A rich unbelieving gentleman feared neither God nor commandment. His maid always wanted to convert him, but he called her mad. One day when the gentleman was walking in the churchyard, he kicked a skull and said: "They say there is life after death, but I don't believe it. If it is true after all, you may come and eat with me tonight!" That evening the doorbell rang on the stroke of midnight. The servant opened the door and saw a ghost with glowing eyes. The ghost came in, drank a glass of wine and then said to the host: "You are my great-grandfather and I have been ordered to take you with me." The ghost seized the struggling gentleman and struck his head against the wall. When the gentleman was dead, the ghost took him away. He went to hell.
185551: A woman going to early mass in Tielt passed a crossroads at around four in the morning. There the woman saw an entirely black figure that had no feet and floated above the ground. The woman said "good day", but there was no answer.
185565: In Zuidschote there was a farm where strange things happened. At night the cows were tied by their tails to the ceiling beams and the horses ran around in the meadow. Yet during the day nothing strange could be seen. Because the people were at their wits' end, they sent for a chaplain. The clergyman advised them to make a little dirt path beside the house. In the morning they would see the tracks of a dog there. "It was a little black dog," the chaplain said, "but it would not come much longer." A few days later it was discovered that a neighbour woman with a little black dog was responsible for the evil. That woman also owned books of magic.
185566: A woman who had been to the market had been given too much change and died shortly afterwards. Her sister saw the ghost of the dead woman appear in the attic. The dead woman said: "You must give that money back." After the woman had returned the money, her dead sister no longer came to haunt.
185587: A brave man was not afraid of a woman from the village who was said to be able to bewitch. The man said: "That woman can come and do what she likes. She can't do anything anyway." The woman came up to the man and did nothing special. But when the woman had gone, the man could hardly walk any more. The man went on a pilgrimage with a neighbour woman. After a while neither the man nor the woman could go on. They both sat down and began to pray. After the two had been on pilgrimage, the witchcraft had no more effect.
185594: A sorceress always went from house to house at night, screaming loudly. A man loaded his gun with a half-franc coin and shot at something sitting on his roof. The next day the man heard that a little woman from the village had lost an eye.
185611: At the Tempeliershof in Oedelem there were haunted cellars. Whenever someone entered those cellars with a light, the light was strangely put out.
185614: A man went to play the accordion at a farm where three girls were standing talking. As he left, the man fell in the mud, and the girls asked: "Are you ill? What's wrong?" The man answered: "No, I'm not ill!" and scrambled back up. After that the man fell twice more. From then on the man no longer dared to go near that farm.
185630: In the old days the dead sometimes returned in the form of little lights. You were not allowed to point at such lights, for then they came closer. When someone did point at a light, it came and settled in a nearby cherry tree. The light probably went away by itself after that.
185639: A woman went on a pilgrimage with her sick child, who was wearing a white neckerchief. When the woman and the child had passed a certain house, the neckerchief was crawling with lice. After the friars had blessed the cloth, the vermin were gone.
185653: A pregnant woman who was about to give birth was visited by a woman who began reading from her books of magic. Because of that witchcraft, the pregnant woman had to lie in bed for three days before her child was born.
185670: A man had himself locked in the church because he wanted to see the witheren (white fathers) who appeared there every night. The witheren competed at jumping the farthest from the pulpit while they shouted: "Korreboet is the farthest". It was said that the passage out of the church ran all the way to Oudekapelle.
185720: A boy who was supposed to go to catechism class went with his friends to the parish priest's garden. While the boy kept watch, his friends climbed into the apple tree to steal fruit. Suddenly the priest came outside and said: "Well, well, now you will stay in that apple tree for as long as I like!" The boys could not get out of the apple tree. Only in the evening did the priest let the boys come down.
185726:
Some people could move a plague of rats or mice from one house to another. If you were struggling with such a plague, you had to send for a friar.
There were also people who could make others full of lice.
185746: In the Zinderdreef in Blankenberge there stood a house where a murder had once been committed. People did not dare walk past that house, and children were not allowed to go near it.
185786: In the wood of Elsegem a procession of about twenty white shades was often seen passing by at night. Beautiful music was played as well. The procession went right through the trees.
185805: When people could not churn butter, they believed there was a witch in the butter churn.
185806: A woman lying on her deathbed could not die. A witch managed to enter the room without opening the door.
185833: A witch used a broken scythe to magic the clothes off someone's body.
185837: Seven men on the run asked the lord of a castle in Scotland for shelter. The lord locked the men in a room and let them starve. Strange things always happened in the castle. Just before his death the lord told everything to his eldest son. Even now, sounds of the people who were locked up there can still be heard in the castle.
185845: In Ruddervoorde people had once seen a fireball or a fire-stone. Such things were natural phenomena that foretold a great disaster. The Northern Lights were also such a bad omen.
185856: When one was ridden by the mare, it seemed as if one was dreaming.
185861: During the First World War there were many English soldiers on the Rode Berg, carrying stones and sand with horse and cart. Because a great many of those soldiers had accidents, people believed that a witch lived nearby who wanted to harm the soldiers.
185878: A girl asked her neighbour: "Have you done the washing?" "No", answered the neighbour, at which the girl replied in surprise: "But I saw your laundry flying to the churchyard!"
185884: If one was ridden by the mare, one always had to put one's clogs with the toes pointing toward the door.
185887: In a house in Beveren people always heard sounds at night as if someone were threshing. When they went to see what was going on, the sound could no longer be heard. One day the farm was on fire. But as soon as people came closer, not a single flame could be seen. In the end the clergy came to the bewitched farm, where they banished the evil to the farthest corner of the field.
185891: One evening a woman went with her two dogs Lize and Danny to fetch her husband, who was in the inn 'De Geit'. When the woman reached the inn, a gentleman dressed in black suddenly appeared in front of her. "Lize, go ahead, and Danny, stay behind me!" the woman cried at once. The next moment two more gentlemen appeared. The woman set the dogs on them, whereupon the apparitions vanished in the blink of an eye.
185918: A rich, miserly framasson (freemason) had signed a contract in blood, declaring that the devil could come and fetch his soul after his death. When the freemason had died, his coffin was carried by six men. Suddenly a sound was heard in the coffin. When they opened the coffin, the body turned out to have vanished; the coffin was filled with earth.
185930: One of the friars from a monastery in Elsegem used to read his breviary in a little field path. One day a beautiful woman called Lange Jeanne appeared there and seduced the friar. When the abbot of the monastery heard what had happened, he put a curse on the woman. During the French Revolution the friars had to leave the monastery. After her death the cursed Lange Jeanne had to haunt. In the end Lange Jeanne was banished to a tree behind the monastery.
185946: The dead returned to point out hidden money. Otherwise they found no rest.
185959: A woman on her way to church saw the man walking in front of her lose his hat, even though there was no wind.
185966: People began digging at the spot where a light appeared every evening. When they brought up a chest, a dog jumped onto it and everything was gone.
185973: A child began to cry after being touched by a witch. The witch was only willing to break the spell if she was paid for it. Otherwise she would let the child die.
185977: A mother had cooked porridge for her little child. While the porridge stood cooling on the floor, a cat came to lick it. The mother threw a wooden knife at the cat, and the animal lost a paw. The next day the mother's neighbour lay in bed. She had lost a leg.
185979: A wizard had a birch hedge whose wood he used to make brooms. One day a man from the neighbourhood also went to that birch hedge to cut off some branches. In the hedge stood a horse that looked at the man with a grin. The wizard had turned himself into a horse to guard his wood.
185984: At about three in the morning a man was returning from Staden, where he had helped with the birth of a foal. When the man came into a small wood, he heard knocking and chopping there as if trees were being felled. The next day not a single branch had been moved at that spot.
186001: A woman who was out in the evenings always saw little white rabbits running ahead of her that could not be caught. One day the woman did manage to catch one of the little animals and put it under a tub. The next day an old woman was found under that tub, all curled up. It was a witch who could turn herself into a rabbit.
186003: A man who was ridden by the mare felt something come over him and had a terrible dream. The man tried to call out, but no sound came. Victims of the mare felt short of breath and could not defend themselves.
186024: A man who had learned sorcery by reading his father's books of magic had sent rats to a farm. The farmer asked the sorcerer to take the rats away again. When the sorcerer had done so, he met another farmer on the way, who said "good day". Because of that, this farmer got the rats in turn. After that the sorcerer sent the rats to the sea.
186027: The daughter of a witch had grown completely crooked and had pimples all over. People believed the child had got these ailments from always looking in the books of magic. The child could not be helped by her mother. That probably meant the witch did not have so much power after all.
186043: Some people who were cleaning the church in the afternoon saw the ghost of a dead priest appear. The priest had to come and say masses he had neglected.
186065: The eternal hunter flew through the sky at night calling: "Tsjagouw!" He was a man who could find no rest because he was cursed. The eternal hunter could only find rest on the green tip of a rush, but the tips of rushes are always brown.
186070: A man coming back from the Oostveld one evening was followed by a goose at the Slabbaertsbuze. The man was drenched in sweat from fear.
186074: A ten-year-old boy was always ill. Every day a woman came to eat with the boy's family. One day the sick boy said to his mother: "That woman acts so strangely. She doesn't mean us well." Then the mother stuck a little palm branch in the keyhole of the door. After that the woman did not visit again and the boy recovered.
186077: A boy wanted to marry the daughter of a witch. When the boy fell ill, he said: "She has my flesh, but not yet my bones!" The boy died all the same.
186079: People who had promised to go on a pilgrimage also had to keep that promise. Otherwise they came to haunt every night after their death.
186083: Some people from Veurne had to pass the house of a witch who lived by the canal. Because the people could not get past, they were forced to return to Veurne.
186091: A man who owned books of magic met a murderer one day, who demanded two francs from him. The sorcerer bewitched the murderer so he was fixed to the ground. Only the next day did the sorcerer let his attacker go.
186108: On a farm in Nieuwpoort Bad there was a little child who cried all the time and grew very thin, although it ate well. One day the new stable hand saw the maid wash the child and put a fresh nappy on it. The farmhand forced the maid to take the nappy off again and found that it was full of pins. Crying, the maid admitted that she herself was ridden by the mare and that she could get rid of it by passing it on to someone else.
186112: In Bergen-op-Zoom lived a woman whose three sons had already died. The woman sought advice from the parish priest, who said: "Don't go to the market any more when you are pregnant." For a witch went about at the market.
186133: A woman whose father had died at a great age always saw a little light in the field after his death. The neighbours advised her to go to the priest. The priest advised her to go up to the light and ask it why it was burning. The light turned out to be her dead father, who returned because there was still a promise he had not kept. After the promise was fulfilled for him, the light did not appear again.
186139: Strange things happened on a farm in Izegem. Every time they went to milk the cows, the animals were full of lice. People believed that a sorceress from the neighbourhood had put a toad in the water pump, so that the animals' drinking water was bewitched.
186168:
When one was ridden by the mare, one felt as if one was going to die. One then tried to call out, but no sound came because the mare squeezed its victim's throat shut.
Perhaps the phenomenon had something to do with the circulation of the blood.
186175: A seamstress from Torhout on her way to Brugge saw a farm on fire near the churchyard. When the seamstress went back to that place the next day, there was no trace of the fire.
186177: People who were ridden by the mare could not lie still. They hung a pine branch above their bed.
186188: In Leke lived a woman who could turn herself into a dog. Nobody let that woman come near their children.
186193: A man who had been out decided to have one last drink in a café where he still saw a light burning. However, the man could not get into the café because a big dog blocked the entrance. When the man went home, the dog kept jumping in front of his feet the whole time. When he got home, the man could not open the farm gate because the dog was standing there again. Only after the man had stood there for half the night did the dog suddenly vanish without a trace.
186202: For eight or ten days, people in Ieper saw a goat flying through the air every evening at about the same time. People came from Wervik and Komen to Ieper to see the goat. The farmer's wife of the farm where the goat always stayed was said to have once had a child by her cowherd. That cowherd was said to have thrown the child into the ramparts, and that crime may have caused the apparition.
186250: On a farm two cats were seen fighting at night. The farmer got up and struck off a paw of one of the cats with a stick. The next morning a woman from the neighbourhood had a broken leg.
186253: A farmer and his wife who were taking their child to be baptised had to pass the house of a witch. At exactly that spot the child suddenly vanished. The child's little blanket lay in the ditch. The witch came outside and said to the people: "Come back some other time and go home now." When the farmer and his wife got home, they saw their baby lying in the cradle.
186254: In Tiegem a child had been bewitched by a witch. Because of this the child's arms were turned back to front. The parents took the child to a healer, who laid it on the table. Then a big spider ran across the table. "The witch is there," said the healer, and he threw the spider into the stove. The child would now soon recover, he predicted. He was proved right.
186256: A soldier wanted to marry a girl from Lombardsijde. The parish priest, however, did not agree and said to the soldier: "If you don't listen to me, you'll get lots of lice!" The soldier did indeed get so many lice that he had to abandon the girl. In the past, priests mastered magic arts they had learned from books of magic.
186259: A farm in Ichtegem was haunted. Whenever people were working in the field there, they always heard someone scraping out a trough. Someone advised the farmer to say next time: "Elzenhoekske is baking a little cake". When the farmer did so, a little later he saw a small cake lying on a beautiful white cloth. The farmer gave the cake to the dog. The next moment the ground split open and the dog sank into it. After that nothing strange happened on the farm anymore.
186274: The parish priest could bewitch people who were talking during mass so they were stuck to their chairs. If there was a fire somewhere, the priest could make the wind turn.
186275: Because a farmer's son was not allowed to marry a girl who worked on the farm, he hanged himself. Since then strange things happened on the farm. The doors opened and closed by themselves, and whenever things had been cleaned, they became dirty again by themselves. The farm was sold, but the haunting never stopped, so in the end the farm stood empty.
186290: A mother whose youngest child cried all the time and whose second youngest grew very thin sought advice from the friars. The friars predicted that the person responsible for the evil would come to ask for a soft brush. One of the children would die, but the other would live. One of the children did indeed die at twelve o'clock.
186305: A woman had scratches all over her face because a witch had bewitched her from a distance with pins.
186306: Whoever was ridden by the mare lost control of themselves and could even jump out of the window.
186314: A man who was drying chicory saw the door of the drying kiln open at one o'clock at night. A man with a goat appeared and went to the fire in the stoking room. After a while the man came back sweating and completely black. In the following days no one could manage to light a fire in the stoking room; the fire always went out.
186352: Osschaart was a big dog that roamed at night with a whole pack of little dogs behind it.
186358: In Zerkegem lived a mother whose child was dying. The child cried all the time and would not sleep. Because the child was also completely full of pins, the mother went on a pilgrimage to Nieuwpoort together with a man from the village. The two set out at eleven o'clock at night. When the man and the woman reached the first station of the Way of the Cross, a woman in clogs came up to them and went the whole way with them. When the man and the woman were at the fifth station, the church tower struck five. The witch walking with them then said: "It is five o'clock! It is five o'clock!" After the woman had answered, the witch suddenly vanished without a trace. The woman should not have answered, for on the way back her companion fell ill, so that he had to be fetched with the dog cart. The sick child did recover in the end.
186375: A poacher often went hunting in the Pilderbos between Roeselare and Ardooie. The man always put half a small gold coin in his gun. If he did not, the gun would fly to pieces when he shot at a hare with it. Such hares were often old women who had turned themselves into animals.
186410: A witch once lived in Gistel. A farmer who owned a large threshing machine took it from one farm to the next with three strong mares. Those small farms had only one horse. One day the farmer and a few men were moving the threshing machine when they saw the witch coming in the distance. The farmer said to the witch: "Watch out, because if you end up under this, you'll be as flat as the ground!" The witch was annoyed and replied: "You just make sure that threshing machine doesn't end up in the ditch!" Ten metres further on, the threshing machine fell into the ditch. They tried every possible way to get the three mares to pull the machine out of the ditch, but it was no use. The witch said: "There is only one person who can do that." She named a woman who had mules. In the end the farmer went to fetch that woman. The woman came along with her two mules. She wore a hat and a dirty apron. The three horses and the two mules together could not get the threshing machine out of the ditch. "That won't work," said the witch, "you must put the mules in front of the threshing machine on their own." When they did so, the threshing machine was out of the ditch at once.
186418: In Proven lived a woman who had special powers. When that woman was sewing, the frogs crawled around her to thread the needles.
186421: In Leffinge there was a farm where the cellar was haunted. After milking the cows in the evening, people put the tubs of milk in the cellar to skim the milk the next morning. In the morning they always found blood in the milk. After a priest had exorcised the farm, nothing strange happened anymore.
186431: On the grounds of the castle of Petegem a hundred and fifty skulls were dug up. In the days of slavery the lord of the castle made his slaves work hard without giving them food. At night the slaves even had to silence the frogs so as not to disturb the lord's sleep. After their death those slaves were buried on the castle grounds. Later it was haunted at Jantje de Knikker's (?) in an underground passage of the castle.
186437: In Zwevegem a man was cursing. Suddenly devils appeared in the shape of rabbits and hens, which wrecked the man's house. The animals ate the man's food and kept coming into the house. In the end the man had to have his house exorcised by the friars.
186441: A man could make rats and mice, which he let run around on a newspaper. The curate wanted to take the man's books away, but he never managed to get into the house.
186442: On a farm with more than twelve cows, one animal after another died. One day someone said: "On Sunday during High Mass someone will come and stand at the gate and ask if you have any meat left. If that happens, you must give that woman a good dressing-down." Once the farmer knew who the witch was, she no longer dared to do any harm.
186459: Whoever was ridden by the mare was seized, could not move and screamed the whole time.
186481: A man who had kicked at a cat was startled when the cat suddenly turned into a woman.
186504: A Freemason from Sint-Baafs-Vijve who never went to church came back to haunt after his death around midnight in the shape of a pig. After the fathers of Tielt had exorcised the farm, the pig no longer appeared.
186507: A farmer's wife was always visited by a woman who came to get eggs. The parish priest advised the farmer's wife not to give that woman any more eggs. Then the woman said to the farmer's wife: "By tomorrow you won't have a single egg left." The next day all the hens lay dead in their coop.
186512: A girl saw a little light burning in a meadow. The child's mother then said: "Oh dear, that is old X who is dead. You mustn't go and look. Just think how much money that woman may have!"
186524: In Oostende lived a witch who wore a little white cap and a hooded cloak. Whenever this witch had come to buy fish at the boat in the morning, the fishermen caught nothing at all that day. People said this witch owned many books of magic. She could make people stand still or make them dance in their beds. It was also said that the witch stuck pins into a burning candle.
186550: At night a man saw a funeral service in the grass. If you said nothing, the ghosts left you alone.
186565: In Ledegem there once worked a Duitse schaper (German shepherd, a travelling shepherd said to have magic powers). The shepherd was always followed by boys who picked up the sheep's dung. One day the shepherd said to one of the boys: "Go to that inn and ask for a jug of beer. When the cellar door opens, look carefully where the tap of the beer is." A while later the boy came back with a jug of beer. He said: "The tap is in the west." Whenever the shepherd was thirsty, he held his staff towards the west. The next moment beer came out of the staff. In the café the beer barrel was empty without anyone knowing how.
186567: In the horse stable of a woman from Eernegem a little doll was found that was pierced with pins from head to toe. In this way witches could torment children.
186585: A man coming back from the fair in Haringe met a nun on the way. As the nun came closer, she grew bigger and bigger. When she stood beside the man, she was twice as tall as he was. When the nun had passed and the man looked back, suddenly there was nothing to be seen.
186588: When the daughter-in-law of a witch was being taken to the church, the horses bolted with the corpse. The horses ended up standing with their forelegs against the church wall.
186607: A man heard chains rattling behind him, as if he were being followed by a ghost. But there was no one to be seen.
186609: A man had to keep walking around with a beam on his back because he had been cursed by a priest.
186617: A farmhand had to roll the field. The field lay opposite the house of a woman who was said to be a witch. The farmhand had worked all afternoon but had not got far. The witch stood watching in her hooded cloak and said: "Boy, isn't it going well?" The farmhand answered: "No, but if you weren't standing there, it would go much better!" Then the witch went away. The farmhand cut a willow twig and used it to mend the chain that had broken. After that the work went much better. The farmhand rolled the whole field with a willow twig.
186629: A woman suspected of being a witch could turn herself into a rabbit. One day a baker cut the ears off all his rabbits. As a result that woman had no ears any more either, and she always had to wear a woollen cap.
186632: A man was chased by black cats on the road between Sint-Michiels and Oostkamp. The man could not catch those cats in any way.
186633: At a farmer's in Wilskerke a doodskeers (death candle) was seen in the tree every evening. One evening a brave farmhand went up to the light. The light said it had to stay there seven more days. It was a soul that still had to wander.
186638: Near Poelkapelle there was a farm where strange things happened. At night the occupants heard wagons driving, though nothing could be seen. After the farm had burned down, the strange events came to an end.
186649: People who slept on their backs were sometimes ridden by the mare and as a result could no longer breathe. To protect oneself against the mare, one had to put one's clogs or slippers with the heels toward the bed.
186653: A man saw a horse go by, heading in the direction of Meulebeke. A little further on, the horse put its hoof against a door and went into a house, where the animal turned everything upside down.
186670: A farm in Ruddervoorde was haunted. People who walked along the bank there at night got soaked. There was also a shed in which all the animals died. When people on that farm tried to pull a bundle of wood out of the woodpile in the evening, they could not. When they finally pulled the whole woodpile down, they heard someone laughing.
186702: If someone had poured hot water over an animal, it could sometimes be seen the next day that a neighbour had burns.
186706:
On a farm in Moen the animals were untied every night. The sound of a flail was also heard there. When people went to look, there was nothing to be seen. When the farmer came home at midnight, he saw an old woman standing there and asked her: "What are you doing here?" The woman answered: "The day is for you and the night is for us..." The woman also gave the farmer a photograph of herself.
The next night there was again a lot of noise on the farm. The woman's photograph could be seen, greatly enlarged, on the wall.
After the fathers of Kortrijk had been consulted, the haunting came to an end.
186709: A woman went to fetch water from her neighbours. The following night the neighbours' cows were lowing, so that they had to get up to milk the animals.
186716: A bewitched woman saw five of her children die. The woman sought advice from the chaplain.
186717: A woman from Oostende stood outside every evening making gestures as if she were fighting someone. The woman claimed it was her boyfriend, who had made himself invisible. In the end the woman married someone else.
186741: A doctor who had to go to a patient at 't Blokske one night was about to fall victim to robbers. But the doctor said to the robbers: "You just stay here! You will stand here until I say so." Then the doctor went and reported the robbers to the police in Waasten. The criminals all got a hefty fine.
186758: A man who had been drinking saw a gentleman and a lady floating in the Maurice Dewulfstraat. The gentleman wore a top hat and a cloak. The man was so frightened that he was instantly sober and ran home.
186762: In their imagination people sometimes thought they saw dead relatives appear.
186764: A little boy could make mice out of clay. When he put the mice on the pavement, they ran away. One day a priest had the boy make mice in the church and put them on the altar. There, however, the mice could not run away. From then on the boy had lost his magic power.
186770:
People who were ridden by the mare felt short of breath and began to sweat heavily. To protect oneself against the mare, one had to put one's clogs upside down under the bed.
Plants whose branches were completely flattened, such as broom bushes, had also been ridden by the mare.
186785: A man went to look in the churchyard because his son had said a kind of mist hung there. The man and his son saw two little lights with droplets on them. Father and son were followed by the light to the grave of a small child. There the light vanished into a little glass cover above a small cross.
186793: After a freemason had died in Assebroek, the man's daughters heard noises in the house every evening. The daughters did not stay living in that house much longer.
186799: Whoever wanted to protect themselves against the mare had to put their shoes toe to toe beside the bed.
186807: Whoever was ridden by the mare could neither move nor speak. If one could say the name of the person one suspected of having sent the mare, one was released.
186817: A farm in Sint-Eloois-Vijve was so badly haunted that all its occupants went bankrupt after a few years. Although the stable door had been closed in the evening, the next morning four horses were found hanged from the beams.
186818: A mother had often been advised by her neighbour to keep the old woman who lived behind them away from the children of the neighbourhood. One day when the mother went to a funeral, she had put her eldest child in the grass behind the house. On coming home, the mother found that her child was behaving strangely. Three days later the child had convulsions. A neighbour advised the woman to go on a pilgrimage and consult a doctor. The child was prayed over by the parish priest, who sweated heavily. When the child woke up, the priest made the sign of the cross. After that it was over (?). They then went on a pilgrimage in honour of Saint Nicholas of Tolentino in the Church of Our Lady.
186820: Around the castle of Rumbeke, a procession without a cross was often seen on summer nights. A man who had gone to watch the procession was bewitched. It seemed as if a dog was lying on the man's shoes. The man had to carry that dog the whole way.
186833: At night ghost coaches carrying several gentlemen and a beautiful lady drove around the castle of Oostrozebeke. Each coach was drawn by four horses.
186844:
One evening a man met a woman he suspected was a witch. The man knew that witches could not walk on your right side if you read the Gospel of Saint John. The witch quickly jumped into the mud on the left.
A stable hand from Houtkerke met a woman one night in the moonlight, who lifted her skirt slightly. When the stable hand reached the Groene Dreef, the woman had vanished. She was a witch.
186874: A farmhand working on a farm in Houtkerke had to manure the field. At a certain moment the farmer's mother came to visit. That woman lived in Steenvoorde. The mother said to the farmhand: "What a fine bull that is in the meadow!" She repeated it as many as four times and then added: "What if that bull were to drop dead!" The farmhand replied: "Such a fine bull won't drop dead!" When the woman was three steps further on, the bull dropped dead in the meadow. That woman could bewitch.
186889: When a farm had a lot of bad luck, people believed the stables had been bewitched by a witch.
186892: In Snaaskerke lived a woman who heard knocking in the chest of drawers in her bedroom every evening. The woman believed it was her late husband who had returned.
186932: In Brugge an old woman met a woman who struck her. The old woman wandered around Brugge for three hours before she could find her bearings again.
186934: In Woumen lived a woman who possessed special powers. Whenever that woman had looked over a stable door somewhere, the animals soon fared badly. People never dared to let their children near that woman.
186950: At the Katteput by the inn 't Sperregat there were always so many cats that nobody dared to go near anymore. Nobody knew what those cats were doing there.
186954: Because the parents of a seven-year-old boy had to go to a wedding, they had the grandmother look after their child. The next morning the boy was paralysed. The parents believed the grandmother had bewitched the child.
186970:
People who were ridden by the mare saw a woman or a man come in by way of the roof or the chimney. Those people were sweating and wanted to call out, but no sound came. A man who had been ridden by the mare walked around his farm with a spade to catch the mare.
Later the man heard from the doctor that the mare had something to do with the blood.
186974: A brave man always had something strange treading on his heels when he went home. A priest asked the man whether he had ever promised anything, to which the man answered: "Yes, I promised to go to Ramskapel and I have not done it." The priest advised the man to go to his father's grave at midnight and say a prayer with arms outstretched in the form of a cross there. While the man was praying, he suddenly saw a peacock in the sky. After the man had gone to serve in Ramskapel, everything returned to normal.
186977: Whoever was tormented by the mare had to pray an Our Father.
186981: In Moorsele chains were always heard rattling and cows lowing under the ground. French nuns had been able to buy that property for a pittance as zwart goed (confiscated church property).
187000: A woman had salted a freshly slaughtered pig. Three weeks later the meat began to stink. It had been bewitched by an old woman.
187045: On a farm struck by the evil hand, butter could no longer be churned. The friars advised the farmer to put salt in the milk. That way the neighbour woman could no longer bewitch the milk.
187046: A sorcerer lived in a house in Nieuwpoort. If a soldier dared to touch an apple on the tree in that garden, he got stuck to the tree. When his maid married, the sorcerer gave her a jug as a wedding present. Whenever the couple went to bed, the jug always started to dance. In the end the woman died of it.
187055:
In a small farmhouse on the Waaienberg there was a baby that cried all the time and would no longer eat. When the child was prayed over by the friars, the clergyman sweated with effort. The friar said to the people: "If anyone comes to ask for something, you must never give anything!"
One day, when the people were baking oven cakes, a woman came by who wanted a few cakes. "The cakes aren't ready yet," they told the woman, who did not believe it. Because those people could no longer churn butter after that, they sought advice from the friars, who gave them a sprig with flowers to put under the door.
187062: On a farm where butter could no longer be churned, on the friars' advice they put horse manure in the churn. A friar had predicted that a woman would come for milk the next day. The next day a woman did indeed come along wearing one shoe and one clog. That is how they found out who was responsible for the evil. After that day butter could be churned again.
187067:
A widower from Koekelare had remarried a woman who could not stand his son. "Go and sell him, even if it's to the devil!" the stepmother had said.
On a dark, stormy night the father went with his son to the woods of Wijnendale. The devil approached on horseback and asked the father: "How much money do you want if I take your son for a year to be doorkeeper in hell?"
A year later the boy came back to his father. He told him that he had let in priests, doctors and lawyers, and even his own godmother.
The boy had only seen the first hall of hell. There he had seen a man from Torhout. He had held a stick under that man's seat and afterwards found that the stick was completely burnt.
187070: Whoever was ridden by the mare could hardly breathe and felt as if two thousand kilos were lying on their body. Branches of trees that had been ridden by the mare became flattened.
187072: A miller's hand had found his master's book of magic in the mill. When the hand began to read the book, a farmer in his field stood stock-still. The miller's hand, however, did not know which spell would make the farmer move again. When the miller came home, he dismissed the hand.
187075: A farmer and his wife wanted to sell a calf and were discussing the price, while a possible buyer stood a good way off. The farmer's wife did not agree with the price her husband proposed and said: "No, I don't want to sell it for that; I'd like five francs more." Although the witch was standing a good way off and could not possibly have heard the conversation, she shouted: "No, you won't! You'll keep the calf here!"
187078: Some farmers who were smuggling linseed saw an old woman standing by the gate, watching. The farmers said: "Little woman, what are you doing here? You'd better go to bed!" The witch answered: "You and your cheeky mouth, just wait! Something will happen to you when you are twenty steps further on!" When the farmers were twenty steps further on, the witch made all three of them fall off the dike.
187094: A man learned sorcery from a sorcerer. When the man went home, the sorcerer asked him whether he was afraid. The man replied: "I'm not afraid of anything!" The sorcerer said: "If you come across something on the way, just step over it." On his way home the man saw a large black dog with chains lying in the street. The man kicked the animal, but his foot kicked only air.
187106: With a book of magic one could bewitch someone so they were fixed to the ground.
187116: A child rode by on a bicycle past the house of a witch who stood in her doorway, without saying good day. Then the witch said: "You big rascal, mind you don't fall!" A moment later the child fell off the bicycle.
187120: A man from Hertsberge went to fetch the doctor from Ruddervoorde for his pregnant wife. The man was found dead at night by a beech lane with a bramble branch around his head. Those woods were always haunted. During the day the women went there to sweep up leaves. At night the men went to collect those leaves. The heaps were covered with a bedsheet.
187127: People who were ridden by the mare were completely drenched in sweat and could not move. They had the impression that a woman was standing beside them. To protect oneself against the mare, one had to put one's shoes under the bed with the toes pointing in.
187129: When a witch had let her pigs out, the animals ran themselves to death against the hedge. If a witch could not bewitch other people or animals, her own animals became the victims.
187132: A little light was always seen at the black mill in Dranouter. People were afraid of that light. One day a man had followed it. He saw the ghost of someone long dead who was counting his money. The next day the man dug up that money and put a cross on the spot.
187133: A weaver going to his weaving room in the morning saw a dead calf lying in a well. At that the man ran away. When the man came back, the calf had disappeared from the well.
187135: When one had eaten too much, one could sometimes be ridden by the mare. To prevent that, one had to lay a knife on one's chest at night. People who did so were not ridden by the mare, but they were hurt by the knife.
187148: A dying woman saw a pack of blue rats come into her house one evening. The rats then went out again through the back door. The next evening the rats appeared again. The animals had been sent, you see. "Just let the rats be," said the little woman, "they'll go away again." On the third night the rats did not appear any more.
187159: A man had experienced something strange at the crossroads of the Engeldreef in Ijvegem. Suddenly a donkey had appeared there. The man had crossed the crossroads on the donkey. Afterwards the animal had vanished without a trace.
187160: A woman had a nine-month-old son. When the woman came home one day, her mother said: "The child wouldn't drink and cried a lot." On Saturday a strange woman dressed all in black had come to visit. That woman had taken the child's dummy and had done something with it. Nine days later the child was cured, after being prayed over by the friars.
187183: A man saw his dead wife crawling over the roof, rattling her money. The family had forgotten to have a mass said. After that promise had finally been fulfilled, the woman no longer appeared.
187189: In Herzele there once lived a man who could send rats to a house. To be able to do this, one had to say a special prayer. The rats could only be sent to a place where they could get enough to eat and drink.
187193: Some people were followed by little lights. These were souls from purgatory that came to ask for something.
187205: A farmer and his wife kept having bad luck with their animals. One day a vet from Slijpe came to look at the animals. On arriving, the vet said: "Who was that little woman in the hooded cloak just now?" But the farmer and his wife had seen no one. When the farmer's wife fell ill herself, they went to the friars in Oostende. After the farmer's wife had been prayed over, she got better. The clergyman had said that the bad luck was due to a little woman who came to the farm every day. Indeed, an old woman in a hooded cloak came for milk every day. That woman had a bad name and always went to the animals. Once the farmer and his wife had chased that woman away, things went much better on their farm.
187223: In Adegem some witches had to stay sitting in the church because the priest had left his missal open.
187262: A woman from the Reiger (1) sometimes sat on her gate crowing like a rooster. People claimed that this woman could turn herself into any animal at all.
187267: A farmer always heard someone singing in front of the door in the evening. One evening the annoyed farmer threw a billhook at the ghost. The next morning an arm with a beautiful gold ring on its finger was found lying in front of the door.
187271: Two men saw a cat sitting on a bridge in the moonlight. A little farther on, near the Merelaer, the men saw a man as tall as a tree, who jumped over the dyke and ran off. A little later someone came driving up with a great deal of noise, though no one could be seen. Exactly a year later one of the men came to the same spot with the dog cart. The dogs jumped over the dyke and would no longer pull the cart. Someone came by who said he had experienced the same thing.
187277: Two men walking home in the evening were followed by a kitten that kept running between their legs. When the men stopped, the kitten sat down too. One of the men wanted to kick the kitten, but his friend advised him not to. In the end, however, the man kicked at the animal anyway. The next moment the man fell over backwards. He was drenched in sweat.
187311: In Bavikhove lived a witch who was out and about all night. On a farm, three daughters had been bewitched by that woman. Because of this, the witch was no longer welcome at that farm.
187318: The Hondspoort in Stavele was haunted. People claimed that passers-by had to turn a spinning wheel there for two hours.
187321: If a clergyman went east, a storm would come.
187331: Because the weather was nice and calm, a woman decided to hang her washing outside. Five minutes after the woman had gone back inside, a strong wind sprang up. As soon as the woman had brought her washing in, it was strangely calm again, so the woman went and hung the washing outside again. The same thing happened three times, until the woman finally decided to hang her washing out the next day.
187347: In Adinkerke a witch had come to look at the rabbits. Shortly afterwards the animals died.
187349: The Berebos (1) was a small wood on the hill that separated the Scheldt valley from the Leie valley. On that hill stood the mill 'Te Clare', from which twenty-five church towers could be seen in clear weather. The people who lived on that hill were isolated from other settlements and practised and believed in all kinds of evil. It was said, for instance, that an old woman who lived alone was a witch who could make children ill by conjuring. When a child somewhere was ill, people noticed that a black cat walked around the sick child's house every night. One night the child's mother threw boiling water over the animal, which ran off howling. The next day the suspected old woman lay in bed with burns.
187355: A girl was always ridden by the mare at night. She then felt as if an old woman or a man was crawling over her. That feeling, however, was due to iron deficiency. When the girl had been given a bottle of medicine by the doctor, she was cured of the affliction.
187368: Bells were said to have once sunk in the bell pits in Koekelare.
187369: The mare was a woman who sat on her victims so that they could no longer breathe. As soon as someone called out the victim's name, the mare was gone.
187370: A man on his way to his girlfriend saw a beautiful woman standing close to her farm, who came towards him. The man hurried on to his girlfriend. The man experienced the same thing many more times, and the beautiful woman stood in the same place every time.
187373: A man going to visit his girlfriend in Wulpen had to swim along the canal because he could not walk any further along the road. This was due to the influence of a parish priest.
187374: One night a woman was ridden by the mare, which made her feel so ill that the priest was even sent for to administer the Last Rites. The next morning the woman felt perfectly healthy again.
187397: In Oostrozebeke lived a farmer who always gave the beggars porridge at midday. One day a beggar woman came who had laid her hand on the back of a pig. A while later that sow rejected her young. The cows gave no more milk and at night all sorts of noises were heard. Neither the friars of Tielt nor those of Steenbrugge could undo the evil. To make matters worse, seven of the farmer's sons died. In the end the farmer moved to Holland. When the farm got new occupants, the friars were able to banish the evil to the farthest corner of the farmyard.
187414: A woman from Uitkerke had to go and clean the house of a witch. On her way home the woman fell over backwards three times, although there was nothing at all on the road.
187438: On a farm in Lichtervelde many animals died. The people went to the friars of Roeselare and were advised to seize the first woman who came to visit. The next day the neighbour woman came by. But they did not dare accuse her and went to the friars again. The clergymen said: "Even if it is your own sister, you must lock her up in your house." The next day the neighbour came again. They locked her up and sent for the friar to pray over the woman. Afterwards someone had to go with the friar to the farthest corner of the field, where the clergyman buried something. After that the evil came to an end.
187461: In Gijzelbrechtegem a headless horse used to walk through the streets. People were so afraid of the phantom horse that they no longer dared to go outside.
187466: On a farm a labourer had handed in his notice. The farmer's wife had become so angry that she said: "I wish he would break his legs!" When the labourer carried a sack up to the loft, he broke a leg. That farmer's wife owned many books of magic.
187480: A parish priest had a black dog. After the priest died, the dog roamed the village at night. When someone called the animal, it came up to the house of the person who had called. Then the dog went back to the presbytery.
187482: In the past it sometimes happened that people were ridden by the mare. Such torments were caused by witches who owned books.
187490: A woman came to a farm in Watou to fetch buttermilk. When milk was poured into her bucket, she said: "That is far too much!" After some milk had been poured from the bucket back into the vat, they could no longer make buttermilk.
187493: A woman walking home heard someone walking in clogs. When she got home, the woman saw light in the henhouse. The door of the hallway flew open. It was probably the soul of a man who came haunting to count his money. The man had killed himself by drowning.
187502: At the 'Droge Boom' (Dry Tree) in Waregem, people used to be able to sell their soul to the devil. A man who had done so had become extremely rich. When the man was dead, no one could get near his coffin because a hundred mice were running around it.
187505: When rattling was heard in a house, the fathers were called in to exorcise the house.
187510: A German shepherd worked on a farm between Nieuwkerke and Kemmel. One day the shepherd was sitting in the grass when someone passed by who did not greet him. A little later the rude passer-by was full of lice.
187518: One day a tobacco seller did not go home by his usual road. He went through the meadow, where he met someone. Shortly afterwards the tobacco seller got lost. That was probably the fault of the man he had met in the meadow.
187527: A man and a woman carried their baby in a little blanket to the church to have it baptised. When they arrived at the church, the child had suddenly vanished without a trace. The child was with a witch.
187546: A girl was not allowed to go outside with her little sister, because the mother was afraid the child would be bewitched. When the girl went outside with her sister anyway one time, the child began to cry day and night. That was the fault of a neighbour woman. The mother decided to go to the parish priest. The mother had only just left when the girl saw the witch coming, who asked: "Where is your mother?" The girl lied and said her mother had gone to her grandmother's. After the priest had prayed over the child, it recovered.
187556: On a farm where they had bad luck with the animals and could not make butter, one day a black cat was seen crawling out of the butter churn. The friars gave those people medals to tie around the cows' legs.
187564: A man coming back from Veldegem was accompanied by a dog that walked beside him the whole time. At a certain moment the dog had suddenly disappeared.
187577: By a willow in a garden in Izegem a little light burned every night. After money had been dug up at that spot, the light no longer appeared.
187600: A boy who had to light the fire one evening was hindered by a cat that kept walking back and forth. The boy poured boiling water over the cat. The next day the boy's mother lay in her bed with burns.
187646: A man who had lit the oven to bake bread saw that a toad had crawled into the oven and said to his wife: "Quickly fetch the Gospel of Saint John, because my mother is bewitching again! She will make the baking fail again!" When the oven was hot, the toad had burned up.
187653: A woman whose child had been bewitched went to the parish priest for advice. The clergyman advised the woman to throw out her seamstress.
187657:
Late in the evening someone came haunting at a well in Beveren.
It was haunted at the Helleketel too. Someone lived there who could conjure up frogs. While people were eating there, the frogs jumped onto the table.
187679: Two brothers who lived at the Ruyterhoek along the road from Zarren to Linde experienced strange things. When the brothers were eating, the forks flew out of their hands. Their father was often pulled by the beard by an invisible force.
187685: A man who had died young came back every night after his death to count the money he had hidden somewhere. The occupants of the house went looking for the money after hearing strange noises. The money was found in the false bottom of a trunk. The money was given to the priest to have masses said.
187702: If a death owl sat on the house, one of the occupants would soon die. At an old man's house an owl sat screeching in a willow. The neighbours chased the bird away, but the next morning the man was dead.
187718: Two boys were out together when one of them suddenly stepped in a little heap of rubbish. A black cat turned out to be sitting in the heap. The boys were very frightened, because they had always heard it said that black cats were witches.
187719: A woman going to mass met a cat on the way, which asked: "Where are you going?" "To mass," the woman replied. When the woman looked behind her, she saw that she had a stick in her hands. (?)
187724: Whoever had been ridden by the mare went to the little chapel by the castle de Mare in Aartrijke.
187729: In Passendale lived a witch. If that witch so much as touched the hedge of a farm, the farmers could no longer churn butter.
187740: Witches owned evil books. They could send their spirit wandering through houses, so that people heard all kinds of noises in the loft without anything being seen.
187742: A man who had to join the army was back home again after a few days. "I might as well die here as there," said the man. His parents asked a former soldier from the area to take their son back to the army. They believed that a witch from the neighbourhood had made their son unwilling to stay in the army, because they had seen that witch talking to their son before he left for the army.
187743: A beachcomber who had got lost had to walk around all night with a beam on his back. At a certain moment the beachcomber met the priest, who said: "If you had gone to vespers, this would not have happened!"
187748: A woman who was ridden by the mare felt a man squeezing her throat shut. The woman began to sweat heavily and called her husband, who was lying beside her. The husband, however, heard nothing of her calling.
187754: A man who worked for a brewer had to take a barrel of jenever to an inn one Saturday. But the man had forgotten. When the man arrived at the inn with a load of beer, the innkeeper's wife was angry because he had forgotten the barrel of jenever. She said to the man: "You ought to fall into the canal with your wagon on your way home!" On the way home, at the Nieuwe Brugge, the man fell into the canal with his horse and cart. After that the man never went to that innkeeper's wife again. He believed she was a witch.
187762: Whoever was ridden by the kokkemare (the mare) felt something crawl over their legs and then felt as if they would suffocate. Victims of the kokkemare tried to call out, but could not make a sound. To protect oneself against the kokkemare, one had to hide one's shoes or put them upside down under the bed.
187764: A woman who had long been dead sat every evening on the threshold of her house in Kuurne. The priest asked the ghost: "In God's name, why do you come?", to which the ghost replied: "There is something under my threshold". When people looked in the daytime, they found all the woman's money buried under the threshold. After the money had been taken away, the ghost did not return.
187766: In the evening dark clouds were often seen in the sky. That was the eternal hunter. It was the soul of a dead man who could find no rest. When there was a storm, someone could sometimes be heard calling: "Houw! Houw! Houw!"
187768: Because a man had hidden money somewhere, he returned after his death in the form of a little light. One day the hedge where the light appeared was pulled out. After that the light was never seen again. It may well be that the men who removed the hedge kept the money for themselves.
187778: A farmer met a Bohemian woman from Oostende who asked for milk for her baby. The farmer refused and gave the woman some water. The Bohemian woman then cursed the farmer. A little further on, the man had a fatal accident.
187783: A woman was home alone because her husband was visiting an aunt who was dying. All evening the woman heard knocking on the shutters and the doors. She lit a candle and began to pray, but the noise did not stop. The next day the friars came to read prayers of deliverance over the house. When that was done, the clergymen said: "Woman, there has been much evil in this house! You still pray too little." The friars gave the woman some prayers to say. A while later there was no more knocking in the house. When one day one of those friars visited the woman, he walked around the house and said: "All evil is gone. Now you can live happily and in good health!"
187788: In Aartrijke lived a witch who could make a cart drive into a pit. Then nothing whatsoever could get the cart free again.
187805: A man who had to roam as a werewolf with a bearskin was sent one day to a remote place to do a little job. Meanwhile the oven was heated and the bearskin thrown into it. The skin had barely caught fire when the man came back sweating to save his skin. But it was already too late for that. The man was released.
187842: In Wulpen a boy had, against his better judgement, mocked a witch. The witch pelted the boy with burrs. When the boy came home, he felt unwell. Because his mother believed the boy was bewitched, she sent her son to the parish priest. "Superstition does not exist!" said the priest, but he did ask the boy to stand in front of him so that he could pray over him. The priest prayed until sweat ran down his forehead. When the boy left the priest's house, not a single burr was left on him.
187845: Some people believed that children could become bewitched after a witch had put feather grass in their mouth.
187848: In Poperinge lived a man who could send rats.
187858: One night a man shot at something that was jumping about among the red cabbages. The man had barely got back inside his house when something struck the door.
187861: A quack came to a married couple asking for shelter. The man took the stranger to a shed where a hen was sitting on a beam. When the man wanted to hit the hen with his stick, the stranger said: "You mustn't do that, because that is no hen." A little later the man looked back and saw that the hen was growing bigger and bigger.
187868: A woman who lived on a farm in Staden was always visited by her aunt, who came to fetch milk. One day the aunt no longer dared to come by; she was afraid that the former occupant of the house would come back to look for his money.
187910: One day three men and a woman went together to the fair in Heist. One of the men was always being hit by a strange woman who was walking about there. When the group went back home, that man heard a goat bleating near the Graafjansdijk. In the light of his bicycle lamp he also saw a black cat. Oddly enough, the others did not see the cat. The next day the others heard that the man had got lost in the meadow. Every week that man saw a black cat when he came back from the fair. The man went to the friars of Zevenkerke for advice. That cat was the woman who had hit him.
187921: Whoever was ridden by the mare felt someone pulling at their body at night without anyone being visible. Whoever wanted to protect themselves against the mare had to put their clogs upside down beside the bed or sprinkle salt on the threshold.
187925: A woman's youngest child had died after being bewitched. The baby had been given a blanket by a woman from the neighbourhood. When the blanket had been in the cradle for only a few hours, the child fell ill. In the end it died.
187943: On his way home, a man always had to cross the canal in a small boat. That man often saw a white calf walking over the dike. In the morning the calf was gone. The man believed it had something to do with witchcraft.
187946: A man gathering wood met the priest, who asked: "Why don't you go to vespers?" The man answered: "If I do that, all the wood will be gone by the time I get back." "You'll regret it," said the clergyman. The man got lost and had to walk around all night with the wood.
187952: A woman who was ridden by the mare in her sleep saw a man with a long beard squeezing her throat shut. After the woman got married, she was no longer ridden by the mare.
187953: The churchyard of Kuurne was haunted. By the two empty little houses that stood there, people saw a glow of light above the graves every evening. Those were returned dead.
187958: When a woman had died in Vichte, a little light was seen moving back and forth above the house. That was a sign that the dead woman had not arrived safely. The people then had masses said for the deceased woman.
187973: A fisherman often passed the house of a witch. If the witch was standing against the front of her house at that moment, the fisherman would catch nothing that day.
187980: A witch could make it so that people could not get past her house. At least, that was what people believed, because in reality it was nothing but superstition.
187982: A man worked on a large farm in Anzegem. Because it was raining hard one day, the farmer's wife said: "You shouldn't go home. Just stay the night here. You can sleep in the loft with the other farmhand. If he is ridden by the mare, you must slap him in the face." When the farmhand grew restless, the man did what the farmer's wife had advised. But the same thing happened again every day. In the end that farmhand succumbed to the torment. It was believed that one could protect oneself against the mare by putting one's clogs upside down and by using Easter nails. The friars said prayers over the farm until they were completely drenched in sweat, but it did not help.
187989: A woman whose husband always had to go haunting with a bearskin decided to burn the skin when her husband had to go to Holland one day. The skin had barely caught fire when the man came running through hedges and bushes to save his skin. But it was already too late. The man then thanked his wife because he was released.
188011: A parish priest visiting a witch in Westkapelle said: "It is fine weather!" The witch replied: "Yes, if only it lasts! Make sure you get home quickly!" Because of the witch, the priest had to go home through the ditches. When he got home, the priest was drenched in sweat, and on top of that it began to rain very hard.
188016: A farmer who could no longer make butter and whose pigs all died was married to a woman who could bewitch. When that woman passed a farm on her way to high mass, the pigs there could not be held. The farmer resolved to bash the woman's head in the next time. The following Sunday, however, the woman was ill, so she could not go to mass. The woman died shortly afterwards.
188041: On the Dries in Avelgem there was a place where nobody dared to build a house because a horse always roamed there. The horse belonged to nobody. Often the horse was invisible and only the trampling of hooves could be heard.
188048: A woman came to the little chapel of Zande to pray a novena. The woman said a decade of the rosary, then went round the chapel praying, and then said another decade on her knees. At a certain moment the woman saw a priest sitting next to her. When the woman went round the chapel, the priest stood up. When the woman knelt, the priest did the same. Although the woman grew frightened, she still prayed the whole rosary. When the woman went home, she saw the priest following her on the inside of the hedge around the church. When she got home, the woman looked through the window above the door. She saw the silent priest standing there.
188057: In De Klitte lived an old woman who was avoided by everyone because people suspected she was a witch. Farmers did not dare walk past the witch's house with their pigs or rabbits; the pigs would jump over the cart and the rabbits would become barren...
188063: A maid who worked in Gijverinkhove and who was ridden by the mare every night went one day to the doctor in Beveren. When the maid asked the doctor whether the mare really existed, the man answered: "Yes, it exists."
188068: The shop of a widow in Knesselare used to be haunted. In the evening the women came to the widow's to spin. But there was always something wrong with the spinning wheels. On one the bobbin would not turn, on another the wheel would not turn. A man who was afraid of nothing went to take a look in the house one day. When the wheel again would not turn, the man jabbed his 'kruldre' (?) into it. A little later the lights went out and the tiles in the house were torn up. Terrified, the man ran away.
188075: Two men went to ring the church bells on a Sunday morning in winter. Suddenly the pair saw a large dog appear, which followed them and did them harm. The hedge of the churchyard opened and the dog disappeared. After the dog had disappeared, doodkaarsen (death candles, ghost lights) danced on the hedge.
