The following Saturday exactly the same thing happened. The men believed they were the spirits of the dead.
188079: On a little lane a man with a note in his mouth appeared at night. The priest advised the people to take the letter and say: "But I wish to live." That ghost was said to have been a priest who had received money but had never said the masses.
188081: A woman whose daughter was about to give birth to twins stuck a nail from an Easter candle under the gate. As a result a witch from the neighbourhood could no longer come in. When the mother came back inside, she saw that her daughter's two babies had been born healthy. The witch had previously been holding back the birth.
188084: In some houses the doors flew open and shut at night. At midnight all kinds of noises could be heard, as if a strong wind were blowing. When paasnagels (Easter nails) were stuck under the door, the sorcerers could no longer get in.
188093:
At the 'Droge Boom' (Dry Tree) in Waregem there once lived a little man with a black beard. The man also had dark eyes that no one dared look into for longer than ten seconds. People believed that this man had made a pact with the devil. One evening the forester had seen a dark figure with a cock under its arm creeping through the woods. The forester had followed the figure to a crossroads where five roads met. There a black gentleman with a pointed beard appeared, who took out a piece of white parchment and pulled a feather from the wing of the black cock. The little man bared his arm and signed the contract with his own blood. At that moment the moon had come out from behind the clouds and the forester had recognised the little man. The forester ran away in fear and found that his hair had turned completely grey. From that day on the little man had a galgenjong (a devil's familiar, literally 'gallows child') that gave him special powers. On the man's neck there was a small red mark where he drew blood to give to the galgenjong.
One day a farmer in the village stood cursing because his horses could not manage to bring a load of wood to the farmyard. The little man appeared, took over the reins, and a moment later the horses moved off effortlessly. The farmer had seen that when eating, the little man poured his first spoonful of porridge onto the table and placed his first potato beside his plate. Only sorcerers did that. When one of the farmhands had warts on his hand, the little man rubbed the hand and made the warts disappear by the next day.
When the little man came into a café one day, an organ suddenly began to play in the attic, and the chairs around the café began to dance. In no time all the customers left the café. Whenever the little man sat down somewhere, the chair could always be heard creaking loudly.
When the man lay dying, a terrible thunderstorm broke out. Although the priest claimed that he did not believe the talk of sorcery, he had still gathered a few brave men to keep watch by the man's coffin on the last night. The four men played a game of cards to pass the time. At the stroke of midnight the dead man's cat suddenly became very restless. The men put down their cards, whereupon a loud bang shook the house and sent the cards flying into the air. The wall clock and all the bottles in the house fell to pieces. A menacing rushing sound was also heard, like the flapping of wings. That same night the priest came to exorcise the house. The next day people said that the devil had come at midnight to fetch the man's soul. At the man's funeral the coffin was full of mice.
To this day the road by that man's house has a bend, because out of fear people always gave the house a wide berth.
188099: A drunkard coming home in the evening was dragged through the water by a sow with piglets. When the man regained consciousness, there was nothing to be seen anymore.
188112: A man did not believe that someone could get lost through witchcraft. A friend of his, who had experienced it himself, replied: "Just wait until you have to walk around all night!" That night the man kept walking back and forth in the street where he lived.
188115: In Dudzele there once lived a woman who went round people's homes repairing sewing machines. Some people whose sewing machine was broken sent for the woman. Although the fault was easy to fix, the witch did not manage to repair the machine. As soon as the witch was outside, the machine was repaired in no time.
188126: A man had seven children who all suffered misfortune. Two sons were kept in Aartrijke because they were mad, one son walked on crutches, one daughter had smallpox scars, another had to wear special shoes and two daughters were mad. The children had all been bewitched by a woman from the neighbourhood.
188143: In Houtkerke a cat roamed about, running between people's legs. It was suspected that a witch from the village had sent that cat.
188163: In the little wood by the Wulfsputten in Wielsbeke, a little light moved from one tree to another at midnight. People said that the mother of Minne G. was making her dead husband swirl through the air that way. That man had been dead for years.
188167: Sometimes a burning candle was put in a clog. When that happened, someone would die.
188168: Every night a man was pulled upwards by his beard. The clergy believed that a sorcerer from the village was responsible for the evil, but the sorcerer claimed that his neighbour woman was to blame. He was right.
188171: A man who liked a drink and often went to play cards was followed on his way home one evening by a white cat that kept getting under his feet. The man kicked at the cat but could not hit the animal. When he got home, the man found that his toe was broken. The man was in the habit of sleeping in the shed so as not to wake his mother and sister. But because the cat sat down on the threshold of the shed, the man was so frightened that he went to call his mother.
188176: A man visiting his girlfriend was constantly pestered by a black cat that rubbed against his legs. The man never managed to kick the animal. One day, however, he did hit the cat. The next day the man met an old woman wearing a large shawl around her head. People said to the little woman: "It's your own fault. You shouldn't go eavesdropping on young people!"
188181: If the farmers could not churn butter after an old woman had passed by, people believed that woman was to blame for the misfortune. They would then have the milk prayed over by the parish priest.
188204:
In Noordschote lived a farmer who had a deaf-mute son. One day the parish priest had said to the farmer: "One day that son will be a great comfort to you!" When the farmer was eighty-four, he indeed had only his deaf-mute son left to keep him company.
When some people were building a barn one Sunday, the same priest had said: "You must never work during high mass. Everything you build then will burn down in the next thunderstorm." What the priest had predicted did come true.
One day when that priest was out walking, someone said to him: "Look, here comes the black one again!", to which the priest replied: "You will stay sitting on that chair until I come back!" The man who had mocked the clergyman indeed could not get up from his chair before then.
188218: A woman had stolen a flower from the curate's garden. At night the woman could not sleep because the mare rode her. Her bed slid from one side of the room to the other. In the end the woman had to go and beg the curate's forgiveness on her bare knees.
188228: On All Saints' Day people were afraid because spirits wandered about then. A girl who had to run an errand on All Saints' Day saw the outline of a person on the stairs. The girl screamed "Murder!" and quickly ran into a house. It was probably a ghost or else Lucifer. When the other people went to look, there was nothing more to be seen. That is as true as Our Lord is in the Mass.
188242: A witch lived next to a farm in Donk. When the witch came one day to ask for twelve eggs, the farmer's wife could give her none, which made the witch angry. The farmer's wife went to fetch twelve eggs at another farm. When she got home, however, she found that the eggs were all rotten.
188246: A woman always heard something ringing when she walked over a little bridge.
188248: A man who had kicked a cat at around two o'clock at night fell ill. That man never knew a healthy hour again.
188252: In the old days people often believed that children had gotten 'de oude man' (the old man, a wasting illness) or had been stuck with pins through the doing of a witch. In reality the children simply fell ill from poverty or neglect.
188254: People who were ridden by the mare during a dream suddenly saw a white apparition before them. They felt the mare at their feet and could hardly breathe.
188274: A maid taking eggs to market met a woman on the way who wanted to buy some eggs. The maid, however, refused to sell anything to that woman. A little further on the handle of the basket broke, and all the eggs fell to the ground and smashed. "If you had sold them to me, that would not have happened!" the woman then said.
188289: A woman who heard ticking in the cupboard concluded that someone in the family would die. And so it happened.
188305: A woman who had gone to fetch a bucket of water had only ten steps to walk back to her house. When the woman got home, she noticed that the bucket was bone dry. The woman went to fetch water again, but when she came back the bucket was empty once more. The same thing happened at least three times.
188315:
A mother had a little child that cried all the time. A cat often came near the child. When one day the mother found that the child's nappy was full of pins, she went to the priest for advice. The priest asked whether strangers ever came into the house, and the mother told him about the cat. The priest advised the woman to pour hot butter on the cat.
After the woman had done so, some children from the neighbourhood came to say that their mother had been burned.
188327: A woman had come to look at a litter of seven piglets. From then on strange things happened to the animals. Some piglets grew fat, others stayed thin. The piglets all broke their legs when they got onto the dung heap. The parish priest said he would name the witch by name, so that the misfortune would end.
188329: Death candles were little lights seen in the dark. Anyone who had seen a death candle would soon die.
188331: In the wood of Piers there was a bell pit in which bells were said to have once sunk.
188333: A man on his way to his girlfriend saw the branches of a hedge striking the ground along the way, although there was no wind.
188347: A woman who did not get on well with her husband sought advice from a clergyman. That clergyman made sure that the husband could not get home or go to sea when he was not with his wife. The man then saw lots of cockerels blocking his way. Other people, however, could not see the cockerels. As relations between the couple improved, the man was less troubled by this witchcraft.
188350: A man who said he was ridden by the mare was believed by no one. After all, the other people could not see the mare. The pigeons, however, did fly about restlessly in the pigeon loft.
188354: In 1913 a man saw a star with a particularly long tail in the sky. The man also witnessed a solar eclipse, which made the chickens go to sleep at midday. These were all omens of the war that was to come.
188369: A woman came to visit a farm, touched one of the horses and said: "Farmer, you have three fine horses!" The next morning one of the horses lay dead.
188371: The parish priest knew that seven witches lived in Alveringem. A fisherman who had a boat in Fortem had to shovel seven heaps of dung out of his vessel every day. To find out who was to blame, the fisherman decided to keep watch in his boat one night. During the night he saw seven women arrive who fouled his boat. He had recognised all seven witches, but he never dared to say their names. The priest did know that those seven women could bewitch, because during the consecration they sat with their backs to the altar. The clergyman demanded that the witches leave the children alone, or else he would make their names known.
188375: In Jabbeke lived a woman who could bewitch. Anyone who did business with that woman always found afterwards that he had been cheated. No one dared to walk past the witch's house in the evening, because the trees along the road struck passers-by with their branches.
188389: On a farm they could not churn butter because the maid had bewitched the milk.
188410: A baby of three or four months old cried all the time after the mother had shown it to a shopkeeper. The mother took her child to the friars of Westvleteren, who made the sign of the cross on the child's forehead. The baby had been bewitched by the shopkeeper.
188416: In the old days people sometimes said that witches owned dolls into which they stuck pins, but that was superstition.
188422: A woman had come to a farm to fetch milk. The woman had been in the cellar and had left a scrap of cloth there. The farmer and his wife had removed the scrap, but they could no longer churn butter. After the friars had blessed the butter churn, the problem was solved.
188432: During the war a man went pear picking to earn some money. During the break the man smoked a pipe. When he knocked out his pipe, however, it broke. A witch sitting nearby then said: "What's wrong? Has your pipe broken? Never mind, I have another one at home." A little later a dirty old pipe was brought for the man, already completely burnt on the inside. Because the man found the pipe far too dirty to use, he put it under his chair. When he left he did take the pipe with him, but on the way he threw it as far as he could into the woods. When the witch saw during the next break that the man did not have his pipe with him, she said: "What's the matter? Have you lost your pipe?", and the man said yes. "Never mind," the witch went on, "I have another one." Then the man was given exactly the same pipe as the one he had thrown away.
188435:
Flat twigs were twigs that had been ridden by the mare.
People who were ridden by the mare felt the mare at their toes.
188437: A woman going to Brugge met a witch on the way, who said: "Well, it is fine weather now!" and tapped her briefly on the shoulder. Although the woman knew Brugge well, she got lost, so that she did not get home that day.
188445: On a farm where they could no longer make butter and where the cows were tied to the beams by their tails, a small chapel was built.
188453: A farm in Westkerke was haunted. At night all the windows and doors there stood open. The grain was mixed up and the animals lay dead in the stable. People said that the farmer who had once lived there came to haunt on his horse.
188472: In the woods between Egem and Wingene lay the Tenteknok, where many lanes came together. One day the man fell over something hairy there that had no head and no legs. The man began to beat the figure, which then ran off into the woods cursing and raging.
188477: A man who heard all kinds of noises around midnight, including the turning of the mill, got up. When the man went to look in the barn, everything went quiet as a mouse again. When the man went to look behind the stable, he came across a dog with a chain. The man stayed outside for an hour because the dog kept blocking his way. After a long while the man managed to get back to his bedroom. In the moonlight it looked as if a woman were lying in the man's bed. As soon as a cloud passed in front of the moon, however, the woman was gone. When the man was back in his bed, a good ten thousand rats crawled over him. The next morning the farmer and his wife turned out to have heard nothing. The man was in the habit of laying his clothes at the foot of his bed. In the morning the man found his clothes in the bakehouse. The rats had dragged the clothes there.
188489: In the Stienoventje (a wood in Meulebeke) there was a hare that nobody could shoot. One day a man went to a priest to have two bullets blessed. When the man fired the blessed bullets, he again missed the hare. But a scream like that of a human could be heard.
188491: A woman was always tormented at night by a witch who came and lay on top of her. To prevent this, one had to put a shoe upside down under one's bed. Others claimed that one had to lay a knife on one's chest, because the mare would then wound herself when she came. When the woman had done that, she found the next day that her neighbour was sitting dead in her armchair.
188492: In a house along the Bruges-Ostend canal an old woman lived with her married daughter. People suspected that the old woman was a sorceress, because her daughter's three children had died of the kwade hand (the evil hand, bewitchment). Moreover, many farmers in Varsenare could not churn butter. One day the old woman was walking through the village with a farmer's wife. Because the farmer's wife wanted to find out things about witchcraft, she said to the woman: "Listen, they are churning butter here!" The woman answered: "Let them, they will never get butter anyway!" At that very moment a black cat ran to the farm where they were churning. Because the farmer could not churn butter, he said: "The witch has gone to market with the butter!"
188494: Along a cart track stood a house with a gate. The man who had lived in that house had died. One evening the dead man was seen leaning on the gate of his house with his arms crossed. A passer-by greeted the man, but there was no answer.
188505: At the Zeveneeke in a wood in Anzegem, seven roads came together. That place used to be haunted. At a certain hour of the night, little lights and floating people who could not be touched appeared there.
188510: In Rumbeke a child had fallen ill after an old woman had come to visit. The people went on pilgrimage for the child and received a medal from the friars. After that the old woman never came into the house again.
188524: In Zerkegem lived a man who could send rats to houses. The sorcerer always made the rats come back again, because he needed them himself.
188531: A young girl was raised by her godmother. After the girl's uncle had died, fire was seen in the room at night. When masses had been said, the fire no longer appeared.
188539: Doodkeersen (death candles, ghost lights) were spirits of dead people who came back to haunt.
188544: Will-o'-the-wisps were the souls of people who had not kept a promise. One had to fulfil the promise in their place.
188548: A man had rats in his cellar that drank all the milk. One day the man sent the rats away to a woodpile. The animals never came back.
188555: A woman who owned books of magic bewitched the sheep in the meadow so that they became skin and bone and stood stock-still.
188577: A woman could not leave the church because the priest had left the gospel open after mass. After that, people began using the Gospel of Saint John.
188623: Two men had agreed that whoever died first would come and tell the other after his death what things were like in the hereafter. When one of the men had died, the other heard a voice saying: "There is nothing here, but there is nothing there either. But those who have to push / carry the wheelbarrow here must drag it there."
188630: When a farm had a lot of misfortune with its livestock, it was often attributed to the kwade hand (the evil hand, malicious witchcraft).
188643: A man saw something like a white sheet or a cloud drifting about near the Vléruskot. People said those were souls for whom you had to pray a great deal.
188645: The Graafjansdijk was haunted. Many people saw strange things there, but nobody knew exactly what he had seen.
188683: A boy was going out with the daughter of a witch. One day, when the boy had taken his girlfriend home, he stayed outside the house listening to what the girl's mother was saying. Suddenly the mother said: "You just go home, boy! It will be long enough before you get home!" The boy got lost and walked around all night in 't Magere Schone (a neighbourhood in Knokke).
188692: In Pittem there was a farm that was rented to a flax merchant with his wife and children. Because the wife was away from home day and night, the owner of the farm grew angry and said: "You are never home! Your children are always playing with the stable lantern! A fire could easily start!" At that the woman flew into a rage and made to scratch the farmer's eyes out. The farmer ran off in fear and was convinced that the woman was a witch. One morning the witch came to a farmer from the village to fetch a kilo of butter. When the witch had gone, the little child lying in the cradle fell ill. The child had blue spots all over its little back and in the end it died. The next day the witch came to look at the dead child. Witches, after all, always came to look at the harm they had done. One day a man stood at the side of the road tending his cows. When the witch passed by, the cows went wild and ran off. A little further on the witch stood laughing.
188696: A quack who was often out in the evenings was returning one evening from a farm where he had gone to tend an animal. On the way, the man saw two altar boys with bells and candles in a wood. The man stood still, terrified, until the altar boys had disappeared. Then he went to look, but he found only a hole. The man decided to go back to the farm he had come from. At that moment the man was thrown flat on his back and saw nothing more.
188712: A woman was ridden by the mare in her sleep. As soon as someone spoke the woman's name, the mare was gone.
188717: People who had not kept a vow came back after their death in the form of a knocking spirit. The knocking went on until someone else had fulfilled the vow.
188734: A man began to scream loudly in his sleep at night, so that his wife had to wake him. As soon as the woman said the man's name, he stopped screaming. After the man had put his clogs under his bed heels first, he was no longer ridden by the mare.
188744: A witch had said to a farmer: "You will never be able to churn butter". The witch's prediction came true.
188770: A café keeper from Poperinge had a little daughter. When a sorceress came to fetch milk one day, she gave the café keeper's daughter a piece of chocolate. The child eagerly gobbled up the chocolate. The next day, however, the girl fell ill; she lay down and could no longer move. The mother took the child to the fathers of Saint-Jex, who read prayers over the poor girl until the sweat dripped from their faces. But none of it helped. The child refused to eat or drink and often had foam on her lips. A few days later the mother took her child to the fathers a second time, but this time too it was of no avail. After a few days the child quietly began to move again. In this way the child slowly recovered from this strange affliction. Until she was nine, however, the girl was often ill. One day the sorceress's husband won first prize at the shooting in the café. The man went to fetch his wife to have a drink in the café. Strangely enough, the sorceress could not get into the café. The sick child's mother had, after all, been given medals by the fathers to place under the threshold. The sorceress never again got into the house where the sick girl lived. When the sorceress had died, magic books with which she could do harm were found in her house.
188775: In Heulendonk a phantom goat with bells always roamed about.
188777: Whoever was ridden by the mare was in reality suffering from a standstill of the blood. A man was always ridden by the mare when he slept on his right side. The man then felt as if someone was grabbing him by the neck. To protect oneself against the mare, one had to place one's clogs crossed next to each other, so that the two outer sides of the clogs touched.
188778: Near the 'spokkelbosselke' (?) a headless horse always roamed at night.
188779: A sorceress from Loppem could pour eggs from one basket into another without a single egg breaking. The sorceress had the finest fruit in the whole region. She often gave a village child a piece of fruit. Because the parents were afraid of the sorceress, they threw the fruit away just to be safe. The parish priest advised the villagers not to have anything to do with the sorceress. In a court case the sorceress lost her land, which was awarded to the church. As a result the sorceress and her children became desperately poor.
188785: Two hunters had often tried to shoot at a fleeing hare, but they had never managed to hit the animal. One day the parish priest advised the hunters to shoot at the hare with a half-franc coin. When the hunters had done so, they found that their neighbour had lost his leg.
188799:
At a Templar farm in Ruddervoorde, someone pulled a bundle of wood out of the woodpile. This took so much effort that in the end the whole woodpile was pulled over. At that moment hand-clapping was heard. 
There was also a shed in which all the animals died. Under that shed was a cellar that no one dared to enter.
188818: Near Beselare lived a woman who was not allowed near small children, because people were afraid the children would be bewitched. Bewitched children had to have prayers read over them by the fathers of Ieper.
188832: At a walled farm between Aalbeke and Marke a horse always appeared, although the gate was shut. Some claimed it was a horse with a rider; according to others it was a horse with a cart.
188836: In Knesselare a sorceress went about who wanted to do people harm. One day the Duitse Schaper (German Shepherd) wanted to put the devil on the sorceress. But when the witch blew on a whistle, the Duitse Schaper's sheep began to dance.
188842: Some children had been given a sweet by a woman. Because people said that the woman was a witch, the children did not dare to eat the sweet. That woman's husband was incapable of anything and sat in his house all day. People claimed that the woman had bewitched her own husband.
188861: A girl had rejected the boyfriend she had been in a relationship with. But the boyfriend still had a neckerchief of the girl's, which allowed him to harm her. Every evening at seven o'clock the girl heard footsteps on the stairs, although only a shadow could be seen. All the people from the neighbourhood came to watch the girl fight the invisible boy. One day they set fire to a handkerchief and a corset full of needles. That did not help, however. After the priest had read prayers over the girl, the invisible boy could get no further than the top step of the stairs. Then they went to the boy's house and took the girl's handkerchief away. After that the boy could no longer harm her.
188866: A learned doctor from Wijtschate could bewitch people so they were fixed to the ground. Thus by the canal the doctor made three people stand still until he let them go again.
188900: A man could make mice by blowing on little balls of clay.
188911: In Wevelgem one evening a house had inexplicably caught fire. Not far from that house lived a sorceress. The parish priest came to the scene and made the wind turn, so that the fire went out. When the clergyman got up the next day, his hair was snow-white. The witch had caused this because she was jealous of the priest's magic power.
188924:
People who were ridden by the mare could be freed by calling their name.
When a cow was ridden by the mare, people sometimes poured water over the animal. Afterwards a woman could be seen sitting on the cow.
188931: In a house where the aunt had died, the daughter had to sleep in the aunt's room. Because the girl always heard noises in the cupboard at night, she no longer wanted to sleep in that room. The parish priest, together with the fathers, drove the spirit out of the cupboard.
188934: People who slept on their back could be ridden by the mare. If one could just manage to turn over onto one's stomach, one was saved.
188940: Two butchers were coming back from a farmer in Sint-Michiels at around eleven in the evening. On the way the butchers got lost, so that at three in the morning they were standing at the farmer's again. "Are you here again?" said the farmer. "Hurry on home!" That time the butchers fortunately did get home.
188952: A little boy was walking outside when a neighbour woman came up to him. Because that woman was not trusted, the boy was brought inside. When the mother saw the child, she said: "What is wrong with that boy? He is so limp!" The doctor was consulted, but he could not make a diagnosis. The fathers held a mass for the child and advised the people to pray at midday before the meal. The people also had to hang a relic above the door. If the child's condition did not improve, they each had to pray three Hail Marys and burn candles. The fathers also said: "The person you suspect will not come again for a long time". When the people got home, the little boy already felt much better. After that the neighbour never came inside again. She always stayed standing by the door and in the end went mad.
188954: At a crossroads in Beveren-Leie stood a farm where spools could always be heard turning from evening till morning.
188983: A woman who was ridden by the mare was frightened and screamed the whole time. As soon as someone called the woman's name, she was freed. A cowherd who was ridden by the mare began to foam at the mouth as soon as he got into bed.
189004: A farmer sitting in his horse stable on Christmas Day heard the horses say that they would take their master to the churchyard that very year. The farmer was very frightened when he heard this.
189008: A maid was frying potatoes while the farmer's wife went to the market. Meanwhile a big cat came in, and the maid struck the animal with the red-hot pan. When the farmer's wife came back from the market, she was burned all over.
189011: Strange things happened at a farm between Houthulst and Klerken. When the people were lying in bed at night, they heard a fierce gust of wind. In the morning the rapeseed and linseed lay on the dung heap.
189013: A farmer had died in Meulebeke. Some girls from the neighbourhood who went to the five o'clock early Mass on Sunday saw the dead farmer appear. The girls told the parish priest why they no longer dared go to Mass. After the curate had read prayers over the street, the ghost no longer appeared.
189028: A shopkeeper was visited by her nephew, who was a parish priest. When the woman asked her nephew to cure her pigs, the priest began to pray until he was drenched in sweat and said: "A woman will come to the shop here. You must send her away". After that was done, there were no more problems with the animals.
189029: A woman who saw a little light burning by a tree claimed that a heap of money was hidden there.
189074: On a farm in Heule worked Duitse schapers (German shepherds, travelling shepherds said to have magic powers) who were distrusted by the villagers. The shepherds always went to the café on Sunday morning. They were also clairvoyant. Every Sunday the shepherds wore a clean seamless shirt, without anyone knowing where they had got it. In the café some men had laughed at the German shepherds. The shepherds had not become angry, but they had said: "Tomorrow you'll be crying!" The next day all the glasses in the café were filled with muck from the cesspit. There was a note with them that read: "Keep quiet or we'll be here again tomorrow!" But the people could not keep the incident to themselves. The next day they stood ready with pistols in hand. At around twelve o'clock the doors flew open without a sound. The pistols did not work; the bullets all fell to the ground. The people then begged for mercy, whereupon the German shepherds vanished like ghosts.
189091: In Koningsheim a child had fallen ill through the doing of a witch. The witch stuck pins into a cushion to torment the child.
189097: When a man's body was being taken to the church by wagon, the dead man's mother was not ready yet. "Let them leave," the mother said, however, "I'll catch up with them. They won't get far, because they'll end up in the ditch." The wagon did indeed overturn in the ditch. When the witch arrived, she said: "You may go on."
189112: A nun going to church in the morning saw on the way something black that bowed down to the ground. Although she did not really know what it could be, the nun said good day. The parish priest said to the nun: "You must no longer go out before five o'clock. Those are souls who did something wrong during the war. You must leave them alone when it is still so early."
189115: At the castle there was a haunted tower where music could be heard at night.
189119: A priest made someone walk around all night with a beam on his back. The poor man could not get the beam off his back.
189136: Some men cycled to the pine wood to shoot wood pigeons. When the men arrived in the wood around two or three o'clock, they saw nothing but pigeons, stock doves and Spanish pigeons hanging on the branches. The first man to shoot missed. The second missed too. However hard the men tried, they could not hit a single pigeon. When the men walked on, they saw an old woman in a hooded cloak sitting a little further along the lane, who asked: "Well, lads, have you caught anything?" The men answered: "No, there are plenty, but we can't hit them. But if you weren't here, it would certainly go better." At that the woman went away. After the witch had left, the men were able to shoot a few pigeons. It was she who had been sitting in the trees.
189141: Some men going to evening school in Knesselare in the evening were accompanied the whole time by a whining cat that got under their feet. One of the men was annoyed by the animal and threatened to kick the cat. His friends strongly advised him against it. After a while the man had had enough anyway and kicked the animal over the hedge.
189143: A farmer had to go to Brugge with some horses. At de Munten a cat suddenly ran between the horses' legs, singing: "X asked me, sweet proud kitty, where are you going?" The farmer demanded that the cat leave the horses alone and threatened to strike it with his whip. Because the cat did not go away, the farmer lashed out with his whip, and the animal rolled over the ground. A little further on the farmer saw a light by the side of the road. He went into the house and saw a woman with a wound on her head. The person bandaging the woman's head said to the farmer: "You're lucky you used holy water this morning. We can't harm you. Otherwise you'd have had something coming!"
189156: In the old days, if you saw rabbits in a dark meadow, you could be sure the animals were really witches.
189161: A man who lived in Oekerke near the French border had an eight-month-old child. One day a clergyman had to be called because the child was full of lice. The clergyman said to the people: "The culprit is a woman. She will never cross your threshold again." From that day on there was indeed a woman who never came to visit any more. One day the man and his wife went to her and said: "When are you coming to visit again?" When that woman came by, she could not reach the door and said she had to go back. The child died afterwards because its little clothes, which were full of lice, had been burned.
189166: A priest from West Flanders could do magic. For example, he could make mice come out of the coffee pot.
189167: A family driving home in a carriage with a newly baptised child fell victim to a witch who made the carriage overturn. The baby lay in the ditch and, remarkably, was unharmed.
189173:
During his sermon a parish priest said to his parishioners: "At this moment two thieves are stealing my cherries." After mass the priest saw the two thieves standing as if nailed to the ground. They each had a cherry in their hand but could not bring it to their mouths. Only when the priest allowed it could the thieves move again.
One day a pair of lovers was standing by the priest's house. The clergyman opened his window and ordered the lovers to leave. "We'll stand here as long as we like!" the two replied. The priest made sure the two lovers had to stay standing there until morning.
Because the priest had mocked the town council, he had to spend some time in prison. To a woman who testified for him, the priest said: "You will live a long and happy life." The woman lived to 97.
When a woman had lost her money and went to tell the priest, the clergyman said to her: "Just go back home. In three days the money will be lying in the drain of your house." And so it was.
189176: Two men coming back from a party met, between Veurne and Koksijde, the ghost of the chaplain who had drowned in Koksijde.
189189: A woman whose child would not grow sent for a father and told the clergyman that an old woman often came to visit her. "You must not believe in such evil", the father had said. A while later the woman went to the Oostveld, where the sisters gave her an Easter nail to put in the cradle. After that was done, the child soon recovered.
189199: Whoever was ridden by the mare in bed tried to call for help, but no sound came out.
189205: Because her eight-month-old child cried all the time, a mother went to the friars to have the child overlezen (read over with prayers). The mother had barely left when her child died. The friars tried to comfort the mother by saying: "The child has suffered a great deal, for it is full of copper pins. It cannot be any higher than in heaven."
189216: During the war a man stayed at the Flèruskot near Wilskerke. A German shepherd named 'Flèrus' worked there. When the shepherd was dismissed, he said: "Flèrus leaves and so does the luck!" The next day the farm was full of rats.
189222: A carter coming home with his cart saw a goat standing by the way. The carter tied the goat to his cart and drove on. The goat, however, kept growing bigger and bigger, so that the carter became so frightened that he ran home without his cart.
189227:
A farmer and his wife were coming home at night with horse and cart. At a certain moment the horse stood still because it had seen a ghost. Animals could perceive ghosts because they had no soul of their own to save.
A farmer passing the little chapel of Our Lady at night heard a rustling in the trees. The farmer took off his cap and began to pray. The man said: "Dear Lady, I will pray here for whatever you ask of me. If you are sent by God, speak. If you are sent by the devil, then in God's name go back where you came from!" When the man had spoken those words, he went on mowing. The rustling was still there and sounded much louder. In the end the man went home drenched in sweat. When the man told the parish priest what he had experienced, the clergyman said: "You must never do that again!" The clergyman knew that all kinds of evil roamed that place.
189230: If someone had done something wrong, the parish priest made sure that person could not get up from his chair after mass.
189247: When people bringing in the harvest met a certain woman, they were told: "Watch out, or you won't get home before your cart has tipped over." A few metres further on, the cart really did tip over.
189252: A woman who was said to be able to work magic got lost near a certain farm. The woman could go no further and turned back. Shortly afterwards the farmer's child fell ill, so that it had to have prayers read over it by the fathers. The fathers did not take such things seriously, but they read prayers over the child all the same.
189257: A woman from Zuienkerke had a son who had been shot dead. The woman's sister had to clean the room where the son was laid out. The sister fell ill and promised to have a mass said. Since then the sister always heard noises at night. The lid of the coffee pot moved up and down all night. After eight or twelve days the sister went to the priest, who asked: "Have you ever promised anything?" To that the sister answered: "Yes, I promised to have a mass said." After the woman had had the promised mass said, she heard no more strange noises.
189259: In a house by the Brugge-Gent canal there were eighteen children. An old woman regularly came to that house. Every time that old woman had visited, the children began to cry. The Benedictine friars advised the children's father not to let that woman in anymore, because she owned a little wax doll whose head she turned backwards. Because of this the children in the house felt pain and began to cry. One day the people were visited by a doctor who travelled by horse and cart. The witch bewitched the horse, so that it reared backwards, fell into the canal and drowned.
189260: Two farmers' daughters from Kemmel, all dressed up and on their way to a wedding, met a German shepherd on the way. "Good day, ladies," the shepherd said as usual, but this time he got no answer. A little further on the girls were full of lice, so there was nothing for it but to turn back. When the girls passed the shepherd again, he said: "Next time you could at least say good day when you meet someone! Go on now, those lice will go away again."
189283: In Zevekote lived a sorceress whom everyone feared. A man who was visiting that sorceress ate a little waffle. That night the man fell ill. That man later became an odd fellow.
189291: In Ardooie lived an old woman suspected of being a witch. Whenever a child was born somewhere, it died almost immediately after birth. When one day the old woman again wanted to go and see a newborn child, the father would not let her in. The woman then walked off angrily. After that incident a mouse always ran around the child's cradle. People caught the mouse and threw the animal into the stove. The next day the little old woman lay dead in her bed. She had died of her burns.
189308: In Gistel a witch went out walking every day. All the mothers were afraid of that witch, because whenever the witch came near a child, she would say: "What a beautiful child" and try to touch it. If she succeeded, the child began to cry. Children who had fallen victim to that witch had to have prayers read over them by the dean. For many years people tried to put a stop to that witch, but they never succeeded.
189313: A man who saw a comet in the sky predicted that a war would come. He was proved right.
189320: A witch had bewitched a woman from Poperinge. That woman's house was full of toads and frogs.
189340: A man and a woman who were walking in the wood of Brugge suddenly saw a house that had never stood there before. When the people touched the latch to enter the house, the building suddenly vanished.
189349: A man who had been sent away by a farmer when he asked for alms took some tobacco and made mice out of it, which ran around the farm.
189350: A gentleman who had a black cat found it strange that all his relatives were dying. When only the man's maid was still alive, he sent for the priest. During the clergyman's visit the cat grew restless and its hair stood on end. Finally the priest said to the man: "The devil has come in here. You must get rid of that cat, or you will die too!" At a certain moment the cat ran off screaming. The man and his maid stayed alive.
189367: A man was startled when at a crossroads a goose suddenly jumped onto his shoulder. The goose was so heavy that the man came home dead tired and was ill for a long time afterwards.
189378: A mother and father went to the Barnabites in Moeskroen for their sick daughter. The fathers told the parents that a neighbour woman was responsible for their child's illness. Once the people had placed a relic under the threshold, that neighbour only came in through the back door.
189382: A farmer's wife from Winnezele had bought a new bonnet. The farmer's wife had died before she had paid for the bonnet. Because the farmer always heard noises in the bonnet's box, he went to the bonnet maker, from whom he learned that the bonnet had not yet been paid for. After the farmer had paid for his late wife's bonnet, he heard no more strange noises.
189391: A veterinarian met a thief, who demanded money from him. "I only have five francs," said the vet, and he gave his money to the thief. But the thief was bewitched so he was fixed to the ground, so that when the vet came back, he begged to be allowed to return the money.
189399: A stable hand who had to go somewhere met a witch, who looked at the animals with a strange gaze. The horses were terrified and very restless.
189406: On a farm where they could no longer make butter, they sent for the friars. The clergymen said a prayer over the butter churn and then advised the farmer to clean the churn. After the farmer had done so, a big spider crawled out of the churn. After that they could churn butter on the farm again without any problems.
189416: A man had gone to play cards in a café. On his way home the man had to cross a little wooden bridge. At that spot, however, the man was tormented by cats that clung to his leg. Because of this the man fell into the water. He had to walk a good two hundred metres through the brook before he was rid of those cats. The innkeeper's wife had caused this torment.
189423: In Blankenberge lived a sorceress who could bewitch children. A pregnant woman said to that sorceress: "Just stay away from me, because you can do more than eat sandwiches!" When that woman's baby was three months old, it fell ill. When the mother had prayers read over the child by the fathers of Steenbrugge, she was told that she would never be able to have children again.
189425: Whoever was ridden by the mare felt as if their throat was being squeezed shut by a person, often someone they knew who was suspected of witchcraft. One could then neither move nor call out. In reality the mare was a standstill of the blood.
189442: A mother had a good little child of nine months. The mother was often visited by a neighbour woman, who said: "You would never say you had a child!" The mother always had everyone stand around the cradle, so that the neighbour could not get to the child. One day, however, the neighbour managed to bewitch the child after all. After that the child cried without stopping. In the end the mother had to have prayers read over the child.
189470: A little boy was often ridden by the mare. When his mother went to call her son one morning to go to school, the boy stayed in bed because he was ill. The boy had seen a little man jump onto his bed and squeeze his throat shut. The boy was so frightened by this that his mother had to send for the doctor.
189490: A woman could turn herself into a hare or another animal.
189499: A farmer from Hoeke going home in the evening was followed by a big black dog with a chain around its neck. The farmer kicked at the dog several times, but the animal did not go away. When the farmer got home, the dog had suddenly disappeared.
189508: A man returning late in the evening from work was accompanied the whole way by a horse. The animal laid its head on the man's shoulders. When he got home, the man found that the horse had disappeared.
189553: A black cat always came into a woman's house. The friar advised the woman to pour hot pig fat over the cat while it was drinking milk. When the woman had done so, she found that one of her neighbours had a burned face. That neighbour could turn herself into a cat.
189571: A farm in Stalhille was haunted. When the people sat eating potatoes at noon, the cooking pot turned over by itself. The farmer's chickens also kept wandering about on someone else's farm, even after their wings had been tied together.
189575: Whoever was ridden by the mare had to put a willow branch in their bed. That branch would then be ridden flat by the mare.
189591:
't Kruise in Beveren was always haunted. A man who passed by there one day saw a white shape floating above the ground. The man was so frightened that he crawled into the ditch and said: "Creator, you must help me, or I'm done for!" 
The next moment the ghost had vanished.
189592: A man from Torhout going to Sint-Joris-ten-Distel at night was followed by a black cat. At a certain moment the man's wife said: "Did you feed that cat? I think she's hungry." At that the cat suddenly stood still. At that moment the man himself could not move a foot either.
189630: At a monastery farm in Elsegem a father was murdered by another brother. After the Augustinian fathers had moved to Gent, the place where the murder had been committed was haunted every night. It was Lange Jeanne who came to haunt there by the oak tree. After a crucifix with Our Lord had been hung in the tree, the haunting became much better.
189645: On a rainy Saturday the Sint-Jan procession could not take place. The next day it was seen that the statue of Our Lady was smeared with mud.
189650: The dead returned at night to the place where they had hidden money. If someone found the money, the dead person was released.
189659: A witch could make someone's washing fall to the ground without touching it.
189660: A little child went to a shop to buy suikerspek (a marshmallow-like sweet). When the child came outside with the sweets, it lay down on the ground and began to cry. Because the shopkeeper had given the child the evil hand, the father came to read prayers over the child.
189665: In a mill a man had chopped off a cat's paw. There turned out to be a wedding ring on the paw.
189684: When German shepherds were angry with someone, they made sure that person could no longer move.
189700: An old woman, said to be a sorceress, always came visiting at a farm. Some people claimed that the rooster on the farm was an incarnation of the sorceress. One day they caught the rooster and held the animal with its head over the fire. When the old woman came visiting again the next day, they saw that her face was completely burnt.
189702: Every evening a man saw a little light hovering beside an alder hedge. One evening the man lay down beside the hedge and pretended to be dead. The light began to tickle him and then took a steam boiler full of money out of the ground. The man watched the light begin to count the money. The man released the light.
189707: Whoever was ridden by the mare felt as if a sack of grain was lying on them. In reality those people were simply having a bad dream.
189712: One night the haunting white monks had disappeared. They were never seen again.
189725: A sorcerer who sold rat poison could send rats to a house and make the animals disappear again. One day a man had refused to buy rat poison because he had no rats. The sorcerer had replied: "But you will get some!" Some time later the man was indeed struggling with a plague of rats, so that he had to beg the sorcerer to make the animals disappear.
189726: In a house in Oostrozebeke the son had fallen ill. The parents went to the fathers of Tielt, who gave them a relic to put under the threshold. After that the witch never came into the house again.
189727: In Westrozebeke lived a carter who owned a carriage. At Easter some children came to ask the carter whether he would take their mother to church, because she could no longer walk well. The carter put the mother in the carriage and closed the doors. But when he arrived at the church, the woman had vanished from the carriage.
189744: People who had done something wrong ended up in purgatory after their death. Such dead often had to return. They would then burn their hand into the door to let their relatives know that they had to pray for them.
189754: To their great fright, some fishermen saw a group of singing clergymen pass by at night.
189758: A man who was gathering potatoes was annoyed by a big dog that kept getting under his feet. When the man went to strike the animal with his three-pronged fork, a woman from the neighbourhood suddenly stood before him.
189763: In Zillebeke lived people who had a great deal of misfortune. The children fell ill, the harvest failed and the animals did badly too. All that misfortune was caused by a woman who worked with magic books. Because nothing could be done about it, those people moved away from Zillebeke.
189772: One night a poacher from Sint-Michiels saw lots of little piglets crawling out of the brook. Wherever the poacher went, he ended up in the same place every time.
189813: A farmer lived next to a little old woman who also owned a piece of land. There were always sparrows on the farmer's field, while the neighbour was not troubled by them. People said that little woman could drive sparrows away.
189843: In the past people were very afraid of certain women who were taken for witches. Such women could, after all, cause children to die, people to lose their jobs or to have accidents.
189847: In Vichte lived a witch who could bewitch people so that they were stuck to the ground, and who could open and close windows and doors. The witch always did her witchcraft with a spider. When she left, she always left the spider behind, and the next day the child was ill. If the parish priest was not fetched quickly, the child would die.
189892: Sorceresses could get through anything. They could even crawl through the eye of a needle.
189898: A man on his way to work was knocked to the ground at a crossroads by the Westkant, although there was nothing to be seen. The same thing later happened a second time.
189906: At a farm butter was churned at night. All kinds of ghostly noises were heard, but in the morning there was nothing strange to be found.
189911: The dunes at Bredene were haunted. There was a well there that kept calling: "Water and milk!" A milk seller used to fetch water from that well to pour into the milk.
189916: A farmhand wearing brand-new trousers had to carry a sack of flour up to a sorceress's attic. When the farmhand came back down, his trousers were torn to shreds.
189937: In 1914 a man had seen a fireball flying from west to east. People said it was an omen of war. A short time later the First World War broke out.
189939: Some people who had a witch in their family fell victim to optical illusions. In those people's rabbit hutches, some saw pigs instead of rabbits. That woman was said to be responsible.
189946: If someone had a strange feeling during their sleep, people said that person had been ridden by the mare.
189953: In Beveren lived a sorceress who went out walking every night. When the farmers wanted to go to their fields at four in the morning, they could not get past the gate because the sorceress was lying on it.
189998: A woman had often visited her neighbour without any problems. One day, however, the woman began to feel oppressed while she was at her neighbour's. She had also often seen that neighbour in a dream. It got so bad that the woman no longer dared to stay home alone and went to stay with her sister. At her sister's the woman slept like a log, but as soon as she lay in her own bed, she felt oppressed again. The woman sent for a parish priest, who advised her to go to the fathers of Ieper. One of the fathers told the woman to pray a prayer of the cross in the chapel. "Witchcraft does exist, doesn't it?" the woman asked the father, to which he replied: "Yes, does it?" The father gave the woman three little rags with something inside. She had to hang those rags by her door, so that the culprit could no longer come in. One day when the woman was at her sister's, the neighbour came there. "You must come round to my place again", the woman said then. The neighbour accepted the invitation and got in without any problems. The woman went to the fathers again and was given the litany of Saint Theresa. She had to read that litany on nine Thursdays. From then on the neighbour ignored her completely. Whenever the woman walked past that house, the neighbour hurried inside. After those nine Thursdays the woman was never troubled again. Whenever the neighbour walked ahead of her and she crossed her footprints, the neighbour looked back.
190023: One evening a young man saw a figure moving along in the field.
190048: People who had neglected a vow had to return after their death to fulfil that vow after all. A dead man from Waregem appeared for nine consecutive days in the form of a white ghost. After that the ghost was seen no more, probably because the dead man had then fulfilled his vow.
190052: In Jabbeke lived a witch of whom the children were very afraid. When a woman lay dying in Snellegem, the witch was sent for because the woman simply could not die. The witch had barely left Snellegem when the woman was dead.
190058: On a farm where they had many cows and no trouble churning butter, they could not keep a single child alive. When the children were about nine months old, they all died. When yet another child lay dying, a priest came by and asked whether the people had enemies. "No," the farmer's wife answered, "but many people come here to fetch milk." The priest then said: "The first person who comes for milk tomorrow, you must make wait, with the excuse that the milk is not ready yet." The first man who came by in the morning worked at a school and so asked how the child was doing. The man played for a moment with the little feet and hands of the child lying in the cradle. The farmer's wife made the man wait five minutes and then gave him his milk. But the schoolmaster did not leave yet, for he could not get up from his chair. A little later the priest came by, saying: "Is there no school today? The boys are all waiting at the gate!" At that the schoolmaster turned bright red. The priest went on: "What evil have you come to do here? And you a schoolmaster! Make sure you are back here within five minutes with your evil, or you will regret it!" A little later the schoolmaster came back with a doll into which he stuck pins. Each time he stuck a pin into the doll's heart, a child died. The priest said to the schoolmaster: "And now you must come with your books, or you will lose your job." The schoolmaster then handed over all his books of magic to the priest.
190079: A man who was afraid of nothing saw someone walking about with a chain and a white sheet one evening at the Schapenbrug in Westkapelle. Out of fear the man jumped into the manure pit.
190102: A man on his way to a wedding met a strange woman, who muttered something along the lines of "don't go on". A little further on the man fell into the mud, so that he was indeed forced to go back home.
190103: In a small chapel in Koksijde was the grave of Sint-Baalten. People had tried several times to take the saint's statue to the church of Koksijde, but strangely enough, the next morning the statue was always back in the chapel.
190107: Some rich people who had hidden their money in a well had died. After their death they came back to haunt in the form of a candle, to show the place where the money was hidden. The candle's flame danced up and then down again. Someone who had beckoned to the flame then quickly ran inside. The door was barely shut when a loud bang was heard. The next morning the door was found to be covered in blood.
190124: A woman who had many problems with her child took the child to the friars. On the way, the child's white neckerchief was suddenly full of green caterpillars. When the mother told the friars what had happened, the clergyman said: "On the way back you will meet a woman. You must give her a cake." On the way home the mother and child did indeed meet a woman. When the mother offered her a cake, the woman refused. After much insisting, the woman accepted the cake after all. After that the mother had no more problems with her child.
190125: Strange things happened on a farm in Snaaskerke. No butter could be made there and the tubs were always knocked over. The priest had to come to the farm to exorcise the devil. If priests did not wear their vestments, the devil would wring their necks. Since the Gospel of Saint John has existed, the devils have all been driven away.
190126: A man moved to the Kruisstraat in Merkem. When the man arrived there with his belongings, a sorceress from the neighbourhood was there too. She went round all the rooms of the house and said: "You will live well here". The man's first child was completely emaciated after two months. The second child, a little daughter, was born without a palate. When the little son was six months old, his fingers began to rot away. The parents often went to the fathers in the hope that their misfortune would come to an end. The son went to live in France. He lost his hands completely. As a child he also had a small mark on his forehead, but that healed. People said that the sorceress had caused all that misfortune.
190128: When a child was playing by a cesspit, a sorceress said to the people: "You needn't watch that child like that; it won't fall into the pit!" The next moment the child was magically made to fall into the pit.
190131: A sorceress came to a farm to fetch pig fat. When the sorceress had gone, the farmer said to his wife: "You mustn't give it to her any more; she'll have to come and get it herself". The farmer's wife put the pig fat on the corner of the table. The next time, however, the sorceress could not get in because there was an Easter nail under the door. Furious, the witch leaned over the door of the pigsty. That bewitched the pigs; they all got lumps.
190148: People who were ridden by the mare got lost.
190161: A stick that was completely warped had been ridden by the kokkemare (the mare). People who were ridden by the mare in their sleep began to scream loudly and wanted to go outside.
190162: In the blue castle near Aalbeke station worked a weaver who had to work through the night because she had to finish a piece of cloth by the next day. Between midnight and one o'clock the woman heard sheep bleating and a dog barking. The weaver thought it strange that the Duitse schaper (German shepherd, a travelling shepherd said to have magic powers) was still out so late. She went to have a look, but there was nothing to see. When the woman went back inside, she heard the sounds again. It was the same story every night.
190167: By the little chapel a farmer's wife saw a woman standing with eyes like balls of fire. The more the farmer's wife looked, the bigger the woman grew.
190171: One night a man found himself in a meadow he could not get out of because he could not find his bearings. Strangely, the man did not know how he had ended up in that meadow either. Only at daybreak could the man find his bearings again. He was convinced that a witch from the village had bewitched him.
190183: A soldier returning in the evening from an inn where he had gone for a drink suddenly saw a dog with a chain walking beside him in the Gasthuisstraat. The soldier had not seen where the animal had come from. When the soldier went on his way, he saw to his great dismay that the dog was growing bigger and bigger. The soldier was too afraid to run the animal through with his sabre. At the Doorgangsstraatje the dog suddenly disappeared. A little later the soldier met a man, to whom he told what had happened. The man said: "Luckily you didn't use your sabre, otherwise it could have ended much worse! It was the nekker that followed you!"
190196: On a farm there worked a farmhand who was ridden by the mare. The farmhand walked on the roof, jumped off and landed in a bed that stood in the corner of a room.
190204: Some boys from Westkerke were coming back from the fair in Eernegem. On the way they saw a café where organ music could be heard. The youngsters went into the café, where they saw all sorts of strange little devils. Because they were so frightened, the boys made the sign of the cross. A moment later everything had vanished.
190213: In a wood in Aartrijke a headless horse that could not be caught often appeared.
190219: A butcher buying a cow offered one franc more than the asking price because it was such a fine animal. When the man went to collect the cow two days later, the animal was skin and bone. A sorceress had caused this.
190230: Late one evening some men were coming through the woods together with a boy whose mother was a sorceress. At a certain moment the boy said: "Damn, it's cold here!" The next moment the whole wood was on fire. The boy's mother had probably caused it.
190244: German shepherds (sheep herders believed to have magic powers) made people lose their way, so that they had to walk around all night.
190245: In the old days people did not dare to go to the churchyard in the evening, because it was said that a ghost sat behind every grave.
190247: The mare made people lose their way or stupefied people in their beds.
190262: In the past there were many women who could bewitch children. Such children had to have prayers read over them by the fathers.
190281: A labourer lived near a farm that was haunted. However, the labourer did not believe the stories about the haunting. One evening the labourer had to go out with a friend. When the two came past the haunted farm, five white cats jumped out of a tree. The labourer was so frightened by this that he wasted away completely and eventually died.
190286: In Ettelgem, every day at around the same time, a woman went about giving suikerspek (a marshmallow-like sweet) to the children. All the children who had eaten the sweet cried until the parish priest read prayers over them. A mother from Ettelgem always made sure her children were inside when that woman made her rounds.
190290: Being ridden by the mare was similar to dreaming. One heard the mare come in and was then seized by the throat, so that one could hardly breathe and began to gasp until one woke up.
190299: At one spot in Hondschote there were always so many cats that the grass was completely trampled flat and people could no longer get away.
190322: In Poperinge, after midnight, one could see two women dressed in white walking the procession route in the wrong direction.
190338: On a farm there was so much misfortune with the animals that the priest was finally sent for. The priest found that an evil spirit was present and stayed alone on the farm to pray. The priest made the spirit leave the farm in the shape of a snake through the water drain. The spirit asked whether it could come back, and the priest answered "yes". The spirit was allowed to come back a little way each year. Since then there has been no more misfortune on that farm.
190342: A mother whose child was ill took her child to the fathers of Brugge. After a father had read prayers over the child, the clergyman said to the woman: "You must not show your child to anyone". On the way back by train the mother kept her child under her cloak. A woman who came to sit beside her said: "You must have a baby under your cloak! There's no need to be afraid, go on, let me see it". When the mother showed the child, it was bewitched. A while later the child died.
190367: A farmhand had to go and fetch syrup. When the farmhand was standing at the gate of the farm, he began to lick some of the syrup. Beside him the farmhand saw a tree stump with a white ghost. Although the farmhand had always claimed not to be afraid of ghosts, he died of fright some time later.
190389: A man from the Zuidhoek in Beselare met a little old woman and said: "What are you doing out on the street at this time of night?" The next moment the man was slapped in the face. The man went on and at once broke out in a sweat. He found that he had lost his cap. When he got home, the man saw the cap hanging on his door handle.
190412: A man who was taking a bundle of straw to his mother met a hare on the way. When the man struck at the hare, the animal kept growing bigger. In the end the hare was as big as a cow. The man never again dared to go along that path.
190415: A man who had to go drumming somewhere one evening was followed the whole way by a horse. The horse laid its head on the man's shoulder. The man struck at the animal with his drumstick, but he could not hit it.
190432: A sorceress lived in Oudezele. During a walk the priest broke his leg. The sorceress was already on her way to visit the priest before he had even got home.
190448: In Veurne a baby lay in its cradle and cried all the time. The mother went to a priest, who gave her an Easter nail to put under the door. After that the witch could no longer come in.
190450: A woman had put fresh pork in a tub with salt when a witch came by. The next day the pork had gone bad.
190466: A man claimed that he always saw the ghost of his father appear. The drowned fisherman would then appear in a dripping wet oilskin jacket. The man once even fell ill because he saw his father's ghost appear.
190471: A man going to Ardooie saw a priest dressed in white walking along, who suddenly vanished.
190473: On a farm in Bavikhove a child had died. Another child fell seriously ill. A frog always came into that farmhouse through the drain hole. The frog always hopped around the sick child. One day they managed to catch the frog and threw the animal into the fire. After that no more children died on that farm.
190496: When people knocked (?) because the fire in the stove had almost gone out, they believed there was a spirit in the house to admonish them.
190517:
a) In the army there was a strange soldier who owned a small black case with books. One day the soldiers were billeted with a farmer. Because the farmer refused to give the men milk, the soldier said to himself: "We no milk, you no milking!" The next morning the farmer could not get into his stable to milk the cows. Even after the farmer had been to the presbytery, the stable door still would not open. A little later the soldier filled the farm with rats. Then the officer came to the soldiers with the message that from now on everyone would get as much milk as he needed. After that the farmer could get into his stable again to milk the cows.
b) One day the farmer asked the soldiers if they could plant beets in the field. While the soldiers were at work, the soldier who owned the books of magic said: "I'll see to it that the work here is done quickly. Everyone lie flat on the ground with your hands over your eyes. You may not look until I say so." The men did as they were asked. A quarter of an hour later all the beets had been planted.
c) Because the farmer was afraid of the soldier with the books of magic, he told everything to the parish priest, who said: "I'll come by tomorrow at one in the afternoon." When the priest came the next day, he could not get onto the lane to the farm. The soldier sat reading his books of magic the whole time to keep the priest away.
d) One day the French soldiers held a big party with performances by conjurers. The soldier who owned the books of magic climbed onto the stage, began reading his books and asked everyone to turn their heads away for a moment. A little later the door opened and four thousand little red soldiers came in. After the party the soldier went to a few cafés with his friends. The soldier with the books of magic paid for everything, although he did not have a penny in his pocket.
e) When the soldiers were quartered in Adinkerke, they got a new commander from Brugge. During the inspection the soldier who owned the books of magic made the commander fly four metres into the air and hang there for five minutes. When the commander came back down, he walked off indignantly. After that the soldiers got their former commander back.
f) When the soldier with the books of magic left the army, he said there were only two like him in all of Belgium. Soon there would even be only one. Then the soldier left and never came back.
190520: A miller went on pilgrimage to Edelare in the month of May. On the way the man came across a strange beast, bigger than a hare but smaller than a dog. The man stood on that road for eight hours because he could not go on. A few days later the miller's neighbour, who was a butcher, also went to Edegem. At the same spot the butcher was stopped by a horse and by that strange beast. When the men got home, they told each other what each of them had experienced. One of the men had set his two dogs Lise and Danny on the beast. An hour later one of the dogs had come back with a bloody muzzle.
190549: On a farm worked a German shepherd who flew home on a billy goat on Sundays. By evening the shepherd was back on the farm. One Saturday evening the horse groom was allowed to fly along with the shepherd. Two billy goats as big as horses stood ready. The German shepherd said to the groom: "You don't need to hold on, but you mustn't say anything." On the way the groom tore his trouser leg on the church tower. In Germany the pair ate to their hearts' content. The next day they went for a walk with the shepherd's wife and children. By evening they were back on the farm.
190556: One evening a sorceress came to visit a house where a baby lay in its cradle. The woman went to the cradle and said: "What a beautiful child!" The next day the little boy was ill. He had blue lumps all over and died some time later. People called this illness 'de plane'.
190561: One day a young lady was sitting in the parlour of the convent when suddenly smoke came out of the chimney and filled the whole room. No one ever knew where that smoke came from.
190564:
a) In Oostrozebeke lived a witch who had bewitched her own husband. The man had been ill for eight years but could not die. After the fathers of Tielt had read prayers over him, he could finally die.

b) On a farm where they could no longer churn butter, the people decided to keep watch one evening. Around eleven o'clock they heard noise in the cellar. They went down and saw a big black cat sitting there. They struck at the animal with a stick but could not hit it. After several attempts someone managed to hit the cat on the paw. When those people went to mass through the snow the next day and passed the house of a witch, they called out: "Hey, aren't you coming to mass?" The little woman answered: "No, I fell and broke my arm."
190568: In the parish of Sint-Jan in Oostende there was a child who was very ill. The curate told the child's parents: "The child will die. When you hear a rustling in the chimney, death is near. During the funeral you will find out who bewitched the child." The child did indeed die. During the funeral there was one woman present who left the church early. She was also the only woman who did not go along to the churchyard. She was the mother-in-law of the child's mother.
190569: A dustman coming home drunk from Beselare met a woman on the way, who accompanied him as far as the chapel. There the woman vanished without a trace. The man was sober at once.
190571: A farmer who owned a buck rabbit was visited by a woman who came to have her rabbits mated. When the buck would not do its job, the woman shook the animal about. That buck never looked at a rabbit again. Later that woman could only die after the priest had come to take away her books.
190573: If one walked past the Koude Schuur in the evening, one was accompanied by a black cat. Such cats could make a person fall into the water. However much one struck at those cats, one could not hit them.
190577: In Roksem a white nun is said to have once walked about at night.
190607: A witch from Haringe had bewitched the cow on a farm. From then on a white cat always roamed about on that farm. Sometimes the cat came to lick milk from a bucket, at other times it sat by the butter churn.
190608: A woman was visited by an old woman who said: "You must repeat what I say." The woman refused, but the old woman stayed seated and began to read. The next moment the woman fell against the coal bin, leaving her face completely crooked.
190611: Devils flew through the air on floating carts. In reality such apparitions were simply falling stones.
190621: Anyone walking along a forest path in Maldegem often saw a hen roll right up to their feet. As soon as people were past the ditch, the hen had disappeared and a laughing tree stump stood there.
190625: If you placed your feet crosswise in a witch's footprints, the witch would look round.
190634: In Kaster lived a woman who could do magic. Wherever that woman visited, something went wrong. A man from the village always advised people to throw that woman out. When they did, a loud scream was heard, after which the woman was gone. Most people, however, did not dare throw her out because she lived nearby. In reality the witch was not a local woman at all; she took on the shape of a neighbour to get into people's houses.
190638: In a house in the Leffingestraat in Oostende a few men often used to gather. By wrapping a knife in a red handkerchief and looking at where the knife pointed, those men could find out in which house people were being ridden by the mare.
190642: A well that seemed to have no bottom was haunted every night. The well had a diameter of about thirty metres (?). Cows that fell into it never got out again. A milk seller who lived near the well had always scooped water from it to pour into her milk. After her death the woman came to haunt with the words: "Hiele, holle, hei! Water and milk. Scantly measured and God has forgotten my soul." Every night something could be seen or heard near the well: sometimes a little light, sometimes an old woman, and otherwise the calling was heard.
190670: A woman whose children were always ill went to the priest for advice. The priest advised the mother not to let a certain woman who often visited come near the cradle any more. After that the child recovered.
190682: To protect oneself against the mare, one had to put one's slippers upside down under one's bed.
190684: By the canal stood a black hunting hut that was haunted at night. All kinds of strange noises were heard there and now and then a light burned.
190698: If the priest forgot to close his missal after mass, no witch could leave the church.
190700: Pregnant women were afraid of sorceresses because they could make children die.
190702: When people took a bewitched child to the priests, the child weighed terribly much, so that they could hardly carry it. After the priests of West-Vleteren had prayed for a while, the child's nappy was full of pins.
190741:
After her husband's death a woman always saw a blue sky. One day the woman remembered that she had promised her husband to go on a pilgrimage to Margriete. After the woman had done so, she no longer saw that strange sky.
If a widower had remarried and his first wife returned after her death, the youngest child had to fulfil the dead woman's wish. After all, the father no longer counted.
190745: A man was ridden by the mare for the first time during his time as a soldier. The soldier felt as if someone was trying to strangle him and he could not make a sound. The man woke up drenched in sweat from fear. Some people claimed that the mare was a standstill of the blood.
190780: A woman who went about cutting nettles for her rabbits and her goat had to dance with the nettles on her back whenever she passed the house of a sorceress.
190787: A farmer coming back from Oostende one night saw a large dance hall with music playing near the Snaaskerke bridge. As soon as the farmer entered the hall, the whole scene vanished. Suddenly the farmer saw a stranger standing there, who asked him whether he would write his name in his blood. The farmer said he would only do so if the stranger could make a rope out of dune sand. The other agreed, on condition that he could put horse dung in the sand. The farmer did not agree to that, and so he was free again.
190789:
