When someone was tormented at night by the mare, that person claimed that the mare first sat in the slippers next to the bed and jumped from there onto its victim. The victim then felt the mare creeping up from their feet. Whoever wanted to protect themselves against the mare had to hold a knife above their heart.
A woman had often told her husband that she was ridden by the mare at night. One night she decided to try the knife tactic. When the woman did so, she heard a loud scream, after which the mare fell out of the bed. The next morning the woman found that it was her own husband.
190790: A woman was always visited by a sorceress who had something against her. The sorceress stole money and made the woman ill. Sometimes the sorceress turned herself into a little light or a grey cat. One evening the woman had put thirty francs on the mantelpiece. The next morning the money was gone. The woman went to have the priest pray over her. After that nothing strange happened any more. Two years later, however, the misery began again. One day the sorceress went for advice to a woman from Torhout who kept a small shop to disguise her dark practices. That shopkeeper was the sister of the woman being tormented by the sorceress! That sister could not bear that the woman sometimes visited her sister-in-law. When one day the woman was visiting her sister-in-law, a little grey cat came in. That was the sorceress, who had turned herself into a cat.
190808: Four people who were going to visit a man saw a white beast fall into a stream on the way.
190826: There used to be a churchyard by the big linden tree behind the church of Anzegem. A man claimed that the ghost of an old woman always sat rustling in that linden tree. The tree stood exactly where her grave had been.
190837: A farm in Pittem was haunted. At night all kinds of noises were heard there, and when people went upstairs the candles were blown out. In the morning the four corners of the tablecloth were rolled up and the flowerpot stood in the middle of the table. In the end the friars came to exorcise the farm.
190871: A man who was ridden by the mare felt as if a stone was falling on him and believed he was going to die. To protect oneself against the mare, one had to turn one's clogs around so that they stood under the bed heels first.
190874: Near the convent grounds was a field that nobody dared to pass because little lights could be seen there. People believed those lights were the wandering souls of the deceased inhabitants of the castle.
190881: A woodcutter came back after his death. People saw the ghost felling trees.
190891: In Houtkerke lived women who could do magic. These sorceresses made the animals die. When people went to the fathers to protect themselves against witchcraft, they were given something blessed to put under the door. After that no sorceress could get into the house any more.
190894: A man laughed at a sorcerer who claimed he could send rats to people's houses. The sorcerer then said: "Don't laugh, you'll see!" Three weeks later the man's house was full of rats. The man went to the procession in Veurne to fetch palm, so that the rats would disappear.
190910: A man travelling with his cart saw a black cat cross the road. The next moment a wheel of the cart broke. One day a man had kicked that same cat. The next day a woman from the neighbourhood was limping.
190912: On a farm there was a small child who often had convulsions because it had been bewitched by an old woman.
190916: A boy who lived at the Rattevalle went to the École Moyenne in Nieuwpoort, much to the annoyance of the parish priest. The boy was constantly tormented by the priest, even after the clergyman had died. For example, the boy was pulled between the rungs of chairs by the priest, who had made himself invisible. The fathers of Oostende said the tormenting would stop as soon as the boy was confirmed. So it was decided to give the boy Confirmation earlier than planned. He was taken to Middelkerke in a wheelbarrow. They could hardly get past the bridge because the wheelbarrow suddenly became extraordinarily heavy. As soon as they had left Slijpe, the wheelbarrow had its normal weight again. The boy shuddered whenever he saw the priest coming. No one else could see the clergyman.
190923: A woman on her way home met an old witch, who asked whether she still had far to go. "That's none of your business," the woman answered. The next moment the witch jumped on the woman's back and had herself carried until the woman was drenched in sweat.
190928: Two men who made brooms went to sell the brooms in Handzame on a Saturday evening. At a farm the sellers' clothes were torn to pieces by two dogs. At the farm they met the farmer, who said: "These are good folk." The sellers replied: "Yes, we are good folk, but our clothes have been torn to pieces by your dogs." The farmer said: "Then you are surely not good, for my dog does not do such things. Come in and eat." In the light the robbers saw that their clothes were not damaged. The farmer offered the sellers shelter, but they left for Handzame that same evening. When they passed that farm again on the way back, they saw a coffin lying there. One of the sellers knocked three times on the coffin and then went on. Further on they saw a cow in the meadow. The cow went along with them and grew bigger and bigger. At a farm the sellers saw a spade standing outside. "Go on, take it with you," said one seller to the other, who then put the spade on his shoulder. Further on, however, the man could no longer carry the spade, for it had become too heavy. The man decided to take the spade back, since he did not really need it anyway. The other seller went on alone, accompanied by the cow, which kept growing bigger. The man came home and went to sleep at once. In the night two travellers came knocking, asking the way to Handzame. The seller's wife said to her husband: "You go with those people to Handzame." When the man came to the place where the coffin had been, a large well could now be seen. At that moment the church clock struck one. The man made the sign of the cross, whereupon his two companions said: "If you had not made the cross, your neck would have been broken." Then those two men disappeared into the well. Scared to death, the man ran home and told his wife what had happened. The man crawled straight into his bed. Two weeks later he was dead.
190931:
Three rascals threw open the church door and shouted: "Woe!" The curate who was in the church at that moment forced one of the boys to kneel. "Just run away!" the others shouted, but the boy could only get up again when the clergyman gave him permission.
In the past, parish priests could also make stolen money come back.
When a married woman had left her husband and fled to Oostende, the priest forced her to return.
190954: Whoever was ridden by the mare could no longer move and felt as if a block of a hundred kilos was lying on them. In reality the mare was a standstill of the blood.
190976: On a farm in Woumen there was a child that cried all the time. An old woman often visited the family to ask for something. Every time the woman had visited, the child cried. In the end the parents took the child to the priests of Diksmuide. After the clergymen had prayed over the child, they said: "The child is regularly pricked with a pin. A woman is doing this to your child. Go home now. That woman will come back tomorrow and she will ask for something she has absolutely no need of." The parents were given an Easter nail to put under the threshold. The next day the woman came to ask whether the people had piglets. At that the farmer's wife cried angrily: "You don't need piglets! Just make sure you never come here again!"
191002: A woman fetching milk met a sorceress, who asked whether she might send her power over that tub. At that the woman dropped her milk and ran away. A farmer working in the field who had seen everything gave the sorceress a sound thrashing.
191005: A drunkard found no more peace after his wife had died. Whenever the dead woman appeared at night, she always pointed her right index finger towards the church. Once when the man was sober, he had the courage to ask his wife what she wanted. So the drunkard learned that he had forgotten to have three masses said. The man told the priest what had happened, and the priest advised him not to drink so much any more. From then on the man no longer drank. Because of that, both his wife and he himself found peace.
191014: A boy had fought in Hertsberge with the son of a witch. When the son had told his mother what had happened, the mother said: "Wait, I'll get him yet!" That night the boy kept ending up in the water or in the nettles, so that he could not get home. After people had gone to the friars, the boy was well again.
191042: A man going to see his girlfriend in Turkien (?) had the feeling he was being followed. The next Sunday the man took his dog along. Suddenly the man was pulled over by his dog and dragged through the mud. Past the Dentergem cobbled road (?) between the Mane and the Eerden mill, the man heard music and was seized by something and forced to dance. The man hung his coat on a branch and danced until he was drenched in sweat. Suddenly the music could no longer be heard. As soon as the man had stopped dancing, not a drop of sweat was to be seen on his body. The next morning, to his great astonishment, the man found that there was not a single stain on his clothes, although he had been dragged all through the mud.
191048: Framassons (freemasons) were beings that floated through the air and made music on the street corner without being seen.
191050: Above a house where a corpse lay, people saw a ball of fire. It was then believed that the dead person was burning for his sins.
191062: In Gistel lived a man who owned a mule. Although the stable doors were shut in the evening, the mule left its stable every night. When the man went to look in the stable at night, he saw a candle burning there.
191074: In Ieper there lived a rich hunchback who was a member of the freemasons. The man owned ninety-nine farms. The hunchback was buried in unconsecrated ground. Many freemasons in white dustcoats attended the funeral. When the coffin was lowered into the grave, it was found that the body had vanished from the coffin.
191105: A woman whose only child had died cried all night. One night the child came back and said: "Mother, you must not cry any more, because my little shirt is always wet in my coffin." The mother stopped crying, and the little shirt was dry at once.
191107: In Vladslo stood a farm that was haunted. There were never any calves there and the piglets had crooked necks. In the morning the cows stood with their tails tied up.
191116: At the Doodlage there used to be an inn where there was partying every day. One day the devil appeared in that inn. When the devil began to dance with the innkeeper's wife, all the people were blown away by the wind. A moment later the innkeeper's wife was gone too. Those people were never seen again.
191123: A farmer's wife sitting by the hearth was visited by a woman with evil intentions. When the woman left, the farmer's wife's head was crooked. A German shepherd advised the farmer to build a big fire and send for the woman. When the woman came in wearing her hooded cloak, they said to her: "Sit by the hearth so you can warm yourself." The German shepherd made the fire hotter and hotter, so that the woman said: "It's getting hot in here." But the woman could not push her chair back. After a while the woman cried: "Put that fire out, then!" but the shepherd said: "Not before you have undone the evil you have done here." The woman then said: "Go to the stable and rub the horses." The shepherd did so and saw pins falling out of the horses' coats. Then the shepherd said: "Now set the farmer's wife's head straight again." After that had been done, the shepherd sent the woman home. He made her go through a well and through a hedge, so that she came home with scratches on her skin and torn clothes. Afterwards it was discovered that the woman was a neighbour.
191137: A man who was ridden by the mare wanted to call out, but he could not.
191141: Doodkeersen (death candles, ghost lights) were restless dead who could not enter heaven because they had hidden money somewhere. These dead had to come back because they had done something unjust. They only found rest when the money was found.
191161: A sorceress who had turned herself into a cat was burned all over when someone poured boiling water over the animal.
191167: A woman woke up at night because she heard noises as if wood were being chopped. After half an hour the woman woke her husband. The man got up but saw no wood.
191174: During the war a man often had to work late in the workshop where soldiers' clothes were made. Usually the man's mother came to meet him to accompany him home. One evening, however, his mother was not there, so the man had to set off alone. As the man walked between two walls, he saw a woman dressed in white approaching in the distance. The man said: "Good evening", but the woman did not answer. A moment later the man looked back, but the woman had vanished without a trace.
191178: Doodkeersen (death candles, ghostly lights) seen moving up and down among the trees were returned dead people. The dead also returned, for example, if they had buried money somewhere.
191181: When the fishermen went to their ship, they carried an iron basket with bread, butter and sandwich fillings on their backs. The fishermen usually stayed away for two to eight days. Those who sailed to Iceland even stayed away for a whole month. On their way to the ship the fishermen looked at the ground without saying a word. They were afraid that someone would wish them a good journey and that this would bring them bad luck.
191198: People who had hidden money somewhere during their lives had to return after their death.
191213: The crossroads at the 'Gekruiste God' (Crucified God) used to be haunted. A girl who worked in the factory in Waregem claimed that little lights could be seen at that spot. After a crucifix had been put up there, the haunting came to an end.
191242: A man who always came home late after visiting his girlfriend came home one evening with a terribly ugly beast. After that the man never went to that girl again.
191250: A man was visiting a witch who was baking pancakes. "Will you have two pancakes too?" the witch asked, and the man replied: "No, I'm going to help your husband lift the beets." To that the witch said: "That won't be necessary, because he'll get it all done by himself anyway."
191261: A woman who had put her two children to bed saw two big black beasts run away after she had made the sign of the cross. The beasts were not dogs or cats. A witch had caused those apparitions.
191263: A timber merchant always heard sighing and wailing and the rattling of chains at night. Because the man believed it was a poor soul, he promised to have a mass said. Since then the timber merchant has not heard any strange sounds.
191272: Whoever was ridden by the mare sweated terribly and felt as if they were being crushed by a man.
191300: In Wakken lived a sorceress who could turn herself into a cat. The cat would then lie by the hearth in a house to bewitch the child lying in the cradle. One day, when the cat was again sitting in a house, a woman threw a pan of hot sauce over the animal. The next day the witch's face was burned all over.
191308:
On a farm in Beselare they could no longer churn butter. One day a father from Ieper came to look at the hearth and the milk. The priest made a few gestures and advised the people to put some dung in the butter churn. He predicted that the next morning a woman in a hooded cloak would come to visit. They were to leave the woman alone and not speak to her.
The next morning a woman did indeed come to visit. She went to the hearth, scooped out some ashes and then went outside again. That woman was never seen again, and there were no more problems with churning.
191320: German shepherds could make horses bolt and bewitch the carter so he was fixed to the ground.
191322: A man who had often shot at a hare in vain put some salt on the bullet. But then the man never got the chance to shoot the hare. For the animals knew that something blessed would always hit them.
191327: The weaving school by the chapel of Onze-Lieve-Vrouw-ter-Rust was haunted. At night cats walked over the looms there. Whatever people did, they could not catch or hit the cats.
191329: By the brook in Langemark, horse bells could be heard jingling at night.
191334: A man whose nephew had died a few days earlier came home from work around midnight. Above the chimney the man saw a little light flying around.
191347: Two men cutting peat took shelter because it had suddenly started to rain. A little later a woman came to ask the way. When the men had shown her the way, the woman said: "Thank you, I will find it now." A little later the woman came back soaking wet to ask the way again. This time too she said: "Thank you, I will find it now." After that the woman was never seen again. It was believed that someone had murdered her for her jewels, but no body was ever found. A few months after her disappearance, one of the peat cutters was hunting hares at that same place. When the man saw a white sheep approaching, he immediately thought of the murdered woman. The sheep went away and came back a little later. Since then that man never went hunting hares at that place again.
191367: In the Haezepoel on the road from Hondschote to Beveren, some people heard a bell ringing at night. The pit in which that bell had sunk could not be filled.
191376:
People who were ridden by the mare had become lost in their dream.
Plants could also be ridden by the mare; mistletoe, for example, has flat twigs and looks like three twigs that have grown together.
191393: At a widow's house the horses dropped dead. At night the trampling of horses and the rattling of chains could be heard. Because of these events the farm almost went bankrupt.
191408: A woman who had much misfortune with her children put her mother-in-law, who lived with her, out on the street. After that the woman was able to raise her children without problems. She was convinced that her mother-in-law had bewitched her children.
191423: A woman stayed sitting all alone in the church. She could not get out because the priest had left the gospel open on the altar.
191431: In Damme lived a woman everyone was afraid of. Whenever that woman had been at a farm, the animals died and the children fell ill.
191448: Shopkeepers who had cheated people by giving them too little came back after their death.
191456: An unmarried young man loved hunting. When the young man's father lay dying, people said: "Surely you're not going hunting now? You'll stay with your father!" The young man protested and said he first wanted to go and shoot a hare. On his deathbed the father said: "All right, let him hunt and shoot a hare. Then let him hunt forever!" When the young man came back from the hunt, his father was dead. Many years later the young man died too. After that people heard the eternal hunter in the woods calling his dog with the words: "Tsjaoe! Tsjaoe!"
191468: When a Duitse schaper (German shepherd, a travelling shepherd said to have magic powers) threw his cap against the door, the door opened by itself.
191477: Sometimes a 'feu follet' (will-o'-the-wisp) was seen in the churchyard. That was a dead person who had returned.
191479: A woman claimed that she had seen some people playing cards in de Biezen. The woman who lived near there could make such apparitions appear.
191481: Two young families from Kortrijk went for a walk together with their two babies. On the way they met a woman who had no children of her own. The woman said: "What beautiful children! They look like twins!" The next day one of the babies was dead. The doctor could find no symptoms of any illness.
191501:
On a farm worked a maid who was simple-minded. One night the maid jumped out of her bed and shouted that the farm was on fire. She claimed that she had had to walk through the flames to the door of her room. The other occupants got up, but there was no sign of any fire. Two weeks later the same thing happened again.
The farmer and his brother-in-law slept in the bed above the horse stable. Next to that bed was a gutter along which the water from the pump trickled to the cows' drinking trough. One night, on the stroke of eleven, the shelf by where the two men lay began to make noise, so that the packets on it fell to the floor. When the men lit a lantern, the noise suddenly stopped and the packets were back on the shelf. Convinced that people from the neighbourhood were out to get them, the farmer said: "When those people come by tomorrow evening, we will set hommelpersen (1) by the moats. We will each stand on one side, so that we can beat the intruders until they jump into the water." The next evening the two men stood ready at the moats at eleven o'clock. This night too the shelf made noise, but strangely enough there was no one to be seen near the farm. Because the ghostly noises returned every night, the farmer decided to feel in the gutter in the horse stable with a special stick. When the farmer did so, his stick was pulled away by a strange force. He never saw the stick again.
Then the farmer decided to tie some bands around the gutter, so that nothing could get through. At eleven o'clock they would then suddenly undo those bands. If the men had not cut the bands in time that night, the walls would have cracked, so it seemed.
In the end it became so bad that the ghostly noises could be heard until two or three in the morning. Many farmhands and maids gave notice, but the farmer and his brother-in-law stayed on the farm.
One day some men who peddled brooms came to ask the farmer for shelter. The farmer let the men sleep in the hay in the horse stable. At midnight the peddlers left, saying: "But farmer, why didn't you tell us anything about that? We are thrown from one side to the other all the time and we don't know why!"
The farmer had already tried everything and had even consulted the friars, but no one seemed able to help him. In the end he and his brother-in-law were the only people who still dared to stay on the farm.
When the farmer and his brother-in-law came into the cowshed one morning, they saw all sorts of strange beasts standing there instead of cows. As soon as the two were properly inside, the animals became normal again.
After a while the farmer had the friars come again. One of the friars claimed that the farmer's wife had once made a vow that she had not kept. When at least thirty friars had come and a little chapel to Our Lady had been set up in the horse stable, the haunting finally came to an end.
191505: When a child somewhere was ill, people often believed it had been bewitched by a woman who had given it a coin. Women who were old and ugly were often suspected of being sorceresses.
191507: A man who was ridden by the mare every morning had been advised by someone to put his clogs upside down next to his bed before going to sleep. When the man had done that, he was freed from the mare.
191520: A boy always saw six or seven dogs running about when he went outside in the evening. Other people could not see those dogs.
191523: A man who sold flax waste was driving some horses from Waarmaarde to Ijvegem. When the man was halfway, his horses suddenly stood still. Strangely enough, the animals could not go on. The man had to wait there for a good hour. Then the horses went on again.
191526: A man from Merkem always heard a knocking at night at about the same time. A brave friend spent a night in the house and heard the knocking too. Because both men were afraid, they went to a clergyman. Money was dug up at the spot where the knocking could be heard.
191530:
a) In Oostrozebeke a castle had sunk. The former lord of the castle often returned there. Around midnight the castle gates flew open and coaches with ladies and gentlemen drove about.

b) At the castle there worked a stable hand who was often drunk. When the drunkard went to the castle one night, he saw a very beautiful lady dressed in black sitting in a field. When the drunkard said: "Miss, you're working late!", the lady answered: "The day is for you, the night is for me". The drunkard could hardly go on, for the lady had herself carried on his back. The next morning the drunkard could not get out of bed. Only after the priest had read prayers over him until he sweated was the man freed. The clergyman gave him this advice: "If you meet something at night again, say nothing more".
191538: Sorceresses could turn themselves into black cats. A farmer warmed a bowl of milk for a cat that always came to the farm. The cat burned itself on the milk. The next day the farmer saw a woman from the neighbourhood with burns. She was a sorceress.
191561: A sorceress lived near Gullegem. When a child in the village fell ill, it was taken to the priest to have prayers read over it. The priest predicted that a woman who often came to visit would never come again. The priest's prediction came true.
191591: During harvest time, at around midnight, lots of white cats came and sat in the fields. The cats sat so close together that one could not take a step without touching one of the animals.
191610: Two men returning from the Geit (1) saw a calf lying on the little bridge over the Lukebeek. The men took the calf home and shut it in the stable. Then one of the men went inside and said: "Come and look, wife, at what I've brought!" When the man opened the stable door, he saw that the calf had grown so big that it reached up to the roof.
191633: People who had neglected a vow during their lives came to haunt after their death in their human form. The people to whom the ghost appeared then had to fulfil the vow in place of the dead person.
191651: A woman went to France with her husband and her two brothers. In Sintemenoul (Oise) the woman heard people dancing the charleston in clogs at night. When her husband went to ask what was going on, the boss replied: "You must never stand there again in future." Perhaps that boss was himself one of the framassons (Freemasons) (1).
191663: Two men met a woman at night with whom they were angry. The men gave the woman a beating. The next day the woman walked around in top form, as if no one had ever hit her.
191667: It was said of a woman who always went to see small children that she was a sorceress.
191675: An old woman who was doing the zeven weeën (a devotion of the Seven Sorrows) around the churchyard of Lombardsijde suddenly heard the church organ playing and saw that a light was burning in the church. The woman quickly went to the village priest, who established that a priest who still had to say a mass was haunting the church. The village priest sent for the sub-dean of Nieuwpoort, the dean of Veurne and the priest of Westende. When those three clergymen entered the church, there was nothing more to be seen. Strangely enough, those three clergymen died that same year.
191704: Two children were lying in the cradle while a neighbour woman was visiting. As soon as the woman had left, one of the children was covered in lice, while the other child had nothing. The mother went with the child to the parish priest, but he sent her away. The woman then went to a healer. After the healer had read prayers over the child, he advised the woman to throw the neighbour out should she come by again. When the neighbour had not visited for a year, the woman one day saw her standing at the door again. The woman threw the neighbour out.
191710: A miller who lived between Watou and Proven had promised to give as many gold coins as there were grains in a fifty-kilogram barrel. Because that was impossible, the mill turned every night.
191723: In Eentveld there used to be many rabbit thieves. When those thieves were conferring one day, they saw the phantom piglet of Eentveld running. The thieves became so frightened that they no longer dared to go home.
191729: In Sint-Kruis lived a witch who went everywhere begging for food but was given nothing anywhere. If that witch came to a pregnant woman, the woman would either die in childbed or have a deformed child.
191755: A farmer was annoyed by a hare that ate his cabbages. The farmer decided to shoot the hare and kept watch by his field for two evenings. He had already tried to shoot the hare, but he had missed. On the third evening the farmer put a coin chopped into four pieces into his gun. He shot at the hare but missed again. When he went inside afterwards, he found that his wife had a wound on her buttock. She had turned herself into a hare.
191772: Being ridden by the mare was something like dreaming. When someone called the victim's name, the mare vanished immediately.
191804: On a farm they were sometimes visited in the morning by a woman who was said to be able to do magic. Every time that woman had been by, they could no longer churn butter on that farm. After the father had read prayers over the farm, the sorceress could no longer get in. After that they could churn butter on that farm effortlessly again.
191817: A man saw a little light floating between the trees in the dark. It was believed that such lights were the returning dead.
191821: In Gits lived a baker who went to a father from Roeselare because his bread would no longer bake in the oven. The priest told the baker: "When you open your door tomorrow, you will see a woman standing there. You must grab her and throw her out." The next morning the baker did what the father had advised. After that the baker could bake bread effortlessly again.
191822: A farmer from Vichte heard bells ringing and tolling every night at the same time. He claimed it was his dead wife coming to haunt.
191825: Some women who were ridden by the mare walked around the attic at night with their blankets on their backs until they were drenched in sweat. The priests claimed that the women had become the victims of a pedlar woman with evil intentions. One of the clergymen broke an egg into a cup. The women saw the face of that pedlar woman in the sheen of the egg. "Nothing can be done about it," said the clergyman, "she will come by again. But then you must accept what she gives you, and that will be the end of the evil." The priests were proved right.
191832: In Esen there lived a man whose house was haunted every evening. The man heard noises and stabbed with his knife in the direction of the sound, but he always missed. Noise could always be heard in the attic as well.
191859: A child always got sweets from a woman. Some time later the child fell ill. No one knew what was wrong with it. It pulled the hair out of its head and could not die. In the end the child was taken to a father from Ieper to have prayers read over it. The father sweated terribly while reading over the child. One Sunday afternoon the mother was visited by a woman from the neighbourhood, who came to see how the child was. "Your child is very ill," the woman said. The following Thursday the child died. That woman never visited again. For the mother had received from the priest a blessed little heart wrapped in leather, which she had to hang by the door. Because of it the sorceress could no longer get in.
191862: People who had neglected a vow came back after their death.
191881: German shepherds owned magic books with a skull on the cover, with which they could summon little devils to help them with their work. By reading in such a magic book, one could also make rats appear. In the end the clergy collected all the magic books.
191888: A woman who was given to drink always went to visit newborn babies. Afterwards those babies got 'de plane' (1).
191892: In Torhout there lived a framasson (freemason) who had to go to Oostende every year for a meeting of the lodge. At each of those meetings a person was chosen who had to die. One day the framasson from Torhout did not come back. Only his coffin, filled with stones, came back.
191893: A mother had a baby that was only a few months old. One day the mother was visited by a woman peddler, who shook the child's hand and said: "You have a lovely child!" The next day the child was crying because it was completely covered in lice. The mother had the friars read prayers over the child. When the mother came home, the child no longer had any lice.
191926: A dead person who had returned said: "It is very strict over there." Then the dead person disappeared again.
191965: Some farmers were plagued by a real rat infestation that someone had sent. The farmers had their farm overlezen (exorcised by reciting prayers). The man who came to do it dug a pit and lured all the rats into it.
191981: On a little lane near the Motehoek, people always saw a kitten running between their legs in the evening. A flickering light could also be seen. When one day a chicory pit was made there, a pot of money was found. Since then the kitten and the light have not been seen again.
191982: In Assebroek lived an old woman who often visited farmers. Whenever that woman had been with the piglets in the pigsty, the piglets died.
192010: On a farm in Heule there was a beautiful child. When the mother went with the child to her sisters one day, she met a woman who wanted to hold the child for a moment. The next moment the child's nose began to bleed. The bleeding lasted two years. The child would not eat and always said: "heh, heh, heh". In the end the child died.
192021:
Witches could make children get the 'plane' (1). The children then got a large black cross or a branch on their back and were dead in no time.
A witch whose two children had both died bewitched the children of a shopkeeper out of jealousy. The children got the 'plane' and died.
192023:
A man went to the fathers because his wife was bewitched. After the woman had put her wedding ring under the threshold, the witch who had bewitched her could no longer get in.
The same witch had also bewitched a child in its cradle. Because the child cried all the time as a result, they went to the fathers for advice. There the child laughed with joy because it felt it would be freed from the evil.
192025: A mother making bobbin lace was visited by a black woman, who went straight to the cradle where the mother's baby lay. The woman jumped up, grabbed the stove poker and chased the black visitor away. A moment later the black woman had vanished without a trace.
192040:
In Waregem there lived a 'lapmeester' (a folk healer) (1) who could work magic. One day a cowherd from Libbrecht had to go and fetch the sorcerer. On the way he met the sorcerer, who was already coming back from the farm, and everything had already been put right.
In the old days farmers often went to 'de drie moren' in Kortrijk to hire people. Because the sorcerer was often there, a man who was ridden by the mare also went there once. Without the man having said a word, the sorcerer already knew what his problem was. He gave the man a small bottle, after which the man was no longer ridden by the mare.
192045: On a haunted farm in Haringe the cows roamed outside at night and there were thornbushes in their feeding trough. When the farmer lay in bed, he heard the mill turning, although there was nothing to be seen.
192055: During the war a man gave a witch half a kilo of butter as a gift. The next day the man's cart broke down.
192059:
On a farm in Waardamme the labourers had to bind up the harvest, even though it was the village fair. The people sought the advice of the Duitse schaper (German shepherd, a travelling shepherd said to have magic powers) who worked on the farm. The old shepherd said: "I'll see to it that the work is done by three o'clock this afternoon. You must all lie on your stomachs in the field without looking." One curious woman, however, looked anyway, until she got a crooked neck from it. A little later all the work was done, except the part of the woman who had looked. She had to go to the priest to have her neck put right.
Only one German shepherd ever worked on a farm. These shepherds could walk through a door that was locked with a lock and a bolt. But they could not get past a door that was closed only with a bolt.
192068: In a house in Kuurne the haunting always began at midnight. Everything in the house would then fly around. In the end the priests were sent for. While those clergymen were praying, the drops of sweat rolled down their foreheads.
192089: In the old days people were often ridden by the mare. Those people then began to sweat heavily until the sorcery came to an end.
192096: Children bewitched by a sorceress got 'de oude man' (the old man). Those children lay wasting away and looked like people a hundred years old.
192108: In the eighteenth century a man from Zillebeke poisoned a woman so that he could live in her house with Frenchmen. Later that dilapidated house was haunted. Figures floated around and a pale light could be seen burning there in the evening. The haunting lasted until the house was bombed flat during the Second World War.
192110: In a house where the devil had crawled out of the cupboard wearing a red-striped garment, a girl said: "Well, you've got your finest clothes on!" The girl's words had barely been spoken when the devil showed his tongue, as red as a burning coal. The father told his daughter to be quiet; otherwise he might no longer manage to drive the devil away. The priest freed the man from his magic power.
192117: A girl who was in the power of a sorceress would at times begin to shake and tremble so badly that even two men could not hold her still.
192146: At night people always heard a rattling and a voice that said: "Where shall I put them, where shall I put them?" One night a brave man answered: "Put them where you got them!" The voice thanked the man and was heard no more. It was the ghost of a farmer who had moved a boundary post. He was released.
192151: A carter said to someone: "Give me your photo so that I can take it to a sorceress. Within nine days you will be begging that sorceress to lift the spell."
192162: A boy who could not die was always visited by a woman in a cloak. In the end they had to pray the boy to death. When the boy was buried, a hellish noise could be heard in the house. The doors slammed shut.
192170: A brave man met a man without a head on his way home.
192177: Near the Madone a farmer had died who had buried money somewhere. After the farmer's death, candles were seen dancing near the farm every evening. The priest told the people that the farmer was coming back to let them know he had left something behind somewhere. After the farmer's money had been dug up, the candles no longer appeared. With that money, masses were said for the salvation of the farmer's soul.
192205: People who were ridden by the mare felt as if they were being held down in their dream.
192206: In De Klitte lived a woman who had been ill for forty years because of a witch. The woman's child was ill too. One day it was decided to send for the priest to take away the evil. After a woman from the neighbourhood had informed the priest, she said: "Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, she won't know any more that I spoke about her!"
192212: The waternekker (water sprite) was a man who could change himself into an animal because he had been cursed. The animal then walked around with a chain around its neck. One day the man was sent far away, so that in the meantime his animal skin could be burnt. After that the man was released.
192231: A priest had a little boy in his parish who could make mice by magic. The priest took the child's magic power away.
192237: In Hoeke lived an old witch who had stolen a woman's cat from a distance and put an ugly cat in its place. When the robbed woman placed a medal under her chair, the witch could no longer harm her.
192250: A man cycling back from a dinner at around half past eleven saw two stoves lying in the road at the sharp bend near Uxem (?). To avoid the stoves, the man rode into the ditch. Strangely enough, he did not get wet.
192266: On a farm where all the pigs were dying, people sought advice from the priests of Steenbrugge. One of the priests advised the farmer to take the head of a calf to a certain house and put it on the table there. After that the misery came to an end.
192269: At a farm where a man came to sell cauliflower, the people answered: "We already have cauliflower ourselves." A little later the people found that their cauliflower was full of lice. The lice were even in their own bed. They had to send for the friar.
192270: When someone made noise near a coffin, the dead man called out from his coffin: "When one is dead, one does not speak, and when one keeps a wake, one does not sing!"
192273: A girl on her way to visit her boyfriend heard music at the locks. When the girl went to the toilet, it turned out to be full of cats. It was her brother who was playing all these magic tricks on her.
192296:
In Rozebeke there lived a sorceress who had made her own daughter miserable by twisting her hands crooked. The chaplain went to collect the sorceress's books and burned them. Once, when the sorceress's husband was drunk, he had said: "I'm going to sleep with my sorceress."
A man who went hunting one morning saw a big dog sitting in the middle of the road. It looked like a red cabbage that did not move. The man crept quietly past the dog and then ran off. When the man went back to that spot the next day, he saw no dog tracks. He only saw cat tracks. That must have been the sorceress...
192297: A woman had met with misfortune after she had gone weeding for a witch.
192317: A man who worked as a farmhand on a farm in Barsdamme always heard the hens cackling and making noise at night. When the farmhand went to look, however, there was nothing strange to be seen. When the farmhand went to milk the cows in the morning, the animals had all been untied. Moreover, no butter could be churned on the farm. A priest who came to exorcise the farm was completely drenched in sweat from the effort.
192341: Two boys were threshing in the barn. As a joke, one of the boys put a noose around his neck as if he wanted to hang himself. The other boy was to free his friend if the game got out of hand. A moment later, however, a hare came into the barn. The other boy let himself be distracted and followed the animal further and further. Meanwhile his friend was in distress and died with the noose around his neck. That hare was the devil in animal form.
192342: Two men who were travelling got lost. They knocked at a house and said: "We have heard that many witches live here." The person who opened the door answered: "Yes, and the captain lives not far from here."
192343: Some people set off for Ichtegem on the morning of All Saints' Day to go to confession. On the way they saw a donkey crossing the cobbled road. A little further on, in the Haringbos, they saw something jump into the ditch. The people, however, did not say a word to each other. On the way back one of them started talking about the strange apparitions. It then turned out that the others had not seen those apparitions. The person who had seen them wore a wedding ring and the others did not.
192345: A cellar used to be badly haunted. People who wanted to go into the cellar to see what was going on never came back. Near that cellar roamed a large black dog that could not be shot in any way.
192390: If a stable had been bewitched by a strange woman, the people had misfortune.
192402: On the Stierhoek there were two cafés: 'De Stier' and 'den Haze'. One evening at around half past eleven a man left one of those cafés for home. When the man reached the wood, he suddenly heard a noise and was flung to the ground. The man scrambled up and fled out of the wood as fast as he could. After that the man never dared to go into that wood again.
192404: At a small chapel in Roksem, mewing kittens roamed about at night at a certain hour. Those cats got under the feet of passers-by.
192443: A man who was pursued by a doodkaars (death candle, a light foretelling a death) claimed that he was being ridden by the mare.
192444: A doctor who could do magic was nearly arrested at a café because people thought he was a vagrant. "Wait," said the doctor, "I'll go and get my papers." He could make people stand still for as long as he liked. It was said that this doctor lived only on eggs. The doctor had special little bottles and could do magic. He always said: "Leave alone those who leave you alone!"
192453: A sorcerer could cover people in lice and fleas.
192460: Some people went on a pilgrimage to Wervik for a child suffering from a heart disease. But the men got lost and ended up in Menen. When the men could find their bearings again, the child was already dead. Someone had it in for them.
192467: A man coming home from work met a woman who said: "Here is a key. I will lead you to a cellar where there is a chest with a lion on it. If you can kill that lion, all the money in the chest is yours". When the man replied that he did not dare, the woman cried: "Until a hundred years from now!" and vanished. At the place where that castle sank, a pit can still be seen.
192483: A man going from Westkerke to Oudenburg met an old woman on the way, to whom he said: "Good evening!" The woman answered: "Good evening! Mind you get home!" After that the man got lost. He could not find his house and had to wander about all night until dawn broke.
192489: A little boy was standing at the door when a witch from Klerken passed by. The boy got a marshmallow sweet from the witch, but afterwards he had convulsions.
192493: If a farm had a cow that would not get in calf, the blame was often put on a woman suspected of witchcraft.
192496: A castle was said to have once sunk near Watou. At night bells could still be heard ringing underground.
192510: People who were troubled by a churn witch who came at night to steal butter from the churn went to the priests. The clergymen prayed and advised the people to wash the cows' udders and clean the churn. Then the churn had to be rinsed out with clear water, for the devil had no power over water. When the people had done that, they could not make butter. The priests knew very well that no butter could be churned in a dirty churn.
192513: The kokkemare (the mare) was a woman who could make people's blood stand still.
192525: Near the Kattinne there was a place where one could not sleep for a week without being ridden by the mare. The mare had something to do with spiritism. Whoever was ridden by the mare tried in vain to call out in their sleep and then woke up sweating.
192584: In Langemark lived three women whom the people were very afraid of. Whenever someone had a baby, those three women came to look at the child. Once it happened that a baby fell ill. The child had to have prayers read over it by the chaplain. After that was done, the clergyman said: "The child has been bewitched!"
192601: The husband of a witch wanted to visit his sister in Hooglede. The man decided to go while his wife was asleep. When the man had nearly reached his destination, however, he was forced by an indescribable power to turn back.
192605: Anyone ridden by the mare could not cry out because their throat was squeezed shut. People who had been victims of the mare were usually very tired the next day. They could even be ill.
192634: A mother from Veurne sent for the priest of Joenkershove because her child's cradle was always full of ants. After the clergyman had read prayers over the cradle, the ants were gone. The priest advised the mother to send away a woman with a little basket who always came to visit.
192644: People who were pestered by a cat sometimes threw hot water or hot butter over the animal. The next day they would find that a woman from the village had burns.
192649: To recognise a witch, you had to place your feet crossed on her footprints. If the suspected woman was a witch, she would look round.
192673: A man could make the devil appear and then disappear again. One evening the man made the devil appear before his friends in the form of a big black dog. But the man had forgotten how to make the devil disappear again. At his wits' end, the man went to fetch the priest. The priest came and began to pray with a large cross in his hands. The priest had to step back three times before the dog, so strong was the evil. The man who had summoned the devil was sweating terribly. When the priest had managed to touch it with the cross the third time, the devil flew away.
192694: In Sint-Joris lived a witch who was as it were compelled to visit every newborn child. Afterwards those children all died. One night a child in the village was ill. The witch's neighbour across the street had got up during the night because he had toothache. The man saw the witch leave her house at two in the morning and go to the house of the sick child. The door there was locked, however. The next morning that sick child died.
192703: A woman from a small farm in Stavele was always out to get near people's children. For that reason nobody trusted the woman. A mother who had seen the woman coming quickly hid the cradle with the baby. Then the woman said: "Is your baby sleeping? Doesn't it ever wake up? I'll come back another time." The mother answered: "No, you won't!"
192718: Some people went to gather wood in Mariakerke one morning. When the church bells began to ring, they met the priest, who said: "Well, don't you hear the bells?" The people answered: "Yes, but we have no time, because we have to gather wood. Otherwise we can't make a fire." The people worked all day. In the evening, however, they could no longer find the way home, so they had to leave all their wood behind in the wood. The priest had done this to them.
192735: To protect yourself against the mare, you had to make a little crown from a flat willow branch and hang it above your bed. A man who was ridden by the mare found a circle in the hair of his head, his moustache and his beard when he woke in the morning. To keep the mare away, you could also pray or place your clogs with the heels pointing towards the bed.
192739: On a farm a ghost goat was always seen walking about at night. After the people had promised to build a little chapel, the goat no longer appeared.
192748: A family from Izegem lived close to a café. One day a beggar woman had visited the house. That night the child's cradle flew up, so that the child flew a good metre into the air. An hour later the same thing happened again. That strange event repeated itself for three nights in a row.
192754: A man who worked in the brickworks in Vimal (France) came home one fine day. The man went for a walk with his wife and child. On the way back, however, the child cried the whole time. In the end the parents took the child to the friars. One of the clergymen said that a woman from the village was responsible for the trouble. When she came to visit again, they were to behave quite normally. After that the woman would never come back.
192761: In Zillebeke there once lived a rich gentleman who had married his maid. One day the maid murdered her husband by pushing him down the stairs. The crime was hushed up. Every three years, however, the house was in uproar and blood appeared on the stairs. The haunting only stopped when the house was donated to the church.
192769: A shoemaker coming home at night always saw a black dog at twelve o'clock. A little later the animal disappeared.
192781: A sorcerer had so much power that he could make people stand still for as long as he liked.
192802: On a fair Monday a carter drove past a witch's house with his threshing machine. Right in front of the witch's house a wheel flew off the cart, so that the threshing machine fell over and the carter lost a leg.
192824: A woman who lived in a small house was often visited by a neighbour who came to ask for something. The woman always answered: "Just take it!", because the neighbour was a witch. When the woman's child was ill, the neighbour was determined to visit the child. The woman went to the priest, who advised her to put an Agnus Dei under the threshold. The child recovered, but the neighbour never came to visit again.
192838: Near the burnt wood a gentleman lay dying. In the wood there was an animal that came closer and closer as the man's condition worsened. The animal kept calling: "Woe…woe…woe". People believed that the gentleman's possessions were all stolen goods. In the end the animal even sat on the threshold of the gentleman's bedroom. When the gentleman was dead, the animal had disappeared.
192845: A mother had a baby that could not sleep because it was always being pinched and so had bruises all over. Whenever the child was asleep, someone was always seen looking through the windows. In the end they went to the priest for the child.
192857: On the estate of Baron Peksteen a haunting bird could be heard calling from the Brand: "Oo...oo...oo...". That was the ghost of the late owner, who had taken the castle unjustly.
192863: A child had got convulsions after an old woman who sold caps had looked at it. People believed that this saleswoman could do witchcraft, for sometimes she was standing inside a house without anyone having let her in. Because the child was gravely ill, they had prayers read over it in Dullemonde (Deulémont). After that the child quickly recovered. Since then that old woman never again came into that family's house.
192864: Between the kursaal and a pier there was said to have once been a part of Oostende that was flooded by the sea. Sometimes the fishermen still heard a little bell ringing there from under the water.
192886: A rag-picker woman from Torhout often gave the children marshmallow sweets. When the children fell ill after eating those sweets, people believed their children had been bewitched by that witch.
192890: Near the neighbourhood 'De Slore' there was a crossroads where one street led to the neighbourhood, another to Izegem and yet another to Lendelede. At that crossroads stood an oak that was haunted every night. People made a long detour so as not to have to pass that oak. The tree was called 'de Toveresseknok' (the witch's tree).
192893:
A happily married woman said to her husband one day: "We are too happy. Something is bound to go wrong soon!"
At Candlemas the woman went out into the snow to fetch wood, when she suddenly heard a voice say: "Someone will die on the farm." The woman was so frightened that she dropped everything and ran inside. When her husband came home that evening, he had a fever and went to bed. A while later the fever went down, but the man felt so ill that he had to be taken to hospital. Shortly afterwards the man died. Not even half a year later one of the woman's sons died of leukaemia.
192898: Two women who were going to gather potatoes in the field had to pass the house of a witch. The witch, in her nightdress, was drawing water from a well and asked: "Where are you going?", to which the two women answered that they were going to gather potatoes. When the women reached the field, they saw the witch standing there with a full sack of potatoes, ready to leave.
192905: Some cattle dealers drove to Brugge with a donkey and cart to sell pigs there. On the way the dealers met a woman. A little further on, the seat of the cart broke. At the market the dealers had nothing but bad luck.
192908: On the Vuufwege lived a man to whom strange things happened. When the man let his cows out one day, one of the animals broke three legs. The man's four children spoke a strange language with each other, which people suspected was Hebrew. After the four children were separated from each other, no more strange things happened. The priests of Roeselare also came to exorcise the farm.
192958: A woman whose house was full of rats every night was advised by the priest to pour a bucket of boiling water over the animals. When the woman had done so, she found that a neighbour had burns.
192962: A woman who peddled goods always tried to get near newborn babies. Nobody let that woman in, because everyone was afraid of her.
192967: Around Christmas or another feast day people often saw a barn on fire. When they came closer, strangely enough there was no trace of the fire left.
192978: On a farm on the Stuver it was haunted at night. The window flew open, although it could not be opened from the outside. Then someone was heard running away and bumping into an iron fish bucket. A gentleman dressed all in white appeared and disappeared again a moment later. All these ghostly apparitions were witnessed by only one person; the other inhabitants of the farm were asleep.
192984: You could be ridden by the mare not only at night but also during the day. When that happened, you became frightened and got lost.
192998:
A young family had come to live on the Knok. One cold winter evening the man found his wife dead in the snow. The woman lay on her stomach and had clawed at the snow with her hands. Tracks of an enormous dog led to the body. Some people had seen the woman being chased on her way home by a big black dog with flaming eyes.
The man remarried a young girl from a neighbouring village. Because the girl did not want to work, the man sent her to boarding school for a while longer. When he went to visit the girl, he told no one that she was his wife. When the girl had time off, the man went to fetch her. In the evening they drove home along a deserted road. The two were almost home when they suddenly saw a funeral procession with four black horses appear out of the mist. The driver was a tall, thin gentleman dressed all in black. On both sides of the hearse walked ladies dressed in black with lanterns in their hands. On seeing all this, the girl quickly made the sign of the cross. At that the hearse broke in two with a loud crack and the whole scene vanished. The girl was so shaken by what she had seen that she fell ill. When the priest heard what had happened, he advised the man and the girl to repeat the whole thing. The priest would follow them at a short distance, because he was convinced the devil had something to do with it. On a stormy evening the man and the girl drove along that road again, this time accompanied by the priest. At the same spot the funeral procession appeared again. As soon as the priest approached the procession, the horses began to rear. The next moment the procession vanished into thin air. The priest came back with big drops of sweat on his head. From that evening on the man and the girl led a happy life. Out of gratitude they had a small chapel built on the spot where it happened.
193003: A man had a baby that was bewitched. For eleven months the child was ill. It cried day and night. After eleven and a half months the child died. The man realised that it was the neighbour woman who had bewitched his child.
193028: In winter werewolves were often seen. Some people who were baking waffles heard a werewolf making a racket outside. Someone threw the yarn from the spinning wheel outside together with some waffles. The wolf ate the waffles but got yarn all over its jaws. The next day a man from the neighbourhood had yarn between his teeth.
193031: In Dudzele lived a witch who made people fall into the water.
193038: In a house where the stove was burning, a woman came to warm her hands, saying: "Oh, oh, it's cold!" After that day the stove never burned again.
193052: On a farm in Beernem the people saw the wagon standing on the roof of the barn in the morning.
193058: A pregnant woman could not give birth as long as a witch stood looking at her.
193066: A witch who kept an inn made the carts of farmers who did not come to her for a drink tip over.
193067:
One night a woman heard her neighbour crying out in distress. Thinking it was a burglary, she rushed to help him. "I've been ridden by the mare again," the neighbour told the worried woman.
Branches that looked dried out and mouldy had also been ridden by the mare.
193089: Every Saturday a German shepherd went to Germany with his horse after speaking the magic formula: "Over everything." One Saturday the cowherd wanted to go along with the shepherd. But he made a mistake with the formula and said: "Through everything." As a result the cowherd got stuck in the first thorn hedge he came to. A second cowherd who wanted to go with the shepherd also got the formula wrong. The boy heard a horseshoe ring. It was the horseshoe of the horse that had caught on the tower of the Church of Our Lady in Antwerp.
193113: A woman who was going to fetch a pot of flaxseed from the drying kiln asked a man to go with her because it was dark. A little further on the woman let herself fall three times. Each time the man picked her up again. Later the man told his friends what had happened. His friends said he had been bewitched. Shortly afterwards the man fell ill. He consulted various people, but no one could cure him, so that the man finally died. When the man was dead, the witch always came to pray, but she was chased away by the widow.
193117: A man coming back from work could not find his house. When the man finally got home after wandering about for a long time, his relatives advised him next time to kneel down and pray an Our Father. For they believed that a certain person from the neighbourhood had made the man lose his way.
193152: A peddler who sold shoelaces had been sent away from a farm. A few days later that farm was full of rats. The farmer went to the peddler and promised to treat him well. After that the rats disappeared at once. That peddler could work magic.
193153: In Koekelare there lived a sorceress who paid people to weed her flax. While those people were working, the sorceress turned herself into a magpie so she could eavesdrop on their conversations.
193163: A man who wanted to know whether a witch from the neighbourhood could do witchcraft told the stable hand to drive his cart into the hedge. Even when eight horses had been brought in, the cart could not be pulled back onto the road. The witch then said to the man: "You asked the stable hand to drive into the hedge. If I weren't the neighbour of one of your relatives, you'd still be standing here tomorrow morning!" Only when the witch had said: "Go on, then," could the cart be freed.
193173: A man went with his mother to the Marktschip. On the way the two were accompanied by a big phantom dog.
193178: A poor family from Avelgem saw a little light appear outside every night. The people would get up and stand watching at the window. The light kept jumping over the tufts of grass. When it came closer to the window, the people quickly crept back into bed. Some people claimed that the light was the former occupant of that house returning. That man had been a drunkard.
193183: A man who was ridden by the mare saw a dog sitting on him, jumping up and down the whole time.
193190: A farmer's son had several times rung the parish priest's bell on Sunday evening. When the maid then called out: "Who's there?", there was no answer. When the joker rang the priest's bell again one Sunday night, the clergyman said to his maid: "You don't need to get up any more." After the joker had rung the bell a second time, his hand got stuck to the doorbell. When the priest left on Monday morning to say mass, he said to the boy: "Go on, go home now. Otherwise people will wonder what you're doing standing here with that doorbell in your hand."
193203: Under an old alder hedge near a farm in Pittem a small case filled with money was found. The case was taken to the farm. When the people went to their animals in the evening, they saw rats running all around their feet. The people consulted the priests of Tielt, who advised them to bury the case again where it had been found. After they had done so, the rats were gone.
193207: In Ieper a goat floated through the air, which was called Kalle Gete or Hemelgete.
193210: For a woman who was about to give birth, someone went to fetch the doctor in Poelkapelle. When the doctor drove past the Schreiboom (1) with his horse and cart, his horse suddenly stopped. The doctor then saw that there was an old woman sitting in the tree. "It's your fault I can't go on," the doctor said to the old woman. The old woman answered: "I have to do something to live." This woman had special powers.
193211: On a farm in Izegem the maid was dismissed because they had found out she was a thief. When the maid came a week later to ask if she could come back, they refused to take her on. "I'll get you yet," the maid had said angrily. The next day thirty pigeons flew away from the farm. As if that were not enough, the horse and several cows also lay dead. After the friars had read prayers over the farm, the misery came to an end.
193226: A man who was going to get a shave met a ghost on the way, carrying its head under its arm.
193235: A farmhand going home in the evening had to cross a brook where a plank served as a bridge. Because a big cat was sitting on the plank, the farmhand said: "If you don't go away, I'll throw this pot of lard at your head!" The farmhand had been given a pot of pig fat by the maid. The cat stayed put, so the farmhand threw the pot at the animal. The next day the farmhand saw that the maid had a bandage around her head.
193241: Anyone ridden by the mare went completely stiff and could no longer make a sound.
193244: Many people claimed that a doodkaars (death candle) was a light created by the vapours rising from the marshes. Older people believed that doodkaarsen appeared in places where money was hidden.
193266: A woman came to a farm peddling thread and ribbons. Because the people bought nothing, the woman said: "If you don't buy anything, you'll remember me yet!" and left. Some time later the people of the farm were covered in lice.
193284: A man who was going to Brugge early in the morning saw turnips lying on the ground along the way. The man knocked the turnips with his stick. At that the turnips ran off to the brook.
193324: To find out whether a woman could do witchcraft, one had to close all the windows and doors while she was in the house. Then one had to make the woman angry. The woman would then want to leave. If she was a witch, she would fly away through the walls.
193371: In Leffinge there once lived a witch who tormented people by sticking pins into a doll.
193373: A twelve-year-old boy lay gravely ill in bed. One day a cat was seen lying under the boy's bed. When the boy had died, the cat ran off through the water drain. A little later the sound of someone walking about in clogs was heard.
193424: During haymaking people saw a beautiful procession every evening. The people in the procession always wore a white robe, but strangely enough they never carried a crucifix.
193426: In Ardooie lived an old woman who could work magic. Whenever that woman had laid her hand on a child's head, the child was covered in lice shortly afterwards.
193427: A girl was learning dressmaking from a widow who lived with her three daughters in Stuverberge (Oostkamp). When the girl went to look at the pigs eating at midday, the animals were suddenly thrown from one wall to the other until they were dead. In the evening the women sat sewing for a long time because they had a lot of work. At midnight the light suddenly went out. Because they could not light it again, the women had to go upstairs in the dark. When the three daughters lay in bed at night, their blankets were pulled off by a creature that crawled around on hands and feet. The blankets of the apprentice girl were always left untouched.
193435: In Zevekote lived a woman who could make a cart of vegetables fall over and make children cry. If a piece of paasnagel (an Easter blessing token) was sewn into the children's clothes, that woman could do them no more harm.
193440: In Klerken, on the road to the Woumen castle, a man saw a cat. He kicked at the cat but could not hit the animal.
193457: A girl from Oostende whose boyfriend had run off went to consult a little old woman from Oostende. The woman advised the girl to pray to Saint Anthony. A while later the runaway boyfriend came back sweating. He claimed that at midnight he had seen his girlfriend's face.
193458: A man from Lissewege was ridden by the mare. A lady dressed in white squeezed his throat shut. The man tried to strike the mare away, but he could not. To drive off the mare, you had to pray a lot.
193461: A married woman whose daughter still lived in Ruddervoorde was compelled to bewitch small children. When she touched such children, they fell ill or died.
193489: In Westkerke there was a farm where music was heard every night. In the morning the cows there had been untied. That farm was haunted.
193499: A woman went to visit her sister who lived close by. But when the woman went back, she got lost. She was on the way for four hours, although the walk normally took only five minutes! When the woman came to the brook, she could find her bearings again. The next day the woman went to the shop. On the way she saw a neighbour standing at her door, who said: "Did your walk go all right yesterday?" At that moment the woman realised who had bewitched her the day before.
193505: In winter, threshing could be heard in an oat barn until a quarter past twelve at night. Moreover, the windmill turned by itself. Nobody was to be seen and in the morning there was nothing strange to be found in the barn.
193509: On some farms noises were heard at night as if someone were threshing. When people went to look, however, there was nothing to be seen.
193526: A woman who went to mass every day one day saw a gentleman standing there, dressed all in black. The gentleman gave her a letter on which the address of the recipient was written. The woman delivered the letter to the recipient, and she never saw that gentleman again. It must have been the devil or a ghost.
193530: A werewolf worked on a farm in Deerlijk. One day they managed to burn the werewolf's skin in the oven, and so the boy was released.
193549: At a farm where all the farmhands met with accidents, a man came asking for work. "It's no use, they all have accidents here," said the farmer. The man was not put off, however, and became a farmhand on the farm. At night the farmhand left the door of the horse stable open. At night he always saw a white horse appear. One night the farmhand managed to seize the animal and ride it until it was drenched in sweat. He had the horse shod by the smith. The next day the farmer's wife lay in bed with horseshoes on her arms and legs.
193557: A woman going from Passendale to Rozebeke passed a witch's house in the Ommegangsbos. The house was on fire and the witch sat inside in her shift, watching. Behind the house stood a man throwing sheets into the fire, but the sheets would not burn. The next day, however, the house looked just as before, without any trace of a fire.
193561: A farm in Kachtem was badly haunted. On winter evenings beautiful music was heard in the attic. The farm was exorcised by the parish priest, but that did not help. The people were advised to hang a paasnagel (a nail blessed at Easter) on the beams. After they had done so, no more music was heard in the evenings.
193562: On a farm that was haunted, the farmer was ruined.
193581: Three people stayed sitting on their chairs after mass. The parish priest had bewitched them so they were stuck to their chairs.
193584: Anyone ridden by the mare during their sleep began to sweat and suffer pain.
193588:
A doctor who was always shabbily dressed could cure anyone. The man often left his donkey with a farmer for two weeks and visited his patients on foot. There were eggshells everywhere in the doctor's house. When the doctor met people who thought he was just a strange fellow, he bewitched them so they were fixed to the ground.
One day the doctor was murdered. No one ever found out who did it.
193613: Some boys always played with a girl who could make mice. One day the priest took the girl's magic away from her.
193619: A man returning from the fair was followed the whole way by a little cat. The man took the cat home, where he put it under a tub and laid his wedding ring on the tub. The next day an exhausted woman was sitting under the tub.
193644: At midnight in Oostende no one could walk across the sluice gates anymore. Every time someone came by, big cats sat on the gates, dancing and blocking the passer-by's way. Only after twelve o'clock could people get through again.
193667: On a farm where a witch often came to fetch butter, one day they could no longer churn butter. Bakelandt came to the farm and said a witch was responsible for the misfortune. He began to pray until the drops of sweat rolled down his face, and he advised the farmer to put dung in the butter churn. It was said that the woman who had bewitched the butter had suffered a great deal.
193685: In Oostende lived a witch who was said to own books of magic. In the mornings that witch often came to buy fish on the boats. If she got none, she cursed the fishermen. One day the witch had given two figs to a woman from the village. But the woman was so afraid of the witch that she did not dare eat the figs. When the woman's sons came home a little later, they said they had lost all the fish they had caught in their nets.
193686: A man who could no longer churn butter went to consult the priest. The clergyman advised the man not to give any butter to the first person who came asking for it. After that had happened, the man could make butter again. But he never told anyone who that first person was who had come asking for butter.
193687: On a farm in Rugge strange noises were heard every night. It sounded as if someone were moving chairs and chopping wood. When the sons got up, there was nothing to be seen. When the curate of Avelgem came to exorcise the farm, he was immediately dragged into the manure pit by the spirit.
193706: The lord of a sunken castle in Beveren came back after his death because he had hidden a large sum of money somewhere.
193714: In Klemskerke there was a house that was haunted. When the people went to bed, they heard noises as if someone were churning. As soon as the people got up, nothing more could be heard. Before feast days candles always burned on the roof of that house.
193730: In the evening stalkeersen (ghost lights) were seen coming out of the ground. People said they were souls from purgatory who came to ask for help. The lights disappeared again once people had prayed for them.
193737: Some people told a peddler that they could not manage to churn butter. Because the churn was bewitched, the peddler advised them to pour dung into it. While they were doing so, the witch walked past.
193757: Little doves were walking about on the sea dyke. When one of the doves went into the sea, a whole lot of little devils appeared.
193781: At the inn 'de Appel' the horses could not go on. A woman from the neighbourhood was fetched, who said: "You aren't holding the reins properly." After that the people could go on with their horse. After the priests had blessed the road with prayers, the witchcraft came to an end. When the curate had taken away that woman's books, the witch could no longer do anything.
193802: In Middelkerke lived a witch who had an excellent memory. She knew everyone's date of birth and death, down to the hour.
193829: A beautiful woman from Adegem often came to visit a man. When the woman was not there, a strange cat sat in the man's house. The man kicked at the animal, but the cat would not be chased away. When the man finally got hold of the cat, it fell on its back. That was very strange, since cats normally never fall on their backs. After that incident the woman from Adegem never visited again.
193832: A girl who worked on a farm in Hollebeke was bewitched. The girl cried all day long. Someone advised the people to pour boiling water around the girl. The day after they had done so, a woman was seen walking about with a bandage around her arm.
193835: People who were ridden by the mare felt in their sleep as if someone was pulling at them. Those people were frightened.
193838: When X had touched a child, the child became paralysed.
193862: In 1925 a man went to France to start a farm there in an old convent called 'Font-Ogée'. About that convent people said: "At Font-Ogée there are hidden treasures." A woman from the area predicted that the man would never have luck with his farm because it was cursed. The woman's prediction came true; the cows, horses and pigs all died and part of the farm even burned down. One day the farmer's wife saw that woman sitting on a post beside the church. When the woman asked the farmer's wife whether she had been to mass, the latter answered: "You know very well I've been to mass, because I go every day!" The next moment the woman had vanished without a trace. She must have had a book of magic with her. In the end the farmer had so many debts that he had to leave the farm. After that the farm was never leased again.
193868: A mother whose little daughter had died at the age of eight was pregnant with her third child. During High Mass the mother was visited by a sorceress with two goats, who came to ask for someone's address. That mother's child suffered a great deal. It seemed as if the child was being pricked with pins all over. Whenever the sorceress stuck pins into a cushion at home, the child was pricked by the pins. The mother sent for a priest, who advised her to make a novena. During those nine days the child always had to wear the same little shirt. Whenever the child's nappies were washed, a drop of holy water always had to be put on them. Every night the child woke at twelve o'clock. It would then start crying and have convulsions. During the last night of the novena, the grandmother slept beside the child's bed. That night the grandmother got a box on the ear that nearly sent her flying against the wall.
193870: In a house in Waarmaarde there was always a sound at night as if someone were shovelling grain, although nothing could be seen. When the neighbour was told what had happened, she said: "The previous occupants once promised to give a hectolitre of grain to the poor." After the people had done so, they heard no more strange noises at night.
193877: Anyone ridden by the mare in their bed could not move and felt as if a sack of flour was lying on them. A man who had got lost near Koekelarebos had also been a victim of the mare.
193897: In Gistel lived a woman who could give children the evil hand. Such children got an illness, for example tuberculosis. Bewitched children had to have prayers read over them by the priest.
193932: A man who went to fetch the midwife was followed by a big dog. The man did not dare say anything and saw every passer-by make the sign of the cross.
193934:
A doctor who had first studied for the priesthood could work wonders. When one night in the Gotschalkbos in Wijtschate the doctor was attacked by two robbers shouting: "Your money or your life!", the doctor answered: "I have no money, but wait a moment. I'll go home to fetch money and bring it to you!" Then the doctor bewitched the two robbers so they were fixed to the ground. The doctor quickly went to alert the police so that the robbers could be arrested.
