One day, when the doctor was returning from Kemmel in the rain, he met two men at a crossroads. "Good day, doctor," said the men, and the doctor replied: "Good evening to you both." Then the men said: "We'd like to get on quickly, because it's pouring down!", to which the doctor replied: "Of course, you needn't wait for me!" However hard the two men tried to get ahead, they kept walking beside the doctor the whole way, and they broke out in a sweat.
The doctor's house was cleaned by a maid, who had a lover. One day, while the maid was at work, the doorbell rang. The doctor opened the door and received a blow to the face, and he fell down dead. The maid and her lover were arrested and taken to prison, where they both died. The parish priest said: "No one needs to be prosecuted any more, because the doctor's murderer has confessed on his deathbed."
193942: A man walking home in the evening saw a nun standing on either side of him. The man was terrified.
193947: On a farm the babies were born with horns. The children had to be killed. At that time there were three evil women living in the village.
193948: In Marke lived a witch who liked to tease people. When she saw women scrubbing, she made those women dance on their brushes. In the evenings people no longer dared go out on the street for fear of that witch.
193963: In Lombardsijde lived a fishwife who could do witchcraft. If people had been given one herring too many by the witch, they threw it into the stove just to be safe.
193971: The cowshed of a farm was haunted every night. When people went to look, however, there was nothing strange to be seen.
193992: A trader taking his goods to Veurne saw the priest standing at his door in a village along the way. When the trader arrived at the market in Veurne, that same priest was strangely enough standing there too.
193994: Anyone ridden by the mare got lost.
194000: A witch had asked a boy whether he would go to the shop for her. But his mother would not let him. The next day the poor boy was covered in sores.
194002: Sorceresses could turn themselves into a goat.
194009: A farmer who came home drunk took his horse out of the stable and rode through the crops. One night the farmer drowned in the well behind the farm. Since then the farm was haunted. At night the cows could be heard drinking and then falling down as if they were dead. In the morning the cows behaved completely normally. One day a chaplain from Sleihage and one from Nieuwkerke came to read prayers over the farm. The farmer's wife said to the clergymen: "I know very well what is going on here."
194021: One day a witch was sitting in the church of Rumbeke. When the parish priest was reading from his book, the pages were so full of lice that the text became illegible. "If you don't stop that witchcraft, I will make your name known," the priest had said.
194023: People who were ridden by the mare had nightmares caused by poor digestion. A person who was ridden by the mare lay shouting and raging and felt something hairy on their feet.
194030: A child that had worms was prayed over by a priest who said: "Tonight a sorceress will come by. She will tell you where a doll full of pins is hidden." After that doll had been burned, the witchcraft was over.
194038: The will-o'-the-wisps that people saw in the churchyard were the souls of the returning dead.
194044: A man returning from Loppem along the railway met people from Zedelgem on the way, who called out: "Aren't you home yet, you bungler?" The man walked on, frightened. When he looked back a moment later, strangely enough there was no trace of those people.
194066: On a farm by the Meerbaan in Zwevezele pumping was always heard at night. The people eventually moved, but they took the manure pump with them, so their new home was haunted too.
194071: A French deserter was hiding in a haunted castle in Staden. The man had warned the owner several times, but every time the owner came to look, there was no sign of the haunting.
194093: A woman whose mother had died three weeks earlier saw her mother's ghost standing at the foot of the bed at night. The mother had once promised to go and serve in Brugge and she now came to ask her daughter to fulfil that promise. After that had been done, the ghost never appeared again.
194099: In Aartrijke lived a witch who bewitched children.
194122: An Iceland fisherman who was back from a voyage wanted to go to the fair in Adinkerke. With an admission ticket for the dance hall one could walk in and out all evening. The man had got the ticket from his neighbour, who had already been dancing and was now going home. When the man wanted to go in with the ticket, the woman checking the tickets said: "I haven't seen you here yet!" "Oh yes you have," the man lied. But the woman stood her ground. Then the man said angrily: "You witch with your crooked mouth!" A little later the man's mouth was crooked too.
194126: A doodkeers (death candle, ghost light) was a little light that moved in all directions. They were dead people who returned because their souls had no rest.
194127: A farmer coming back from Staden saw something lying on the road. It was a man lying flat on his back. When the farmer came closer, the man began to growl and got up on his hands and knees. The farmer knew what was going on; the man had been bewitched by a woman who had special powers.
194134: There used to be a song about a dead man who was buried under the floor of the church of Beernem. The dead man returned to ask for prayers for his soul, which was in purgatory.
194146: In an inn a little baby lay in a cradle. One day a woman came to visit and said: "What a lovely baby!" Since the woman was a mother herself, she wanted to pick the child up to feel how much it weighed. When the woman had left, the child began to cry without stopping. The innkeeper advised his wife to take the child to the friars. So the mother walked to the friars with her bewitched child. The friars were willing to make the witch pass by, so that the mother could see who it was. But the mother answered: "No, better not, because my husband is very hot-tempered and he would be capable of going to the witch's house and murdering her." When the mother went home again, her child no longer cried. The woman put a little cross under the threshold, as the friars had advised her. The child grew up into a healthy man, who later became a soldier.
194157: Young people with a high fever sometimes lost control of themselves, jumped up and began to scream because they felt someone was holding them. Of such people it was said that they had been ridden by the mare.
194160: When a light was seen on the water or by the mast of a ship, bad weather was coming and no fish could be caught.
194161: A farmer's wife had a maid who was ridden by the mare every night. The farmer's wife advised the girl to take a bread knife to bed in the evening and point the blade towards her body. But the maid made a mistake and held the knife the other way round. The next day the farmer's wife lay dead by the trough.
194213: The dead returned to point out their hidden money. In the old days people were very afraid that they would return after their death.
194216: A parish priest from Reningelst was threatened one night in Poperinge by a thief, who said: "Your money or your life!" The clergyman replied: "I have no money on me, but if you like, you can have my wristwatch." When the thief held out his hand to take the watch, the priest said: "You will now stay standing there until I decide you may leave again." The thief indeed had to stand there stock-still.
194226: A house where three unmarried daughters lived was haunted. Around midnight twenty-one cats came into the house through the drain hole for the water. The youngest daughter was annoyed by the cats and poured boiling water on the last cat she saw. The next morning the eldest daughter was still lying in her bed with burns on her face.
194236: When a rich geus (Protestant) lay on his deathbed at night, music was heard playing. The dying man's wife opened the window, after which the devils came to take the corpse away. The man's brains were stuck to the wall.
194239: A shoemaker who was also a wizard could make people lose their way. One day, when the wizard was standing at the market with another man, he said: "Come on, let's see who gets home first!" The next morning the other man was still out walking, because he had got lost.
194267: People who were ridden by the mare in their bed were having a dream or had trouble with their blood pressure.
194271: Doodkeersen (death candles, ghostly lights) appeared in places where something was hidden or where something had happened. If you had beckoned to such a light, it came closer. If you then had nothing to give, you were struck to the ground.
194272: A witch hurried to a woman who had just given birth. When the witch had gone, the baby began to cry until it was dead. The parish priest had tried to take the witch's books from her, but she would not give them up. When the witch rode along with a man to Mariakerke, the man said: "Don't you dare touch my daughter, mind!"
194274: A magpie that seemed to laugh always flew towards the house of a witch from the village.
194279: In Lapscheure lived a woman who was never allowed near small children. That woman could make children get 'the black burn'. No doctor could help those children then.
194296: A sorcerer could send a plague of rats to someone he was angry with. In the same way the sorcerer could also make the rats disappear again and send them to another house.
194306: A woman came to visit a farmer's wife, bringing two eggs with her. The farmer's wife refused to boil the eggs for the woman. The next day the farmer's wife's bread was mouldy. The parish priest advised her to bake a new loaf. Because that bread went mouldy too, the priest advised her to try baking a loaf at her sister's. Strangely enough, it worked there. After the priest had said prayers over the farmer's wife's house, the problems came to an end.
194316: In a house where a woman had died, music was heard in the attic. The sacks that stood in the attic had disappeared. That woman had once been told by a neighbour that she would be full of lice when she died. Although the woman had always lived very hygienically, she was indeed full of lice when she died.
194350: A woman could not get along with a farmer from the village. Whenever that woman walked past the farmer, the poor man's load tipped over. The load could then not be lifted to put it back.
194370: On the Doorn in Kleit lived a man who had seen the witte wagen (white wagon) or hellewagen (hell wagon) rolling. When that man was coming back from Maldegem, he saw a barrel lying by the Jonge Jansdreef. The man walked around the barrel but did not touch it. When the man came back to the same spot the next day, the barrel had disappeared, and the footprints were still undisturbed.
194379: A ghost ship was said to sail around off Heist, whose crew could be heard calling out.
194387: In Veurne lived a woman who owned books of magic. A man from the village had a little son and a little daughter. The son died in a strange way. Two years later the little daughter lay in her bed with her eyes open. The girl would not eat or drink and did not speak. After forty days the father went to the parish priest. But the clergyman said it was already too late.
194394: The bell of the church of Sint-Martinus was said to have once sunk into a bottomless pit. On Christmas Day that bell could be heard ringing.
194401: On a farm in Beselare all the cows died for an unknown reason. A friar was brought from Ieper, but he could not help. In the end they consulted a quack from Beselare. The man cut one of the cows open, sprinkled something into it and then said prayers over the animal. After that, there was no more misfortune on the farm. The farmer had fallen victim to a woman who wanted to do him harm.
194407: Near Pittem there was always a mewing cat that followed passers-by. One day a man had kicked the cat. Strangely enough, the landlady of a nearby café knew that the man had kicked the animal.
194417: Duitse schapers (German shepherds, travelling shepherds said to have magic powers) could tap beer from the ground with their staffs.
194428: Every night a woman was tormented by a man or a woman she had to fight. People to whom this happened had to be woken by calling them by name.
194433: One evening a farmer was walking home along a road bordered by a hedge on one side and a ditch on the other. Many cats were always seen on that road. If one kicked at them, one could never hit them. One day the farmer did manage to hit one of the cats. The next moment, however, the man was thrown into the ditch by a strange force.
194438: An innkeeper's wife had a married daughter whose children, strangely enough, all died. After the innkeeper's wife had moved away, the daughter had eight more children. The evil hand had, after all, been put out of action.
194444: A sick man consulted the friars of Tielt. The friars said to the man: "You are very ill. Nothing more can be done. A woman who visited you did this to you. You will never see that woman again." One Saturday evening the man had been visited by his sister. When the man had washed, he had forgotten to put back on the blessed object he had received from the friars of Izegem.
194446: A café owner had to fetch beer from the cellar for the people who had attended a christening. The café owner gave her child a potato from the pot on the stove. After that the child would eat nothing but potatoes. The child also began to have epileptic fits. The woman went with a coal merchant to the friars of Roeselare. The woman had to say a prayer for nine days. But on the ninth day her child died. The café owner knew who had bewitched her child. A woman sometimes came and stood in front of the café, sticking out her tongue. One day the café owner threw that woman out. The woman then said: "This is a public place, so you can't throw me out." The woman left all the same.
194452: A man walking home one evening was followed the whole time by a cat. The man kicked the animal in the backside and in doing so ended up in the ditch himself.
194462: Anyone who fell victim to the mare at night could hear the trapdoor to the attic open. Then they turned pale and felt short of breath. They could not move, nor could they make any sound. The mare could lie on her victim for as long as half an hour.
194464: On a farm chains could be heard rattling every evening. It was so bad that people no longer dared to go outside at night. They believed the rattling was caused by returning dead from the old castle of Beselare.
194468: When a barn owl sat by the back door, someone in that house would soon die.
194469: A woman never wanted to walk across the churchyard because a white goat haunted it.
194496: Hardly anyone dared to go into the Boeschepestraat, because the ghost of a dead person always appeared there. One night a father and son decided to keep watch in that street. That time no ghost appeared at midnight.
194499: A parish priest had to walk a long way to help with a funeral in a village. On the way the priest saw a drunkard lying by the road, who said: "Just keep going, black crow!" The offended clergyman made sure the drunkard could take only ten more steps. When the priest came back in the afternoon, he saw the drunkard still lying on the ground. This time the man said: "Good day, Father!" The clergyman replied: "So now I'm Father, and this morning I was still a black crow! Get up and go home. Make sure it doesn't happen again!"
194506: Some boys who were manuring the field saw an apple, a grape and a nut lying on the field next to which a witch's house stood. The boys talked a bit about the witch's sorcery and then went into her house. "I'd stop talking about me if I were you!" said the witch. Later the boys said to each other: "You see, she is a witch! She heard everything while we were in the field and she was sitting inside her house!"
194511: If the priest left his missal open, he could see the witches in the church with a candle on their heads. Moreover, the witches could not leave the church as long as the book was not closed.
194545: A boy who had kicked a black cat was never able to find a woman of his choice to marry.
194546: On the threshold of a house in Moerkerke sat a little dog only as big as a fist. A woman walking past the little dog said a few short prayers. Twenty metres further on, the woman saw the little dog turn into a ball that rolled after her. Frightened, the woman ran away.
194570: A sorceress from Stavele owned a little doll. When she pressed on the heart or hand of that doll, she could make a child cry with pain. With such practices a sorceress could even make people die.
194580: Some men out together were followed by a cat. After one of the men had made the sign of the cross and kicked the animal, the cat disappeared.
194591: On a farm in Nieuwkerke there was much misfortune because evil reigned there. During High Mass a curate from Roeselare came to exorcise the farm. When that was done, the clergyman was completely drenched in sweat. After that the evil had gone from the farm.
194663: On a farm in Bekegem butter could no longer be made. The farmer's wife was convinced that a sorceress from the neighbourhood was responsible for the misfortune. Because of this, the farmer's wife would not stay on the farm for any money.
194664: A woman going to the five o'clock Mass on Christmas Day was followed along the way by a roll.
194668: A woman had narrowly escaped death three times after being bewitched by her neighbour. The parish priest of Lichtervelde said prayers over the woman. All the doors had to be shut. The clergyman predicted that a woman would come by who would do everything to get inside. A little later the neighbour did indeed come rattling at the door. The sick woman's mother threw the neighbour out. The sorceress even took the little gate with her and set it up in her own garden, so as to get into the sick woman's house that way after all.
194686: Some people were travelling by horse and cart. At a house on a hill, the horses suddenly refused to go on after the woman who lived there had come outside. The men grew angry and threatened the witch, saying: "We'll beat you to death if you don't let us go on!" After the witch had gone inside, the horses could go on again.
194687: On a farm there was a real plague of rats. It was so bad that the rats crawled over the backs of the cows and horses. On the farmer's wife's advice, the farmer sent for a friar. The clergyman told the cowherd to gather bramble branches and lay them on a heap of straw. Then the friar set the straw alight. All the rats then ran to the burning straw and died. The procession was closed by a big rat that walked very slowly to the fire.
194689: One day in Poperinge the procession was cancelled because it was raining too hard and because people did not want the beautiful clothes of the statue of Mary to get dirty. Although the rain kept on, the statue of Mary went out alone that night. For the next day the priest of the Sint-Jan church found that the statue's clothes were completely dirty. Since then the procession has never been cancelled again, however bad the weather.
194696: Some farmers on their way to a farm met a woman with a pig. Because that woman had conjured up spruce woods around the farmers, the farmers got lost.
194712: Some people playing cards in an inn suddenly saw frogs jumping about everywhere. There was a witch sitting in the inn.
194714: A man on his way to Brugge thought that a walking stick was going along with him the whole time.
194721: A man whose brother was at sea heard a noise in the warehouse as if all sorts of things were being smashed. Yet there was no one to be seen. A while later the man learned that his brother had been killed in an accident.
194732: In Sint-Andries a dog roamed about that always pushed people into the water. A man had often tried to catch that dog, but he had never succeeded.
194740: A farmer's wife who had a beautiful child was often visited by an old woman who came to fetch milk. Every time that woman visited, the child began to cry. A beggar whom the farmer's wife had told what was going on wanted to have a word with that woman. In the end the woman admitted that she had bewitched the child, and she brought out a little doll into which she had stuck pins. When the last pin was stuck into the doll, the child would die. The beggar forced the woman to take the pins out of the doll again. While the woman did so, the child cried. When the last pin had been taken out of the doll, the child fell silent.
194758: During the First World War a woman whose husband was in the army saw her husband appear with a big dog at twelve o'clock on three consecutive nights. A large plate of food was put out for the dog. Strangely enough, the plate was empty the next morning. The woman developed epilepsy.
194767: A sorceress went from one farm to another to tend the pigs. Whenever that woman met a horse cart in the street, the horses immediately bolted. When the farmers heard that, they no longer dared to let that woman near their pigs.
194780:
A man and a woman were coming back from the market in Torhout with a pigeon. When the man wanted to show the pigeon to someone else on the way, it flew out of his hands. The man then said: "Pigeon, I order you to sit on that stake". The pigeon came back to the man, who had special powers.
The same wizard had a relationship with a woman who also had a second lover. Whenever that other lover visited the woman, there was always a black cat sitting on the windowsill that would not be chased away. That cat was the wizard, who had turned himself into an animal.
194807: A skipper always had bad luck when he was at sea. The man saw swans on the water that came close to the ship and would not go away. One day when the skipper hauled in his fishing nets, there was only one sole in them. Because the catch was far too poor, the skipper threw the sole back into the sea. Then the man went to the parish priest, who said: "You are bewitched. If you had thrown that sole into the fire, the witch would have been burned." The clergyman then said prayers over the skipper and gave him holy water. But the man still had a lot of bad luck at sea. The priest gave him a crucifix to hang on the fishing net. After a long time things improved.
194819: A man had been reading books in someone else's house. When the man came into his own house the next day, he found rats everywhere. The man had read wrongly.
194830: Whistling was not allowed on a ship. People believed that a storm would then rise or that the wind would suddenly drop.
194838: During a heavy thunderstorm a witch said to the people standing next to her: "Look at the sky tearing open over there! Let the others get wet; we will stay dry!"
194852: In Avelgem a witch always walked the streets. One day a girl said to her friend: "Oh, X is there! I'm going home quickly!" That friend told the witch that the girl had run away from her. When the girl came home, her mother's socks were full of lice.
194861: During the Second World War a strange apparition was always seen on the Rode Berg. The English went there.
194877: Some men who were going to plough the field saw a little table with a bottle and two glasses standing by the Kattenput. When the men came closer, everything had vanished.
194898: A house near the Kouter was so badly haunted that nobody dared to walk past it.
194905: On a farm worked a maid who was ridden by the mare. Someone advised her to lay a four-pronged fork on her chest before going to sleep. The next day the maid found that the cowherd had four holes in his head.
194916: A man was beaten up by an invisible figure in the moonlight. The man believed that a witch from the neighbourhood had done this to him.
194918: A farmer and his wife from Wenduine were driving their livestock past Nieuwmunster to the market in Bruges. When on the way they saw lights still burning at a haunted farm, they knew it was still very early in the morning. At that farm there were also always beautiful little foals lying in the meadow in the evening. In the morning those foals had always disappeared. One day the farmer of the haunted farm went to the priest for advice because he had so much misfortune. The clergyman said to the farmer: "It is unfortunate, but I can give you only one piece of advice: make sure you all get along well with each other, then the haunting has no power." After that the farm was no longer haunted.
194933: A man who was afraid of nothing was coming home one evening from visiting his sweetheart. At a thorn hedge, around eleven o'clock, the man saw a girl dressed in white floating some thirty centimetres above the ground. "Good evening", said the man, but the white figure did not answer. Just past the thorn hedge the strange apparition had vanished. When he got home the man fell ill with fright. The doctor was the first person the man told about what he had experienced.
195002: A woman whose child cried all the time sent for the parish priest. "That child is being pricked by pins," said the priest, and he began to pray. When the priest had finished praying, the child's bed was full of pins.
195007: A man who was still working in his potato field at eleven o'clock at night saw the parish priest coming from the station. "You're late," the priest said to the man, to which the man replied: "So are you, Father!" After that the man could not move a foot in his field for an hour.
195018: In the Galgebos between Kerkhove and Elsegem shouting and raging could be heard. There was also always a lot of wind. People who walked through those woods at night got a hunchback or another disability. People claimed that dead freemasons came to haunt those woods.
195025: A farmer had a stable where strange things happened. Every time the farmer put a horse in the stable, the animal lay dead the next morning. The priest advised the farmer to pretend to be dead and lie in the stable at night. When the farmer did so, he saw two ghosts come in, dig up a chest of money and start counting it. The priest advised the farmer to dig up the money himself. In the money chest the farmer found a letter that read: "Have masses said with this money and we will be saved". After the farmer had masses said, the ghosts did not return.
195047: Behind a little chapel in Aartrijke people heard music and rattling and saw lights. When they came closer, however, there was nothing to be seen. Sometimes a funeral procession could also be seen passing by at night.
195061: Anyone who passed a witch's house always had bad luck. People broke a leg, fell off their bike or saw all the fruit fall off the cart.
195126: A woman claimed she could give the schoolboys lice.
195130: People troubled by a plague of rats or mice went on pilgrimage to Bovekerke because they believed witchcraft was involved.
195142: In Slijpe a priest had died who, after his death, appeared at night in the churchyard in the form of a large flame.
195150: An Iceland fisherman did nothing but curse the whole time. One day one of the other fishermen saw a whale swimming alongside the ship. At that the fisherman called out to the curser: "The devil is after you!" The curser was too afraid to leave his cabin.
195163: When people went for a walk in the evening, they were often followed by a gentleman who sometimes wore shoes and sometimes clogs. When they looked back, strangely enough, there was nothing to be seen.
195172: A man coming home in the evening or at night saw a little man sitting on the wall of a farmstead. That was a returning dead person.
195201: A man who woke up at night could not get up because a heavy weight lay on him. When someone began to talk to the man, the mare suddenly vanished.
195202: A man found a little box by the side of the road and took it with him. In the box were three little devils. Such little devils had to be given a lot of work every day, for example by scattering colza seed and rapeseed. Otherwise one was beaten by the little devils oneself. Once one had such a box, the only way to get rid of it was to lose it.
195214: People who slept on their left side felt a weight. That was the mare coming to ride them.
195229: The dead often came back because they still had a debt to settle or because something had not yet been arranged.
195237: A man who did not dare to drive past a witch's house decided to go by boat. The witch made the boat capsize.
195254:
To protect yourself against the mare, you had to say:
"Mare, mare, keep far away
through dyke and dale, through copper and steel
through all the gutters
before you reach my bed".
195256: A German shepherd asked a man: "Aren't you going to Christmas in England? It's so beautiful!" The German shepherd and the man flew to England on two horses. On the way one of the horses struck a church tower with its leg. After mass the man wanted to stay a little longer. The shepherd, however, flew back home. The next year the man went to mass again. When he saw the German shepherd there, he asked: "Can you take me back to Belgium?", to which the shepherd replied: "Yes, on condition that you say nothing." The man flew along with the shepherd on a little billy goat. At a certain moment, however, the man said: "Such a little billy goat and such a big leap!" At that the goat flew off and the man fell into the water.
195265: If someone felt uneasy during their sleep, it was said that the person was being ridden by the mare.
195289: Two men going hare hunting saw two eyes as red as fire in the distance. When the men had shot at a hare leaping away, the eyes had suddenly disappeared.
195293: A woman whose child was gravely ill went to the Friars Minor of Tielt, who said: "You must give a large piece of meat to the first woman who comes to visit tomorrow." The people did as they had been advised. The next day the neighbour came to visit. Afterwards that neighbour never came to those people again, and the child recovered.
195307: A girl had to take a pig to a butcher in Bulskamp. When the girl arrived, it turned out that the butcher's wife had already sold the pig, even though she had not known that the girl was bringing a pig.
195313: At the Schoendale farm the dead lord returned. Every evening he drove along the lane in a beautiful coach drawn by four horses.
195316: In winter a ghost giving off a green light could be seen walking about in Dudzele.
195330: A doctor from Abele was riding home on horseback after visiting a sick person. On the way the doctor was stopped by a robber, who shouted: "Your money or your life!" Using his magic powers, the doctor made the robber stand still, so that he could no longer get away.
195336: People who were out at night sometimes saw a dog, a cat or an alarm clock around them. That was the devil.
195352: At 't Sas in Ruddervoorde there lay a bluestone threshold. One day people went to fetch that threshold with two wheelbarrows. When they got home the people were dead tired. At midnight they heard a goat bleating. A little later the goat stood with its forelegs against the windowsill. The people looked outside and saw a big snow-white billy goat dancing on the bluestone threshold. The same thing happened twelve nights in a row. After that the people took the threshold back to 't Sas.
195375: The mare was something that roamed about at night and fell upon people. Some people placed their shoes upside down under their bed to prevent being ridden by the mare.
195396: A man and his wife were getting ready in the morning to go to early mass. When the woman pulled up the shutters, she saw that the yard was full of hens. The woman went out to the street, where a farmer was just passing with his cows. "Haven't you seen any hens?" the woman asked him, to which the farmer said he had seen nothing. The man and woman sent for the priest to have their farm exorcised. The clergyman refused, however, because he had cancer and such an intervention would undermine his health. "Go to the Capuchin fathers in Izegem," the clergyman told them. When the fathers had exorcised the farm and given the man and woman a medal to hang in the house, the farm was no longer haunted.
195400: One Sunday evening a man was coming back from 'de Barriere', a café in Elsegem on a remote road from Oudenaarde to Kortrijk. Suddenly the man saw something lying in the grass that looked like a skeleton holding out its hand. Terrified, the man ran home. When he came along that road again the next day, the grass was standing nicely upright everywhere. There was no sign anywhere that anything had lain on the grass the evening before.
195413: Some people claimed they had seen lots of rabbits on their way home. In reality it was simply imagination.
195436:
The maid of 't Haantje in Lichtervelde always heard strange knocking at night. Sometimes it was so bad that the maid was thrown out of her bed. Every time she went to fetch the farmer, the haunting suddenly stopped. In the end the maid fell ill from the events. She had prayers of deliverance read over her by the clergy and made a novena. Still, the girl afterwards gave notice at the farm.
The cows gave milk, but the farmer could not churn butter.
195463: A pregnant woman from Houtkerke was assisted during childbirth by a midwife from the village who was in reality a witch. The midwife rocked the baby in her arms all the time. The child's mother went to the friars, who told her that her child was being bewitched by a woman who came to the house every day. The clergymen advised the woman to hang something blessed above the door. When the woman had done that, the midwife could no longer come in.
195477: A boy who had been bewitched by his godmother would no longer eat and cried all night. After the witch had been thrown out, the boy no longer cried.
195482: A woman who was reading in the evening struck at a toad that had come in. The next day the woman's husband found that her employer had lost a leg.
195483: Being ridden by the mare was really a kind of dream.
195485: A smith whose tools were always in disarray in the morning decided one night to keep watch in his workshop. When the man heard noises at midnight, he began swinging a red-hot iron bar about in the dark. The next day the smith met three old women who had burns on their faces.
195488: One Sunday a joker was sitting in a café having a drink. When a man from the village came into the café, the joker said mockingly: "Look who we have here! Our wizard! They say you can do magic!" The wizard, however, pretended not to hear. At midnight the joker said to the wizard: "It's twelve o'clock. Shouldn't we go home?" The wizard replied: "You go ahead, I'll be along shortly. I'll have one more drink first, and then I may well be home before you." A little later the wizard went home and got into bed. At six in the morning the joker ended up at the Paardenmarkt; the wizard had made him lose his way because he had mocked him.
195500: In a cellar stood a chest with a large beast sitting on it. No one dared to go near that chest. At night the knights (Templars) came riding up in coaches. They were dressed in gold and silver, and on the stroke of twelve they disappeared into a rampart.
195518: A woman who was half asleep felt the mare coming. She grabbed the mare by the finger, but it still got away. It was a witch from the neighbourhood, who later lost her power through the doing of a clergyman. The victim put salt under the threshold and placed her shoes 'nose to nose' so as to be spared by the mare from then on.
195520: A mother who had just had a child met a witch at the christening party who wanted to see the child. The mother refused. A little later the witch still got the chance to come near the child. "Now go on raising it diligently," the witch had said. A while later the child fell ill. Two days after the mother had taken the child to the friars, the child was cured.
195550: A mother travelled by train to Komen with her little daughter. A strange woman sitting in the train gave the child a pear. As soon as the child had eaten the pear, it began to cry incessantly. In the end the mother had to have the friars say prayers over her daughter.
195560: A farmer's wife was visited by a poor woman. That woman never asked for money or food, but she did want clothes. One day the woman said: "I need slippers, because I have a hole in my shoes that makes my toe hurt." The farmer's wife answered that she had no slippers. When the woman had left, the farmer's wife got a pain in her toe, in exactly the spot the woman had pointed to.
195562: Some people returning from a pilgrimage to Arneque saw a strange apparition on the road and said: "If you are sent by the devil, go away. If you are sent by God, stay." The next moment there was nothing more to be seen.
195563: In the woods of the Duc d'Arenberg in Roeselare there was a pit in which a bell was said to have once sunk.
195569: A man went to the Ermietshoek in Ichtegem to listen to the calling of the eternal hunter. It was the howling of the wind.
195572: A man laughed at someone who claimed that one could not poach on the evening of All Saints' Day. To put it to the test, the two men decided to go hunting on that very evening. When the men saw a rabbit and one of them wanted to shoot it, the gun did not work. A bit further on a paper bag lay on the ground. The man shot at the bag, and this time his gun did work. When a hare appeared a little later, the gun again did not work.
195583: In Hazebroek lived a woman who had cursed her child with the words: "I'm going to sell you, even if it's to the devil!" The next day the child was collected in the woods by a gentleman dressed in black, driving a coach drawn by black horses. The child stayed away for three years to work as doorkeeper in hell. When the child came back, everyone called it 'de hellevent' (the hell lad).
195629: When a child had been touched by an old person, it often happened that the child cried all the time afterwards. Parents tried to avoid such old people as much as possible.
195634: A beggar woman with a wound on her forehead claimed that she had once been a hare and that someone had shot at her. Everyone was afraid of that beggar woman.
195637: In Otegem lived a woman whose children all died. One day the curate had said: "This evil must stop here, or I will name the guilty ones from the pulpit!" After that things went better for a while, but one day the misfortune began again.
195638: A witch was, as it were, compelled to go to a newborn baby. But as soon as the child had been baptised, the witch's power was broken.
195648: In the past the Concordia could be seen sailing by the beach. That sailing boat was a ghost ship.
195657: People who were ridden by the mare put a branch above their bed.
195663: At a farm troubled by a plague of fleas, the clergy were sent for. After prayers had been read over the farm, all the fleas had disappeared.
195682: On a farm, a man had hanged himself from a beam. Since then the farmhand always saw that beam burning.
195688: In a house in Wijtschate, all sorts of noises were heard in the attic at night. After a pot of money was found in the attic, the noises were heard no more.
195692: The mare was a bad dream you got from having eaten a heavy meal in the evening.
195717: A church was said to have sunk in the Marelputten. Every year the tower rose up again and bells could be heard ringing.
195718: From one day to the next, a weaving mill was plagued by white mice. Strangely, there was no way at all to catch the mice.
195725: A schelfdekker (1) was working on a farm where a Duitse schaper (German shepherd, a travelling shepherd said to have magic powers) was staying. Every Saturday evening this shepherd flew to Germany on a ram to fetch a clean shirt. When the shepherd was thirsty, he drank from his 'makke' (2). On Sunday he went to pay the café landlady for that beer.
195734: A newly married woman went to live in her husband's café. The woman did not know, however, that the house was haunted. One day the woman had had to work long in the field because a thunderstorm was coming. When she came home late in the evening and went to make the beds, she heard a creaking under one of the beds. The woman was always terrified whenever she had to sleep in that bed.
195739: A woman who was gathering pine needles had set her baby on a sack near her. Strangely enough, at a certain moment the child had suddenly vanished. A strange little woman also lived nearby. When the mother stood wailing in panic, the strange little woman came up and said: "What's the matter that you're wailing like that?", to which the woman replied: "The baby that was sitting on that sack has disappeared!" The little woman then said: "Oh no, that's not true. Look, the child is sitting right there!" The child was indeed sitting on the sack again.
195744: In one family a child was born every year. But because the children all died, they went to the friars, who advised the people to throw out a certain woman. After they had done so, there was no more misfortune in that house. Later that woman was shown the door everywhere. The woman became completely emaciated.
195764: When the mayor was walking home one evening, he was followed by a cat. At the gate of his house the mayor struck the cat with a stick, wounding the animal on the head. The next day the parish priest had a scratch on his face. The clergyman could turn himself into a cat.
195768:
A woman going home one night around Twelfth Night was followed by a werewolf. The woman quickly took off her cloak so that the werewolf would have work to do. The werewolf had to tear the cloak completely to pieces before it could go after its victim again. When the woman saw the werewolf coming again, she took off another piece of clothing.
When something like that had happened, people often found the next day that some boys from the village still had fibres of the cloth between their teeth.
195781: A mother who had already seen six or seven of her babies die consulted the parish priest. The clergyman gave the mother an Easter nail to hang above the cradle. A woman from the neighbourhood who always came to look under the blankets of a newborn baby could no longer come in because of that Easter nail.
195787: Witches could bewitch people because they consorted with the devil.
195799: The Tempelhof in Mannekensvere was haunted. When the farmer's wife was milking the cow there, she was assisted by an invisible figure who milked the other two teats of the udder.
195801: In Oostduinkerke there was always a cat sitting and meowing. One day people burned the cat's whiskers with a poker from the hearth. Shortly afterwards they found that the moustache of a man from the village had been burned.
195807:
On the Diesveld in Otegem there used to be a castle owned by the Van Otto family. That family gave Otegem its name.
At midnight a lady always drove to that castle in a coach with six horses. The drawbridge lowered by itself to let the coach in. It was the ghost of a woman who had been murdered there.
195822: The freemasons had to sell their souls to the devil. To do so they had to sign their name in blood. A man had sold his little child and had to bring it to the Kruisstraat. But the man regretted his deed. When he set the child down, it began to draw little crosses on the ground. Because of that the devil never got the child in his power.
195825: A man riding his bicycle found that a goat was running along with him. The goat, however, was invisible.
195845: A sorceress always kept burning candles in her attic. When the woman dropped a basket of eggs one day, strangely enough not a single egg was broken.
195848: A schoolboy made mice in class and let them run around on his bench. When the priest visited the school in Alveringem one day, he took the boy's magic power away.
195862: During her sleep a woman felt something walking on her. She struck at the apparition, which then disappeared. It had been the mare.
195885: If you saw a black cat in the evening, you would have bad luck.
195893: When the children came back from school on their bikes, they shouted on the way at the witch who wandered about in Gistel: "Toot-toot!" The witch then said: "Excuse me! You ought to get two flat tyres!" Five metres further on the children did indeed have two flat tyres.
195901: A drunkard staggering home on Sunday night met the parish priest on the way, who looked at him angrily. At that moment the drunkard, strangely enough, could not move a foot. The priest had made him stand still because he had not gone to mass that morning.
195911: A man who went fishing with a basket on his back was pestered by a witch. The witch secretly conjured the fish and the hooks out of the basket.
195914: A woman lying in her bed felt short of breath and as if something was pressing on her chest. As soon as she woke up, the feeling was gone.
195916: A woman had touched a piglet in a sty. The next day the animal lay dead. Because that woman always came near children, those children got 'the old man' (an illness) and died.
195917: The orchard of a farm in Rollegem was haunted. The trees were felled and a new orchard was planted. Shortly afterwards a new garden was also laid out. Some people believed that something (a treasure?) had been found in the haunted orchard.
195977: Every evening a mother saw a cat come into her house through the drain hole for the water. Someone advised the mother to pour boiling water over the animal. The next day the mother saw that a woman from the village had burns on her face.
195979: A sixteen-year-old girl saw the ghost of her father, who had been dead for two years. Her confessor advised the girl to ask the next time whether the ghost was sent by God or by the devil. The girl had hardly asked the question when her father answered: "By God. And you must go to church for me with three persons and hear a mass. That is a vow I neglected. If you do that, I will be released." When the girl was on her way to church, her father walked ahead the whole time. When the girl came out again, her father said: "I thank you with all my heart, my dear child." The girl was so shocked by the whole event that she lived only one more year.
195983: A man and woman who had not been married long were lying in bed together. Because of the wind, a plant kept knocking against the door of the pigsty. When the man heard the sound, he said to his wife in fright: "What do I hear there? Your mother never promised anything or something, did she?"
195985: A farm by the Roomputten in the Roobaardstraat was haunted. A brave man who often had to pass by there was terrified.
195997: A woman had gone to Roesten to fetch milk in an earthenware butter pot tied shut on both sides with a towel. On the way the woman met a strange woman, who said: "Mother dear, aren't you afraid your butter pot will break?" The woman had not gone ten metres further when the butter pot did indeed break. She still had the top of the pot in her towel.
196000: A woman with several children decided to convert the henhouse next to the house into a bedroom. The boy who then slept in the room saw, every time he woke up, a cow's head with eyes like lanterns. Because the strange phenomena did not stop, it was decided to turn the room back into a henhouse. When that was done, the hens could be heard fluttering about all night. In the end the henhouse was turned into a coal shed.
196021: A boy was in a relationship with a girl who lived near him. The boy's previous girlfriend was the daughter of a witch. One day, as the boy was walking to his new girlfriend's house, he was hindered by a cat that kept getting under his feet the whole time. The boy got annoyed with the cat and kicked at the animal. The next day a woman with a broken hip was found in the ditch along the road. That woman was the mother of the boy's previous girlfriend. When the parish priest went to visit the injured woman, she said: "Well, Father, I have been badly knocked about!" To which the clergyman dryly replied: "If you hadn't been walking there, you wouldn't be hurt now!"
196022: A parish priest who was threatened on the summer road by a robber with the words "Your money or your life" outwitted the criminal. The clergyman said: "Do I still have time to take a pinch of snuff?" As he suited the action to the word, the priest made the robber stand still as if nailed to the ground.
196025: The doodkeersen (death candles, ghost lights) that were seen flying through the air at great speed were souls that still had to wander.
196036: A woman who did much evil could send a plague of rats to a farm.
196043: Because people suspected that some women in the village were witches, the sexton decided to put it to the test. When the sexton left the Gospel book open on the altar on Sunday, the witches could not get out. As soon as the sexton had closed the book, the witches could go outside. Before they left the church, however, they said to the sexton: "We'll get you yet!" The next day the sexton was sitting in his underpants on the church gate. Because the sexton could not get away, the parish priest had to bless him with prayers.
196045: A man returning from the fair in Koekelare with four friends kicked three times at a kitten sitting on a culvert by the side of the road. With each kick the man was thrown into the brook by the animal.
196051: In Aartrijke lived a sorceress who always wore three aprons and often sat by the front wall of her house. The woman owned five or six dogs. People believed this sorceress could trim a hedge with a sieve.
196064: People who had been ridden by a werewolf had to have the friars read prayers over them.
196067: Two men coming home along the beach at low tide saw a woman wrapped in a cloak standing by the pipes between Mariakerke and Middelkerke. At the sight of that strange apparition, one of the men ran away terrified. Cats also often roamed about at that same haunted spot.
196075: Every night a ghost with a golden chain appeared at a farm, calling all the time: "More water or milk, scantly measured, my soul forgotten!"
196076: When a horse was sick in Wulvergem, the priest asked a witch from the neighbourhood whether she could come by. The witch refused, however, saying: "Give the horse a draught of water. It will recover!" After the farmer had given the horse water, the animal was indeed cured.
196096: When a witch's daughter was buried, the wagon with three horses drove off the dike.
196104: On the road to Kortrijk stood a farm that was haunted. At night the animals there were untied, even though the farm gate was closed. The fathers of Kortrijk advised the people to stay in the stable for one night and then ask: "Who are you? Who sent you? Why do you come?" Because none of the occupants dared to do that, the fathers came to spend the night in the stable themselves. The fathers were drenched in sweat after their intervention, but everything was normal again with the animals.
196106: On a large farm in Maldegem they always had bad luck. When several animals had already died, they went to the friars. "If you want to know who is causing this evil, I will tell you." But the people did not want to know. The friars then came to Maldegem.
196116: A man who was often ridden by the mare was advised to hang 'flat beet seed' above his bed or to set his clogs straight.
196149: Witches were often female pedlars who leaned over a child's cradle and bewitched the child that way. When such a pedlar had not been able to sell anything, she often stood at the farm gate making strange gestures. Because the occupants then became afraid of being bewitched, they called the pedlar back and bought something from her.
196172: In Westkapelle lived a woman who at the market could pour eggs from one basket into another without breaking a single one. That woman probably mastered the black art, for she owned two handwritten books which she gave to the priest when she died.
196173: One evening two men came home drenched in sweat. The men had seen a horse wearing bells around its neck.
196175: A farmer saw all the tubs and tools flying around in the cowshed. When people went to look, strangely enough, there was nothing to be seen. One day, however, a dove was seen sitting on the door.
196186: An old woman could turn herself into a cat. The cat always crept into a farmhouse through the drain hole for the water and lay down under the stove. On that farm they had not been able to make butter for a year. When they sent for the parish priest, he beat around the butter churn with brushwood. "Doesn't a cat come here?" the priest asked, and the farmer said yes. Then the priest said: "You must hit the cat on the head with a red-hot poker." Only eight days later did the old woman come to fetch milk again. She had a cloth around her neck, because it was completely burnt.
196221: Farmer H. came back to haunt after his death in the shape of a big white dog. The farmer was punished because he had not paid his farmhands enough and made them work far too hard.
196233: A man who owned a book of magic could make mice come to a house. When the man left, the mice went along with him. The dean took away that man's books of magic. The mice never came back after that.
196243: Two farm boys always went dancing in an inn. One of the boys was in love with the daughter of the innkeeper's wife. One morning the boys' hair had all fallen out. One of the boys went to the inn and got angry. The other boy stayed bald his whole life.
196244: A Belgian who had been a soldier in France sat boasting in the café 'Het Katje' that he was no longer afraid of anything. As part of a bet, Frans accepted the challenge to spend the night in a haunted farmhouse. In the evening Frans began baking pancakes in the farmhouse. At twenty to twelve the man suddenly heard a strange noise: the doors of the room, the cellar and the attic began to rattle, though nothing could be seen. Suddenly a human leg fell down the chimney into the pan. Coolly, Frans took the leg out of the pan and threw it into a corner. A little later more bones fell, and finally a skull, into the pan. Frans threw everything together in a corner. Suddenly a complete skeleton stood in the corner. Frans struck at the skeleton with a stick, but the stick went right through it. Three times the skeleton beckoned with its finger for Frans to go to the cellar. Only the third time did Frans agree, saying: "If you go first, I'll come along." In the cellar the skeleton wanted Frans to open the door. After the skeleton had pointed at the door three times, Frans said: "Open it yourself!" Then the skeleton wanted Frans to go into the cellar. After the skeleton had asked this three times, Frans said: "Go first, I'll follow you." In the end the skeleton went first and led Frans to a very heavy stone that he had to lift. "I can't," said Frans. The skeleton asked three times, until Frans said: "Lift it yourself with all your might!" The skeleton lifted the stone and beckoned Frans to crawl into the pit. The third time Frans said: "Crawl in yourself!" The skeleton brought up two stone pots with two handles. Then Frans had to fetch the third pot from the pit. The moment Frans took hold of the pot, a loud thunderclap sounded and Frans's candle went out. Frans struck matches, went upstairs and found that the skeleton had vanished. On the first pot lay a note reading: "This is for the parish priest, to help the poor." On the second pot lay a note saying: "This is for the mayor, for roads and streets and other expenses." On the third pot lay a note that said: "This is for the finder." Frans went on baking until morning and then took the money to the priest and the mayor. From then on the farmhouse could be lived in again, for it was the treasures that had caused the haunting.
196279:
A woman who had two daughters often read mysterious books. One day the daughters went to tell the parish priest about it. The mother, however, refused to give up her books.
One Sunday afternoon the daughters' sweethearts saw a white horse walking in the meadow. One of the boys said: "That is your mother's witchcraft!" and he shot at the animal with his gun. When the daughters came home, their mother was lying unconscious beside the armchair.
196280: During the war a woman went to Gent. On the tram to Zomergem the woman saw two witches sitting. When the woman got on another tram in Zomergem and asked for a ticket to Gent, the driver said: "But madam, you are going to Knesselare!" The woman had been led astray by those two witches.
196297: When the sorceresses held a gathering, they turned themselves into cats. After the meeting the cats took on their human form again.
196299: A farmer from the Koude Schuur cursed all day long. One day, as the farmer drove through the meadow with horse and cart, his dead daughter appeared to tell him he must not curse like that.
196304: A house along the Stadenstraat was haunted. In the middle of winter, apples were shaken from the trees there. One day the cows had all been untied, so that people had to seek advice from the priest of Zarren. The clergyman, however, did not manage to tie the cows up again and sent for the priest of Staden. When the two priests tied the ropes together, everything stayed normal.
196314: A farmer drove past a witch with a cart of hay. The witch said to the farmer: "Your cart will tip over!" The witch was not ten steps further on when the cart did indeed fall over.
196320: Witches only gained power over someone if they had touched that person.
196321: If a sorceress struck you on the arm, you always had to strike her higher up to make her powerless.
196352: In Kuurne a sorceress went peddling with a basket in her hand. This sorceress could bewitch people so that they fell ill. So in many places the woman was no longer welcome.
196369: People who were ridden by the mare at night were suddenly very frightened because they were having a bad dream.
196370: Against his better judgment, a boy always joked around with a woman from the village. People had often told him that he would get bewitched that way one day. One day the woman threw gooseberries on the boy's head. In the evening the boy felt ill and had spots all over his body. His mother sent him to the priest, but the priest claimed that witchcraft did not exist. When the boy had been alone with the priest, all the spots had disappeared.
196400:
People who owned books of magic could torment others.
In a street in Elverdinge there were thirteen houses. In the last house lived a very old woman. One day, as that woman passed by, a boy from the sixth house threw a bucket of water outside. The woman then said to the boy: "You will regret that your whole life!" The boy developed epilepsy, and in 1914 he chased the French soldiers with knives. The boy eventually died in a psychiatric institution in Ieper.
196403: In Steenkerke lived a sorceress of whom people were very afraid. When they came back from Veurne with vegetables and meat, on arriving home they found that all the food had turned into pencils.
196406: For a long time a great cannon could be seen in the clouds above Staden. At the start of the war a woman saw a great cross appear from the direction of Passendale. That was a sign that the battlefield was approaching.
196409: A woman who lived close to the French convent often heard ghostly noises. One day the woman said: "If you are from God, speak. If you are from the devil, be silent." The priest, who had heard this, said to the woman: "You must be silent. Those are spirits that could do you harm!"
196410: For a good three or four weeks people in Voormezele heard a goat screaming by a pigsty. A little later the goat flew away through the air. People from Kemmel came to watch the scene.
196430:
A woman from the neighbourhood always came to a house in Poperinge to collect rags. When the woman came in, she always went straight to look at the baby lying in the cradle instead of going to the mother first.
The baby's brother did not trust the woman and rode his bicycle to a friar. The clergyman said to the boy: "That is a woman who reads bad books. I will give you a medal, which you must put under the threshold. When the woman is at the door, you must also pray an Our Father and a Hail Mary." The boy did as the friar had advised and found that the woman indeed could no longer get in. A little later the priest came in by the back of the house to see how things were. The friar advised the boy to keep the medal his whole life. On leaving, the friar said to the witch: "What do you keep coming here for? If you have something to settle, you must do it with the child's mother, but you must stay away from the child itself. Every time you have been with the child, it is sick the next day. We will look into this matter!" The next day the police found a tall pile of bad books in the witch's house. The friar had also asked the witch which mass she attended, and she had answered: "The half past eight one." The next day, during the half past eight mass, the friar began to sing during the Gospel, although that was very unusual. After the mass the witch could not get up from her chair. The friar walked to the altar and declared that there was witchcraft in the parish and that the guilty person would go to prison. The next day they fetched the witch from her house. It is thought that she died in prison.
The boy wore the medal on his chest his whole life.
196431:
In Sint-Denijs lived a man who could send rats from one farm to another. 
Perhaps this can be explained rationally. In the old days people sometimes hung up a rat, and that animal made so much noise that the other rats ran away.
196434: Two men who were threshing suddenly saw a hare and took out their gun. One of the men hit it. A while later a woman from the village was seen walking around with a bandage around her head.
196448: A man whose son was ill went to the friars, who advised him to chase away the first woman who came by. When the neighbour came to visit the next day, however, the man did not dare to chase her away. Because the boy grew sicker and sicker, they sent for the friars. The clergymen gave the child's parents a book to read from. The people prayed until they were drenched in sweat, but the child died. When it was too late, they chased the neighbour away.
196469: A farmhand who was ridden by the mare saw an old woman standing at the foot of his bed. After the farmhand had gone to Assebroek barefoot, he was no longer ridden by the mare.
196472: Thieves who went to steal nuts in Vinkem got stuck to the tree or got stuck in a hole in the hedge.
196484: A house in Lichtervelde was haunted. A father was sent for to exorcise the farm. While the father did so, drops of sweat rolled down his face. Afterwards a black dog was seen running away through the roof. That father is said not to have lived long after his intervention.
196488: A schoolchild filled the classroom with mice by reading in a magic book. When the teacher got angry, the child made the mice disappear again at once.
196504: A man went to learn sorcery from a sorcerer. The sorcerer put white plates on the table and told the man to say they were black plates. As soon as people came in, the plates were indeed black. When the man went home that evening, the sorcerer said to him: "Aren't you afraid? Otherwise I'll send a companion with you." A little later a large black dog appeared, which walked along with the man, barking, until he was home. On arriving home the man found that the dog had vanished without a trace. On the way he had tried several times to kick the dog, but he had never been able to hit the animal.
196513: A man who lived in Sint-Kruis was annoyed by a cat that kept getting under his feet. After the man had given the cat a kick, the animal had vanished. The man was convinced that the cat was a sorceress.
196529: A man had been visited by a suspicious woman from the village. Some time later the man's daughter said: "Father, come and look! Your bed is full of fleas!" The man prayed the Gospel of Saint John and then told his daughter to make up the bed again. Half an hour later all the lice had gone.
196535: A mother whose little daughter lay in the cradle was visited by a peddler woman selling pins. While the mother went to get her money, the peddler secretly went over to the child. Because the little girl cried all the time afterwards, the mother went to the friars, who managed to solve the problem.
196554: A man saw a ball of fire moving back and forth over the hedge. The ball came from the direction of Steenvoorde and moved towards Poperinge. It was a witch who had created that fireball.
196561: A sorceress from Brugge owned books of magic. If this sorceress had touched a child, she could make that child cry itself to death. After the sorceress had been made to hand over her books of magic, she joined the Protestants.
196568: A cowherd had to close the gates and doors of the farm in the evening. Because the gates opened again by themselves a little later, the farmer sent for the friars. The knights came to haunt the farm because they had hidden their money in the cellar. A man from the neighbourhood went to confession and communion twice so that he would find the treasure, which lay hidden somewhere near the bakehouse. But no one has ever found the treasure.
196584: On a farm, because of the kwade hand (the evil hand, witchcraft), butter could no longer be made. There was always dung in the butter churn. Someone advised the people to put dung in the butter churn. After that they would be able to churn butter again. And so it was.
196589: Sorcerers could send rats, mice and other animals to a house, so that the people there had a real plague on their hands.
196600: To unmask a witch, you had to follow her on her way to church. You then had to place your feet side by side and stand still. If the suspected woman was a witch, she would look round.
196613: A man and a woman from Lokeren were on their way to a wedding when they met a Duitse schaper (German shepherd, a wandering shepherd believed to have magic powers) on the road. The couple did not greet the shepherd and walked on. Further along the man and the woman found they were covered in lice. The couple turned back home and passed the shepherd again, who said: "Next time, say good day when you meet someone!" The next moment the lice were gone.
196635: In Rollegem lived an old woman who was said to be able to work witchcraft. On a farm in Rollegem they could no longer churn butter. Many cows had lost their tails or had died. When a cat was seen in the barn, they wounded the animal in the paw. The next day it was noticed that the suspected woman was limping. The farmer went to the friars in Ieper and told them there that three cows had died. The friars answered: "There are already four." While the man was on his way to Ieper, a fourth cow had indeed died.
196638: It was haunted at 't Kruis in Beveren. A kind of lantern could always be seen floating there and moving up and down.
196658: A farm in Pittem was haunted. At night the flour bin could be heard falling down the stairs, although nothing could be seen. When one of the daughters woke one night, she saw a white cow standing in her room, growing bigger and bigger. The girl tried to wake her sister, but could not. A little later the cow grew smaller and smaller until it finally disappeared. The girl woke her sister and said: "It's X again." X was the former occupant of the farm. He had many ill-gotten goods and could find no rest until he had paid back all the money. That is why all kinds of noises were heard on the farm at night. Sometimes the light went out by itself or the doors opened by themselves. At a certain point the people could not even churn butter any more. A friar gave them a medal to put on the butter churn and advised them to pray a novena. After that the people had butter again. In the end the people moved away.
196673: People who were ridden by the mare could no longer breathe or speak. A young man who was ridden by the mare eventually had to move house to get rid of it.
196695: The kwade hand (the evil hand, witchcraft) was sometimes also called 'de oude man' (the old man), 'de kanteerns' or 'de koeke' (in Kortrijk).
196715: At a farm in Harelbeke a woman in a white cap always rode along the dike. That woman chased after the farm's maids. Whenever the maids went to pump water, rats and mice came out of the pump. That woman stayed there for nine days.
196720: After the First World War a village was plagued by a real rat infestation. After the priest had prayed a little, the animals ran off. The clergyman said: "They will go to another place and they will do no more harm."
196747: A farmer's wife wearing new slippers met a woman from Varsenare on a walk, who said: "Those are pretty slippers!" When the farmer's wife got home, she had a nasty fall. The farmer's wife never fully recovered from her injuries. The sorceress had done this to her because she was jealous of the pretty slippers. In the hospital they took the sorceress's books of magic away from her.
196759: On a farm at the Westhoek in Zonnebeke, the cows were always tied to the beams by their tails at night. The boots stood with their feet upwards. At night the drainpipes for the water from the stables could always be heard rattling. In the end the occupants of that farm had to move. When they drove away with their wagons, jays flew all over their heads. The farm was demolished.
196765: A house in Ostend was haunted by the ghost of a dead person who could find no rest. Every night the furniture could be seen dancing and rattling there.
196770: Children who had been given a sweet or a mint by a woman often fell ill and died. Women could also bewitch children by picking them up in their arms.
196774: The flying goat regularly flew over Beselare. Thousands of people came to Beselare to hear the sound of the goat. Later it turned out that there is a bird that makes the same sound as a goat.
196781: The Doornen Bilk, a sheep pasture near the little chapel of Bredene, used to be haunted. When pilgrims from Ostend reached the Doornen Bilk, they had to say: "Go ahead, I will follow." If they forgot to say it, they immediately felt a heavy weight on their shoulders. It was the ghost of a returning dead person who had itself carried and grew heavier with every step. The victim was then helped by the other pilgrims as far as the chapel, where the burden of the invisible ghost suddenly vanished. Pilgrims who had said "Go ahead, I will follow" found it much easier to make progress from the Doornen Bilk onwards.
196782: During their sleep people were sometimes ridden by the mare. They never managed to catch hold of it.
196804: A witch from Houtave could make a cart of hay tip over. She could also read cards and palms.
196811: In Zevenkote lived a sorceress who was often out and about at night. In a nearby bakery they could not bake bread because the flour was bad. That was the sorceress's doing. It was said that the sorceress's ears had been cut off, but this was hard to see because she always wore a cap.
196817: A witch had bewitched her own children. At thirty years of age the children were still going to school. Whenever one saw that witch, one always saw a whole pack of cats as well.
196825: In a brewery in Bissegem they could no longer brew beer. Instead of beer they got manure. One day a cat was seen walking in the brewery. They burnt the animal's snout with a red-hot iron. The next day an old woman was seen walking about with a burn on her face.
196849: Near the field of Passendale in Zillebeke stood a house full of rats. The farmer sought advice from a man, who said: "I will make the rats go away, but you must leave the animals alone. You must not kill them. In four or five days there will not be a single rat left in the house." What the man had predicted indeed came true. But a few days later a neighbour suddenly had a real plague of rats. The people said nothing, for they themselves were rid of their rats.
196853: A church had sunk in the bell pits in Eernegem.
196855: On a farm the calves died after an old woman had made the sign of the cross over the animals. For there were different kinds of signs of the cross.
196872: If a Tsachoe bird flew over a house, someone in that house would die.
196875: A woman got up at four in the morning because she had to go somewhere. On the way the woman was pushed into the hedge by a terribly large beast.
196877: The priest's maid had put four Easter nails under her mattress because she was ridden by the mare every night. A woman suspected of being a witch always came to the presbytery. Because of the Easter nails, the witch could no longer talk to the maid.
196885: On a farm in Proven they had six or seven cows that rejected their calves. The priest claimed that the misfortune was caused by a witch who came to fetch buttermilk, and he read prayers over the stables. The clergyman also predicted that the witch would come for buttermilk one more time and advised the farmer to give her the milk. When that had happened, the witch stayed away for good.
196886:
A boy who was ridden by the mare in his sleep saw a skinny, ugly little woman sitting there. The boy was very frightened.
Some people claimed that the mare was a stoppage of the blood.
196904: On old farms, noises were often heard at night as if someone were churning or the harvest were being brought in. During the winter the noise of someone threshing could be heard. When people went to look, there was never anything to be seen.
196906: A farmer's wife who had to leave her home because her husband was a drunkard and did not pay his rent said to the next occupants: "You will not have one healthy hour!" Within three months the new occupants lost four horses, eleven sows and a child. The people sprinkled everything with holy water and, at their wits' end, tore down the stables, but nothing helped. After the friars had read prayers over the farm, the spell was broken.
196919: In the evening ugly beasts were seen in the churchyard.
196921: Sorceresses owned a little doll that they could stick full of pins. When that happened, the children felt pain as if they themselves were being pricked by the pins. To protect themselves against such evil, people put silver by the door so that the sorceresses could not cross the threshold. When the parish priest came to pray over a bewitched child, he sweated terribly.
196929: On a farm where the farmer's wife could do witchcraft, all the animals died. One day the farmer saw his wife walk to the horse, pull open the animal's mouth and spit fire into it. The next day the horse lay dead. The farmer's wife was possessed by the devil. The friars came to read prayers over her. A short time later the farmer's wife died.
196935: People believed that wandering little lights were returning spirits.
196939: A woman from Varsenare had bought some hay at a small farm. When the woman saw a furrow along the road, she said: "That's a fine furrow!" The next moment all the hay fell into the furrow.
196951: A man who could make blue rats appear always came to the Mokker (1).
196965: During the Second World War some boys were walking to school. On the way the boys laughed at a Duitse schaper (German shepherd, a wandering shepherd believed to have magic powers) standing there. The shepherd then conjured up mice that crawled over the boys' backs and necks. A little later the shepherd made the mice disappear again. One day the Duitse schaper predicted that the sheepfold would burn down. That happened too.
196985: The Vingerlienkput was a deep pit in which someone who was damned was held. People often saw little blue flames floating above that pit.
196990: A brave man walking home in the evening saw a cat sitting by a brook. The man kicked at the animal, whereupon he was surrounded by white cats and could hardly make any headway. The man was drenched in sweat when he got home.
197023: A farmer who had quarrelled during a card game one evening could not get home. The next morning the farmer was still walking around in the meadow.
197024: On a farm they had a good harvest every year, so that they had to borrow the threshing machine from some people in the neighbourhood. Every time the people finished threshing with the borrowed machine, it began to rain. A woman from the neighbourhood, who was suspected of being able to do witchcraft, always came by when they were threshing.
197030: A sorceress had sown turnips in a farmer's field. The farmer wanted to pull up the turnips and throw them away, but strangely enough that was impossible.
197051: On a farm in Proven lived a woman who could do witchcraft. When that woman quarrelled with one of her hens, she laid a little stick on the hen's neck. After that the animal fell silent.
197084: A man from Blankenberge claimed that his dead wife had returned to divide her jewellery among her children so that there would be no quarrelling.
197086: A man went to visit his girlfriend, who lived between Rozebeke and Ingelmunster. When on the way the man wanted to jump over a ditch, he always saw a coffin standing in front of his feet, so that he could not get to the other side of the ditch. After the man had said a prayer of the cross on his knees, the coffin was gone and he could go on.
197087: In a house the loom could be heard working by itself at night.
197090: A man coming home from work one evening was followed by another man. When there were three people, that other man did not show himself. In the end the priest exorcised the ghost.
197101: On a farm the maid always heard the sounds of a flail at night. When the maid came downstairs and sprinkled holy water on the floor in the shape of a cross, the sounds stopped. The Koddebende, a gang made up of three young brothers, had something to do with that haunting. A woman who saw the pots and pans in her kitchen dancing at night was also able to put an end to the haunting by throwing holy water.
197102: Children who were ridden by the mare usually died of it.
197107: In Ruddervoorde a farmer and his farmhand went to manure the field. On the way the farmhand struck at a doodkeers (death candle, ghost light) with his whip. At that the doodkeers said: "You'll find out. If you had left me alone for two more days, my time would have been up!" Two days later the farmhand fell ill and he died shortly afterwards.
197151: A woman who was ridden by the mare had bad dreams and also felt as if someone was trying to pull her under the bed by her arm.
197159: A cleaning woman worked for a Jew. The Jew was in love with the woman, but she wanted nothing to do with him. One day the woman had taken off her corset because she was very sweaty. The Jew managed to get hold of the garment and took it to a witch. By burning candles and sticking pins into the corset, the witch got the woman in her power. In the end the woman was climbing the walls in misery. The woman went to the priest, who gave her holy water to make signs of the cross over the threshold. But none of it helped, because the witch had great power over the woman since the sweat had soaked into the corset. After a while the bewitchment came to an end by itself.
