197162: A man was hunting by moonlight near a haunted farm. Although there was no wind, the man suddenly heard the gates of the farm banging open and shut. Moreover, a strange force drove the man towards the water, so that he had the greatest difficulty staying away from it.
197171: A man had to move some things from one side of Steenkerke to the other. On the way the man met a woman who wanted to sit on the cart. "There's no room," said the man. Although the woman kept insisting, the man refused to let her sit on the cart. A little later, however, the man could go no further. As a result he was forced to leave the cart behind and go home with just his horse. When the man went to fetch the cart with his horse the next day, the animal, strangely enough, could pull the cart without trouble.
197212: A woman who was ridden by the mare could not move and felt as if an animal was lying on her. You could drive the mare away by praying.
197216: If a broom bush had been ridden by the mare, its twigs were round instead of flat. People took such a twig with them to protect themselves against the mare.
197231: A woman from Blankenberge had misfortune with her children. Each child was born healthy but died at the age of three weeks. When the woman had another child, she went with it to the friars. One of the clergymen asked: "During your pregnancy, did you never receive something from a stranger?" The woman answered: "I once got some whiting from a neighbour." The friar replied: "That woman will be the first to come and visit you soon." What the friar had predicted indeed came true. "Get out or I'll smash your head in!" the woman said to her neighbour. That neighbour never visited again, and the woman's baby survived.
197238: A man who worked on a farm saw an old woman come to his bed at night; she grabbed him by the throat and whispered something in his ear. When the woman had gone, the man was sweating terribly.
197269: On a farm the animals always ran loose at night. When people went to look, however, they found that the animals were tied up.
197274: A woman who had gone to fetch coal with the cart was ridden by the mare on the way back, so that she lost her way. After the woman had talked for a while with a farmer in the field, she found her way again.
197279: At a farm in Zandvoorde, every evening after sunset two goats appeared that rode around in a little cart and then jumped into a well. Strangely enough, the next day the goats had not drowned.
197296: People who were ridden by the mare at night were the victims of someone who had sent that evil to them.
197302: A witch always sent cats whenever her husband was drunk. Then a good hundred cats would jump in front of the man's feet, so that he nearly fell.
197311: On a farm they could not keep a single animal alive because of a woman who had it in for those people.
197325: On a farm worked a nineteen-year-old maid from Dottenijs who could do witchcraft. The girl often sat reading a book with her feet by the stove. When the maid had been home alone for a while and the people came back, they saw everything on the mantelpiece dancing. Eventually the maid was dismissed. After that she found work on a farm in Bellegem, but it was the same story there.
197346: A man went every week to the rehearsal of the music society at the Zwijnebak. Every time the man walked home in the evening, he heard a goat screaming by the 'Douve', a little brook that flowed there. Because the man no longer dared to walk home alone, he had a group of friends accompany him. On the way the company heard a sound that resembled the bleating of a goat. More and more people came to listen to the goat, so that the local inn sold litres of beer. Every evening the sound was heard ten minutes later than the evening before. Because the sound seemed to come from the sky, two hunters from Nieuwkerke resolved to shoot the goat down. They never succeeded, however.
197351: In Dadizele there was a haunted castle. When people went to look there by day, there was nothing to see, but at night people came out of the castle. Yet the building was uninhabited.
197380: A man who had bought two piglets at the market met a woman on his way home, who said: "You have two fine piglets!" When he got home the man put his piglets in a pen. Immediately the animals began to fight wildly, so that the man had to fetch the priest. The clergyman placed something by the door and predicted that the piglets would calm down again because the witch could no longer get in. And so it was.
197396: Some people went to the friars of Steenbrugge because their child cried all the time. The friar advised the people to pray that evening. If they did so, the guilty person would come with a little rose and pluck off its petals.
197399: During the war a woman lived in Poperinge who had to live off her rabbits. It was said of that woman that she could do witchcraft. One day her neighbour, a farmer and innkeeper, was working on the hedge that separated her land from his. In doing so the farmer damaged the woman's rabbit hutches, so that all the animals ran away during the night. A few days later the farmer's horses, cows and pigs died. After a while the farmer himself fell ill too. Every time something went wrong at her neighbour's, the woman told a friend from the village about it. When the farmer was close to death, the friend felt she had to intervene and advised the farmer to have the friars of Sint-Sixtus read prayers over him. After that the farmer recovered. He lived another thirty years and no more of his animals died.
197401: A boy had been given an apple by a woman. The next day the boy did nothing but scream and cry. He was terrified and kept talking about a black cat he saw walking about.
197452: To prevent being ridden by the mare, one had to say: "Mare, mare, how far must you still travel. Over all the chimneys of the roof, before you pass the night".
197488: A carter was coming back from Roeselare with two horses and an empty cart. When the man reached the hill in front of the church, he could not get to the top. No matter how hard the horses were whipped, the animals could go no further. Suddenly someone said: "X is standing over there reading a book!" As soon as the woman had walked away, the horses could move on again.
197489: In a house the glass of the paraffin lamp broke every evening at around the same time. A witch was behind it.
197501: Every evening a sorceress in the shape of a black cat sat at a certain spot. After a little statue of the Virgin Mary had been placed at that spot, the cat was no longer seen.
197507: A man who was ridden by the mare felt a hand squeezing his throat shut.
197514: A chaplain was coming home at about three o'clock in the morning after administering the Last Sacraments to someone. On the way the chaplain met a thief, who threatened him with the words: "Your money or your life!" The chaplain explained that he had no money on him, but was willing to hand over his watch. After the thief had received the watch, the chaplain bewitched him to the ground so that he could no longer get away.
197518:
A little child from Poperinge was ridden by the mare at night. The girl was barely a few months old.
One day the girl's father had said to the workwoman: "I can't give you any bread this week. You will get it next week. We will bake then and you will get twice as much bread". The worker, however, held it against the man and bewitched his child. When they took the child to the friars of Ieper, the clergymen said: "That child has been ridden by the mare. You have refused someone something". After the friars had read prayers over the child, it was cured.
197544: Will-o'-the-wisps came out of the meadows and always quickly disappeared again. People said that will-o'-the-wisps were souls that found no rest.
197553: When a farmer had a plague of rats, he sought advice from a sorcerer, for he could send the rats to a nearby farm.
197557: Between 'de Zeug' and 'de Spriet' on the road to Poelkapelle, horses were stopped in their tracks and butter could not be churned. Moreover, the cows stood back to front in their stalls.
197571: Women who were ridden by the mare could do a lot of harm. One man lost three children that way. When that woman died, the misfortune came to an end.
197576: A woman's maid slept in the attic room. At midnight the maid woke up and saw a little flame flying from one window to the other. The woman's parents had died in that room and their wardrobe and bed were still there. The woman had said that the maid should come and knock if anything like that happened. But the maid did not dare and crept further under the sheets.
197596: A woman could make people lose their way. She could even make people fall into the water.
197609: A mother who had been to the friars with her youngest daughter was warned by one of the clergymen: "When you go home, you will meet x." On the way back the mother did indeed meet x. At that moment she could hardly carry her child any longer.
197610: A man on his way home was pestered by kittens running between his legs. The man did not dare to kick the animals.
197626: A man milking his cows saw a witch come by with smuggled goods. The witch said to the farmer: "That must be a good cow!" When that cow was due to calve some time later, the calf turned out to look like a dog. The cow was put out in the meadow. Some time later the witch walked past the meadow. At that moment the cow went mad and swam through the brook. It seemed as if the cow understood that this woman had bewitched her.
197653: A woman walking home in the evening was followed the whole way by a little cat. Annoyed, the woman gave the animal a beating. The next day a woman from the neighbourhood was injured. She was a sorceress who owned books of magic.
197659: In Oedelem lived a sorceress who owned books of magic. One day the sorceress laid a beautiful apple in a child's cradle. At that the child began to cry incessantly. The mother took the child to the fathers of Steenbrugge. The clergymen said: "It can no longer help, just go home". On the way home the child died.
197663: A shopkeeper saw a woman with one white shoe and one black shoe appear on eight nights in a row. The priest advised the shopkeeper to go to mass. After that she would no longer see the strange apparition. The woman went to mass and indeed did not see the ghost again.
197666: A woman rented a house from a witch. The cupboards of the house were full of ants and the bed was full of lice. When the woman opened the cupboards, however, the ants had suddenly disappeared. The woman always saw a witch with a little pointed cap, and at night she was ridden by someone who looked like the owner of the house. The woman told the dean that she was so frightened she no longer dared to sleep.
197683: Some young people returning from the fair saw a pretty little cat by the road and took it with them. At home the animal was put in the attic. At night, however, the cat made so much noise that someone went to have a look. In the attic sat a beautiful woman. The woman of the house consulted the curate, who advised her to take the cat back to the place it came from. When the people came home, they found that the woman had turned into a cat again. They took the animal back, but lost it on the way. The curate had said he would be there, but he was not.
197687: Every night a doodkeers (death candle, a ghostly light) appeared in the Kerkdreef in Vichte. One night a fearless man stuck his walking stick into the light. The next day the stick was completely burnt. The man began digging in that spot and found a pot of gold.
197711: A man grinding millstones one evening was hindered the whole time by a cat. When the man kicked the cat, there were suddenly some fifty cats around him. The man knelt down and made the sign of the cross. At that all the cats vanished. That must have been the work of a sorceress.
197734: To his surprise, every morning a farmer found a black horse standing in his stable, although the horse was not his. The farmer could not get the horse out of the stable, but all the farmhands together managed to get it to the field. The horse was harnessed to the plough and turned out to work even better than the other horses. So that very same day the horse was given horseshoes. The next day the strip where the black horse had worked turned out to be unploughed again. Moreover, the farmer's wife was lying in bed with horseshoes on her hands and feet.
197742: A woman who was ridden by the mare while lying in her bed woke up and could not move.
197780: A man who insisted that he did not believe in witches suddenly saw a white cat standing beside him. When the man kicked the animal, it turned into a woman. After that the man did believe in witches.
197783: Some people saw a ghost appear by the side of the bed in the evening when going to sleep. The priest advised the people to go on a pilgrimage. Because the people from Pittem could not make progress, the priest said: "You must say: 'The ghost goes ahead and we follow.'" When the pilgrims had said that, they could go on very easily.
197791: A girl who was moving her household goods by horse and cart was annoyed that the horses would not go forward. A little later the girl's mother came by and said: "Go on!" At that the horses moved on.
197792: Some people were sitting in a café when the maid from a farm came running in with the news that everything on the farm was being smashed to pieces. The farmer's wife had hidden in a cupboard with her little son. The lumps of plaster lying in the house were much bigger than the window openings. Moreover, no culprits were to be seen.
197808: In a village lived a woman who did harm to children. All the mothers in the village stuck an Easter nail under the door, so that the woman could not enter their houses.
197811: In Handzame lived a woman who sold all kinds of wooden goods. A woman from the village was so afraid of the seller that she never dared walk past her without greeting her. When that woman went to fetch bread one day, the seller came up to her and said: "Good day, good woman!" On the way back the woman was so afraid that she ran as fast as she could. On Friday the woman had to walk in the middle of the procession in the tableau of the nine choirs of angels. The next day the woman itched all over because she was covered in lice. Two days later all the lice had gone.
197818: On a haunted farm, fire broke out three or four times.
197831: Fishermen never let a woman come aboard a ship, because they believed it would bring bad luck.
197832: On a farm that had much misfortune there was always a black cat. One day they managed to hit the animal with a shovel. The next moment the cat turned into the neighbour woman.
197865: In Meetkerke a little statue that someone had fished out of the sea had been taken to the church. The next day it was lying in the dunes. It was taken to the church, but a day later it was lying in the dunes again. At their wits' end, people put the statue on a little donkey. The donkey stopped at the door of the church of Meetkerke. Since then a fishermen's pilgrimage to Meetkerke has always been held on the second or third Sunday of May.
197870: A woman coming home from work in the dark one evening saw a figure walking by the 'estakade' (?) and asked: "X, is that you?", to which a voice answered: "No". The woman quickly fled. She suspected that the figure was someone from the village whom everyone feared.
197884: A woman who went to gather mussels one night saw a seventh procession approaching. That was the Roesschaart.
197909: In the old days it sometimes happened that a farmer who went to fetch his cows in the evening got lost in the meadow. Through the doing of the evil hand he could no longer find the way out of his own meadow.
197918: A woman threw her sweater into the stove because the garment was full of lice. Together with her daughter the woman had to hold the lid of the stove firmly shut, because otherwise the sweater would jump out. One of the woman's daughters sent for a father from Steenbrugge. The father stayed a whole night in the attic to pray. The next morning he said to the people: "You must have a mason remove the threshold at the front door, so that we can put a blessed medal under it". This was done at the thresholds of all the outside doors. One day when it was raining hard, one of the daughters saw a woman walking outside and said: "I'll ask her if she wants to come in". The woman came up to the door, but she could not get over the threshold. She was responsible for the evil.
197919:
A woman innkeeper was suspected of being a witch, because wherever she visited, something went wrong. 
One day two brothers went to the Leie to ret flax. When they were about fifty metres from the inn, the load (?) overturned. The men went and knocked at the inn. The innkeeper came to look and tied the stacking presses (?) together with a rope. After that there were no more problems.
197953: In Vichte lived a framasson (freemason) who was immensely rich, although he did nothing. When the man went for a walk in the evening, he would stop by an old willow. There the devil was said to appear to give him money. When the framasson died, the coffin had to be filled with stones because the corpse had been taken by the devil.
197955: A hearse carrying a coffin had to cross the Zielebrug in Zuienkerke. But the horse would not cross the bridge, so the driver began to curse. That made the horse nervous and it shot forward. The coffin fell into the water and could never be brought up again. Since then the soul of that dead person haunts the bridge.
197958: In the old days haunting cats could often be seen roaming about. When people came outside, the cats jumped on their backs and feet. The animals also spat fire.
197960: In a back house lived a witch who had bewitched her husband so that he was stuck to a little chair. The man had to stay sitting in that chair for ten years. In the end the witch was burned.
197963: Farm Dee in the Biezen was haunted. The mill there turned by itself, and in the horse stable a plank at least a hundred years old was tied to the beam. On the plank, a stone lay on the rope with which the plank was tied. Yet nobody would have dreamed of touching that plank.
197967: A farmer had a meadow bordering the house of a supposed witch. One day, when the witch was sitting on a chair in the sun, the farmer's cows suddenly ran through the hedge and the barbed wire, injuring their hides and udders. The witch must have said something. Angry, the farmer went to the witch and said: "I'll damn well bash your head in if that happens again!" The witch answered: "They won't come any more!" And indeed, after that the cows no longer came near the witch.
197973: A man coming home through the wood got a fright when the branches of the trees suddenly struck him in the face. Some people claimed they had been kicked and beaten in the wood and had seen the patertjes (little fathers, a kind of goblin) dancing around them.
197998: A woman walking through the meadow to Westkapelle got lost through the doing of a sorceress. As soon as the woman began to read the Gospel of Saint John, she could find her bearings again.
198008: A man pushing a wheelbarrow home met a woman on the way. That woman made the man lose his way, and he had to wander about with his wheelbarrow for a long time.
198028: A carter was driving a heavy load from Brugge to Aartrijke. On a slope where an old woman lived, the horses suddenly could go no further. The carter was absolutely convinced that the old woman had bewitched the animals.
198034: When the fishermen were overtired, they believed they were being ridden by the mare. In reality it was just a bad dream. If you put your clogs upside down next to the bed, you were protected against the mare. The parish priest claimed that you had to call the sleeper's name twice to chase the mare away.
198057: One day they could not manage to pull a cart along with several horses. Then the men said: "We'll harness the devil to the cart." The next moment the devil appeared in the form of a horse. When the cart had been moved, the devil disappeared again and the farmer made the sign of the cross because everything had ended well.
198064: It was haunted at Maria's Linde in the Koestraat. At Sint-Maarten in the years 1906-1907, some men wanted to set fire to the lime tree. At about eight o'clock the men went to the tree with two bundles of straw. The next day as many as 15 white pipes lay around the tree.
198066: A hunchback from Ieper was a member of the freemasons. When the man had died and his coffin had to be carried to the church, no one managed to carry the heavy-as-lead coffin. The coffin turned out to be full of stones because the corpse had been taken away by the devils.
198068: One Sunday evening a man from Ardooie was sitting in the inn 'Het Zwijn' in Pittem, on the road from Kortrijk to Brugge. It was said that the woman innkeeper had special powers. When the man went home late that night, he got into bed with a nightcap on his head. The next morning the man had no hair left. Even his moustache and eyebrows had disappeared. Some time later the hair began to grow again. When the man died in 1918, his hair was still jet black.
198071: In Wijtschate lived a doctor who always wore a large hat and a wide cloak. This man owned books of magic. When children mocked him, he made them stand still on the spot or made sure they could no longer find their way. One day the doctor was murdered. The culprit was never found.
198091: A man was very often ridden by the mare. A ghost would then press on his heart, so that he could not cry out.
198093: A parish priest could make someone who came to steal apples from him stay in the tree until morning, so that he could see who the culprit was. Someone who rang his doorbell at night as a prank had to stay standing there until morning.
198109: A man went to steal plums from a woman's tree. The man could not get down from the tree, however, because the woman had bewitched him so that he was stuck there.
198121: A sorceress always went to a farmer to fetch milk. Because the woman kept coming earlier and earlier, the farmer said one day: "You mustn't come so early any more". The sorceress was angry about this, and as a result the farmer could no longer churn butter. After the horse doctor had read prayers over the farm, everything returned to normal.
198126: Some hunters shot at a hare several times but never managed to hit it. Convinced that they were bewitched, the hunters put crushed silver coins in their guns, for silver was blessed. When the hunters shot at the hare with that silver the next day, a woman from the area lost her buttock.
198145: A boy who had read in a special book made mice out of a handful of earth at school. One day the curate took the boy's magic power away.
198155: Two children whose brother had died of smallpox slept in the bake oven because there was not enough room in the house. In the evening the children always saw a ball of fire. Eventually they found their dead brother's pocket money on the beam of the oven. After the money had been found, the fireball no longer appeared.
198158: A woman who went walking in the wood with her father experienced some frightening moments. Although there was no wind, the trees could be seen moving back and forth. As soon as the two had left the wood, everything became quiet. When that man was asked on his deathbed whether they could have his books, he answered: "No, the books would bring you misfortune!"
198174: A woman who had gone to fetch shrimps met a witch who wanted some shrimps. The woman refused, however. Further along all the shrimps had turned into fleas. When you met such people, it was best to make the sign of the cross.
198185: When people had eaten crab, they must never throw the shells into the water before crushing them. It was believed that otherwise the shells would turn into a boat in which a witch would sail along the sides of the ship at night.
198187: Above the wet hay meadows along the Scheldt, a goat could be heard bleating on moonlit evenings, though there was nothing to be seen. When people then went to call the man who lived all alone in those meadows, he never turned out to be at home.
198220: A poacher who lived at a mill and wanted to shoot a hare at night had accidentally shot at a black cat, causing the animal to lose an eye. The next day a woman who had lost an eye came by the mill. That same woman had turned herself into a cat on that very night.
198235: In the past people believed that the stalkeersen (ghost lights) hanging over the land in the evening were ghosts.
198238: A man coming home from work in the evening got lost in a meadow. When the man made the sign of the cross, he saw a bridge right in front of his feet. The man had fallen victim to wizards.
198242: During the sermon some people in the church were laughing. After mass the priest asked why those people were staying in their seats. "We can't get away," the people answered. The priest then said: "If you behave a bit better next time, it won't happen again!"
198248: The priest made sure the witches could not leave the church by leaving his missal open at the part containing the Gospel of Saint John.
198263: If the first bird you saw in the morning was a magpie, something bad would happen that day.
198283: A mother always went to the fish auction to buy turbot, brill and sole. One day the mother met a woman who said: "I'd like to buy some brill from you; how much do you want for it?" But the two women could not agree on the price, after which the strange woman said: "You will walk around with your fish all week and sell nothing!" That week the mother indeed sold almost nothing. That woman had bewitched her.
198311: A woman who had spoken ill of a woman in the village suspected of witchcraft passed the house of the supposed witch with a sack of animal feed. In front of that house the woman had to dance for hours with the sack on her back.
198338: In a house in Meulebeke there was always a hellish noise at night, as if everything was being smashed to pieces. But nothing could be seen and in the morning there was no trace of what had happened. When the friars of Tielt came to exorcise the house, sweat dripped from their faces. The friars had to come back every seven years because the evil came one step closer each year.
198344: At a farm infested with blue rats, the people sought advice from the parish priest. The priest advised them to dig a pit a little way off. Then the priest drove all the rats into that pit, which the farmer then filled in. The rats had been sent by a witch.
198382: On the road to the church stood an old wayside chapel where as many as ten or twenty cats sat. The people going to mass no longer dared to walk past it because those cats dragged passers-by into a well.
198385: It was haunted at the moated castle of Loppem. A man had seen a procession there at night with singing people dressed in white.
198428: A witch in the shape of a cat crept into a house through the drain hole for the water. The woman who lived in that house poured a pan of hot butter over the cat. The next day the witch was walking around with burns on her face.
198433: By a brook lived a witch who could make every passing wagon drive into the water.
198453: A man travelling with a cart full of grain fell victim to a witch who owned books of magic. Right beside a steep drop the cart fell over, although nothing was broken. Later people went and took the witch's books of magic from her.
198462: When the children came back from school, they could not move forward. They were bewitched.
198467: Raverschoote was haunted. When people lay in their beds at night, they heard sounds as if plates were being washed, butter churned and cows fed. The next morning, however, there was no sign of any of it.
198484: During the occupation a witch lived in Oostduinkerke. Everyone who drove past the witch's house with a cart had bad luck. The cart fell over or a wheel broke off.
198490: By the marshes in Voormezele a goat always came bleating. People believed that the goat was a ghost and came from far and wide to listen to the bleating. Later it turned out that the innkeeper was responsible for the haunting; he wanted to lure many customers to his inn.
198491: A man returning from Kortrijk had to pass a field where nothing grew. Suddenly the man saw a glass castle standing there, from which he heard noise and chatter. The man went up to the castle and said: "Praised be Jesus Christ". A moment later the castle had vanished. When the man got up the next morning, his hair had turned grey.
198509: The eternal hunter always had to wander because he had been cursed by his father or mother.
198515: One Sunday afternoon a farmer's wife was showing her piglets to a visitor. The visitor slapped one of the animals on the backside. At that the pig began to squeal loudly and ran around in a frenzy.
198520: In the past Heestert suffered from a real plague of witches. People went to church in a hooded cloak and a fine sheet. When they left the church, they found that a large piece had been cut out of the sheet. One day the priest threatened in church to deal with the culprits. After that the sheets were no longer cut.
198530:
The landlady of a café was a sorceress. If the farmers walked past her café without coming in, she turned their feet around. One day a man asked the landlady: "Can you bewitch me?" As the man walked home, he saw three beautiful young ladies. The man spoke to the ladies, but there was no answer. When the man was bewitched a second time, an exceptionally large roller came towards him. The third time, the man was thrown into the water on the way without getting wet. 
One day the landlady had touched a child's hair. The next day the child was dead.
198534: The occupants of two farms built opposite each other were quarrelling. The farmer of one farm said: "It's strange that it always starts raining when we go threshing! That's the fault of that black one over the way!"
198542: People who were ridden by the mare had a nightmare. Those people had the friars read prayers over them. The clergymen advised them not to eat meat or other heavy food in the evening. They also advised them to wash well in the morning.
198567: In the old days people did not dare to pass the churchyard because they were afraid of the returning dead.
198574: A man who had been to the butcher met two women on the way. The man was so frightened that he fell ill. When two priests came to read prayers over the man, they told his brother to go and fetch medicine. If the brother met those two women on the way, he was not to look at them or speak to them. Suddenly the sick man said to one of the priests: "They're there!" The clergyman answered: "We see them. They will come back once more, but after that you will never see them again". And so it happened.
198583: A sorcerer put a birch broom into a bucket of water. All the drops that then fell on the ground turned into mice.
198595: On a road between Kortemark and Koekelare a man was driving a cart loaded with tiles. When a little fellow sat down on the cart, the horses suddenly could go no further. "Get off that cart!" the carter said to the little fellow. After the little fellow had climbed off the cart, the horses could move on again without any trouble.
198621: A man who had been ridden by the mare had lost the hair on his head and his beard in the morning. But that could also happen because one had had a bad dream.
198623: Some fishermen's children made mice out of clay during catechism class. After they had blown on the mice, the animals ran away. "What are you doing there? Do that again!" said the priest. On the fourth attempt the children could no longer make mice.
198629: One evening a parish priest was threatened by sorcerers who came out of the woods. The clergyman asked whether he could first take a pinch of snuff. Meanwhile the clergyman quickly said his prayers, so that the sorcerers were bewitched to the ground and had to stay standing until the next morning.
198632: A farmer's wife who had a two-year-old daughter was visited every day by a woman who came to fetch 2.5 litres of milk. The woman always paid for the milk straight away. The farmer's wife's child was afraid of that woman and in the end would not even eat, drink or sleep any more. When the farmer's wife slept with her child in another bed, the child flew a good fifty centimetres into the air. A tobacconist from the village had a son of twenty-six or twenty-seven. One day the woman had struck that son on the shoulders. Two weeks later the son began to talk nonsense, so his father went to a card reader in Wervik. The card reader said to the man: "You have a son who is no longer right in the head. He had a girlfriend, but you and your wife did not approve. You had better have let him marry, because now he will probably not recover. Go to the friars. The boy's condition may get better or worse." The man went to the friars and his son's condition got even worse. One day the tobacconist went to the farmer and his wife, whose child was also bewitched. The man advised the farmer to go to the card reader as well. From that woman the farmer heard: "You have a sick child who will only live fourteen more days. Go to Ieper." The farmer hurried home and went to Ieper with his child. From the friars the farmer received something blessed that he had to use for nine days. Because that had not helped, the farmer went to Ieper again. This time the friar said: "You must not believe in such things. I will send another friar to your house." When the neighbour came for milk the next morning, she said: "I've forgotten my money, I'll pay next time." At about ten o'clock the friar came by. The clergyman advised the farmer to open the stable doors and he hung a blessed cloth on the door. The next day the woman did not come for milk. She never came again after that. A while later the child began to eat again. When the girl had grown up, she always began to tremble and cry when she saw that woman. She would then cry out: "There's a witch over there!" Yet no one had ever told the girl what had happened in her childhood.
198638: In 1273 Arnold van Maldegem founded a hospital which three hundred years later was stolen by the Sint-Jansheren of Bruges. At the place where the hospital had stood, a voice could be heard every night calling: "Justice!" Later Canon Andries started a lawsuit against the Sint-Jansheren. Compensation of 270,000 gold francs (1) was paid. Since the day of the payment the voice has not been heard calling.
198647: A child lying in a pram was visited by a woman from the neighbourhood. The child began to cry without stopping. In the end the priest was sent for.
198677: In a house a black cat was always walking about, which opened the door itself by jumping onto the latch. Because the people living in that house always had bad luck, they decided to chop off the cat's head. The attempt failed, however; the cat managed to escape with a cut in its neck. A while later the residents found that a little old woman from the neighbourhood was lying in bed with a wound in her neck.
198703: In Westrozebeke lived a woman who could work magic. The woman forbade her husband to go to work in France. When the woman was visited by a farmer's wife who wanted her goat to be covered, the woman said: "I won't take my billy goat out of the stable. Your goat will never be with young again". What the woman had said came true.
198719: A farmer had moved the boundary post of his field to get a bigger piece of land. After his death the farmer had to haunt. One day a farmer met someone holding a boundary post. "What are you going to do with that?" the farmer asked. As soon as he saw it was a boundary post, he added: "Put it where you got it!" The next moment the man with the boundary post had vanished.
198747: A woman who had worked as the priest's maid could work magic. She could make a little light appear in the fir wood. When people came closer, strangely enough, there was no light to be seen any more. The woman never went to bed before midnight and behaved like a sanctimonious bigot.
198757: Rats had to be sent to an enemy who lived not too far away and who had food in the house. One then had to say: "I swear in God's name that all these rats will move to x." Then one had to shout and kick everything over. In every place where there were rats, one was surrounded by the animals, which, led by a big fat rat, went to the place they were being sent to.
198758: Many people coming back from Oostende got lost on the way. They only found their way again when the witch came to release them. Suddenly an old woman would appear and say: "Well, what are you doing here?" After that, they could find the way again.
198762: A large church was said to have once sunk in Heestert. After that, the ringing of bells was heard at that spot every year on Ascension Day. That is why the procession in Heestert is held on Ascension Day.
198773: The woods of Anzegem were haunted. Two friends who went from Anzegem to Oudenaarde one day saw a woman with a black veil walking in those woods. The man said to the woman: "You must speak or I will strike." The woman answered: "For me it is night and for you it is day." That woman was probably a returning dead person.
198776: A mother whose child was very thin asked a neighbour to go with her to Steenbrugge. The woman went along and carried the child. The closer they came to Steenbrugge, the heavier the child became. In Steenbrugge the child was prayed over by a father. At a certain moment, however, the clergyman walked away because he could not bear it any longer. Another father gave the people something that broke the spell. The child's mother had borrowed a red nappy from someone. A child had once died in that nappy. After the fathers intervened, everything was all right.
198787: People who were ridden by the mare in their beds could no longer breathe.
198788: Some people who had a small child were visited by an old woman who stroked the child and praised its beauty. When the woman had gone, the child began to cry without stopping. Because the child would no longer eat either, the fathers were sent for. The fathers prayed over the child and advised the parents to go on a pilgrimage and to go to confession and communion on seven consecutive days. In the end the old woman was driven out of the parish.
198810:
Toveressen (sorceresses) were women who had power over someone. 
People whose child cried all day went on a pilgrimage. On arrival they saw a black cat sitting on a wall. That was the witch. The fathers advised the people to throw everything the witch gave the child into the stove. When the child was given a dummy, the mother threw it into the fire. After that the witch could do the child no more harm.
198826: Doodkeersen (death candles, ghost lights) that moved back and forth were spirits of the dead who returned.
198835: On a farm plagued by rats, they sent for a man who could make the rats disappear. After the man had done his work, however, they refused to pay him. So the man made the rats come straight back.
198838: Priests tried to get hold of the witches' books of magic, but usually they did not succeed. If a priest left his missal open on the altar after mass, the witches could not leave the church. In this way a witch was unmasked in Sijsele.
198842:
Near the Kruiskassei in Lichtervelde stood a house where strange things happened. At night an inner door in that house opened and closed by itself, although there was nothing to be seen.
On some old houses there was a little bell that began to ring by itself at night.
198844: Witches could turn cats into dogs and vice versa.
198877: Two poachers had shot at a hare several times, but they could not hit the animal. A little further on the poachers met a dog that blocked their way. After that the poachers got lost. A little further on the poachers met a witch. She had been tormenting them.
198889: A farmer milking the cows in the evening always heard music coming from the sieve and the milk can. As soon as the sieve was closed, it went quiet. One evening the farmer saw movement at the skylight. He fired his double-barrelled gun through the skylight. After that he no longer heard the sounds and saw no more movement there.
198901: A woman who claimed she was being ridden by the mare walked up and down the stairs. Then she sat down on the floor and held something in her hand that she believed was the mare.
198923: On a farm that had much misfortune, people sought advice from the fathers of Sint-Sixtus. The fathers gave the farmer something blessed to put under the door. After that the witch came by once more. She knocked on the window, then went on and broke a leg.
198930: Whoever was touched by a witch was bewitched and became completely emaciated. To protect oneself against witchcraft, one had to strike the witch higher, so that she was powerless. People who wore a scapular or used holy water could still get lice through a witch, but they could not be bewitched.
198937: In Waarmaarde there was a haunted spot where people sometimes had to stand still for no apparent reason. It was as if they were nailed to the ground.
198943: If you had beckoned to a doodkeers (death candle, a ghostly light), you had to go inside quickly and slam the door. Doodkeersen were the souls of people who had hidden money and had told no one. Doodkeersen always moved up and down. You had to ask the lights what they wanted, because they did not say so of their own accord.
198957: In summer the priests of Tielt went to collect grain from the farmers. When they went to collect butter in the month of May, they came to a farm where the farmer's wife could no longer churn butter. The priest asked for a bucket of manure and poured it into the churn together with the milk. Then the priest went to pray in the cellar behind a closed door until he was drenched in sweat. Then he said: "Now pour milk into the churn and start churning." The people had never had such good butter. The priest said: "Now they have gone off with the manure instead of the butter."
198965: On a farm in Waregem there were a hundred rats. A wizard put a big basket in the middle of the house and began reading from a big book until he was sweating heavily. The more the wizard read, the more rats appeared and crawled into the basket. When the wizard had finished reading, the farmer was rid of the rats.
198973: In Gullegem there was a farm where every night noise was heard in the horse stable. When the door was opened, however, there was nothing to be seen. The whole stable was haunted.
198980: During a storm, a man was hitting at the crows sheltering under the branches of the trees. Suddenly the man saw a fire fly out of the ditch.
198992: Whoever was ridden by the mare in bed felt as if something had been thrown onto his feet, which then crept up along his legs. Then he was nearly strangled by a heavy weight. To protect oneself against the mare, one had to put one's clogs under the bed with the heels first.
199007: A newly married woman whose husband was in the army had to go to bed alone every night, to her great fright. As soon as the woman lay in her bed, she felt as if her throat was being tied shut and her hands were being seized.
199034: Whoever was ridden by the mare began to sweat heavily and could no longer see. The mare always came in by the door or through the roof tiles and then grabbed her victim by the throat. A man who was ridden by the mare once threw a bucket of hot water over the mare. A moment later his mother fell to the floor beside him.
199036: In the past, when children from Beselare had walked past the cottage of an old woman suspected of being a sorceress, they washed themselves with soap when they got home, because they were afraid they would otherwise get pimples.
199040: Some people were coming back from the woods, where they had gone to gather heather to make brushes. On the way the people sat down for a short rest. At that moment a kitten came along. One of the men took out his knife to strike at the animal, but the other said: "Leave alone everything that leaves you alone." The man attacked the animal anyway. On the way home that man could hardly carry his bundle of heather any more. Three days later he was dead.
199049: Two men going from Westkerke to Oudenburg came across a cat that kept getting under their feet. The men tried several times to kick the cat, but they could not hit the animal. When they got home, the men found that the cat had disappeared.
199069: In Nieuwpoort lived a certain Jeanne Panne, who could turn herself into a bird or a waternekker (water sprite). When the fishermen had to go on board at night, they got lost through the doing of the witch.
199077: Whoever had worked too much could be ridden by the mare in his sleep.
199098: A witch's spirit could leave the body and float from one place to another. In this way a witch could make children's blood stand still.
199130: A dead man came to haunt a house in Deerlijk. The man sat in a corner of the room counting his money. When he was asked why he came back, he said he had hidden money somewhere. The occupants of the house had to dig for the money. When the people had found the money, they gave it to the ghost, who counted it over with him. As soon as that was done, the released dead man disappeared.
199193: Framassons (freemasons) were unbelievers who had sold their soul to the devil for a number of years. In return the devil gave them everything they wanted. In the end the devil struck his victim dead because he had had so much trouble with him.
199194: A woman suspected of being a witch touched some cloths hanging on a washing line. The next moment the cloths were full of fleas. It was said that this witch's daughter could also work magic.
199196:
When a few people were coming back in the dark from Ichtegem, where the friars had come to preach, one of them saw a fire burning on the other side of the ditch.
In the old days there was a lot of witchcraft.
199205: In the evening, witches came hopping into a house on one leg. They threw down their stick, so that no one could move anymore. After a while the witches left again.
199225: At the castle of Loppem a procession could be seen in the evening. The cows there were always untied at night.
199236: In Beernem lived a man who owned a book of magic with which he could make rats and lice appear. One day the man said to a shoemaker: "Will you believe that in five minutes this place will be full of rats?" And so it was.
199243: A man who went to fetch his horse found to his amazement that there were two horses, although he had only one. That was witchcraft.
199269: A man heard that his uncle came back exactly one year after his death. The dead man could be heard making noise all night long.
199285: If a fisherman set off for his ship with his basket full of clothes and a woman wished him a good journey, the fisherman would invariably turn back home. People believed that such wishes brought bad luck.
199286: A woman whose child had 'the old man' (rickets) and cried all day went on a pilgrimage to Aalbeke. One day, while the woman was cleaning the stove, a visitor had bewitched the child in the cradle.
199319: In Avelgem lived a witch who liked to tease people. One day a group of people came past her house, returning from church with a newly baptised baby. When the cart drove past the witch's house, it tipped over and the baby landed in the witch's bed.
199329: In Elverdinge the ringing of bells was often heard at night, and no one knew where it came from.
199353: Some people who woke from their sleep at night saw people sitting silently at a large table. Those were the 'vramassons' (1).
199356: In a house where a toad had come in, a girl stamped the animal to death and threw it in the stove. When the girl went upstairs a little later, she found her mother lying dead in bed.
199370:
A little dog was always seen sitting on a tree stump. No one knew where the dog came from, as only a small hole could be seen. Moreover, near that stump not a single hare could be shot anymore. One day a pot of money was found there. That was probably money that had been stolen or embezzled.
After that day the little dog was no longer seen and the hunters could catch hares again without trouble.
Since the Gospel of Saint John has been read after Mass, evil has no more power.
199392: A family had a little son who lay crying in his cradle day and night. They took the child to the fathers, who said: "A woman comes to visit you every day. That woman will never come again". In the child's nappies a whole packet of pins was found. Someone had magically put those pins into the child's body.
199393: In the Valkestraat lived a woman who one evening received a visit from relatives from Oostende who wanted to stay the night. The woman was happy for them to stay, but she warned them that a strange noise could always be heard at night. During the night the two men were woken by a sound, but they pretended to be still fast asleep. So the men saw two strange figures come in. The ghosts came to check whether the men were really asleep and then pulled a tile out of the hearth. From a hole they took a large bag of coins, which they began to count. "Yes, everything is correct. We'll put it back with the papers," said the ghosts. Then they disappeared. After the men had told the woman everything in the morning, they brought up the money together. The woman took the papers to the parish priest. Once the instructions had been carried out, the priest told her that the rest of the money was hers. The woman added an extra storey to her house and never saw or heard anything at night again.
199399: Some women could lay the evil hand on children. Such children wasted away completely and eventually died.
199417: In a house a tapping was always heard in the cellar at night, although there was nothing to be seen. It was as if someone was knocking on the inside of the wall.
199421: A brave nun had heard noises in the convent at night as if the tables and chairs were being thrown about. The next morning that nun only dared to go downstairs if three other nuns went with her. Downstairs they found that there was nothing strange to be seen.
199430: A woman always saw a witch or a doodkaars (corpse candle, a light foretelling death) whenever she went to a nearby farm.
199436: A family was visited by a neighbour who gave everyone a sweet and gave the bag with the leftovers to the child. Because the little boy then cried all the time, the mother went to ask her own mother for advice, who told her to hang something blessed above the door. When that was done, the witch could no longer enter the house.
199442: A man kicked at a white cat sitting by the side of the gravel road. The man missed and the cat ran off. Further on the cat appeared again, but this time on the other side of the road. This went on the whole time until the man was home.
199497: Near a little chapel in Avelgem lived some devout Christian ladies, said to be related to the German officer Rommel. One day the two ladies had died. When a farmer and his wife went to early Mass at Christmas and passed that chapel, they saw the two ladies floating in the air in white and disappearing into a copse at two o'clock at night. The farmer's wife went back home and afterwards lay in bed for weeks because she had been so frightened.
199498: On a farm in Merkem the cows were found untied in the morning. What is more, the animals there gave no milk.
199499:
In West Flanders lived a doctor who was always poorly dressed but who had special powers. This doctor managed to cure people whom other doctors had given up on. A man from Mesen who had been declared incurable received medicine from this doctor, which made him vomit up lots of frogs' legs, although he had never eaten frogs' legs. In the end the man was cured.
Once when the doctor was walking through the Kriekbossen, he was threatened by robbers who demanded his money. "Wait here a moment," said the doctor, and he went home while the two robbers stood bewitched to the ground. The next day the doctor said to a man from Wijtschate: "Go to the Kriekbossen and tell those two men there that they may move on."
One day the doctor was beaten to death. Because it was never known who did it, people believed that devils had killed the doctor.
199500: A woman who was pregnant with her third child saw a black cat. Because of this the woman became very ill. She believed that the black cat was a sorceress.
199503: By the stump of a felled walnut tree a doodkeers (death candle, ghost light) danced every evening. The children were not allowed to beckon to that doodkeers, or else the returned dead person would torment them.
199522: In a house in Watou there was a child that cried all the time. A father believed that someone had the child in their power and said: "The first person who comes to visit tomorrow morning, you must throw out". But the people did not dare follow the father's advice. After that the child became very thin.
199544: It was said of a sick child that it had been bewitched by an old woman while it lay in the cradle.
199556: A poacher who lived near a churchyard one day saw a hare running in the churchyard. The man went to the churchyard, but the gate was locked. He saw the hare run off at the sight of the light made by the corpses. Later those lights were called 'doodkaarsen' (death candles).
199558: Today is Saturday, it is God's day. The mare was an evil spirit. A wicked woman who was often ridden by the mare made the sign of the cross with holy water over her bed every evening.
199569: On a farm the cows gave hardly any milk and no butter could be churned. On the day before Christmas everything on the farm was ablaze and devils were seen dancing there. After a friar had come to pray there, the strange goings-on came to an end. After a while, however, the haunting was said to return. It was caused by a murder or by the sinful life someone had led.
199576: On Christmas Eve a ghostly procession went around in Veldegem. That procession could not get past a crossroads.
199592: In Halewijn two girls were walking past the church to the fair. On the way they met a Duitse schaper (German shepherd, a wandering shepherd believed to have magic powers), who said: "Young ladies, may I come along with you?" The girls answered: "Aren't you ashamed!" and turned their heads the other way. When the girls got to the fair, they were covered in lice, so that they had to go back at once. The Duitse schaper saw them again and said: "Are you back already?", to which the girls said: "You bewitched us and now we're covered in lice!"
199594: A man went to fetch the midwife for his wife. While the man was away, a witch wandered around his house. Later the man got a heart disease. The witch had done that to him. After a pilgrimage had been made for the man, he was cured.
199595: A farmhand who was ploughing saw a witch standing in a thicket, breaking branches. The next day the farmhand was covered in lice.
199610: A twenty-year-old man was ridden by the mare. It was a stopping of the blood, which could be felt rising from his feet. The man's brother had set out a bucket of water to pour over the mare the next time, so that she would become visible. The next time the man saw one of the neighbour girls lying beside him. The girl asked him if she could stay and sleep with him.
199618: Parents returned after their death if they had been wronged too much.
199632: A hedge in Deerlijk used to be haunted. At night and even during the day the hedge kept swaying back and forth, although there was no wind. A great many curious people came to look at that hedge.
199637: A sorceress lived in Izegem. One day a man saw the sorceress's cat lying dead in the street in a pool of blood. Strangely enough, the next day the animal was walking about alive again. One day while the man sat working, he felt that the sorceress's cat was watching him. As soon as the man had made the sign of the cross, the cat had vanished without a trace.
199643: In a family in Esen all the children died, so at a certain point the people decided to go to the fathers. The fathers predicted that a woman would come to visit the next morning. The next morning a woman came asking whether the farm happened to be selling pigs. The farmer's wife said no and sent the woman away. After that no more children died on that farm. The misfortune had been caused by the reading of little books.
199667: A sick woman could not die. The woman had quarrelled with another woman from the village. After they had tried three times to fetch that other woman, she came and asked forgiveness. After that the sick woman could die.
199698: In Oekene there were places where white cats always sat. People who saw the cats were afraid and tried to stab the animals with a spade. But they could not hit the cats.
199720: Every Thursday a man went to the market in Staden with his girlfriend. The pair came home around three in the afternoon. One day the man was a little drunk when he came home, which made his mother angry with the mother of his girlfriend, a woman who was said to be able to work magic. The sorceress said to the man's mother: "Just let your son marry my daughter. He will be allowed to spend a franc every day on cake and ham". The mother said to her son: "You go and rest a bit. We're going home". When they thought the son was asleep, the mother went home. On the way, however, her son caught up with her. The boy was forced to walk behind his mother for eight days. After that the mother truly believed that the sorceress had special powers.
199733: A woman who had had a child and was going to her churching with another woman met a witch on the way, who immediately came up to her and said: "How are you doing now?" When the mother got home, she could no longer breastfeed her child, because she had no more milk.
199735:
A man going to Hertsberge saw hundreds of black cats sitting in the trees at night. There was also a cat sitting in the middle of the road. The man left the cats alone and carefully drove past them. They were all sorceresses.
When that man's brother was coming home at night with the horse and cart, he saw a little black cat sitting there and threw a stone at it. A little further on the man drove through water and then through fire. The man came home as pale as death.
199767: In the past a witch whom everyone feared lived in Gijzelbrechtegem. One day the witch came into a stable where the farmer's wife was milking the cows. Suddenly the farmer's wife's stool was flung away. The farmer's wife put the stool back, after which the same thing happened again. When the farmer's wife saw the witch standing there, she gave her a good box on the ear. That made the witch powerless.
199774: A woman who had not been given any butter said to the farmer: "I wish all your animals would die!" While the woman was going home, the animals died.
199797: Near Knesselare a pig used to roam about. A man going to play cards was followed by the animal as far as the Maldegemweg. On the way back, too, the pig walked along with the man. When the people in the café made noise, the little pig leaned with its front legs on the windowsill. When a man kicked at the pig, the animal flew off through a fence in which there was no opening!
199802: In the past it often happened that a child fell ill after a witch had taken it in her arms.
199812: A boy met a dirty old man who could work magic. The boy asked the man: "How are your lice doing?", to which the man replied: "Just make sure you don't get any!" The boy then said: "You can't do anything to me!" When the boy came home, however, he was covered in lice, so that he had to go and beg the sorcerer to take the lice away.
199823: During Mass in the church of Hulst, many cloaks were cut to pieces by witches. The priest warned the witches with the words: "If this business with the cloaks doesn't stop, I'll make your names known!"
199829: In the old days there were witches who went out at night. A woman went to church with a small child. In the church she realised that the witch was sitting behind her.
199858: Whoever wanted to keep the mare away had to put his clogs crossed under the bed.
199864: On the cobbled road from Rumbeke to Rollegem-Kapelle, between the café 't Kruuschge and the café de Vuulpanne, a man met a woman whom he suspected of being a witch. "If you can do anything, go on and do it!" the man said to the woman. Shortly afterwards the man fell ill. He went to the priest of Rollegem-Kapelle and told him what had happened. The priest advised the man to go back to the place where the woman had bewitched him. The man would meet the woman there again, but he was not allowed to speak to her. After that the man would be cured. What the priest foretold did indeed come true.
199865: A woman from Oostende often went to Gistel with her small child. Because the child behaved strangely and someone had said that it might be bewitched, the woman sought advice from someone. That person told her: "When you go home, you always meet a woman who kindly strokes your child. Next time you must place an Easter nail by the child. The woman will then not be able to touch your child." And so it was.
199889: People who lay flat on their backs could be ridden by the mare. Without opening the door, the mare came in and grabbed her victim by the throat. Whoever was ridden by the mare tried to cry out, but no sound came. To protect oneself against the mare, one had to put a row of clogs beside the bed from front to back. One must never look at the stars or point at them, or one would also become a victim of the mare. One must not touch plants with flattened branches, because those too had been ridden by the mare.
199892: If a witch had touched a child, the child cried itself to death.
199895: A woman was cutting grass for her rabbits together with her child. Suddenly the woman saw a wolf that threatened to come near her child. The woman then cut off one of the animal's legs with a sickle. The next day a woman from the neighbourhood had lost her arm.
199898: A witch had bewitched a pig on a farm. Because of this the animal kept running around until it finally dropped dead.
199927: A woman keeping watch over a dead person in Ghent or in Bruges heard twelve knocks on the coffin at the stroke of midnight. When the coffin was opened, it turned out to be empty.
199934: A woman always saw a coach driving along the road, which burst into flames. When one came closer, the whole scene had vanished.
199938: Near the Keiberg in Beselare stood a farm that was haunted. There were no witches there, however, because they lived in another street.
199983:
People who were ridden by the mare had to say the following prayer three times:
"Mare, mare, in the evening the mare rides. Saint Peter, if you can, keep the mare far from me. And I know that you can, I ask that you grant it to me too. Therefore, before I go to sleep, help me to the grace of God, that the mare may ride over every hedge and fence, over all blades of grass, over all plants and sticks, so that she is very tired before she can reach my bed!"
Because the mare then had so much work, she would not yet have reached her victim by the next morning.
199987: In Poelkapelle lived a woman who was suspected of being able to bewitch. On a farm where one of the children was bewitched, people sought advice from the friars of Ieper. The clergymen decided to hold a novena. During that novena, the little woman came one day to look through the window of the back door. The next moment she turned around and left.
200042: A woman who went to fetch food for her cows was followed the whole time by a cat. The woman took the cat home and put the animal on the windowsill. When the woman's brother went to the meadow with his cows, the two cows died. That was because the man had shot the cat dead.
200065: A woman who had toothache one night got up and heard noise in the street. A man with a dog cart could not go on because a witch was blocking his way. When a drunkard had struck the witch with a whip, the man with the dog cart could go on again.
200105: When people saw a doodkaars (death candle, a ghostly light) somewhere, they believed it was a returned dead person who had hidden something in that spot.
200117: The spot where the little chapel of Onze-Lieve-Vrouw-ter-Ruste was built used to be haunted. At night the looms could always be heard working there, although no one was at work. Once the chapel had been built there, the haunting came to an end.
200119: A man who could not churn butter sought advice from the friars. The man had to put an oak stick in the butter churn and hang medals everywhere. A few days later the man found a whole mound of butter in the grain. After that the man could make butter again. A woman from the neighbourhood never visited again after that.
200128: A lady and a gentleman are said to have once lived in the Maurice Dewulfstraat. At midnight the people of the village saw the gentleman appear in a black tailored suit and a tall silk hat. The lady wore a long dress. Arm in arm the lady and the gentleman floated to the end of the street. Then they turned back and went inside, after which there was nothing more to be seen.
200146: On a farm there were always problems when a horse or a cow was due to give birth. At such times a neighbour woman was always at the farm. She bewitched the pregnant cows and horses.
200149: Doodkeersen or stalkeersen (death candles, ghost lights) were the souls of returning murderers who came out of the ground and flew through the air, to the great fright of the people.
200158: People who claimed they had been ridden by the mare suffered from a certain illness.
200165: A witch could sit with her toe in the fire without burning herself.
200168: A cobblestone layer walking to work through the Waterstraat in the morning saw a sudden storm wind beat the branches to the ground. He also saw a horse cart go by, which a moment later had vanished without a trace.
200174: In Oostende lived a woman who peddled shrimp. If people did not buy shrimp from her, she would set the devil on them at night, for she owned many books. Her husband suffered a great deal from her. In the end the dean of Oostende came to collect the woman's books. The woman then had to do the Stations of the Cross on her knees every day. While she did so, the church was closed because no one was allowed to see her. In this way the woman's husband was delivered.
200179: In a house on the Kleine Weg in Roeselare the children fell ill during the war, so that a pilgrimage had to be made for them. The woman who lived in the house saw a man standing in her room at night. As long as the apparition stood there, the woman could not utter a word. It was the previous owners of the house who caused all those strange things.
200183: In the haunted house in Ramskapelle the spirits of the dead came to dance on the floor.
200196: A woman claimed that little souls wandered about the churchyard of Westkapelle and that voices rose from the graves.
200210: A woman had died in Westkerke. After her death, the neighbours heard shuffling in her house, as if someone were walking around in slippers. The people then went to inform the dead woman's daughters. In one of the walls of the house the daughters found a loose stone behind which a fortune was hidden. After that no more strange noises were heard in the house.
200216:
The house of a widower was badly haunted. The plates and clocks hanging on the wall rattled.
One day the farmhand and the maid who worked for the widower went to fetch the man's books from the attic. Once the books had been taken away from there, everything in the house went back to normal.
200224: At a farm in Moerkerke an insolent and headstrong farmhand was dismissed. A few days later the farm's barn was full of rats.
200225: A man's mother had drowned in a well. Because the man was always pursued by doollichten (will-o'-the-wisps), people said that the man had murdered his mother.
200234: A man who could not churn butter always heard noises in the stables at night, though there was nothing to be seen. In the end the man went to have prayers read over him by the friars. The clergyman said to the man: "Your neighbour woman is doing this to you. She will come to visit tomorrow morning, but you must not let her in and you must never look at her or speak to her." When the man followed that advice, he had no more misfortune.
200242: A shepherd had a young son. At night the shepherd always heard a noise as if the pots and pans were being thrown about. Strangely, there was never anything to be seen. At midnight a woman always came who claimed she came from Spain. One day the shepherd's son went to the friars, who gave him the following advice: "You must stay awake until that woman has come by, and you must hold a bread knife with the point upwards. The mare will then lie down on that knife". When the boy did as the friars had advised, he heard a woman's voice say: "Ow". Since then he has been able to sleep peacefully every night.
200251: In Knesselare werewolves went about wearing an animal skin. Passers-by had to carry the werewolves. A butcher who was jumped on by a werewolf one evening drew his knife and stabbed the beast. The werewolf then changed into a farmer's son, who dropped dead a little later.
200288: A farmer's wife who had sold a cow had tied the animal to the wall. The next morning the animal had been hanged, without anyone knowing how it had happened. The farmer's wife sought advice from the friars of Steenbrugge, who said: "Go back home. On the way you may greet passers-by, but do not stop to talk with them. When you are home, I will make the witch pass by, and then she will have no more power."
200312: One evening a couple from Brugge came home by horse and cart. As they entered the town they saw a little woman leaning out of the window of one of the cottages. When the man and woman got home, their horse would not stand still. Only when the man and woman began talking to passers-by did the horse stand still.
200314: Near Nieuwkerke there had lived a man who was said to have come back after his death. Many people believed it.
200317: A woman went to the friars of Ieper with the child of a mother from the village. From the station of Staden to the church of Ieper, the woman was followed by a tall red-haired woman. The friars read prayers over the child until they were drenched in sweat. They predicted that the woman would no longer be followed on the way back. The child died nevertheless.
200318: A widower who at four o'clock at night saw the ghost of his dead wife lying beside him hurried to the parish priest to tell what had happened. The man had also heard the clogs under his bed rattling. After the priest gave him a prayer, the man went back home. The dead woman was still lying in the bed. The man crawled into his bed and began to pray. A little later the ghost had vanished.
200319: On a farm they could not churn butter, so they sent for the friars of Steenbrugge. A friar sat in a room to pray until he was drenched in sweat. Meanwhile the people had to churn. When the farmer saw a woman approaching again, he said: "We won't have any butter again." The friar replied: "That is not true. That woman already has the butter under her skirt." The woman had indeed stolen the butter from the churn. From that day on the people on that farm could make butter again. However, they were never allowed to mention the woman's name, or the evil would return.
200335: In Knesselare lived Bohemians who could give people a plague of lice. Once those men had put a louse on someone's house or bed, the people could only get rid of the lice by having the friars read prayers over them.
200341: No one dared to enter the cellar of the Vollebeke castle in Hooglede. If you stuck a stick into it, it burned up completely. Even the Germans did not dare to enter the castle.
200345:
During the sermon a parish priest said: "Some thieves are stealing my cherries." After mass the thieves were still sitting in the cherry tree. The priest said to them: "In half an hour you may come down."
When two lovers stood behind the priest's hedge, the clergyman asked: "What are you doing here?" The pair replied: "That's none of your business!" The priest then said: "You will stay standing here as long as I wish." The priest bewitched the lovers to the ground and left them standing until the next morning.
This priest could also make stolen gold jewellery come back.
200351: A boy could make little mice and make them run around by blowing on their backsides. After the priest had been to see the boy, he could no longer make mice.
200353: In Koekelare lived a boy whose stepmother had said to his father: "You must have him work for someone, even if it is the devil!" The boy set out with his father through the woods of Wijnendale. In the distance the two saw a rider approaching. The man on the horse learned that they were looking for work for the boy and suggested that the boy come and work for him. Because the man offered very good pay, the father agreed. He was not allowed, however, to make the sign of the cross over his son before he left. Then the boy was taken to hell by the devil, where he had to be the doorkeeper. The stairs of hell were full of doctors, lawyers, prelates and other prominent figures. The only poor person the boy had to let into hell was his godmother. One day the devil had to go and fetch a framasson (freemason) in Brugge. When the boy had worked enough, the devil brought him back to the wood of Wijnendale. The boy did not live long after that.
200354: A woman who had quarrelled with her son and daughter-in-law had said: "I won't let that go unpunished." At night the woman got up to stick pins into a little doll. The son and daughter-in-law felt it as they lay in bed. The police searched the witch's house and took away the pins and the books of magic. Because the witch was already eighty years old, however, she was not punished.
200369: Whoever was ridden by the mare at night could no longer speak and felt as if a heavy, broad weight was lying on him.
200372: A farmer from Westouter went to the friars of Ieper because he could no longer make butter. Whenever the witch responsible for the evil came to the farm after that, the farmer always had great difficulty controlling himself; his hair stood on end and he wanted to kick the witch. But the farmer was not allowed to touch the witch.
200373: On a farm in Ledegem beautiful music was always heard in the cow shed. When people went to look, strangely enough there was nothing to be seen.
200379: A mother whose child was bewitched had been given something blessed by the priests to put under the child's mattress. Because of this the witch, who had previously pricked the child with pins, could no longer come near her victim.
200380: A little woman went to the fair with her little donkey on Christmas Day. At the corner of the wood the donkey always stopped and then turned back. Suddenly the woman saw a table with white gentlemen playing cards.
200397: Dreaming about a dead person was a sign that one had to pray for that dead person.
200416:
Children who suffered from 'the old man' had a large head and looked like an old man. A child who had 'de kanteirn' (a children's illness) turned completely blue. Such a child had to be held quickly upside down under the pump. The contact with the cold water would startle the child and make it vomit. Then it was saved. Such illnesses could be caused by witches.
When a woman had just given birth, the doctor advised her not to let old people near the child.
200425: Some people passed the churchyard of Eggewaartskapelle at night. There they saw a black cat and chased the animal away. At the churchyard of Wulveringem the same cat appeared again.
200437: Strange things happened on a farm in Veldegem. A vagrant is said to have once been locked up in the underground cellars there. Every time an animal was shut in the pen, that animal turned out to have disappeared the next morning.
200438: A rich woman had said on her deathbed: "Whoever dares to keep watch over me for three nights after my death will inherit all my money". A brave man from the neighbourhood decided to keep watch over the rich woman's corpse. The first night the man was bothered a little. The second night the devils crawled over him up against the wall. The third night the man was tortured to death by the devils. No one ever dared to claim the woman's money because people believed that the woman had associated with the devil.
200440: In Houtem lived an old man who tormented passers-by by making their horse stand still or die. The parish priest took his books away from him, so that he could no longer do magic.
200461: A man coming home from work always met a girl in the Klerken Smissestraat who walked a little way with him. "Are you lost?" the man asked the girl, but there was no answer. When the man reached the end of the street, the girl had vanished.
200463: A man who had been to the mission was covered in lice when he came home. People claimed the man had fallen victim to a witch. The man washed himself thoroughly and put on other clothes, after which he was rid of the lice.
200488: In a house in Kerkhove there was a little child that had 'de oude man' (the old man, a wasting illness). The sick child always lay in a cradle by the window. The people had often seen a strange cat sitting outside on the windowsill. An acquaintance had said: "If you see that cat again, come and fetch me so I can shoot it." But when the man wanted to shoot the cat, the animal had suddenly vanished. Immediately afterwards the child recovered.
200491: A man who had gone dancing at the Esenkruis on a Saturday evening walked home. On the way the man saw a pig blocking his path. A moment later the animal had vanished. Some other men who had gone dancing got hopelessly lost on their way home. The next day, after mass, the man told a friend that he had seen an enormous pig. The friend replied: "Yes, you played the accordion and danced at that cross. No wonder something happened to you!" The man decided never to dance at that place again.
200492: Two girls going to the fair met some Duitse schapers (German shepherds, wandering shepherds believed to have magic powers) on the way. The shepherds said good day, but the girls did not answer. Then one of the shepherds said: "They'll be back soon!" Further along the girls found they were covered in lice. There was nothing for it but to go back home. When the girls passed the shepherds again, one of them said: "We did say you would be back soon! But it's all right this once." A little later the lice had all gone. After that the girls always said good day when they met someone.
200516: In Sint-Andries lived a witch who could make the wheel fall off a passing cart.
200521: In the past the little souls that had done evil had to return after death. If someone had the courage to speak to the soul, it was released. Now the souls stay in purgatory to do penance.
200539: On a farm in Koolskamp, a little woman was seen every morning pulling leaves from the trees. In the mornings they could never make butter on that farm. They chased the little woman away and put something blessed by the gate. After that they had butter again.
