200545: On the road from Hooglede to Dottenijs a man met a woman one night. When he asked her where she was going, the woman answered: "That's none of your business," and she boxed the man's ear. The next moment the woman had vanished. She was one of the ghosts who lived in the castle.
200549:
A parish priest handed out the money of the rich farmers to the poor.
A man working in his potato field was visited by the priest, who said: "You don't need to work any more now. You should be at home now." The man replied: "And what about you, Father?" The man was then bewitched to the ground. He could only move again when the priest went to sleep.
One Sunday the priest said during his sermon: "At this moment someone is sitting in my cherry tree stealing my cherries." After mass people did indeed see a thief sitting in the tree, who was trying to bring a cherry to his mouth but could no longer move.
200563: A schoolboy stuck his finger into a little heap of sand and made a mouse come out of it. After the priest had been to see the boy, he could no longer make mice.
200567: A woman who owned books of magic had bewitched her own child by sticking it full of pins. In the end people came to take away the pins and the books of magic.
200570: In Izegem lived a woman who had sold her soul to the devil. The woman nearly went mad from it. When she stood at her ice-cream cart, she always cried out that she saw devils everywhere. No one else, however, could see them.
200573: On a farm in Watou the farmer was tormented by a witch. Whenever the farmer went to fetch turnips, the cart always tipped over, so that he had to return without turnips. Something always went wrong with the cows too. Even the friars could not help the poor farmer. In the end the farmer went to try his luck in America. Since then he has been back in Belgium only once.
200576: People who were ridden by the mare in their sleep were drenched in sweat and felt as if their throats were being squeezed shut.
200578: People who were ridden by the mare felt they would suffocate because a woman was pressing her knees into their chest.
200594: A farmer from Gullegem saw a dancing white figure in the air. A little later the maid of the curate of Kortrijk also saw the figure. It was assumed to be the ghost of the farmer, returning. After a chapel had been built, the ghost was not seen again.
200595: A mother whose child had fallen victim to a witch went to the priests. There they found that there were pins stuck in the child's body. The priests gave the mother something blessed to put under the child's mattress. Because of this the witch could no longer come near the child.
200619: A dead farmer appeared in his Sunday clothes and leaned over the stable door. The people still had to fulfil a vow.
200640: A farm in Torhout was haunted. A man who was mowing was suddenly found dead amid a heap of money. The man had found cursed money. If one had cursed money, the problem could be solved by having a few Masses said.
200645: A farmhand from Les Moères had to go to Houtem with a horse and cart. Because a sorcerer was standing by the road, the farmhand could not manage to turn the cart.
200649: A woman who drank a lot and lived in a wretched little house was always chased by devils on her way home. One day the woman jumped through the roof out of fear. She fell dead on a stone.
200667: A woman was weeding flax together with some other women. When the woman noticed that the others were laughing at her, she said: "If you don't keep quiet, I will make mice run across the field and crawl under your skirts." The woman carried out her threat.
200672: A man who did not want to go to the mission was told by the priests that something bad would happen to him if he did not go. The next morning the man lay dead in his bed. The horses that had to pull his coffin to the church could hardly move forward.
200693: On a farm on the Ruyterhoek the cows were untied. In the evening marbles rolled down the stairs. When people went to look, however, there was nothing to be seen. A lot of noise was heard in the attic. One night the farmhands had to watch over three sows. "If you hear anything, just call me", the farmer had said. There was a small hole in the ceiling. At a certain moment the farmhands saw a finger poke through that hole, but they did not dare to call. The farmer had the priest come to exorcise the cow shed. The clergyman said: "If I stay away longer than twenty minutes, you must come and have a look". After twenty minutes the farmer saw that the clergyman was drenched in sweat. After that the priest was delivered.
200719: In Ichtegem there was a child who did not grow because it was bewitched. When the child came into the church, it sighed loudly. In the end the child was taken to the friars of Steenbrugge to have prayers read over it. As soon as a friar came near, the child became very restless.
200722: Doodkaarsen (death candles, ghostly lights) were dead people who returned because they had hidden something somewhere or because they had not kept a promise.
200733: A farm where all the animals died was haunted. One farmer after another went bankrupt and had to leave the farm. Although the farm had already been exorcised ten times, there was no end to the misfortune. The priest advised the farmer to demolish all the buildings and build a new farm. Once that had been done, nothing strange happened any more.
200744: A widower whose wife had been dead for three weeks felt wind blowing in his face around midnight. When the man began to pray, the wind disappeared. The next day the man heard a sound that frightened him. That evening the widower put a candle beside his bed. At midnight the candle was blown out, although all windows and doors were shut. It seemed as if a hand was rubbing the man's face. The next day the man went to the chaplain, who at first believed none of the story but in the end promised to come in the evening. The man had to put a candle beside his bed and leave his bedroom door open. While the man pretended to sleep, the chaplain would keep watch. At midnight the chaplain began to pray. Since then nothing strange ever happened to the man again.
200754: A man and a woman were walking together along the Tunnedreef. The little child lagged a bit behind. A little later the child was found murdered in the ditch. Since then people saw a doodkeers (death candle, ghost light) at that spot every evening. The man probably had a child and had then married another woman, who murdered that child (?).
200770: A woman who was sleeping under a walnut tree in the afternoon was ridden by the mare and was completely stiff. The mare was something caused by sorceresses.
200783: To protect oneself against the mare, one had to wear a blessed Easter nail on one's chest. For horses, one had to put an Easter nail in the harness.
200789: A man coming home late in the evening from work suddenly saw a woman walking along arm in arm with him. The man was scared to death. When the man looked again a moment later, the apparition had vanished without a trace.
200803: A woman who was always tormented by a white cat gave the animal a hard kick one day. After that the woman was no longer bothered by the witch's cat.
200805: The Flying Dutchman had to sail about the sea on his boat forever. He had cursed all his crew, so that he alone remained. People who had seen the Flying Dutchman met with disaster.
200816: At night the dead came out of their graves in the churchyard and walked back and forth.
200837: By the hawthorn hedge near the mill between Slijpe and Mannekensvere, doodkaarsen (death candles, ghost lights) were sometimes seen. They were people who had to come back after their death.
200847: On a farm in Zillebeke they could not churn butter. The vet could not help, for the misfortune had been caused by a woman who had been seen sitting on the milking stool and had then run off.
200853: In Haringe lived a boy who was ridden by the kokkemare (the nightmare). In such a case one had to pray a few Our Fathers and say: "Kokkemare, will you hear me, will you go through dikes and valleys and through the roofs before you can reach our bed".
200871: Broom makers were sometimes jumped on by 'den beir' (the werewolf), which had itself carried a short way.
200905: After an old woman had laid her hand on a newborn child, the child began to cry. In the end the child even died.
200924: Two horse grooms were murdered by the farmer's wife during their first night on a farm. The third farmhand who entered service there did not go to sleep, but stayed sitting on the edge of his bed reading. Suddenly the farmhand saw a headless horse come in. At midnight the farmhand took the horse to the blacksmith to have it shod. When the farmhand got up the next morning, the horse had disappeared. The farmer discovered that his wife had horseshoes on her hands and feet.
200929: In Hoeke lived an old woman who owned books of magic. When that woman was angry with a farmer, she made all his calves die.
200957: The Jehovah's Witnesses worshipped a horseshoe. After their death they came back to haunt in the shape of a cow, a bull or another animal.
200993: Two brothers from Geeraardsbergen who had always got on well fell out, so that the two would not even enter the church by the same door. One day one of the brothers was walking through the woods and said three times: "If I knew how, I would sell my soul to the devil!" A little further on the young man saw a man dressed in black leaning against a tree. The young man said: "What are you doing here in the middle of the night on my land? Speak or I'll stab you with a knife!" The black figure answered: "Don't touch me, or I'll break your neck!" The young man was so frightened by that answer that he fainted. When he came to, he sold his soul to the devil for eight years. When the eight years were over, the young man asked the devil whether he might do one more thing. The devil agreed, and the young man bewitched his brother's farm; two big black dogs were always there. When the devil came to claim the young man's soul, the young man threw his lamp into the pond. After all, he only had to go with the devil once the wick had burnt down completely. In this way the young man had managed to outwit the devil after all. To celebrate his victory the young man threw a big party with much dancing and drinking. After a few hours a tall gentleman came in and crossed the ballroom three times. "Flee, flee," the gentleman cried, "for tonight the castle will sink!" No sooner had he spoken than the castle sank into the ground. Everyone had been able to flee except the young man, who sank into the ground with the castle.
200999:
A girl who was raised by her godmother had to pray twenty Our Fathers before going to sleep. She had to dedicate the first prayer to Saint Joseph the Dreamer to have good dreams. The second prayer was dedicated to the girl's guardian angel, the third to her scapular, the fourth to Our Lady of Rest, and so on. One of the prayers was also meant to keep the mare away. The mare was a spirit that wandered about at night. People who were ridden by the mare felt as if something was lying on them and could no longer breathe. Whoever wanted to protect themselves against the mare had to pray twenty Our Fathers or say this one prayer:
"Ware the mare, I beseech the mare that she may pass over us here tonight, over all garden stakes and scandals, before she reaches our house".
201009: Some women could bewitch children by putting pins in their cradles. Such children had to be prayed over by the dean.
201047: A twenty-eight-year-old man coming home around midnight saw a herd of goats walking ahead of him. The man ran home as fast as he could. Because it was often haunted at that spot, a little chapel was hung on a tree there.
201053: A man walking in the churchyard kicked a skull and sang: "If there is still life in you, then you are invited to my table at midnight." "I am here, I am your grandfather."
201058: In the Maurice Dewulfstraat a gentleman and a lady came haunting at midnight. Arm in arm they floated back and forth through the street. When they reached the end of the street, they suddenly vanished.
201072:
A farmhand who had been out late on a Sunday evening saw, on coming home, the farmer's wife in her underwear gathering pears together with her children. When the farmer's wife asked the next day what time the farmhand had come home, he answered: "You know that well enough, because you were still gathering pears then." But the farmer's wife denied it.
A week later the farmhand had to go and fetch help because a calf was about to be born. When the farmhand opened the door, he saw a woman sitting with her legs over the gate. It was the farmer's wife.
201083: A man said he had been ridden all night by the kokkemare (the nightmare). He had heard from someone that he should hang a darning needle above his bed. The mare would then have to crawl through the eye of the needle to reach her victim. This mare, however, had still managed to accomplish that task.
201092: A farmer bringing in his harvest saw a witch standing by the road. Although there was no wind, the farmer's cart suddenly tipped over.
201118: A farmer who went to his cattle one evening got lost and claimed he had ended up in a world of magic.
201121: Some people walking home on a Sunday evening had to go through a lane where white cats were said to haunt. When the people were in that lane, someone said mockingly: "Well, where are those white cats now?" The next moment the lane was full of white cats, which followed the people all the way to their house. A farmhand wanted to shoot at the cats with a gun, but he was forbidden to. That farmhand fell ill from fear.
201162: A man going to the Kruiskassei was accompanied by a white cat that came out of the woods. At a certain moment the cat suddenly vanished. It was a sorceress.
201167: A witch lived in Kerkhove. One day a man was talking in a café when the landlord suddenly said: "X, there's someone at the door!" The man wanted to jump aside quickly when he saw the witch standing there, but it was as if he was nailed to the ground. Then the witch slapped her buttocks and said: "X, you can't get me, can you!"
201181: In a shop in Wevelgem, a woman from the street came in several times asking for someone's address. Although the shopkeeper had given the same answer each time, the woman kept coming. Eventually the shopkeeper began to fear that the woman had bewitched her child. After the shopkeeper had hung a Saint Anthony above the door, the woman no longer came by.
201198: One day a statue of Mary was found in the Onzeheertjesbos. It was taken to the church, but the next day it was lying back in the mud in the wood. When the same thing happened once more, people decided it was a sign and built a little chapel on that spot in the wood.
201206: In Tiegem lived a carpenter whose mother was said to be a witch. One day the carpenter had to build a stable roof somewhere. Strangely, the man bent every nail he hammered. When he hung his coat on a nail in the wall, the nail suddenly vanished, so that the coat fell into the pig trough. The longer the carpenter worked, the more crooked the nails became. The man went home furious and gave his mother, who was reading a book, a sound thrashing. After that he could carry on working without any trouble.
201233: A man went home past a pond in which a woman had once drowned. When the man passed there, a pig jumped between his legs. At that the man ran off as fast as he could.
201242: No one dared enter the wood anymore because a corpse had been seen there at night. It was a returned dead person.
201243:
A sorcerer could make it thunder and lighten inside his house while outside there was no sign of a storm. He could also send lice. Once a man shook the chair the sorcerer had been sitting on. Afterwards that man had lice himself.
The priest took away the sorcerer's books.
201249: A man on his way to visit his family got lost. After a while he met an old woman in a hooded cloak and asked her the way. "It's that way," said the old woman. A few minutes later the man knew where he was again.
201253: People who were ridden by the mare could hardly breathe. The mare could only be driven away by calling the victim by name.
201276: A man who met a sorceress between the Zuidhoek and the Beek said: "Good evening". The apparition answered: "The days are for you and the nights for us". The woman wore black silk clothing and had a hat on her head. A man coming home around half past twelve at night from visiting his sweetheart saw, to his great fright, the same woman floating across the road.
201279: Just above the dunes a little light could be seen, which said: "The deeper, the more". It was the eternal wheelbarrow pusher, who as punishment had to push his barrow forever.
201284: A man always put his clogs upside down next to his bed to prevent being ridden by the mare.
201296: A child whose head had been stroked by a witch usually died.
201312: In a house in Egem one morning the wheel of the butter churn was found turning, hanging on the attic stairs. No one knew how the wheel had got there, because it was so big that it could not fit through any door.
201317: Between the 'Kwakkel' and the Molenhoek, or between the 'Kwakkel' and Ter Hand, one could often see a tall white lady walking. A man who had seen the lady said: "Good evening". When the woman did not answer, the man said: "You're a proud one!" After that the man was struck to the ground.
201333: Small lights floated in the air. They were dead people who returned because they had not fulfilled a promise.
201338: A gravedigger had dug up a skull in the churchyard of Grijsloke. The man could not bury the skull again; it kept coming back up and moving back and forth. Terrified, the gravedigger went to the priest, who came to sprinkle the spot with holy water. The skull, however, just went on dancing. After a while the skull suddenly disappeared after all.
201341: Some girls coming back from sewing school one evening were followed by a cat. When she got home, one of the girls told about the cat, whereupon her mother said: "That was a sorceress! You must never accept anything that someone offers you along the road!"
201346: At a party where there was dancing, some people had summoned the devil. The next moment three gentlemen came in. Because the people had become frightened, they sent for the priest, who said to the gentlemen: "You must leave this place!" The gentlemen answered: "Yes, but we were summoned," to which the priest replied: "Yes, but I was asked to come here, and that is much stronger than being summoned." The priest had to pray until he was drenched in sweat, but in the end the gentlemen did leave.
201349: A man from Houthulst went with the horse and cart to visit his girlfriend. The woman he visited was suspected of being a sorceress. At midnight the man pretended to have fallen asleep. So he saw the woman take a little box from a cupboard by the chimney and rub herself with something that looked like shoe polish. Then the woman said: "Over everything and above everything" and she was gone. Then the man also rubbed himself with the stuff and said: "Over everything and through everything". At that the man was thrown against everything. Covered in blood, he arrived at the crossroads where the sorceresses gathered.
201365: A mother was often visited by two old women, to whom she sometimes gave something. One day the mother's little son was bewitched. The mother managed to persuade her unbelieving husband to take her and the child to the friars. The woman received medals from the clergymen. In the end the son was cured.
201371: On a farm there was a small child with something strange going on. Every time the child was left alone in its cradle for a moment, its clothes were torn. One day the farmer, cursing, went to seek advice from the friars of Steenbrugge. The clergymen said to the man: "You curse far too much on your farm. And send that suspicious woman away too!" When the farmer had done so, nothing strange happened on the farm any more.
201376: A witch was reading in her book of magic to do harm to her pregnant friend. But because the witch read too far, all the harm befell herself and not her friend. After that the witch could no longer read in that book.
201397: Whoever was ridden by the mare felt unwell. Victims of the mare had to pray a lot.
201398: Before the First World War, a bewitched woman lived in Poperinge. Willing people often went to keep watch at the sick woman's bedside. Around ten, eleven or twelve o'clock at night the woman would suddenly fly out of her bed and leap onto the cupboard, something no normal person could do. Because everything in the house began to spin around, the person keeping watch fled outside and fetched the chaplain. Although that chaplain was known for his power to dispel witchcraft, he could not even get into the house. Then the friars of Ieper were sent for. But when the friars reached the house, the woman had already died.
201423: In Oedelem there lived people whom a witch had covered in lice or fleas.
201428:
When the corpse of a framasson (freemason) had been laid in a coffin, it could already be gone the next day. After all, after their death framassons were fetched by the devil.
Framassons were prominent people who associated with the devil in exchange for a lot of money. They did not believe in God and did not go to church.
201431: In Geluwe there once lived a German shepherd. When the shepherd passed a house with his sheep, the little woman who lived there said: "You must leave that grass for my sheep!" The shepherd replied: "Yes, that's fine, but then you must guard the grass so my sheep don't get at it." When the shepherd passed by again that evening, the little woman was still standing in the same place. The German shepherd said to her: "Did they eat any of it? You may go now." He had bewitched the woman to the ground.
201437: A mother saw a figure with a chain hanging above her child. The child was being ridden by the kokkemare (the nightmare).
201455: Some witches sitting in the woods cut off a branch and walked around a cauldron, beating on it and calling: "Little pot, boil! Little pot, boil!" A moment later the contents of the cauldron were boiling, although there was no fire anywhere to be seen.
201457: A widower from Menen saw a ball go down the stairs every evening. It was the ghost of his dead wife, who came to show where the money was hidden. The parish priest claimed that the ghost was hanging by a thread in purgatory.
201464: At the black lime trees next to the castle of Diesveld many people were said to have been hanged in the old days. Later, at night, many doodkaarsen (death candles, ghostly lights) could be seen at those limes, jumping from one tree to the other. A friar who walked past that place one night saw lots of white cats that leapt at him and ran between his legs.
201466: A man walking to Meulebeke at night saw a pack of cats at twelve o'clock. There were so many cats that the man could hardly move on. When the man had kicked at the animals, they suddenly vanished.
201471: People who were ridden by the mare could no longer breathe and felt as if a heavy weight had fallen on them.
201506: A man who had suffered a lot during the night believed he had been ridden by the mare. Trees that had grown crooked had also been ridden by the mare. Whoever wanted to protect himself against the mare had to put his clogs upside down next to the bed.
201526: A woman came to visit a little boy who was three months old. At that moment the child began to cry. The little boy cried until he died. He had been bewitched by the visitor.
201545: A man and a farmer went to the meadow with a brand-new rope, which they laid across the brook. At a certain moment the farmer said: "X is there!" The witch had heard it and replied: "I'll get you. I wish you'd fall into the brook!" Strangely, the brand-new rope broke, so that the man and the farmer did indeed fall into the brook.
201552: A woman going to her churching after childbirth saw a pair of scissors and some pins lying on the way. But the woman was not allowed to pick up those objects, because they were bewitched.
201577: A man going to visit his girlfriend met a man and a woman on the way, who said: "Come with us." The man seemed forced by a strange power and went with the two. When the man and the woman said at the Blauwhuis: "Now go back!", the man turned back. The next day the man was ill. He had a fever. Perhaps the man had already been ill before his meeting with that strange man and woman.
201584: Some men were manuring the field while a bit further on three hunters were hunting. A little later a bird landed some fifty metres from the hunters. Each hunter fired two shots, but the bird flew off unharmed. A little later the same thing happened again, and this time too the bird was not hit. When the bird then landed right next to the hunters, they no longer wanted to shoot. The farmer said to the hunters: "Even if you shoot at that bird a thousand times, it will never die."
201603: During the month of May the witches gathered to dance in a circle. Where the witches had danced, the grass had a different colour. The witches themselves were invisible.
201632: In the wheat field there was always a hare that nobody could shoot. When a little blessed salt had been put in the gun, the hare could be hit.
201650: Some children were doing their homework. Suddenly the clock made a sighing sound. The mother superior asked whether anyone dared to stop the clock. One of the girls did. At that moment it seemed as if a block of a hundred kilos fell down.
201665: Anyone driving a cart through the castle lane at night often saw screaming cats sitting in the trees. At one point the cart was even thrown onto the embankment.
201667: A pig dealer coming back from Lapscheure saw a cat walking in the street. When the man tried to coax the animal, six cats suddenly appeared, so that the man could not take another step.
201672: A mother was visited by an old woman. As soon as the old woman had left the house, the mother's little daughter began to cry. The child cried day and night for nine days. After the mother had put something blessed under the door, the witch could no longer come in. "I'd like to see the child!" she called, but in vain.
201727: People who were ridden by the mare in their beds were terribly frightened.
201728: On a farm coffee was made every morning for the neighbour woman. Because, strangely enough, a cow lay dead every morning, the people went to a friar, who said: "You must not give the neighbour so much coffee anymore". When the people stopped doing so, indeed no more cows died.
201775: A woman from Elverdinge who lived in Hooglede always went to buy meat from a butcher's wife in the neighbourhood. She always paid the money to the farmer's wife's daughter, to whom she then gave her hand. One day the butcher's wife bought a fine fat cow from that woman, which she would come to collect two weeks later. When the butcher's wife went to fetch the cow, the animal was as thin as a rake.
201806: In Zandvoorde lived a woman whose husband had died. Every evening at about the same time the dead man came knocking on the door.
201808: In Kaster a ghost in the shape of a dog always roamed at night. That ghost was called 'Klinkaard'. Because the dog rattled its chains all the time, it could be heard coming from afar. People no longer dared to go outside at night for fear of seeing that dog. A man claimed that one night he had seen the dog walking with a child's dummy in its mouth. The dog could make itself very small so that it could get in anywhere. When it attacked someone, it made itself very large.
201813: A German shepherd who peddled rat poison called on the farmer's wife at a castle farm. The woman refused to buy anything and said: "We have no rats; we have a good dog." The next day that farm was swarming with rats. The dog could not catch even one of them. The shepherd had sent the rats there from another farm where they had bought poison.
201837: On a farm they could not make butter. Opposite the farm lived a woman with a bad reputation. When the farmer's four sons saw the woman in the field, they blocked off the four corners of the field and drove the witch to the middle. There the boys saw a black cat lying with its paws in the air. The abbot was sent for to read prayers over the field. The clergyman stood at the far end of the field and began to pray until he was drenched in sweat. After that the black cat had disappeared. The butter plunger was found in the field together with some lumps of butter. From that day on they could make butter on that farm again. The abbot forbade the witch ever to go to that farm again.
201860:
A weaver claimed that he consorted with the devil and had already been to hell. Because the man had special powers, he could weave exceptionally well.
The man lived in a semi-detached house. When he quarrelled with his neighbour, the weaver said: "I'm going to set your house on fire!" The words had barely left his mouth when the house was already ablaze. The neighbour's house burned down completely, but the weaver's remained standing, even though the two were joined!
In those days many children were murdered in the village. On the door of a barn it was written how many more children had to die. The heads of the murdered children were always placed on a sawn-off tree, and there was a hole in the children's scapulars. People believed that the weaver was responsible for the murders of the children and that he could make himself invisible.
201872: No one dared to go to the moated castle of Loppem any more because it was haunted. The dead who had neglected a vow returned there.
201875: Some fishermen by the canal heard a horse stamping to break loose. When the fishermen went to look, however, there was nothing to be seen.
201895: One afternoon a man went for a walk in the snow. In a clover field the man saw hare tracks and decided to return in the evening. That evening a bitter north-easterly wind was blowing. Around eleven o'clock the man saw the hare for the first time. The man waited another half hour for the animal to come close enough to shoot. A little later there were two hares playing in the snow. At that moment the man knew that the hare was in reality a witch. When he got home, the man saw the two hares playing in his little yard.
201902: One evening a farmer saw the ghost of his dead father arriving on horseback.
201931: A woman lived in a house where someone had died who had promised to go on a pilgrimage to Oostakker but had never kept that promise. The woman always heard banging on the front door and the back door and in the attic. After a while the ghostly noises disappeared.
201933: On a haunted farm the pigs and cows flew back and forth. The haunting was caused by the maid, who came from Izegem. That maid consorted with the devil. After the maid had been sent to America, no more strange things happened on the farm.
201935: To protect yourself against the mare, you had to scatter salt beside your bed or set your slippers upside down beside the bed.
201937: A woman went to a farm to ask for buttermilk. When the people said they had no buttermilk left, the woman said: "Go ahead and churn." After that those people could no longer churn butter, so they had to send for the priest. The clergyman then hung a medal somewhere, which solved the problem. The priest often had to act against the evil that witch had done.
201943: People who were thrown out of their beds at night and ran off had been ridden by the mare.
201953: During the war a friar came to the farmers to get food. When the friar had gone, the animals on the farm became restless. A friar came to exorcise the farm, after which the animals behaved normally again. After that, however, horse carts were heard driving in the attic. The friar had to ask the bishop for permission before he could lend his help. The bishop said to the friar: "You may, but you must bear the consequences yourself". After his intervention at the farm that friar went mad.
201976: All the returning dead gathered at the Stereik in Anzegem. All kinds of lights, cats, dogs, posts and white planks were seen there. At midnight the dead went to the places where they had to haunt.
201987: Little lights were often seen burning in a churchyard. Such lights were also often seen in foggy weather. People said they were the souls of the returning dead.
201999: At the end of the nineteenth century a woman lived in Blankenberge whom everyone feared, because people believed she was a witch. She lived alone and sold herbs she had gathered. She owned herb books and could make statues move from their place and make objects disappear. One day a child fell ill after being touched by that woman. If you were touched by a witch, you always had to strike higher to break her power. When fishermen on their way to sea met the witch, they turned back saying: "I've forgotten something." They believed that meeting the witch would bring bad luck. A clergyman collected the witch's books and burned them.
202010: When a witch's daughter had died, the witch said to the man who was to carry the coffin: "Will it be all right with two horses?" A little later the horses began to foam at the mouth and drove off the dike. Everyone who came past there on a bicycle rode down the dike.
202018: Doodkaarsen (death candles, ghostly lights) appeared in places where money was buried.
202019: A woman went to keep watch at night over a sick man. When the woman wanted to drink coffee that night, she went to the cellar. At that moment all the windows and doors flew open. The woman hurried to close the windows and doors, but she saw no one. A little later everything flew open again. Meanwhile the sick man lay dying in his bed. The next morning he died in the most terrible pain. After that the haunting came to an end.
202031: Anyone who wanted to protect himself against the mare had to place his clogs under the bed heels first. People who were ridden by the mare felt as if they were lying under a woodpile. Those people then woke up sweating.
202034: One night two men with lanterns were seen coming along the beach from Nieuwpoort-Bad. One man walked by the water, the other by the dunes. The lanterns, which were as big as a door, came closer together, climbed onto each other's backs and finally disappeared into the sea.
202046:
A man who was ridden by the mare at night was completely out of breath, so that he could not call his mother for help. When the man was freed from this torment, he saw a small black dog jump off his bed. He went after the dog and shouted: "I'm going to beat you to death! I'm going to beat you to death!" But the dog leapt into the attic and disappeared a moment later.
The mare was a discontented lover who had been rejected.
202055: A man was still out late in the evening when a terrible thunderstorm began. When he passed a café, the landlady offered him shelter. The man stayed the night in the café. The bed he slept in moved up and down all night, right up to the ceiling. Strangely enough, the man felt no pain anywhere.
202067: A woman was visited by a peddler selling rat poison. Because the woman refused to buy anything, the peddler made sure her house was full of rats the next day.
202082: Two friends on their way to Gistel saw a coffin standing on a culvert. The front of the coffin was facing towards Westkerke. When the men came back later that day, the coffin was still there, but this time with its front facing Gistel.
202088: The mare was a woman who sat on people's hearts and prevented them from screaming. The mare then gently stroked the face, arms and hands of her victim.
202093: Strange things happened on a farm in Esen. A woman who stayed up one night keeping watch in the farmhouse told the maid the next morning that she had heard a watch ticking all night. She had also heard sounds as if someone was cooking and frying, but in the morning there was nothing to be seen. The door of the horse stable always flew open by itself. Butter could not be churned on the farm. The friars came to exorcise the farm several times and sweated terribly while doing so. In the end the farm had to be demolished.
202132: A woman who skinned rabbits carried a black cat in her apron. As the woman neared her house, the cat grew heavier and heavier. When she got home the woman put the animal under a barrel and laid a wedding ring on it. The next morning a farmer's daughter sat naked under the barrel.
202151: In a gully in the dunes someone always walked around calling: "Where must I put that? Where must I put that?" When a passer-by answered: "Put it back where you got it", the dead man was released.
202171: In Knesselare two witches from Gent used to go around, telling the farmers: "Every bit you plough will be unploughed again tomorrow." And so it was.
202179: On a farm plagued by rats, the farmer went to the friars for advice. The friars told him that on his way back he would meet a big rat. And so it happened. When the farmer got home, there was not a single rat left on his farm.
202190: A witch lived in Snaaskerke. Some people set out at night to find out what the witch got up to. They got lost and only found their way home at daybreak.
202194: People walking past the Biesteert late in the evening saw a woman there, dressed entirely in black. Passers-by were accompanied by this woman as far as the first houses of Aalbeke. A little light was also often seen at that spot.
202195: In Maldegem there was a baby of two or three months old that cried all the time. Because the child was full of pins, people claimed it was bewitched. A woman often came peddling paraffin at the farm. Someone advised the child's mother to go to the friars of Brugge. The clergymen predicted that a woman with paraffin would come and take the child in her arms. That woman would come back once more, but then the mother must say the child was asleep. After the mother did so, the peddler never came by again. The baby was cured.
202205:
A woman who was often ridden by the mare felt as if something was being thrown on top of her. Victims of the mare tried to call out, but no sound came.
Some claimed that the mare was a standstill of the blood.
202217: Some people were sitting with a deceased woman of their family when suddenly a little woman came in to make a sign of the cross over the dead woman. When the little woman had gone, the dead woman was covered in lice. The family quickly fetched the priest, who said: "I must do something here that goes against my heart, but I will do it anyway. I would rather die than..." After the priest had said his prayers, all the lice were gone. The priest walked back to the church and dropped dead on the way.
202223: A chaplain had to go to Nieuwpoort Bad for a court case. People believed the clergyman would be harassed on the way back by the liberal gamekeeper and offered to go with the chaplain. But he replied: "No, that's not necessary." The gamekeeper spent the whole time floundering in a thorn hedge. For in the old days clergymen had magic powers.
202225: On a farm there was a baby that lay crying all the time. Because the child's health grew worse day by day, a friar was called. When the friar came to pray over the child, sweat dripped from his face. A niece of the family had given the child the evil hand.
202248: People who were ridden by the mare in their sleep could hardly breathe.
202258: A witch could not leave the church if the priest had left his missal open on the altar.
202262: Anyone ridden by the mare felt as if something was lying on him and could no longer speak or move. Victims of the mare were completely rigid. Anyone who wanted to protect himself against the mare had to set his shoes upside down beside his bed.
202302: A woman drove a dog cart to the market in Veurne, where she was going to sell fish. When the woman came past a witch's house, her little cart fell over. The people working nearby came straight to the poor woman and said: "That is the witch's doing!"
202327: It was often haunted at the Posthoornhoek. One night, three times over, people heard a racket there. In the morning the ceiling had collapsed.
202333: The eternal hunter never found rest because he was cursed. He kept calling: "jouw!"
202346: A woman went to the priest because her nine-month-old son would no longer breastfeed. The clergyman asked the mother whether anyone had patted her on the shoulder. The mother then remembered that a woman had indeed patted her on the shoulder and said: "What a lovely baby!" The priest prayed over the woman and the child.
202348: A girl worked as a maid for a farmer's wife in France. One day two women from Les Moères came to the farm, one of whom 'had the name' (was reputed to be a witch). Because the women wanted to buy a cow, the farmer's wife went with them to the cowshed. She explained that only one cow was for sale. The witch, however, wanted another cow, which was in calf, and slapped the animal on its rump. After that cow gave birth to her two calves, she dried up completely. The farmer's wife then went to the friars of Saint-Jex, who gave her medals. The farmer was not allowed to know anything about it.
202355: In Meulebeke two farmers lived next to each other. The mother of one of them was suspected of being a witch. A woman who had visited the witch was covered in fleas the next day. A woman walking past a beech hedge by moonlight on a windless night was startled when the hedge suddenly began swaying so hard that it touched the ground. The woman saw the witch standing in the middle of the hedge. One day the two farmers had fought, and the witch's son had lost. That night the trees in the other farmer's garden began swaying so violently that they fell over. The witch was seen standing in the middle of the garden. In the morning all the farmer's animals lay dead. In the end the farmer had to move away out of poverty.
202373: In a house in Houtave there was a plague of rats in the attic. After the priest had read prayers over the house, all the rats were gone.
202394: Women with special powers could bewitch children by looking at them or touching them.
202399: A witch lived in a café. During catechism class the priest had warned the witch's daughter. One day the clergyman asked the witch's husband whether he could do nothing. "When she has her fits, nobody can do anything about it," the man said. One night, for example, the witch had set a whole row of empty bottles along the road. Another time she had made four people from the village ill. They were only cured of the heart complaint after going on pilgrimage to Sint-Elooi-Winkel.
202407: Some people set off for work on a summer's day. On the way they met a woman who greeted them. One of the men in the group then had a sneezing fit that lasted the whole day. It was the man who had returned the woman's greeting.
202418: Anyone who tried to drive past a barn in Ardooie before sunrise could not get through. The barn was haunted.
202449: A woman felt suffocated when she lay in bed at night. When she threw off the blankets, she could just feel the mare's hair, but she could not grab hold of the mare.
202463: In Sint-Joris-ten-Distel a drunkard was walking around one evening when he heard a voice calling: "Where must I do that, where must I put that?" The next day the drunkard told everything to the priest, who said: "When you go home on Sunday evening, you must say: 'Put it where you found it'." When the drunkard had done so, the ghost was released. It was the ghost of a man who had moved the boundary post of his field to have more land.
202473: In Dranouter there was a shop where they had a child that cried all the time and ate nothing but raw cabbage and beetroot. The child's troubles were caused by a certain woman who came into that shop.
202499: A woman who had to go to the pharmacy for her sick husband got lost. She had left in the morning and only got home at night. After all, anyone who was bewitched always had to strike harder than the witch, and this woman had not done so...
202520: A peddler who had been struck by the evil hand was cured after the White Fathers of Oostende prayed over her.
202534: A girl who stayed at the presbytery for three months to clean and help with a move always heard noises at night. The parish priest checked the books to see whether all the masses for the dead had been said. The priest admitted that the noises might have something to do with the masses that had not yet been said.
202544:
In Zillebeke two vagabonds had lost their way. They went to the parish priest and made him believe he had to come with them to administer the Last Sacraments to a dying woman. "I'm an old man already," the priest replied, "you'll have to come with me." The priest took the two fellows home. When they were almost home, the men said: "We've got home now, you can go back." The priest bewitched the two lads to the ground.
The next day they were still standing there. "Make sure that doesn't happen again!" said the priest, and he let the lads go.
202570: If a witch had been near a child's cradle, the child began to cry. When the priest had prayed over the child, it fell quiet again.
202573: On a farm where they could no longer churn butter, they sought the friars' advice. A friar came and asked: "Do you sell buttermilk? Does a woman come here for milk?" The people were amazed that the friar knew all this. The clergyman went on: "That woman won't come anymore." Indeed, the woman no longer came for buttermilk and the people could churn butter again.
202574:
Strange things happened on a farm. At night the baby lying in its cradle was pushed by a strange force. People heard the slurry pump working and the cows pulling at their chains. When they went to look, strangely enough there was nothing to be seen. As soon as they left the cowshed, they heard the sounds again. Two priests were sent for to come to the farm. One of the clergymen was never able to say mass again afterwards. The other always had to be helped during the consecration.
The evil was finally rooted out by reading the Gospel of Saint John after mass, along with 'Holy Michael the Archangel, defend us in battle'.
202587: A mother from Steenkiste went with her two-month-old child to visit acquaintances. On the way she met a witch, who said: "Oh, what a lovely baby that is!" The witch took hold of the baby and played with it for a moment. Shortly afterwards the baby turned completely black. In the end it died. When the witch died, her body was carried off by devils. During her life the witch had always seen fireballs under the eaves of her house.
202601: A man who was ridden by the mare in his sleep felt as if a heavy weight was pressing on him. The man tried to call out, but he could not make a sound.
202605: The sexton was ridden by the moon. When the moon was full and shone into his room, the sexton did not go to sleep.
202609: It used to be very haunted at the castle of Anzegem. No one dared to enter that wood any more because every night cats, dogs and even pigs ran back and forth there. After a little chapel had been built there, no more animals appeared in the wood. Shortly after the chapel was put there, a man who had killed his wife hanged himself there. That man had been given a prison sentence of five years. People believed that it might well have been that man who had caused all that evil.
202615: Near a house and a castle in Loppem it was haunted. People often saw a procession passing by there.
202632: During the sermon the priest said that people must no longer sow weeds. Otherwise he would leave his missal open, so that the culprits could not leave the church.
202643: In Loppem lived a witch who could cure the Sint-Katrienewiel (Saint Catherine's wheel, a neck ailment) by pressing a blessed gold ring into the sick person's neck to leave a mark.
202652: A woman came to visit a house that was full of flies and said to the lady of the house: "Why make a problem of that? Just put the flies a bit further off on that thorn hedge." The woman of course could not do that. But when the visitor had left, not a single fly was to be seen in the house.
202659: Witches were old women who went to work in the fields. These women had a glib tongue and could make people believe anything.
202660: The train always derailed by the house of an old woman in Rexpoe (Herzele?). People believed the old woman was responsible.
202682: At the home of a farmer's wife who could do witchcraft, people were stopped at the gate by a ghostly fire. When they had made the sign of the cross, the fire was gone.
202694: On a haunted farm all kinds of noises were heard at night. When the people got up, however, there was nothing to be seen.
202709: On a farm where many children died, there were frequent visits from a woman who lived in the café 'de Sparappel' in Ardooie. That woman had a bad name. One day the farmer and his wife went to the friars of Tielt, who gave them something to put above the door. After that the woman never came to the farm again.
202715: A woman was often ridden by the mare. When that happened, she saw a creature crawl up past her feet, and a moment later it was on her neck pulling at her hair. The woman wanted to call her husband, but it seemed as if her throat was being squeezed shut. The woman slept on a pillow that refugees had once left behind. After the woman had cut the pillow open and thrown the feathers away, she was no longer ridden by the mare.
202724: While the parish priest was busy with his sermon, some thieves were stealing apples in his orchard. "I'll just carry on calmly," thought the priest, "those apples won't run away." When the priest went to his orchard after mass, the thief was stuck to the tree. "What are you doing here?" asked the priest. "Clear off and make sure it doesn't happen again!"
202730: Old women could torment children by sticking pins into a little wax doll. Such children had to be prayed over by the priests. People also had to put kitchen salt or a wedding ring on the threshold so that the sorceress could no longer come in.
202748: A woman whose child was ill sent for the doctor. Because the doctor could not help, they consulted the priest, but he did not know what to do either. When the child's mother went to the friars of Tielt, she was told: "Don't be afraid, your child will be cured. Tomorrow a woman will come asking for alms, and she will also ask to see your baby." The next day a neighbour did indeed come asking for alms. But the mother did not show her the baby.
202753: In a café where a witch lived, a fight broke out and the police had to be called. As soon as the policemen's horses reached the café, they bolted. The policemen had to stay seated on the horses.
202769: In Torhout there was always a hare that nobody could shoot. One day the friars of Steenbrugge shot at the animal with a blessed wedding ring. Afterwards a woman from the village had a ring in her head.
202797:
't Watergat was haunted. A goat roamed about there that was always screaming.
Later it was discovered that a local innkeeper made the noises to lure in lots of customers.
202807: Some people eating by the roadside saw a flea jump. "Look, a flea!" said one of them. A witch then said: "You will come across more of them!" Three days later the people could no longer work because there were so many fleas.
202816: A man was driving to Brugge at night with horse and cart. When the man wanted to harness his horses to the cart, there were some cats sitting in the cart. The man lashed at the animals with his whip. The next morning a woman from the village had a swollen face and swollen eyes. One day that witch had made a man's cart collapse.
202820: In the old days there were hemelgeiten (sky goats) in the wood. They were large, cruel animals that lived in the trees.
202861: A child who had convulsions was taken to the friars to have prayers read over it. Two days later the child died, and all the other children died too. For some time a black cat had been seen walking around the house. The father threw boiling water over the animal. The next day a woman passed by whose face was completely burnt. She had turned herself into a black cat.
202878: When the priest left the missal open on Sunday after the last gospel, eight witches could not leave the church.
202949: A man who slaughtered pigs destined for consumption in England employed a workman. The workman often worked until midnight and then walked home. One night the workman saw a table by the church, where many people in fine clothes sat at a laid table. The people called to the workman: "Come and have a glass of wine too!" The man accepted a glass and said: "To your health". The next moment the whole scene had vanished. Because the man never wanted to experience such a thing again, he never worked past midnight after that.
202955: Every night a farmer's wife saw a tall woman with long black hair come in. That woman laid her hand on the farmer's wife's throat, so that she felt suffocated and could not make a sound. One night the farmer's wife told her husband what was going on. But the man did not see the black woman.
202968: A man claimed that a woman came to bewitch all the animals on his farm. Once, when people looked into a bucket of water, they could see that witch's face.
202982: Because the altar boys believed a witch was coming to mass, they had stuck Easter nails under all the chairs. After mass two women could not leave the church.
202986: A man and a woman were followed by a witch who could cast spells. Suddenly the witch struck the man on his backside. From then on the man could never walk again. He should have struck back.
202987: Some people walking along a row of willows saw singing black cats sitting in one of the trees. When the people passed, the cats fell silent, but afterwards they began to rant and curse. The cats had women's voices.
203022: A man who was in a wood between midnight and one o'clock suddenly saw the spruce branches lashing against the ground.
203029: An elderly woman made passers-by lose their way. People then had to walk around for two or three hours before they found the way again.
203035: In Otegem there lived a man who always walked around at night with a bearskin on his back. Because the man's wife and children did not know what to do, they asked someone for advice. They were to give the werewolf a letter stamped in France, saying that he had to go to an uncle's funeral. When the werewolf had been on his way for quite a while, they heated the oven and threw the skin into the fire. The next moment, however, the man was already standing by the oven and jumped into the fire to save his skin.
203052: When children had been touched by a witch, their little heads stood crooked.
203075: A woman went with the dog cart to the friars to have a small child prayed over. When the cart drove past a witch's house, the dogs broke the straps, so the woman did not get to the friars.
203077: People who took an afternoon nap were sometimes ridden by the mare. Because of the pressure of the stomach on the heart, they then had a strange feeling. People believed that a sorceress came and lay on top of them.
203107: In Bulskamp lived a woman who could make mice by sticking a straw into a lump of clay. After the priest had visited the witch, she could no longer make mice.
203112: A man peddling rat poison in Dranouter came to a woman who did not want to buy anything. "We never have rats here, so we don't need poison either!" the woman had said. "If you don't want to buy anything, that's your own business," the peddler had replied. Eight or ten days later the woman's farm was completely full of rats. That was witchcraft.
203144: A pregnant woman always saw a black cat near her. Such cats were often sorceresses. The woman had a difficult delivery.
203158: On a farm where the children fell ill and all the animals died, a clergyman was called. He prayed over the stables and the cows and said that the first woman to come by the next morning must be chased away with a stick. Although the first visitor was the neighbour, they chased her away as the priest had advised. Strangely, the neighbour did not leave by the gate but went straight through the hedge without breaking a single twig.
203161: Some hunters used small silver coins to be able to hit a strange rabbit. The next day a witch was lying in her bed with a gunshot wound. The clergy came to collect that witch's books of magic.
203165: At 'De Puydt' (1) in 't Nieuwland people heard water splashing in the evening. People believed the place was haunted.
203182: In Steenkerke there was a bridge that had to be raised whenever a ship came by. The woman standing at the bridge raised it, although she could easily have let the priest, who was just arriving, cross first. The woman began to laugh, whereupon the priest said: "It seems to me you raised the bridge a little too early!" The priest walked on and crossed the water by the Gastesbrug. Some even claimed the priest had walked over the water. When the ship had passed, the woman could not get the bridge back down. On his return the clergyman said to the woman: "Don't torment people any more in future!"
203186: A boy who was ridden by the mare saw in his dream a large body of water surrounded by monsters that wanted to drag him into the water. The boy could not flee, because his blood stood still.
203193: A man was walking past a wood at night with his neighbour. The 'hole' (?) of the lantern fell to the ground and the men could not find it again. The wood of Ardooie was haunted.
203210: The barn of a farm in Lissewege was haunted at midnight. Much noise caused by spirits could be heard then. As part of a bet, a labourer agreed to spend a night in the haunted barn. When the ghosts appeared at midnight, the labourer pretended to be asleep. Three times the ghosts lifted the man up to the ceiling of the barn. The man was terrified, but he kept still. The next Sunday the man told the farmhands with whom he had made the bet: "I sweated water and blood with fear. Even if you gave me half of Lissewege, I would not want to do such a thing again."
203219: A woman who raked her little path every day met a wizard, who asked: "But why do you always do that?" The woman replied: "Every evening the wizard's dog comes past here". The wizard answered: "Oh no, the wizard's dog has no paws". The dog was the wizard himself!
203228: A man worked at a haunted castle. One evening the man saw a returned dead person lying in the castle.
203231: A man who was in the cowshed in winter got a fright when his cap was knocked off his head by a turnip flying through the air. It was a green turnip, which was very strange because all the turnips in the whole of Rumbeke were frozen.
203234: A man was pushing his wheelbarrow in the rain past a house where a woman stood outside. At exactly that spot the man went into the ditch with his wheelbarrow. Convinced that the woman had caused it, the man shouted: "I'll smash your head in!" When the woman then went inside, the man could carry on without any trouble.
203246: Two people walking home in the dark suddenly saw a woman walking beside them. A moment later the woman had vanished without a trace. When the same thing happened again, they tried to grab hold of the woman. At that moment the people received a violent blow that made them lose consciousness at once.
203258: Some people coming out of a café in the dark saw some cats jump out of the dike. The animals began to fight and then ran off quickly. They were sorceresses in the shape of cats.
203312: On fishing boats a right shoe was sometimes nailed to the mast, because people believed it brought luck. Once a clog was supposedly taken from a ship's boy to nail to the mast. Because of this the boy had to walk home barefoot.
203313: Two women were talking when suddenly a violent storm arose. Then one woman said to the other: "Don't be afraid. We will pray the Gospel of Saint John." The next moment a cat came past that looked just like a ball of fire. That cat was a woman from the neighbourhood.
203321: A girl who had to fetch food for the rabbits accidentally left the door of the hutch open. When she came back, she found thirty-two rabbits among the rye and the oats. A witch managed to get all the rabbits back in their hutch within a quarter of an hour.
203331: A man came round a corner with two cows and a dog. The man's dog chased the cat of a woman from the village. When the man came back later that day, a hundred cats were sitting in front of that woman's door. The man's dog was nearly killed by the cats!
203339: On a Saturday evening at All Saints, a family sat at table eating porridge when a woman from the neighbourhood came to fetch a dish of meat. The father spooned sugar into his eldest child's porridge, whereupon the woman promptly put the sugar bowl by the wife and the other child. A few days later that child could no longer eat. It cried until the Saturday after All Saints. The mother took the child to the priest. The clergyman did not believe the child was bewitched and sent the mother to the doctor. Because the mother was still convinced the child was a victim of witchcraft, she had the curate pray over it. That did not help, because the curate himself did not believe in witchcraft. The mother then took the child to the friars of Steenbrugge. On the way back she met the woman from the village who had visited at All Saints, and spoke with her. When she got home the child was cured, but the mother was bewitched. She had a purplish-blue colour and the whites of her eyes were whiter than normal. At night the woman felt a hand at her heart. When she jumped out of bed and began praying a paternoster, the strange feeling stopped. People said the mother had 'de koek aan het hart' (heart disease). The mother then went to the midwife in Edegem. That woman associated with the friars of Steenbrugge and had special powers herself. The mother had to go to Bissegem and to the Kelderke van Mizerie in Kortrijk. On the way she had to eat the cake she had been given by the midwife. She also had to wear a ribbon until she lost it. After going to Bissegem, the woman no longer had palpitations. Fourteen days later she went back to the midwife, who said: "You should go on pilgrimage to France and take communion eight days in a row. I will send two girls from the village to France. If you get through half the illness in the first days, you will be cured. Otherwise you will be dead and buried." The mother recovered, to the great joy of the midwife who had helped her.
203345: A man who was ridden by the mare felt as if someone had grabbed him by the throat. When his wife called his name, the man was freed from the mare. If you were ridden by the mare, you had to throw something over yourself so that you could catch the mare.
203351: One evening, at a house where the occupants were already in bed, a man rang the bell and called: "Get up and light a lantern! A sorceress has come along with me in the shape of a black cat." The man beat the cat until it was nearly dead. After that the man was too afraid to go home alone.
203358: A clergyman was threatened by a robber who said: "Your money or your life!" The clergyman replied: "Friend, wait a moment," and pretended to look for his wallet. Meanwhile the clergyman bewitched the robber to the ground and left him standing there all night. When the sexton was about to leave for mass the next morning, the priest said to him: "On the road you'll see a robber standing. You can let him go now."
203390: In Westrozebeke lived a woman who had two daughters and one son. This witch often wore a hooded cloak and always tried to get near pregnant women. She had made her daughter unhappy, and her son made mice when he was at school.
203436: A rich man from Beselare claimed he could lay a five-franc coin on every cobblestone from the Kortekeer to the church. Every year this man bought clothes for about ten children making their solemn communion. One day the man said: "There are seven witches in Beselare. On Sunday after high mass I will make all seven of them stand at the churchyard railing. They won't be able to move on until I give them permission." In this way the witches were unmasked.
203450: In Assebroek an object or an animal had been thrown into the fire. The next day a woman from the village was lying in bed with burns.
203452: A boy had always heard that black cats were ghosts. When one day the boy came back from school a little later than usual, he saw a black cat sitting on a bridge, growling angrily. The boy gave the cat a kick, so that it flew a good six metres.
203453:
On a Templar farm between the Schare and the Kortekeer lived an old farmer with his maid. At night it looked as if the farm was ablaze, but it was no real fire raging there. A friar banished the evil from the dung heap to the farthest end of the field. While the clergyman did so, wailing was heard, whereupon the friar said: "You must not complain. You will be happy later". At the place where the evil had been banished to there was an avenue of oak trees. The following year all those trees died.
When the farmhands were preparing the grain for sowing, a figure always came and stood beside them and said: "The day is for you and the night is for us".
When two farmhands were closing a furrow, one said: "What is that dog doing there beside you?" The other farmhand, however, could not see the dog.
By a tall tree with a little chapel hanging on it, people often saw a coachman reading his newspaper in the evening.
At night on the farm people heard sounds as if butter was being churned, but when they went to look, there was nothing to be seen.
203462: If you met a witch, you often got a pat on the shoulder while the witch asked: "How are you?" Many people to whom this happened feared they had been struck by the evil hand.
203490: A man from Poperinge who owned books of magic was visited by the friars, who came to take the books away. The friars had been informed by some boys who had been bewitched to the ground as they left the sorcerer's house.
203494: In a house in Leffinge there was always a strange little cat. One day the people, annoyed, struck at the cat. The next day a woman from the village was injured.
203500: A woman came to a neighbour to fetch christening clothes. As soon as the woman was inside, the neighbour's child began to cry loudly. The neighbour sought advice from the friars of Steenbrugge. The clergymen advised her to go to confession and communion. The first person she met on her way home would be the guilty one. On her way home the neighbour met the woman who had come to fetch christening clothes from her.
203504: In an old house lights were seen every night. Those were the ghosts of dead people who had been forgotten by the living. During their lives those dead had promised to have masses said, but they had not done so. After those masses had been said, the house was no longer haunted.
203508: Strange things always happened at the Stadenkasteel. Although no one lived there, people always saw coaches without horses there.
203510: The mare was a kind of standstill of the blood.
203523: A ghost goat appeared at the little window above the door.
203527: When people in the old days were ridden by the mare, they could no longer breathe or move.
203530: People who were ridden by the mare at night had to have cold water poured over their heads. That way the mare could be driven off.
203552: On a farm near Zillebeke there were thirteen cows. One day all the cows had fallen ill. The people decided to clean the cowshed in the hope that the cows would recover, but they did not. The priest came and prayed over the cows for a quarter of an hour until the sweat rolled down his face. The clergyman said: "Someone has been here and you gave her nothing."
203558: There were so many cats on a farm that the occupants could no longer sleep because of the mewing. People believed that all this was caused by a sorceress from the neighbourhood.
203567: A woman and a girl went on pilgrimage to Zwevegem for someone who suffered from a heart disease, since such a pilgrimage always had to be made by two people. When the woman and the girl were tired, they sat down to rest on the doorstep of a little house. Then the girl suddenly said: "Don't you hear that noise in that house?" But the woman heard nothing. No wonder, because the noise was being made by the girl herself!
203572: On a farm the ghost of 'den Hogen Brand' could always be heard calling. When the owner of the farm had died, the tenants no longer heard the sound.
203607: A woman walking home got lost and felt she was being followed. The woman believed it was all the work of a witch who owned a book of spells.
203633: A mother who was searching the rubbish bins in Oostende saw a woman in a black cloak approaching, who was angry that someone had got there before her and said: "You filthy bitch! Go home and wash your boys!" When the mother got home, she found that all her children were full of lice. Moreover, the next morning the pig lay dead in the sty. The mother then went to the white nuns, who gave her little bags of blessed objects. The mother hung one of these bags on every door.
203638: In Keiem it often happened that children wasted away completely after being touched in their cradle by a witch.
203653: A child had been given an apple by a woman. After the child had eaten the apple, it did nothing but scream. Because the doctor did not know what to do, the mother had to send for the priest.
203656: Two men were building a cowshed when suddenly a rat came running up. One of the men kicked at the animal, but the other said: "No, you mustn't do that!" and stroked the rat. That man could send a plague of rats to a house, so that the straw in the mattresses was eaten and the rats came in by the front door and went out again by the back door.
203665: On a farm that was haunted, the animals and the cows lay dead. The friars came and placed a cross by the farm gate.
203692: A farmer often had visits from an old woman who always wanted to go and look in the stables. One day the farmer could no longer churn butter. He had the milk tested at the dairy, but nothing turned out to be wrong. When the farmer went to the vet, he met the old woman on the way and said to her: "You may not come onto my yard anymore, nor into the farmhouse!" In the end the farmer had the priest pray over his stable. The clergyman was drenched in sweat from the effort. After that, the farmer could churn butter again.
203709: A young carpenter was bewitched by the wife of his predecessor. Whenever the lad had nailed a plank in place, it came loose again shortly afterwards. The curate prayed over the young carpenter for nine days.
203736: A young man had to marry his pregnant girlfriend. In the church a woman asked the young man for holy water. The young man suffered a great deal during his girlfriend's pregnancy because that woman had asked him for holy water.
203744: A man walking past the Bekkem bridge at night saw a coffin standing there. The man tried to get closer to the coffin, but he could not. The next day there was nothing to be seen on the bridge.
203753: If someone did not behave normally, people said that person had been ridden by the mare.
203766: In 't Vrijgeweed will-o'-the-wisps were always seen. They were jets of flame that rose from three metres underground through small holes in the peat layer. If one could say very quickly: "Praised be Jesus Christ", one had freed a little soul from purgatory.
203770: In the past it was said that the doodkeersen (death candles, ghost lights) in the churchyards were spirits. Some thought rather that they were glow-worms.
203796: In Veldegem there lived a woman who bewitched children. All the mothers were afraid of that woman.
203816: Anyone ridden by the Koppe Maore (the mare) was not ill, but did have to stay in bed. One could be ridden by the mare as many as three or four times a day.
203817: A woman from Oostduinkerke had a baby that was six days old. Two fingers had been pressed into the baby's throat and its little thumb was blue. Because the father suspected the neighbour woman of having bewitched his child, he shouted angrily: "I'll smash her head in with a spade!" At that very moment the neighbour woman laid her hand on the fence around her house. The child was dead. During the summer the woman had raised a litter of young rabbits. One day the neighbour woman asked if she might see the animals. As the woman bent down to pick up a rabbit, the neighbour woman laid her hands on her back. The woman was bewitched.
203824: A married couple and a little boy were travelling somewhere by coach. When they met an old woman on the way, the little boy began to laugh at her. The man then said: "Don't laugh at that old woman, or we might get into trouble!" On the way back the horse broke loose, at exactly the spot where the little boy had mocked the old woman. Because of this the woman fell through the window of the coach.
203832: Just after the First World War, at dusk, a soldier was seen rising in the churchyard of Wervik and walking about with his rifle on his shoulders. No one dared pass the churchyard anymore for fear of this fallen soldier who came haunting.
203833:
A man from Wulvergem coming home from work in the evening was terrified to see a fireball. That was an omen of war.
Near Rijssel a girl had also once seen a fireball flying. The ball had burst over a cemetery and afterwards flowers could be seen everywhere.
203834: In Sint-Eloois-Vijve there was a haunted farm. Anyone who wanted to walk past that farm at night was stuck to the ground and could not go any further. The former occupant said that he had often seen little lights at night flying into the stables. Afterwards the cows had been untied. Masses are still said for a man who once lived on that farm, so that the hauntings would stop.
203856: In Eernegem there lived a woman who had special powers. Because everyone was afraid of her, no one dared refuse her anything. When a cow had to be loaded onto a cart, the woman made sure it could be done without any trouble.
203868: If a hedge had a flattened branch, people said the branch had been ridden by the mare.
203873: A man had fled to France because he had been falsely accused of stealing a pig from a farm. His grieving wife went to a woman who had special powers. "Do you have money?" asked the sorceress. "A quarter is enough, but I may not do it for nothing." The sorceress then fell to her knees before a crucifix, saying: "Sacré Coeur de Dieu, aidez-moi" (Sacred Heart of God, help me). Then the sorceress said to the woman: "He will come home this very evening." That evening, as the woman lay in bed, she suddenly heard someone knock on the door and say: "Wife, I'm back. I don't know what's the matter with me, but it was as if I was forced to come here. I'm all sweaty from the effort." When the woman told a priest what had happened, he said that her visit to the sorceress would be forgiven. The priest would pray for the woman all day and also submit a special request to the bishop.
203880: A man from Westkapelle wanted to slaughter a pig and so sent his thirty-year-old son to the butcher. The son let the butcher's wife talk him into eating some meat with them. When the son came home again, he threw his clogs up in the air and put glowing coals from the stove in his mouth. The young man fell ill. Because the doctor did not know what to do, they sent for the parish priest. The priest said to the sick man's parents: "I am going home and I will not come back." But when the priest reached the end of the lane, the sick man shouted loudly that the priest had to come back. After the priest had visited the sick man a second time, the same thing happened again. When the priest left for the third time, he took a different route and the sick man no longer called after him.
203897: A man who had been ridden by the mare said that an old woman in black clogs had been standing on his heart.
203904: A man going to Langemark one evening saw a spinning aalkarteel (a ghostly spinning wheel-like apparition) in the Papedreef. When the man had passed the last turnstile, he no longer saw the aalkarteel.
203913: The priest's maid was ridden by the mare every night. An old woman who was suspected of being a witch always came to the presbytery. One day the priest's maid was advised to fetch four Easter nails from the sacristy and put them under her mattress. After that the maid would no longer be ridden by the mare. And so it was.
203920: Large cats roamed around near Flabbaert. Anyone who met one of those cats would have a lot of bad luck.
203927: At the beginning of the Second World War the people on a farm had promised to build a chapel if the farm was spared from the bombs. After the war, one night a white wagon with two white horses and two white men was seen. The closer one came to the wagon, the further the wagon moved away from the people. The priest asked the people whether they had promised anything. After the chapel had been built, the ghostly apparitions were seen no more.
203933: Anyone ridden by the mare saw an apparition standing at the foot of his bed. A woman who had fallen victim to the mare screamed out. Some people claimed that the mare was a standstill of the blood.
203939: Strange things happened on a farm in Westvleteren. The animals ran with their tails in the air to the Kemmelbeek. Some animals jumped into the water, others ran back and fell into a well, so that they could only just keep their heads above water. Several vets had already visited, but none of them knew what to do. A priest claimed that a woman from the neighbourhood was causing the evil. That woman regularly came to fetch buttermilk. After an Agnus Dei had been hung on the gate, the woman could no longer get in. But all the cows that were already sick could not be saved.
203942: In a house a loud bang was always heard, after which all the plates fell off the wall. In the morning there was no trace of any of it. One night three knocks were heard. The man opened the door and grabbed into the darkness, but there was nothing in his hand. A friar had said that a curse of vengeance hung over the house.
203947: A sorceress could bewitch people so that they were stuck to the ground and could not move a foot.
203951:
A farmer who had no money for a new farmhouse summoned the devil at midnight. The devil appeared and said that the new house would be standing before the cock crowed the next morning. The farmer went home and told his wife about the agreement he had made. In the evening the devils began to work on the new farmhouse. When one of the devils said, "Ten more tiles and it's done!", the farmer said to his wife, "Crow!" The farmer's wife made a crowing sound, whereupon the cock began to crow too. At that, all the devils suddenly vanished.
Since then, however, that house has been bewitched. It is still haunted every night.
203958: A woman saw a magpie sitting on the well. However hard the woman tried to chase the magpie away, it always came back. The magpie stayed there for four weeks. On the day the woman's husband was killed in the war, the magpie disappeared for good.
