203964: On a farm in Beveren they could not churn butter. After cream had been poured into the churn, coals came out. When they sent for a parish priest, he had to hold on to a tree because he was sweating and very exhausted.
203966: On a farm in Koolskamp all the animals died. Every evening a woman wearing a neckerchief walked past that farm. It was said that the woman could work witchcraft and could turn herself into a cat. Anyone who insulted that cat was bewitched. Because the sorceress could not die, the priest had to come and pray over her. The sorceress had predicted that she would die at midnight, and that is what happened.
203987: Three witches once lived in Oostkamp. A farmer who had loaded his harvest onto a cart said to the bystanders: "Over there by that house the cart will tip over." And so it happened.
203990: It was believed that people who had led bad lives returned after their death.
203995: A man out walking with his neighbour suddenly saw a hare running and said: "If I had my gun now, I'd shoot that hare!" But the neighbour believed it was no ordinary hare. He walked up to the animal and suddenly found himself in a strange glow of light. Both men ran home in fear. On the way they were followed by the glow, and when they were home, the house was completely surrounded by light.
203999: If you wanted to meet the devil, you had to stand at a crossroads at midnight with a black hen.
204004: When a Duitse schaper (German shepherd, a travelling shepherd said to have magic powers) was refused food somewhere, he threw his hat against the door, which made the door open for him. What German shepherds could not do was open two crosswise bolts.
204020: A farm was connected to another farm by an underground passage. On that farm no farmhand could ever be kept on for longer than one night. One farmhand did stay longer, but he did not live long. At midnight ghosts came in down the chimney with a sack. They came to see whether the farmhand was asleep. He was not asleep, but he pretended to be. Then the ghosts began counting their money.
204026: A woman returning from the fair with her husband around midnight was followed the whole time by a skeleton with a light inside it. The couple did not dare to speak. A little later the doodkeers (death candle, ghost light) broke a branch and flew away. When the man and woman told the priest what they had seen, they learned that the light was a returning soul that wanted to say something. Because the man and woman had not spoken, the soul had angrily flown into a branch.
204031: In the old days people were often accompanied in the evening by ghost cats, which they were very afraid of.
204057: On a farm in Ardooie they could not churn butter. Every week the farm was visited by a woman with a bad reputation. The farmer went to the friars to have his farm exorcised with prayers. The friars asked whether a woman perhaps came to visit and then said: "You must keep that woman away." The friars came to exorcise the farm and put the evil onto a little tree, which they then buried. Grass never grew on that spot again. The grass was eaten by the evil.
204061: A woman who had to milk the cows in a distant meadow got lost because of the German shepherds (sheep herders believed to have magic powers).
204074: Some people drove around Kortrijk for a long time because they could no longer find the way. There was a man standing there who was making fools of them.
204076: A man taking his animals to the meadow met a sorceress in a hooded cloak on the way, who asked: "Where are you going?" Suddenly the animals became so wild that the man could not get into the meadow.
204086: At 's Graventafel in Passendale a castle of the Templars had sunk into the ground. People often saw the trees there flying against each other when there was no wind. Small creatures also flew about, which people said were the returned Templars.
204126: In the past one often heard of children who were bewitched. Sensible mothers did not let old women near their child's cradle. A child that had caught 'the old man' through a witch's doing cried all the time. The friars of Diksmuide exorcised the child with prayers, because the ordinary parish priests could not do it.
204146: A woman always came into a certain house and asked whether they needed anything. The people usually said they did not want anything. One day the woman asked for some red cabbage. When they gave her what she asked for, she ate the whole pot empty. Two weeks later those people's child was dead. That woman had caused it.
204164: In a parish plagued by rats, the priest stood in the church porch and began to pray. The next moment the rats came running, with two animals in front. The rats came closer, to within two metres. Then the animals turned around and ran away. They never came back.
204185: Between Ramskapelle and Westkapelle stood a farm where a woman lived who could work magic. One day a shopkeeper went to take hats to Ramskapelle. However, the shopkeeper got lost and ended up back in Westkapelle. Yet before leaving she had made the sign of the cross and said: "It is Friday today, God reward it."
204192: A house in Oostende was so badly haunted that no one wanted to go on living there. A man had once drowned a woman there in a copse.
204201: Between Passendale and Zonnebeke a goat always appeared. It was a dead man who had returned, who during his life had swindled people out of all sorts of things. In a castle near the place where the goat appeared, everything was always turned upside down in the morning. People were so afraid of the ghost goat that they no longer dared to go to Moorslede.
204204: In the evenings a man always saw cats jumping into the fire of the chicory kiln. For a long time the man also heard a goat screaming in the marshes. When people went to look, however, there was nothing to be seen. The curate came to exorcise the place. After that, however, the clergyman could no longer say mass because the evil was stronger than he was.
204214: The mare was a standstill of the blood. People who were ridden by the mare heard someone approaching and felt something on the blankets. They felt as if someone was tickling their nose or ear with a piece of straw. Victims of the mare were drenched in sweat and tried to call out, but no sound came.
204223: Anyone ridden by the mare in his sleep was stabbed in both sides.
204226: During the war a family stayed in another house. The children who slept in the attic always saw a man with a big hat and a long beard appear at night. When the father also saw the strange apparition, he was so frightened that he sought shelter elsewhere with his family. The strange apparition was probably a returned dead person.
204227: On a farm the doors always flew open and shut by themselves. Sometimes praying friars were also seen walking about there. A farmer's son who lived there died of fright. In the end the haunting did come to an end.
204233: A man transporting fish drove into the ditch after he had come past a witch's house.
204240:
While out walking, a pregnant woman met a woman who struck her on the belly and said: "Isn't that out yet?" Some time later the baby was stillborn.
That woman did not become pregnant again until she had herself exorcised with prayers. For she had been struck by the black hand.
204247: A farmer's wife churning butter early in the morning suddenly heard the door open. An old woman appeared and asked for coffee. The farmer's wife answered: "I have no coffee, but you can have some milk." "I don't want that," said the old woman, "but I would like a few slices of bread." When the farmer's wife had given her half a loaf, the old woman said: "Thank you. I will pray for you a lot." The old woman patted the farmer's wife on the shoulder and the farmer's wife did the same to the old woman. At this the old woman began to grumble and left. The farmer's wife carried on working, but she could not churn butter. So she decided to start again in the afternoon with fresh milk. The farmer's wife made the sign of the cross and threw a few leaves of blessed palm into the milk, saying: "Saint Benedict, help me." Half an hour later the farmer's wife had as much butter as she wanted. Two days later she again failed to make butter. This time too the palm sprigs helped. Three times the farmer's wife had to throw palm into the milk. Only then was the spell broken.
204265: A man on his way to his girlfriend met a horse on the road, which blocked his path. The man closed his eyes and made the sign of the cross.
204277: By the high Zandberg near Zillebeke stood a tank that was haunted at night. When the tower clock of the church in Ieper struck midnight, all kinds of noises were heard in that tank. A man coming back from the Westhoek one day was afraid because he had to walk past the tank at around twelve o'clock. Nothing strange happened, however.
204284: A small church was said to have once sunk in the bell pits in Eernegem. At night the bells could still be heard ringing at that spot.
204302: A woman always came to visit a farm in the evening when the farmer was not home. On those evenings the horses could be heard snorting in the stable. Although the farmer's wife knew for certain she had shut the stable doors, she found them open. When they went to look in the cowshed one evening, they found snakes and blood under the planks. Three days later the parish priest advised the farmer's wife not to let in the woman who visited in the evening any more. Since then nothing strange has happened on the farm.
204309: On a farm footsteps could always be heard.
204329: On a farm where a man had died, the animals dropped dead in the stable. At night the windows and doors could be heard banging open and shut. But when the people got up, there was nothing strange to be seen. The friars came to exorcise the farm. They banished the evil to the farthest part of the land. Every year the evil comes three centimetres closer.
204337: A man eating his midday meal suddenly saw a hare sitting on the windowsill and quickly went to fetch his gun. When the man came back, however, the hare was gone. A little later the hare was sitting on the windowsill again. The man shot at the animal several times, but the hare did not move. That hare was a witch.
204340: The mare was a person with a book who caused people to fall ill and made it impossible for their family to visit them, for example because they lived too far away.
204342: A farm girl put her skirt on the wrong way three days in a row. Shortly afterwards the girl died.
204354: A woman claimed that her child was bewitched and said firmly that she would never let that witch in again.
204378: In Kemmel there lived a witch whose daughter was about to give birth. Several doctors had already seen the girl, but they had not managed to deliver the child. The girl's mother said: "Go away, I'll do it." A few minutes later the mother came out with the newborn child in her arms. Her daughter died shortly afterwards.
204381: A baby lying in a cradle began to cry without stopping after a witch had been in the house. Because the doctor could not help, the child cried itself to death.
204392: On a haunted farm people were keeping watch over the body of the dead maid. When they went outside for a moment during the night, they saw ghostly lords in gold and silver riding around the bakehouse. The knights were looking for a treasure. In the morning the animals on that farm were dead.
204401: A brewer who could no longer brew sent for the priest, because he believed the kwade hand (the evil hand, bewitchment) had something to do with it. The priest began to pray until he was drenched in sweat. Suddenly a witch in the shape of a mouse ran outside. From then on the brewer had no more problems.
204416: A man who had bought a new horse went to a smith in the village for horseshoes. When the man came back with the shod horse, he met a neighbour, who also worked as a smith and said: "Why did you go to that other smith?" In revenge the smith sent a horde of rats to the man's house. The more rats the man killed, the more there seemed to be. One day someone came by who could drive the rats away. A particularly large rat brought up the rear of the procession at the stable door.
204425: If you wanted to know whether someone was a witch, you had to walk in the suspected woman's footsteps. If the woman was a witch, she would look back.
204440: In Vlamertinge a German shepherd went peddling rat poison. After the shepherd had made a sale at the brewery, he went to the castle. There, however, they did not want any rat poison. The shepherd had barely left the castle when it was full of rats. He had sent the rats from the brewery to the castle.
204452: It used to be haunted at the Kruis in Beveren. Black cats and all sorts of strange figures could be seen there. A man who passed there one night saw as many as a hundred cats walking in a circle. The man sat down on the ground and prayed a few Our Fathers. After that the cats had vanished without a trace.
204469: The boundary post between two fields had been moved. At night people kept hearing someone calling: "Where should I put them, where should I put them?" One night a farmer answered: "Put them, damn it, where you found them!" The ghost replied: "Thank you", then put the post back and was never heard from again.
204483: On a farm where the calves were dying, the people were advised to put a white goat in the cowshed. Once they had done so, no more animals died in the shed.
204495: Sometimes people were ridden by the mare in their sleep. If someone could say the name of the mare's victim, the mare disappeared.
204505: A woman had been cursed by her grandmother over a dish of meat. The grandmother had said she would haunt her granddaughter all her life. When the grandmother was dead, the woman was indeed plagued by strange forces. When she was working in the field, her skirt began to flap and her clogs flew a good three metres. At night it seemed as if fifty devils were in the house. Whenever this happened, the woman made the sign of the cross and began to pray. All her life she was plagued by her dead grandmother.
204518: With a family in Loppem the cows stopped giving milk and the animals grew thinner every day. When they sent for the vet, he stayed in the stable for a while and then said to the farmer's wife: "Quiet, you mustn't speak too loudly. There is a bucket of water in the stable. Go and look in that bucket and you will see the face of a witch." The farmer's wife went to look and of course saw the reflection of her own face in the water. The vet advised the farmer's wife to put a few buckets of grain and linseed meal in the trough every day. Then the cows would give milk again.
204521: A farmer from the Gistenhoek often saw horse-drawn coaches with ladies and gentlemen driving around his farm at night. After the coaches had circled a few times, they disappeared.
204523: A baby bewitched by a witch cried all the time and had to be exorcised with prayers by the friars.
204530: On the road to Ichtegem lived a woman who could do witchcraft. Many people had shot at that woman, but they could never hit her, because she could turn herself into a dog. Whenever a cart drove past her house, it nearly always overturned. A man who had put a half-franc coin in his gun shot at the dog. The very first shot hit. The witch had a wound in her loins.
204533: Strange things happened at the little chapel of Troost en Nood in Kortemark. At night many candles could be seen burning there. The priest removed the statue of Mary from the chapel twice, but twice the statue returned by its own power. The third time the statue was carried in a procession to the church, where it still stands today.
204536: On a farm where a strange cat always came in, one day they threw boiling water over the animal. A while later the farmer heard that one of the neighbour women was lying in bed with burns.
204559: A strange maid worked on a farm in Lendelede. In the mornings everything on the farm was in disarray. The churn had fallen over and the wheels had been taken off. The animals jumped about restlessly. A clergyman advised the farmer and his wife to send the maid away. After her dismissal the maid went to America. The people of Lendelede were rid of her witchcraft, but she probably did exactly the same in America.
204564: A man coming home on New Year's Day saw a woman standing at his door and wished her a happy New Year. The woman then gave the man a shot of liquor. The man was ill for a week from that drink. That woman's husband, a police sergeant, was always ill when he had leave, so he could never go on holiday. The witch did that to her husband herself. While the man was ill from the drink, he did nothing but pray to break the spell. One day the sergeant came to ask him to stop praying.
204599: A woman who had thirteen children lost four of them within one week. All of that woman's children died before the age of nine, except for one daughter. At her wits' end, the woman sent for the curate. She said to the clergyman: "I don't know what is happening here. The children are full of pins and they are dying of it." The clergyman then said: "Tonight close all the shutters and put out the light. Then you will see the culprit." The culprit turned out to be the neighbour, who owned books.
204604: A farmer who had been milking his cow met a witch on his way home, who looked into the bucket. When he got home, the farmer found that the milk was sour. The next time the farmer came back with his milk, he chased the witch away before she had a chance to look into the bucket.
204615: In the time of the German shepherds, a castle was said to have sunk in the Tegelbos.
204620:
In Moorsele lived a woman descended from knights. The woman was very rich and lived in her sister's castle. She led a questionable way of life, but she gave a lot to the poor. When the woman died, her will stated that the castle was to be given to the orphans. The widower, however, hid the will. One morning the man was found dead. Moreover, the place smelled of paper and sulphur. In the evenings flames were often seen at the castle and a language was heard that no one understood. The will also stated that a Calvary costing 1200 BEF was to be put up at the church. The Calvary that was later erected was only one of 4000 BEF. Once the Calvary was put up, the haunting came to an end.
When the woman lay dying, a priest had been sent for from Kortrijk. But the wheel of the priest's cart broke, so the clergyman arrived too late. That priest was also named in the woman's will, but the bishop would not allow him to accept the inheritance. He did so anyway, but met with a fatal accident on his way home.
The French convent was haunted for a long time.
204626: One day a boy went for a walk in the churchyard carrying his little sister in his arms. When the boy came home, his mother had to send for a friar, because the boy was so ill he could hardly stand. The friar exorcised him with prayers. The little sister died the next day because she was bewitched.
204640: There was always a hare near a farm. After someone had shot at the animal, a woman from the village had a bandage over her eyes.
204644: A man standing in a shop was touched by a strange woman. When the man came home, he was ill. After the curate had exorcised him with prayers, he recovered.
204661: A woman came to a farm to beg for alms. The farmer's wife refused and sent the woman away. In the evening the farmer's wife heard a hellish noise of horses striking the gate with their hooves. That was the black hand. A little later the beggar woman was seen coming out of the attic room wearing the farmer's wife's best clothes.
204663: On a farm lived people who always saw a white goat at night. After the people had built a chapel at that place, the goat no longer appeared.
204667: When someone was ridden by the mare, the victim's mind and blood stood still. People could only be freed from the mare by having prayers read over them or by means of an Easter nail.
204671: Someone always came to steal pears from the parish priest. One day the thief got stuck in the pear tree. A man who always rang the priest's doorbell as a prank got stuck to the doorbell.
204683: In an inn sat a small, emaciated man who claimed he could make the devil appear. Everyone present laughed at the man, but at a certain moment a rattling was heard, and everyone began to scream with fear. When the little man went home, he jumped onto a waterduivel (water devil) and rode away. That same little man once made the devil dance on an organ in a dance hall.
204686: On a farm the horses and cows were always untied. After people had been to the friars of Kortrijk, the haunting came to an end.
204689:
A boy from Aaigem often came to a farm where there were several daughters, to court one of the girls. When the boy set off home one evening, his girlfriend said: "You mustn't go down that lane, because strange things sometimes happen there." The boy did not take the warning seriously and walked down that lane anyway. At the farm in that lane he got lost. What is more, the trees seemed as big as churches. When the boy got home and had to milk the cows, he had to hold his arms high in the air to reach the udders.
An old man had seen a deer near the farm in the haunted lane, and it followed him. As soon as the man reached the yard of another farm, the deer had vanished. Two girls coming back from the fair in Aaigem were surprised when a strong wind suddenly began to blow in that lane. One day a white horse was seen wandering near the farm. Someone threw a dung fork at the horse and hit the animal in the rump. The next day a woman lay in bed with a broken leg.
204704: Plants that had been ridden by the mare had a flat stem. Anyone who hung such plants above his bed could not be ridden by the mare himself.
204722: A woman was tormented by her ex-boyfriend, who still had a neckerchief of hers. The boyfriend stuck needles into the neckerchief and into candles. Every evening the woman could be seen fighting her boyfriend, who had made himself invisible.
204727: A parish priest who had visited a witch was tormented by her until his death. The priest had asked the diocese several times for a transfer, but his letters never arrived.
204754: At the 'Vierkoaven' (?) a white horse always roamed at night.
204755: In a house in Sint-Andries a woman was frying fish. At a certain moment a cat came in and asked the woman: "Won't you give me a little fish?" A little later the cat had vanished.
204764: In Westkerke stood a farm with a small tower. A stone in that tower always came loose. The farmer often tried to brick up the hole in the wall, but the stone always came loose again. One day the mason found a fortune in that wall. The former owner came to haunt the place to count his money. With that money the mason bought at least three houses.
204774: A witch lived in Beselare. If you accepted a mint sweet from her, you fell ill and had to be exorcised with prayers by the friars.
204812: A farmer's wife woke up around midnight because she heard a noise in the grain loft. It sounded as if someone were shovelling grain. A little later it sounded as if the boards under the roof were being pulled loose. Then stones were heard rolling down from the roof. The dog did not bark, but crept fearfully between the legs of the farmer, who had meanwhile woken up too. When the farmer and his wife went to look a while later, there was nothing strange to be seen in the loft. After they had told the priest what had happened, the priest said: "Ghosts existed in the past, and they have not been gone for so long. The noises were probably caused by spirits of the dead who neglected a vow. The later occupants of such a farm must then do penance." After the priest had sprinkled the farm with holy water and laid a sprig of blessed palm there, nothing strange happened any more.
204818: In Lichtervelde lived an old man who said he would come back after his death. When the man was dead and buried, his relatives saw him sitting by the stove one evening. Frightened, the people asked what things were like in the hereafter. The ghost replied: "They are very strict and exacting there. The least thing you have done is counted against you". Then the ghost disappeared for good.
204827:
A farmer's wife milking the cows was visited by a woman from the neighbourhood. The woman asked whether she might milk a few cows too. The cows milked by that woman gave blood instead of milk. In the end those cows died.
Some people owned books of magic, which were later collected by the clergy.
204834: The castle of Tervichten was haunted. Under the gateway sat an evil spirit that smashed everything if people did not say enough prayers or did not go on pilgrimage often enough.
204836: A woman who had a pretty little daughter was visited one day by a woman peddler. The mother bought something. While she was away fetching her money, the peddler went to the daughter's cradle. The child fell ill and died exactly thirteen months later.
204842:
On a farm in Sint-Jan strange things always happened during the night before a feast day. The people heard someone walking across the attic in heavy clogs and the doors slamming. The noise lasted until morning. When they went upstairs to look, strangely enough there was nothing to be seen.
Only after the First World War did the haunting come to an end.
204844: A man who owned books of magic had put one of the books on the mantelpiece and urged his wife not to touch it. One day while cleaning, the woman picked up one of the books and read a bit of it. At that moment her husband stood stock-still where he was, as if nailed to the ground. The priests had to be called to free the man.
204854: A boy was in the same class as the son of a witch. That son could do magic. For example, he could conjure up mice by rubbing some earth in his hands. The teacher sent for the priest, who read prayers over the boy while he was making another mouse. Shortly afterwards the boy lost his magic power, so that he could no longer make the mouse disappear.
204857: A widow with two sons noticed that one of her sons was becoming as thin as a rake, while the other looked quite normal. The thin son always lay sweating and sighing in his bed at night. One night the two sons swapped beds. The healthy son took precautions and put a kruisbreidel (a bridle with a cross-shaped bit) by his pillow. When the boy felt something like a sack of grain roll onto him, he struck at it with the bridle. At that a horse appeared. That same night the boy took the horse to the blacksmith to have it shod. When that was done, the boy put the horse with the other horses. The next morning the mother of the two boys stayed in bed. "I'm ill," she said. One of the boys pulled back the sheets and saw that the woman had horseshoes on her hands and feet.
204864: A woman visiting the grave of her dead child saw two little candles burning in the churchyard. A bit further on the woman saw a skull. The woman was so frightened that from that day on she no longer dared to go outside in the evening.
204866: On a farm in Wingene a shepherd heard a tinkling when he stuck his staff into a beech tree. He put his hand into the tree and felt a little statue of Our Lady. The shepherd took it to give to the farmer's wife, but the next day it had disappeared. The same thing happened three more times. The Kutskapelletje was then built on that spot.
204870: A sorceress could make people lose their way and walk through the water. One day the sorceress said to a boy: "Go on home, for you'll never get there anyway!" The boy walked the whole way in the ditch, until someone came and pulled him out.
204878: In Westende there used to be a farm that was full of rats and mice. Someone had sent that vermin. The priest drove the animals away.
204888: A young man sometimes woke up at night and then could not move. He wanted to call out, but he could not.
204902: A pig had been touched by an old woman who had said: "This animal will bring no luck." Some time later the pig got 'the old man' (a disease).
204988: A man who was home alone lying in bed suddenly heard someone kicking his bed with heavy shoes. The man got up, but there was nothing to be seen. "Go on and kick until you're sick of it!" said the man. After that the banging stopped.
204989: A man was sometimes ridden by the mare when he slept on his back. He then heard screaming and was grabbed by the throat. To avoid being ridden by the mare, you had to set your shoes 'toe to toe' beside the bed.
204991: A parish priest threatened by a robber said: "I'll take a pinch of snuff first, because I'm shaking so badly I can't find my money." The priest made the robber stay standing still until the next morning.
205008: At All Saints' will-o'-the-wisps were often seen wandering about. They were the souls of wicked people who had to come and atone for their sins. A woman from Oostende prayed every evening that God would come and take those lights away.
205009: A carter coming back from Brugge had dropped off a load at a house. When the carter took hold of his horse's reins, the animal would not move. The carter struck his horse with the whip. Suddenly the carter saw a cat jump out of the cart. As soon as the cat had gone, the horses could move on by themselves. At the house across the road stood a woman whose arms and face were all grazed by the whip. That woman could do witchcraft.
205017: Some farmers who had gone with horse and cart to fetch liquid manure were harassed at the Smedenpoort by a goat that jumped onto the cart and ran between the horses' legs. None of the farmers managed to catch the goat.
205037: Today is Saturday, God's day. A witch could make the table dance and the beer glasses on the table move. She could also draw beer from a table leg.
205040: When an old woman swept away a little heap of dirt, the heap suddenly said: "Ouch, ouch!"
205047: Anyone ridden by the mare in his sleep was in reality having a standstill of the blood. Such people screamed in their sleep. To protect yourself against the mare, you had to put a stick above your bed that had itself been ridden by the mare and was therefore flat rather than round. The mare would then sit on that stick.
205060: After the First World War a witch had to give lodging to some soldiers. Those soldiers could do magic, but the witch's magic was much stronger. When the soldiers wanted to leave the house at night, they found they could not. The witch had magically shut the door with her book.
205061: A boy walking in the churchyard with his friends kicked a skull and said: "If there is still life in you, come and eat at my table tonight." That same evening the doorbell rang. The ghost came in and was given a roemer of wine. Then the ghost struck the host in the teeth and flew away, saying: "With me you must burn forever in the fire of hell with much clamour!"
205066: A farmer transporting grain met a witch, who said: "You'll never get home! You'll have a late evening." A little further on the wagon's wheels broke, so that the wagon fell over.
205070: Doodkaarsen (death candles, ghostly lights) flew from one dung heap to another. Doodkaarsen were also often seen in a churchyard. People believed they were ghosts.
205093: A woman going to mass always heard a sound behind her on the way. When the woman reached the church, she looked behind her and saw that she had been followed by a magpie. After mass the magpie was there again. The woman threw a stone at the bird, but the magpie kept following her until she was home. At home the woman found that her child had typhoid. Yet the child had been healthy when the woman left.
205094: Along the Roeselarestraat there was a bell pit. The bells that had sunk there could be heard ringing at night.
205095:
The chimney of a brickworks in Ramskapelle was haunted.
By the canal in Ramskapelle stood a farm of the Witheren (Norbertine canons), which was later haunted. It was so bad that no German dared to set foot on the farm because it was a devil's farm. Many people died on that farm.
205102: When there was a sick person in the house, a kind of ticking was often heard. People called it 'the little frog'. If the little frog had been heard, the sick person would die.
205117: The mare was something that could not be stopped. People were troubled by the mare mostly when they lay on their backs.
205122: An old woman who always tried to get into houses where small children lived was thrown out everywhere. People were afraid of her.
205126: In the evenings a woman heard the former occupant of her house stirring the pots and pans. Only she could hear the sound.
205141: In Sint-Michiels there was a shed in which the animals lay dead every morning.
205148: A witch tormented children by sticking pins into a piece of butter. With every pinprick the child felt pain.
205163: A woman flew on a goat wherever she wanted after saying: "Over everything and above everything". One day the woman's daughter wanted to imitate her mother. But she made a mistake speaking the magic formula and said: "Over everything and through everything". Because of this the daughter flew into everything and came back covered in injuries.
205180: A house in Lombardsijde was haunted. The people always heard noises there in the evening, although there was nothing to be seen. After a witheer (Norbertine canon) from Oostende had been sent for, the haunting was over.
205183: A farmer was annoyed by a cat that always came and sat with him when he was milking the cows. One day the farmer hit the cat on the head. The next day one of the soldiers was walking around with a bandage around his head.
205193: A married couple went to the friars in Roeselare because their brick kiln would no longer burn. A Redemptorist came to exorcise the kiln with prayers. Whenever the people lit the kiln, a woman always came by to fetch some fire with a little shovel. After the friar's visit the kiln still would not burn. The people went back to the friar, who told them: "If someone comes by, you must chase that person away." Some time later the old woman came by again, but they did not chase her away. Because the kiln still did not burn after that, the couple went to the friars once more. "You didn't do what I said," said the friar, "you must chase her away!" The next time the man and woman chased the old woman away. After that they could get the kiln to burn again.
205205: A fisherman went to his skipper, with whom he was to sail. Because the weather was rainy, the skipper decided not to leave until the next morning. The man went back home through the wood and there met a calf with a curly tail, which blocked his path. When the man came closer, he saw that the calf had turned into a big dog. Terrified, the man ran home. The next morning the man set off for his skipper a second time. In the wood he saw only his own footprints from the day before. Since then the man never again dared to go through that wood.
205210: Some farmers had dug up the potatoes and gathered them in sacks. At a certain moment a witch with a magic wand passed by and made all the potato sacks fall over.
205217: A man from De Panne could make mice, which he let run around in the church. In the end the priest took the man's magic power away.
205253: A man always cycled to France, where he worked in the beet fields. Every time he rode past a witch without greeting her, he had a flat tyre a little further on.
205294: In the old days it sometimes happened that someone struck a cat and afterwards a woman was seen walking around with a wound.
205326: A woman bewitched someone who had refused to give her a piece of meat.
205328: After his death a farmer came haunting his farmstead in his everyday clothes. The parish priest said to the man who had seen the ghost: "Have a mass said for father". After a mass had been said, the ghost did not appear again.
205330: A farmer from Ingooigem who had three cows could no longer churn butter. An old woman who was said to be a witch always came to the farm. The parish priest gave the farmer this advice: "Disinfect the churn thoroughly and give your cows clean drinking water. I will then pray that the witch has no more power." After that had been done, everything went well on the farm again.
205336: A man went hare hunting in the snow. When the thirteenth hare ran past, the animal said to the man: "Just stay sitting there, for many more will come after me." The man wanted to raise his arm to shoot, but he could not. His arm was as stiff as a board.
205339: A farmer had gone to Brugge to fetch a bell for a farm. On the way back the cart overturned, and the bell fell into a pit. However much people dug, that bell was never found again. That is why the pit was later called 'de klokkenput' (the bell pit).
205340: The eternal hunter was a boy who had been cursed by his parents. In the Wijnendale woods he could be heard calling: "tjagouw". He was seen jumping from one tree to another.
205348: The football field in Sint-Andries was also called 'Klokkeveld' (Bell Field) because bells were said to have sunk there around 1600. Some people claimed those bells could be heard ringing on Christmas night.
205361: A sorcerer who was attacked in the woods of Wortegem bewitched his attacker to the ground.
205390: When strangers had been in the house, it often happened that a child cried day and night afterwards. Bewitched children had to be taken to the parish priest.
205404: On a farm lived a farmer who suspected his maid of being a witch. One Sunday the farmer saw a toad come into his house. He grabbed the animal with the stove poker and threw it into the fire. At that a loud thunderclap rang out. When the maid came in, she had burns all over.
205411: On Christmas night at twelve o'clock the Concordia could be seen sailing on the beach instead of in the water.
205413: On a farm where the farmer and his wife had died, the children quarrelled over the inheritance. Some time later the farm was plagued by rats. The priest advised the children to dig a pit. After the clergyman had prayed for a while, all the rats went into that pit, and they were rid of the plague.
205431: People who had eaten too much and slept on their backs could sometimes be ridden by the mare. In the old days people put palm branches behind the window shutters to keep the mare out of the house. In reality the mare was a bad dream. People who had such a dream made a lot of noise, but once they were woken up, they were freed.
205437: A wheelwright kept coming back for a long time after his death. The dead man would sit working at night.
205453: Sorcerers and witches could give people lice. People to whom this had happened had to have prayers read over them.
205454: A girl always saw the ghost of her brother, who had died young. When the girl had to pump water, she felt as if she had to hit her brother's head with the pump handle. After a while the girl no longer dared to pump water. The girl's mother thought her son wanted to let them know in this way that he needed many prayers. After the girl had two masses said, her brother no longer appeared.
205456: In the monastery one of the workmen had kicked a cat. At night chains could be heard rattling in that monastery. The sound of a moving cart could also be heard. Someone who got up saw a big black cat with a black eye. That cat had the face of the man who had kicked the animal. The next day that man came to work with a black eye.
205464: A farmer coming back from the café one evening could not get across the bridge because a cat appeared that said: "The day is for you, the night is for us."
205492: On a bewitched farm the devils came and untied the horses. Every morning the horse stable had been torn down.
205502: People who heard chains rattling in their attic every night went to the friars. It was their dead grandmother who came haunting. The clergymen gave the people this advice: "You must speak to the ghost, and when she holds out her hand, you must throw a towel at it." The people said to the ghost: "If you are sent by the devil, then go. If you are sent by God, then speak." The ghost burned a hand into the towel and said that a good many masses still had to be said. When the masses had been said, the dead woman returned once more to thank her family.
205522: A woman had picked up an apple in a meadow and stuck it on a little stick to hold it over the fire. After a while the apple flew up the chimney with the words: "I'm roasted enough!"
205524:
A woman knew a formula against the mare, which went as follows:
"Mare, go far away,
creep through all the cracks in the roof
before you get into my bed."
205538: A mother had a small child that had been crying day and night for a week. The father decided to have prayers read over the child by the friar. While this was happening, the mother had to wait in another room. The friar said to the parents: "Tomorrow a toad will come into your house and will jump straight to the cradle. You must throw that toad into the fire at once and hold the stove tilted so the toad cannot jump out. Then you must put the lid on at once so the toad cannot crawl out again." When the toad appeared, however, the mother did not manage to catch the animal. So she went back to the friar, who said: "I thought as much. Tomorrow the toad will come back and then you must catch it." The next day the woman made the sign of the cross and drank a shot of liquor before going after the toad with the tongs. The mother managed to throw the toad into the stove. Then her husband put the lid on the stove. The toad made a lot of noise in the stove and disappeared after a while. That same week the mother saw a woman walk by whose jaw was completely burnt. That woman came every week to ask for alms and had always been given something. Shortly afterwards the witch died.
205558: At the Ter Doest farm in Lissewege the cows were all lying with their legs in the air. A woman had buried a rotten egg in a wheat field. The farmer dug the egg up and went to bury it in that woman's field. The egg brought a disease into the grain that turns the flour into black dust. The man threw horse manure with lime on the wheat field.
205559: A woman whose husband had not come home on time went to fetch him at night. On the way the woman suddenly saw a skeleton walking along with her. Terrified, the woman said: "If you are sent by God, speak. If you are sent by the devil, go back where you came from!" A little later the skeleton had vanished.
205569: A farmer from Schapenbrugge was coming back in the afternoon from high mass in Westkapelle. On the way the farmer met two sisters and chatted with them. When a drunkard passed by, the sisters began to laugh at the man. The drunkard then said: "You may laugh now, but it won't last long!" On their way to the fair the sisters were suddenly full of lice. When they turned back, the lice were suddenly gone. The sisters then decided to go to the fair after all, but before they got there, they were full of lice again. The same thing happened three times. Only after they had begged the drunkard to leave them alone did the torment end.
205574: A woman who was said to be a sorceress had two farmhands and two maids. This sorceress could make people draw a good or a bad number in the conscription lottery in Langemark. During that period the sorceress went around six times a day to extort money from people. In the evening nobody dared walk past her house anymore. Two black cats sat on the gate of her house, and people were very afraid of them. In the meadow next to her house the cows always broke through the hedge.
205576: Some people were working in the field when a man with special powers came by. Suddenly the horses stopped and began to sweat. Only after the passer-by had spoken could the horses move on again. The man was a sorcerer who owned black books.
205593: A boy whose father had died came home late one evening, which made his mother angry. The boy began to sulk and went to his bedroom. There the boy suddenly felt a blow on his cheek, although no one could be seen. The next morning the boy saw that a black hand had been burned into the door.
205595: On a farm a white horse was seen walking in the yard every night. Strangely enough, in the morning that horse had vanished. The same horse was also seen on a road and by a little chapel. On the farm closest to that chapel, butter could not be churned at night.
205597: A farmer whose cows were bewitched sought advice from the friars, who gave him holy water to sprinkle the farm with. When the farmer had done so, he found the next day that his wife was tied up. It was the farmer's wife herself who had bewitched the farm.
205607: At the Spletlinde, a split lime tree with a cross in it, it was badly haunted. After the friars of Tielt had exorcised the place, the haunting came to an end.
205619: In Houtkerke there was a little child who cried all the time and no longer wanted to lie in its cradle. After the parish priest had blessed the cradle, the child cried no more.
205623: A mother had laid her baby on a little blanket when a woman came by peddling shoe polish and said, "Madam, what a lovely child you have!" while moving her hand over the child. Shortly afterwards the child began to cry and got diarrhoea. Because the child was dying, the parish priest was sent for to read prayers over it. After that had been done, the witch could no longer get into the house.
205627: A man had shot out a toad's eye with a bullet made with salt. The next moment a woman was lying dead on her bed.
205628: A parish priest claimed he could draw disobedient people into a bottle. When some rascals tried to steal apples in the priest's garden during the sermon, the thieves got stuck to the tree. They were only freed when the priest came out of church.
205641: On winter evenings a man always saw a cat come in through the drain hole for the water. One evening the man saw three black cats walking by the churchyard. When the cats tried to attack him, the man kicked at one of the animals. The next day a farmhand from the village was lying in bed. He could turn himself into a cat.
205646: Three men, one of them a wizard, were coming back from the fair in Vlamertinge in pouring rain. The man whose house they would reach first said to the other two: "I'm almost home, but you two will get soaked!" The wizard replied: "Yes, we'll see about that. You might well be on the road longer than us!" The two men went on. The next day one of them met the man who should normally have been home first the day before. That man said: "Well, I've had quite an experience! This morning at a quarter to five I was still looking for my house!" The wizard had made the man lose his way, so that he was soaked to the skin and had caught pneumonia.
205648: People who were ridden by the mare in the evening or at night could not move.
205657: A man from Dottenijs met a skeleton without arms and without legs one evening. "Good evening," said the man, but there was no answer. Terrified, the man ran away.
205661: In Avelgem lived a man who was always quarrelling with an invisible apparition that followed him. "Don't you see anyone?" the man always asked passers-by, but he was the only one who saw the apparition. Every time the man wanted to do something, that hand held him back. It was the evil hand.
205663: A piano teacher who had been near a witch found that his head was full of lice.
205666: A man who went to see someone one evening about a job saw a whole pack of little white rats running at his feet. That must have been witchcraft, because white rats were otherwise not seen very often.
205672: At the fair in Leke the priest had told the people not to gamble. A man who ignored that ban was told by the priest: "If you gamble anyway, the devils will dance in your house." The man gambled anyway, and some time later his house was indeed full of devils. All the people from the village came to look at the devils, but they saw nothing. There was, however, a terrible stench in the house.
205678: At ''t Watergat' on the Zwijnebak a goat could always be heard screaming. Because many people came to listen to that strange phenomenon, the inns in the neighbourhood sold a great deal of beer.
205707: In a haunted house everything was thrown about, although no one could be seen.
205722: A girl heard her father making noises in his sleep. The girl's mother then said: "He is being ridden by the mare again". In Zonnebeke there did indeed live a mare who tormented people, so that they could no longer speak because their throats were squeezed shut.
205726: At night a man saw a figure at the window, which said: "I am going to take your wife". Shortly afterwards the man's wife died.
205748: A man from Westkerke had to go to the doctor in Oudenburg for one of his children. On the way the man met a young kitten that ran under his feet. The man kicked at the animal, but it did not go away. In the end the man took the kitten with him. After a while, however, the animal became so heavy that the man had to leave it behind.
205751: A man was always ridden by the mare at night. The man claimed that the mare was the ghost of someone who had died in his house. The ghost came knocking on the wall every night and then sat on the man. The priest advised the man to scatter sand around his house. In the morning, however, there were no footprints to be seen in the sand. After the man had put a paasnagel (a nail blessed at Easter) somewhere, the mare no longer came. The last time, though, the mare had ridden him much harder than usual.
205756:
A family from Bikschote was always visited during High Mass by a woman who went to pray at the little chapel by the toll barrier. The woman would then come inside sighing. A man who went hunting at night ran into the woman.
That family from Bikschote could not churn butter.
205758: Evil spirits and damned souls came around the churchyard to ask for help.
205767: A woman who was taking sheep away met a witch, who threw leaves on the animals. Because of that the sheep would not go any further.
205783:
To protect oneself against the mare, one had to say:
"O Mare, you ugly beast
Do not come here this night
All waters you shall sail
All trees you shall strip of leaves
All blades of grass you shall count
Do not come to torment me this night".
205789: On a haunted farm the ghostly phenomena were worst in the cowshed and in the cellar, the places where the maid spent most of her time. The farmer was terrified whenever he talked about the haunting. In the evenings the farmer's wife often went to the poor dressed in a hooded cloak. The maid's whole family moved to America and the same ghostly phenomena occurred there. Medals and scapulars hung on the farm. One day the farmer went to fetch help somewhere. Two gentlemen appeared at the farm, and some people claim those gentlemen were friars.
205790: Some men who worked for a farmer went home every evening. In Stalhille the men heard shuffling, although there was nothing to be seen. The sound came closer and closer.
205800: If someone felt hunted during their sleep, people said that this person was being ridden by the mare.
205811: Two friends were coming back at night from the fair at the Sas van Heist. When the two met a black tomcat on the way, one of the boys said: "I'll give that beast a kick!" But his friend replied: "No, you mustn't do that, because that tomcat is my father!"
205814: In Ruddervoorde people once saw a great fire. That was an omen of war or of another disaster. Such fires could even be seen as far as Africa. Perhaps they had something to do with the Northern Lights.
205846: A woman who was pregnant with her third child went on a pilgrimage to Saint Symphorian. From there one had to bring back a kilo of sugar to put in the child's food for nine days. One also had to take baby shirts for nine days and have the priest read prayers over them. When the woman had been pregnant with her first child, the witch had come to look at the cradle. Although the cradle was still empty, the child became bewitched and died. During her second pregnancy the woman lived in a place the witch did not know. Strangely, the witch still stood by the house when the child was one day old. The child had eaten well that morning, but after the witch's visit it got foam on its lips and died. It had been the kwade hand (the evil hand, a harmful bewitching touch).
205855: A devout woman who went to mass very often always hurried home when she had met a black cat.
205856: On a farm in Anzegem someone had seen a procession passing by one evening. In front walked a large dog with chains, followed by a group of white figures. There was praying and beautiful songs were sung. One could even smell the incense. The procession went right through the trees.
205867: A man walking along the lock from Oostende to Bredene saw a tall woman in front of him. The man greeted the woman, but she did not answer.
205882: Some women could give children the kwade hand (the evil hand, a harmful bewitching touch). Such bewitched children had to have prayers read over them by the parish priest.
205902: A fisherman saw a woman pass by, who said, "You must be catching a lot?" After that the man caught no fish at all. When the woman was in a good mood and said, "You can't be catching much?", the man caught a lot of fish.
205921: When the Sint-Jan procession had been cancelled because of bad weather, the statue of Mary went out by itself. In 1978 the procession again could not take place because of bad weather. The statue of Mary was then placed in a cart and driven around.
205924: At a farmstead in Veldegem people often saw a procession of little men in red jackets. In one of the pens no animal could be kept alive; whenever a new animal was put in, it was found dead the next day.
205925: A mother whose child had been bewitched after an ugly woman had visited went to the priests for advice. On the way she met that ugly witch. The witch asked the mother where she was going, to which the mother replied: "That's none of your business!" The priests advised the mother to search carefully at a certain spot in her garden. The mother found a little doll with pins in her garden. Her child died that same week.
205930: A man who saw a cat early in the morning gave the animal a kick. The cat broke in two and vanished.
205945:
A parish priest on his way to the station met a farmer working in his field. The priest said something, and the farmer gave a mocking reply. When the priest came back from the train that evening, the farmer was still standing in the same place. The clergyman had bewitched him to the ground.
One day during his sermon the priest said that someone was sitting in his cherry tree and that the thief would stay there until the priest came home.
The same priest once also bewitched a courting couple standing next to his house to the ground until the next morning.
205947: A widower heard chains rattling every night. It was the ghost of his dead wife, who came to ask for prayers.
205984: Some people who came to a well suddenly heard music and no longer dared to go on.
205988: In the old days there were old women who could force people to go somewhere.
206011: When a disease destroyed the potato harvest in Flanders in 1865, people believed the disaster was caused by the steam of the trains. They consulted a sorcerer, who pointed his stick at a train travelling from Gent to Waregem. The next moment the train came to a stop. The sorcerer then said to the people: "You see that I can, but I won't. Later it would do more harm than good."
206025: In a house a beautiful bouquet of flowers always appeared on the table at midnight. At that moment the farmer was thrown out of his bed and heard the cows lowing. A miller and a butcher who did not believe this went to have a look one night. When they found that the stories about the haunting were indeed true, they ran home in fear.
206035: The oven house of a farm where a childless couple had lived was always haunted. At midnight a man in a sheet walked to the oven house, where he loosened a stone and took out a small chest. Then the apparition began counting the money in the chest. One day a brave man went up to the ghost and asked what was the matter. The ghost answered: "An old woman lived with us. We did not give her money to her family but kept it ourselves. Because our conscience was not at ease, we hid the money here." The man advised the ghost to give the money to the people who were entitled to it. Because the ghost did not dare, the man advised it to give the money to the parish priest. The priest in turn gave the money to the family.
206052: A man who had done something wrong had to go to the prison in Veurne for eight days. "All right," the man had said, "but I'm not walking to Veurne." So the man went to Veurne by coach with two policemen. When the coach reached Diksmuide, the policemen saw the man standing there in the market square.
206078: The mare was a stagnation of the blood. A woman was ridden by a male mare; a man by a female mare. People who were ridden by the mare heard footsteps on the stairs, after which the door was opened and the blankets were pulled off the bed. Then the victim felt a weight of a hundred kilos. People ridden by the mare could not breathe or cry out. When one was given a shove, one was freed from the mare.
206087: A gentleman who had already lost thousands of francs gambling came into the café one day saying: "I am completely ruined!" When the gentleman went outside, a black figure was waiting for him and asked him what was wrong. After the gentleman had explained his problem, the black figure said: "I can make sure you have plenty of money, but then you must sign a piece of parchment in blood, promising to give me your soul after your death." The gentleman agreed and signed the document. Then he went back to the inn, where he won heaps of money. The gentleman became extremely rich and led a debauched life. As he grew older, however, he began to worry and told a good friend what he had done. The friend advised him to go to the superior of the monastery. The cleric in the monastery said to the gentleman: "I can help you, but then you must surrender yourself completely to Our Lord." By means of an exorcism the father tried to get the parchment back. At that a voice rang out saying: "You will never get that parchment back!" The second time the same thing happened. When the father had spoken an exorcism for the third time, a rustling was heard and the parchment was seen lying on the communion rail. Thus the gentleman was saved.
206096: A farmer always heard strange noises in his barn at midnight, though there was nothing to be seen. The dog would then start barking and the livestock became restless. The calves had left their stall and stood lowing in the farmyard. Half an hour later, strangely enough, everything went back to normal. The friars of Dendermonde came to read prayers over the farm until they were drenched in sweat. When the clergymen had kept this up for nine days, the haunting came to an end.
206100: Two neighbour women did not get on. One of them had special powers and one day said to her neighbour: "You will be sorry for that! You will hear from me yet!" The next day the neighbour's house was full of big rats.
206108:
In Zwevezele lived a man who had special powers. When this wizard was visiting someone one evening and wanted to go home, they said to him: "Don't you need to take a light?" The wizard answered "No" and left. The wizard had only just gone, and already he was nowhere to be seen.
In a café some men were talking about women. One of these men, who was a wizard, said at a certain moment: "Shall I have a woman from Lichtervelde come here? She'll be here at once." A little later a woman from Lichtervelde did indeed appear.
206122: People and horses could be ridden by the mare. The mare had to do with witchcraft and was caused by people who could not stand a certain person. Horses ridden by the mare never grew fat.
206141: A house was plagued by rats through the doing of a witch.
206148: When fishermen went to sea, you were not allowed to wish them a good journey, because people believed that brought bad luck.
206152: People who were ridden by the mare felt as if a ghost was crawling on them, trying to strangle them.
206156: When a man went to visit his girlfriend in Ijvegem, he was followed by a coffin in the Otegemstraat. After a while the coffin disappeared into the trees. Wieske was so frightened by the whole incident that he never went to see his girlfriend again.
206173: A boy who worked for a farmer was joined by a sorceress. The sorceress made sure the work in the field was done in no time.
206188: In Kaster there lived a little woman who was only fifty centimetres tall. She had thick little legs and a big head. She always sat in the hedge and could cover people in lice. One day a mother who had taken her children to school was called by that strange little woman. The mother did not answer, however, and walked on. When she got home, the mother was full of lice. Even after she had changed her clothes, she could scrape the lice off her legs. At her wits' end, the mother had prayers read over her. After that there was not a single louse left on her clothes.
206195: A man and a woman coming home one evening saw a strange figure approaching them. It was a black figure with a bent back. The man overcame his fear and asked: "Who are you? Ghost or no ghost, who are you?" But as soon as the figure stood upright, the man and the woman became so afraid that they ran straight home.
206219: On a farm in Beselare, for several weeks people heard a goat screaming every evening. The goat was sitting in a tree.
206229: On a haunted farm, noise was always heard in the attic in the evening. It sounded as if a cart was being pushed back and forth up there. When the people boiled potatoes, at noon the potatoes flew out of the bowl by themselves into the postman's face. The cradle in which the baby lay rocked by itself. The people went to the dean, but he said: "The evil has gone too far. We can no longer master it."
206235: A girl was advised by her mother to place her slippers with the toes pointing towards the door. In that way the girl was protected against the mare.
206255: Some farmhands on their way to work saw three women with little bells approaching, who jumped over a gate and a moment later had vanished.
206267: A midwife by the canal in Damme was hindered by a dog that kept getting under her feet. The man who was with her, however, did not see the animal. When the midwife stood at the childbed, she could not manage to deliver the child. "Give me holy water," said the midwife. After the midwife had sprinkled half the market square of Damme with holy water, the child could be born.
206268: It was claimed that black cats were sorceresses. Since the Gospel of Saint John has been read at the end of Mass, the evil has been driven away.
206270: Two brothers who were at odds would not even enter the church by the same entrance. That is why the church of Beveren had two doors. After their death the brothers were cursed. They turned into two black dogs chained to each other. Every night the dogs had to go to the chapel of Kortekeer.
206288: On a farm in Houtkerke they could no longer make butter. Moreover, the farmer and his wife's child cried all the time. One day when the farmer and his wife were away, a woman was sitting by the open hearth in the farmhouse. The farmhand made the fire hotter and hotter until the witch said: "Please, stop that!" to which the farmhand replied: "If you stop harming the child!" The witch then took a pincushion and pulled out all the needles. After that the child cried no more.
206292: A midwife lost her way after seeing a phantom dog or phantom cat.
206310: A man who had gone to fetch the midwife was followed by a cat on his way home. On the way the man said irritably to the midwife: "I'm going to throw my clogs at that cat!" But the midwife replied: "No, you mustn't do that. Otherwise you might well have a lot of bad luck. You must never harm cats."
206334: On a farm, through the doing of a sorcerer, there was suddenly a plague of rats from one day to the next.
206370: A beggar woman came to a farm in Sint-Andries asking for butter. When the beggar woman had gone, butter could no longer be churned on the farm. The friars of Steenbrugge advised the people not to give the beggar woman alms the next time. After that the people could make butter again without any trouble.
206375: A farmer's wife was pushing a wheelbarrow to the farm in the evening. Suddenly she became so tired that she could do nothing more. She sat down on the ground and saw the wheelbarrow roll on by itself all the way to the farm.
206385: A mother was visited by a woman who owned books and was suspected of being able to work magic. The mother held her one-year-old son firmly by the hand so the sorceress could not touch the child. Two days later, strangely, the little boy could no longer walk. The child was taken to the friars of Tielt to have prayers read over him. While this was happening, there was a knock at the door. But they were not allowed to open it. The friars showed the sorceress's face in a mirror.
206399: A man had six sons and one daughter. When the daughter went missing one day, the people of the village searched for her in all the woods and fields. In the end the girl was found by a brook, sitting motionless on the ground. When they asked her why she had not come home, the girl said: "I couldn't, because I was sitting by a brook." The people were convinced that a woman who lived in a nearby house had bewitched the girl.
206414: The statue of Our Lady of Sint-Jan was carried in the procession every year. If this was not done, the statue of Mary went out alone. The next day people would then find that the statue's clothes were completely dirty.
206417: In a café the oil lamp was lit in the evening. When a customer raised his glass a little later, the flame suddenly went out. A sorceress had bewitched the oil.
206418: A man who went to a woman with a 'baste' (?) knocked and called: "Is anyone home?" The witch answered: "No, but the book is on the table." The man never set foot in that house again.
206419: Two men saw a carriage with a fine horse appear by a brook. One of the men let his friend dare him to take a ride in the carriage. The man flew over hill and dale.
206439: A woman who had heard a loud bang in the room found that the mirror had fallen to the floor and broken. Strangely, the screws were still in the wall and the cord was not broken. "Something must have happened," said the woman. An hour later she learned that her son had drowned by the quay.
206447: Near Bulskamp lived an old woman who made the straw fall off the wagons.
206463: A man on his way to Moorslede suddenly saw water everywhere near a farm, so that he could go no further. Suddenly the man saw a small boat that took him to the other side. On his way back the man found that the water and the boat had vanished.
206489: Near the castle of Stavele a little white rabbit always ran about. Nobody managed to catch the animal.
206491: A carpenter went to fell a tree in Zwevegem. The tree would not fall in the right direction because the wind was blowing the other way. In the end the carpenter climbed into the tree while two men stood watching. A woman came walking up who was said to be a witch. She was ordered to leave, but she stayed where she was. At that very moment the tree came down. The carpenter held on to the chains and jumped from a height of several metres. Then the witch quickly ran off. Nobody trusted her.
206493: Because people thought a house in Emelgem was on fire, they hurried past a café to see what was going on. The woman who ran the café told them, "You needn't go, it's only a house where bread is being baked."
206502: The bells of Papinglo have sunk into a pit.
206504: On a farm in Zonnebeke not a single animal could be kept alive. A woman who often came to visit there was the cause of the misfortune.
206532: A man from Lombardsijde who came out of a café in the evening was surrounded by little white cats.
206535: A man who had gone threshing got lost on his way home. Although the man did not have far to walk, he only got home the next morning. Moreover, the man never drank alcohol. Perhaps a wizard had made him lose his way.
206544: A woman who was home alone was visited by a witch. The witch poured the woman a cup of coffee, and the woman carelessly drank some. That night the woman did not sleep a wink. She shook like a leaf. The witch had done that to her.
206548: Witches always tried to get to the cradles of newborn children. When that happened at a farm in Sint-Andries, the child began to cry loudly.
206561: If the priest left his missal open after mass, no witch could leave the church.
206564: In a house, noises were always heard in the attic as if chains were being dragged across the floor. Some people became so frightened by it that they wanted to move.
206569: A little woman often heard knocking on the door in the evening while she was doing her needlework. Then a skull would come in and spin around on the table.
206578: People who were ridden by the mare felt suffocated and felt as if a thousand kilos were pressing on them. One could hear the mare coming. If one placed one's clogs upside down under the bed, one was protected against the mare.
206600: A man from Poperinge was in the habit of drinking a few glasses every evening in a nearby inn. When the man came home, he always saw a strange figure standing in front of his door. As soon as the man came closer, the figure had disappeared.
206602: During a heavy storm the helmsman of a ship had fallen overboard and drowned. When the ship moored, the dead man's son was waiting on the beach. But none of the crew had the courage to tell the boy what had happened. Every time the ship came back to the place where the helmsman had drowned, no one dared to stay alone on deck, because a voice could be heard calling.
206604: In an inn some men were teasing a parish priest. The priest bewitched one of those men to the ground with his glass in his hand.
206611: In Waregem there lived a witch. The witch's husband always sat weaving at night while white rats ran over the loom.
206632: In Zeldonk a friar could sometimes be seen at night, endlessly drifting along.
206640: An eighty-year-old man from Normandy claimed that ghosts were always walking around his table. Yet he was a sensible man who was not superstitious at all.
206642: A man who was ridden by the mare at night screamed with pain. When the mare had gone, the man crawled out of bed and went to sit downstairs by the stove because he did not dare lie down in his bed again. On his wife's advice, the man slept in his bed again a week later. That night the man was ridden by the mare again. The man woke up at once and recognised his neighbour, who quickly left the room. The man ran after the woman and called out her name. After that he was never ridden by the mare again.
206643: Strange things were sometimes seen in a street. At one time there was a pig, at another a little woman in a hooded cloak.
206644: A strange light could be seen near a hedge. A farmer who lived nearby asked the person who lived there whether he could have some blackberries. After a jug full of gold had been taken out of the hedge, the light was never seen again.
206687: A man returning from Zulte with two fat horses had to stop at the chapel in Ingelmunster because the sweating horses could go no further. On the wagon sat a doodlichtje (death light) and on the road ran a pack of cats. The man got down from the wagon and began kicking at the cats. The more the man kicked at the cats, the more cats appeared.
206692: A man coming home in the dark was followed by seven white goats. The man ran home as fast as he could. As soon as the man had jumped over the gate of his farm, the goats had strangely enough disappeared.
206693: An uncle had promised his nephews and nieces a great deal, but he had not been able to give it because of his family. (?) At night the uncle appeared to his nephews and nieces. After his niece had read out the deed, the uncle came to haunt no more.
206708: A cat always came into a broom maker's house through the drain hole for the water. The next day the neighbours always knew what had been said in that house. One evening the broom maker poured boiling water over the cat. The next day one of the neighbours had burns.
206721: At the funeral of a framasson (freemason) it was discovered that there were stones in the coffin. People believed that the freemason's corpse had been taken by the devil.
206755: People who were ridden by the mare at night had a stagnation of the blood.
206771: A brewer was annoyed by a cat that kept running between his legs. At a certain moment the man threw the cat into the boiling brew. When the brewer went inside a little later, he saw that his wife was lying burnt in bed.
206774: A woman who had had a baby was visited by a sorceress who wanted to see the child. The moment the sorceress took the child in her arms, it turned black and blue.
206780:
Two married couples were coming back together from the procession in Veurne. The husband and wife walking in front suddenly saw rats everywhere. The other couple did not see the rats.
A sorcerer could send rats to someone's house. When someone in a café had said something the sorcerer did not like, the sorcerer said: "You will regret that!" Afterwards the woman's house was full of rats.
206797:
A woman going to the old people's home with her two children was approached by an old woman who said, "You mustn't shake X's hand, because she can bewitch small children!"
From the very first day that witch lived in the village, people knew she could work magic. After all, she owned books of magic.
206802: The Vondelbeke castle on the road to Kortemark was haunted. Knocking was always heard there and no one dared to go and look. The former occupants had ten children, six of whom were unfortunate. After a pilgrimage service had been held in Halle, the seventh was perfect (?).
206804: In Kaster lived a certain Jus who had said that after his death he would come back in the shape of a pig. At eleven o'clock at night two women were returning from the field by moonlight. At the house where that man had lived, the women saw to their great fright a pig sniffing about. As the women passed the pig, they said: "Good evening, Jus." At that the pig ran after the two women. As soon as one of the women had taken the bread knife at home, the pig had vanished.
206822: A farmer from Koekelare was plagued by a real rat infestation. When the priest visited one day, the farmer asked him for advice. The priest said to the farmer: "I'll stand in the middle of the yard and take out my breviary. Then all the rats will come to me." When all the rats were with the clergyman, he said to the animals: "You may never come here again!" After that the farmer was rid of his rats for good.
